It operates a production Azure API Management gateway at api.finthrive.com (aliased as api.nthrive.com) with a public developer portal at api-portal.nthrive.com, but every API and product listed there is visible only after an Azure Active Directory or FinThrive-issued evaluation sign-in, so no machine-readable contract is published to the public.

providers.name: Food Safety and Inspection Service
providers.description: The Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS) is a branch of the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) responsible for ensuring the safety of the nation's commercial supply of meat, poultry, and egg products. FSIS publishes a Recall API that provides machine-readable access to recall and public health alert records.

providers.name: Function Health
providers.description: Function Health is a consumer longevity and preventive-health membership that runs 100+ lab biomarkers twice a year through Quest Diagnostics, adds clinician review, a biological age calculation, and an AI health companion via a web and mobile dashboard. As of this catalog Function Health does not publish a public or partner developer API; member data is accessed through the member dashboard, PDF export, in-product Connected Apps (wearable sync), and an opt-in ChatGPT app that shares a high-level summary of results.

providers.name: Houzz
providers.description: Houzz is a home renovation and design platform that connects homeowners with home professionals, products, and design inspiration, and operates Houzz Pro, an all-in-one business management SaaS for contractors and design professionals (3D floor plans, takeoffs, estimates, invoices, scheduling, CRM, and marketing). For commerce, Houzz runs a marketplace and exposes an official Seller/Vendor Commerce API (opened to third-party partners in 2016) that lets merchants sync product listings, inventory, pricing, and orders. API access is gated: sellers enable it under Settings > API in the Houzz dashboard or request it via sellerapi@houzz.com, then authenticate integrations with an App ID, Token, and User Name. Houzz does not publish a general-purpose public developer portal, OpenAPI spec, or first-party SDKs; integration is handled through the Seller/Vendor programs and Houzz Pro's pre-built integrations (QuickBooks, Zapier, Gmail, Google Calendar/Drive, Gusto).

providers.name: LaunchRock
providers.description: Launchrock is a hosted launch-page and customer-acquisition tool for early-stage founders. It provides a drag-and-drop WYSIWYG builder for pre-launch marketing pages, email capture forms, viral referral and social-sharing mechanics, and simple survey questions, so a founder can stand up a "coming soon" site and collect a waitlist of early users before a product ships. The platform pairs the builder with an education layer of founder courses, masterclass videos and how-to guides on customer acquisition, plus a community of mentors and founders. Launchrock is operated as one product line of the Startups.com platform, alongside Fundable, Bizplan and Clarity.fm, and is bundled into the Startups Unlimited subscription; its help content is served from the Startups.com knowledge base. Vevo, HotelTonight and theCHIVE are cited as sites that launched on the platform. Launchrock was originally a 500 Global (500 Startups) portfolio company. As of this profile Launchrock publishes no public API, developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI description, SDKs, CLI, webhook catalog or sandbox; delivery is entirely through the hosted web application.

providers.name: MeetAsh
providers.description: Ash (MeetAsh / Ash Wellness) is a New York-based health technology company, founded in 2019, that powers white-label at-home health testing programs for health plans, digital health companies, and public health organizations. Through a single, developer-friendly REST API integration, partners can trigger test kits, manage shipping logistics, and securely transmit results back into an EHR or patient portal across a national network of CLIA- and CAP-certified laboratories. Ash offers 120+ at-home diagnostic panels (hormone, cancer, allergy, STI, chronic condition, and infectious-disease testing with self-collected blood, stool, urine, saliva, and swab samples), care-gap-closure programs for HEDIS measures, kitting and fulfillment, physician-of-record services, and real-time reporting dashboards. The platform is fully HIPAA compliant and SOC 2 Type II certified, with enterprise-grade encryption protecting PHI. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched into the API Evangelist network; the developer documentation is partner-gated (password protected).

providers.name: Memory Store
providers.description: Memory Store is a Y Combinator (Spring 2026) startup building a universal, shared memory layer for teams and AI agents. It automatically collects insights from communication and productivity tools — Gmail, Slack, Granola, Claude, ChatGPT and more — and synthesizes them into an organized, searchable "company brain." Memory Store is delivered primarily as a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, letting AI clients such as Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and Raycast record what matters and recall it anywhere without changing existing workflows. A signature feature, "Briefs," maintains self-updating living documents (decision logs, team status, customer requests) as new information arrives.

providers.name: mxHero
providers.description: mxHERO Inc. is the pioneer of email-to-cloud content management, based in San Francisco and a long-time Box partner. Its Mail2Cloud platform is a bridge that intelligently captures email and attachments (in-flight or at-rest) over SMTP/S and IMAP/S and routes them, bi-directionally, into cloud content platforms such as Box, Egnyte, Microsoft OneDrive, Google Drive, and Dropbox — without retaining the content itself. Mail2Cloud Advanced adds an AI email-knowledge layer: captured email is deduplicated, metadata-preserved, and stored in an isolated per-tenant vector database that an official Model Context Protocol (MCP) server exposes to AI agents for secure email search and knowledge recovery, with a V3 REST API for dataset and S/MIME management.

providers.name: Netflix Conductor
providers.description: Conductor is a microservices orchestration platform originally created by Netflix, providing a workflow engine for coordinating and managing complex distributed processes across multiple services with built-in retries, error handling, and observability.

providers.name: Newton
providers.description: Newton is a Linux Foundation open source physics engine, contributed by Disney Research, NVIDIA, and Google DeepMind. Built on NVIDIA Warp and integrating MuJoCo Warp as a backend, Newton targets roboticists and simulation researchers, providing GPU-accelerated, differentiable, OpenUSD-compatible physics simulation for AI training, robotics, gaming, and scientific research.

providers.name: Norwegian University of Science and Technology
providers.description: The Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU) is Norway's largest university, headquartered in Trondheim with campuses in Gjovik and Alesund. NTNU operates no consolidated institutional developer portal and publishes no OpenAPI, AsyncAPI or other machine-readable API contract of its own. Its one openly callable, institution-operated surface is the OAI-PMH interface of NTNU Open Access Journals at www.ntnu.no/ojs, which answers Identify, ListMetadataFormats and ListSets over sixteen NTNU-published journals. NTNU also runs an institutional API gateway at api.ntnu.no, but every path on it is behind Feide OAuth and no public documentation, contract or scope list is served without an institutional account. Everything else that looks programmable under NTNU's name is operated by somebody else and entered here as a tenant relationship, not as NTNU engineering: research data in the NTNU collection of DataverseNO (run by UiT The Arctic University of Norway on Dataverse software), research information in Cristin and the national research archive NVA (both run by Sikt), timetables in TP on educloud.no, identity in the Feide federation where NTNU exists as the scope ntnu.no on Sikt's national IdP rather than as its own eduGAIN entity, and teaching in a hosted Canvas tenant. This repo previously carried 35 OpenAPI files and 87 derived artifacts that were splits of the generic Dataverse 6.6 product contract; they were the vendor's, not NTNU's, and have been removed.

providers.name: Office of the Federal Register
providers.description: The Office of the Federal Register is responsible for publishing official government documents. This includes the publication of presidential proclamations, executive orders, and regulations from federal agencies. The office also compiles and publishes the Code of Federal Regulations, which contains all federal regulations currently in effect.

providers.name: Open Service Mesh
providers.description: Open Service Mesh (OSM) is a lightweight, extensible, cloud native service mesh built on Envoy and the Service Mesh Interface (SMI) specification. OSM provides traffic shifting, mutual TLS, access control, observability, and automatic sidecar injection for Kubernetes-based microservices. The project is now archived by the CNCF.

providers.name: Photoshop
providers.description: Adobe Photoshop provides API capabilities through Adobe Firefly Services and the Photoshop API, allowing developers to automate photo editing, apply Photoshop actions, manipulate layers and smart objects, generate renditions, and leverage AI-powered image editing at scale.

providers.name: plateop-com
providers.description: plateop-com is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: mcp-registry) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.

providers.name: RapidSOS
providers.description: RapidSOS operates what it calls "the world's largest Safety Network," an intelligent safety platform that connects public safety agencies (911 / ECCs), enterprises, and hundreds of millions of connected devices to deliver AI-powered emergency detection, verification, and escalation for faster, more informed emergency response. RapidSOS exposes partner APIs so technology partners can send emergency-related information into the safety platform and public-safety partners can consume incident data, alongside products including Alerts and IAR (IamResponding). The developer documentation at developer.rapidsos.com is partner-login gated and RapidSOS does not publish an open OpenAPI specification. Backed by Insight Partners and Playground Global.

providers.name: RedCircle
providers.description: RedCircle is a podcast advertising platform that connects brands with podcasters to create authentic host‑read ads. Founded in 2018, the company offers a self‑serve ad platform, creative services, and detailed performance metrics. It serves over 1 billion ad impressions across 10 k+ partnered podcasters, handling everything from campaign setup to reporting. RedCircle aims to simplify podcast advertising for brands while ensuring creators are fairly compensated.

providers.name: RISC-V International
providers.description: RISC-V International advances the RISC-V open standard instruction set architecture (ISA), promoting open hardware development and reducing dependency on proprietary processor designs. The organization maintains the canonical RISC-V ISA specifications, profiles, non-ISA specifications, extensions, and a rich ecosystem of open-source tools including simulators, compilers, debuggers, and verification frameworks.

providers.name: Rocket
providers.description: Rocket (rocket.new) is an AI "vibe solutioning" platform for builders and founders that combines three products: Solve for market research and business analysis, Build for turning natural-language prompts or Figma designs into production-ready React, Next.js, and Flutter web and mobile apps, and Intelligence for tracking competitors across product, hiring, and funding signals. Build ships apps with one-click deploy to Netlify, custom domains, APK/App Store packaging, GitHub two-way code sync, and 26+ connectors (Stripe, Supabase, OpenAI, Anthropic, Twilio, HubSpot, and more) wired into the generated app from chat. Rocket is a no-code/AI app-builder product surface: it consumes external APIs (imported via Postman, cURL, or Swagger) rather than publishing its own public REST API, SDK, CLI, or MCP server. Backed by Accel, Electric Capital, and Sierra Ventures.

providers.name: SugarSync
providers.description: SugarSync provides cloud file syncing, sharing, and backup services across devices, offering personal and business plans with secure storage, collaboration tools, and mobile apps. Users can store, sync, and share files, photos, and videos, with features like versioning, folder sharing, and automated backups, accessible via web, desktop, and mobile applications.

providers.name: SwiftConnect
providers.description: SwiftConnect operates a "connected access network" that unifies digital identity, physical access credentials and building infrastructure into one platform, so an employee badge can live in Apple, Google or Samsung Wallet and open the doors an employer has authorized. Founded in 2020 and headquartered in Stamford, Connecticut, the company sits between access-control systems (LenelS2, Software House C-CURE 9000, Genetec), credential providers (HID, LEGIC, Wavelynx), identity providers and workplace platforms, and automates credential issuance, permission changes and revocation across all of them. It exposes that capability programmatically through the SwiftConnect Developer API at https://api.swiftconnect.io — a JSON REST API using bearer JWT authentication and a versioned `application/vnd.swiftconnect.v2+json` media type — plus a mobile "universal provisioning SDK" for adding credentials to a device wallet. The API reference is published on a password-protected ReadMe hub, so no machine-readable contract is public.

providers.name: Vegeta
providers.description: Vegeta is an open source HTTP load testing tool and library written in Go for generating constant request rates to measure API performance and reliability under sustained load. Supports CLI and library usage with attack plans, rate limiting, duration control, and detailed result metrics including latency histograms and success rates.

providers.name: Weyerhaeuser
providers.description: Weyerhaeuser is one of the world's largest private owners and managers of timberlands, operating approximately 10.4 million acres of timberlands in the U.S. with management rights over 14 million additional acres in Canada. The company grows and harvests trees, builds homes, and manufactures forest products including engineered lumber, oriented strand board (OSB), plywood, and lumber. Weyerhaeuser operates a developer-facing API Management (APIM) portal enabling partners and customers to integrate with its digital systems for wood products ordering and supply chain management.

providers.name: Wget
providers.description: GNU Wget is a free, open-source command-line utility for non-interactive downloading of files from the web using HTTP, HTTPS, FTP, and FTPS protocols. It supports recursive downloading, resuming aborted downloads, mirroring websites, proxy support, and can be run from scripts and cron jobs. Wget2 is the next-generation successor, written from scratch with multi-threading, HTTP/2, and a plugin API via libwget.

providers.name: Youi
providers.description: Youi is an Australian general insurance carrier headquartered at Sippy Downs on the Queensland Sunshine Coast, authorised by APRA and operating under AFSL 316511 (ABN 79 123 074 733). It is a wholly owned subsidiary of Youi Holdings Pty Ltd, part of OUTsurance International Holdings, with the South African-listed OUTsurance Group as ultimate holding company. Youi writes personal and small-business property and casualty lines direct to consumers - car, NSW CTP Green Slip, SA CTP, motorcycle, caravan and trailer, watercraft, home building and contents, and small business cover including public liability - and is a member of the Insurance Council of Australia and a signatory to the General Insurance Code of Practice. Its positioning is direct-to-consumer telephone and online underwriting rather than broker distribution. On API posture the honest finding is that Youi publishes no public API surface at all. Probing on 2026-07-25 found no developer portal (the developer., developers., docs. and api. subdomains do not resolve, and /developers, /api, /developer, /partners and /integrations all return HTTP 404), no downloadable OpenAPI or Swagger, no public Postman collection, no GraphQL, and no webhook or event catalog. The only integration-adjacent hosts are the customer self-service policy portal at portal.youi.com.au (HTTP 200, robots noindex, an Angular single-page app behind a login) and its private first-party backend portalapi.youi.com.au (HTTP 404 at root, serving no swagger or openapi document). No ACORD, AL3, ACORD XML, NGDS or IVANS reference was found anywhere on the public site. Australia's Consumer Data Right, which opened banking and energy, was designated for general insurance and then deferred, so no regulatory forcing function exists, and Youi's direct-to-consumer model gives it no broker or agency-management integration seam either. Recorded as partner-gated and customer-login-gated only, with no public self-serve API.

providers.name: 99 Data Rooms
providers.description: 99 Data Rooms (operated by 99 Developers Ltd) provides a UK‑hosted virtual data room platform that enables secure document sharing, e‑signature, and page‑by‑page viewer analytics. The service offers revocable links, a free tier for three rooms, GDPR‑ready compliance, and advanced tracking features for businesses of all sizes.

providers.name: Adaptive Insurance
providers.description: Adaptive Insurance is an Austin, Texas managing general agent and insurtech platform founded in 2024 by former Hippo executives Mike Gulla and Arik Yelovitch, writing parametric and specialty coverage for climate and weather risk in the United States. Its flagship product, GridProtect, is a parametric power-outage policy that pays automatically on a verified third-party outage trigger, typically within days; the portfolio also includes residential and commercial wind/hail deductible buy-backs, standalone residential flood coverage, equipment breakdown, and a Restaurant Recovery product offered by Tokio Marine HCC and powered by Adaptive. Distribution runs through appointed agents and brokers who quote, bind and issue online in under five minutes in a portal backed by the company's own identity tenant, plus embedded and white-label partner arrangements. Adaptive publishes no public developer program - no portal, reference, or machine-readable specification - so this profile records the identity and discovery surface it does serve.

providers.name: Anaplan
providers.description: Anaplan is a cloud-native connected planning platform used by enterprises for financial planning and analysis (FP&A), supply chain planning, and sales performance management. Its REST API (Integration API v2.0) allows integrators to import and export data, trigger model processes, and manage Anaplan workspaces programmatically. Beyond bulk data operations, Anaplan exposes dedicated APIs for financial consolidation, identity management via SCIM, audit event streaming, application lifecycle management, and CloudWorks custom integrations. All API access requires authentication via the Anaplan Authentication Service API, which issues tokens using username/password credentials or client certificates.

providers.name: Arbol
providers.description: Arbol is a global climate risk solutions platform providing parametric and traditional insurance and weather derivatives. Founded in 2018 and headquartered in New York, Arbol combines AI/ML-driven underwriting, institutional-grade climate data sourced from NOAA, NASA and ESA, and dedicated risk capital to close the global insurance protection gap. Coverage spans agriculture, energy, travel, wildfire and reinsurance, with parametric products that pay out on objective weather triggers rather than loss adjustment. Its licensed underwriting arm, Arbol Insurance Services, holds binding authority from an A.M. Best "A" rated carrier and Lloyd's coverholder status, and distributes named storm, precipitation, temperature, wind, snow, solar and soil-moisture products through licensed producers across all 50 U.S. states and the United Kingdom. Arbol does not publish a public developer API — the quoting, binding and policy-issuance surface is delivered through its broker/agent web platform.

providers.name: Asipipes
providers.description: Asipipes provides hosted YAML pipelines that agents can call as MCP tools, offering a library of reusable data processing pipes. Users can sign up with an invite code, create API keys, and integrate pipelines for tasks like SEC filings checks, news digests, and price snapshots, reducing token usage and improving efficiency. The platform emphasizes reproducibility, low token cost, and easy integration for developers.

providers.name: Bandung Institute of Technology
providers.description: Institut Teknologi Bandung (ITB) is a public technical university in Bandung, Indonesia, and one of the country's oldest and most selective engineering and science institutions. ITB publishes no developer portal, no API gateway, no API terms of service and no specification of any kind — api.itb.ac.id and data.itb.ac.id do not resolve, and no open-data portal was found. What it does operate, on its own domain and its own address space, are two protocol endpoints with no contract behind them: a campus-wide Apereo CAS single sign-on whose ticket-validation endpoints return machine-readable CAS XML, and an Open Journal Systems installation at journals.itb.ac.id that exposes a live, fully open OAI-PMH 2.0 data provider across twenty journal sets. Both are institution-operated; neither is institution-specified — the OJS software and its REST API are the Public Knowledge Project's, and that REST API is credential-gated (403). ITB is additionally a registered Crossref member through its research institute LPPM (member 3613, DOI prefix 10.5614, 6,568 DOIs) and carries a ROR identifier. The Ganesha Digital Library repository is publicly browseable but its historical OAI-PMH and RSS endpoints stayed dead after a platform migration, and the library site lib.itb.ac.id now returns a database error. This profile records institution-operated surfaces with no institution-published contract, which is the honest result rather than a gap to be padded.

providers.name: Benchmarq
providers.description: Benchmarq provides an AI readiness audit for websites, running over 200 standardized tests to evaluate how well a site can be discovered, read, and trusted by AI search agents. It scores each site from 0 to 100, highlights critical issues, and offers a prioritized fix list. The service includes free plans for developers and supports enterprise features via Enso DX.

providers.name: Blueprint Health
providers.description: Blueprint Health provides an AI‑powered assistant platform for therapists, helping with clinical documentation, administrative tasks, and patient care. The solution integrates with existing electronic health record (EHR) systems or can be used as a standalone all‑in‑one EHR, delivering automated note‑taking, billing support, and workflow automation to improve efficiency and reduce burnout among mental‑health professionals.

providers.name: bodo.ai
providers.description: Bodo.ai provides a modern enterprise analytics platform that bridges data teams, business users, and AI agents. Built on open‑source foundations under the Apache 2.0 license, Bodo enables scalable, high‑performance analytics and AI workloads with familiar tools like Python, Pandas, and SQL. Its products include the Bodo Engine for distributed compute and PyDough for trusted answer layers, offering governance, performance, and modularity for enterprise AI workflows.

providers.name: BoekenBase
providers.description: BoekenBase is a Dutch online catalogue of the books market, offering searchable access to over 2.2 million titles in natural language. Users can create free accounts to manage personal bookshelves and wishlists, browse detailed book information, and discover new reads. The platform provides an API for developers to integrate book data into applications, supporting queries by title, author, ISBN, and more, with comprehensive metadata and multilingual support.

providers.name: Code24
providers.description: CODE24 B.V. is a Dutch healthcare software company in Alkmaar that builds mConsole, a modern, modular electronic health record (EPD) for care and mental-health (GGZ) organisations, together with a family of "24" modules — Lab24, Opname24 (admissions), CrisisMonitor24, CTB24, Connect24, Router24, Dynaform24, Financieel24 and DataWarehouse24. Its architectural position is that a modern EPD must be open: care data is stored in standardised form using openEHR archetypes and Dutch zibs (zorginformatiebouwstenen), and every record is readable and writable through a software interface (API) so other care systems can be integrated without duplicate data entry. Connect24 exposes a FHIR REST API for collecting and transforming patient data to the Dutch MedMij standard; Router24 is a MedMij-qualified DVA that performs the authentication and resource-server roles for routing data to personal health environments (PGOs). CODE24 is also a Value Added Reseller of the Cadasto openEHR open data platform. The API surface is real but commercial: no developer portal, no public API reference and no machine-readable contract are published on any CODE24 host.

providers.name: Codekeeperbv
providers.description: Codekeeper BV provides software escrow and continuity solutions, helping organizations protect source code, SaaS applications, and AI models. Their platform offers vendor risk and compliance services for regulations like DORA, NIS2, and CRA, alongside secure storage, backup, and verification tools.

providers.name: Complutense University of Madrid
providers.description: Universidad Complutense de Madrid (UCM) is Spain's largest public research university, founded 1499 and ranked #164 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. UCM operates no central developer portal and publishes no OpenAPI, AsyncAPI or SDK of its own — a re-profile on 2026-08-30 probed every candidate host and found none. What it does operate, verified live, is two things. First, Docta Complutense (docta.ucm.es), its institutional repository, self-hosted on UCM's own domain running DSpace 7.6.5: the DSpace REST/HAL API answers at /rest/api and an OAI-PMH 2.0 endpoint answers verb=Identify at /rest/oai/request with twelve metadata formats. The repository is UCM's; the API contract is DSpace's open-source one and is not saved here. Second, UCM is registered in eduGAIN through the Spanish RedIRIS SIR federation as a SAML 2.0 Identity Provider (entityID https://www.rediris.es/sir/ucmidp, scope ucm.es, Sirtfi asserted) — machine-readable, institution-scoped, but hosted on RedIRIS infrastructure, so recorded as a tenant relationship. UCM's open data is not self-hosted either: it is published through UniversiDATA, a five-university DKAN consortium portal (UAM, UCM, UHU, UVa, URJC) that exposes DataStore, CKAN and DCAT APIs. Thirteen of the portal's seventy-one datasets are UCM's — degree programmes, faculties, departments, budgets, mobility and procurement. UCM's data, the consortium's platform, so every UniversiDATA surface below is x-operator tenant, not institution. No course/timetable API, no library discovery API, no research-computing or campus-life API was found on any ucm.es host.

providers.name: Day.ai
providers.description: Day.ai provides an AI-powered platform that helps businesses automate and optimize their daily operations through intelligent assistants, workflow automation, and data-driven insights. Leveraging large language models, the service offers natural language interfaces, task scheduling, and integration with existing enterprise tools, enabling teams to streamline processes, improve productivity, and make informed decisions based on real-time analytics. The company focuses on delivering scalable, secure, and customizable AI solutions for a wide range of industries, from finance to healthcare.

providers.name: Dev Proxy
providers.description: Dev Proxy is a Microsoft command-line tool for simulating, testing, and debugging API interactions during development.

providers.name: DFINITY
providers.description: The DFINITY Foundation is a Swiss-based not-for-profit research organization that created and stewards the Internet Computer Protocol (ICP), a public, decentralized "frontier cloud" that hosts software and data entirely inside a mathematical network protocol. Applications run as canisters (WebAssembly smart contracts with persistent state, native HTTP, and a reverse gas model paid in Cycles) that are tamperproof, unstoppable, and free from vendor lock-in. ICP uses Chain Key cryptography and Chain Fusion to transact natively on Bitcoin and Ethereum without bridges, and is governed on-network by the Network Nervous System (NNS). DFINITY publishes first-party developer tooling — JavaScript/TypeScript agent libraries under the @dfinity npm scope, Rust agent and Canister Developer Kit crates, the icp/dfx CLIs, and an AI agent skills library — plus a public HTTP interface for reading from and calling canisters.

providers.name: DiagramZu
providers.description: DiagramZu is an MCP server plus shared workspace where Claude Code, Cursor, ChatGPT and any other MCP client write Mermaid diagrams directly. Its fourteen MCP tools search, create, read and update diagrams, browse folders, trace version history, build presentation decks, leave comments and analyze a rendered diagram for problems. Teams get a versioned share link they can open, comment on and embed with no login needed to view, and no LLM runs inside the app. A hosted MCP endpoint is documented at https://mcp.diagramzu.ai/mcp.

providers.name: EasyAccessPDF
providers.description: EasyAccessPDF provides an automated PDF accessibility service that tags PDFs for screen readers and validates them against PDF/UA (ISO 14289) using the open‑source veraPDF validator. It offers a flat‑rate per‑document pricing model, free compliance checks, and EU‑based processing, aiming to help businesses meet Section 508, ADA Title II/III, and the European Accessibility Act requirements. The platform also includes AI tools for diagram generation and various PDF conversion utilities, with membership plans for unlimited usage.

providers.name: Evidence
providers.description: Evidence is an open-source (MIT) business-intelligence-as-code framework that turns SQL queries plus Markdown into fast, version-controlled static data apps and dashboards. It is built on Svelte/Vite, runs queries through a DuckDB-WASM "Universal SQL" engine, and is consumed as a framework/CLI rather than a hosted REST API. Evidence Cloud adds managed hosting, a managed query engine, scheduled data syncs, and AI authoring assistance.

providers.name: FreeToGame
providers.description: FreeToGame is a platform that offers a wide selection of free-to-play online games for gamers to enjoy.

providers.name: Garmin
providers.description: Garmin is the global leader in GPS-enabled wearables, cycling computers, outdoor handhelds, marine electronics, aviation avionics, and automotive navigation. Garmin's developer surface spans the Connect IQ wearable app platform (Monkey C, watch faces, data fields, widgets, device apps), the Garmin Connect Developer Program cloud APIs (Health, Activity, Women's Health, Training, Courses), the Health SDK for direct BLE streaming from wearables, the FIT SDK that defines the industry's de-facto endurance data interchange format, Navionics marine cartography, inReach satellite messaging, the ANT/ANT+ wireless protocol, and specialized APIs for golf, aviation flight data, fleet telematics, and custom outdoor maps.

providers.name: Halo Collar
providers.description: Halo Collar is the consumer GPS dog-fence and dog-tracking product built by Protect Animals With Satellites LLC (d/b/a Halo), founded in 2017 by Ken Ehrman, Michael Ehrman and dog behaviorist Cesar Millan. The product pairs a cellular- and GPS-connected smart collar (currently Halo Collar 5, with Halo Collar 4 still sold) with a companion iOS/Android app that lets an owner draw virtual GPS fences, watch real-time location, trigger Cesar Millan-designed training feedback, and read activity reports. The service runs on a required Pack Membership subscription in Bronze, Silver and Gold tiers that carries unlimited cellular data, an increasing virtual-fence allowance, accessory discounts and third-party partner perks. Halo publishes no public developer program: the app is served by a first-party, undocumented backend at api.halocollar.com (an ASP.NET service that self-identifies as Halo.Web.Api), and there is no developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI/GraphQL contract, SDK or webhook surface anywhere on the company's public web properties.

providers.name: Hulu
providers.description: Hulu is an American subscription streaming service offering live and on-demand TV shows, movies, and original content. Operated by Hulu LLC, a joint venture between Disney and Comcast, it provides various plans including ad-supported and ad-free options, as well as a bundle with Disney+ and ESPN+. The platform streams across web, mobile, and connected TV devices, delivering a broad library of entertainment for subscribers.

providers.name: Hyground
providers.description: Hyground GmbH (Hamburg, Germany) builds a sovereign, self-hosted AI SRE (Site Reliability Engineering) agent for European enterprises. The multi-agent platform deploys as a Kubernetes-native Helm chart inside the customer's own perimeter and correlates Kubernetes, observability (Prometheus, Loki, Elasticsearch), cloud (AWS/Azure/GCP), CI/CD, and ticketing data to produce evidence-backed root cause analysis, autonomous incident response, and scheduled operations work such as CVE blast-radius mapping, RBAC drift audits, cluster right-sizing, and cost triage. It runs read-only by default, is bring-your-own-model (Azure OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, Gemini, Bedrock, Ollama), and keeps all data in-cluster with no external egress, targeting GDPR, BaFin, DORA, and NIS2 compliance requirements. Backed by partech; raised a EUR 3M pre-seed round.

providers.name: Koala Health
providers.description: Koala Health is a digital pet pharmacy headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts that dispenses prescription medications, vitamins, supplements and veterinary diets for dogs and cats direct to pet parents, with an emphasis on chronic-condition medication management. Orders are packaged into date- and time-sorted pouches, refilled automatically, and prescriptions are fetched and verified directly with the pet parent's veterinarian. Koala also runs KoalaVet, a clinic-facing platform that integrates with veterinary PIMS (practice information management systems) to sync client and patient records two-way, let clinic teams review, approve and submit prescriptions in a few clicks, and operate a branded managed online pharmacy for the practice. The company is a licensed non-resident pharmacy across US states, is LegitScript certified and .pharmacy (NABP) verified. Koala Health publishes no public developer API, developer portal or API documentation as of this profile; api.koala.health resolves to an internal Rails/Heroku administrative application behind sign-in.

providers.name: Microsoft Stream
providers.description: Microsoft Stream is an intelligent video service for enterprise video management. Videos are stored in OneDrive and SharePoint with video-specific capabilities accessible through Microsoft Graph and SharePoint APIs.

providers.name: Nextra
providers.description: Nextra is an open-source, Next.js-based documentation framework for building fast, modern, and beautifully styled documentation sites. It extends Next.js with MDX support, file-system routing, built-in search powered by Pagefind, syntax highlighting via Rehype Pretty Code, LaTeX rendering, static image optimization, i18n support, and a full-featured docs theme with sidebar, navbar, TOC, dark mode, and breadcrumb navigation.

providers.name: Panorama Education
providers.description: Panorama Education is a K-12 education technology company whose student success platform is used by thousands of school districts to turn student data into action across academics and behavior (MTSS/RTI), universal screening, social- emotional learning (SEL) and survey instruments, attendance, graduation planning, and family and staff engagement. The platform ingests data nightly from 24+ student information systems, learning management systems, and 100+ benchmark and state assessments using the OneRoster standard and secure file transfer. Panorama does not publish a public self-service developer API; integrations are delivered as managed B2B data synchronization. The company is SOC 2 Type 2 attested, 1EdTech Data Privacy certified, ESSA Level II/IV rated, and a Student Privacy Pledge signatory (FERPA/COPPA/PPRA/CCPA aligned).

providers.name: Polimorphic
providers.description: Polimorphic is a New York-based government technology company building a complete AI platform for local, county, state, and federal government service delivery. Its product suite pairs a Constituent Relationship Manager (CRM) with an AI Chatbot & Search, a Voice Agent (VoiceAI), and Workflows so public agencies can answer residents 24/7 in 75+ languages and guide them through permits, licenses, applications, and payments from intake to resolution. Polimorphic connects to existing government systems of record (ArcGIS, Tyler, Accela, Salesforce, Laserfiche, Stripe, and more) and is used by 200+ public-sector departments serving tens of millions of residents. Founded by Parth Shah (CEO) and Daniel Smith (CTO), the company is backed by General Catalyst, M13, and Shine.

providers.name: Protocol Labs
providers.description: Protocol Labs is a pioneering research, development, and deployment organization focused on building the protocols, tools, and services that underpin the decentralized web. Founded by leading technologists, the company creates open-source infrastructure such as IPFS, Filecoin, and libp2p, enabling distributed storage, content addressing, and peer-to-peer networking. Its mission is to accelerate the adoption of decentralized technologies by fostering innovation, supporting developers, and collaborating with a global community of contributors and partners across the blockchain and web3 ecosystem.

providers.name: Pulse Grow
providers.description: The Pulse API is an HTTP API that is designed to interact with your pulse account and devices.

providers.name: Rivia
providers.description: Rivia is a clinical trial intelligence platform based in Zurich, Switzerland that unifies fragmented clinical trial data from any vendor into a single, structured foundation for biotech and pharmaceutical companies. Its products include Rivia Core (data harmonization), Rivia Detect (AI agents that continuously identify and resolve data quality issues), and Rivia Spark (visual analytics with a conversational AI assistant for exploring trial data through natural language). The platform supports medical and clinical science, safety monitoring, clinical operations, and executive oversight use cases, promising go-live in under 20 days. Rivia raised a $15M Series A and is backed by investors including Earlybird and Speedinvest. The company is a sales-led enterprise platform with no public developer portal or API surface as of this profile; onboarding is via demo request.

providers.name: RunAnywhere
providers.description: RunAnywhere is a Y Combinator (W2026) infrastructure company building the layer for deploying fast, private, multimodal AI on-device at scale. It ships one open-source C++ core runtime with native bindings for Swift, Kotlin, React Native, Flutter, and the browser, plus hand-written GPU/NPU inference engines (MetalRT for Apple GPUs, QHexRT for Qualcomm Hexagon NPUs) that run LLM, VLM, speech-to-text, text-to-speech, and embedding workloads locally. The SDKs handle model delivery, extraction, storage management, versioning, and observability, and support hybrid routing that tries on-device inference first before optionally falling back to the cloud. A hosted control plane (api.runanywhere.ai) manages model delivery and configuration via API key.

providers.name: Sardine
providers.description: Sardine is a San Francisco-based fraud prevention, AML compliance, and risk management platform for fintechs, banks, marketplaces, and crypto VASPs. It unifies onboarding (KYC, KYB, document and bank verification), device intelligence and behavioral biometrics, payment and card fraud scoring, AML transaction monitoring, sanctions screening, and case management into a single risk operating system. Sardine's "agentic" layer applies atomic agents (OSINT, data analysis, transaction monitoring, business due diligence, sanctions screening) to compress investigation time from days to minutes, while Sonar provides cross-industry fraud intelligence across the consortium. The platform serves 400+ enterprise customers including FIS, GoDaddy, Intuit, Nubank, Novo, and bunq, has screened $1.3T+ in payments, and profiled 5.4B+ devices. Sardine has raised ~$170M from Andreessen Horowitz, Visa, Experian, Google Ventures, FIS, and others. Public docs cover the risk landscape and integration overview; full API reference, SDKs, and sandbox access are gated and require a Sardine account.

providers.name: University of Sussex
providers.description: The University of Sussex is a research-intensive public university at Falmer near Brighton in the United Kingdom, a member of the Russell Group's peer set of UK research institutions and ranked #247 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. Its programmable footprint is small and almost entirely indirect, and this profile says so rather than padding it. The one surface the university genuinely operates and publishes machine-readably is its own Shibboleth identity provider: idp.sussex.ac.uk serves signed SAML 2.0 metadata with an entityID of https://idp.sussex.ac.uk/shibboleth and a shibmd:Scope of sussex.ac.uk, running on a Sussex-controlled Azure deployment rather than a vendor's multi-tenant service. Everything else that looks like a Sussex API is a vendor product running under a Sussex name: Okta for single sign-on at okta.sussex.ac.uk, Instructure Canvas for the VLE at canvas.sussex.ac.uk, Figshare for the research repository at sussex.figshare.com, and Ex Libris Primo for library discovery. Those relationships are recorded here as tenant surfaces because they are real institutional facts, but the contracts behind them belong to the vendors and are scored against the vendors' own profiles. Sussex operates no public developer portal, publishes no OpenAPI of its own, and its GitHub organization has no public repositories. The former Sussex Research Online EPrints repository and its OAI-PMH endpoint have been decommissioned and now redirect to an HTML publications page.

providers.name: Wine Vybe
providers.description: Wine Vybe is a wine, beer, and liquor database API platform that provides access to comprehensive beverage data including wine regions, grape varieties, tasting notes, food pairing recommendations, awards, producer information, brewery and distillery details, and custom taste profiles. The platform serves app developers and businesses through RESTful APIs hosted on RapidAPI.

providers.name: Zefr
providers.description: Zefr is an ad-tech content intelligence company that classifies social video, image, audio and text so advertisers can buy and measure media against brand safety and suitability standards. Its classification engine labels content across YouTube, Meta (Facebook and Instagram), TikTok, Snapchat, Google Ads and DV360 against the 4A's and GARM frameworks, and its Brand Suitability Suite gives brands pre-bid controls and post-bid measurement from a single console. Zefr has no public developer program: production API infrastructure exists (api.zefr.com is a Google Apigee gateway, alongside api2.zefr.com and api-eu1.zefr.com) but no developer portal, API reference or machine-readable contract is published anywhere, and access runs through a demo request. The only machine-readable documents Zefr serves publicly are the OpenID Connect and OAuth 2.0 Authorization Server Metadata discovery documents on its Auth0 custom domain, login.zefr.com.

providers.name: Accenta
providers.description: Accenta is a French energy and carbon performance company for real estate portfolios, founded in 2016 and headquartered in Boulogne-Billancourt. It combines AI-driven building control (an intelligent building management system plus an Accenta Communication Box for sites with no BMS) with low-carbon heat and cold production built on shallow geothermal energy, inter-seasonal geostorage, heat pumps and solar, and it wraps the whole package in audit, design, build, operate, financing and performance-contract services. Accenta says it manages roughly 10 million square metres of real estate for owners such as Airbus, Prologis, Icade, Redevco and Decathlon, targeting energy reductions up to 80% and CO2 reductions up to 95%. Its software platform is effiPilot, acquired in 2020, delivered as a per-customer tenant on accenta.ai with a web application, an Android app and an HTTP API whose reference documentation sits behind the customer login.

providers.name: AI Commander
providers.description: AI Commander provides remote shell and long‑running job execution for AI agents on user‑owned machines. It supports Claude, ChatGPT, Codex, Grok and other models, offering outbound‑only connections, encrypted traffic, and file transfer capabilities. Users can install agents on macOS, Windows or Linux, obtain a session code, and let the AI run commands, scripts, or training jobs without exposing inbound ports. Free tier supports up to 10 machines; paid plans add more machines and file transfer.

providers.name: AI Visibility Index
providers.description: ChatGPT・Claude・Gemini・Perplexityで調査したEC104社のAI可視性スコアとランキングを無料公開。対象外ドメインは、4エンジンの新規測定・競合比較・改善提案を含む個別診断を選べます。 公開ランキング対象のEC104社について、ChatGPT・Claude・Gemini・Perplexityの保存済みスコアと順位を確認できます。対象外ドメインは、個別診断で新規測定・競合比較・改善提案まで受け付けています。

providers.name: Akiflow
providers.description: Akiflow brings tasks, calendars, and AI into one time‑blocking planner, helping busy professionals plan focused days and follow through. From a simple idea to an all‑in‑one platform, Akiflow is building the ultimate time‑blocking app, imagining the future of work together.

providers.name: Alkera Ai
providers.description: Alkera is an AI data-engineering agent that works across your data stack from the command line and inside your editor to build, migrate, optimize, and debug data pipelines. It ships as a CLI and an IDE extension (VS Code and Open VSX forks such as Cursor and Windsurf), and pairs a cross-platform column-level lineage engine with a living knowledge base so the agent understands what your data means and what your team already decided about it. Alkera connects natively to 14+ platforms including Snowflake, Databricks, BigQuery, dbt, and Airflow, builds new pipelines end to end (sources, models, tests, orchestration), migrates legacy systems while verifying functional equivalence, removes dead pipelines, refactors slow models, and performs root-cause analysis with blast-radius awareness. It ranked first on DataAgentBench (83.28% Pass@1). Enterprise deployments add SSO/SAML, SCIM & IAM, audit logs, pooled usage, VPC and on-prem deployment, zero data retention by default, data residency controls, and SLAs.

providers.name: Apiboost Developer Portals
providers.description: Apiboost Developer Portals provides a multi-gateway developer portal solution that helps organizations avoid vendor lock‑in, visualize and manage APIs across platforms, and accelerate integration. The platform offers features such as API spec rendering, AI‑assisted SDLC, comparison tools for major API gateways, and industry‑specific solutions for fintech, manufacturing, logistics, and healthcare. With a free 30‑day trial, Apiboost enables teams to consolidate API governance, improve developer experience, and drive digital transformation across the enterprise.

providers.name: Arbor Networks
providers.description: Arbor Networks is the DDoS protection and network-visibility division of NETSCOUT (Arbor Networks was acquired by NETSCOUT in 2015). Drawing on more than 25 years of experience and visibility into roughly 800 Tbps of global internet traffic across 550+ service-provider and enterprise customers, Arbor builds products that detect and mitigate distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks and provide network traffic analytics. Its portfolio includes Arbor Sightline (formerly Peakflow SP) for service-provider-scale monitoring, analytics and mitigation orchestration; Arbor Edge Defense (AED) as an inline stateless perimeter appliance; the Arbor Threat Mitigation System (TMS); Arbor Cloud managed scrubbing (16 global scrubbing centers, 15+ Tbps); and Arbor Spectrum/Insight for advanced threat analytics. Arbor exposes programmatic control primarily through the Sightline "SP REST API" (a JSON:API-compliant interface rooted at /api/sp/ on the appliance) and the Edge Defense Manager (EDM) API, with first-party client tooling published on GitHub and PyPI.

providers.name: AU10TIX
providers.description: AU10TIX is an identity verification and document authentication provider delivering KYC, document analysis, biometric face comparison, liveness, and fraud detection through a single REST API (the Back Office Server, "BOS") and web/mobile SDKs. The platform orchestrates verification workflows/sessions, returns structured results, and notifies clients via webhooks.

providers.name: BarnBridge
providers.description: BarnBridge is a risk tokenization DeFi protocol that allows users to hedge yield sensitivity and price volatility by transforming debt pools into structured products with varying risk and return characteristics. It offers SMART Yield bonds with junior and senior tranches, SMART Alpha for price volatility management, SMART Exposure for automated rebalancing, and yield farming analytics via a REST API.

providers.name: Briefcase
providers.description: Briefcase is an AI-native accounting and bookkeeping automation platform for UK accounting firms and businesses. Founded in 2024 in London by Reuben Steenkamp and Ján Stehlík, and backed by Earlybird Venture Capital, Entrepreneur First and Tiny, Briefcase describes itself as building the world's first AI autopilot for accounting firms. The product uses multimodal AI and agentic workflows to automate the most tedious parts of accounting: extracting data from invoices, receipts and bank statements, categorising transactions against a firm's chart of accounts, handling VAT (with embedded HMRC legislation for standard, reverse-charge and zero-rated VAT), automating prepayments and expense claims, and driving month-end and financial close. It publishes results into Xero and QuickBooks. Briefcase is delivered as a cloud SaaS application (app.briefcase.so); it is a consumer of accounting APIs rather than a public API producer, and at the time of this profile it publishes no developer/API documentation, OpenAPI, or SDKs.

providers.name: Budbee
providers.description: Budbee provides a flexible, last‑mile delivery service across Europe, offering home delivery and returns with convenient time‑slot booking via its app or website. Founded in Sweden, Budbee focuses on sustainable logistics, using renewable diesel and optimizing routes to reduce emissions. It serves merchants and consumers, enabling easy parcel tracking, flexible Box locations for pick‑up and drop‑off, and integrates with e‑commerce platforms. Budbee aims to enhance the online shopping experience by ensuring reliable, environmentally‑friendly deliveries and returns.

providers.name: Certinal
providers.description: Certinal provides a Healthcare Consent & Compliance Platform that digitizes consent capture, electronic signatures, and patient intake, integrating directly with EHR systems such as Epic, Cerner, MEDITECH, and OpenEMR. The platform is designed for healthcare organizations to meet regulatory requirements including HIPAA, 21 CFR Part 11, CMS‑0053‑F, DPDP, and PDPA, and to automate consent workflows across surgical, clinical trial, telehealth, and general treatment contexts.

providers.name: Containous (Traefik Labs)
providers.description: Containous SAS is the France-founded (2016) cloud-native networking company that created Traefik, the open-source reverse proxy, ingress controller, and load balancer written in Go and downloaded billions of times from Docker Hub. Containous was surfaced through the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Balderton Capital, which led its Series A alongside Elaia Partners, 360 Capital, Kima Ventures, and OSS Capital. The company subsequently rebranded to Traefik Labs and its original containo.us domain now redirects to traefik.io. Under the Traefik Labs name it ships the open-source Traefik Proxy plus the commercial Traefik Hub product line (API Gateway, API Management, AI Gateway, and MCP Gateway). This repo is the company/parent profile; the full product and API surface (OpenAPI, CRDs, examples) lives in the api-evangelist/traefik repo.

providers.name: Dovri
providers.description: Dovri provides an AI‑powered support desk that integrates directly into your product’s chat interface. Teams can read conversations within Dovri and reply inside the customer’s chat, enabling seamless assistance without leaving the app. The platform offers free workspace for one app, supports email and Telegram, and includes flat‑rate paid plans for AI answers with no per‑seat charges. It emphasizes privacy, requiring Google sign‑in, and is built by LaserFocused OÜ.

providers.name: Dukon AI
providers.description: Dukon AI provides an AI-powered integration that connects your BILLZ accounting system to Claude and ChatGPT, enabling natural language queries for revenue, profit, inventory, and reports. It offers a free 20‑day trial with no credit card required, and multiple pricing plans in USD and UZS.

providers.name: Instapaper
providers.description: Instapaper is a read‑it‑later service that lets users save web articles to read later across devices such as iOS, Android, desktop browsers, and e‑readers. Founded in 2008, it offers a clean, distraction‑free reading experience, supports offline access, highlights, notes, and integrates with services like Pocket, Flipboard, and Twitter. The service provides a simple HTTP API for developers to add, retrieve, and manage saved items, documented at https://www.instapaper.com/api/1.

providers.name: JB Hi-Fi
providers.description: JB Hi-Fi Limited is an ASX-listed Australian retailer of consumer electronics and home entertainment, founded in 1974 by John Barbuto with a single store in East Keilor, Victoria, and floated on the Australian Stock Exchange in October 2003. It describes itself as Australia's largest home entertainment retailer, selling computers, tablets, TVs, cameras, hi-fi, games, music and movies through its stores and its online store at jbhifi.com.au, alongside JB Hi-Fi HOME stores, JB Hi-Fi Business, a BYOD education portal and the JB Hi-Fi Marketplace. Its online store publishes an agents.md guide advertising Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) discovery and an MCP endpoint for agentic shopping.

providers.name: Jimdo
providers.description: Jimdo is a website builder platform that provides REST APIs for managing website content, blog posts, online store products, and customer data for small business websites. The platform offers AI-powered website creation tools, ecommerce capabilities, and developer integrations enabling businesses to build and manage their online presence programmatically.

providers.name: lightsyncpro-com
providers.description: LightSync Pro enables automatic synchronization of Adobe Lightroom, Figma, Dropbox, Shutterstock, Canva, and other media sources to WordPress and Shopify sites. It adds AI‑generated images via OpenRouter and extends syncing to Google Drive, OneDrive, HubSpot, Contentful, Webflow, and a generic HTTP API, offering a low‑code solution for content creators and e‑commerce merchants.

providers.name: Noble Minds Media
providers.description: Noble Minds Media is a technology company focused on providing advanced trading and financial data APIs for MetaTrader 4 platforms. It offers real-time market data, historical price feeds, and automated trading tools, targeting developers and financial institutions seeking to integrate MT4 capabilities into their applications. The company emphasizes low latency, high reliability, and comprehensive documentation to support seamless integration.

providers.name: Open Design Alliance
providers.description: Open Design Alliance (ODA) is a non‑profit consortium that provides developers with tools and libraries to create, view, and edit CAD (Computer‑Aided Design) files across multiple platforms. Founded in 1998, ODA offers the Teigha platform, which supports a wide range of DWG, DGN, and other industry‑standard formats, enabling interoperability among CAD applications. The organization focuses on fostering collaboration among its member companies, delivering high‑quality SDKs, documentation, and support for building robust engineering and design software solutions. Through its open‑source initiatives and extensive developer resources, ODA empowers engineers, architects, and software developers to integrate advanced CAD capabilities into their products, accelerating innovation in the design and manufacturing sectors.

providers.name: put.io
providers.description: put.io is a cloud storage service that lets users download files from public sources such as torrents, direct links, and video sites, storing them in a personal cloud. Users can stream media on various devices, manage files via web, apps, or CLI, and automate actions with IFTTT, FTP/WebDAV, and other integrations. The service emphasizes privacy, offering private storage without public sharing, and provides a RESTful API for programmatic access to file management, transfers, and account information.

providers.name: Qwak
providers.description: Qwak is an end-to-end production machine learning platform that lets data science and ML engineering teams build, train, deploy, monitor, and manage models with minimal engineering friction. The platform unifies MLOps, LLMOps, and a Feature Store, covering model registry and management, GPU/CPU training, production deployment as real-time API endpoints, batch inference or streaming, real-time monitoring and anomaly detection, LLM prompt management, and vector storage. Developers interact with the platform through the `qwak` CLI, the Python SDKs (qwak-sdk, qwak-core, qwak-inference), and a public Go SDK. Qwak was acquired by JFrog and rebranded JFrog ML; its documentation now lives on docs.jfrog.com and the successor SDK is `frogml`. Surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners.

providers.name: reviewpaper-ai
providers.description: ReviewPaper.ai is an AI-powered platform that generates peer‑review style feedback for academic papers submitted to major conferences such as NeurIPS, ICLR, and ACL. By simulating the exact review format of each venue, it provides a predicted score, a ranked list of suggested improvements, and the ability to iteratively re‑review revised drafts or draft rebuttals. The service offers three free reviews per user and aims to help researchers strengthen their submissions before official review.

providers.name: Ripl
providers.description: Ripl is a social media marketing platform for small businesses, helping owners create, schedule, and publish engaging content across Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, YouTube, and other channels from customizable, industry-specific templates. It bundles branded post design, stock media, royalty-free music, scheduling, multi-account management, team collaboration, and an AI caption writer so restaurants, retailers, real estate agents, nonprofits, and other small businesses can maintain a consistent, professional online presence without a dedicated marketing team. Ripl is a Techstars portfolio company. Its public website (ripl.com) is built on Wix and exposes no first-party developer API; the app at app.ripl.com is the primary consumer product.

providers.name: Superfluid
providers.description: Superfluid is a money-streaming protocol for real-time, on-chain cashflows, enabling continuous "payments by the second" to any wallet address across EVM networks. Built by Superfluid Labs, the protocol powers salaries, subscriptions, rewards, airdrops, vesting, and incentive distributions as programmable token streams and distribution pools. Developers integrate via first-party TypeScript SDKs (@superfluid-finance/sdk-core, sdk-redux), the on-chain smart contracts (@superfluid-finance/ethereum-contracts), an embeddable checkout Widget, and a public GraphQL Subgraph API served through The Graph for querying streams, pools, accounts, and token statistics. The protocol has streamed over $1.6B to 1.27M recipients across DeFi, SocialFi, and gaming use cases.

providers.name: Taddy
providers.description: Taddy is a GraphQL API for podcasts and comics, giving developers access to over 4 million podcasts and 200 million episodes, plus real-time full-text search, automatically generated episode transcripts, chapters, iTunes metadata, daily top charts, webcomic and creator data, and webhook notifications for new or updated content. All queries hit a single GraphQL endpoint at https://api.taddy.org authenticated with X-USER-ID and X-API-KEY headers.

providers.name: Vareto
providers.description: Vareto is an AI-native financial planning and analysis (FP&A) platform that helps finance teams build financial models, budgets, and forecasts — including headcount and capacity planning, sales revenue forecasting, and P&L, balance sheet, and cash flow modeling — with real-time multiplayer collaboration, executive and board reporting, and data integrations spanning ERPs (NetSuite, SAP, QuickBooks, Sage Intacct), HRIS platforms (Workday, ADP, Rippling, and 25+ more), CRMs (Salesforce, HubSpot), data warehouses (Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift), and spreadsheets. Vareto is SOC 2 Type 2 attested with a public Drata trust center, but does not currently publish a public developer API surface.

providers.name: Velocity Global
providers.description: Velocity Global (now Pebl) is a global employment and Employer of Record (EOR) platform with REST APIs for international hiring, managing employee records, payroll processing, and compliance management across 185+ countries. The platform enables organizations to onboard global employees, process payroll, administer benefits, and maintain local labor law compliance without establishing local entities.

providers.name: Voxer
providers.description: Voxer is a San Francisco push-to-talk (PTT) communication company whose walkie-talkie app combines live voice, voice messaging, text, photos, video, and location sharing across iPhone, Android, and the web. Voxer Business provides secure private PTT networks for frontline teams in hospitality, transportation, field services, construction, and logistics, and Voxer Pro + AI adds AI message summaries. Voxer publishes no public REST API; its developer surface is a gated early-access mobile SDK (Android/iOS, with public API reference docs on GitHub) plus a Zapier integration. Backed by IVP.

providers.name: 艾赋 AIFU
providers.description: 艾赋 AIFU 提供基于私有化部署的 AI 客服解决方案，帮助企业在 10 分钟内构建能够使用自有产品资料和话术的智能客服。用户可将产品手册、FAQ、历史客服话术导入系统，AI 即可自动回答常见咨询，并在无法回答时转接人工。服务无需收集联系方式或信用卡信息，支持免费试用，数据完全留在企业内部，确保信息安全。通过简单的代码嵌入，可快速集成至官网、公众号或微信平台，实现高效、可靠的客户交互。

providers.name: Alium
providers.description: Alium provides a platform where brands can access in‑depth, AI‑synthesized interviews with technology vendors. The service gathers compensated research from over 1,000 brand leaders, delivering actionable insights on vendor performance, risk, and suitability. Alium’s AI analyses these conversations to help marketers, CISOs, and IT directors make data‑driven decisions about technology partners.

providers.name: ALLO
providers.description: ALLO is a visual project workspace for creative teams, offering a unified canvas for briefs, files, feedback, and decisions. It integrates with tools like Figma and Google Drive, enabling teams to collaborate on designs, content, and project planning in one place. The platform provides features such as AI‑assisted studio, canvas basics, project tracking, and secure admin & billing, aiming to streamline creative workflows and reduce re‑work across design, e‑commerce, education, and game studios.

providers.name: AMZ Vault
providers.description: AMZ Vault provides settlement-accurate Amazon profit-and-loss (P&L) reporting and full-funnel PPC management, powered by a native AI connection. The platform offers fee-level drill-down P&L, campaign builder, automation with approval gates, and a flat $49 pricing with no percent-of-spend fees. Users can try the whole platform without signup, access detailed analytics, and manage Amazon advertising efficiently.

providers.name: arcreport-ai
providers.description: ArcReport AI provides a platform that evaluates whether AI agents can successfully navigate e‑commerce checkout flows. By running automated pre‑checks across thousands of online stores, it offers insights into agent capabilities, highlights friction points, and helps developers improve AI‑driven shopping experiences. The service is free, open‑source, and continuously updated with new store data and methodology documentation.

providers.name: Artashippinginc
providers.description: Artashippinginc is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: secondary-market) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.

providers.name: Breef
providers.description: Breef is an online agency marketplace and payments platform that connects brands with vetted marketing, creative, digital and web agencies. Founded in New York in 2019 as Curated and rebranded to Breef in 2021, the company is now headquartered in Denver. Brands scope a project on the platform, receive curated pitches from hand-picked agencies across 50+ project types in days rather than months, and then run contracts, milestones and payments through Breef — including Breef(Pay), its agency-now-pay-later payment product. The network spans roughly 25,000 vetted agencies across 27 countries. Breef is a hosted end-user SaaS product: it publishes no public developer program, API reference, SDK or webhook surface.

providers.name: Car Background AI
providers.description: Car Background AI offers an AI‑powered car photo editor that removes or replaces vehicle backgrounds, enhances lighting and detail, and provides bulk processing and dealership branding tools. The service is aimed at car dealers, photographers, private sellers, online marketplaces, and dealer‑management systems that need consistent, marketplace‑ready images at scale.

providers.name: cardmachinepricing-co-uk
providers.description: Card Machine Pricing aggregates the in‑person transaction rates that UK card‑machine providers publish on their own websites. By regularly scraping each provider’s pricing page, the service records the quoted rate together with the date it was read, offering a transparent, up‑to‑date comparison of merchant‑card‑machine costs across the UK market. The data is provided via a public API that returns the provider name, the printed rate, the source URL and the read date, enabling developers to build pricing dashboards, cost‑analysis tools, or integrate the information into fintech applications.

providers.name: colaunched-ai
providers.description: Colaunched is a platform that surfaces business ideas derived from real public demand, scores them for feasibility, timing, market gap, and personal fit, and provides a ninety‑day launch plan with verified first‑revenue milestones. Users can explore ideas, receive detailed scoring, and access AI‑assisted tools such as Claude and ChatGPT to evaluate and execute concepts.

providers.name: Crayon
providers.description: Crayon is a Boston-based competitive intelligence platform that automatically captures, analyzes and distributes competitor activity — website and pricing changes, product updates, social posts, news, reviews, job postings and review-site sentiment — and turns it into battlecards, competitor profiles, win/loss stories, objection handling and email digests for product marketing, sales enablement and go-to-market teams. Crayon AI adds automated summarization, dynamic battlecard updates and the 2026 'Sparks' feature, which reads a competitor's strategic moves and writes them up for revenue teams. On 2026-09-04 Crayon shipped what it describes as the first competitive-intelligence MCP server, a hosted OAuth-protected Model Context Protocol endpoint that exposes a customer's own curated Crayon content to Claude, ChatGPT, Glean, Microsoft Copilot, Google Gemini and internal Slack or Teams assistants. Crayon also markets a Content API and an Answers API, but publishes no developer portal, reference or machine-readable specification for either. NOTE: Crayon (crayon.co) is unrelated to Crayon Group ASA (crayon.com), the Norwegian Microsoft CSP.

providers.name: Cruxinformatics
providers.description: Cruxinformatics, operating under the Cruxdata brand, provides AI‑driven data onboarding, transformation, and monitoring solutions for financial services and other industries. Their platform offers managed services, self‑service tools, and extensive integrations with data providers such as Morningstar, Moody's, and MSCI, enabling clients to ingest, validate, and enrich external data streams in real time.

providers.name: dealerific-com
providers.description: dealerific-com is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: mcp-registry) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.

providers.name: Dynamsoft Web TWAIN
providers.description: Dynamsoft provides SDKs for document capture, barcode reading, and MRZ scanning across web, mobile, and desktop platforms. Their Dynamsoft Web TWAIN product enables developers to integrate scanning and barcode capabilities directly into web applications using JavaScript. The company offers trial licenses, detailed developer documentation, and a range of SDKs for various use cases such as mobile document scanning, barcode reading, and server-side processing.

providers.name: Elephas Biosciences
providers.description: Elephas Biosciences Corporation is a Madison, Wisconsin precision-oncology company that builds elive, a first-in-class functional immune-profiling platform that measures how a patient's own live tumor tissue responds to immunotherapy. The platform combines elive Edge (an automated instrument that cuts core-needle biopsies into uniform 300-micron viable fragments), elive Gel (a proprietary hydrogel that preserves the native tumor microenvironment) and the elive Method (a sequential treatment and cytokine-analysis strategy) to return a functional response readout within roughly 72 hours of biopsy. Clinicians receive elive test reports through a secure, cloud-based web application; researchers and drug developers receive custom reports plus raw data for in-house analysis. The company raised a $40M Series B-2 in November 2025 to commercialize elive as a laboratory developed test. Its digital surface is the Elephas Portal (portal.elephas.com), an Angular single-page application backed by an ASP.NET Core API at portal.elephasapis.com that is authenticated with Azure AD B2C on the company-controlled na.login.elephas.com identity host. No public developer program, API reference or machine-readable contract is published.

providers.name: Emitrr
providers.description: Emitrr provides AI-powered communication tools for healthcare and other businesses, offering services such as texting, webchat, reviews, team messaging, VoIP phones, cloud faxing, AI agents, local numbers, online scheduling, digital forms, and more. Their platform aims to streamline patient engagement, improve operational efficiency, and enable 24/7 virtual assistance across various specialties.

providers.name: Emma
providers.description: Emma provides an email marketing platform that helps businesses design, personalize, segment, and automate targeted email campaigns. The service focuses on delivering measurable results through advanced analytics, A/B testing, and integration with various CRM and e‑commerce tools. Emma’s platform aims to improve customer engagement and drive revenue growth for marketers of all sizes.

providers.name: Flexe
providers.description: Flexe provides on-demand warehousing and logistics infrastructure for the world's leading retailers and brands. Its REST APIs enable integration with a network of 800+ warehouse operators across North America to manage warehouse programs, inventory, fulfillment orders, and supply chain flexibility across distributed fulfillment nodes via a single technology platform supporting API, EDI, and XML integrations.

providers.name: Garden
providers.description: Garden is an open-source Kubernetes-native development and CI/CD platform. Garden Core, a declarative CLI and engine, models a project as a graph of Build, Deploy, Test, and Run actions powered by pluggable providers (kubernetes, local-kubernetes, container, exec, jib, helm, terraform, pulumi). Garden Cloud / Garden Enterprise add a hosted control plane for remote container builds, ephemeral preview environments, team dashboards, team-wide caching, secrets, RBAC, audit, and SSO. The CLI integrates with any CI system and IDE; teams use Garden to standardize how dev, preview, staging, and prod environments are built and deployed.

providers.name: General Dynamics
providers.description: General Dynamics Corporation is a global aerospace and defense company headquartered in Reston, Virginia. The company operates across five business segments: Aerospace, Marine Systems, Combat Systems, Technologies, and Mission Systems, providing business aviation, ship construction, land combat vehicles, weapons systems, and technology products and services.

providers.name: Handoff
providers.description: Handoff is an AI-native construction management and estimating platform built for residential contractors — remodelers, home builders, handymen, and trade contractors. It handles estimating, AI takeoffs, proposals, project management, scheduling, CRM, change orders, invoicing, and financial management end-to-end, generating detailed, localized estimates in seconds from descriptions, photos, drawings, or voice. Built by 1build and backed by Initialized Capital, Greycroft, Y Combinator, and Masco Ventures, Handoff serves 10,000+ monthly active users managing billions in annualized residential construction projects. Handoff does not currently expose a public developer API; it offers a Zapier integration for connected workflows, with an API on its public roadmap.

providers.name: Kivra
providers.description: Kivra provides a digital mailbox service for individuals and businesses in Sweden, allowing users to receive, store, and manage electronic mail, invoices, and official documents securely. The platform aims to reduce paper usage and streamline communication between citizens, companies, and public authorities, offering features such as digital receipts, payment handling, and identity verification through Kivra ID.

providers.name: Kyash
providers.description: Kyash Inc. (株式会社Kyash) is a Tokyo-based fintech founded in 2015 that operates a consumer mobile wallet and Visa prepaid card in Japan, covering charging, peer-to-peer transfers, shared accounts, buy-now-pay-later, personal finance management, and contactless payment through Apple Pay, Google Pay, and Samsung Pay. Kyash is a registered Funds Transfer Service Provider (Kanto Local Finance Bureau No. 00082) and a third-party Prepaid Payment Instrument Issuer (No. 00698), and is ISO/IEC 27001:2022, PCI DSS, and TRUSTe certified. Its business-facing product is Kyash Payout, a mass payout service that sends funds to Japanese domestic bank accounts or Kyash wallets at a flat 50 yen per transfer, integrated either by Zengin/CSV file upload or by direct API integration including a balance API. Kyash previously sold Kyash Direct, an API-based Visa card issuer processing platform launched in 2019. All API access is sales-gated: Kyash publishes no developer portal, API reference, specification, SDK, or sandbox.

providers.name: Labayh
providers.description: Labayh (لبيه) is a Saudi Arabian digital mental-health platform delivering online psychological, psychiatric and family counselling to the Arabic-speaking Gulf market. Patients book scheduled or instant video and audio sessions with more than 1,000 licensed specialists, and can also enrol in structured therapeutic programs for depression, anxiety, OCD and social phobia, join peer support groups, take psychological assessments, track mood daily, and watch live and recorded webinars. The company reports over 70 million minutes of consultation delivered. Alongside the consumer app it runs Labayh Business, a corporate employee-wellbeing arm, and Labayh Academy, a training platform for practitioners. Labayh is backed by 500 Global. It operates no developer program and publishes no OpenAPI, SDKs or developer portal; the API catalogued here is the anonymously readable WordPress REST surface behind labayh.net, whose OpenAPI description API Evangelist derived from the server's own discovery document.

providers.name: Levelpath
providers.description: Levelpath is an AI-native procurement platform that unifies intake and orchestration, strategic sourcing, contract lifecycle management, supplier management, third-party risk management, invoice automation, and category pipeline reporting into a single enterprise system. The product is built around AI agents that run sourcing events and generate RFPs, scan contract repositories to answer questions and flag risk, monitor supplier compliance signals, and process invoices. Levelpath is a closed enterprise platform: it operates customer and supplier applications at app.levelpath.com and supplierhub.levelpath.com, and its status page confirms a production APIs component, but it publishes no public developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI definition, or SDKs. Integrations with SAP, Ariba, Coupa, Oracle, NetSuite, Docusign, Ironclad, OneTrust, Slack, and Microsoft Teams are delivered through the platform rather than a documented public API. Backed by Battery Ventures, Menlo Ventures, and Redpoint Ventures.

providers.name: Looking Glass Factory
providers.description: Looking Glass Factory builds group-viewable 3D holographic (light field) displays that require no headset — the Looking Glass Go, Portrait, and the 16", 27", 32", 65" and 86" Light Field and Hololuminescent displays.
