providers.name: VXT
providers.description: VXT provides AI-powered call and meeting note automation for law firms, turning conversations into structured legal paperwork, call recordings, time tracking, and email drafts. Integrated with major legal software, it aims to recover extra billable minutes and streamline workflow for lawyers.

providers.name: 0DTE Confluence
providers.description: 0DTE Confluence provides live 0‑day‑to‑expiration (0DTE) options dealer walls, classified flow, and graded A+/B setups with invalidation for major equity indices such as SPY, QQQ, IWM, SMH, and GLD. The platform offers a Decision Desk that displays live dealer walls, expected‑move bands, and a tape of market activity, along with quantitative tools like the Confluence Tape, GEX map, and exposure metrics. Users can subscribe to Desk Bundle ($159/mo) or Pro MCP ($199/mo) for advanced alerts, quant tools, and session updates. Educational guides are available in the Learn Hub, covering what 0DTE means, how the Decision Desk works, and how to interpret graded alerts. The service is advisory‑only; customers place their own orders.

providers.name: Abcuro
providers.description: Abcuro is a clinical-stage biotechnology company headquartered in Newton, Massachusetts, developing first-in-class immunotherapies that precisely modulate highly cytotoxic T cells for autoimmune disease and cancer. Its lead candidate, ulviprubart (ABC008), is a monoclonal antibody targeting KLRG1 that selectively depletes highly cytotoxic T cells, evaluated in the registrational Phase 2/3 MUSCLE study in inclusion body myositis (IBM) and in T cell large granular lymphocytic leukemia (T-LGLL) and mature T and NK cell lymphomas. Abcuro publishes no commercial developer platform or product API; its only machine-readable surface is the public WordPress REST API behind abcuro.com, which anonymously serves the corporate content graph — press releases, pipeline and science pages, scientific publications, leadership and board people records, investor records, and media assets — and is catalogued here as a read-only content API rather than a product API.

providers.name: Agari
providers.description: Agari is an email-security provider that pioneered and helped author the DMARC email-authentication standard to protect organizations from phishing, business email compromise (BEC), email spoofing, and brand impersonation. Founded in 2009, Agari was acquired by HelpSystems (now Fortra) in May 2021 and is delivered as Fortra's email-security portfolio, including DMARC Protection / Brand Protection, Phishing Defense, and Phishing Response. The Agari Platform exposes a RESTful JSON API secured with OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials for retrieving security telemetry, auditing users and domains, tracking DMARC policy enforcement, and integrating Agari data into SIEM and SOAR tooling. It was originally backed by Norwest Venture Partners and other venture investors before its acquisition.

providers.name: Alchemer
providers.description: Enterprise survey and experience management platform with a REST API for managing surveys, accessing response data, managing contacts, and automating survey workflows. The Alchemer REST API v5 supports multi-region deployments across US, EU, Canada, and Australia, with API key and OAuth 1.0 authentication. API access is available exclusively on Business Platform accounts.

providers.name: Analytics Legends
providers.description: Analytics Legends provides an AI‑driven platform for SAP analytics experts, delivering verified missions, market signals, and learning assets in a daily workflow. The service aggregates SAP analytics postings, offers a curated knowledge base, and supports consultants with benchmarks, directories, and freelance opportunities, all without affiliation to SAP.

providers.name: Arclo
providers.description: Arclo builds and manages your website, improves your SEO, and tracks your search performance. Powered by 15 AI specialists. No contracts. You own the code. It offers website and technical SEO, content, search and competition, authority, serving local businesses, shops, studios, health and wellness practices.

providers.name: Arvow
providers.description: Arvow provides AI-powered SEO tools that automate content creation, backlink building, and search ranking optimization. Their platform offers AI article writers, SEO editors, news generators, video‑to‑blog conversion, automated backlink exchange, and visibility trackers for various AI models. Targeted at marketers and agencies, Arvow promises to boost organic traffic without manual effort, integrating with popular website builders and offering white‑label solutions for agencies.

providers.name: Authentic8
providers.description: Authentic8 is a cybersecurity company best known for Silo, a cloud-based secure browser and digital investigations platform. Silo isolates web activity in the cloud so analysts, investigators, and enterprise users can browse the surface, deep, and dark web anonymously with managed attribution, region masking, and full audit and governance controls. The company serves intelligence, law enforcement, financial crime, fraud, and corporate security teams, and delivers its service as a FedRAMP-authorized SaaS with SOC 2, ISO 27001/27701, PCI DSS, HIPAA, and GDPR compliance. Authentic8 is backed by Foundry Group and does not currently publish a public developer API. This profile tracks the company in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Bizzabo
providers.description: Bizzabo is a B2B event experience platform with REST APIs for managing conferences, speakers, ticketing, attendee data, and event analytics and performance metrics. The open API enables developers to build custom integrations, automate event workflows, synchronize attendee data with CRM and marketing platforms, and deliver personalized event experiences at scale.

providers.name: Bloomberg Products and Platforms
providers.description: Bloomberg Products and Platforms covers the breadth of Bloomberg's integrated offerings spanning the Bloomberg Terminal, Enterprise data products, API platforms, trading systems, analytics, messaging, media, and government intelligence solutions. Bloomberg serves financial professionals with an interconnected ecosystem of products and platforms for data, analytics, and communication.

providers.name: BMW
providers.description: BMW is a German multinational company specializing in manufacturing luxury vehicles and motorcycles. BMW provides automotive data APIs through the Aftersales Online System (AOS) portal and the BMW Open Data Platform, enabling dealers, repair shops, and developers to access vehicle identification, maintenance, technical campaign, pricing, and diagnostic data.

providers.name: Boon
providers.description: Boon is an agile referral hiring platform that helps organizations source talent through employee, vendor, customer, and external referral networks. Using AI-driven semantic matching and proactive referral requests, Boon surfaces hidden candidates, manages reward and gamification programs, and syncs with existing HR/ATS tech stacks (Workday, Greenhouse, Lever, iCIMS, Ashby, JazzHR, Slack, Teams, and 50+ others). Founded in 2014 and backed by 500 Global and Redpoint Ventures, Boon markets faster time-to-hire and lower cost-per-hire through community-driven recruiting. This profile was seeded from VC portfolio data and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Boon exposes a private integration API (api.goboon.co) but publishes no public OpenAPI or developer portal.

providers.name: BridgeStackAPI
providers.description: BridgeStackAPI provides a lightweight API gateway that enables per‑client usage control, rate‑limiting, and custom routing without rebuilding the gateway. It offers dashboards, real‑time logs, and integration guides for Node.js, cURL, and Python, helping developers quickly enforce policies and monitor API consumption.

providers.name: BuddyLists
providers.description: BuddyLists is an independent AI agent pilot platform that enables users to join without email or account. It offers a free pilot where agents can connect, communicate, and conduct escrowed contracts. The service provides tools, a job board, chat rooms, and a Corkboard for evidence submission. Founded by a human in Massachusetts, USA, BuddyLists operates as a zero‑person company where agents run the system. Documentation, API specs, and policies are publicly available.

providers.name: Buggazi
providers.description: Buggazi provides a PM tool that lets coding agents run their own sprints, plan features, track bugs, and collaborate in real-time via agent channels and DMs. It offers integrated bug tracking, feature planning, and sprint management, positioned as a simple Git‑like experience for teams, with pricing starting at $30 per month.

providers.name: Build My Digital
providers.description: Build My Digital provides hand‑coded websites for local home‑improvement firms and private clinics, offering a pay‑per‑booking model where they are only paid when bookings come in. They manage Google ads, business profiles, missed‑call handling, quote chasing and review requests, ensuring high‑ticket jobs are booked efficiently.

providers.name: Can I Vibe
providers.description: Can I Vibe provides a live availability monitoring service for AI coding providers. It aggregates status information from 22 providers, offering a free JSON API, CI gate, and instant webhooks. Users can embed status badges in README files and receive alerts when providers experience issues. The platform aims to improve reliability of AI development pipelines by making provider outages visible and actionable.

providers.name: CardinalOps
providers.description: CardinalOps is a cybersecurity company delivering agentic detection engineering for security operations centers (SOCs). Its Threat Coverage Optimization Platform continuously assesses detection posture across SIEM and EDR tools (Splunk, Microsoft Sentinel, CrowdStrike, SentinelOne, Cortex, Elastic and others), maps existing detections to the MITRE ATT&CK framework, surfaces coverage gaps, and automatically remediates broken or noisy rules. The Agentic Fleet and Cardinal AI use large language models to extract atomic TTPs from threat intelligence and generate new, validated detection rules. CardinalOps is backed by Battery Ventures and serves enterprise SOC teams. It publishes no public developer API; this profile captures the company's public developer-adjacent, security, and compliance surface.

providers.name: CircuitHub
providers.description: CircuitHub is an on-demand electronics manufacturing platform that provides rapid, low-cost turnkey PCB (printed circuit board) assembly for hardware and robotics teams. Engineers upload their CAD and BOM files (Altium, EAGLE, KiCAD) to an automated web application that reconciles the bill of materials against 35,000+ stocked common parts, generates an instant quote, previews a virtual build, and manufactures small prototype-to-production batches in the USA — with 81% of full turnkey orders shipping within three days and real-time quality metrics for transparency. CircuitHub has delivered over 1.5 million boards and placed 87 million parts for more than 20,000 engineers. The company operates a web application rather than a public developer API; user authentication is handled through an Auth0-hosted OpenID Connect tenant.

providers.name: Collective Health
providers.description: Collective Health is an independent third-party administrator (TPA) for self-funded employer health benefits, combining plan administration, claims adjudication, payments, care navigation, and member advocacy into a single connected benefits experience. Its Collective TPA platform, member app (My Collective), Benefits Hub partner ecosystem, and Collective AI tools serve employers, benefits leaders, brokers, consultants, and members. The company integrates with network and digital point-solution partners via enrollment file sharing, outbound claims data feeds, and payments, and is HITRUST r2 and SOC 2 Type II certified. It currently publishes no public developer API program; this profile tracks its identity, trust, and security posture in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Comulate
providers.description: Comulate is an accounting automation and revenue intelligence platform built for large insurance brokers. It captures carrier statement data across spreadsheets, PDFs, and email, then automatically reconciles direct-bill and carrier-payables transactions against policies to eliminate manual back-office accounting work. Its Revenue Intelligence layer adds commission forecasting, variance tracking, and missing-commission detection. Comulate is delivered as a hosted application at app.comulate.com with native connectors to broker management systems including Epic, BenefitPoint, AMS360, Microsoft Dynamics, and Salesforce. The company was surfaced as a Bond Capital portfolio company and enriched in the API Evangelist network; it publishes no public developer API or documentation as of this profile.

providers.name: CSC Generation
providers.description: CSC Generation is an AI-native retail holding company that acquires overlooked store- and catalogue-based retailers and rebuilds them on Genesis, its agent-orchestrated operating platform. Genesis combines a Data Fabric — a Data Management Platform that ingests and normalizes data across every brand without replatforming, and a Data Intelligence Platform that turns it into decision-ready signals for operators and AI agents — with an automation engine, proprietary retail AI tools, and centralized shared services covering customer experience, supply chain, technology and compliance. The company powers 13 brands and more than $1B in revenue, including Backcountry, Competitive Cyclist, Steep & Cheap, MotoSport, BikeTiresDirect, Level Nine Sports, Sur La Table, One Kings Lane, Seattle Coffee Gear and Home Consignment Center, and operates from Chicago, Austin, Los Angeles, Toronto, Seattle and Salt Lake City. CSC Generation publishes no corporate developer API; its machine-readable surface is per-brand — portfolio storefronts advertise Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) merchant profiles at /.well-known/ucp that point agents at MCP endpoints for catalog search, cart and checkout.

providers.name: Danse Ici
providers.description: Danse Ici is a Paris‑based platform that aggregates and promotes dance events, classes, workshops and social dancing opportunities across the city. It provides a searchable calendar of salsa, bachata, kizomba and other Latin dance activities, offering details on venues, times, prices and instructors, helping dancers discover where to practice and enjoy dance in Paris.

providers.name: DaVita
providers.description: DaVita Inc. is a Fortune 500 kidney care company operating in-center hemodialysis, home hemodialysis, and peritoneal dialysis programs in the United States and abroad, alongside transplant support, integrated kidney care, hospital partnerships, and clinical research. DaVita runs no developer program and publishes no API documentation, but its own web platform serves a live, public, unauthenticated REST API at https://www.davita.com/wp-json/ with a first-party davita/v1 namespace: a dialysis center locator, a Kidney Smart class finder, a USDA-sourced food and nutrient lookup shaped for the kidney diet, and 1,258 kidney-friendly recipes, 570 education articles and a kidney vocabulary alongside them. Clinical integration remains sales-led through payer, hospital and physician partnerships and EHR data exchange; there is no public FHIR endpoint.

providers.name: disclosedby
providers.description: disclosedby provides a searchable archive of subprocessor lists for over 450 companies, preserving each version with dates to enable verification of data handling changes. The service tracks entries, companies, and changes, offering a paid watch feature for continuous monitoring. Updated through November 2026, it aims to improve transparency in vendor data processing.

providers.name: DODO
providers.description: DODO is a decentralized exchange (DEX) and on-chain liquidity provider built on the Proactive Market Maker (PMM) algorithm, engineered for capital-efficient liquidity and low slippage across many EVM blockchains. Its Trade / Route API aggregates prices across DODO v1/v2, 1inch, 0x, ParaSwap, professional market makers, and DODO's own aggregation algorithm, returning real-time swap quotes plus executable ABI calldata that developers send directly to the DODORouteProxy / DODOV2Proxy contracts. DODO is backed by Pantera Capital and ships open-source smart contracts, JavaScript/TypeScript SDKs, a contract request library, and embeddable swap widgets.

providers.name: DVC
providers.description: DVC (Data Version Control) is an Apache 2.0 open-source CLI and Python library for versioning datasets, models, pipelines, and ML experiments on top of Git. It is not a network service — there is no DVC REST API.

providers.name: Elegen
providers.description: Elegen is a synthetic biology company founded in 2017 and headquartered in Menlo Park, California that manufactures high-accuracy synthetic DNA through its proprietary cell-free ENFINIA platform. Rather than relying on traditional cell-based cloning, ENFINIA combines microfluidics, artificial intelligence, and robotics to produce long, clonal-quality, high-complexity DNA at speed and low cost. The ENFINIA product line includes Linear DNA up to 7 kb delivered in 6-8 business days, Plasmid DNA up to 15 kb, and IVT Ready DNA with encoded poly(A) tails for mRNA workflows, each NGS-verified to 99.999% per-base accuracy. Elegen serves researchers and therapeutics developers across mRNA vaccines, cell and gene therapy, CRISPR genome editing, and protein expression. Customers submit and order sequences through the online ENFINIA ordering portal; Elegen does not currently publish a public developer API. The company is backed by a16z Bio + Health, KdT Ventures, 8VC, Digitalis Ventures, Agilent, and others, and raised a $35M Series B in 2024.

providers.name: everlane
providers.description: Everlane is a San Francisco-based direct-to-consumer apparel and footwear brand known for its "Radical Transparency" model — publishing factory sourcing, true costs, and markups on everyday wardrobe essentials. As an API Evangelist network entry, Everlane has no bespoke public developer program; its online store runs on Shopify and exposes an agent-facing commerce surface: a live Storefront MCP server at everlane.com/api/mcp (product search, cart, product details, and policy/FAQ lookup), a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) profile at /.well-known/ucp, a published /llms.txt of agent instructions, and Shopify Customer Account OIDC/OAuth2 authentication. Surfaced as a Slow Ventures portfolio company and enriched from its public agent, well-known, and authentication surfaces.

providers.name: Faraway
providers.description: Faraway is a web3 gaming company building an interoperable gaming ecosystem for players, creators, and studios. Its platform lets game studios integrate player-driven, blockchain-based economies into their titles across EVM-compatible chains and Solana, with a unified player identity and wallet (id.faraway.com), a creator platform for user-generated content and monetization (create.faraway.com), and an in-game marketplace and secondary-trading shop (shop.faraway.com). Faraway publishes a developer platform with an API reference and an llms.txt index at docs.faraway.com. The company is backed by a16z, Lightspeed Venture Partners, and Pantera Capital.

providers.name: Flashpoint
providers.description: Flashpoint is a threat intelligence company delivering decisive intelligence for cybersecurity, fraud prevention, corporate and physical security, vulnerability management, insider threat, and national security teams. Its Ignite platform and Flashpoint API surface data collected from illicit online communities, the deep and dark web, chat services, and open sources — exposing threat actors, compromised credentials, vulnerabilities, and fraud indicators. Flashpoint makes this finished intelligence and raw data available programmatically through a REST API at api.flashpoint.io, documented at docs.flashpoint.io, so security teams can integrate alerting, data feeds, and finished intelligence into SOC, SIEM, and security automation workflows.

providers.name: Flow
providers.description: Flow (Flow Engineering, operated by TRC Space Ltd) is a requirements-management platform built for hardware and systems engineering teams. It centers on a Systems Graph that connects requirements, design artifacts, tests, and components, with AI agents that continuously align CAD, simulation, code, and test — automating impact analysis, budget tracking, and compliance checking. Flow supports branching and merging of requirement baselines, iterative build gates, and an integration ecosystem spanning CAD (Onshape, Fusion 360, Siemens NX), simulation (Ansys), and dev tools (GitHub, GitLab, Jira, Linear, Slack, Notion, Confluence). It is SOC 2 Type II, NIST 800-171, and ITAR/EAR aligned with self-hosted and AWS GovCloud options. A first-party API exists (referenced in the changelog) but is gated behind login with no publicly published OpenAPI or developer documentation.

providers.name: Flower Shop Network
providers.description: Flower Shop Network is a platform that connects customers with local florists across the country. They provide an online marketplace where users can browse and purchase a wide variety of floral arrangements for all occasions, and expose a JSON API for partner POS systems to authenticate, look up products and florists, and exchange wire orders across the FSN florist network.

providers.name: freetoken-link
providers.description: FreeToken.link provides a platform for discovering and testing free-access Large Language Model (LLM) APIs. It aggregates model information, key testing guides, and tool setup instructions across multiple providers such as NVIDIA, Google Gemini, Groq, and SiliconFlow. Users can compare models, obtain API keys, and run browser‑direct requests to evaluate free‑tier limits and compliance. The site also offers documentation, pricing details, and a community‑driven watchlist for monitoring changes in model availability and access policies.

providers.name: Gotenberg
providers.description: Gotenberg provides a Docker-based API for converting documents to PDF and other formats. It offers a simple HTTP interface where users can POST files like HTML, Markdown, or Office documents and receive a generated PDF. The service runs as a container, making it easy to self‑host, and supports features such as merging PDFs, adding headers/footers, and applying custom CSS. Documentation, examples, and a quick‑start guide are available on its website.

providers.name: HELP
providers.description: This profile was surfaced as a portfolio-linked lead of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. The website pointer on this record resolves to Venturz (operated by GoVenturz, LLC), an all-in-one business operating system for founders that bundles 15+ tools — website builder, CRM, email marketing, payments, and analytics — behind a single dashboard alongside an "AI co-founder" assistant, a founder community, a startup academy, and Venturz Capital funding. As of this enrichment pass Venturz publishes no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDKs, or /.well-known discovery surface, so no machine-readable API artifacts could be harvested. See x-identity-note regarding the stub name versus the linked brand.

providers.name: Intellectible
providers.description: Intellectible is an AI build platform for enterprise service providers - federal and state government contractors (GovCon), professional services firms, and economic development organizations - that turns portals, emails, CRM data, and market signals into structured opportunity, proposal, pricing, and knowledge workflows. Its horizontal build environment (project workspaces, visual workflows, document libraries, PostgreSQL databases, applications, pages, jobs, and queues) is exposed programmatically through the Intellectible Public API and a Code Execution SDK, letting teams run workflows synchronously, manage Library files, and query project databases directly from code.

providers.name: Juli
providers.description: Juli is a US-based (Hull, Massachusetts) digital-health company building an AI-powered mobile platform that helps people manage complex, hard-to-treat chronic conditions — including asthma, migraine, depression, and bipolar disorder. The app combines patient-reported symptoms, wearable and phone sensor data, and environmental context (weather, air quality, pollen) to surface the micro-behavioral triggers that worsen or improve a person's condition, then nudges small, sustainable changes through daily check-ins, reminders, and gamified "daily dares." Juli's efficacy has been evaluated in two randomized controlled trials (asthma and depression), published in JMIR and a SAGE journal, and the company reports retention far above consumer-health norms. Founded by Bettina Duehrkoop, Juli raised a $3.8M seed round in March 2022 co-led by Speedinvest and Norrsken VC. It serves consumers directly plus provider, employer, education (juli.education), pharma, and research (juli.science) channels. Juli is a consumer/clinical app with a HIPAA / SOC 2 / GDPR compliance posture; it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Kaizo
providers.description: Kaizo is an AI-powered quality assurance, coaching, and performance management platform for customer support teams working in Zendesk and Salesforce. Its AutoQA engine automatically scores 100% of support conversations in real time, analyzing sentiment and empathy, generating conversation summaries, surfacing escalation risks, and turning support data into performance insights. AI coaching builds data-driven improvement roadmaps for agents, while dashboards and reporting help support leaders compare team and individual outcomes. Kaizo delivers its product primarily as native apps for the Zendesk Marketplace and Salesforce AppExchange rather than as a public developer API. The company is SOC 2 certified, ISO 27001 certified, GDPR compliant, and continuously monitored by Secureframe. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Partech and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: Lano
providers.description: Lano provides a global payroll consolidation and Employer of Record (EOR) platform, enabling companies to hire, pay, and manage employees and contractors across 170+ countries. Their solution includes payroll, compliance, benefits, and payments, with integrations to popular tools. Lano’s API allows developers to automate workforce management, retrieve payroll data, and integrate hiring workflows into their own systems.

providers.name: Meadow
providers.description: Meadow provides a comprehensive cannabis point‑of‑sale (POS) and e‑commerce platform for dispensaries across the United States. Founded in 2014, Meadow offers integrated inventory management, compliance reporting, delivery logistics, and retail analytics, helping cannabis retailers streamline operations and scale across multiple states. The platform supports integrations with major partners and delivers a unified dashboard for sales, compliance, and customer engagement.

providers.name: Medallion
providers.description: Medallion is an AI-powered healthcare operations platform for provider credentialing, enrollment, and licensing, operated by FirstLayerAI, Inc. It positions itself as the AI operations partner powering healthcare's first real-time CVO (Credentialing Verification Organization), NCQA-certified, and serves provider groups, payers, health systems, RCM organizations, and digital health companies. Capabilities span provider data management, delegated credentialing, roster management, privileging, cross-state licensing, ongoing credential monitoring, and CredAlliance, its proprietary payer clearinghouse. Medallion is SOC 2 compliant and publishes a Trust Center. As of this profile there is no public developer API surface; enrichment captured the company's identity, compliance posture, and domain security.

providers.name: mobcrm-au
providers.description: Mob is a personal customer relationship management (CRM) platform that helps users capture and organize information about the people in their lives—notes, reminders, birthdays, and relationships—using natural language input. It includes native MCP (Mobile Cloud Platform) support, allowing seamless integration with mobile devices. The service offers documentation, pricing plans, and open‑source code on GitHub, providing a comprehensive tool for personal productivity and contact management.

providers.name: Next Matter
providers.description: Next Matter is a technology company that provides a platform for managing and automating complex workflows across various industries. Their solutions enable businesses to integrate disparate systems, orchestrate processes, and gain real-time insights through a unified interface. Backed by Crane Venture Partners, Next Matter focuses on delivering scalable, secure, and customizable automation tools that help enterprises improve efficiency, reduce manual effort, and accelerate digital transformation initiatives.

providers.name: pangolinfo-com
providers.description: Pangolinfo provides structured Amazon and search engine data through APIs, MCP servers, and AI skills. It helps developers, e-commerce teams, and AI agents access product, review, seller, category, and search result data for market research, competitive analysis, and workflow automation.

providers.name: Perfect Day
providers.description: Perfect Day is a Berkeley, California food-technology company, founded in 2014, that makes animal-free dairy proteins with precision fermentation. Rather than farming cows, Perfect Day ferments microflora carrying milk's protein-coding genes to produce ProFerm, a non-animal whey protein with no lactose, cholesterol, hormones or antibiotics, which it sells business-to-business to consumer brands making ice cream, cream cheese, milk, yogurt, protein powders and bakery products. The company is a member of the Precision Fermentation Alliance. Perfect Day publishes no product or developer API; the single machine-readable surface it operates is the WordPress REST API (wp/v2) behind perfectday.com, which exposes anonymous read access to its blog posts, newsroom items, success stories, pages, media, taxonomies and site search, plus authenticated write operations via WordPress application passwords. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline from that live surface.

providers.name: Postmates
providers.description: Postmates was an on-demand delivery platform founded in 2011 that pioneered urban courier-style delivery of food, groceries, alcohol, and convenience goods across the United States. Uber acquired Postmates in December 2020 for approximately $2.65 billion, and by 2023 the Postmates merchant, courier, and consumer experiences were fully absorbed into the Uber Eats and Uber Direct product lines. The historical Postmates Fleet API (courier dispatch) and Postmates Customer API (anonymous delivery) have been retired and replaced by Uber Direct as the supported on-demand delivery API surface. The Postmates consumer brand still operates as a front door that funnels orders into the Uber Eats marketplace. This profile is maintained as a historical record and redirect pointer to the successor Uber developer APIs.

providers.name: Prized
providers.description: Prized is an AI-powered platform that lets non-technical operations, support, and finance teams build, deploy, and share secure internal tools without engineering. Users describe a workflow in natural language (or bring their own coding agent such as Claude Code) and Prized builds real software on company data that is pre-connected and scoped, with least-privilege database access per tool, credential isolation, outbound-traffic proxying, and an audit trail on every access. Tools deploy behind corporate authentication and connect to 20+ services including Salesforce, Postgres, Slack, Stripe, and Notion. Prized is a Y Combinator (Summer 2026) company founded by Hudson Griffith and Marinos Eliades, both formerly of Gander (YC F24, acquired by Archer Aviation). Added to the API Evangelist network via the VC-portfolio pipeline and enriched from the company's public web surface.

providers.name: Qatar University
providers.description: Qatar University is the national public research university of the State of Qatar, in Doha, founded 1973 and registered as https://ror.org/00yhnba62. Its institution-operated programmable footprint is small, real, and not where the June 2026 profile said it was. That pass recorded QSpace — the institutional repository at qspace.qu.edu.qa — as Qatar University's own API. It is not: qspace.qu.edu.qa CNAMEs to qataru.cname.openrepository.com and terminates on Amazon eu-west-1, making it a tenant of Open Repository, a commercial hosted-DSpace service. The 66,950 records, the Handle prefix 10576 and the administrative contact are Qatar University's; the DSpace REST and OAI-PMH contracts are the hosting platform's engineering, and they are recorded here as a tenancy rather than saved as Qatar University's contracts. What the earlier pass missed is the part Qatar University actually runs. It operates its own identity provider at sso.qu.edu.qa — a WSO2 Identity Server on QUNET, its own RIPE allocation — publishing both a SAML 2.0 IdP metadata document and a complete OpenID Connect discovery document, which together are the strongest machine-readable contract in this profile. Qatar University Press self-hosts Open Journal Systems 3.3.0.7 at journals.qu.edu.qa, also on QUNET, serving an anonymous OAI-PMH 2.0 endpoint over eight journals and 3,186 records in Arabic and English, and registers DOIs as Crossref member 11655 under prefix 10.29117. Learning is a Blackboard Learn tenant and library guides are a Springshare tenant. There is no developer portal, no changelog, no status page, no API terms of service, and no published OpenAPI for anything — and there is an institutional API gateway at api.qu.edu.qa that fronts a live production API pool while publishing no route, documentation or access path whatsoever. Three verified defects sit on the surfaces Qatar University does run: sso.qu.edu.qa and journals.qu.edu.qa both serve an incomplete TLS chain that a default client cannot verify, the SAML entityID is a bare hostname rather than a URI so the IdP cannot be federated as published, and the OAI-PMH endpoint emits record identifiers that its own GetRecord verb rejects.

providers.name: RE/MAX
providers.description: RE/MAX Holdings, Inc. (NYSE: RMAX, SIC 6531, Denver, Colorado) is one of the world's largest real estate brokerage franchisors, licensing the RE/MAX brand to independently owned and operated brokerages across more than 110 countries and territories, and franchising mortgage brokerages in the United States under the Motto Mortgage brand with loan processing through wemlo. Its home market is the United States, where it sits in the value chain as a franchisor and consumer portal operator rather than as a data owner: the listing content behind remax.com is licensed from roughly 500 local Multiple Listing Services under IDX and syndication agreements, so RE/MAX is a consumer of MLS data, not a publisher of it. Its API posture reflects that position honestly. RE/MAX is a RESO Class D member (Brokers, Agents and Appraisers) and holds a seat on the RESO Board of Directors, but it does not appear in the RESO certification directory of certified data providers and publishes no RESO Web API, no OData $metadata document and no Universal Property Identifier surface. In the United States there is no developer portal, no published API program and no machine-readable contract of any kind; developer.remax.com, developers.remax.com and docs.remax.com are only wildcard DNS entries pointing at the kvCORE agent website platform, and api.remax.com is a dangling CNAME to a decommissioned booj host that no longer resolves. The only real, publicly documented RE/MAX API surface belongs to RE/MAX Europe, whose Datahub franchise-operations API and Listings API are published as public Postman documentation with OAuth 2.0 authentication, but whose credentials are issued only to RE/MAX regional master franchisees, offices and their vendors — documented, but not self-serve. The only anonymously callable, self-describing RE/MAX endpoint family found anywhere in the estate is the WordPress REST API on the RE/MAX Europe marketing site (remax.eu/wp-json, 42 namespaces and 791 routes), which also exposes an auth-gated Model Context Protocol endpoint via the WordPress MCP Adapter — a CMS surface rather than an API product, but the closest thing to agent-accessible RE/MAX infrastructure that exists today.

providers.name: ReadySet
providers.description: Readyset is a realtime SQL caching engine for Postgres and MySQL. It sits between applications and the database as a wire-compatible proxy, automatically caching the results of costly SELECT queries and keeping them up to date from the database replication stream with no application code changes or manual invalidation. Written in Rust and available as open source (BSL 1.1), a self-managed Private deployment, and a fully managed Readyset Cloud offering on AWS, it also ships Readyset AI — an MCP server plus the rdst diagnostics CLI — so AI assistants and developers can inspect caches, analyze slow queries, and deploy caches directly. Backed by Amplify Partners and Index Ventures.

providers.name: restor3d
providers.description: restor3d is a Durham, North Carolina medical device manufacturer, founded in 2017 as a Duke University spinout, that designs and 3D-prints personalized musculoskeletal implants and the single-use instrumentation that goes with them. The company unites additive manufacturing of osseointegrative titanium and cobalt-chrome lattices, biomechanics research, and AI-driven planning and design-automation software to produce patient-matched total ankle, total knee, total hip and shoulder reconstruction systems, plus foot-and-ankle and spine fixation devices. Manufacturing and design are vertically integrated in-house, and the company sponsors device performance research at Duke. restor3d is a regulated device maker rather than a software vendor - it publishes no developer portal, no product or clinical API, no SDKs and no public OpenAPI. The only machine-readable surface it serves is its own corporate WordPress site, which exposes the standard WordPress REST API and an OAuth-protected Model Context Protocol endpoint over site content.

providers.name: Scimar
providers.description: Scimar (Scimar Ltd., formerly styled SciMar) is a privately held Canadian life-sciences company founded in 2009 with its head office in Dauphin, Manitoba and research laboratories in Winnipeg. It commercializes the work of co-founder and Chief Scientific Officer Dr. W. Wayne Lautt, who in 1996 identified hepatalin — known in the literature as hepatic insulin-sensitizing substance, or HISS — a liver hormone Scimar describes as the missing link in nutrient partitioning, prediabetes and type 2 diabetes. Its pipeline pairs diagnostics with therapeutics: SciMar NuPa Test, a diagnostic test meal that measures hepatalin production and is in Phase 2 clinical trials in Canada; SciMar NuPa Renew, a pre-meal pharmaceutical preparing for Phase 2B; SciMar NuPa Daily, an antioxidant supplement intended to protect hepatalin production; and Hepatalin-S, a synthetic hepatalin for advanced-stage disease. Alongside the science the company runs the Wellness Transformation Network, a community outreach program with nonprofits, Indigenous communities and Manitoba businesses, and produces the Webby-nominated science podcast Inside the Breakthrough hosted by Dan Riskin. Scimar publishes no product or developer API and operates no developer program. The machine-readable surface on scimar.ca is CMS-provided: a served llms.txt generated by All in One SEO, the anonymously readable WordPress REST API (wp/v2) that returns news stories, pages, team profiles, media and site search as JSON, and a WordPress MCP Adapter that advertises two Model Context Protocol endpoints plus RFC 8414 and RFC 9728 OAuth discovery documents — all of which are authentication-gated.

providers.name: SentiLink
providers.description: SentiLink is an identity fraud prevention platform that empowers financial institutions to transact confidently by stopping synthetic identity fraud, account takeover, and first-party fraud at the point of account application and beyond. The platform provides a REST API delivering real-time scores and signals derived from behavioral and identity data, enabling lenders, banks, credit unions, and fintechs to make instant, accurate decisions without adding friction to the onboarding experience.

providers.name: Speedtest Tracker
providers.description: Speedtest Tracker is a self‑hosted application that monitors internet performance and uptime. Built with Laravel and the Ookla Speedtest CLI, it can be deployed via Docker and provides a web UI, API, and extensive documentation. The project aims to give users a historical view of their connection quality and ISP reliability, offering dashboards, notifications, and integrations for personal or community use.

providers.name: SportsAPIs.dev
providers.description: SportsAPIs.dev curates a comprehensive directory of over 45 sports odds and sports data APIs, providing detailed reviews, feature comparisons, and integration guidance for developers building betting applications, odds comparison tools, and sports analytics platforms. The site offers free read‑only access to its Multi‑Channel Platform (MCP) registry, allowing users to explore API offerings without authentication.

providers.name: tppflow-com
providers.description: tppflow-com is a stub entry in the API Evangelist catalog, originating from the MCP registry harvest. The company’s public presence and API offerings are currently undocumented, and no verifiable website or API documentation has been identified. This profile aims to gather accurate identity information, including a proper description, tags, and link properties, once reliable sources become available.

providers.name: Transfr
providers.description: Transfr Inc. is a New York City based workforce-education company that builds immersive virtual-reality job-training simulations for schools, colleges, workforce development boards, non-profits and justice-impacted programs. Its two products are Transfr Trek, a career-exploration program covering more than 150 occupations, and Transfr Train, hands-on VR skills training across sectors including manufacturing, healthcare, construction, automotive, aviation, diesel technology, electrical construction and hospitality. Learner and classroom data is administered through the Transfr dashboard, with rostering and single sign-on delivered through third-party education platforms (Clever, ClassLink, Canvas) rather than through a Transfr-published API. As of this profiling pass Transfr publishes no public developer program, API reference or machine-readable contract.

providers.name: Trustdock
providers.description: TRUSTDOCK Inc. (株式会社TRUSTDOCK) is a Tokyo-based digital identity and eKYC (electronic Know Your Customer) provider founded in November 2017. The company delivers high-precision, fast, and low-cost online identity verification and digital ID infrastructure via API, serving more than 300 enterprise and government clients across finance, insurance, ride-sharing and car-sharing, telecommunications (MNO/MVNO), real-estate crowdfunding, second-hand/reuse goods, recruitment, matching apps, and public-sector onboarding. TRUSTDOCK offers both browser-based and mobile-app-based verification flows, holds ISMS (ISO 27001) certification and the Japanese PrivacyMark, and participates in the OpenID Foundation Japan KYC Working Group and the FIDO Alliance. Its API documentation is provided to customers under NDA rather than published to a public developer portal.

providers.name: Universiti Teknologi Malaysia
providers.description: Universiti Teknologi Malaysia (UTM) is a public research university in Johor Bahru and Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, one of the five institutions designated a Research University by the Ministry of Higher Education and ranked #181 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. UTM publishes no developer portal, no API documentation and no OpenAPI, AsyncAPI or JSON Schema of its own, and there is no route by which an unaffiliated developer can obtain a credential for anything it runs. Its programmable footprint is entirely made of standards it exposes rather than interfaces it designed, and every one of them sits on UTM's own APNIC allocation (161.139.0.0/16, netname UTM-MY): the UTMIK Repository, a DSpace-CRIS institutional knowledge repository whose OAI-PMH 2.0 endpoint answers anonymously in twelve metadata formats including rioxx, etdms and an OpenAIRE CERIF-for-CRIS profile; the UTM Press journal platform, whose Open Journal Systems OAI-PMH interface has been harvestable since 2011 and whose REST API v1 answers 401; and a Microsoft Entra ID tenant whose signed SAML 2.0 metadata and OpenID Connect discovery document are the most completely specified machine contract in this profile. UTM is registered in ROR, and its own publishing arm, Penerbit UTM Press, is Crossref member 4787 with prefix 10.11113 and 12,640 registered DOIs. The older EPrints repository at eprints.utm.my, still listed by ROAR, OpenDOAR and Sherpa and still linked from the UTM Library, refused connections on both ports from three independent networks on 2026-09-01 and is recorded here as unreachable rather than as a surface.

providers.name: Upfluence
providers.description: Upfluence provides an influencer marketing platform that connects brands with creators. Their solution includes a robust API and MCP (Marketing Collaboration Platform) enabling programmatic access to creator data, campaign management, analytics, and payment processing. Powered by Jaice AI, Upfluence offers tools for discovery, vetting, outreach, and performance measurement, supporting e‑commerce, agencies, affiliate programs, and user‑generated content initiatives.

providers.name: Voxist
providers.description: Voxist provides Speech AI solutions built in Europe, offering products such as Voxcept for enterprise knowledge capture, Voxlive for real‑time translation, Voxlingo for multilingual call handling, Voxreply smart voicemail, and Voxmemo for meeting dictation. Their developer platform includes the Voxist API, enabling integration of speech‑to‑text, translation, and AI‑driven voice agents into applications. The company focuses on privacy‑first, European‑hosted AI services for contact centers, enterprises, and developers.

providers.name: World Fuel Services
providers.description: World Fuel Services, which rebranded as World Kinect Corporation in 2023, is a Miami-based Fortune 100 global energy management company that supplies fuel, energy and related products and services across three segments — aviation, marine and land. It sells and distributes jet fuel, marine bunker fuel, diesel, gasoline, natural gas, power, lubricants and renewable fuels to airlines, business aviation operators, airports and FBOs, shipping fleets and ports, commercial and industrial customers, government and military accounts, and retail petroleum networks in more than 200 countries and territories. Its technology brands include the myWorld aviation portal and app, Trip View, AVCARD and EPIC fuel cards, the World Kinect Online energy portal, and the trip-support business acquired from Universal Weather and Aviation in 2024. Digital delivery is customer-portal-first: integrations such as fuel-price feeds into flight-planning platforms are arranged commercially rather than through a public developer program.

providers.name: Accrete
providers.description: Accrete is a dual-use enterprise and government AI company founded in 2017 and headquartered at 17 State Street, New York, that licenses specialized Expert AI Agents built on its Knowledge Engine Platform. The platform compresses tacit human domain expertise and unstructured data into autonomously constructed knowledge graphs, which its agents reason over with long-term memory and multi-agent collaboration. Its product lines are Argus for government — supply-chain FOCI risk, narrative intelligence, information operations and law enforcement — and Nebula for commercial customers, covering IT service management and change-risk prediction (Nebula ITSM, shipped as a Snowflake Native App) and social narrative and brand-influence detection (Nebula Social). Customers include the U.S. Department of Defense, U.S. Special Operations Command, the U.S. Army, and Fortune 500 companies in media and entertainment, consumer goods and gaming. Accrete publishes no public developer API, SDK or machine-readable API contract; its agents are delivered as licensed products and through partner marketplaces such as Snowflake.

providers.name: AdLiftr
providers.description: AdLiftr is a media buying platform that lets performance marketers, DTC brands, and agencies bulk launch ads to Meta, TikTok, Google Ads, and Snapchat in minutes. Connect once, upload your creatives, and launch batches without Ads Manager repetition — from the dashboard, the REST API, or your AI assistant via MCP. 7-day free trial, no credit card required.

providers.name: ALLSALE
providers.description: ALLSALE Corp. operates ALLSALE, a TikTok Shop growth and creator-marketing automation platform for consumer brands. It runs three AI agents — a Creator Discovery Agent that finds and engages relevant TikTok creators, a Budget Optimization Agent that recommends budget allocation and commission adjustments, and a Performance Analyst Agent that tracks GMV and predicts results — automating the full workflow from creator discovery and outreach through performance tracking and ROI analysis. The company is a 500 Global portfolio company and reports 100K+ creators engaged and $50M+ in customer revenue generated across its brand clients. Plans run from a $399/month Starter tier to a $599/month Pro tier, with custom Enterprise pricing offering unlimited messaging, multi-brand support, and white-label options.

providers.name: Apache Ozone
providers.description: Apache Ozone is a scalable, redundant, and distributed object store optimized for big data workloads. It provides an S3-compatible interface and a Hadoop-compatible file system interface for seamless integration with existing big data tools.

providers.name: Assistant Gym
providers.description: Assistant Gym builds a platform to improve AI assistants for better outcomes, lower costs, and fewer mistakes. It offers tools like Decision Audit, Handoff Check, and a suite of bounded utilities to evaluate, train, test, verify, certify, and audit assistants in real work contexts.

providers.name: BankruptcyObserver
providers.description: Stay ahead of US business bankruptcies without repeatedly checking bankruptcy websites. Get next-morning alerts, verify changes against the court record, and connect your AI agent through MCP for case-specific answers. Standard and Heavy include a 7-day free trial. Cancel anytime.

providers.name: BaseHub
providers.description: GraphQL-first documentation and content platform where content is queried via a TypeScript-native GraphQL client with full type safety generated from the content schema.

providers.name: Benevity
providers.description: Benevity is a Calgary-based corporate purpose software platform for workplace giving, matching, grantmaking, and employee/customer volunteering. Its Giving API lets partners embed nonprofit-of-choice donations, optional matching, and charitable gift cards into e-commerce, banking, and rewards experiences; the Cause Search API exposes Benevity's vetted global nonprofit database; the Spark API lets existing Spark Employee Engagement clients surface giving and volunteering opportunities in other interfaces; and the Location Services API lets clients manage locations (stores, franchises, offices) inside the Benevity ecosystem. The API follows the RESTful/OpenAPI standard and is documented publicly at developer.benevity.org, but credentials are partner-gated - access requires requesting a demo/business relationship with Benevity rather than self-serve signup.

providers.name: Billables Ai
providers.description: Billables AI is a San Francisco based legal technology company that builds AI-powered automatic time tracking software for lawyers, consultants, and professional services firms. Its platform passively captures billable activity as people work across the tools they already use — Microsoft 365, Outlook, Teams, Zoom, Adobe, and the Chrome and Edge browsers — then uses AI to draft time entries, assign the correct client and matter, and write narrative descriptions, learning and adapting to each user over time. Privacy is user-controlled, with only the individual able to view or edit their own time records before they are submitted. The company is venture-backed (Series A) and was surfaced through the Wing Venture Capital portfolio.

providers.name: Brivvy
providers.description: Brivvy builds AI‑powered writing tools that help modern teams create consistent brand voice across blogs, emails, and posts. Founded by Colin Pace, the platform offers voice creation, template management, and real‑time content generation, integrating with popular AI models like Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, and Cursor. It aims to eliminate brand‑voice drift and improve workflow efficiency for marketing and product teams.

providers.name: Cardless
providers.description: Cardless, Inc. is a San Francisco fintech that operates an embedded co-branded credit card platform, letting consumer brands launch and run their own credit card programs natively inside their own apps and websites. The platform pairs a partner API surface with pre-built components covering the full credit journey — application and identity verification, real-time decisioning, checkout with instant virtual cards, card management and transaction disputes — while Cardless handles issuing-bank relationships, card production, underwriting, fraud, KYC/AML compliance, servicing and support behind the scenes. It is network-agnostic across Visa, Mastercard and American Express. Named partners include Coinbase (Coinbase One Card), Bilt, Qatar Airways Privilege Club, Alibaba.com, LATAM Airlines, Avianca LifeMiles, TAP Air Portugal and Avelo Airlines. Developer documentation at docs.cardless.com is gated behind a partner login, so no public OpenAPI, SDKs or sandbox credentials are published.

providers.name: Colossal Biosciences
providers.description: Colossal Biosciences is a Dallas, Texas based de-extinction and species-preservation biotechnology company founded in 2021 by Ben Lamm and Harvard geneticist George Church. It applies ancient-DNA sequencing, comparative genomics, CRISPR multiplex genome editing, cloning and artificial-womb research to restoring extinct keystone species — the woolly mammoth, thylacine, dodo, moa, dire wolf and blue buck among them — and to conserving critically endangered living species. Colossal spun out the computational life-sciences platform Form Bio, runs the non-profit Colossal Foundation, and publishes its research code through the colossal-compsci GitHub organization. Colossal publishes no product or developer API; the machine-readable surface on colossal.com is the WordPress REST API (wp/v2) that serves the company newsroom, pages, media and site search as JSON, plus a WordPress MCP Adapter endpoint that is present but authentication-gated.

providers.name: Conexiom
providers.description: Conexiom is an AI-powered sales order and invoice automation platform for manufacturers and distributors. It captures order and document data from any format (PDFs, Excel, email bodies, scans, and handwritten notes), validates and corrects it against ERP systems, and pushes clean, touchless transactions into a customer's order-management workflow. The platform surfaces its own document API (retrieving document lists and attachments) and a set of ERP integrations, documented in an authenticated help center rather than a public developer portal. Conexiom is backed by ICONIQ Capital and runs on Microsoft Azure with a SOC 2 Type II and GDPR-aligned security posture.

providers.name: Darrow
providers.description: Darrow is an AI legal-intelligence company (founded 2020, offices in New York, Miami, Arizona and Tel Aviv) that scans public real-world signals — regulatory filings, court dockets, incident reports, corporate disclosures and web behavior — to detect legal violations at scale, size the affected class, predict outcomes and value the resulting cases. Its platform serves plaintiff law firms (case origination, predictive litigation analytics, portfolio management, PlaintiffLink intake), insurers (predictive underwriting) and corporate compliance teams (Privacy Radar, listed in the Microsoft Marketplace). Darrow publishes no public developer program: the product is delivered through an Auth0-protected customer portal at portal.darrow.ai, and the only machine-readable surface reachable without credentials is the OpenID Connect discovery document served by its identity tenant.

providers.name: DeepHow
providers.description: DeepHow is an enterprise Physical AI platform that helps industrial companies capture, verify, and optimize operational knowledge across manufacturing, pharmaceutical, and electronics assembly environments. It turns expert know-how into searchable digital workflows, uses vision AI for live standard-operating-procedure (SOP) verification and on-demand visual inspection, and applies time-and-motion AI for task analysis and operator training and enablement. DeepHow is used by 100+ enterprises including Stanley Black & Decker, Anheuser-Busch InBev, Foxconn, and GSK. It is backed by Sierra Ventures and Techstars.

providers.name: Defense Unicorns
providers.description: Defense Unicorns is a defense-technology company that makes running modern software on military systems easy — from cloud to edge, satellites to submarines. Its UDS (Unicorn Delivery Service) platform is a secure-by-default, airgap-native software delivery stack built on Kubernetes and Zarf, bundling Istio, Keycloak, Authservice, Prometheus/Grafana, Vector/Loki, Falco and the Pepr policy engine. The company ships its developer surface as open-source CLIs and libraries — the UDS CLI, Pepr, Lula (compliance-as-code / OSCAL), and the Maru task runner — rather than a hosted REST API. Offerings span UDS Core, UDS Fleet, UDS Enterprise, software factories, compliance automation, and forward-deployed engineering. Backed by Sapphire Ventures.

providers.name: Digital Shadows
providers.description: Digital Shadows is a London-founded digital risk protection (DRP) company whose SearchLight platform monitors the open, deep and dark web for data leakage, exposed credentials, brand impersonation, exposed infrastructure and threat-actor activity affecting a customer's organization. ReliaQuest acquired Digital Shadows in July 2022 and the entity now trades as ReliaQuest UK Limited, with SearchLight folded into ReliaQuest GreyMatter Digital Risk Protection. The SearchLight Portal API remains live at portal-digitalshadows.com/api/ and is consumed by first-party tooling (the shadowline Python CLI and the Splunk SOAR connector) and by a wide third-party integration surface (Cortex XSOAR, ThreatConnect, Splunk, Sekoia, Axonius, TheHive, Atlassian Marketplace). The API reference itself is published only inside the authenticated customer portal.

providers.name: Element
providers.description: Element (Element Finance) is an Andreessen Horowitz-backed decentralized finance protocol for fixed and variable yield on crypto assets. The protocol splits an interest-bearing position into tradable Principal Tokens (PTs) and Yield Tokens (YTs) so users can lock in a fixed rate by buying discounted principal, or take variable-rate exposure, redeeming at face value on maturity via on-chain AMMs. It also ships the Council governance framework (voting vaults, delegation, the Governance Steering Council) that powers the Element DAO. Element is a smart-contract protocol on Ethereum rather than a hosted REST API: developers integrate through the on-chain contracts, the elf-sdk TypeScript library, and the published contract reference. The team has since rebranded to DELV (delvtech).

providers.name: Firefly Health
providers.description: Firefly Health is a virtual-first primary care practice and clinically integrated health plan founded in 2016 and headquartered in Watertown, Massachusetts. Members get a dedicated care team - a primary care physician, nurse practitioner, health guide and behavioral health specialist - reachable by chat and video through the Firefly Health app, backed by the Firefly Nearby network for in-person, at-home and specialty care. Firefly sells an employer-sponsored alternative health plan alongside its virtual primary care service, and in 2025 became the first national primary care practice to earn NCQA Virtual Care Accreditation. Firefly publishes no public developer program, portal, documentation or specification: the member web and mobile apps are served by a private first-party API at api-prod.firefly.health under an /api/v2/ base path. Included Health signed an agreement to acquire Firefly Health in July 2026.

providers.name: Firstbase
providers.description: Firstbase is an all-in-one startup operating system that helps founders form, run, and grow a US business from anywhere in the world. Its products cover incorporation (Firstbase Start for LLCs and C-Corps in Delaware, Wyoming, New York, Texas and more), ongoing compliance and registered-agent services (Firstbase Agent), bookkeeping, invoicing and tax-ready financials (Firstbase Accounting), tax filing, and a virtual business address (Firstbase Mailroom). Firstbase markets an embedded "Incorporation API" for platforms that want to offer company formation to their own users, but publishes no public developer documentation, OpenAPI specification, or self-serve developer portal for it. Firstbase is a venture-backed company (a16z portfolio) added to the API Evangelist network and enriched from its public web surface.

providers.name: Flipboard
providers.description: Flipboard is a content curation and social magazine platform that aggregates articles, videos, and social media posts into personalized, magazine-style feeds. Founded in 2010, Flipboard allows users to curate content into magazines around topics of interest and follow curators and publishers. Flipboard has embraced open web standards, implementing ActivityPub to federate with the Fediverse and supporting RSS for publisher content distribution.

providers.name: GraphQL Request
providers.description: Minimal, isomorphic GraphQL client for JavaScript/TypeScript originally from the Prisma team, now evolved into Graffle — with support for file uploads, batch requests, custom headers, TypeScript type inference, and a powerful extension system. Runs in Node.js and browsers.

providers.name: HeartFlow
providers.description: Heartflow, Inc. (Nasdaq: HTFL) is a healthcare technology company founded in 2010 and headquartered in San Francisco, California. Its Heartflow One platform applies AI to coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) to non-invasively diagnose and manage coronary artery disease, bundling Roadmap Analysis, FFRct Analysis, Plaque Analysis, Plaque Staging and the PCI Navigator, and delivering results back into hospital PACS and EMR systems. More than 650,000 patients have been analyzed across 1,800+ institutions. Heartflow runs a production REST API at api.heartflow.net and customer documentation at docs.heartflow.net, but both are authenticated: there is no public developer program, no published OpenAPI, and no self-serve signup.

providers.name: INFINIT
providers.description: INFINIT is an AI application for Web3 financial execution that lets anyone research, create, and execute DeFi and trading strategies through AI agents. Its Prompt-to-DeFi experience turns natural-language intents into agent-powered, one-workflow on-chain strategies, and its AI-managed trading vault marketplace lets independent strategy managers deploy non-custodial vaults that depositors access through a single workflow. For developers, INFINIT publishes the open-source INFINIT Library and INFINIT CLI — a TypeScript action framework and command-line tool for programmatically deploying and interacting with DeFi protocols including Aave v3, Uniswap v3, Pendle, and INIT Capital, distributed as npm packages under the @infinit-xyz scope. Backed by Electric Capital and EQT Ventures.

providers.name: Keysight Technologies
providers.description: Keysight Technologies is an electronic design, emulation and test company (Fortune 1000, rank 617). Its developer surface is product-side: the CyPerf network performance and security test platform exposes a REST API (/api/v2, OAuth2/OpenID Connect via a Keycloak 'keysight' realm) on each self-hosted or cloud controller, with an official generated Python SDK (cyperf on PyPI) and an experimental local stdio MCP server (cyperf-mcp, 100 tools). Keysight also publishes ixnetwork-restpy and snappi client libraries and Terraform modules for its virtual test products on GitHub.

providers.name: Mitigata
providers.description: Mitigata is an India-based, IRDAI-licensed integrated cyber resilience platform that bundles cyber insurance, 24x7 security operations, and compliance under one accountable pod. It offers smart cyber liability, D&O, E&O, crime and EPLI insurance; an in-house Bengaluru SOC with MDR, EDR/XDR, SIEM, SASE, ZTNA and DFIR; automated compliance for ISO 27001, SOC 2, PCI DSS, DPDP, GDPR, HIPAA, RBI and SEBI-CSCRF; and Gordon AI, an autonomous AI SOC covering dark-web monitoring, attack-surface management, third-party risk and phishing simulation. Mitigata publishes eleven purpose-built APIs (cyber score, email security, asset discovery, phishing protect, dark-web scanner, security checklist, third-party risk, employee risk, attack assist, cyber insurance and claims) but gates technical onboarding behind a booked API walkthrough.

providers.name: OSSIO
providers.description: OSSIO is an orthopedic fixation medical device company headquartered in Woburn, Massachusetts and founded in Israel in 2014. It develops and sells OSSIOfiber, a bio-integrative, metal-free implant material used for screws, suture anchors, staples, bone pins and trimmable fixation nails in foot and ankle, hand and wrist, sports medicine and pediatric procedures. OSSIO ships physical implants, not software, and publishes no developer program, no product API and no OpenAPI. Its one machine-readable surface is the corporate website itself: ossio.io runs WordPress with the MCP Adapter installed, exposing an OAuth-protected Model Context Protocol server plus RFC 8414 and RFC 9728 metadata documents at /.well-known/ — a site-content agent surface, not a product API.

providers.name: Parsec Finance
providers.description: Parsec Finance is an institutional-grade on-chain analytics platform for DeFi and NFT markets. Its modular "Command Center" lets traders and analysts drag and drop dozens of real-time components — live trade firehoses, liquidity-depth charts, wallet trackers, lending dashboards and NFT floor monitors — across many EVM chains. Beyond the app, Parsec exposes a Pro GraphQL API at api.parsec.finance for programmatic access to on-chain market data: DEX trades, OHLCV candles, lending markets, liquidity pools (including concentrated-liquidity positions), NFT collections and trades, token holders and balance changes, transfers, transactions, contract logs, trending contracts, trade metrics and address label resolution. A first-party Python SDK (parsecfi) wraps the API. Parsec is used by firms such as Polychain and Galaxy Digital.

providers.name: Peoples Group
providers.description: Peoples Group is the operating name of Peoples Trust Company, a Vancouver-based Canadian trust company and chartered-bank group founded in 1985 and owned by the Triple Five Group. Alongside its mortgage, deposit, and commercial-lending businesses, Peoples Group runs a fintech and payments arm that provides embedded banking-as-a-service to program managers, fintechs, brokers, and merchants across Canada: prepaid and credit card issuing under Visa and Mastercard BIN sponsorship, merchant acquiring, trust account services, and API-driven money movement including Interac e-Transfer (send, request money, and autodeposit), Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT) for CAD and USD debits and credits, bill payment to more than 12,000 Canadian billers, and push-to-card payouts via Visa Direct and Mastercard Send. In February 2026 Peoples Group partnered with Fiserv to build a next-generation, always-on payments platform carrying rich ISO 20022 data over direct connections to Canada's payment systems, positioning it for Payments Canada's Real-Time Rail. Its APIs are real and in production, but access is partnership- and sales-gated: there is no public self-serve developer portal, no downloadable OpenAPI/Swagger specification, and no public Postman workspace. Integration is arranged through a client relationship and the product documentation lives on the corporate fintech site.

providers.name: Piper
providers.description: Piper (Piper Learning, Inc. / Piper LLC) is an educational-technology company that makes hands-on STEM learning kits — most notably the Piper Computer Kit, a buildable wooden computer that teaches circuitry and coding through Minecraft, and Piper Make, a browser-based platform for exploring electronics and Python. Its consumer storefront runs on Shopify and exposes an agent-commerce surface: a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) merchant profile with an MCP endpoint plus Shopify Customer Account OpenID Connect, letting AI shopping agents search the catalog, build carts, and check out with explicit buyer approval. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched from its live public agent/discovery surface.

providers.name: PortSwigger
providers.description: PortSwigger is the UK-based security research company behind Burp Suite, the industry-standard web and API security testing platform used by penetration testers and enterprise AppSec teams worldwide. The platform is available as Burp Suite Community Edition (free), Burp Suite Professional (manual testing toolkit), and Burp Suite DAST (enterprise dynamic application security testing). Developers can automate and integrate with Burp Suite DAST via a GraphQL API and a REST API, both secured with API key authentication. PortSwigger also provides the Montoya extension API for building custom Burp Suite extensions and an official MCP Server extension that bridges Burp Suite with AI clients such as Claude Desktop.

providers.name: R.E. Merrill & Associates
providers.description: R.E. Merrill & Associates, Inc. is a Texas industrial pump distributor and manufacturers' representative (founded in Houston in 1987 by Ron Merrill Sr., led since 2020 by Ron Merrill Jr.; based in Wimberley, TX) that applies, quotes and supports 13 pump lines — Vanton thermoplastic pumps (exclusive Texas representative for 30+ years), Grundfos dosing and multistage pumps, Continental progressing cavity pumps, DP Pumps, Pinnacle-Flo, Vertiflo, Simtech, TF Seals, Garbarino, GreenPumps, Pemo, Victor and Walrus — for chemical processing, semiconductor, water/wastewater, boiler and petrochemical service. It publishes one machine-callable capability: a deterministic pump line finder that takes a pumping duty (fluid, flow, pressure or head, service) and returns which represented lines fit, citing the manufacturer catalog page for the smallest covering model, then hands off to a human engineer for quotation. The capability is exposed as an unauthenticated REST endpoint (POST https://www.remerrill.com/api/line-finder) and as an Agent2Agent v1.0 agent (JSON-RPC 2.0 at /api/a2a) with a JWS-signed agent card at /.well-known/agent-card.json, a published JWKS, and an llms.txt as its developer documentation. No pricing is returned by the API; quotes come from an engineer.

providers.name: SamaCare
providers.description: SamaCare operates a medical benefit prior authorization platform used by specialty practices in oncology, rheumatology, neurology, retina/ophthalmology and infusion care to submit, track and renew prior authorizations for provider-administered ("buy and bill") drugs across every payer in one place. The platform combines payer-specific form intelligence and auto-fill, human-in-the-loop AI, status tracking and expiration reminders with one-click re-authorization, and a market-access analytics layer that pharmaceutical manufacturers license for benchmark and patient-access insight. SamaCare states it has processed more than two million medical benefit prior authorizations representing over $6B in annual drug spend, and integrates into practice systems — NextGen Enterprise and ModMed EMRs among them — over an API-based two-way exchange of demographic data and clinical documentation. The platform API is served from api.samacare.com behind an OAuth 2.0 Bearer challenge and is arranged through EHR/RCM partnership rather than a public developer program; no public API reference, OpenAPI contract or self-serve key issuance is published.

providers.name: Skullcandy
providers.description: Skullcandy is a US consumer-audio brand that designs and sells headphones, wireless earbuds, gaming headsets, and Bluetooth speakers. Its e-commerce storefront at skullcandy.com runs on Shopify, and rather than a traditional developer program the brand exposes a modern agentic-commerce surface: an agent-facing llms.txt / agents.md, a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) merchant profile with a hosted Model Context Protocol (MCP) endpoint for catalog search, cart, checkout and fulfillment, a Shopify Customer Account API secured with OpenID Connect / OAuth 2.0 (including a customer-account MCP scope), and read-only storefront JSON endpoints for products and collections. This profile captures that agent- and API-facing surface as discovered on the live site.

providers.name: Taylor & Francis
providers.description: Taylor & Francis Group is a British academic publisher offering REST APIs for searching and accessing journal articles, books, metadata, and bibliographic records from over 2,700 Taylor & Francis and Routledge publications. Their API surfaces include content download APIs for books and chapters, KBART holdings automation for library systems, COUNTER 5 SUSHI usage reporting, and text and data mining access for institutional subscribers across humanities, social sciences, science, technology, and medicine.

providers.name: Thread AI
providers.description: Thread AI builds AI orchestration infrastructure for the enterprise. Its platform, Lemma, is a composable AI infrastructure and workflow-orchestration layer for building and running production-grade AI agents and workflows in regulated, mission-critical operations. Lemma pairs a drag-and-drop workflow builder with a code-first SDK and REST, gRPC, and GraphQL API access, adding full audit trails, governance, human-in-the-loop approvals, and reliability controls across email, voice, text, transcription, document extraction, and system-update worker functions. Deployment options span VPC, on-premises, and multi-tenant SaaS, and the platform is SOC 2 Type 2, HIPAA, GDPR, CJIS, and CMMC 2.0 Level 1 aligned (CMMC 2.0 Level 2 and FedRAMP underway). Thread AI is backed by Homebrew and Index Ventures.

providers.name: Trader Interactive
providers.description: Trader Interactive is a Norfolk, Virginia digital marketplace and dealer-services company operating a portfolio of vertical vehicle marketplaces — RV Trader, Cycle Trader, ATV Trader, PWC Trader, Snowmobile Trader, Aero Trader, Boatmart, Trade-A-Plane, Commercial Truck Trader, Equipment Trader, Next Truck, Rock & Dirt and Tradequip — alongside the Commercial Web Services and RV Web Services dealer website businesses and Statistical Surveys market research. It reaches over 13 million monthly unique visitors and has been wholly owned by CAR Group (formerly carsales.com Ltd) since 2022. Its integration surface is the TraderOnline (TOL) REST API, served from api.traderonline.com behind AWS API Gateway and consumed by dealers and syndication partners through first-party OAuth 2.0 client-credentials clients that Trader Interactive publishes as open source on GitHub, Packagist and npm. There is no public developer portal, no published API reference, and no machine-readable specification.

providers.name: UBIX Labs
providers.description: UBIX Labs is a no-code, cloud-based AI platform designed to democratize artificial intelligence for business users. The platform provides end-to-end AI capabilities including data integration, model development, deployment, and conversational AI through modular components. UBIX offers over 80 pre-built connectors and an Insights API for seamless integration with existing enterprise systems across 12+ industry verticals.

providers.name: Wealthsimple
providers.description: Wealthsimple is a Toronto-based Canadian financial technology company, founded in 2014, offering a full suite of consumer financial products: managed investing (Invest), self-directed stock and ETF trading (Trade), cryptocurrency, tax filing (Tax), spending, saving, and cash and card products. It serves more than four million Canadians with roughly CAD $125 billion in assets under administration and reached a CAD $10 billion valuation in its 2025 Series F round. Wealthsimple does not publish an official public developer API or OpenAPI specification; programmatic account access is available only through open-banking aggregators (SnapTrade, Plaid) and community-built unofficial libraries. This profile captures the company's public trust, security, and developer-adjacent surface (security.txt, HackerOne bug bounty, Trust Center, status page, verified GitHub organization).

providers.name: Xapo
providers.description: Xapo Bank is a members-only private bank and Bitcoin custodian founded in 2013, combining regulated fiat banking with institutional-grade Bitcoin custody in a single app. Members earn interest on Bitcoin and USD balances, borrow against Bitcoin without selling, invest in US stocks and ETFs, and transact globally in multiple currencies. Xapo Bank Limited is regulated by the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission as a credit institution (Permission No. 23171), with Xapo VASP Limited licensed as a DLT Provider (Permission No. 26061). The company publishes SOC 2 Type II / SOC 3, PCI DSS, and GDPR compliance claims but operates app-only today, with no public developer API or portal; legacy Xapo Bitcoin API SDKs remain on PyPI and RubyGems from its pre-bank wallet era.

providers.name: École Normale Supérieure de Lyon
