providers.description: École Normale Supérieure de Lyon (ENS de Lyon) is a French public grande école and research university, one of the four Écoles normales supérieures, ranked #187 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. It operates no public developer portal, publishes no OpenAPI, issues no API keys and runs no documented open-API programme — api.ens-lyon.fr, data.ens-lyon.fr and developer.ens-lyon.fr do not resolve — and this profile says so rather than padding the gap. What ENS de Lyon does operate, and what is recorded here, is standards-based identity and scholarly infrastructure. It self-hosts a Shibboleth Identity Provider on its own domain (idp.ens-lyon.fr, scope ens-lyon.fr, on the school's own 140.77.0.0/16 allocation), registered by RENATER in the Fédération Éducation-Recherche, carrying the REFEDS Research & Scholarship entity category and exported to eduGAIN; it runs an Apereo CAS single sign-on service at cas.ens-lyon.fr that answers the CAS 3.0 protocol; and it holds a Microsoft Entra ID tenant with live OIDC discovery. Its research output is machine-readable only as the ens-lyon collection on HAL, the national open archive operated by CCSD/CNRS — 106,836 records, harvestable over OAI-PMH and Solr search at api.archives-ouvertes.fr. That data is ENS de Lyon's; the platform, the contract and the admin contact (contact@archives-ouvertes.fr) are HAL's, so those surfaces are recorded as tenancies and HAL's generic reference and SWORD APIs are deliberately not claimed here. The school is registered in ROR and in the Crossref Funder Registry; it holds no DataCite membership and no Crossref depositor membership of its own.

providers.name: ABB Robotics
providers.description: ABB Robotics is the robotics and discrete-automation business of ABB Ltd, the Swiss-Swedish multinational headquartered in Zurich, Switzerland. ABB was formed in 1988 from the merger of ASEA (Sweden) and Brown, Boveri & Cie (Switzerland), with ASEA's IRB 6 (1974) considered the world's first microprocessor-controlled industrial robot. ABB Robotics manufactures a broad portfolio of articulated industrial robots, collaborative robots (GoFa, SWIFTI, YuMi), delta robots (FlexPicker / IRB 360), painting and welding robots, and autonomous mobile robots, paired with the OmniCore family of controllers running RobotWare 7 and the RAPID programming language. The developer surface is anchored by Robot Web Services (RWS) — a RESTful HTTP/HTTPS API for IO, RAPID, motion, file service, controller, e-log, subscriptions over WebSockets, and user authentication — plus the PC SDK (.NET) for native controller applications and the RobotStudio SDK (.NET 10 / RobotStudio 2026) for building Add-Ins and SmartComponents. RobotStudio Cloud extends offline programming and simulation into a collaborative browser surface. ABB also boosts RobotStudio with NVIDIA Omniverse libraries for AI-driven simulation. The company sells robots, controllers, software licenses, and PowerPac add-ons; RobotStudio Basic is free, RobotStudio Premium is sold by annual subscription via local sales.

providers.name: ABN AMRO
providers.description: A Dutch banking and financial services group serving retail, private, and corporate clients across Europe. ABN AMRO publishes a public developer portal exposing PSD2 Open Banking, Tikkie payment-request, and corporate payment APIs.

providers.name: Adbloop
providers.description: Adbloop is a Meta Verified technology provider that enables users to bulk‑create Facebook and Instagram advertising campaigns directly from Google Sheets, a web dashboard, or AI assistants like Claude and ChatGPT. Offering over 150 campaign templates, the platform automates ad creation, dynamic creative testing, and management in under two minutes per campaign, all for a flat $19 per month. The service targets marketers and agencies seeking rapid, scalable Meta ad deployment without the complexity of traditional Ads Manager.

providers.name: AECOM
providers.description: AECOM is a global infrastructure consulting firm providing professional services across planning, design, engineering, program management, and construction management for clients in transportation, water, energy, and the environment. AECOM operates in over 150 countries and is listed on the NYSE as ACM. The firm serves governments, businesses, and organizations worldwide, delivering integrated lifecycle solutions from advisory and design through construction and operations.

providers.name: Aeon
providers.description: Aeon provides real-time, plain‑language data on insider trades, congressional transactions, fund holdings and federal contracts. Pull JSON feeds or use the API to get up‑to‑date filings from SEC, House, Senate, White House and USAspending sources. Free tier offers 500 daily requests, with paid plans for higher volume and faster latency. The service aims to make complex financial disclosures accessible to developers, analysts and AI assistants.

providers.name: Agoric
providers.description: Agoric is a Cosmos-based Layer 1 blockchain that lets developers build secure cross-chain smart contracts in Hardened JavaScript (SES). Its Orchestration API abstracts multiple chains so a single long-lived contract can manage assets, accounts, and services across the multi-chain universe. The platform is built around Zoe (a smart-contract framework that enforces offer safety), ERTP (the Electronic Rights Transfer Protocol for issuing and transferring digital assets), and SwingSet (its deterministic async VM). Developers ship dapps with the `agoric` CLI and `agd` Cosmos daemon, query chain state through vstorage, and integrate with the network over Cosmos RPC and IBC. The developer surface is delivered as first-party `@agoric/*` npm packages rather than a REST API. Originally surfaced as a Polychain portfolio company, this profile has been enriched from Agoric's public developer platform.

providers.name: AIDataParser
providers.description: AIDataParser provides a schema‑first data‑extraction API that turns messy PDFs and images into structured JSON for AI agents and developers. It offers credit‑based pricing, a free tier with 50 credits, and a quick‑start guide. The service emphasizes clean JSON output, confidence scoring, and easy integration via a simple POST request.

providers.name: Alexandria Archive
providers.description: Alexandria Archive is a professional digital archive dedicated to preserving and exploring the history of Alexandria, Egypt through photographs, documents, maps, and collections. Founded on 6 September 2023, it offers an open, youth‑led cultural‑heritage platform where the community can contribute historic photos, articles, and stories. The site provides an OpenAPI specification at /api/openapi.json and a machine‑readable llms.txt index for developers.

providers.name: Alloplex Biotherapeutics
providers.description: Alloplex Biotherapeutics, Inc. is a privately held clinical-stage cellular immunotherapy company founded in 2016 and headquartered in Woburn, Massachusetts, with a wholly owned subsidiary, Alloplex Australia Pty Ltd, in Adelaide, South Australia. It develops non-engineered, autologous multi-cellular therapies intended to retrain a patient's own immune system against solid tumors and autoimmune disease. Its ENLIST platform uses an irradiated, engineered melanoma cell line expressing multiple immunomodulatory factors to activate, differentiate and expand a patient's peripheral blood mononuclear cells; the resulting product, SUPLEXA, is manufactured by a defined, GMP-compatible process that uses no genetic engineering and no feeder cells and yields a full course of treatment from a small blood draw in roughly one month. The first-in-human Phase 1 SUPLEXA-101 trial, conducted in Australia in 35 patients with metastatic solid tumors who had exhausted standard options, met its endpoints, and the FDA granted SUPLEXA Fast Track designation for MSI-H colorectal cancer. Alloplex Biotherapeutics runs no developer program and publishes no product API, developer portal, SDK or API documentation; the only machine-readable surface reachable without credentials is the WordPress REST content API behind alloplexbio.com, catalogued here.

providers.name: Amber Group
providers.description: Amber Group is a global digital asset financial services firm founded in 2017 by former traditional-finance traders, providing trading, liquidity provision, wealth and asset management, staking, and treasury solutions for institutions and high-net-worth clients. Its institutional platform, Amber Premium (Nasdaq: AMBR), operates from financial hubs including Singapore, Hong Kong, and Dubai, and publishes the Amber Premium Global API service suite so clients can integrate trading, liquidity, and account services into their own systems. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of DCM Ventures, Pantera Capital, and Paradigm and enriched with the company's public developer, legal, and support surfaces.

providers.name: Ambix
providers.description: Ambix provides a shared product context platform that centralizes strategy, priorities, decisions, and learnings as structured data. Teams can collaborate using AI tools like Claude or Cursor, linking insights to initiatives and enabling seamless navigation without meetings. The service offers a free 30‑day trial and then a subscription model, with data stored in the EU and built in Sweden.

providers.name: AuditBoard
providers.description: AuditBoard (rebranded in 2026 as Optro) is an AI-powered GRC (governance, risk, and compliance) SaaS platform used by more than half of the Fortune 500 to run their audit, risk, and compliance programs. Its connected-risk suite spans Controls Management (SOX), OpsAudit (operational/internal audit), RiskOversight (enterprise/operational risk), CrossComply (IT risk and cybersecurity compliance), ESG, RegComply (regulatory compliance), and AI Governance. Optro exposes a developer platform at developer.auditboard.com (a login-gated ReadMe portal) for programmatic access, plus documented integrations with systems such as ServiceNow, Workiva, and Microsoft 365. AuditBoard was surfaced as a Battery Ventures portfolio company and enriched here from its public web surface; the API reference itself sits behind an end-user login, so no public OpenAPI is captured.

providers.name: Aussie Broadband
providers.description: Aussie Broadband is an Australian telecommunications provider, founded in 2003 in regional Victoria, selling award-winning nbn and Opticomm internet, mobile SIM plans, hosted phone and network services to homes, businesses and enterprises. It also runs a wholesale division and Carbon, its self-service business and wholesale portal for qualification, ordering, billing, support and its on-net Aussie Fibre ethernet service. No public developer API or API documentation was found on its site.

providers.name: busabase-com
providers.description: busabase-com is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: mcp-registry) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.

providers.name: BusUp
providers.description: BusUp Technologies provides a cloud‑based platform that enables businesses to digitize and automate their procurement, invoicing, and expense management processes. The solution offers real‑time analytics, integration with ERP and accounting systems, and a mobile app for on‑the‑go approvals. Targeted at mid‑size enterprises, BusUp aims to streamline spend management, improve compliance, and reduce manual effort across the purchase‑to‑pay lifecycle.

providers.name: Candex
providers.description: Candex is a fintech "master vendor" platform that lets large enterprises engage, track, and pay long-tail, one-time, and hard-to-onboard suppliers across more than 50 countries without setting each vendor up in their own ERP or finance systems. A buyer configures Candex once; when it needs to purchase from a small or irregular supplier, it transacts with Candex, which handles supplier onboarding, tax and banking validation, compliance scans, PO and non-PO invoicing, and cross-border payment execution, then remits to the actual supplier. By consolidating tail-spend vendors and their records, Candex reduces administrative overhead, increases spend visibility and control, and makes "No PO, No Pay" policies achievable. The company integrates with existing procurement and finance stacks via API and bulk upload, but publishes no public developer portal or API reference.

providers.name: canyougrab.it
providers.description: canyougrab.it provides a Bulk Domain Availability API that allows users to check the availability of multiple domain names in a single request. Leveraging real-time DNS and WHOIS lookups, the service returns structured JSON responses indicating registration status, expiry dates, and registrar information. It offers a free tier with generous rate limits, supports up to 100 domains per batch, and is designed for developers needing reliable bulk domain checks for brand monitoring, domain portfolio management, or automated registration workflows.

providers.name: CARFAX
providers.description: CARFAX is a vehicle history reporting company that provides VIN-based history reports, dealer inventory solutions, QuickVIN license plate decoding, and used car valuations based on service records, accident history, ownership history, and title data. APIs are available to dealers, lenders, insurers, and service shops through enterprise partnership agreements.

providers.name: CFI
providers.description: Corporate Finance Institute (CFI) provides online finance education, certifications, and training programs for individuals and teams. It offers courses in financial modeling, valuation, FP&A, and AI for finance, serving professionals seeking to advance their careers. CFI’s platform includes a resource library, career maps, and enterprise solutions for organizations, positioning itself as a leading provider of finance skills and certifications worldwide.

providers.name: Coin IRA
providers.description: Coin IRA offers a $0‑fee self‑directed cryptocurrency IRA, allowing investors to hold Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP and other digital assets alongside traditional holdings like fractional gold and silver. The platform provides free cold storage, no account fees, and tools for tax‑advantaged crypto investing, targeting both individual and retirement accounts. It emphasizes security, compliance, and easy access through a web portal and mobile app.

providers.name: CYGNVS
providers.description: CYGNVS (an acronym for "CYber GuidaNce Virtual Space") is a Silicon Valley SaaS company that operates an out-of-band command center for cyber crisis preparedness and incident response. The platform runs independently of an organization's corporate infrastructure so that response teams — security, legal, executives, insurers, and external stakeholders — can coordinate securely even when internal systems are compromised or down, preserving legal privilege and chain of custody. CYGNVS provides guided playbooks, tabletop exercises, regulated-response execution with regulatory reporting templates across many jurisdictions, and bundles CISO personal-liability insurance underwritten by AIG. Founded in 2020 by Arvind Parthasarathi, the company raised a $55M Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz in January 2023. This API Evangelist profile was enriched from public surfaces; CYGNVS exposes no public developer API — the application is delivered as a secured out-of-band product across regional domains.

providers.name: Cylance
providers.description: Cylance, now part of Arctic Wolf, provides AI‑driven endpoint protection and threat detection solutions. Leveraging machine‑learning, the platform prevents malware, ransomware and zero‑day attacks before they execute, helping enterprises reduce risk and meet compliance. The company’s technology integrates with broader security operations, offering visibility, automation and advanced analytics for modern cyber defenses.

providers.name: dopost
providers.description: Social media scheduler API. Schedule and publish posts across Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, Pinterest, X (Twitter), and YouTube from a single REST API. Multi-account, multi-network publishing built for solo creators, agencies, and SaaS embedding.

providers.name: Finicom
providers.description: Finicom offers a platform that synchronizes bank transaction data with applications such as Google Sheets, Notion, Airtable, Zapier, and Slack. It supports connections to over 12,000 financial institutions in the US and Canada and provides features like AI‑powered receipt and statement imports, real‑time notifications, and team collaboration tools. The service is available for personal use at no cost and includes paid tiers for additional connected banks and destinations.

providers.name: FlexPoint
providers.description: FlexPoint is an AI-native billing and accounts receivable (AR) platform built specifically for managed service providers (MSPs). It automates the invoice-to-cash lifecycle across five jobs: Sync (pull billing data from PSA and accounting systems), Send (issue invoices), Collect (chase and recover overdue invoices), Process (card and ACH payments including Same-Day ACH and AutoPay), and Reconcile (match deposits to the general ledger via GL Connect). FlexPoint's AR Agents autonomously send payment reminders, follow up on overdue invoices, and surface collection priorities. The platform integrates with the accounting, ERP, PSA, quoting, and automation tools MSPs already run (QuickBooks, Xero, Sage Intacct, NetSuite, Business Central, ConnectWise, HaloPSA, Autotask, SuperOps, Quoter, QuoteWerks, Rewst, DataGate) and offers API access for custom integrations. FlexPoint is backed by Foundry Group and Techstars.

providers.name: Försäkringskassan
providers.description: Försäkringskassan is Sweden’s national social insurance agency responsible for administering health insurance, parental benefits, pensions, and other welfare services. It provides digital services and APIs for citizens and businesses to access information, submit applications, and retrieve status updates. The agency focuses on secure, reliable, and user-friendly digital interactions, supporting a wide range of social security processes across the country.

providers.name: Genspark
providers.description: Genspark is an all-in-one AI workspace and autonomous "Super Agent" platform that plans and executes multi-step tasks on a user's behalf. It bundles a suite of AI agent tools — deep research, AI slides, AI sheets, AI docs, AI chat, a "Call For Me" voice agent, and a built-in AI browser — into a single natural-language workspace, alongside companion products such as Genspark Claw, Speakly, GenClipboard, and GenTerminal and native iOS and Android apps. For developers and agents, Genspark operates a hosted, remote Model Context Protocol (MCP) server at /api/mcp that exposes its tools, resources, and prompts over HTTP, gated by OAuth 2.1 (authorization_code with PKCE, refresh tokens, and dynamic client registration). Genspark is backed by Emergence Capital.

providers.name: Giga
providers.description: Giga (legal name Giga AI, Inc.; formerly Giga ML) is a San Francisco-based agentic AI company that builds human-like voice, chat, and multimodal AI agents for high-volume enterprise customer support. Its agents run on a unified real-time orchestration layer that listens, reasons, checks connected systems, and responds in roughly half a second, resolving issues end to end rather than merely deflecting. Agents are built in Agent Canvas, a low-code studio that auto-writes policies from uploaded transcripts, and support 90 languages with real-time hallucination correction. Backed by Redpoint Ventures, Y Combinator, and Nexus Venture Partners (USD 61M Series A); customers include DoorDash, Toast, Postman, and Capital.com.

providers.name: Gnowbe
providers.description: Gnowbe is an AI-powered workforce enablement and performance platform for enterprise learning, enablement, and alignment. It turns static content and communication into mobile-first microlearning experiences with AI-powered activation and execution tracking, so teams do not just learn but perform. Trusted by 500,000+ learners across 100+ countries, Gnowbe combines authoring, AI content creation, group-based delivery, completion and engagement analytics, and integrations (SSO/SAML, LMS/SCORM, xAPI/LRS, HR systems, Slack, Microsoft Teams, and Zapier's 5,000+ tools). Gnowbe is a portfolio company of 500 Global.

providers.name: Hokkaido University
providers.description: Hokkaido University (北海道大学) is a national research university in Sapporo, Japan, founded in 1876 as Sapporo Agricultural College, a member of Japan's Designated National University group and ranked #173 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. It operates 12 undergraduate schools, 21 graduate schools and numerous research institutes. Its public programmable footprint is small and honest: the university publishes no developer portal, no API gateway and no documented public REST API — api., data., opendata., developer. and status.hokudai.ac.jp all fail to resolve, and the WordPress REST API on its English site is explicitly disabled. What it does operate, and what this profile is built on, is scholarly identity infrastructure. It runs its own SAML 2.0 / Shibboleth identity provider registered in GakuNin, the Japanese national academic access federation; it holds Handle System prefix 2115 and JaLC DOI prefix 10.14943 for the HUSCAP institutional repository; and it publishes crawlable XML sitemaps for both HUSCAP and its main web estate. HUSCAP's OAI-PMH endpoint is the one real regression: IRDB still harvests the repository by OAI-PMH, but no base URL has been publicly documented since the December 2025 platform migration and eighteen candidate paths were probed unsuccessfully.

providers.name: IRALOGIX
providers.description: IRALOGIX is a Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania fintech that operates a cloud-native, white-label IRA (Individual Retirement Account) recordkeeping and administration platform for financial institutions — banks, wealth managers, brokerages, recordkeepers and advisors — who use it to offer digital IRA programs under their own brand. The platform covers onboarding, contributions, trading, distributions, rollovers, compliance monitoring and administration end to end, and the company markets "API-driven connectivity and real-time data flows" that integrate with existing custodial and recordkeeping infrastructure rather than replacing it. The developer surface is partner-gated: documentation at docs.iralogix.com sits behind Okta visitor authentication and the partner console at partner.iralogix.com behind an Auth0 tenant, so no public OpenAPI, AsyncAPI or SDK is published. The company states SSAE SOC 2 Type 1 and SSAE SOC 1 Type 2 attestation.

providers.name: Jules
providers.description: Jules is Google's autonomous, asynchronous AI coding agent, developed inside Google Labs and powered by the Gemini family of models (currently Gemini 2.5 Pro on the free tier and Gemini 3 Pro on paid tiers). Jules connects to a user's GitHub repositories, clones the target repo into a sandboxed Google Cloud VM, generates a multi-step plan, and then executes coding tasks such as bug fixes, refactors, dependency bumps, test authoring, and small feature builds, ultimately opening a pull request for human review. Jules ships three surfaces beyond the web app at jules.google.com: a documented REST API in alpha at jules.googleapis.com/v1alpha (Sources, Sessions, Activities) authenticated via X-Goog-Api-Key, a lightweight CLI called Jules Tools installable via npm, and a Gemini CLI extension that exposes Jules as a /jules slash command. Access is gated to Google account holders and the API is experimental. Jules is sold as part of the Google AI subscription bundles, with a free introductory plan (15 tasks/day, 3 concurrent), Google AI Pro at $19.99/month (100 tasks/day, 15 concurrent, Gemini 3 Pro), and Google AI Ultra at $124.99/month (300 tasks/day, 60 concurrent, priority Gemini 3 Pro access).

providers.name: Keyboardio
providers.description: Keyboardio is a hardware company that designs and sells premium ergonomic mechanical keyboards, including the sculpted hardwood Model 100, the ultra- portable Atreus, and the upcoming Preonic. Its keyboards run fully open-source, reprogrammable firmware (Kaleidoscope) configured through the cross-platform Chrysalis GUI, both developed in the open on GitHub. Keyboardio sells direct through a Shopify storefront at shop.keyboard.io; customer login and account management use Shopify Customer Accounts (OpenID Connect / OAuth 2.0) bound to the keyboard.io domain. Keyboardio has no first-party public HTTP API — this profile captures the real developer, open-source, and identity surfaces the company publishes.

providers.name: King Abdulaziz University
providers.description: King Abdulaziz University (KAU) is a large public research university in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, serving over 100,000 students across 30 faculties and institutes including a branch campus at Rabigh. Its programmable footprint is small but, unusually for this cohort, partly its own. KAU operates a genuine institution-run Open Data API at opendata.kau.edu.sa returning aggregate student enrollment and graduation statistics as JSON over eight documented, unauthenticated GET invocations, and it operates its own SAML 2.0 identity provider at iam.kau.edu.sa/oamfed/idp/samlv20 on Oracle Access Manager Federation, self-hosted in KAU's own 192.162.72.0/24 address block with no managed-IdP vendor underneath it. Everything else that looks like a KAU API belongs to somebody else. The best machine-readable surface associated with the university — a complete OAI-PMH 2.0 data provider carrying its journals back to 2000 — is Elsevier's Digital Commons at kauj.researchcommons.org, administered from dc-support@elsevier.com. Its learning platform is a Blackboard Learn SaaS tenancy on lms.kau.edu.sa, and its scientific platform at libsp.kau.edu.sa is an Al Manhal tenancy. All three are recorded here as tenant relationships and none of their contracts is claimed as KAU's. KAU is a Crossref member in its own right under DOI prefix 10.4197 and is registered in ROR. It holds no DataCite account, publishes no SAML metadata, and belongs to neither the Maeen national identity federation nor eduGAIN although thirty-eight Saudi entities do. There is no developer portal, no API key or client registration of any kind, no official GitHub organisation, and no OpenAPI — the specification in this repository is derived by API Evangelist from KAU's published endpoints and a real response body, not published by KAU.

providers.name: Knocknoc
providers.description: Knocknoc provides a platform for secure, low‑latency communication between IoT devices and enterprise back‑ends. The service offers device provisioning, real‑time messaging, and analytics dashboards, all accessible via RESTful APIs and MQTT. Founded in 2022 and backed by Decibel, Knocknoc focuses on edge‑compute integration, OTA updates, and compliance with industry security standards, targeting smart‑home, industrial automation, and fleet management sectors.

providers.name: Kount
providers.description: Kount is a Boise, Idaho-based fraud prevention and chargeback management platform, now operating as part of Equifax. Kount combines AI-driven risk scoring, device fingerprinting, identity intelligence, and a multi-tenant global data network to help merchants, payment processors, and digital businesses stop payment fraud, account takeover, and chargebacks while reducing false positives. The Kount 360 platform offers Payments Fraud, Account Takeover Protection, Chargeback Management, and Identity Trust services exposed through REST APIs, mobile SDKs, a JavaScript Data Collector, and e-commerce platform plugins.

providers.name: Lizzyai
providers.description: Lizzy is a generative-AI platform for legal professionals, delivering a secure Gen AI workspace across all practice areas through both a web application and a Microsoft Word/Outlook add-in. It supports contract drafting, review, analysis, and proofreading, customizable legal workflows and playbooks, in-document citations, redlining and track-changes, and the handling of long, scanned, watermarked, and multiple documents. A multi-LLM approach routes each task to the most capable model, and firms can train a private model that embeds their own know-how. Built for enterprise IT with a zero-trust architecture, no training on customer data, PII anonymization, SSO via SAML and OAuth 2.0, and shared, VPC, or self-hosted deployment options.

providers.name: MotherDuck
providers.description: MotherDuck is a serverless cloud data warehouse built on DuckDB. Connectivity is via DuckDB clients (Python, Node.js, Wasm, Go, JDBC) using access tokens or SSO; the service does not publicly document a separate REST management API.

providers.name: Netstock
providers.description: Netstock is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: new-submission) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.

providers.name: Notable
providers.description: Notable is an intelligent-automation company purpose-built for healthcare, applying AI agents to administrative and operational workflows across patient access, revenue cycle management, care operations, and contact-center automation. Its platform pairs a library of prebuilt AI Agents with Flow Builder, a low-code interface for designing, training, and deploying automations, Sidekick, a human-in-the-loop AI co-pilot for clinically complex work such as prior authorization, and Flow AI, a conversational assistant for workflow builders. Integration runs bi-directionally against Epic, Oracle Health/Cerner, MEDITECH, athenahealth and eClinicalWorks over a mix of FHIR APIs, HL7 interfaces, RPA and third-party APIs. Notable reports deployment at 12,000+ sites of care serving 38M+ patients, with customers including Intermountain Health, MUSC Health, CommonSpirit Health and CityMD, and is backed by ICONIQ Growth, Greylock, F-Prime, Oak HC/FT, Maverick Ventures and 8VC. Notable publishes no public API contract; its developer documentation sits behind customer SSO. This profile is enriched from the company's public trust, security, and llms.txt surfaces.

providers.name: Okapi
providers.description: Okapi (okapi.bot) bills itself as "Dependabot for APIs": a free GitHub App that finds the third-party APIs an application and its AI agents call, tracks those providers' changes, and opens a pull request with the code fix before a deprecation or breaking change lands. Its site reports reading 1,173 API providers' own pages and tracking 841 upcoming breaking changes, and it publishes a public breaking-changes feed and provider directory. Its terms say automated use of this data goes through Okapi's check API, which is available by emailing hello@okapi.bot. The product is in early access.

providers.name: Omnea
providers.description: Omnea is an AI-native procurement platform that automates the full source-to-pay (S2P) process, unifying intake management, strategic sourcing, third-party risk management, and supplier management behind autonomous agents. Buyers raise requests conversationally through Slack, Microsoft Teams, or an OAuth-protected remote MCP (Model Context Protocol) server, and Omnea routes intelligent workflows, price-intelligence benchmarking, continuous supplier monitoring, and automated approvals. The company is backed by Accel, Insight Partners, and Point Nine, and exposes a documented public REST API plus a hosted MCP endpoint for agent integrations. Added to the API Evangelist network from VC-portfolio discovery and enriched from live probes of its public surfaces.

providers.name: Open Geospatial Consortium (OGC)
providers.description: The Open Geospatial Consortium is the standards body for geospatial interoperability — a member-funded consortium founded in 1994 and headquartered in the United States, with 362 member organizations plus 159 individual members across government, commercial, academic and non-profit sectors. OGC wrote the web-mapping layer the public sector has run on for two decades — WMS, WFS, WCS, WMTS and CSW, the OWS suite — and is now replacing it with the OGC API family: a set of resource-oriented, OpenAPI-described standards sharing a common core, of which eleven are approved (Features, Common, EDR, Tiles, Processes, Maps, Moving Features, Records, Connected Systems, DGGS and SensorThings) and seven more are in draft. Its API posture is genuinely open where it counts and closed where most standards bodies are: every adopted standard is a free download, the schemas and OpenAPI documents are served anonymously from schemas.opengis.net, and drafting happens in public on GitHub across 361 repositories — while portal.ogc.org, where Technical Committee documents, votes and delegate rosters live, returns HTTP 401 to the public. OGC runs a compliance and certification programme (CITE) and publishes its active member roster as a CSV, which is unusual and makes the coalition measurable. The distinction this repo keeps is that OGC publishes SPECIFICATIONS, not services: the contracts here have templated servers and describe what a conformant implementation must offer, so they must never be read as a callable API.

providers.name: opendocs-cloud
providers.description: opendocs-cloud provides a cloud-based platform for creating, sharing, and collaborating on API documentation. It enables developers to host interactive API docs, generate client SDKs, and manage versioning with ease. The service integrates with popular API design tools, supports OpenAPI and AsyncAPI specifications, and offers customizable theming and access controls for teams of any size. By centralizing documentation workflows, opendocs-cloud helps organizations improve API discoverability, reduce onboarding time, and maintain up-to-date reference material for internal and external consumers.

providers.name: Pango
providers.description: Pango is a Y Combinator (Summer 2026) startup building an AI-powered operating system for e-commerce post-purchase and logistics operations. The platform positions itself as an "agentic OS" — autonomous AI agents that handle back-office logistics tasks — and consolidates multi-carrier delivery management, checkout delivery options, branded order tracking, and returns processing into a single unified system. Pango advertises multi-carrier orchestration across 100+ shipping providers with AI-powered routing and rate optimization, self-service return portals with automated approvals, warehouse pick-and-pack automation, and AI agents that resolve exceptions and automate workflows. It integrates with major commerce platforms (Shopify, WooCommerce, BigCommerce, Magento, Salesforce Commerce, NetSuite) and 100+ carrier, WMS, marketing, and support partners. Added to the API Evangelist network as a Y Combinator portfolio lead; as of this enrichment pass the company markets an "API-first architecture" but publishes no public developer documentation, API reference, OpenAPI spec, or SDK.

providers.name: Pipe
providers.description: Pipe is an embedded financial OS that lets platforms — vertical SaaS, payment facilitators, and marketplaces — offer capital and cash-flow tools to the small and medium-sized businesses on their platform without those businesses ever leaving it. Its marquee product, Capital, delivers pre-approved funding offers priced from a business's transaction data, with repayment tied to sales performance rather than fixed monthly payments. Partners integrate via prebuilt embedded UI components, a zero-code Pipe-hosted flow, or a customizable REST API, while Pipe handles the banking partnerships and compliance. Backed by Anthemis and Creandum. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline from Pipe's public pages; the full API reference lives behind password-gated partner docs at docs.pipe.com.

providers.name: Project Gutenberg
providers.description: Project Gutenberg is a free ebook library providing access to over 75,000 public domain books via the Gutendex REST API. The API enables developers to search and retrieve bibliographic metadata for books and authors, filter by language, copyright status, topic, and MIME type, and access download links for multiple formats including EPUB, Kindle, HTML, and plain text. Project Gutenberg has pioneered free ebooks since 1971 and the Gutendex API makes its catalog programmatically accessible via a simple JSON REST interface with no authentication required.

providers.name: ReadySetAuction
providers.description: ReadySetAuction provides a cloud‑based auction software platform designed for nonprofit organizations, schools, faith‑based groups, sports teams, and other charitable entities. It supports silent, live, mobile, and online fundraising auctions, offering features such as guest management, RSVP tracking, table assignments, meal selections, and real‑time auction monitoring. The solution aims to streamline auction planning, increase proceeds, and simplify event logistics for a wide range of charitable fundraising activities.

providers.name: Risklytics
providers.description: Risklytics is an AI-native property and catastrophe risk company (Y Combinator Summer 2026, based in San Francisco, founded 2026 by Samuel Gold and Alexander Risio). It builds hyper-localized disaster risk models that simulate specific natural hazards - wildfire, flood, wind, earthquake, and debris runout - against individual home structures rather than ZIP-code averages, creating a per-structure digital twin from building footprints, lidar, and public records. Its Ember API returns property risk scores, modeled annual loss estimates, and retrofit-impact modeling used for insurance risk selection and portfolio triage (currently California-only, production model ember-1.3.0-firewall). The company also operates the FireCast platform and an AI-native brokerage for hard-to-place commercial insurance. API access is via a personal API key issued through the platform dashboard; there is no public OpenAPI, developer portal, or blog published to date, so this profile captures the company identity, the documented Ember API plans and authentication model, and the security posture of its web surface.

providers.name: StoreHub
providers.description: StoreHub is Southeast Asia's leading all-in-one cloud-based point-of-sale (POS) and business-management platform. Founded in 2013 and headquartered in Malaysia, it powers over 18,000 restaurants, retailers, and service-based businesses across Malaysia, the Philippines, and Thailand. The platform bundles POS, inventory management, multi-location management, employee management, reporting and analytics, QR Order & Pay, e-invoicing (LHDN/BIR compliant), loyalty and cashback, SMS marketing (Engage), Beep Delivery online ordering, a branded webstore, and marketplace and food-delivery integrations. StoreHub exposes a private, partner-gated REST API for custom integrations (dedicated API access is an Enterprise-tier feature); credentials are issued by Customer Care on request and there is no public OpenAPI specification or self-serve developer portal.

providers.name: Symetra Financial
providers.description: Symetra Financial Corporation is a diversified financial services company headquartered in Bellevue, Washington, providing employee benefits, annuities, and life insurance products to individuals, families, and businesses through independent advisors and financial institutions. A subsidiary of Sumitomo Life Insurance Company since 2016, Symetra offers medical stop-loss insurance, group life and disability income protection, supplemental health coverage, fixed and indexed annuities, registered index-linked annuities, income annuities, term life, and permanent life insurance. The company offers API and EDI-based data integrations for benefits administrators and HR platforms.

providers.name: UniCredit
providers.description: UniCredit is a leading European banking group offering a full range of financial services, including corporate and investment banking, retail banking, asset management, and digital solutions. With a strong presence across Europe and a focus on innovation, UniCredit serves corporate clients, SMEs, and private customers, providing tailored financing, payment services, and advisory. The group emphasizes sustainability, digital transformation, and customer-centric approaches, operating in over 20 countries with a robust network of branches and digital channels.

providers.name: Union Pacific
providers.description: Union Pacific is one of the largest freight railroad networks in the United States, operating across 23 states in the western two-thirds of the country. The company transports a diverse range of commodities including agricultural products, automotive goods, chemicals, energy resources, and industrial materials. Union Pacific's API platform gives businesses programmatic access to real-time shipment tracking, equipment management, intermodal planning, and supply chain exception handling, enabling seamless integration with logistics and supply chain management systems.

providers.name: Upstream Security
providers.description: Upstream Security is a cloud-based automotive and smart-mobility cybersecurity company. Its purpose-built vehicle data platform delivers Cyber XDR detection and response for connected vehicles, runtime AI and API security, proactive quality detection, and advanced analytics, alongside AutoThreat PRO threat intelligence and Vehicle Security Operations Center (vSOC) services for OEMs, Tier 1 and 2 suppliers, fleets, insurers, EV charging, and mobility IoT operators. Upstream publishes no public developer portal or API; the platform is sold as enterprise SaaS with demo-based onboarding.

providers.name: Vivoo
providers.description: Vivoo is a wellness technology company offering science-backed, at-home urine test strips paired with a mobile app that turns results into personalized nutrition and lifestyle recommendations. Its lineup includes the 8-parameter Vivoo Wellness Test, an at-home UTI test, fertility/ovulation and vaginal pH tests, and a connected Smart Toilet. The direct-to-consumer store runs on Shopify and exposes a native agent-commerce surface: a published llms.txt/agents.md, a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) merchant profile at /.well-known/ucp, and a hosted UCP shopping MCP server for agent-driven catalog search, cart, and buyer-approved checkout. Backed by 500 Global and Techstars.

providers.name: WebPT
providers.description: WebPT is a rehabilitation-therapy software company providing a cloud practice-management platform for physical, occupational, and speech therapy and behavioral-health clinics. Its integrated suite spans clinical documentation and EMR, billing and revenue-cycle management, front-office scheduling and digital patient intake, benefits verification, home exercise programs, patient engagement and outcomes tracking, marketing, and practice analytics. WebPT connects to 60+ EHR and healthcare systems (Epic, athenahealth, Veradigm, McKesson, Meditech, Oracle Cloud, ModMed and others) through an integrations program built on HL7 interfaces (ADT, BAR, DFT, MDM/ORU). WebPT does not publish a public REST API, developer portal, or OpenAPI definition; integration is arranged through its partner and integrations program. WebPT is a Battery Ventures portfolio company.

providers.name: Westlaw
providers.description: Westlaw, a Thomson Reuters legal research platform, provides AI‑enhanced tools, extensive case law, statutes, and practical guidance for law firms, businesses, and government agencies. Leveraging over 175 years of legal expertise, Westlaw delivers trusted research, drafting assistance, and compliance solutions across a wide range of practice areas.

providers.name: x402supply-com
providers.description: x402 Supply provides a suite of pay-per-call API tools designed for AI agents, enabling developers to integrate specialized functionalities such as timezone conversion, token verification, and data extraction on a per-call basis. Operating on the Base blockchain with USDC payments, the platform eliminates the need for traditional API keys or accounts, offering a frictionless, usage‑based billing model. The service catalog includes tools for financial data, compliance checks, and AI‑enhanced utilities, all accessible via simple HTTP endpoints.

providers.name: Zartico
providers.description: Zartico is a Salt Lake City based destination-intelligence software company, founded in 2019, that operates the Zartico Destination Operating System (ZDOS) for destination marketing and management organizations, states, airports, attractions and ski resorts. The platform fuses daily geolocation observations, credit-card spending data, lodging and short-term-rental data, event demand and DMO digital analytics into a single integrated data model, and surfaces it through the Z5 visualization suite, Event Pulse and visitor-journey modules. Zartico publishes no general-purpose developer portal or REST API reference; its public machine-readable surface is an anonymously readable OGC GeoServer estate (WMS 1.3.0, WFS 2.0.0, WCS 2.0.1) at geoserver.zartico.com and two Okta-hosted OpenID Connect / OAuth 2.0 authorization servers at login.zartico.com and platform.zartico.com. Customer-facing integration is inbound rather than outbound - Zartico is granted read access to a destination's Google Analytics, ad server and CRM, and deploys a per-client geolocation attribution pixel.

providers.name: 8base
providers.description: 8base is a comprehensive Backend-as-a-Service platform that transforms the entire software development lifecycle by providing AI-assisted design, auto-generated serverless GraphQL infrastructure powered by AWS, and low-code full-stack App Builder tools. The platform enables developers and digital agencies to build scalable, production-grade cloud applications with SOC 2 and HIPAA compliance options without managing DevOps complexity.

providers.name: adextract
providers.description: adextract provides ad intelligence for AI agents, allowing searches across Meta, Google, TikTok, and LinkedIn ad libraries. The hosted MCP server lets Claude, Hermes, OpenClaw, Codex, Cursor, and other agents retrieve competitor ads in plain language. It normalizes results with advertiser, headline, body, media URLs, dates, and adds structured marketing insights such as creative description, marketing goal, target audience, emotion scores, and industry fields. Users can compare creatives across platforms, with quick setup via a single MCP URL and API key or OAuth, and start with 50 free searches.

providers.name: Adwarp
providers.description: Adwarp is an open-source terminal-based agent that lets you manage LinkedIn Ads and Google Ads via CLI, supporting AI assistants like Claude, Codex, Cursor. It runs locally, requires no spending until you activate campaigns, and is free to use.

providers.name: Aeroz
providers.description: Aeroz provides supply chain traceability and product authentication solutions for regulated goods. Their platform uses NFC/UHF chips and GS1 2D codes to give each unit a unique identity, recording custody events via GS1 EPCIS 2.0. It supports compliance with DSCSA, EU Digital Product Passport, battery regulations, and other global standards, offering a secure, end‑to‑end digital product passport and connected packaging.

providers.name: aetherAI
providers.description: aetherAI (雲象科技, aetherAI Co., Ltd.) is a Taipei-based medical-imaging AI company and one of Asia's leading digital-pathology vendors. It builds regulated diagnostic software for hospitals, reference laboratories and pharmaceutical R&D: aetherSlide, an FDA-cleared (K233126), CE-marked and TFDA-approved whole-slide image management and viewing system; aetherWeb, a cloud digital pathology education platform; aetherAI Hema for bone-marrow smear differential counting; aetherAI Endo for real-time computer-aided polyp detection in colonoscopy; and aetherAI Ortho for whole-spine radiograph measurement. The company was founded in Taiwan, raised NT$765 million in Series B funding led by CDIB Capital, Quanta Computer, Taiwan Business Bank VC and Cathay Venture, listed on Taiwan's Emerging Stock Board in November 2024, holds ISO/IEC 27001 certification, and has filed for the Taiwan Innovation Board. aetherAI publishes no public developer API, no OpenAPI or other machine-readable contract, and no developer portal; its clinical software is sold and deployed through a direct enterprise motion and its application sits behind a customer login. The single publicly callable surface is a Wix-provided Site MCP endpoint on its own domain, which serves website content rather than any clinical product.

providers.name: Agents Wiki
providers.description: Agents Wiki provides a public text knowledge service across topics and languages, allowing external agents to search, contribute, discuss and correct information via an API. The site hosts multilingual content, tracks contributions without cookies, and operates under MK Groups Schweiz in Switzerland. It emphasizes open registration, no advertising, and transparent content provenance.

providers.name: AnonPing
providers.description: AnonPing is an anonymous chat platform for adults that enables random text conversations, friend connections, media sharing, and AI integration via MCP. Users can start chats without email or phone, keep connections, share pictures and voice messages, and post public thoughts in Time Square. The service emphasizes privacy, provides recovery codes, and offers guides on safety, privacy, and community rules.

providers.name: Apache Tez
providers.description: Apache Tez is an application framework that allows for complex directed-acyclic-graph (DAG) based processing of data built on Apache Hadoop YARN. It is designed as a successor to MapReduce for executing Hive and Pig queries, providing a flexible API for creating DAG execution pipelines, in-memory data passing between tasks, and session reuse for reduced startup latency. Apache Tez is an Apache Software Foundation top-level project.

providers.name: APIANT
providers.description: APIANT provides an AI‑driven integration platform that lets users build, test, and run API integrations automatically. The service offers a visual editor, automation and assembly tools, and a marketplace of pre‑built connectors for SaaS applications like Mindbody, Shopify, and many others. Users can start for free, connect their APIs, define workflows, and deploy them to production with monitoring and error handling. APIANT targets SaaS companies, system integrators, and enterprises seeking to accelerate integration development with AI assistance.

providers.name: APIsec
providers.description: APIsec (listed as "Fxlabs" in Canaan Partners' portfolio directory, which resolves to apisec.ai) is an AI-powered API and application security platform that delivers continuous, automated security testing across the full API lifecycle. Rather than only flagging potential issues, APIsec combines threat modeling, attack-surface mapping, and AI-driven exploit validation to prove which vulnerabilities are actually exploitable at runtime — producing replayable evidence and remediation guidance. Its products span the APIsec Platform (continuous scanning and OWASP API Top 10 coverage), apisec Surface (open-source mapping of APIs, endpoints, and AI connections), and a large practitioner community through APIsec University (150,000+ practitioners) and Discord (15,000+ members). The company also publishes open-source security tooling and Agent Skills that embed OWASP API Security Top 10 intelligence directly into AI coding agents such as Cursor, Claude Code, and Copilot.

providers.name: appStrategy
providers.description: appStrategy provides an all‑in‑one data management and AI automation platform that helps enterprises govern, migrate, replicate, and integrate data across cloud and on‑premise environments. Their solutions include AI‑driven automation, data governance, and a suite of connectors for seamless data flow, aiming to accelerate digital transformation and operational efficiency for businesses of all sizes.

providers.name: Archome AI
providers.description: Archome AI provides AI‑powered virtual staging, architectural rendering, and design tools for architects, designers, and real‑estate professionals. The platform offers instant photorealistic renders from sketches, floor plans, or photos, with a suite of AI tools for interior, exterior, material swapping, video creation, and more. Over 750 K users across 180 countries rely on Archome AI to accelerate design workflows, reduce costs, and deliver client‑ready visualizations in seconds. Free trial credits are available without a credit card, and paid plans scale for individuals to enterprises.

providers.name: Auregistre
providers.description: Auregistre provides historical data on French companies from the official commercial register. Users can search for any enterprise, view changes in directors, headquarters, financial statements, and procedural events since its creation or from 2008 for older records. The service aggregates official bulletins and the Sirene directory under an open licence, offering alerts via email for updates on monitored entities.

providers.name: AutoKitteh
providers.description: AutoKitteh is an open-source workflow automation and orchestration platform tailored for developers. It enables creation, management, and monitoring of code-centric automations and durable workflows. AutoKitteh offers built‑in integrations, managed deployments, event‑driven execution, durable fault‑tolerant processing, rich telemetry, and a developer‑first CLI, positioning it as an alternative to no‑code platforms and a complement to Temporal.

providers.name: Beanstalk
providers.description: Beanstalk provides a complete workflow platform for writing, reviewing, and deploying code, supporting both Git and SVN repositories. It offers features like branch management, code reviews, permissions, notifications, and integrations, serving over 70,000 companies worldwide. The service includes pricing plans, support resources, and a status page for operational transparency.

providers.name: Bed Bath And Beyond
providers.description: Bed Bath & Beyond was a chain of domestic merchandise retail stores selling home furnishings, bedding, kitchenware, and other home goods. The company filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in April 2023. The brand was subsequently acquired by Beyond Inc. (formerly Overstock.com), which relaunched Bed Bath & Beyond as an online retail destination. Beyond Inc. also owns Overstock, buybuy BABY, and related brands.

providers.name: BostonGene
providers.description: BostonGene is a Waltham, Massachusetts precision-oncology company that combines an in-house CLIA-certified and CAP-accredited clinical laboratory with an AI-powered bioinformatics platform. It integrates whole-exome and whole-transcriptome sequencing, liquid biopsy (cfDNA/cfRNA), single-cell RNA sequencing, flow cytometry, spatial proteomics and digital pathology into multimodal molecular and immune profiling. Its clinical products include the Tumor Portrait test, immune system profiling, an immunohistochemistry (IHC) test and an Unknown Primary test; its biopharma services cover target analysis, biomarker discovery, clinical trial support, drug indication expansion and unmet-need identification. BostonGene publishes open-source research software (Kassandra cell deconvolution, Molecular Functional Portraits, pyigmap) on GitHub, but exposes no public developer API, SDK or API documentation; clinician ordering and report delivery run through an authenticated Salesforce Experience Cloud customer portal.

providers.name: CAN-TAP Verified
providers.description: CAN-TAP Verified provides Canadian businesses with a verified door badge, a counter tap stand, and an online business record that customers can check. The service offers NFC tap‑to‑review hardware and a searchable evidence profile, enabling easy verification and reputation management across Google Business and other platforms.

providers.name: Causaly
providers.description: Causaly is an agentic AI platform for life sciences R&D, helping pharmaceutical and biotech organizations accelerate drug discovery, target identification, biomarker research, disease pathophysiology analysis, indication expansion, competitive intelligence, and clinical evidence validation. The platform is built on a high-precision biomedical knowledge graph of roughly 500 million facts and 70 million directional relationships across ~5 million biomedical concepts and 150+ ontology categories, paired with a Scientific Information Retrieval System (SIRS) that filters hallucinations. Causaly exposes this graph programmatically through its Bio Graph API (API-token access plus R/Python client libraries), alongside agentic research, Bio Graph, and Pipeline Graph products.

providers.name: Cerapedics
providers.description: Cerapedics is a global, commercial-stage orthobiologics company headquartered in Westminster, Colorado, that develops and commercializes bone repair products built on its proprietary P-15 synthetic small peptide technology — an osteogenic cell-binding peptide discovered in 1996. Its FDA premarket-approved (PMA) products are i-FACTOR Peptide Enhanced Bone Graft, approved in 2015 for single-level anterior cervical discectomy and fusion (ACDF), and PearlMatrix P-15 Peptide Enhanced Bone Graft, approved in 2025 for single-level transforaminal lumbar interbody fusion (TLIF). Cerapedics publishes no public developer program, OpenAPI definition or SDKs; the only machine-readable surface discovered by the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline is an OAuth-protected Model Context Protocol (MCP) server at mcp.cerapedics.com, gated behind the company's Microsoft Entra ID tenant.

providers.name: Cuseum
providers.description: Cuseum is an engagement platform for museums, cultural attractions, nonprofits, and membership organizations. Its core product issues digital membership cards that members save to Apple Wallet and Google Wallet, replacing plastic cards with passes that update in real time and support tap-to-scan entry. Beyond membership, Cuseum offers mobile visitor guides, audio tours, guest passes, loyalty programs, donor engagement, and automated lifecycle communications. It syncs member and donor data with existing CRM, ticketing, and POS systems (Salesforce, HubSpot, Tessitura, Blackbaud, NeonCRM, PatronManager, ACME Ticketing, Ticketure) via CSV upload, SFTP, Zapier, and API-based integrations. Cuseum was part of the Techstars accelerator and serves cultural institutions worldwide.

providers.name: Danu
providers.description: Danu provides a modern astrology platform that calculates full birth charts using the Swiss Ephemeris, tracks planetary transits, and explains the astrological placements behind each reading. The service offers free access to core features and aims to make accurate, personalized astrology accessible to anyone interested in understanding their sky.

providers.name: DaySmart Vet
providers.description: DaySmart Vet provides cloud-based veterinary practice management software that streamlines scheduling, medical records, billing, client communication, and inventory management. The platform integrates AI tools, supports multi-location clinics, and offers extensive integrations for labs, pharmacies, and payment processors, helping veterinary practices improve efficiency and patient care.

providers.name: Didi
providers.description: DiDi Global is a mobility technology platform best known for ride-hailing, taxi-hailing, and enterprise employee travel across China and international markets. DiDi exposes a public developer surface through DiDi Enterprise Services (DDES) — an Open API for corporate travel management covering approval workflows, bills, budget/cost centers, orders, single sign-on, users, roles, and company entities. The DDES API (base URL https://api.es.xiaojukeji.com) is documented at opendocs.xiaojukeji.com/version2024, secured with OAuth 2.0 client_credentials plus per-request signing, and shipped with official Java and Go SDKs under the github.com/didi organization. DiDi is backed by Hillhouse and the SoftBank Vision Fund.

providers.name: DocDriven
providers.description: DocDriven provides a visual API design platform powered by AI, enabling frontend and backend teams to collaboratively create, document, and evolve APIs. The tool offers real‑time collaboration, AI‑assisted code generation, and a unified workspace to keep API specifications, documentation, and implementations in sync, reducing miscommunication and accelerating development cycles.

providers.name: Docugami
providers.description: Docugami provides an AI-powered document automation platform that transforms unstructured business documents into actionable knowledge graphs. Their technology enables enterprises to extract, organize, and act on data locked in contracts, reports, and other files, supporting use cases such as contract lifecycle management, data extraction, and workflow automation. By leveraging proprietary AI, Docugami helps reduce manual effort, improve compliance, and accelerate decision‑making across industries.

providers.name: DroneClear Thailand
providers.description: DroneClear Thailand provides full-service drone registration and compliance in Thailand, handling CAAT and NBTC registration, pilot exam preparation, and liability insurance for visitors. Based in Hua Hin, they offer transparent pricing, detailed guides, and support to ensure safe drone operations under Thai regulations.

providers.name: Essendant
providers.description: Essendant is a national wholesale distributor and third-party logistics provider of workplace products — business and office supplies, furniture, janitorial and breakroom (JanSan), foodservice, industrial and automotive aftermarket items — operating a network of 35+ distribution centers carrying 49,000+ SKUs. Built on the United Stationers, Lagasse Sweet and Azerty brands and owned by Staples since 2019, it sells through independent resellers rather than direct to end users, and its Connected Commerce and Fulfillment Services arms add marketplace access, retail drop-ship, B2C fulfillment and Amazon SFP/FBA prep. Its integration surface is trading-partner EDI and the ECDB product-content feed rather than a public API: no developer portal, OpenAPI, MCP server or agent card is published on any Essendant host.

providers.name: Finaeo
providers.description: Finaeo Inc. is a Toronto-based Canadian insurtech operating a digital marketplace that connects life insurance carriers, independent brokers and their clients. Its platform gives independent life brokers a product marketplace across carriers and hundreds of products, side-by-side product comparison and quoting, a place-a-policy checkout flow with selected carriers, a white-labeled client portal with digital onboarding and custom Financial Needs Assessments, contact and document management, broker landing pages, and team and distributor white-label offerings. Its home market is Canada, with expansion into the United States through IMO and broker-agency partnerships. Line of business is life insurance distribution — Finaeo is a distribution and agency technology vendor, not a risk carrier. Its API posture is honestly one of absence — Finaeo publishes no public developer portal, no API reference, no downloadable OpenAPI or Swagger, and no SDK. No developer, docs or api subdomain resolves in DNS, and a sweep of 2,840 archived first-party URLs turns up no developer surface at all. Finaeo's own carrier marketing explicitly positions its integration story against APIs, describing a "no-code toolkit to digitize products, configure applications, and launch custom workflows" that works "without the need for bulky APIs." The only documented carrier integration is a bilateral, partner-negotiated data handoff (Empire Life Fast & Full Life Application, 2021). Everything else sits behind a broker login or a book-a-demo form, making Finaeo a partner-gated, no-public-API provider.

providers.name: Firefly
providers.description: Firefly Systems Inc. is a data-first moving out-of-home (mOOH) advertising network that turns taxis, rideshare vehicles, and other mobility assets into digital and static advertising surfaces across 15+ major North American markets and several countries. Its network of tens of thousands of GPS-connected screens delivers geo-targeted, contextual, and programmatic digital out-of-home (DOOH) campaigns with advanced tracking, attribution, and measurement. Firefly offers digital and static car tops, full and partial car wraps, in-car TaxiTV, around-car activations, and experiential LED and hologram truck formats. Programmatic demand reaches Firefly inventory through third-party DOOH supply-side platforms rather than a Firefly endpoint — its own advertising-solutions page names Place Exchange, Vistar Media, Hivestack and Broadsign, alongside a VIOOH integration, and supports Programmatic Guaranteed and open-marketplace deals. The company is backed by investors including 500 Global, Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), and GV (Google Ventures).

providers.name: Furhat Robotics
providers.description: Furhat Robotics builds the Furhat social robot, a customizable robotic platform with a back-projected, animated digital face and multi-language voice synthesis designed for natural, multi-party human-robot conversation. Developers build interactions using the Kotlin Skill API and the Furhat SDK (with a Virtual Furhat for desktop development), stream live data through the Realtime API over WebSocket, and rapidly prototype LLM-driven characters with the FurhatAI Creator. A deprecated REST Remote API with an official Python client is also available. Furhat is widely used across academic research, clinical training, mental health, hospitality, and automotive human-machine interaction.

providers.name: Graphite Health
providers.description: Graphite Health is a member-led, non-profit 501(c)(4) health-data infrastructure company founded by Intermountain Health, Presbyterian Healthcare Services and SSM Health, later joined by Kaiser Permanente and Emory Healthcare. It operates a platform that ingests, standardizes and integrates clinical data across member health systems — a connector library for clinical and external systems, a single interoperable data model, managed container runtimes, developer APIs and a data sandbox — and governs the S2 standard, an information standard encoding the operational semantics of health data whose adoption is funded by Gates Ventures. On top of the platform it runs an application marketplace whose apps must be certified under Graphite's Digital Hippocratic Oath. As of this profiling pass Graphite publishes no public developer documentation and no machine-readable contract; its FHIR, platform-core and identity hosts exist in DNS but refuse connections from the public internet.

providers.name: Ground
providers.description: Ground News is a news aggregation platform, built by Snapwise Inc. and backed by Techstars, that helps readers see every side of every story. It gathers coverage of each news event from across the political spectrum and pairs every story with media bias ratings, factuality assessments, and source-ownership transparency. Signature features include the Blindspot Feed that surfaces stories disproportionately covered by the left or right, a per-story bias-distribution bar, local news customization, daily briefing newsletters, browser extensions, and iOS/Android apps. Ground News does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation, and its one live machine surface, api.ground.news, is the private backend of its own apps. The single integration point it does publish is an unauthenticated embeddable iframe story widget. This profile captures that widget, the company's public web and commercial surface, the contract-discovery probe record, and its domain-security posture.

providers.name: Hammerspace
providers.description: Hammerspace, Inc. is a Redwood City, California software company behind the Hammerspace Global Data Platform (formerly the Global Data Environment), a parallel file system and software-defined data platform that unifies unstructured data across on-premises storage, edge sites, and AWS, Azure and Google Cloud into a single global namespace. Data is reached through standard protocols — NFS, pNFS v4.2 with Flex Files, SMB, S3, and CSI for Kubernetes — while placement, replication, tiering, snapshots and retention are driven by declarative objectives rather than by manual data movement. The platform is administered through a GUI, an admin CLI, the open source hstk Python toolkit, Ansible and Terraform automation, and the Anvil metadata server REST API at /mgmt/v1.2/rest. The 2026 AI Data Platform release adds Tier-0 NVMe pooling on GPU servers, Milvus vector search, and a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that exposes enterprise data to AI agents and RAG pipelines.

providers.name: IDOVEN
providers.description: Idoven builds artificial-intelligence solutions for cardiovascular care. Its flagship platform, Willem, is a CE-marked Class IIa medical device that analyzes electrocardiograms (ECGs) to detect, diagnose, and monitor cardiac disease, identifying 22 cardiac patterns and 4 intervals across ambulatory devices, diagnostic ECGs, and insertable cardiac monitors. Idoven serves MedTech companies, Life Sciences (cardiotoxicity monitoring and disease-risk scoring for pharma trials), and preventative remote-screening programs. The Willem API supports bi-directional data exchange in EDF, HL7, DICOM, JSON, XML, and PDF. The company is headquartered in Spain, holds an extensive ISO and IEC certification program, and is backed by Insight Partners and Northzone. Sector: healthcare / cardiology AI.

providers.name: Ingram Micro
providers.description: © 2025 - All Rights Reserved. Ingram Micro Inc. - Privacy Policy | Terms of Use.

providers.name: Juma
providers.description: Juma provides AI-powered marketing automation for agencies and marketing teams, delivering end‑to‑end AI marketing flows that generate ads, reports, SEO articles, carousel creatives, and campaign briefs. The platform integrates with popular advertising and analytics tools, enabling users to create, optimize, and track campaigns with minimal manual effort. Juma offers a free‑to‑start tier and a paid SaaS model, targeting marketers who want to leverage generative AI to accelerate content creation and improve performance.

providers.name: KEBA
providers.description: KEBA provides innovative automation solutions across industrial automation, banking, public services, and energy sectors. Their portfolio includes control panels, HMI interfaces, servo controllers, motors, safety technology, and digital services such as AI assistants and e‑charging solutions. The company focuses on integrating hardware and software to enable efficient, secure, and intelligent automation for factories, ATMs, parcel lockers, and more.

providers.name: Lit Protocol
providers.description: Lit Protocol is a decentralized key management network providing Programmable Key Pairs (PKPs), Lit Actions (off-chain JS execution), threshold encryption, and access-control conditions. The Chipotle Express API exposes account, PKP, and Lit Action management as REST endpoints alongside the JavaScript SDK.

providers.name: Mediakreativ UG
providers.description: Mediakreativ UG provides CalDAVConnect, a service that synchronizes CalDAV calendars with major platforms such as Google Calendar and Microsoft 365. Hosted in Germany, it supports Nextcloud, SOGo, Radicale, Baïkal, Synology, Infomaniak and more, offering GDPR‑compliant calendar syncing for individuals and businesses. Users can start a free trial, choose from various plans, and access comprehensive documentation and support.

providers.name: Mirai
providers.description: Mirai (trymirai.com) is an on-device AI infrastructure company building uzu, a high-performance, Rust-based inference engine that runs large language, text-to-speech, and classification models directly on consumer hardware — Apple Silicon, iOS, macOS, and beyond — with zero inference cost and full data privacy. The uzu SDK exposes a single high-level API across Python, Swift, TypeScript, and Rust, adding speculative decoding, structured output, and built-in performance metrics, plus an optional cloud path for hosted models. Founded by the co-creators of Reface and Prisma and backed by a $10M seed round led by Uncork Capital.

providers.name: National Council on Disability
providers.description: The National Council on Disability (NCD) is an independent federal agency that advises the President, Congress, and other federal agencies on disability policy and programs. Established in 1978, the NCD promotes equal opportunity, economic self-sufficiency, independent living, and full participation in all areas of society for individuals with disabilities. The agency conducts research, gathers information, and provides recommendations to improve policies, programs, and services. NCD publishes policy reports spanning civil rights, healthcare, transportation, employment, housing, and emergency management for people with disabilities.

providers.name: Omada Health
providers.description: Omada Health is a virtual-first healthcare company founded in 2011 and headquartered in San Francisco that delivers integrated, evidence-based care programs for chronic disease management. Omada combines one-on-one health coaching, connected smart devices (cellular scales, blood pressure monitors, glucose meters), interactive lessons, and peer communities to support people managing prediabetes, type 2 diabetes, hypertension, high cholesterol, and musculoskeletal (MSK) conditions, along with GLP-1 medication support and weight health. The company sells to employers, health plans, benefit consultants, and health systems rather than to individual consumers directly, and operates as a HIPAA covered entity and business associate. Omada Health is publicly traded and is a portfolio company of Andreessen Horowitz (a16z). It has no publicly documented developer API surface; this profile captures the company's public identity, security/compliance posture, and operational transparency pages.

providers.name: OpenAny
providers.description: OpenAny is an open marketplace for AI agents operated by Alephant AI LLC in San Francisco. It offers a unified API key and prepaid balance to access a catalog of AI models, data APIs, and portable skills. Users can browse the catalog, read documentation, create an account and API key for free, and pay per use without any subscription. The platform emphasizes one‑key access, usage‑based billing, and integration flexibility for developers building intelligent agents.

providers.name: Oxford Nanopore Technologies
providers.description: Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) develops and sells portable real-time DNA and RNA sequencing devices, consumables, and analysis software. Their platform enables researchers to sequence long reads directly from biological samples, supporting applications from genomics and transcriptomics to clinical diagnostics and environmental monitoring. ONT’s technology combines nanopore hardware, flow cells, library preparation kits, and cloud‑based informatics to deliver fast, scalable sequencing solutions worldwide.

providers.name: Pinboard
providers.description: Pinboard is a social bookmarking service designed for introverts, allowing users to save, tag, and share web pages. It offers a simple, read‑only API for retrieving bookmarks, adding new ones, managing tags, and searching. The service emphasizes privacy, minimalism, and long‑term storage, and provides paid plans for unlimited bookmarks. Its API documentation is publicly available at https://pinboard.in/api/.

providers.name: Preciser
providers.description: Preciser is an AI and computer-vision sports analytics platform that automatically converts basketball and baseball game footage into statistics, trends, and player insights, removing the traditionally manual work of video tagging. Its three-part product covers Capture (InstaStats converts video to stats), Analyze (a Data Management System that generates statistics and insights), and Monetize (APIs that expose live stats feeds and widgets). The Preciser API advertises game chart-data and opponent-team-data endpoints under https://plg-api.preciser.io/v1. The company reports roughly 85% average accuracy, a two-hour average turnaround per game, and 10x faster analysis than manual tagging. Preciser is backed by 500 Global and the NVIDIA Inception Program.

providers.name: Quantilia
providers.description: Quantilia is a Nice, France based financial data and portfolio reporting platform for institutional investors, family offices, asset managers, private banks, insurance companies and corporates and endowments. It aggregates fragmented investment data from custodian banks, fund administrators, fund managers, private equity and real estate GPs, ESG score providers and benchmark vendors such as MSCI and Bloomberg, then extracts, tests, categorizes, standardizes, labels, enriches and controls it into a single auditable reporting layer with full financial data lineage. Products cover tailored portfolio monitoring, multi-source data aggregation, security-level and private equity lookthrough, structured products monitoring, ESG and risk reports, quantitative analysis, document generation and AI services, with regulatory output for Solvency II, QRT, COREP, CRR3, SFDR, PAI and LEC29. Delivery is via dashboards, report packs, Excel, PDF and API feeds. The company states ISO-27001 certification, GDPR and DORA compliance, and EU/Swiss based hosting. No public developer portal, API reference or machine-readable specification is published; the API surface is delivered to contracted clients.

providers.name: Rentec Direct
providers.description: Rentec Direct provides property management software with a REST API for managing rental properties, tenant screening, online payments, maintenance requests, and financial reporting. The Open API (v3) is available to all Pro and PM plan subscribers at no additional cost, enabling workflow automation, data analysis, and custom application development.

providers.name: Rime
providers.description: Rime is a realtime text-to-speech platform optimized for low-latency conversational agents. Models include Arcana v3, Arcana v2, Mist v3, and Mist v2. The TTS API supports streaming HTTP, WebSocket (binary and JSON), Server-Sent Events, and JSON envelopes for MP3, mu-law, OGG, and WAV audio.

providers.name: Satisfi Labs
providers.description: Satisfi Labs is an agentic AI platform for the sports, entertainment, and tourism industries, delivering specialized conversational AI agents that are built and tuned by industry experts to sell more tickets, scale guest support, improve the fan and visitor experience, and collect first-party customer data.
