There is no open, self-service public REST API: machine control runs over an MQTT interface (us/cn.mqtt.bambulab.com:8883, TLS, authenticated with a Bambu account user id and MQTT token), and a firmware-level "printer control authorization" mechanism now gates binding, firmware updates, camera streams, and print/movement commands. Third parties integrate through Bambu Connect, LAN Developer Mode, or by applying for SDK access; the practical API surface today is community-reverse-engineered (OpenBambuAPI, Bambu-Lab-Cloud-API, and Python/Rust client libraries). Added to the API Evangelist network from the IDG Capital portfolio and enriched from public sources.

providers.name: bidrover-com
providers.description: BidRover provides a searchable directory of public government contracts, RFPs, grants, subcontracting notices and international tenders, matching them to the services a business sells. It aggregates data from 137 official sources across the United States, 47 countries and multiple international organizations, and offers free browsing and weekly email alerts, with a paid Team plan for deeper match scoring and collaboration tools.

providers.name: Boulder Care
providers.description: Boulder Care is a Portland, Oregon telehealth provider founded in 2017 by Stephanie Strong that delivers evidence-based outpatient treatment for opioid and alcohol use disorder entirely through a mobile app. Participants connect to a collaborative care team — addiction medicine clinicians, peer recovery specialists and care coordinators — over secure video and messaging, and are prescribed medications for addiction treatment including buprenorphine/naloxone (Suboxone), naltrexone (Revia, Vivitrol) and acamprosate (Campral). The company focuses on Medicaid beneficiaries and other historically underserved populations, contracts with health plans, health systems, employers and correctional and jail-based referral partners, and has served more than 12,000 participants across states including Oregon, Washington, Colorado, North Carolina, New Mexico, Ohio and Michigan. Boulder Care raised a $35M Series C in 2024 led by Advance Venture Partners. It ships software only as an end-user patient product: there is no developer portal, no published API documentation, no SDK and no machine-readable specification anywhere on its public surface.

providers.name: Brigit
providers.description: Brigit is a fintech company offering cash advances, credit building, and financial management tools to help everyday Americans avoid overdraft fees, build credit, and save money. Their mobile app provides instant cash, credit builder, budgeting assistance, and personalized financial guidance, serving over 15 million users.

providers.name: Chucho
providers.description: Chucho provides digital guest guides for vacation rentals, enabling hosts to offer multilingual, AI‑enhanced information to their guests. The platform lets property owners create free public listings, customize guide content, and compare plans for their properties, improving guest experience and operational efficiency.

providers.name: Curalate
providers.description: Curalate provides a visual commerce platform that enables brands and retailers to harness user‑generated content, shoppable photos, and influencer marketing to drive sales. After being acquired by Bazaarvoice, Curalate’s technology integrates with Bazaarvoice’s suite to deliver social commerce solutions, allowing shoppers to purchase directly from images and videos across web and mobile experiences. The platform offers analytics, content moderation, and campaign tools for marketers seeking authentic, visual-driven engagement.

providers.name: DeckSpace
providers.description: DeckSpace provides an AI‑powered platform for creating presentations, diagrams, and dashboards. Users can start from templates, craft content with AI assistance, refine their work, and share it from a single home. The service offers free starter plans, integrates with ChatGPT and Claude, and supports exporting decks for collaboration. It aims to streamline visual storytelling and data storytelling for individuals and teams.

providers.name: DeepStream Technologies
providers.description: DeepStream Technologies (deep.stream) is a London-based AI-enhanced eSourcing and source-to-contract platform for mid-market procurement teams. It digitalizes buyer-to-supplier sourcing with best-of-breed eRFx, supplier discovery, supplier pre-qualification, eAuctions, contract management, management reporting, and AI-driven RFP generation and conversational analytics, aiming to help procurement teams work faster, reduce risk, and gain visibility while keeping implementation simple. Customers include Walkers Shortbread, BrewDog, Abbott, and Free Now. DeepStream does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer documentation; integrations with ERP and PO systems are delivered as a service. This profile was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and enriched with public company and infrastructure signals.

providers.name: DICE
providers.description: DICE is a live music and events ticketing platform (dice.fm) connecting fans to gigs, club nights, festivals, and experiences, with a fan-facing mobile app and a partner platform (MIO) for promoters, venues, and festivals. For partners, DICE exposes a documented but access-gated GraphQL API - the Ticket Holders API at partners-endpoint.dice.fm/graphql - that lets downstream systems query events, tickets and ticket holders, orders and sales, returns and transfers, fans, and venues. API tokens are generated inside MIO and passed as a Bearer authorization header; the API is available to DICE partners rather than as an open self-service developer program.

providers.name: Doxy.me
providers.description: Doxy.me provides a simple, free, and secure telehealth platform that enables healthcare providers to conduct video visits with patients without the need for downloads or installations. The service supports up to one million providers worldwide, offering HIPAA‑compliant video, screen sharing, and chat features. Users can sign up in under a minute, and the platform emphasizes privacy, ease of use, and integration with existing practice workflows.

providers.name: Ellipsis Labs
providers.description: Ellipsis Labs builds decentralized finance applications and infrastructure on Solana. Its flagship product is Phoenix, a fully on-chain, atomically-settled limit order book exchange for spot assets, now expanded with Phoenix Perps for on-chain perpetual futures. The team also develops Atlas (a high-performance DeFi Layer 2), Gavel (token distribution and liquidity bootstrapping), and Plasma (a sandwich-resistant AMM reference implementation). Ellipsis exposes its protocol to developers through open-source SDKs (TypeScript, Rust, Python), command-line tools, and on-chain Solana programs rather than a hosted REST API. Backed by Electric Capital and Paradigm.

providers.name: elvex
providers.description: Elvex provides an enterprise AI agent platform that enables teams across various functions—such as IT, HR, operations, marketing, and sales—to build, share, and control AI-driven agents. The platform offers a library of pre‑built agents, customizable integrations, security controls, and tools for rapid deployment, allowing organizations to automate workflows, enhance decision‑making, and improve productivity. Elvex’s solutions cater to industries including technology, publishing, insurance, consulting, legal, financial services, healthcare, and media, delivering a comprehensive AI‑powered experience for modern enterprises.

providers.name: Forma
providers.description: Forma is a flexible employee benefits platform, founded in 2017, that lets companies design, customize, and scale employee spending accounts from a single system. Employers select from a suite of Lifestyle Spending Accounts (LSA), Health Spending Accounts (HSA), Health Reimbursement Arrangements (HRA), and Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA), and employees access benefits through the Forma Store, the Forma Visa Card, or reimbursement claims. Forma connects to employer systems through 40+ HRIS and payroll integrations (Workday, ADP, UKG, Paylocity), SCIM provisioning, SAML2 SSO, and file feeds. Forma does not publish a public developer REST API; its technical surface is HRIS/SSO/SCIM integration and its trust posture (SOC 2 Type 2, HIPAA, GDPR). Backed by Emergence Capital, Ribbit Capital, and Uncork Capital.

providers.name: gpu.nz
providers.description: gpu.nz provides on-demand GPU server rentals and graphics card access via a RESTful API. Users can browse available GPU models, pricing, and regions, then rent servers by the minute for workloads such as AI model training, rendering, and inference. The platform offers a command‑line interface and a streamable MCP endpoint for AI agents, supporting both ruble and dollar billing. Documentation includes quickstart guides, API reference, CLI usage, and integration examples for developers and AI agents.

providers.name: junct-dev
providers.description: Junct is an agent‑readiness platform that converts any API specification into ready‑to‑use tools for leading AI agent frameworks such as Claude, GPT, LangChain and five others. By uploading OpenAPI, contract ABI, llms.txt, or Etherscan URLs, users instantly receive generated tools—over 1,200 tools hosted across 30 MCP servers. The service simplifies integration of web APIs into AI agents, offering a one‑line configuration to turn APIs into actionable agents.

providers.name: Linte
providers.description: Linte is a Brazilian legal-technology company offering an AI-powered contract lifecycle management (CLM) platform for large enterprises. Its product family spans Linte CLM for document automation and contract lifecycle governance, Linte AI for contract review that summarizes versions and flags risk against a customer playbook, Linte BI for contract analytics dashboards, and Linte Intake for legal demand intake and triage. The platform integrates natively with digital signature providers including ClickSign, DocuSign and D4Sign, and is sold to enterprise legal, procurement and compliance teams primarily in Brazil. Linte publishes no public API program, developer portal or API reference; its only public developer-facing artifacts are npm-published embeddable "Linte Docs" form components.

providers.name: Lunar Outpost
providers.description: Lunar Outpost is a space robotics company founded in 2017 and headquartered in Golden, Colorado, with additional operations in Australia and Luxembourg. It builds lunar surface mobility and robotic infrastructure — the MAPP (Mobile Autonomous Prospecting Platform) rover, which operated at the lunar South Pole in 2025 as the first commercial rover on another planetary body, and the Eagle and Pegasus Lunar Terrain Vehicles developed for NASA's Artemis programme. Alongside the hardware it ships an integrated mission-operations software suite: Stargate, a spaceflight-proven command, control and communication platform that reached TRL 9 with 99.998% uptime on Lunar Voyage 1; Starweave (formerly MARS), a distributed autonomy and mesh-networking layer built under AFRL and AFWERX contract for coordinating heterogeneous robotic fleets in GPS-denied environments; and Spark, an AI mission-operations assistant. None of these products expose a public API, developer portal or machine-readable specification — Lunar Outpost sells to government and defence customers rather than through a self-serve developer channel. Its only public machine-readable surfaces are a Wix platform-generated llms.txt and an unauthenticated site MCP endpoint.

providers.name: Melty
providers.description: Melty is a French digital media brand for youth culture — news and entertainment coverage of series, cinema, television, celebrity, gaming and lifestyle aimed at a 15-34 audience. Founded in 2008 in Paris and operated by EEPLE SAS, Melty was a Serena Capital portfolio company before Reworld Media acquired 100% of the business in a distressed M&A process completed in 2021-2022; melty.fr is now published by EEPLE within Groupe Reworld Media and monetised through advertising and native content rather than software licensing. Melty publishes no developer program, no public API product and no machine-readable API contract. Its only public developer surface is the meltygroup GitHub organisation, which carries the identity servers Kisee and Pasee — MIT-licensed, self-hosted Python HTTP API servers written in-house and released to PyPI, last published in 2021.

providers.name: Mountain Protocol
providers.description: Mountain Protocol is the issuer of USDM, a regulated, institutional-grade yield-bearing stablecoin backed by short-term US Treasury securities that pays daily rewards to holders through an ERC20 rebasing token. The company operated a Primary-User account platform with a private REST API for depositing and withdrawing USDM and USDC, querying account balances, and checking USDC liquidity, alongside on-chain proof-of-reserves and a smart-contract security program audited by OpenZeppelin with an Immunefi bug bounty. As of 2025 the protocol entered an orderly wind-down: the primary market closed on August 22, 2025, redemptions moved to secondary markets, and Phase 3 provides on-chain proof-of-reserves so holders can independently verify USDM backing. Backed by Multicoin Capital.

providers.name: NoCodeAPI Pte. Ltd.
providers.description: NoCodeAPI Pte. Ltd. provides a no‑code integration platform that turns popular SaaS services such as Google Sheets, Airtable, Google Analytics, Twitter, and many more into secure, ready‑to‑call API endpoints. Users can create projects, configure authentication once, and call generated endpoints without writing backend code, enabling rapid prototyping, automation, and AI‑driven workflows. The service offers a marketplace of pre‑built connectors, pricing tiers, and a developer portal for documentation and support.

providers.name: OneDev
providers.description: OneDev is an autonomous development platform that integrates Git repository hosting, issue tracking, pull requests, CI/CD pipelines, package management, wikis, and AI‑assisted workflows. It enables teams to manage the full software development lifecycle in a single self‑hosted application, offering both community and enterprise editions with extensible plugins and customizable automation.

providers.name: Pasqal
providers.description: Pasqal is a French neutral-atom quantum computing company headquartered in Palaiseau, France and co-founded in 2019 by 2022 Physics Nobel Laureate Alain Aspect. Pasqal builds commercial-grade neutral-atom quantum processors (the Fresnel QPU family) that use arrays of laser-trapped Rydberg atoms to run both analog and digital quantum programs, and packages them as on-premise systems and as Pasqal Cloud Services — a pay-as-you-go quantum computing platform also distributed through Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure Quantum, OVHcloud, and AWS partners. The developer surface is anchored by Pulser, the open-source (Apache-2.0) Python library for pulse-level/analog programming of neutral-atom devices, the pasqal-cloud Python SDK for submitting Pulser sequences and workloads to QPUs and emulators, and the Pasqal Cloud Services REST API (with Auth0-based authentication and v1/v2 endpoints for batches, jobs, devices, workloads, projects, members, billing, and OVH integrations). The broader ecosystem includes Qadence (digital-analog programming), Pulser Studio (no-code visual programming), the EMU-MPS and EMU-SV GPU-accelerated emulators, and quantum application libraries — QEK (Quantum Evolution Kernel for graph ML), QUBO-Solver, Maximum-Independent-Set, and QoolQit (Rydberg analog algorithm development). Pasqal serves 35+ commercial engagements across energy, finance, logistics, automotive, and pharma — including BMW, Thales, Capgemini, Sumitomo, Aramco, CMA CGM, and KAIST — and partners with NVIDIA (CUDA-Q), IBM, Google, and Microsoft. In May 2026 Pasqal demonstrated logical qubits outperforming physical qubits on differential equations, and in March 2026 announced 340M+ euros of new financing ahead of going public via business combination with Bleichroeder Acquisition Corp II.

providers.name: Paua
providers.description: Paua is a UK business EV charging platform that consolidates public, home, and workplace electric-vehicle charging into a single EV charge card, driver app, and fleet dashboard, with one monthly invoice across the UK's 95,000+ charging connectors. Paua offers products including Paua Access, Paua Reimburse, Paua Share, Paua PRO, and Salary Sacrifice charging, and exposes partner and Paua Pro APIs for fleet charging data (charging history, costs, energy, timestamps) and chargepoint location data. API access is not public - it is provided to partners and Paua Pro customers after a technical discussion. Paua is backed by Seedcamp and Speedinvest.

providers.name: PikaPods
providers.description: PikaPods provides a platform for managing and distributing smart pet accessories, focusing on IoT-enabled pet care solutions. The company offers APIs for device provisioning, real-time telemetry, and integration with third‑party services such as payment processors and analytics platforms. Their services aim to simplify pet owners’ interaction with smart devices, enabling automated feeding, health monitoring, and activity tracking through a unified developer experience.

providers.name: pnpm
providers.description: pnpm is a fast, disk space efficient package manager for JavaScript and Node.js projects. It uses a content-addressable store and a strict, symlinked node_modules layout so every version of every package is stored exactly once on disk and projects can only access dependencies they explicitly declare. pnpm provides first-class monorepo support via pnpm-workspace.yaml, the workspace protocol, Catalogs, package filtering, and a shared lockfile, and ships supply-chain safety features such as minimumReleaseAge, opt-in lifecycle scripts, dependency overrides, and a built-in patch workflow. Developed in the open under the MIT license on GitHub with an Open Collective sponsorship model, pnpm is used by major JavaScript projects including Next.js, Vue, Vite, Nuxt, Material UI, Prisma, Astro, and SvelteKit.

providers.name: Preamble
providers.description: Preamble provides cybersecurity and compliance solutions for generative AI, protecting against prompt injections, data leakage, and regulatory risks. Their platform offers policy enforcement, monitoring, and risk assessment tools tailored for AI developers and enterprises, ensuring safe and trustworthy AI deployments across various industries.

providers.name: Presentations.ai
providers.description: Presentations.ai is an AI-powered presentation platform that turns ideas, documents, and data into professional, on-brand slide decks in minutes and exports fully editable PowerPoint files. The product markets programmatic deck generation via a REST API and webhooks, no-code Zapier and Make connectors, white-label embedding, and data-source connections to Salesforce, HubSpot, Google Sheets, Snowflake, and 50+ others, though it publishes no public developer documentation or API reference. Backed by Accel, the company operates under Singapore terms of service.

providers.name: Quartet Health
providers.description: Quartet Health is a value-based behavioral healthcare enablement and delivery platform that identifies, engages, and connects patients with mental health services across 39 states. It serves health plans, health systems, and community mental health centers with care coordination, patient-to-provider matching, and direct delivery of behavioral health care through its own medical group, focused on whole-person care for individuals with serious mental illness and other behavioral health needs. Quartet was acquired by NeuroFlow. Added to the API Evangelist network as a life-sciences company profile; the public site exposes no developer or API surface, but does publish a substantive security and compliance program.

providers.name: Ratify
providers.description: Ratify is a CNCF Sandbox open-source verification framework for container images and other supply chain artifacts in Kubernetes environments. It enables policy-driven artifact ratification by coordinating any number of pluggable verifiers (signatures, SBOMs, scan results, attestations) against a given policy, integrating with Kubernetes admission webhooks via the Gatekeeper policy engine. Ratify is developed by the ratify-project GitHub organization (originally a Microsoft open-source project), written in Go, and distributed as a CLI tool, Go library, and Kubernetes admission webhook server. It supports OCI-compliant artifact stores including Azure Container Registry, Amazon ECR, and Docker Hub. Ratify exposes an internal HTTP verification API (v2alpha1) consumed by its webhook server but does not publish a public-facing REST API or OpenAPI specification.

providers.name: Revibe
providers.description: Revibe (Revibe Technology FZ-LLC) is a UAE-based e-commerce marketplace for certified refurbished and renewed electronics — iPhones, Samsung phones, MacBooks, laptops, iPads, TVs, and accessories — sold with a 12-month warranty, a 10-day return window, free UAE delivery, and buy-now-pay-later options (Tabby, Tamara, Split). Every device passes a 50-point quality check and the company reports accepting only one in four supplier lots. Revibe operates in the UAE (revibe.me), Saudi Arabia (sa.revibe.me), and South Africa (revibe.co.za), and runs a trade-in program (sell.revibe.me). The storefront is built on Shopify and natively implements the Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP, ucp.dev), exposing a hosted MCP endpoint for agent-driven catalog search, cart, and human-approved checkout, plus a published /llms.txt and Shopify Customer Account OpenID Connect discovery. Backed by Partech.

providers.name: runrelay-io
providers.description: RunRelay provides a real-time travel execution platform that enables banks, fintechs, and AI agents to search, book, and manage flights, hotels, payments, and logistics through a single API. The service combines automated booking with human concierge support 24/7, offering white-label solutions that can be integrated quickly into banking and platform products. RunRelay’s API delivers live pricing, reservation management, and ancillary services such as eSIM travel, insurance, and lounge access, all backed by a human fallback for complex edge cases. The platform is built for high-volume, enterprise-grade integrations and supports compliance and security standards required by financial institutions.

providers.name: Seerr (Overseerr + Jellyseerr)
providers.description: Seerr is a free, open‑source request‑management and media discovery platform that unifies the capabilities of Overseerr and Jellyseerr. It enables users of Jellyfin, Plex and Emby to request, discover and organize media content through a modern web interface, supporting integrations with Radarr, Sonarr and other automation tools.

providers.name: Starfish Space
providers.description: Starfish Space is a satellite-servicing company founded in 2019 by Trevor Bennett and Austin Link and headquartered in the Seattle, Washington area (Tukwila). It builds Otter, a small, low-cost, electrically propelled servicing vehicle that performs autonomous rendezvous, proximity operations and docking (RPOD) with satellites that were never designed to be serviced — extending their life, relocating them, or disposing of them at end of mission. Its Otter Pup demonstration missions target the first-ever commercial satellite docking in low Earth orbit, and the company has been awarded a $54.5M U.S. Space Force contract for a dedicated Otter servicing vehicle. Starfish Space publishes no developer product API; the machine-readable surface catalogued here is the public WordPress REST API and the OAuth-protected Model Context Protocol (MCP) server served from starfishspace.com.

providers.name: SynergySuite
providers.description: SynergySuite is a back-of-house restaurant management platform for multi-unit and enterprise restaurant operators, founded in 2011 and operating across the United States, United Kingdom and Ireland. The suite covers inventory and purchasing, recipe and food costing, food safety and HACCP checklists, labor scheduling, cash management, human resources and business intelligence, delivered through a web interface and mobile applications. Its operational value depends on integration: SynergySuite ingests sales and order data from point-of-sale platforms including Toast, PAR Brink, NCR Aloha, Appetize by SpotOn and Oracle MICROS Simphony, and exchanges data with accounting, payroll, supplier and HR systems over POS integrations, EDI and data services. That integration surface is operated as a first-class product — it is monitored as named components on the company status page — but the API contract and reference are distributed through a partner portal that requires a login rather than a public developer site.

providers.name: The Andersons
providers.description: The Andersons, Inc. (NASDAQ: ANDE) is a diversified North American agribusiness headquartered in Maumee, Ohio and founded in 1947, operating across four segments: Agribusiness / commodity merchandising through The Andersons Trade Group grain elevators and terminals, Nutrient & Industrial through The Andersons Plant Nutrient Group and its turf and specialty products, Renewables through its ethanol production and marketing joint ventures, and premium food and pet-food ingredients. The company publishes NO public developer API, no developer portal, no OpenAPI or other machine-readable contract, and no SDKs. Its customer-facing digital surface is a set of authenticated end-user applications — the GRAINweb grain account portal, the Farm2Market SmartTicket delivery-ticket web app at andersonstickets.com, the AndeConnect and Trade Group mobile apps (the AndeConnect app is operated on the company's behalf by the ag platform vendor Bushel), and portal.andersonsinc.com account management — all federated through an Active Directory Federation Services identity provider at portalauth.andersonsinc.com. Business-to-business integration is handled through EDI and direct merchant relationships rather than a self-service API. NOTE ON IDENTITY: the domain andersons.com belongs to Anderson's of White Bear Lake, Minnesota, an unrelated prom and school-spirit party-supply retailer; The Andersons, Inc. is at andersonsinc.com.

providers.name: Wealthfront
providers.description: Wealthfront is an automated investment service offering REST APIs and integrations for portfolio management, financial planning, tax optimization, direct indexing, and cash account management. Founded in 2008 and headquartered in Palo Alto, California, Wealthfront manages approximately $95 billion in assets for over 1.4 million clients as of 2026. The platform provides automated investing with tax-loss harvesting, direct indexing for accounts over $100,000, high-yield cash management accounts with FDIC insurance up to $8 million, and stock investing with no advisory fees. Wealthfront went public on Nasdaq (WLTH) in December 2025.

providers.name: whatagentsbuy-com
providers.description: What Agents Buy provides independent reviews and data on x402 APIs that power agentic commerce. It aggregates transaction data from multiple blockchain networks, offers a live dashboard of USDC payments, and publishes detailed receipts and analyses for developers and researchers. The platform aims to increase transparency in the emerging AI‑driven commerce ecosystem by delivering open data and insights.

providers.name: Winc
providers.description: Winc is a direct-to-consumer online wine club and retailer (winc.com) offering curated, personalized wine subscriptions and single-bottle purchases matched to a member's palate profile. The winc.com storefront runs on Shopify and exposes a modern agentic-commerce surface: a hosted UCP (Universal Commerce Protocol) MCP endpoint, Shopify Customer Account API authentication (OpenID Connect), and published /llms.txt and /agents.md agent instructions that let AI shopping assistants discover the catalog, build carts, and drive buyer-approved checkout. Originally surfaced as a VC portfolio company and enriched from its public agent-facing surface by the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: A-du, LLC
providers.description: A-du is a marketplace built around Accessory Dwelling Units (ADUs), operating in Los Angeles County, San Francisco, San Diego County and New York City. Rent or list a permit-verified ADU, a house or a room; manage the tenancy; or choose a pre-approved ADU plan, test it on your lot, estimate permit fees and hire licensed professionals directly. A-du does not design, permit or build ADUs.

providers.name: AdCab
providers.description: AdCab (Адкаб) — коннектор MCP: подключите рекламные кабинеты Яндекс Директа, VK и Авито к Claude или ChatGPT. Сбор семантики, запуск кампаний, статистика и чистка площадок РСЯ прямо в чате. Любое изменение применяется только после вашего подтверждения.

providers.name: Agentsvc
providers.description: Agentsvc.io is a pay‑per‑call API marketplace that enables AI agents to purchase a wide range of web services on demand. It offers over 127 endpoints covering web scraping, content summarization, data extraction, citation, document conversion, compliance checks, crypto data, and more, all billed in USDC across multiple blockchains. The platform requires no account or API key, providing instant access via the x402 payment protocol.

providers.name: Aidoc
providers.description: Aidoc is a clinical artificial intelligence company whose aiOS platform runs, orchestrates, and governs FDA-cleared clinical AI across health systems. Its modules span radiology, cardiology, neurovascular, and vascular care — detecting acute findings (stroke, pulmonary embolism, brain aneurysm, incidental findings) and coordinating care teams at the point of care. aiOS is a vendor-neutral platform that runs both Aidoc and third-party algorithms and integrates into existing hospital IT stacks (PACS, EHR, mobile) using standard healthcare interoperability protocols (DICOM, HL7, FHIR) rather than a public developer REST API. Aidoc reports adoption across more than 1,600 medical centers worldwide. Surfaced as a general-catalyst portfolio company and enriched here for security posture, interoperability conformance, and identity; no public developer API surface is published.

providers.name: alternativeassetliteracy-com
providers.description: Alternative Asset Literacy provides research‑backed educational content on alternative asset classes, decentralized finance, behavioral economics, and gender‑focused investing. The platform offers modules, quizzes, glossaries, and tools to help investors build knowledge, assess risk, and make informed decisions across private equity, real estate, art, crypto, and ESG assets.

providers.name: Amkor Technology
providers.description: Amkor Technology is the world's largest US-based provider of outsourced semiconductor packaging and test services (OSAT), serving integrated device manufacturers, fabless semiconductor companies, and contract foundries. The company offers advanced packaging technologies including flip chip, wafer-level packaging, 2.5D/3D TSV, System-in-Package, and chiplet integration solutions for AI, automotive, communications, computing, consumer electronics, industrial, IoT, and networking markets.

providers.name: Amtrak
providers.description: Amtrak (the National Railroad Passenger Corporation) is the federally chartered operator of the United States national intercity passenger rail network, headquartered in Washington, D.C. It runs the Northeast Corridor including Acela, the state-supported corridors, the long-distance network, and the Amtrak Thruway Connecting Service bus network, and its published GTFS feed covers 61 routes, 646 stops, 2,948 trips and 20 operating agencies across the United States and into Canada. In the distribution chain Amtrak sits as a GDS-intermediated supplier of its own inventory: its content reaches third-party booking tools through Travelport Universal API, through Sabre, Apollo and Worldspan on the RailAgent channel, and through rail aggregators including SilverRail, Travelfusion and RailKey Technologies, alongside its own amtrak.com, mobile app and call centre. Its API posture is honestly stated as one open-standard data feed and nothing else. The only machine-readable contract Amtrak publishes is a static GTFS schedule archive at content.amtrak.com, which is completely ungated - no key, no registration, no click-through - but which Amtrak advertises nowhere: there is no developer portal, no documentation page, no OpenAPI, no AsyncAPI, no GraphQL, and no published terms of use for the feed. Everything transactional is closed. The developer., docs., data. and partners. subdomains of amtrak.com do not resolve, developers.amtrak.com resolves only to a Microsoft Entra application proxy, api.amtrak.com answers 401 on every path from Akamai NetStorage, and www.amtrak.com returns 403 to every non-browser client, so no first-party terms of service could be retrieved programmatically. A developer who wants shopping, booking, payment, ticketing or servicing does not sign up; they are accredited through Travelport or an aggregator, complete an Amtrak test-case worksheet, pass a three-week UAT, and commit to supporting Amtrak refund fees and eVoucher issuance before production credentials are issued.

providers.name: Apryse
providers.description: Apryse provides document processing technology for developers, offering SDKs for web, server, mobile, and data capture. Their platform enables creating, editing, converting, and securing PDFs and other documents, with integrations for Salesforce, Mendix, and more. Apryse (formerly PDFTron) focuses on developer-friendly APIs and tools to embed viewing, editing, and advanced document features into applications.

providers.name: AskAiRank
providers.description: AskAiRank provides an AI Visibility Tracker platform for SaaS founders and marketers, enabling them to monitor how their brand appears across AI-powered search and chat interfaces such as ChatGPT, Google AI, and other large language model platforms. The service offers product features like AI visibility tracking, brand monitoring, citation tracking, competitor analysis, and website scanning, with a free 3‑day trial followed by paid plans starting at $19 per month. The platform aims to help companies understand and improve their AI-driven discoverability and reputation.

providers.name: Atsena Therapeutics
providers.description: Atsena Therapeutics is a clinical-stage gene therapy company based in Durham, North Carolina, in the Research Triangle, developing first- and best-in-class genetic medicines for inherited retinal diseases with the goal of reversing or preventing blindness. Founded by ocular gene therapy pioneers Shannon Boye and Sanford Boye, the company builds on two proprietary AAV delivery platforms: a laterally spreading AAV.SPR capsid engineered to reach retinal cells without the surgical trauma of a subretinal bleb, and a dual-vector technology that splits genes too large for a single AAV across two vectors. Its clinical pipeline includes ATSN-201 for X-linked retinoschisis (XLRS) in a pivotal Phase 3 trial, ATSN-101 for LCA1 (Leber congenital amaurosis 1) advancing to a pivotal trial with partner Nippon Shinyaku, and IND-enabling programs ATSN-301 for Usher syndrome 1B and ATSN-401 for Stargardt disease. Atsena runs no developer program and publishes no product API, no developer documentation and no specification of its own. The only machine-readable surface it exposes is the anonymously readable WordPress REST content API behind atsenatx.com, which serves the company's press releases, program and platform pages, and media library as JSON; the OpenAPI in this repo is derived by API Evangelist from that surface's own live route index.

providers.name: Avery Dennison
providers.description: Avery Dennison is a global materials science and manufacturing company specializing in the design and manufacture of labeling and functional materials, packaging, and intelligent labels. Its RFID and digital-identification business runs atma.io, a connected product cloud that assigns digital IDs to physical items and underpins its Digital Product Passport offering; the atma.io API is gated behind an OAuth 2.0 login and no public contract is published.

providers.name: Avision
providers.description: Avision is airspace infrastructure for drone and Advanced Air Mobility operations. The platform delivers FAA airspace services — LAANC flight authorizations, B4UFLY airspace awareness, TFRs, NOTAMs, and advisory information — alongside UTM / U-space coordination and prioritization for safely integrating uncrewed aircraft into national airspace. Avision serves commercial Part 107 pilots, recreational (Section 44809) flyers, public-safety and first-responder agencies, airports, and critical-infrastructure operators through web and mobile apps, with a flexible REST API integration offered to enterprise customers and drone manufacturers. The company holds an FAA LOA for BVLOS operations and has completed a UTM production rollout in Switzerland.

providers.name: besot
providers.description: Besot is a catalog of fandom style across the resale market, indexing resale listings for clothing designed, worn, or inspired by notable people. It provides lineage and source information for each piece, offering a searchable database for fans and collectors to discover the origins of fashion items.

providers.name: BizPlanner
providers.description: BizPlanner provides an AI‑powered financial flight simulator for entrepreneurs, allowing users to input their business numbers and instantly see cash‑flow projections, break‑even analysis, and funding requirements. The platform offers free plan creation without signup, detailed reports for banks or investors, and a suite of tools to test viability before committing resources. It aims to give clear financial clarity, helping founders pivot or proceed with confidence.

providers.name: Blink
providers.description: Blink is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: vc-portfolio; backed by lightspeed-venture-partners) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.

providers.name: BlockSec
providers.description: BlockSec is a Web3 security and compliance platform offering smart contract audits, infrastructure audits, blockchain penetration testing, AML/CFT compliance tools, and real‑time threat detection. Founded to protect decentralized applications and crypto enterprises, BlockSec provides a suite of products including Phalcon Security, Phalcon Compliance, MetaSleuth, and a public intelligence network for illicit fund monitoring.

providers.name: Bloomberg Government (BGOV)
providers.description: Bloomberg Government (BGOV) is a comprehensive intelligence platform for professionals working at the intersection of government and business. BGOV provides legislative tracking, regulatory intelligence, government contracting data, federal budget analysis, and policy research tools. It offers APIs and data feeds for integrating government and regulatory data into enterprise workflows.

providers.name: Brain Scanner
providers.description: Brain Scanner is a web application that helps developers review, pivot, and manage AI coding agent decisions. It records change histories, decision trails, and provides a workspace to connect coding agents like Claude Code or Codex. Users can sign up for a free account, explore project graphs, view change reports, and integrate with MCP settings to streamline AI agent workflows.

providers.name: Bsportsolution
providers.description: bsport provides a boutique studio management platform that automates class scheduling, booking, payments, membership management, team payroll, and marketing tools. It serves yoga, pilates, indoor cycling, dance, boxing, martial arts, bootcamp, HIIT and other fitness studios, including multi‑location and franchise operations.

providers.name: Car Handshake
providers.description: Car Handshake is a consumer-facing platform that aggregates new and used car listings from participating dealerships across the United States and Canada. It allows shoppers to compare vehicles, filter by price, make, model, and location, and directly contact dealers. The service also offers a public API (https://api.carhandshake.com/v1) providing vehicle inventory data for developers. Operated by Dealer Handshake Inc., Car Handshake emphasizes transparent pricing and a no‑login shopping experience.

providers.name: Claim Genius
providers.description: Claim Genius is an AI vehicle-inspection and automated damage-assessment company serving auto insurance claims, underwriting, dealerships, salvage, lease and rental, fleet and collision repair. Its GeniusINSPECT engine converts vehicle photos and video into structured, decision-ready data — per-part damage classification (scratch, dent, tear, glass, wheel), repair-versus-replace decisions, labor and paint hours, OEM part pricing, repairability status and total-loss probability. The capabilities are packaged as products (GeniusINSPECT for Claims, GeniusINSPECT for Underwriting, GeniusPrepost, GeniusOPS) and exposed to integrators through the GeniusAPI Suite, a JWT-authenticated REST API with asynchronous pipeline processing. The company has operated across the US, EU and Asia since 2018.

providers.name: Clip
providers.description: Clip (legal name Payclip) is a Mexico City-based fintech and SMB acquirer often described as the Square equivalent in Mexico. Founded in 2012, Clip enables merchants of all sizes to accept card, contactless, and QR payments through a family of mobile point-of-sale (mPOS) terminals — Clip Plus 2, Clip Pro 2, Clip Ultra, Clip Total 3, and the high-volume Clip PinPad — as well as Tap to Pay on iOS/Android smartphones, an online Checkout payment gateway, payment links, and the Clip Cuenta digital business account with same-day settlement and SMB loans. Clip operates the developer portal developer.clip.mx, which publishes the Checkout Redirect, Checkout Transparente, Transactions, Deposits, Refunds, and PinPad APIs along with the Checkout Transparente SDK and a Terminal SDK for embedding card acceptance into third-party POS apps. The company is backed by strategic investors including American Express Ventures, Banorte, Capital Group, and Morgan Stanley, and is consistently ranked among Mexico's top private fintech employers.

providers.name: Clone
providers.description: Clone Robotics develops musculoskeletal, intelligent humanoid androids and robotic hands built on Myofiber, its artificial-muscle technology pioneered in 2021, driven by water-based hydraulics and biomimetic joints. Its flagship Clone Alpha is a full-body biomimetic humanoid with synthetic organs; the Clone Hand is its foundational dexterous-manipulation platform. The developer surface is a first-party Python client (clone_client) exposing a high-level gRPC (proto3) API to directly control the Clone Robot over the local network — actuating muscles via impulses/pulses/pressures, driving pinch and hydra valves, managing the water-pump pressure source, streaming IMU/pose/joint telemetry, and configuring cameras. There is no public HTTP/REST API or hosted endpoint; control is LAN-scoped gRPC discovered over zeroconf/mDNS by robot name or IP. Co-founded 2021 by Dhanush Radhakrishna and Lukasz Kozlik.

providers.name: Cloud Ex Machina
providers.description: Cloud ex Machina (CxM) builds Dex, an agentic AI teammate for cloud cost and governance management. Dex continuously maps AWS, Azure, GCP and Kubernetes estates read-only and agentless, infers resource ownership by keeping the cloud connected to the organization's people and code, investigates cost and governance findings, and delivers review-ready remediation — pull requests, scripts and CLI instructions — to the engineers who can act, inside the tools they already use. The platform integrates with GitHub, GitLab, Jira, Linear, Notion, ServiceNow, Slack and Microsoft Teams, ingests non-cloud AI spend from Anthropic, and runs as a per-tenant SaaS with SAML 2.0 SSO. Cloud ex Machina publishes no public REST API or machine-readable specification; its developer-facing surface is cloud onboarding distributed as a Terraform Registry module, a CloudFormation template and a GitHub Action.

providers.name: Coast
providers.description: Coast is a fintech company providing a unified payments platform for fleet-based and field-service businesses, combining a smart Visa fuel card, corporate card, field card, and bill pay into a single program with granular spending controls, GPS- and tank-capacity-based fraud prevention, fuel rebates, and a fraud guarantee. Coast operates a stable v2 REST API (the Coast API) behind a developer portal that lets businesses programmatically access cards, drivers, vehicles, transactions, receipts, and controls, alongside native integrations with telematics (Samsara, Geotab, Verizon Connect), accounting (QuickBooks, NetSuite, Sage Intacct), and fleet management (Fleetio, Whip Around) platforms. Coast is backed by Accel and ICONIQ Capital.

providers.name: Context Window Supply
providers.description: Context Window Supply is a clothing label for AI builders, offering heavyweight tees and midweight hoodies with AI‑themed jokes. Established in 2026, the small studio runs the store with AI assistance and human oversight, printing items to order with no dead stock. They provide a return policy for damaged or misprinted goods and contact via hello@contextwindowsupply.com.

providers.name: Crane Worldwide Logistics
providers.description: Crane Worldwide Logistics is a global third-party logistics provider delivering air freight, ocean freight, customs brokerage, warehousing, trucking, and supply chain solutions across more than 30 countries. Crane exposes a developer API portal powered by Tyk that gives partners and customers programmatic access to shipment, booking, and tracking data across the company's supply chain operations.

providers.name: Creduse
providers.description: Creduse is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: g2-catalog) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.

providers.name: Crystallize
providers.description: Crystallize is a headless product information management (PIM) and commerce platform built around a set of GraphQL APIs. It separates product storytelling from the commerce engine, exposing a Catalogue API for reading structured product data, a Discovery (Search) API for browse and search, a Shop API for cart and checkout, an Order/Subscription API, and a Core/PIM API for managing shapes, items, and tenants.

providers.name: Docketwise
providers.description: Docketwise provides cloud-based immigration law practice management software, enabling attorneys to manage cases, clients, and documents efficiently. The platform offers tools for client intake, case tracking, document generation, and collaboration, helping firms streamline immigration workflows and improve client experiences.

providers.name: DripRaven
providers.description: DripRaven provides AI‑powered messaging campaign tools, enabling WhatsApp, SMS and future channels directly from AI assistants like ChatGPT and Claude. Users can import contacts, build segments, and launch campaigns via chat, with a focus on seamless integration and automation.

providers.name: dulieu-dev
providers.description: DuLieu.dev provides a Vietnamese economic data dashboard offering exchange rates, gold, silver, weather, fuel, coffee, pepper, groceries, drugs, electronics and more. It aggregates public economic indicators and market prices, presenting them via a web interface and API for developers to integrate Vietnamese market data into applications.

providers.name: Elpha Secure
providers.description: Elpha Secure is a New York-based cyber insurance managing general agent (MGA) for small and midsize businesses that bundles a first-party cybersecurity software agent with the insurance policy itself. The Elpha Agent ships endpoint detection and response, Malware Guard anti-malware, encrypted offsite backup, multi-factor authentication for remote desktop access, email security (ES Mail), financial fraud detection, vulnerability and security-posture scoring, and XDR integrations with SentinelOne, Sophos, Trend Micro and CrowdStrike, all managed from the Elpha Secure Portal. Policies are distributed through appointed brokers who quote and bind in the broker portal. Elpha Secure publishes no public developer portal, API reference or machine-readable specification; its Terms of Service define "Elpha Secure API's" as SOAP- or REST-based interfaces made available to customers and integrators under agreement.

providers.name: Envisics
providers.description: Envisics is a British deep-technology company headquartered in Milton Keynes, United Kingdom, that pioneers dynamic holography for automotive augmented-reality head-up displays (AR HUD). The work began with Dr Jamieson Christmas' PhD at Cambridge University in 2004, continued through Two Trees Photonics (founded 2010, acquired by DAQRI in 2015) which built the world's first laser holographic HUD for Jaguar Land Rover, and was spun out as the independent company Envisics on 1 January 2018. Its Dynamic Holography Platform and next-generation Holographic Waveguide Technology combine proprietary algorithms with simpler, fewer and more robust optics to deliver multi-plane AR imagery at under 10% of the optical power of conventional systems; first-generation technology shipped in over 150,000 Jaguar and Land Rover vehicles and second-generation technology was slated for the Cadillac LYRIQ-V and 2026 Cadillac VISTIQ. Investors included Hyundai Mobis, General Motors Ventures, Stellantis, InMotion Ventures (Jaguar Land Rover) and Tarsadia Investments. Envisics is an automotive hardware and optics supplier rather than a software vendor: it publishes no commercial or developer-facing product API, no developer portal, and no SDKs. The only machine-readable interface it exposes is the WordPress REST content API behind its corporate website at envisics.com, captured here for discovery purposes and anonymously readable but read-only. Envisics Ltd. entered administration on 22 April 2026 under the Insolvency Act 1986, with Geoff Rowley and Simon Carvill-Biggs of FRP Advisory Trading Limited appointed as Joint Administrators.

providers.name: Finli
providers.description: Finli is a financial technology platform serving two markets. For small and medium-sized businesses it provides a full digital back office — professional invoicing and quoting, payment processing (ACH, credit card, and Apple Pay), customer relationship management, inventory tracking, and autopay. For banks and credit unions it delivers those same tools as a white-labeled offering so financial institutions can attract and deepen small-business relationships, keep deposits, and own their customer data without taking on operational risk. Finli is SOC 2 Type II certified and PCI DSS compliant, and was founded by CEO Lori Shao. Added to the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio company; Finli publishes no public developer API at this time.

providers.name: getardaro-com
providers.description: Ardaro (brand: getardaro.com) provides construction management software for contractors, enabling field crews to capture voice notes, track job progress, manage estimates, schedules, e‑signatures, costs and profit without extensive typing. The platform offers features such as voice‑field notes, 3D builders, metal building support, estimating takeoffs, proposals, change orders, and a customer portal. It serves general contractors, remodelers, deck, roofing, plumbing, electrical, HVAC, and other specialty trades across the United States, with paid monthly plans in USD.

providers.name: Gotham Greens
providers.description: Gotham Greens is an American fresh food and indoor farming company founded in 2009 by Viraj Puri and Eric Haley in Brooklyn, New York, where it built one of the first commercial-scale rooftop hydroponic greenhouses in the world. The company owns and operates a national network of climate-controlled hydroponic greenhouses across the United States, growing pesticide-free leafy greens, lettuces and herbs year-round using a fraction of the land and water of conventional field agriculture, and delivering them to retail, restaurant and foodservice customers within hours of harvest. Under its own brand it sells packaged salad greens, salad kits, fresh herbs, salad dressings, dips, pestos and cooking sauces. Gotham Greens is a consumer packaged goods and controlled-environment agriculture business rather than a software vendor, and publishes no commercial or developer-facing product API. The only machine-readable interface it exposes is the WordPress REST content API behind its corporate website at gothamgreens.com, captured here for discovery purposes.

providers.name: Halcyon
providers.description: Halcyon (Halcyon Tech, Inc.) is a cybersecurity company that builds a purpose-built, adaptive anti-ransomware and cyber-resilience platform. Its lightweight endpoint agent combines automated detection and disruption across the full ransomware attack lifecycle — pre-execution, encryption, and data exfiltration — with encryption-key recovery, a managed 24/7 Ransomware Operations Center (ROC), and a ransomware recovery warranty. Halcyon exposes a REST API for device/asset data and a universal API that streams alerts into SIEM, SOAR, and XDR platforms such as Splunk, Microsoft Sentinel, Google SecOps, Sumo Logic, and Exabeam, alongside backup integrations with Veeam, Cohesity, Acronis, and Commvault. Backed by Bain Capital Ventures and Obvious Ventures.

providers.name: Harmonic
providers.description: Harmonic Inc. (NASDAQ: HLIT) is a video streaming and virtualized broadband technology company. Its VOS®360 Media SaaS orchestrates the entire live and on-demand video pipeline — ingest, transcoding, packaging, encryption, playout and delivery — while its cOS platform delivers virtualized DOCSIS 4.0 and fiber broadband access via Distributed Access Architecture (DAA) and Remote PHY. Harmonic serves 150+ operators worldwide including Comcast, Charter and Vodafone. The VOS 360 platform exposes a public REST API secured with OAuth 2.0 for managing assets, channels, services, live events, storage, DRM and jobs, enabling integration with third-party CMS and media workflows. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners and enriched from Harmonic's public developer surface.

providers.name: Kimba
providers.description: Kimba is an AI-powered sleep technology company building a bedside device that uses personalized scent therapy to improve sleep quality. The device reads biometric data from wearables (Oura, WHOOP, Apple Watch, Garmin), monitors sleep architecture, breathing, movement and disturbances, and releases natural, water-based scent formulations at precise moments in the sleep cycle to enhance rest, reduce nighttime disruptions and support cognitive performance. Kimba is a Techstars-backed direct-to-consumer hardware and subscription brand whose online store runs on Shopify; it exposes an agent-facing commerce surface via the Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP), a hosted MCP endpoint, and Shopify Customer Account API (OIDC) authentication rather than a traditional developer API.

providers.name: LAKRIDS BY BÜLOW
providers.description: LAKRIDS BY BÜLOW is a Danish gourmet liquorice maker founded by Johan Bülow, who opened his first shop in Svaneke on the island of Bornholm on 07.07.2007 and built the brand by cooking liquorice on-site so the aroma drew customers in. Trading as Lakrids by Johan Bülow A/S (CVR 33041586) from Sydholmen 5, 2650 Hvidovre, Denmark, the company makes plain and chocolate-coated liquorice — its flagship being "A - THE ORIGINAL", a gluten-free sweet liquorice core coated in milk chocolate — and sells direct to consumers across Europe alongside concept stores, retail partners and a B2B corporate gifting business. The company operates no public developer program: its storefront runs on the BigCommerce Stencil platform, and the only API surface reachable on its own host is platform-provided and documented by BigCommerce.

providers.name: Magical
providers.description: Magical is an AI-agent platform that automates repetitive administrative and operational workflows without requiring API integrations, instead driving the same web applications and databases a human worker would use. Originally known for its cross-application autofill and text-automation product, Magical has focused on healthcare operations, deploying specialized AI agents for patient access, revenue cycle management, prior authorizations, referrals, benefits verification, records requests, revenue integrity, and payment posting across EHR and payer systems such as Epic, Cerner, athenahealth, eClinicalWorks, ModMed, Availity, and major insurers. Agents can be deployed individually or combined into autonomous suites, with the company reporting high task accuracy and multi-week deployment timelines. Magical is backed by Bain Capital Ventures, Greylock, and SV Angel. Notably, Magical operates through user-interface automation ("no APIs or integrations are required") rather than by exposing a public developer API.

providers.name: mcp-market-ru
providers.description: MCP Market RU is a Russian marketplace platform that aggregates various digital services and products, providing a centralized API for developers to integrate listings, pricing, and transaction capabilities. The company focuses on enabling seamless e‑commerce experiences through standardized RESTful endpoints, comprehensive documentation, and support for multiple authentication methods. It aims to foster a vibrant ecosystem for third‑party developers and partners, offering tools for catalog management, order processing, and analytics.

providers.name: Microsoft Viva
providers.description: Microsoft Viva is an employee experience platform built on Microsoft 365 and Teams. It provides APIs for Viva Connections, Viva Learning, and Viva Insights to integrate employee experience capabilities into custom applications.

providers.name: Miter
providers.description: Miter is a Human Capital Management (HCM) platform purpose-built for construction contractors, consolidating payroll, HR, benefits, field operations, and expense management into a single connected system. Its construction payroll automates prevailing-wage, certified-payroll, and union compliance, multi-state tax handling, and fully-burdened job-cost tracking in real time, while its HRIS covers recruiting, benefits, performance, and learning. Field Operations adds time tracking, scheduling, daily reports, production tracking, and safety, and Expense Management handles reimbursements, per diems, and corporate cards. Miter connects to construction ERPs and accounting systems (Sage Intacct, NetSuite, Acumatica, QuickBooks, Procore, Viewpoint, and more) through off-the-shelf integrations or a custom REST API. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners.

providers.name: Nailedit
providers.description: Nailedit provides a free AI-powered mock interview platform that helps job seekers practice interview questions. Users can paste job postings, answer aloud, and receive scores on five key interview criteria. The service aims to improve confidence and performance in real interviews, offering a free starter tier and AI-driven feedback.

providers.name: Nitric
providers.description: Nitric is an open-source cloud framework and infrastructure-from-code SDK plus CLI for building cloud applications in TypeScript, Python, Go, or Dart. You declare resources - APIs, schedules, queues, topics, buckets, key-value stores, secrets, and websockets - directly in your application code, and Nitric provisions them across AWS, Google Cloud, or Azure via pluggable Pulumi or Terraform providers. Nitric is a framework / IaC tool, not a hosted REST API - the APIs you build are deployed to your own cloud.

providers.name: Peaxy
providers.description: Peaxy, Inc. is a San Jose, California industrial AI and digital-twin software company founded in 2012, with offices in Stockholm, Sweden and Cagliari, Italy. Its Peaxy Lifecycle Intelligence (PLI) platform threads design, test, manufacturing, field and service data for mission-critical physical assets into a single cloud-based source of truth, then applies machine learning to predict failures, extend asset life and support warranty, quality and readiness decisions. Product lines cover battery and energy-storage analytics (R&D through manufacturing, deployment and second life), defense readiness and predictive maintenance for the U.S. Department of Defense and Department of Energy, critical infrastructure and airport/circuit-level AI, a battery LIMS, and EcoGrid for renewable energy communities. Peaxy markets "a range of open APIs" for platform integration, but publishes no public developer portal, API reference or machine-readable contract — access runs through a demo request and a customer engagement. The platform is SOC 2 Type II certified and aligned to NIST 800-171.

providers.name: Radiant Security
providers.description: Radiant Security is an AI-powered Security Operations Center (SOC) platform that automates alert triage, investigation, and response so security teams can scale coverage without adding headcount. Founded in 2021 and headquartered in the SF Bay Area with offices in Tel Aviv and Sao Paulo, Radiant ingests alerts from 120+ security tools across email, endpoint, identity, network, cloud, insider-threat, SIEM, WAF, DLP, and OT/IoT sources, triages 100% of them with transparent AI reasoning, and escalates only genuine risks to analysts. It pairs automated investigation with integrated, SIEM-cost-free log management (unlimited retention with customer S3 buckets) and one-click response actions. The product is delivered as a hosted SaaS console; its public surface is product documentation and inbound connectors rather than a developer-facing REST API.

providers.name: Rakuten Viber
providers.description: Rakuten Viber is a messaging and calling app. Its developer hub publishes the Viber REST Bot API (chatapi.viber.com/pa) for building bots that send and receive messages, with webhook callbacks and official Node.js and Python SDKs.

providers.name: Red Electrica (e-sios)
providers.description: Red Electrica (e-sios) operates the Spanish electricity market data platform ESIOS, providing transparent access to generation, consumption, market prices, demand forecasts, and system operation metrics. The service offers extensive datasets through a public API, supporting developers, analysts, and energy stakeholders in building applications, visualizations, and research tools. It emphasizes open data, regulatory compliance, and real‑time updates, fostering innovation in the energy sector.

providers.name: Rhythmos
providers.description: Rhythmos (rhythmos.io) provides modern analytics for managing electric-vehicle charging and grid infrastructure. Its platform coordinates fleet charging needs against utility and wholesale market conditions to lower energy costs and defer costly grid infrastructure investment, serving EV fleet owners, utilities, municipalities, and market aggregators through Fleet, Grid, and Market applications. Rhythmos maintains a SOC 2 Type II report and is GDPR compliant. The company is now part of Electron (electron.net). No public developer API, SDK, or developer portal is published at this time; this profile captures the company's identity, website properties, and security/compliance posture.

providers.name: Send Technology
providers.description: Send Technology Solutions Ltd is a London-headquartered insurtech software company, founded in 2017, that builds an underwriting workbench for commercial and specialty insurers, MGAs and reinsurers. Its platform covers submission management, quote and rate lifecycle management, risk workflow, binder management, bordereaux ingestion, entity management, post-bind processing and portfolio data and insights, with product lines for direct underwriting, delegated underwriting and reinsurance underwriting. Its home market is the United Kingdom and its centre of gravity is the London Market — Lloyd's managing agents, syndicates and MGAs — where it ships pre-built connectors to the electronic placing platforms PPL and Whitespace and aligns with Lloyd's Blueprint Two. Send markets itself as an API-first platform, and it exchanges ACORD Standard placing, accounting and claims transactions through ACORD Solutions Group's ADEPT (ACORD Data Exchange Platform and Translator) via API, having joined ACORD as a member. Despite that posture, Send publishes NO public self-serve developer portal and NO downloadable OpenAPI: developer., developers., docs. and api.send.technology do not resolve in DNS, and /developers, /api, /developer and /integrations all return 404. The only integration surface is partner- and customer-gated, arranged through sales, implementation partners and the ACORD/placing-platform seam rather than through public documentation — a faithful example of the London Market's broker- and syndicate-facing modernization being invisible from the outside.

providers.name: Shoptiques
providers.description: Shoptiques is an online marketplace that brings thousands of independently owned local boutiques online, letting shoppers discover unique, one-of-a-kind fashion and home decor from over 5,000 stores. Founded in 2012 by Olga Vidisheva, the business rebranded its merchant/POS arm as Material in 2023 while continuing to operate the Shoptiques consumer marketplace. The storefront at shoptiques.com now runs on Shopify and exposes a modern agent-facing commerce surface: a published llms.txt / agents.md, Shopify Customer Account OpenID Connect + OAuth 2.0 authentication, and a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) MCP endpoint for buyer-approved, agent-driven shopping and checkout.

providers.name: Stratasys
providers.description: Stratasys Ltd. (Nasdaq: SSYS) is a global leader in polymer additive manufacturing (industrial 3D printing), headquartered in Rehovot, Israel and Eden Prairie, Minnesota. Stratasys builds FDM, PolyJet, stereolithography (SLA), selective absorption fusion (SAF) and powder-bed (P3) printing systems, the materials that feed them, and the GrabCAD software platform that drives them. Its developer surface is the GrabCAD ecosystem: GrabCAD Print / GrabCAD Print Pro for job preparation, GrabCAD Control and GrabCAD Shop for fleet and shop management, and the GrabCAD Software Development Kit — a partner program of connectivity SDKs (Printer Connectivity SDK, MT Connect SDK, PLM SDK) that use standard protocols and APIs to integrate Stratasys printers with ERP, PLM, MES and smart-factory systems for automation, data collection and analytics.

providers.name: Superfuel AI
providers.description: Superfuel is an AI agent for Amazon sellers that reads competitor data, customer reviews, brand analytics, and product features, then writes and measures optimized product listings — most notably Amazon titles and the new 125-character Item Highlights field. Sellers connect their Amazon Seller Central account and run pre-built or custom Workflows (schedulable, with execution traces) that automate repetitive catalog and market-analysis tasks, while a measurement system isolates a change's real impact on CTR, sessions, and conversion by stripping out price, ad spend, seasonality, and deals. Superfuel is an end-user SaaS product (credit-metered plans) rather than a developer API provider; it publishes product documentation on Mintlify but no first-party public REST API. Backed by Accel; sector: ecommerce.

providers.name: TestGorilla
providers.description: TestGorilla is an AI-powered talent-assessment and skills-based hiring platform that helps organizations screen and evaluate candidates objectively. It offers a library of 350+ pre-employment tests (cognitive ability, personality, role-specific skills, coding, language, and situational judgement), AI interviews, and anti-cheating monitoring, and is used by companies such as PayPal, Equifax, and PepsiCo. TestGorilla advertises ATS integrations but does not publish a public self-serve developer API; this profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Balderton Capital and Partech and enriched with the company's real public web, security, and trust surfaces.

providers.name: Testlio
providers.description: Testlio is a managed software testing and quality assurance company that pairs a global, vetted community of expert testers with a testing-management platform (powered by its Leo AI Engine) to deliver on-demand manual, automated, functional, regression, payments, localization, accessibility, usability, and AI testing across web, mobile, streaming, and voice experiences. Founded in Estonia and headquartered in Austin, Texas, Testlio is a Techstars-backed company serving enterprise engineering and QA teams. It exposes no public REST API; the platform integrates with engineering toolchains (Jira, GitHub, Azure DevOps, GitLab, TestRail, Xray, Slack, BrowserStack, SauceLabs, Playwright) and ships first-party CI/CD integrations, including a CircleCI orb and a Jenkins plugin, alongside a documented Trust Center.

providers.name: Token
providers.description: Token Security is a cybersecurity company that secures non-human identities (NHIs) and AI agents across on-premises, hybrid, and cloud environments. Its platform continuously discovers every AI agent, service account, and machine identity, maps ownership and security posture, detects identity threats, and automates remediation. Capabilities span NHI inventory, security posture management, lifecycle management, secrets, and identity threat detection and response. The company also ships the Token MCP Server and a native Token AI Agent so security teams can query and act on NHI data conversationally from Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, or Cursor. Backed by Bloomberg Beta, GGV Capital, and Qiming, Token Security serves enterprise security teams, CISOs, and IAM professionals governing machine and agent identity at scale.

providers.name: TolaData
providers.description: TolaData provides a cloud‑based platform for nonprofit and development organizations to manage projects, track results, and report on impact. The service includes tools for data collection, monitoring, evaluation, and collaborative planning, helping NGOs and donors improve transparency and effectiveness. TolaData’s API enables integration with external systems for data exchange and automation, supporting a data‑driven approach to development work.

providers.name: University of Navarra
providers.description: The University of Navarra (Universidad de Navarra) is a private research university founded in 1952, headquartered in Pamplona, Spain, with campuses in San Sebastian, Madrid and Barcelona. Its programmable footprint is small, and most of it is bought rather than built: the library discovery layer is an Ex Libris Primo VE tenancy, the DADUN institutional repository runs on a hosted DSpace whose host CNAMEs to a third-party platform, the research portal is a Dialnet CRIS tenancy operated by Fundacion Dialnet, and the library guides are Springshare LibGuides. Three surfaces are genuinely the institution's own. The Servicio de Publicaciones operates a self-hosted Open Journal Systems instance at revistas.unav.edu with a live, unauthenticated OAI-PMH 2.0 harvesting interface across 100 sets — the only institution-operated machine-readable API confirmed here. The university runs its own SAML Identity Provider, published through the RedIRIS SIR2 federation and interfederated into eduGAIN since 2018 with REFEDS Sirtfi declared. And it is a Crossref member with its own DOI prefix, 10.15581, covering more than 33,000 registered DOIs. There is no central developer portal, no open-data platform, no documented registrar, timetable or campus API, and no verifiable institutional GitHub organization.

providers.name: USAID
providers.description: The U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID) provides programmatic access to foreign assistance data, development finance records, project tracking, aid flow analysis, and global development datasets through a suite of REST APIs. Key offerings include the ForeignAssistance.gov Data API (OAS 3.0) for budgetary and financial foreign aid data across U.S. government agencies, the Development Data Library (DDL) powered by the Socrata Open Data API (SODA) for querying and filtering open datasets, and the Development Experience Clearinghouse (DEC) API for programmatic access to USAID-funded international development documentation. These APIs support researchers, policymakers, journalists, and developers building tools around international aid transparency and global development outcomes.

providers.name: WeStock
providers.description: WeStock is a shopper-marketing platform that helps consumer packaged goods (CPG) brands drive product trial, build first-party retail audiences, and manage trade and shopper marketing strategy from a single dashboard. It combines digital rebates and promotional campaigns, paid social advertising (primarily Meta), in-store sampling and demos, retail media management across Amazon, Walmart, and Instacart, email/SMS automation, and influencer marketing, alongside a consumer discovery web app used by 600,000+ shoppers to browse new products. Campaign data — trials, conversions, and repeat behavior — is unified in one place. A Techstars-backed company; its entire public surface is a Webflow marketing site, a Help Scout knowledge base of product how-tos, and login-gated dashboard and consumer apps. WeStock runs a real first-party backend at api.westock.io — hardened Node/Express that answers HTTP 401 on every path including the root — but ships no developer program: no API reference, no OpenAPI or GraphQL schema, no SDK on any registry, no webhooks, and no API pricing. Its documented integrations run the other way: WeStock consumes Klaviyo and Attentive using keys the customer pastes into the WeStock dashboard.

providers.name: A-Bio Materials
providers.description: A-Bio Materials Co., Ltd. (에이바이오머티리얼즈) is a South Korean life-science company, founded in 2020 and led by founder and CEO Sijun Park, that develops and manufactures exosome-derived bioactive materials for cosmetics, aesthetics and medical devices. It produces plant-, human- and microbial-derived exosome formulations and PDRN raw materials through its own Exo-traction, Celltivation and Escentraction purification and cultivation processes, supplying skincare and medical-device manufacturers with ingredients for cell signalling, inflammation reduction, collagen synthesis and tissue regeneration. Its North American arm, ABio materials USA Inc. of Tustin, California, is the official importer and distributor for the region and operates the company's English-language storefront. A-Bio Materials runs no developer programme and publishes no API specification; the machine-readable surfaces recorded in this profile are the WordPress, WooCommerce and WebMCP endpoints its North American storefront serves.

providers.name: AccessFintech
providers.description: AccessFintech operates Synergy, a post-trade data and workflow network for capital markets that connects buy-side firms, broker-dealers, custodians, hedge funds, order management systems and vendors onto a shared view of trade, settlement and collateral data. The platform normalizes fragmented data across securities, derivatives and alternatives, detects breaks and exceptions across counterparties, and lets the parties to a trade resolve them collaboratively on a single record instead of by email and reconciliation files. AccessFintech describes Synergy as API-first, with bi-directional integrations, ingestion of JSON, XML, CSV and delimited text over push or pull, and Snowflake-native data sharing on AWS. The API surface is not self-serve: the Synergy application and its GraphQL and REST endpoints sit behind an Okta-backed customer login at login.accessfintech.com, and no public developer portal, reference or machine-readable specification is published.

providers.name: Admera Health
providers.description: Admera Health is a CLIA-certified and CAP-accredited genomics service provider and contract research organization headquartered in South Plainfield, New Jersey, established in 2014 as a spinout of GENEWIZ. It runs 100% US-based next-generation sequencing, library preparation and bioinformatics operations for academic, biotech and biopharma customers, spanning whole genome and whole exome sequencing, metagenomics and amplicon sequencing, bulk and small RNA-seq, single-cell sequencing on 10x Genomics, Parse Biosciences and Takara Bio platforms, spatial transcriptomics on Visium HD and STOmics Stereo-seq, epigenomics, proteomics and metabolomics, plus BioEcho nucleic acid purification products. Customers submit and track projects through EraTrack, a login-only web portal. Admera Health publishes no public developer program, API reference, SDK or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: Adobe Commerce
providers.description: Adobe Commerce (formerly Magento Commerce) is an enterprise e-commerce platform for building and operating online storefronts, marketplaces, and B2B/B2C catalogs across web, mobile, and headless experiences. The Adobe Commerce Web APIs expose REST and GraphQL access to products, categories, customers, carts, orders, inventory, and configuration with OAuth 1.0a and token-based (Bearer) authentication against a merchant-hosted base URL.

providers.name: Agent Traffic Lab
providers.description: Agent Traffic Lab provides a routing platform that connects AI agents to supported tasks such as search, extraction, summarization, translation, and classification. It evaluates provider eligibility, applies policy and budget constraints, and executes tasks with bounded fallback, delivering durable outcomes and performance metrics.

providers.name: AgentDataFeed
providers.description: AgentDataFeed provides factual, source‑verified datasets for AI agents. It offers a variety of public‑sector data such as Amsterdam events, security advisories, vulnerability watches, EU and UK public tenders, funding calls, medical data, sanctions, product recalls, legislation, drug shortages, and public holidays. Users pay per query with x402 (USDC on Base) while metadata and sample records are free. Each record includes verification details and indicates if placement was paid. The service emphasizes open‑licence data and official publications, enabling AI agents to answer queries about events, security risks, procurement opportunities, and more with reliable, up‑to‑date information.

providers.name: Alcoven
providers.description: Alcoven is a web‑based collaborative project management platform that lets teams store briefs, documents, and tasks in a single project and interact with AI assistants such as Claude, Codex, and ChatGPT. Users can open a project in any of the supported AI agents, capture generated content, and have it saved back to the project.
