providers.description: Automaton Colony builds tools for governed memory, economic Solidity analysis and contract verification on Base. It offers three products—Nebula for AI memory, Colony for contract verification on Base, and Scorpio for Solidity analysis—providing context, limits and evidence before decisions. The platform emphasizes verifiable decision systems, visible limits, and human control.

providers.name: Autonomy
providers.description: Autonomy provides a month-to-month car subscription service, allowing customers to drive a variety of vehicles without long-term loans or leases. Users select a vehicle, pay a start fee and monthly payment, and can keep, swap, or return the car at any time. The platform emphasizes flexibility, no commitment, and includes an app for managing subscriptions, payments, and vehicle selection across SUVs, trucks, and electric models.

providers.name: BetterView Marketplace
providers.description: Betterview is a market-leading Property Intelligence platform that delivers actionable insights to property & casualty insurance underwriters, agents, and insureds to increase efficiency and profitability. Its API lets carriers order and retrieve property profiles enriched with the Roof Spotlight Index (RSI), peril risks, flags, and third-party Partner Connect data, subscribe properties to PropertyPulse monitoring, and query PropertyNow pre-processed datasets by address or coordinates. Betterview integrates with core insurance systems including Guidewire (a Marketplace accelerator for PolicyCenter 10), Duck Creek, and Socotra, and supports SSO, Secure FTP, ImageRight drop, an embeddable geospatial iframe UI, and an External Data Warehouse (EDW) SQL connection.

providers.name: Blipsmith
providers.description: Blipsmith provides an AI-powered sound effect generator for game developers, allowing users to describe a desired sound and receive royalty‑free, game‑ready WAV files within seconds. The service offers free first sound, tiered pricing, seamless loops, variations, and a web interface for quick creation, positioning itself as a SaaS solution for rapid audio asset creation in interactive entertainment.

providers.name: Breaking Bad
providers.description: Community-built REST API exposing characters, quotes, episodes, and on-screen deaths from the Breaking Bad and Better Call Saul television universe. The original hosted service at breakingbadapi.com is no longer reachable as of 2026-05-29 (DNS does not resolve). The canonical source code remains at github.com/timbiles/Breaking-Bad--API under BSD-3-Clause and is the basis for the historical OpenAPI and capability artifacts in this repo.

providers.name: Caimera
providers.description: On-brand fashion visuals from sketch to sale. Caimera provides an AI visual production platform for fashion teams, offering AI fashion models, flat‑lay to on‑model catalog, editorials, video and tech packs in one solution. Try free.

providers.name: CastHost
providers.description: CastHost provides reliable internet radio hosting services, offering free Shoutcast and Icecast hosting with a 7‑day free trial, 24/7 expert support, and affordable plans. The platform also includes cPanel web hosting and mobile app development services, serving customers worldwide from its Canadian base.

providers.name: Clubhousesoftware
providers.description: Clubhousesoftware is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: secondary-market) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling. The company appears to be a software provider targeting club management solutions, but no official website could be verified. Public references point to a potential domain clubhousesoftwareinc.com, which was unreachable at the time of probing. Further investigation may be required to confirm its online presence and product offerings.

providers.name: CoachClub
providers.description: CoachClub — branded "CoachClub by Move Your Fit" — is a French direct-to-consumer online sport and wellness coaching service founded in 2010 in France by Leslie Vartabedian and backed by Serena. Subscribers answer a questionnaire covering goals, physical ability, health and availability, and receive a tailored training and nutrition programme drawn from a library of more than 1,100 on-demand coaching videos spanning over 30 disciplines — fitness, musculation, yoga, danse, cardio boxe, pilates, stretching, bien-être and prénatal/postnatal — graded across three difficulty levels and paired with twelve weeks of healthy recipes, accessible 24/7 from computer, tablet, smartphone or television. The public marketing site runs on WordPress and the member application is a hosted Kajabi tenant at mon.coachclub.com. CoachClub sells an end-user subscription only: it publishes no public API, SDK, webhook catalog, developer portal or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Constantinople
providers.description: Constantinople is a Sydney-based fintech providing an AI-native core-banking platform that lets banks run product, technology, data, operations, and compliance as a single modern fabric. It powers retail, business, and embedded banking across accounts, payments, cards, lending, mortgages, and term deposits, with headless APIs and SDKs, digital onboarding, an AI concierge for customers, and the "Justinian" AI workbench for bankers. Risk and compliance (fraud, financial-crime detection, regulatory reporting) are built into the platform, which is SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified. Constantinople is backed by Prosus Ventures (Series A, A$50M). The developer/API surface is a gated B2B platform; enrichment here is sourced from the company's public web presence.

providers.name: Cyberhaven
providers.description: Cyberhaven is a data security company that unifies Data Security Posture Management (DSPM), Data Loss Prevention (DLP), Insider Risk Management, and AI Security into a single AI and data security platform. Its data lineage-first architecture traces data from origin to exfiltration across endpoints, cloud, on-prem, SaaS, and AI tools, coaching users and blocking leaks across email, web, cloud, removable storage, and AI assistants. Cyberhaven exposes a REST API (v1 and v2) that lets teams pull incidents into third-party security tools using API-key authentication, and integrates with directory services, SIEM/SOAR platforms, and cloud applications. Backed by Costanoa Ventures, Redpoint Ventures, and Wing Venture Capital.

providers.name: Danfoss
providers.description: Danfoss is a global family‑owned engineering company that creates innovative solutions to increase machine productivity, reduce emissions, lower energy consumption and enable electrification. The company serves a wide range of industries including automotive, building‑commercial, marine, and energy, offering products such as drives, climate solutions, and power solutions. Danfoss is committed to sustainability and long‑term value for stakeholders, as described on its corporate website.

providers.name: DDMarketer
providers.description: DDMarketer provides a data-driven platform that surfaces validated SaaS opportunities derived from real customer complaints and market gaps. Users can explore weekly updated opportunity lists, access detailed gap analyses, and leverage the MCP server to query validated ideas programmatically. The service offers free tools for idea validation, a paid plan for deeper insights, and integrates with AI coding assistants to streamline product development based on proven demand.

providers.name: Deeploi
providers.description: Deeploi (deeploi GmbH) is a Berlin-based all-in-one IT management (ITSM) platform for mid-sized businesses and startups, primarily across the DACH region. It centralizes employee onboarding and offboarding, device and inventory management, software and license/account administration, cybersecurity and compliance policies, and unlimited expert IT support in a single dashboard priced per active employee. Deeploi operates an Information Security Management System aligned with ISO/IEC 27001 and is GDPR compliant, publishing its posture through a Kertos-powered Trust Center. The company is backed by Atomico. Deeploi does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile captures its identity, security posture, and public web properties.

providers.name: DocuWare
providers.description: DocuWare provides cloud‑based document management and workflow automation solutions for businesses of all sizes. Its platform enables secure capture, storage, indexing, and retrieval of documents, along with advanced features like intelligent document processing, electronic signatures, and integration with popular enterprise applications. DocuWare helps organizations streamline processes, improve compliance, and enhance productivity through a scalable, SaaS‑delivered service.

providers.name: Economic Development Administration
providers.description: The U.S. Economic Development Administration (EDA) is an agency in the United States Department of Commerce that provides grants and technical assistance to economically distressed communities in order to generate new employment, help retain existing jobs and stimulate industrial and commercial growth through a variety of investment programs. EDA works with boards and communities across the country on economic development strategies.

providers.name: Elderly Care Match
providers.description: Elderly Care Match is a Washington State senior-care directory and placement service that helps families find and compare licensed adult family homes (AFH), assisted living, memory care, nursing homes / skilled nursing and independent living, with listings that are free to browse, many cross-checked against the WA DSHS/ALTSA licence registry, and coverage strongest across the Seattle-Tacoma-Bellevue / Puget Sound metro. Its only machine interface is an Agent2Agent (A2A 1.0) agent: a card served at /.well-known/agent-card.json and a JSON-RPC 2.0 endpoint at https://www.elderlycarematch.com/a2a/v1 that answers anonymously with four read-only skills — search facilities by location, care type, Medicaid acceptance, vacancy and price; fetch a facility's public profile; search the Learning Center guides; and hand a family off to a care advisor by returning a public form URL. It publishes no OpenAPI, SDK or MCP server; llms.txt is the documentation and robots.txt explicitly welcomes AI crawlers on /.well-known/ and /a2a/.

providers.name: Elevate
providers.description: Elevate is an AI-powered, cloud-native consumer-directed benefits administration platform for health savings accounts (HSAs), flexible spending accounts (FSAs), health reimbursement arrangements (HRAs), and commuter, lifestyle, and family-forming accounts. Built API-first and white-label, the platform lets benefits administrators, third-party administrators (TPAs), PEOs, brokers, financial institutions, and health plans embed real-time account management, instant claims processing, and reimbursement into their own front ends. Members view, plan, and manage every pre-tax benefit from a single web and mobile dashboard with one card across all accounts. Founded in 2020, Elevate is backed by Anthemis, Fin Capital, Norwest Venture Partners, Greycroft, Bowery Capital, Firebolt Ventures, and SaaS Ventures. Its complete API set is partner-gated (access via demo/contract); the platform is HIPAA and AICPA SOC compliant.

providers.name: Exotec
providers.description: Exotec is a French warehouse automation manufacturer and integrator, founded in 2015 and headquartered in Croix, France, that builds the Skypod robotic automated storage and retrieval system (AS/RS) and the Deepsky warehouse execution system (WES) that orchestrates it. Skypod combines autonomous three-dimensional mobile robots, modular racking, picking workstations and inbound exchangers into an all-in-one goods-to-person system; Deepsky is the software layer that coordinates the robots, stations and third-party equipment and connects the installation to a customer's WMS or WCS over a RESTful web-services interface. Exotec reports more than 10,000 robots deployed across over 200 customer sites for more than 50 brands including Decathlon, Renault Group, DSV, Carrefour, Gap and Uniqlo, serving apparel, general merchandise, aftermarket parts, grocery, third-party logistics and healthcare fulfillment. The Deepsky WMS integration interface is delivered as customer-specific documentation under a commercial deployment rather than a public developer program, so Exotec publishes no open developer portal, API reference or SDK. It does publish an llms.txt at its web root and holds ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certification and SOC 2 Type 2 compliance.

providers.name: FastMCP
providers.description: FastMCP is the fast, Pythonic framework for building Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, clients, and apps. Originally created by Jeremiah Lowin and maintained by PrefectHQ, FastMCP 1.0 was adopted into the official Anthropic MCP Python SDK in 2024, and the standalone FastMCP project (now at v3) remains the most widely used way to ship MCP servers in Python — the project reports powering roughly 70% of MCP servers across all languages. FastMCP turns ordinary Python functions into MCP tools, resources, prompts, and apps via decorators, auto-generates JSON Schemas from type hints, handles transport negotiation (stdio, Streamable HTTP, SSE), and ships first-class OAuth/OIDC authentication, server composition and proxying, OpenAPI/FastAPI import, a CLI for running and installing servers into Claude Desktop / Claude Code / Cursor / ChatGPT / Gemini CLI / Goose, middleware, lifespan management, elicitation, sampling, progress reporting, OpenTelemetry, and a client library and apps runtime for building interactive UIs rendered inside MCP host conversations.

providers.name: HData
providers.description: HData is the AI-native operating system for energy regulation. Founded in 2018 by Hudson Hollister, the platform turns disconnected federal and state regulatory filings, dockets, and proceedings from sources such as FERC, EIA, and state utility commissions into standardized, citable, machine-readable data. It combines centralized regulatory data, domain-specific AI trained on more than 20 million citable documents, and purpose-built tools — including HData Analytics, Regulatory Intelligence, Gateway for FERC data extraction, and Data Request Management — to help utilities, regulators, advocates, advisory firms, financial institutions, and large energy customers accelerate rate cases, resource planning, compliance reporting, and policy research.

providers.name: HDVI (High Definition Vehicle Insurance)
providers.description: HDVI (High Definition Vehicle Insurance) is a Chicago-based commercial trucking insurance company delivering modern, data-driven coverage for small and mid-size fleet operators. Its flagship HDVI Shift product uses integrated telematics and safety data to dynamically price premiums, rewarding safe driving with monthly discounts of up to 20 percent, and its Fleet Portal gives fleets tools to improve safety, reduce risk, maintain compliance, and lower costs. HDVI was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of 8vc. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or OpenAPI; it operates a customer-facing Fleet Portal and telematics/ELD/dash-cam partner integrations rather than an open developer program. This profile captures the company's real public identity, its published llms.txt, its SOC 2 Type 2 compliance posture, and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Highway9
providers.description: Highway 9 Networks is a Silicon Valley company delivering AI Wireless Infrastructure as a Service through its Virtual Mobile/AI Cloud (VMC) platform. The platform combines a cloud control plane (Mobile Center), a distributed 5G core and edge AI services (Mobile Edge), private 5G wireless infrastructure (Mobile Network), and connected device/workload groupings (Mobile Zones) to give enterprises deterministic, ultra-reliable private mobile networks and in-building cellular coverage. It targets manufacturing and warehousing (autonomous robots, drones, logistics), higher education (AI labs and research), and energy (predictive maintenance, remote operations). The Mobile Center Streaming APIs let partners integrate configuration, device management, monitoring, analytics, and operational workflows with the platform. Founded by an ex-VMware team behind NSX/SDN, hybrid cloud, and the Telco 5G/Edge cloud platform.

providers.name: Hive Power
providers.description: Hive Power SA is a Swiss software company (Manno, Ticino) building FLEXO, a Flexibility Orchestrator that connects distributed energy assets — electric vehicles, stationary batteries, solar systems, and smart appliances — to electricity markets and grid services. FLEXO pairs an AI optimization engine (weather, price, and behavior forecasting) with a REST API mid-layer and end-user/admin interfaces to deliver smart charging (V1G/V2G/V2X), virtual power plant (VPP) aggregation, battery monetization, energy-community management, and local optimization. The platform is hardware-agnostic, integrating EVs, chargers, batteries, and solar/EMS via IoT platforms and manufacturer APIs (Enode, ABB, Huawei, LG, SMA, Easee, ChargePoint) and protocols such as MODBUS, MQTT, and OCPP. Backed by Techstars.

providers.name: Inscope
providers.description: Inscope is an AI-powered financial reporting and automation platform for accounting firms and enterprise finance teams. It drafts accurate, GAAP-compliant financial statements, cash flow statements, and audit workpapers in minutes, keeping a human reviewer in the loop to review and sign off. The platform targets the financial close, reporting, and audit workflow, and states SOC 2 Type I and Type II certification with GDPR/CCPA compliance. Inscope is a private SaaS backed by Norwest Venture Partners; it publishes no public product API or developer portal today. Customer sign-in runs on a PropelAuth-hosted OpenID Connect tenant at auth.inscopehq.com.

providers.name: IVIX
providers.description: IVIX is an AI-powered financial-intelligence platform that analyzes publicly available data at scale to surface hidden and unreported business activity, helping government tax authorities and law-enforcement agencies combat the shadow economy, tax evasion, and financial crime. The platform ingests open and third-party data to detect non-compliant businesses, quantify unreported revenue (including short-term rentals and crypto markets), and map illicit networks for enforcement teams. IVIX is a closed, government-facing product — it is sold and deployed with authorities rather than exposed as a public self-serve API — and it is ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certified for information security. Backed by Insight Partners; headquartered in New York with former IRS Commissioner Charles Rettig on its board of advisors.

providers.name: Kenerate AI
providers.description: About Kenerate AI: the AI image, video, music, voice and 3D studio at kenerateai.com, built by a self‑funded team in Darbhanga, India. 200+ models; credits never expire.

providers.name: Levels
providers.description: Levels is a continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) metabolic-health app that pairs glucose sensors with lab testing and personalized guidance. The platform is a consumer product delivered through iOS, Android, and a member web portal; it consumes health data (Apple Health, wearables, uploaded labs) but does not publish a documented public or partner developer API as of this catalog date.

providers.name: Maintainerr
providers.description: Maintainerr is a free, self‑hosted tool that automatically cleans up unwatched or unwanted movies and shows from Plex, Jellyfin, and Emby. It offers powerful, customizable rules to keep media libraries tidy, runs in Docker and on Linux, Windows, macOS, and integrates with popular media servers to improve storage efficiency and user experience.

providers.name: Moonchild
providers.description: Moonchild AI provides a chat‑based design assistant that transforms product requirement documents into production‑ready UI screens. By leveraging AI, it helps product managers, designers, and developers accelerate design workflows, generate prototypes, and export code directly from design systems. The platform offers a web interface, Discord community, and studio tools for collaborative design, aiming to close the gap between product vision and implementation without scaling design teams.

providers.name: Oculus
providers.description: Oculus is the virtual-reality company founded in 2012 that Kickstarter-launched the Rift headset and was backed by Spark Capital, Matrix Partners and others before Facebook acquired it in 2014 for roughly two billion dollars. The Oculus consumer brand has since been folded into Meta Quest, and the Oculus developer platform now lives as the Meta Horizon developer program at developers.meta.com/horizon. It offers the Oculus/Meta Platform SDK, the Meta Spatial SDK, OpenXR-native, Unity and Unreal engine integrations, and Immersive Web tooling for building mixed- and virtual-reality apps for Horizon OS and the Horizon Store. The oculus.com domain now redirects to Meta Quest, and developer.oculus.com redirects to the Meta Horizon developer portal.

providers.name: ogenalabs-com
providers.description: Ogenalabs provides automation solutions for AI agents, focusing on blockchain and AI security research. Their platform offers tools to streamline AI agent workflows, integrate secure blockchain technologies, and enhance AI-driven automation. The company emphasizes a mission-driven approach, combining cutting‑edge research with practical product offerings to empower developers and enterprises in building trustworthy AI systems.

providers.name: Onepot
providers.description: Onepot (onepot.ai) is a San Francisco-based startup building an AI-powered, fully automated custom synthesis platform for small-molecule drug discovery. It combines ultra-high-throughput lab automation in its POT-1 lab with an AI organic chemist ("Phil") and reaction foundation models to search, quote, and synthesize make-on-demand molecules end to end, aiming to replace slow, error-prone CRO workflows. Onepot exposes a developer API and a Python client (published on PyPI as "onepot") that lets teams run Tanimoto similarity and SMILES/SMARTS substructure search over the full onepot CORE compound space, perform retrosynthetic decomposition with building-block and price/risk filters, stream real-time results over server-sent events, and place synthesis orders programmatically from their own pipelines using an API key.

providers.name: PLACE
providers.description: PLACE, Inc. is a Bellingham, Washington real estate technology and business-services company founded in 2020 by Ben Kinney and Chris Suarez. It sells an end-to-end operating platform to real estate teams, agents and brokerages — a CRM with lead-generation websites, transaction management, automated marketing, mobile apps and AI tooling — bundled with shared back-office services covering accounting, hiring, training, finance and digital advertising, plus adjacent mortgage, title and escrow, insurance, property management and home-services offerings. PLACE partners with teams in 500+ locations across the United States and Canada, raised a $100M Series A led by a division of Goldman Sachs Asset Management at unicorn valuation, and acquired MLS data platform Remine to extend its technology ecosystem. The platform is delivered only to contracted teams behind single sign-on; PLACE publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Raise
providers.description: Raise is a digital gift card marketplace and commerce platform. Raise for Business exposes the Raise Commerce API — a REST/JSON API that lets partners programmatically browse a catalog of retailer gift card brands, purchase fixed- and variable-load gift cards, check and manage card balances, and reconcile transactions and commissions across 180+ currencies and many countries. Authentication is OAuth 2.0 bearer tokens (server-to-server client credentials, plus app/web auth with SR25519/RSA key pairs, SMS, or TOTP). The API uses a JSON:API-style data envelope, page-based pagination, request metadata, and client_order_id idempotency. Prior investors include Accel, PayPal, and NEA.

providers.name: RedwoodJS
providers.description: Full-stack JavaScript framework with a built-in GraphQL API layer (Yoga + Envelop stack), schema-first development, and automatic SDL generation for Prisma-backed services.

providers.name: Revelio Labs
providers.description: Revelio Labs is a workforce intelligence company that builds a universal HR database from public professional profiles, job postings, employee reviews, and WARN layoff notices. It maps more than 1.1 billion profiles across 20 million+ companies and 5,000+ skills into standardized datasets covering workforce dynamics (headcount, hiring and attrition flows, transitions), job postings (the COSMOS dataset), sentiment, layoffs, and individual-level user, position, education, and skill files. The data is delivered through a REST API, bulk data feeds, and an interactive dashboard, letting investors, corporations, and researchers analyze companies, labor markets, and talent trends in near real time.

providers.name: Scaled Agile
providers.description: Scaled Agile, Inc. is the provider of SAFe® (Scaled Agile Framework), the world's leading framework for business agility at scale. SAFe helps organizations plan better, work smarter, deliver faster, and scale sustainably by aligning people, processes, and technology. The framework provides guidance for enterprise agile transformation across software development, hardware, and business operations, with over 2 million trained professionals in more than 20,000 organizations worldwide. SAFe 6.0 incorporates AI-Empowered Agility as a core element of the framework.

providers.name: SwiftComply
providers.description: SwiftComply is a cloud compliance-management platform for water utilities and municipalities, used by more than 700 organizations across North America to run their Backflow prevention, Stormwater (MS4), Industrial Pretreatment, and FOG (Fats, Oils, and Grease) programs. The software replaces paper and spreadsheet workflows with online program management, direct customer and service-provider reporting, real-time compliance dashboards, audit-ready timestamped record keeping, and pre-configured state reporting. SwiftComply advertises API integrations with GIS, utility billing, and other municipal platforms, and has held SOC 2 Type II certification since October 2021. The company was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company; this profile is maintained by the API Evangelist network. No public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable API description was found during enrichment.

providers.name: TimeSolv
providers.description: TimeSolv provides cloud‑based time tracking, billing, and practice management software for law firms and professional services. Its platform automates billable hour capture, invoicing, trust accounting, client portal, and integrates with QuickBooks, Xero, NetDocuments, Dropbox, LawPay and AI tools. TimeSolv aims to improve efficiency, compliance, and revenue visibility for legal practices.

providers.name: Trope
providers.description: Trope is an AI-native platform that helps ERP implementation partners deliver successful implementations faster, deploying AI agents across discovery, requirements, fit-gap analysis, data migration, approval workflows, UAT scripts, training guides, documentation, and go-live readiness — built for Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central consultancies and other implementation teams. Trope also maintains Trope CUA, an open-source MCP-native computer-use agent for background desktop automation on Windows and macOS. Y Combinator Summer 2026 batch, based in San Francisco.

providers.name: U.S. Access Board
providers.description: The U.S. Access Board is an independent federal agency that promotes equality for people with disabilities through the development of accessibility guidelines and standards. The Board develops criteria for accessibility in the built environment, transportation, communication, and information and communication technology (ICT). It enforces the Architectural Barriers Act (ABA) for federally funded facilities and provides technical assistance, training, and guidance documents to help organizations implement accessibility requirements under the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) and Section 508 of the Rehabilitation Act.

providers.name: UCSI University
providers.description: UCSI University is a private, multi-campus university in Kuala Lumpur, Terengganu and Sarawak, Malaysia, established in 1986 and ranked #265 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. It operates no developer portal, no public API programme, no open data portal, no institutional repository on its own domain and no verifiable public code: the GitHub organisations matching "UCSI" carry no identifying metadata and zero public repositories. Its entire ucsiuniversity.edu.my estate — the main site, the library services site, the Koha catalogue, the IIS student portal, the alumni and mobile hosts — sits behind a Cloudflare bot-management challenge that answers HTTP 403 to every automated client, including one presenting full browser headers, so nothing hosted by the institution can be read programmatically. Three surfaces are nonetheless established off-host: a Microsoft Entra ID tenant (3c5f2d31-81d8-4455-a2bf-531fbc398144, branded "UCSI University") whose SAML 2.0 and OpenID Connect metadata are publicly retrievable and which is the institution's own identity provider; a CourseNetworking learning-management tenancy at ucsi.thecn.com that lms.ucsiuniversity.edu.my redirects into; and a ROR registration. UCSI is NOT in eduGAIN and holds no entity in Malaysia's SIFULAN federation, and no Crossref or DataCite membership exists under its name. The Koha library catalogue is institution-operated and may expose OAI-PMH, ILS-DI or REST services, but that cannot be confirmed through the bot challenge and is recorded as unverifiable rather than as either present or absent.

providers.name: ugc-fans
providers.description: ugc-fans is a platform that enables creators and fans to connect through user‑generated content. It offers tools for content sharing, monetization, and community engagement. The service provides APIs for managing user profiles, media uploads, fan interactions, and payment processing, allowing developers to integrate UGC functionality into their applications.

providers.name: unitQ
providers.description: unitQ is an AI-powered customer feedback and product quality platform founded in 2018 and backed by Accel and Creandum. It unifies feedback from support tickets, app-store reviews, social channels, and surveys into a real-time quality signal (the unitQ Score) across products including monitorQ, supportQ, metricQ, socialQ, competeQ, interviewQ, and agentQ. unitQ publicly names a User Feedback Upload API for ingesting feedback data and a Data Enrichment API for attaching user attributes, platform details, and KPIs such as CSAT and NPS to feedback; the API reference lives in its login-gated help center.

providers.name: Valence Security
providers.description: Valence Security is the leader in SaaS and AI Security, built for the agentic era. The platform provides SaaS security posture management (SSPM), AI security posture management (AI-SPM), identity threat detection and response (ITDR), and risk remediation across 175+ SaaS and AI applications including Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, Salesforce, Okta, GitHub, OpenAI, and Anthropic.

providers.name: Vida Health
providers.description: Vida Health is a San Francisco-based virtual care company founded in 2014 that combines an AI-powered mobile app with a national network of licensed clinicians, coaches and therapists to prevent, manage and reverse chronic cardiometabolic and behavioral health conditions including obesity, diabetes, hypertension, depression and anxiety. Vida sells a turnkey enterprise programme to employers and health plans, layering GLP-1 prescribing and clinical oversight on top of behavioral coaching, and its platform ingests real-time readings from more than 100 connected devices and consumer health apps to feed outcome reporting back to its enterprise buyers. Vida publishes no public developer portal or API documentation: the API host api.vida.com is live but returns 401 on every path, and data/EHR integration for health plans and employers is arranged through enterprise sales rather than self-service onboarding.

providers.name: Western And Southern Financial
providers.description: Western & Southern Financial Group is a diversified family of financial services companies headquartered in Cincinnati, Ohio, offering life insurance, annuities, mutual funds, asset management, and other financial products through multiple subsidiary brands including Western & Southern Life, Gerber Life, Columbus Life, and Fort Washington Investment Advisors.

providers.name: Wynd Network
providers.description: Wynd Network (now operating as Wynd Labs) is the company behind Grass, a decentralized physical infrastructure network (DePIN) on Solana that rewards users for sharing their unused internet bandwidth. The Grass Network routes and verifies web traffic through a network of nodes, routers, and validators to collect and structure public web data for AI training and business intelligence. Grass ships consumer apps and a node network rather than a public developer API; its documentation covers network architecture, the GRASS token, staking, and points.

providers.name: Xoom
providers.description: Xoom is PayPal's international money transfer (remittance) service, operating since 2001. Consumers use Xoom to send money to bank accounts, debit cards, mobile wallets, UPI, and PIX, send cash for pickup or delivery, and reload mobile phones in countries around the world, with up-front fees and exchange rates. U.S. transfers are provided by PayPal, Inc., a licensed money transmitter; UK/EEA service is provided by PayPal (Europe) S.a r.l., regulated by the Luxembourg CSSF. Xoom is a consumer service and publishes no public developer API on the xoom.com domain.

providers.name: Yash12007
providers.description: Yash12007 is a software development company offering next‑gen solutions including 3D Studio, advanced antivirus (SERA 3.0), and real‑time analytics (Metrica). It provides cloud platform services, customizable pricing, and a suite of products aimed at modern enterprise architectures and consumer tools, empowering minds through elegant software design.

providers.name: Zafran Security
providers.description: Zafran Security is an AI-native threat exposure management (CTEM) platform for security teams buried in vulnerabilities and manual remediation work. It brings vulnerability findings together across an organization's existing scanners and tools to create a unified view of exposure across the hybrid enterprise, then determines actual exploitability by analyzing runtime presence, internet reachability, and existing compensating controls. Zafran maps vulnerabilities to controls the team already owns to mitigate risk before patching, and its RemOps capability uses generative AI to consolidate overlapping CVEs into a clear get-well plan routed to the right owners through existing ticketing platforms. The platform is delivered as a SaaS product accessed at api.zafran.io behind Descope-based authentication with API-key access for integrations (Axonius, Palo Alto Cortex XSOAR); it does not publish a public developer portal or OpenAPI. Zafran is backed by Menlo Ventures.

providers.name: Alkira
providers.description: Alkira delivers Network Infrastructure as a Service (NaaS) through its Cloud Services Exchange, letting enterprises build, deploy, and manage a global multi-cloud network from a unified portal without provisioning physical hardware. The platform connects clouds, sites, remote users, and SaaS through Cloud Exchange Points (CXPs) with built-in segmentation, routing, integrated firewall/security services (Palo Alto, Fortinet, Check Point, Cisco, Zscaler, Infoblox, F5), and full-stack visibility. Everything provisioned in the portal is driven by the Alkira Portal REST API and exposed as infrastructure-as-code via an official Terraform provider, a Go client library, and a published Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for AI agents.

providers.name: ApiNotes
providers.description: ApiNotes is an interactive API documentation tool that generates developer portals with live endpoint testing, code examples in multiple languages, and shareable documentation from OpenAPI and Swagger specifications.

providers.name: App Onboard
providers.description: AppOnBoard, Inc. is a Los Angeles-based technology company founded in 2016 that builds AI-driven creative and advertising tools for app and game marketers. Its best-known product is Buildbox, a no-code platform for making games and apps without programming, and its current flagship is Quvy, an AI ad-creation and testing platform that generates static, video, and concept ad variations and predicts their performance against synthetic audiences before any real ad spend. Quvy targets marketers, indie and studio game developers, SaaS companies, and brands that want to replace slow, expensive A/B testing and agencies with fast simulation-based creative optimization. AppOnBoard is backed by 500 Global; its original apponboard.com domain now redirects to the Quvy product at quvy.com. This profile carries the company identity and website properties; AppOnBoard publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or OpenAPI at this time.

providers.name: Arsaze
providers.description: Arsaze is an AI-native video editor for agents and humans. It provides a cursor-like interface for video editing, enabling AI-driven multi-track timeline edits, versioned changes, and client review on exact frames.

providers.name: BKK Staff
providers.description: BKK Staff provides a hiring assistant service for small businesses, screening job applications, following up with candidates, and delivering a shortlist of interview‑ready applicants. Priced at $99 per open position for 30 days with no monthly fees, the platform supports multiple languages and integrates via email or Slack notifications. It aims to simplify hiring for owners and small HR teams by handling applicant communication and qualification without acting as a job board or recruitment agency.

providers.name: Bloomfilter
providers.description: Bloomfilter is a process intelligence platform that gives enterprises end-to-end visibility, traceability, and control over how AI agents and humans execute software delivery work. It unifies data across development and design tools such as Jira, GitHub, Azure DevOps, and Figma into a structured, AI-enabled data stream and builds a connected process graph across the software development lifecycle. Teams use Bloomfilter to govern hybrid human-agent workflows through process mining, compliance monitoring, cycle-time analysis, and performance measurement, so leaders can see how work actually flows and where value is created or lost. The company is a Techstars portfolio company and was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead for enrichment.

providers.name: Bookmax
providers.description: Bookmax is an online bookmark manager founded in 2003, offering free and premium accounts for storing bookmarks, lists, contacts, notes, documents and RSS feeds. It operates from Austria with servers in Germany, provides web, iOS and Android access, and includes features like folder organization, tagging, and synchronization across devices.

providers.name: Botika
providers.description: Botika is an AI fashion-photography platform that helps online clothing and e-commerce brands replace traditional model photoshoots with generative AI. It turns flat-lay, mannequin, and basic on-model product photos into studio-quality images featuring fully AI-generated fashion models, poses, and on-brand backgrounds. Founded by Eran Dagan and Yarin Didi Meir and backed by an $8M seed round with participation from Seedcamp, Botika ships a web console, a native Shopify app, and an iOS app, cutting photoshoot costs by up to 90% and speeding time-to-market roughly 3x. A public API is on the company roadmap but is not yet released, so this profile currently captures company identity and public web properties rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: By Miles
providers.description: By Miles is a London-based insurtech that pioneered pay-by-mile motor insurance in the United Kingdom, founded in 2016 for low-mileage drivers who cover under roughly 7,000 miles a year. Its single line of business is UK private motor (personal lines property and casualty), priced as a fixed annual premium covering the parked car plus a per-mile charge for the distance actually driven. Mileage is measured either by the OBD-II "Miles Tracker" telematics dongle or, on its "connect" trackerless policies, by pulling odometer data directly from the manufacturer's connected-car platform after the driver links a Tesla, Ford or Mercedes-Benz account. By Miles was acquired by Direct Line Group in April 2023 and, following Aviva's acquisition of Direct Line Group, has been wound down — it stopped quoting new business and, from 6 January 2026, stopped offering renewal quotes to existing customers. Its API posture is that of a pure API CONSUMER, not a producer: it was the first UK insurtech directly authorised by the FCA as an AISP/PISP to consume Open Banking APIs (January 2020), and it consumes OEM connected-car APIs for mileage, but it publishes no public self-serve developer portal, no reference documentation, no OpenAPI, no Postman collection and no webhook catalogue. The only integration surface is a partnerships email address and a private AWS API Gateway host serving its own mobile app, so this record is a partner-gated stub by design.

providers.name: CiviCRM
providers.description: CiviCRM is an open-source constituent relationship management (CRM) platform designed for non-profit, civic sector, and advocacy organizations. It provides a web-based suite of tools for managing contacts, fundraising, events, memberships, email communications, and case management, integrating with popular content management systems like WordPress, Joomla, and Drupal. The platform is community-driven, extensible via extensions, and supports multilingual deployments, helping organizations engage supporters and streamline operations.

providers.name: CrowdMade
providers.description: CrowdMade partners with online creators from YouTube, Instagram, Snapchat and beyond to design, produce, warehouse, and ship official merchandise their fans are proud to wear. The public storefront at crowdmade.com runs on Shopify and, as of 2026, exposes a machine- and agent-facing commerce surface: a published Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) MCP shopping endpoint, Shopify Customer Accounts OpenID Connect / OAuth discovery documents, an llms.txt, and an agents.md describing how AI shopping agents can search the catalog, build a cart, and complete a buyer-approved checkout. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and profiled into the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: DERATE
providers.description: DERATE provides a mobile app that scans truck dashboard or scanner codes (SPN/FMI) to instantly diagnose faults, estimate repair costs, and generate work orders. Available on iOS and upcoming on Android, it targets drivers, operators, and owner‑operators seeking quick, accurate fault code interpretation without specialized equipment. The service offers free usage with optional paid plans for advanced features.

providers.name: Dresser House
providers.description: Dresser House is a UK‑based retailer specialising in chests of drawers, bedside chests, tallboys and related bedroom furniture. The online store offers a curated range of products from multiple brands, providing detailed specifications, pricing and stock information directly sourced from suppliers. Customers can browse categories, read buying guides such as “How to choose chests of drawers”, and purchase items with delivery across the United Kingdom. The site emphasizes comparison of features and values to help shoppers make informed decisions.

providers.name: DSGVO.pro
providers.description: DSGVO.pro offers a free compliance scanner for German websites, checking up to 33 GDPR‑related modules such as DSGVO, TDDDG, KI‑VO, BFSG and BGB. The tool runs in about 60 seconds without registration, generating cookie‑banners and compliance reports. It aims to help site owners avoid fines by providing automated privacy audits and detailed legal references.

providers.name: Dukaan
providers.description: Dukaan is an enterprise e-commerce platform, built by Growthpond Technology Private Limited (India), that lets businesses launch and run online stores without code. The platform bundles a store builder with curated themes, catalog and order management, pan-India logistics via Dukaan Delivery, payments, and an extendable plugin ecosystem. Dukaan's public developer surface is its Themes platform: a documented theming system (docs.mydukaan.io) built on HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and the Nunjucks templating language, with a "Dukaan Data" store-object model, "Dukaan Functions", and first-party plugins (wishlist, countdown timer, product scarcity). Dukaan does not publish a public REST/OpenAPI programmatic API; its extensibility is theme- and plugin-oriented rather than API-first. Added to the API Evangelist network from the Lightspeed Venture Partners portfolio.

providers.name: Eastman Kodak
providers.description: Eastman Kodak Company is a global commercial printing and imaging company that provides hardware, software, consumables, and services to customers in the print, packaging, publishing, manufacturing, and entertainment industries. Kodak does not currently publish a public developer program or API portfolio.

providers.name: Eden Health
providers.description: Eden Health was a primary and virtual care company that delivered app-based medical care, behavioral health, and care navigation to employers and their employees, integrating with health systems and insurers (backed by Insight Partners). It was surfaced as an Insight Partners portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. Its public marketing site is no longer reachable over TLS, but its primary backend service — the "Grdn" (Guardian) API at api.edenhealth.com — still serves a Swagger 2.0 description covering patients, appointments, membership, documents, care teams, and clinician tooling.

providers.name: Eindhoven University of Technology
providers.description: Eindhoven University of Technology (TU/e) is a public technical university in Eindhoven, the Netherlands, and one of the four institutions of the 4TU federation. It operates no public developer portal, publishes no institution-authored API contract, and offers no self-serve API keys — and this profile says so rather than padding the gap. Everything machine-readable that carries the TU/e name is a deployment of somebody else's software: the TU/e Research Portal and its Pure Web Service REST API are Elsevier Pure 5.35.x running at pure.tue.nl, the student mobile app at osiris.tue.nl is Caci Osiris, library discovery is OCLC WorldCat, and research datasets are minted through the 4TU.ResearchData Figshare consortium. What TU/e genuinely operates on its own domain is narrower and real: a live, fully conformant OAI-PMH 2.0 harvesting endpoint at pure.tue.nl/ws/oai serving seven metadata formats and the OpenAIRE CERIF 1.2 CRIS profile, and a SAML 2.0 identity-provider entity registered in the SURFconext federation and so reachable through eduGAIN. Thirty-seven OpenAPI documents previously attributed to TU/e in this repository were Elsevier's Pure product contract (info.title "Pure …", contact pure-support@elsevier.com, relative servers "/ws/api", shipped identically by nine other universities) and have been removed; the tenant relationships they described are recorded here instead. Departmental research groups publish open source across many separate GitHub organizations, but the university runs no single official engineering org.

providers.name: Frends
providers.description: Frends is an integration platform as a service (iPaaS) that provides enterprise-grade API and integration capabilities.

providers.name: Fylamynt
providers.description: Fylamynt is a comprehensive cloud orchestration, automation and response platform that unifies case management, automation, real-time collaboration and incident remediation. It serves cloud engineering teams across the incident lifecycle, orchestrating across hundreds of cloud products to standardize and automate processes for faster response times and increased team productivity.

providers.name: HTTPX
providers.description: HTTPX is a fully featured HTTP client for Python 3 with sync and async APIs, HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 support. It is broadly compatible with the popular requests library while adding modern features such as strict timeouts, type annotations, direct WSGI and ASGI transport, SSL verification, cookie persistence, proxy support, and multipart uploads.

providers.name: HyBird
providers.description: HyBird is an industrial software company behind Clarity, a modular Industrial Operating System built on a self-updating, photorealistic living digital twin. Clarity unifies 3D twin and document management, engineering and management of change, P&ID management, intelligent (preventive, predictive, reactive) maintenance, EHS, robotic inspection with AI defect detection, structural integrity, asset performance monitoring, and an AR-guided connected workforce for heavy industries such as oil & gas, cement and building materials, energy, terminals, and nuclear. It integrates with EAM/CMMS platforms including SAP PM, S/4HANA, Microsoft Dynamics, and IBM Maximo. HyBird is a Techstars-backed company profiled in the API Evangelist network; it publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs at this time.

providers.name: Imper
providers.description: Imper (imper.ai) is a workforce identity-verification and impersonation-defense platform that detects and prevents social-engineering and AI-driven deception attacks across the entire employee lifecycle. Rather than guarding against unauthorized break-ins, Imper confirms that the person on a call, video meeting, candidate interview, help-desk request, or account-recovery flow is the real, authorized employee. Its agentless engine analyzes network, device, and digital identity markers combined with organizational context, and pairs an impersonation-detection layer that spots attacker-controlled environments with an AI-driven contextual verification layer that confirms real employees through dynamic, work-based questioning. Imper integrates natively with ITSM, HR, and ATS systems (Workday, Greenhouse, ServiceNow and more) to enforce identity assurance at high-risk lifecycle events such as hiring, enrollment, help-desk support, and continuous verification. Founded in 2022 and headquartered in Tel Aviv, the company is backed by Redpoint Ventures, Battery Ventures, Maple Capital, Vesey Ventures, and Cerca Partners.

providers.name: Lemni
providers.description: Lemni provides a platform to set up custom AI agents quickly, enabling businesses to personalize customer interactions across channels such as phone, email, and proactive outreach. The service promises to scale interactions without increasing headcount, offering a free trial and emphasizing ease of deployment for enterprises seeking to enhance support and engagement.

providers.name: Lexion
providers.description: Lexion is an AI-powered contract lifecycle management (CLM) platform that centralizes agreements in an intelligent repository, extracts key terms and dates, and drives no-code intake and approval workflows across legal, sales, procurement, finance, and HR. Founded in 2019 out of the Allen Institute for AI, Lexion was acquired by Docusign in May 2024 for ~$165M and folded into Docusign's Intelligent Agreement Management (IAM) platform and Docusign Navigator. Lexion exposes an enterprise, sales-led integration API but does not publish a self-serve, openly documented public API.

providers.name: Lord & Taylor
providers.description: Lord & Taylor is one of the oldest American department-store apparel and home-goods retail brands, now operating as a direct-to-consumer online store at lordandtaylor.com. The storefront runs on the Shopify commerce platform, so its public, agent-accessible API surface is the Shopify commerce stack: OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect customer authentication (issued via Shopify Customer Accounts) plus two hosted Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers — an unauthenticated Storefront MCP exposing product search, cart, product-detail and store-policy tools, and an OAuth-protected Customer Account MCP exposing order-status, return-request and store-credit tools. Surfaced into the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub and enriched from live discovery documents and MCP tool listings.

providers.name: Microsoft Sway
providers.description: Microsoft Sway is a presentation and storytelling application that enables creating interactive, web-based content. It integrates with Microsoft 365 for sharing and embedding interactive presentations, newsletters, and reports across an organization.

providers.name: Mimo
providers.description: Mimo is an interactive coding education platform that teaches programming languages such as Python, JavaScript, HTML, and CSS through gamified lessons. Founded in 2014 in Vienna, Austria, it offers mobile and web apps for learners to build real‑world skills at their own pace. Backed by Techstars, Mimo serves millions of users worldwide.

providers.name: Monograph
providers.description: Monograph is firm-management software purpose-built for architecture and engineering (A&E) practices, unifying project management, resourcing and staffing, time tracking, budgeting, invoicing and client payments in one connected system. Used by thousands of US-based A&E firms, it integrates with QuickBooks Online, Stripe, Google Workspace and Microsoft 365, but publishes no public developer API, webhooks, or SDKs. Backed by Homebrew and Index Ventures.

providers.name: Obligate
providers.description: Obligate (formerly FQX) is a Swiss digital-securities infrastructure provider for regulated on-chain debt capital markets. Its AssetOS platform lets companies issue tokenized bonds and short-term notes as blockchain-based eNotes and eTrackers under the Swiss DLT Act and Code of Obligations, while institutional investors access regulated on-chain private credit, asset-backed securities and trade-finance yield products. Obligate automates the bond lifecycle with smart contracts across multiple blockchains, with built-in KYB/KYC, settlement and enforcement, reducing issuance cost and time versus traditional debt issuance.

providers.name: Orolabs
providers.description: ORO Labs provides an agentic procurement orchestration platform for enterprise spend management. It coordinates people, processes, systems, and data so employees can get what they need without friction, unifying intake management, supplier onboarding and lifecycle, risk and compliance orchestration, and AI-driven workflow automation. The platform offers a no-code workflow builder, a purpose-built agent builder for custom procurement AI agents, and bring-your-own-LLM flexibility, with secure, semantically rich integrations across the procuretech landscape. ORO Labs is backed by Felicis and Norwest Venture Partners.

providers.name: Outfunnel
providers.description: Outfunnel provides a sales and marketing workflow platform that synchronizes CRM data with email, spreadsheet, and other marketing tools, automating data flow to eliminate manual work. The service offers features such as contact syncing, engagement tracking, lead forms, integrations with popular apps, pricing plans for startups to enterprises, a help center, blog, and resources. It aims to give sales teams more context and streamline marketing operations across platforms.

providers.name: Pingdom
providers.description: Pingdom is a website uptime and performance monitoring service from SolarWinds that tracks availability, response time, transactions, real user monitoring, and page speed from a global network of probe servers. It alerts teams via email, SMS, webhooks, and integrations when websites, APIs, or critical user journeys experience downtime or degraded performance. The Pingdom Public REST API (v3.1) provides programmatic access to checks, results, alerts, contacts, maintenance windows, and reports using Bearer token authentication.

providers.name: Rentvine
providers.description: Rentvine is a modern property management platform offering a fully open RESTful API for managing properties, leases, tenants, maintenance requests, financials, and owner portals. The API provides real-time data access and supports custom integrations, workflow automation, and third-party software connectivity. API access is included with all subscriptions at no additional cost, with no usage restrictions or rate limit quotas published.

providers.name: Royco
providers.description: Royco is a decentralized finance (DeFi) protocol offering transparent, structured yield markets for capital allocators. Through Royco Dawn, users allocate capital into tranched yield markets - senior tranches prioritize base yield with first-loss protection, junior tranches accept first loss for amplified yield - or delegate allocation to independent curators via vaults, with Loop leverage and a coming secondary market and fixed-rate structures. All deposits flow through the RoycoEntryPoint gateway, deployed on Ethereum and Avalanche, with critical upgrades gated by 3-of-5 council approval and timelocks. The protocol has undergone 5 independent audits and formal verifications (Hexens, Cantina, Certora, Nethermind, Immunefi) and ships an official TypeScript SDK plus subgraphs for building frontends on top of it.

providers.name: Siebly
providers.description: Siebly provides JavaScript, Node.js, and TypeScript SDKs for major cryptocurrency exchanges such as Binance, Bybit, OKX, Gate, Bitget, KuCoin, Coinbase, Kraken, HTX, and Hyperliquid. The platform offers REST and WebSocket API integrations, comprehensive documentation, examples, and release notes, enabling developers to build trading applications quickly and securely.

providers.name: sigit-si
providers.description: siGit is a Git hosting platform for the AI era, offering versioned repositories and open‑weights model storage with full model cards and LFS‑backed files. It provides a unified UI where code and large AI models coexist, enabling developers to manage source code and massive model weights side‑by‑side. The platform exposes an Agent Client Protocol that lets AI coding agents interact directly with repositories, simplifying integration of AI workflows into standard development pipelines.

providers.name: Skechers U.S.A.
providers.description: Skechers U.S.A. is an American lifestyle and performance footwear company (Fortune 500) that designs, develops, and markets a diverse range of footwear for men, women, and children across 170+ countries. Skechers operates direct-to-consumer digital commerce through its website and mobile app, wholesale partnerships with retailers, and a global network of owned and franchised retail stores. Their digital commerce infrastructure relies on e-commerce APIs for product catalog management, inventory, order management, customer accounts, and loyalty programs.

providers.name: Solvo.ai
providers.description: Solvo.ai is a revenue-orchestration company building the decision layer for revenue management in container logistics. Its live pricing engine ingests market rates, capacity manifests, booking history, port congestion, customer behaviour and contract terms, then uses models trained on tens of millions of historical bookings to produce a ranked, capacity-aware rate recommendation per lane, equipment type and segment. Trade managers accept, adjust or override these recommendations on Solvo's Decision HUB, and every decision feeds back as training signal through a bidirectional integration with the carrier's commercial stack. Founded in 2021 and backed by Speedinvest, Solvo positions itself as the only proven, live pricing engine built specifically for container shipping, with one of the world's top carriers in production. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a Speedinvest portfolio company; Solvo currently publishes a marketing and insights site only, with no public API, developer documentation, SDKs or specifications.

providers.name: STACK
providers.description: STACK Construction Technologies makes cloud-based preconstruction software for on-screen takeoff and estimating used by contractors across most trades. STACK does expose a real, documented REST API (v2), but access is gated - you must be a STACK customer on an API-Enabled Subscription (or an approved partner) to obtain credentials. Authentication is OAuth 2.0, offered as two-legged (client-credentials, server-to-server) and three-legged (authorization-code, on behalf of a user) flows. Tokens are issued by a per-tenant authorization server (base pattern https://{server}/api/v2). The full endpoint reference sits behind an access request; the API surface catalogued here is modeled from STACK's public developer overview, authentication guide, and tutorials - it is not sourced from an official machine-readable OpenAPI document.

providers.name: Synop
providers.description: Synop is a software platform for commercial electric vehicle fleet charging and energy management, describing itself as "the operating system for commercial EV fleets." Its hardware- and software-agnostic platform integrates vehicles, chargers, and the grid across the U.S. and Europe, spanning charge management (remote charger control, real-time alerts, EVSE interoperability across 100+ charging station models), energy management (AI-based load and time-of-use optimization, curtailment, demand response, and vehicle-to-grid events), vehicle management (state-of-charge and efficiency via telematics), payment management (billing, driver reimbursement, and transaction reporting), utility management, and SynopLink edge connectivity for site-level operations. Synop cites 500+ MWh under management across 800+ commercial depots. Its API integrations surface live time-of-use rate data and export reimbursement data to accounting and expense systems, though the developer documentation is a password-gated ReadMe admin guide rather than a public developer portal.

providers.name: The Clinician
providers.description: The Clinician is a New Zealand-headquartered digital health company whose product, The Clinician Platform (TCP, formerly ZEDOC), is an outcomes-intelligence layer for value-based healthcare. TCP captures patient-reported outcome and experience measures (PROMs, PREMs, CROMs) omnichannel over SMS, email, web and native mobile in 20+ languages, scores and benchmarks them automatically against MCID thresholds, runs configurable digital care pathways with a threshold-triggered alert engine, and returns outcomes to the EMR via FHIR. It sits alongside an EMR/PAS rather than replacing it, and the company markets an API-driven architecture aligned with HL7 FHIR (incl. SMART-on-FHIR), HL7 v2.x, openEHR and DICOM, plus an OMOP Clinical Events API. No public API reference, developer portal or machine-readable contract is published — API access runs through an enterprise sales engagement.

providers.name: The Giving Block
providers.description: The Giving Block is a crypto-native fundraising platform that lets nonprofits and enterprises accept cryptocurrency, stock, and card donations. Through its Public API and embeddable donation widget, partners can build their own donation experiences or embed The Giving Block's donation form to route gifts to more than 1,000 nonprofit organizations in its network. The API securely accepts Bitcoin, Ethereum, and 100+ other cryptocurrencies, instantly converts crypto donations to cash so nonprofits never have to touch crypto, and also supports stock and donor-advised-fund (DAF) giving. It is a RESTful, JSON API with JWT-based authentication, AES-256 encrypted webhook notifications, and separate production and sandbox environments. The Giving Block was surfaced as a portfolio company of Multicoin Capital and enriched into the API Evangelist network from its published developer documentation.

providers.name: Tresata
providers.description: Tresata is a Charlotte, North Carolina enterprise software company building what it describes as the foundational data layer for agentic AI. Its platform is marketed under the product names AB (Asset Builder), AU (Unreal Data Engine) and AF (Agent Foundation), alongside the Deduce and Discover surfaces, and automates data accuracy, entity resolution and enrichment across AWS, Azure and Google Cloud with a low-code interface. Pricing is usage-based, metered in Tresata Transaction Units (TTUs). Tresata publishes first-party open-source Scala/Spark libraries under the com.tresata group on Maven Central and co-authors the NANDini research effort with MIT on decentralised agentic data architectures. As of this profile it operates no public developer program: the platform is reached only through a login-gated tenant application, and no API reference, OpenAPI, GraphQL SDL, AsyncAPI or other machine-readable contract is published on any Tresata host.

providers.name: Tridge
providers.description: Tridge is a South Korea-headquartered global agri-food trade intelligence and sourcing platform. It combines a data layer of structured cross-border trade, price, production, seasonality and weather data (the company cites 682M+ trade data points and 65M+ price records across 200+ markets), a network layer of verified buyers and suppliers in 190+ countries, and an AI layer that runs trade workflows from discovery through deal closure. Products include Market Curations, Sourcing Hub, Data & Analytics, Tridge Eye (market intelligence) and Tridge Ark (AI-driven export sales outreach). Tridge advertises an API for integrating its global price and trade data into customer systems, but publishes no public developer portal, reference documentation or machine-readable contract — access is arranged through a sales conversation.

providers.name: tweekit-io
providers.description: TweekIT provides a universal file translation service for AI workflows, offering fast, stateless APIs that convert any media type into optimized assets. The platform includes REST and Widget APIs, detailed documentation, pricing plans, and a managed MCP server for seamless integration into AI pipelines.

providers.name: VolunteerLocal
providers.description: VolunteerLocal provides a cloud‑based platform that helps nonprofit organizations manage volunteers, schedule shifts, track hours, and communicate with participants. Its features include volunteer databases, communication tools, scheduling, reporting, and integrations, enabling efficient volunteer program administration.

providers.name: Von
providers.description: Von (vonlabs.ai) is an AI RevOps agent from Rattle Software, the Insight Partners and Sequoia backed team behind gorattle.com, positioned as an AI data scientist for revenue teams. Von connects to CRMs, data warehouses, call recorders, and sales engagement tools - Salesforce, HubSpot, Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, Gong, Outreach, Salesloft, and more, plus 100+ integrations consumed via MCP - to automate pipeline forecasting, win/loss analysis, churn detection, sales coaching, and Salesforce administration. Von publishes no public API or developer program; its security posture is documented at trust.vonlabs.ai (SOC 2 Type 2, SOC 3, ISO 27001, CASA Tier 2).

providers.name: Ziff Davis Enterprise
providers.description: Ziff Davis (Nasdaq: ZD) is a vertically focused digital media and internet company whose portfolio includes leading brands across technology, entertainment, shopping, health, cybersecurity, and marketing technology. Its brands include PCMag, Mashable, IGN, Lifehacker, RetailMeNot, Spiceworks, Everyday Health, IPVanish, Ookla (Speedtest), FullContact, and iContact, among others. The company operates a portfolio of advertising, subscription, and performance-marketing businesses rather than a single first-party public API product. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as an Insight Partners portfolio lead; a public web crawl of the corporate site found an active investor-relations, newsroom, brands, privacy, and terms surface but no developer portal, API reference, or published API specification at the corporate (ziffdavis.com) level. A second enrichment pass on 2026-08-13 ran full contract discovery against www.ziffdavis.com — OpenAPI, Swagger, GraphQL, MCP, llms.txt and every /.well-known/ path returned 404, and the WordPress REST root returned 401 — confirming the absence, while surfacing three real corporate programs: a Bugcrowd-hosted Responsible Vulnerability Disclosure Program, a published data-protection compliance program (Data Privacy Framework self-certification for 32 named group entities, GDPR DPAs, CCPA request metrics, EU DSA statement, NIST SP 800-88 vendor security exhibit), and five first-party PHP packages in the ziffdavis Packagist namespace — none of which is an API client library. Ziff Davis brands with their own API surfaces are profiled as separate entries.

providers.name: Adionics
providers.description: Adionics is a French cleantech company founded in 2012 in Paris by Guillaume de Souza, out of research into liquid-liquid salt extraction started in 2007. It develops and licenses a patented Direct Lithium Extraction (DLE) process built on Flionex, a proprietary, thermally regenerated and highly selective liquid salt absorbent that captures lithium salts from brine at ambient temperature and releases them at higher temperature in a closed loop, with no traditional reagents and more than 90% less water than evaporation ponds. The company sells a staged engagement to mining operators — a proprietary modeling study, a lab-scale bench test, an on-site pilot plant, and basic engineering plus commissioning support for a commercial plant — targeting lithium-rich salars, geothermal brines, oil-and-gas produced water, industrial effluents and battery recycling streams. It has run 1,500 hours of continuous lithium extraction in the Salar de Atacama, opened a pilot test centre in Salta Province, Argentina, and raised roughly $40M across four rounds. Adionics is a process-technology and engineering company, not a software vendor, and publishes no developer portal, no product API, no SDKs and no OpenAPI. The only machine-readable interface it exposes is the WordPress REST content API behind www.adionics.com, which is anonymously readable, read-only for the public, and captured here for discovery.

providers.name: AgentPlaybooks
providers.description: AgentPlaybooks provides a platform for creating, sharing, and deploying AI agent playbooks. It offers self‑hosted documentation, a blog, and tools for integrating with various LLMs and agents. Users can explore use cases, customize skills, and manage MCP servers, all in a vendor‑neutral environment. The site includes resources like documentation, privacy policy, terms, and a GitHub repository for open‑source contributions.

providers.name: Algolab
providers.description: Algolab provides Vietnamese stock market data, AI-driven investment signals, and analysis tools. It offers real-time prices, backtested buy/sell signals, VN-Index forecasts, analytical reports on 50 securities, and an AI assistant via MCP for Claude and ChatGPT. The platform serves investors with data, charts, and AI insights, operated by CTCP Tập đoàn Algospace.

providers.name: Altro Health
providers.description: Altro Health provides a digital health platform that connects patients, providers, and payers to streamline care coordination, telehealth visits, and health data analytics. Founded by a collective of healthcare innovators, the company focuses on improving outcomes through integrated technology solutions and secure data exchange across the healthcare ecosystem.

providers.name: Autofleet
providers.description: Autofleet is a fleet and mobility optimization platform founded in 2018 in Tel Aviv by Kobi Eisenberg and Dor Shay, and since 2024 an independently operated, wholly owned subsidiary of Element Fleet Management Corp. (TSX: EFN). Its AI-driven software plans, dispatches, routes and simulates vehicle-based operations across postal and parcel delivery, last-mile logistics, rental and car sharing, corporate motor pools, microtransit, NEMT and school transport, taxi and rideshare, field service, and autonomous mobility, in more than 20 countries. The platform is sold as an integration hub — Autofleet markets a public API and webhooks for connecting telematics, GPS, keyless access, maintenance, booking, dispatch, CRM and ERP systems — and adds Nova, a fleet-specific generative AI layer for natural-language operational questions. The API gateway is live at api.autofleet.io, but the developer reference at docs.autofleet.io is a password-protected ReadMe hub, so no machine-readable contract is publicly retrievable.

providers.name: Autonomous University of Madrid
providers.description: The Autonomous University of Madrid (Universidad Autónoma de Madrid, UAM) is a public research university in Madrid, Spain, founded in 1968 and ranked #198 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. UAM publishes no developer portal, no API terms and no OpenAPI description of anything, and it issues no API keys — but unlike most institutions in this cohort its machine-readable surfaces are genuinely its own rather than a vendor's contract running under its name. Every host carrying a surface below resolves inside RIPE inetnum 150.244.0.0 – 150.244.255.255, netname UAM, org ORG-UADM1-RIPE, with no CNAME to a vendor platform: UAM licenses DSpace, Open Journal Systems and Moodle and runs them on its own address space. What is anonymously consumable today is the Biblos-e Archivo repository (a DSpace 7.6.5 HAL REST API, an OAI-PMH 2.0 endpoint and an OpenSearch descriptor) and a second OAI-PMH 2.0 endpoint over the university's Open Journal Systems journals portal at revistas.uam.es. Beyond that, UAM operates a Shibboleth service provider on its own repository host, is registered as an identity provider in SIR/eduGAIN through RedIRIS, runs two Moodle instances that publish live LTI 1.3 signing keys, and is a Crossref member minting DOIs under prefix 10.15366. No vendor product specification is stored in this repository: a generic DSpace, OJS or Moodle contract describes the vendor's engineering, not UAM's.

providers.name: AvidXchange
providers.description: AvidXchange is a fintech provider of AI-powered accounts payable (AP) and payment automation software for middle-market businesses. Its platform digitizes invoice capture, approval workflows, purchase orders, and supplier payments, integrating with more than 220 accounting and ERP systems and connecting buyers to a large supplier network for paperless, straight-through AP processing. AvidXchange publishes a partner and integration developer portal (ReadMe-hosted) for connecting ERP systems and building against its payment and invoice automation platform; the API reference is gated behind partner login. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bain Capital Ventures, QED Investors, and Sapphire Ventures and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Betterment
providers.description: Betterment is a robo-advisor and financial planning platform offering automated investment management, tax-loss harvesting, retirement planning, and goal-based portfolio rebalancing. Founded in 2010, Betterment serves individual investors through its Digital and Premium Advisory plans, and employers through Betterment at Work — a 401(k) plan administration product that integrates with 350+ payroll providers via a private partner API. Betterment does not offer a public developer API; third-party application developers access Betterment account data through open banking aggregators such as Plaid and BankSync. Betterment Engineering maintains an active open-source presence on GitHub, publishing internal tools for background job processing, split testing, Flutter golden testing, and Rails security.

providers.name: BILT
providers.description: BILT is a financial technology company offering a loyalty and payments platform that lets members earn rewards on rent and mortgage payments. It provides a co‑branded credit card, rent‑payment reporting to credit bureaus, and a suite of neighborhood benefits, aiming to transform housing expenses into valuable points and perks for users.

providers.name: BioAegis Therapeutics
providers.description: BioAegis Therapeutics, Inc. is a privately held, clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered at the NJ Bioscience Center in North Brunswick, New Jersey. Founded in 2011 around the discovery work of the late Dr. Thomas P. Stossel at Harvard Medical School and Brigham and Women's Hospital, the company develops recombinant human plasma gelsolin (rhu-pGSN) — a protein replacement therapy built on plasma gelsolin (pGSN), an abundant naturally occurring human blood protein that acts as a master regulator of the innate immune response by keeping inflammation localized to the site of injury and boosting the body's ability to clear pathogens. Its lead programme, BTI-203, is a 600-patient, 75-site, 13-country randomized double-blind placebo-controlled Phase 2 study of rhu-pGSN in moderate-to-severe acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), supported by a $20M BARDA DRIVe contract (75A50123C00067); a second Phase 2 programme targets inflammasome-driven decompression sickness under a U.S. Navy Office of Naval Research contract with the University of Maryland School of Medicine. The FDA has granted Fast Track designation for both ARDS and DCS indications. BioAegis holds an exclusive worldwide license from Brigham and Women's Hospital and more than 40 issued patents spanning inflammatory disease, infection, renal failure, neurologic disease and frailty. BioAegis Therapeutics runs no developer program and publishes no product API, developer portal or API documentation. The only machine-readable surface reachable without credentials is the WordPress REST content API behind www.bioaegistherapeutics.com, catalogued here.

providers.name: Bloomberg Television and Radio
providers.description: Bloomberg Television is a 24-hour global business and financial news television network, while Bloomberg Radio provides all-news financial radio coverage. Bloomberg TV and Radio deliver breaking market news, interviews with business leaders, economic analysis, and market commentary. Content is distributed via cable, satellite, streaming, and digital platforms globally.

providers.name: Bloomberg TV
