Swimm also runs large-scale modernization engagements (.NET, Java, monolith-to-microservices, and mainframe/COBOL). Swimm publishes product documentation, a getting-started guide, IDE and CI integrations, and a GitHub organization, but does not expose a public REST/developer API, SDK packages, or OpenAPI specification at this time.

providers.name: ThreeFlow
providers.description: ThreeFlow (WatchTower Technologies, Inc. dba ThreeFlow) is a benefits placement system (BPS) for employee-benefits brokers and insurance carriers, bringing quoting, RFPs, analysis, renewals, and presentation into one shared workflow. Its ThreeFlow Connect integration layer automates placement data flow across broker AMS, carrier, and partner systems. The platform reports $3.7B+ premium under management, 450+ broker locations, and 75+ certified carriers, and is SOC 2 Type 2 and HITRUST E1 certified. Developer documentation is partner-gated; a public status page monitors the Broker Portal, Carrier Portal, and API.

providers.name: TiLT
providers.description: Tilt is a leave management platform that helps companies manage employee leave in-house. The service offers a suite of tools including a leave planner, HR reporting dashboard, and integration capabilities. Tilt emphasizes a human-centered approach to leave, providing resources such as research guides, case studies, and a blog. It offers pricing plans, broker partnerships, and a demo request option. The platform aims to simplify leave administration while ensuring compliance and employee satisfaction.

providers.name: tubexperto-com
providers.description: TubExperto provides AI-powered experts that analyze entire YouTube channels, delivering precise answers with exact video timestamps. It offers creators and viewers advanced tools to extract insights, transcriptions, and summaries from video content using artificial intelligence, enhancing engagement and accessibility across platforms.

providers.name: tyntec
providers.description: tyntec is a CPaaS (Communications Platform as a Service) provider whose api.tyntec.com REST APIs let businesses verify, authenticate, and engage mobile consumers worldwide. The platform covers phone number verification and number information (Verify API plus HLR lookup and global number portability), SMS messaging, WhatsApp Business and other chat-app channels via the Conversations API, and two-factor authentication / one-time passwords via the 2FA API. tyntec is an authorized WhatsApp Business Solution Provider. All APIs authenticate with an account API key sent in the apikey request header; tyntec publishes OpenAPI definitions for them in the public tyntec/api-collection GitHub repository.

providers.name: Weis Markets
providers.description: Weis Markets is a regional supermarket chain operating grocery stores in the mid-Atlantic United States, with 197 store locations across Pennsylvania, Maryland, Delaware, New Jersey, New York, Virginia, and West Virginia. The company operates a digital commerce platform, loyalty rewards program (Weis Rewards), mobile app, and vendor/supplier integration ecosystem using EDI and supply chain APIs. Weis Markets uses Toshiba ELERA commerce platform for unified in-store and online commerce.

providers.name: Ylookup
providers.description: Ylookup is a London-based fintech (founded 2025, EQT Ventures-backed) building an agentic workflow engine for fund administration, corporate services, tax, audit, and deal advisory firms. Its platform embeds trusted AI agents into existing tools (Excel, PDFs, Investran, Paxus) as a centralized processing layer — no data migration required — with specialized agents for extracting data from financial documents (LPAs, debt agreements, KYC/AML and tax forms), real-time reconciliation across spreadsheets and sources, financial analysis, and four-eye review. The company reports an average 76% time saved across live processes such as fund-accounting migration, client onboarding, financial-statement preparation, and K-1 data extraction. Ylookup publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs at this time; this profile captures its identity and published security/compliance posture.

providers.name: AdAdvisor
providers.description: AdAdvisor is an AI‑powered command center for paid media that automates media buying, campaign management, and creative generation across Meta, Google, TikTok, Snap and other major ad platforms. The platform combines data engineering, machine learning models, and a unified dashboard to help advertisers scale spend, improve ROAS, and reduce manual workload. Founded by a digital‑marketing agency team, AdAdvisor offers a 7‑day free trial and tools such as calculators, generators, and a Nova AI buyer that runs ad accounts autonomously.

providers.name: AdButler
providers.description: AdButler provides a retail, commerce and media network platform that enables modern media networks to serve ads, activate first‑party audiences, power self‑service buying, and measure performance across onsite and offsite channels. The platform supports retail media, programmatic supply‑side, native, video, email, mobile, and digital‑out‑of‑home advertising, offering comprehensive tools for advertisers and publishers.

providers.name: Adyton
providers.description: Adyton (Adyton PBC) is a veteran-founded defense technology company building secure, mobile-first, zero-trust software for the U.S. military and defense enterprises. Founded in 2019 by Special Forces veterans James Boyd and JJ Wilson, Adyton delivers the Adyton Operations Kit (AOK) — a mobile productivity suite whose modules include Mustr (real-time personnel accountability and muster), Log-E (distributed logistics and equipment/hand-receipt tracking), and Skeds (planning and scheduling) — plus the Atlas edge platform for disconnected, denied, disrupted, and intermittent (DDIL) environments. The platform is engineered for IL5/IL6, FIPS 140-2 Level 3 encryption, FedRAMP+ and NIST 800-53r5 controls, runs on AWS GovCloud, and supports CAC/PIV, WebAuthn/FIDO2, and OAuth2 authentication. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Initialized Capital and Kindred Ventures.

providers.name: Agent-ready
providers.description: Agent-ready provides a Swiss directory of companies, making their information readable and contactable by AI agents like ChatGPT, Claude, and Perplexity. The platform structures business profiles so AI agents can understand offerings, sources, and contact details, offering analytics, managed implementation, and visibility audits for a subscription. It aims to improve AI visibility for SMEs in Switzerland, offering free verification calls and tiered pricing.

providers.name: Agents Get Paid More
providers.description: Agents Get Paid More provides a monetization kit for external agents, enabling them to implement x402 MCP capabilities with a $49 handoff. The service includes guidance on wallet setup, spend caps, rate limits, and an acceptable use policy, plus optional metered tools like CAPTCHA solving. It targets developers building agent-based services on Base network, offering a compliant, human‑administered solution.

providers.name: AgentsKit
providers.description: Build agents without gluing many libraries together. AgentsKit offers a composable TypeScript foundation for runtime, tools, memory, RAG, and chat interfaces. It supports OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Kimi, local models, and custom adapters, providing six interchangeable contracts that let developers swap layers without touching the rest of the stack. Users can install ready-made agents, scaffold new ones from descriptions, run them on any provider, and diagnose setups directly from the terminal. The platform presents a connected toolkit ranging from source code to production-ready delivery, emphasizing flexibility, low overhead, and a tiny core under 10KB.

providers.name: AiAkiv
providers.description: AiAkiv is a Korean-language platform that captures the context of AI-assisted work, turning AI-generated memories into searchable, shareable records for teams. It offers features like RAG, memory organization, project management, and integrations with popular models such as ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini, helping users retain and reuse AI insights across projects.

providers.name: Alcove
providers.description: Alcove is an AI-powered procurement and project management platform built for interior designers, contractors, event planners, and purchasing agents. It consolidates product details, quotes, financials, and order tracking into a single hub, automatically tracking orders across vendors and projects, managing tasks and timelines, calculating profitability and markups, and offering a purchasing service with Designer Net discounts. An AI assistant surfaces financial insights, suggests markups, reviews approvals, and powers filtering. Alcove is a Menlo Ventures portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass it publishes a marketing site and web application but no public API, developer documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Alif Semiconductor
providers.description: Alif Semiconductor is a fabless semiconductor company headquartered in Pleasanton, California with engineering operations in Grenoble, France. It designs secure, AI/ML-enabled 32-bit microcontrollers and fusion processors for edge computing, built around Arm Cortex-M55 cores and dedicated Arm Ethos-U55 Neural Processing Units. Its Ensemble (E1C, E1, E3, E4, E5, E6, E7, E8) and Balletto (B1) product families target battery-powered edge AI and generative-AI workloads, pairing hardware AI acceleration with autonomous aiPM power management and a multilayered hardware Root of Trust security subsystem. Alif ships an embedded developer surface rather than a public web API: a Zephyr-based SDK, CMSIS Device Family Packs, VS Code project templates, the Conductor configuration tool, evaluation kits, datasheets, and reference manuals published across its support hub and GitHub organization. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners and Mayfield.

providers.name: American Equity Investment Life Holding
providers.description: American Equity Investment Life Holding Company is a leading provider of guaranteed income solutions, specializing in the design, development, and sale of fixed indexed and fixed-rate annuity products distributed through independent agents and broker-dealers. The company offers products including IncomeShield, AssetShield, EstateShield, and GuaranteeShield annuities, providing retirees with lifetime income, principal protection, tax-deferred growth, and legacy planning options.

providers.name: Apartments.com
providers.description: Apartments.com is the largest United States rental-listings marketplace, owned by CoStar Group since its 2014 acquisition and operated from Arlington, Virginia as the anchor of the Apartments.com Network — a group of consumer rental sites that also includes ApartmentFinder.com, ApartmentHomeLiving.com, ForRent.com, ForRentUniversity.com, WestsideRentals.com, Apartamentos.com, After55.com and CorporateHousing.com. It sits on the demand side of the US residential value chain as an Internet Listing Service (ILS): apartment owners and property managers buy advertising, and their inventory, availability, pricing, media, concessions and fee data flows in from property management systems (Yardi, RealPage, Entrata, MRI, AppFolio, ResMan, Rent Manager, Funnel, EliseAI and others) rather than from any public API, while leads flow back out to the advertiser's CRM. Its API posture is closed. Apartments.com publishes no developer portal, no OpenAPI or OData $metadata contract, no SDK, no webhooks and no Postman collection; developer.apartments.com, developers.apartments.com and docs.apartments.com do not resolve in DNS, and api.apartments.com resolves only to the same Akamai edge that returns HTTP 403 Access Denied to every non-browser request, including robots.txt. The one documented machine-to-machine seam is the Digital Feeds Program — an approval-and-contract path in which an approved third-party feed vendor syndicates a paying advertiser's listings into Apartments.com over FTP using an XML listings feed whose specification guide is available only on request to Feeds@apartments.com. A second inbound seam lets licensed agents opt in to rental-listing syndication through their own MLS (Bright MLS, ARMLS, REcolorado, OneKey MLS, SmartMLS, NorthstarMLS, MLS PIN, Garden State MLS, New Jersey MLS and Aspen Glenwood MLS are documented), which requires MLS membership. On RESO, the honest reading is absence rather than "certified but unreachable": Apartments.com does not appear anywhere in the RESO certificates list, and its own property-manager help centre returns zero results for "RESO". It is a consumer of MLS rental feeds, not a certified RESO endpoint, and no unlicensed open dataset is published.

providers.name: b/cited
providers.description: b/cited tracks how AI answer engines like ChatGPT, Claude, and Perplexity cite websites, providing SEO‑focused citation metrics, dashboards, and actionable briefs. Built by Clinton Munkres of the Boringhaus portfolio, it offers free scans, paid plans, and a public leaderboard of tools, operating independently of AI providers. The service reads Google Search Console data read‑only to generate citation scores without training models or selling data.

providers.name: Bareun AI
providers.description: Bareun AI provides a free AI‑powered Korean spell‑checking and grammar‑checking service. It corrects spelling, spacing, and grammar errors in real time, supports long documents such as cover letters and reports without splitting them, and explains each correction with underlying Korean orthography rules. The platform offers a custom dictionary and an API for team integration, with no sign‑up required for trial use. It also supplies documentation, FAQs, privacy policy, and refund policy pages.

providers.name: Beyond Payday
providers.description: Beyond Payday provides a personal finance platform that helps users track income, bills, debts, net worth, and retirement planning. Built by Shane Stebner through HTMLGuy LLC in St. Petersburg, Florida, it operates without venture capital, investors, or data sales, offering free and paid plans for comprehensive financial insights.

providers.name: Billecta
providers.description: Billecta provides a cloud‑based invoicing and payment automation platform for businesses in Sweden and beyond. Their solution automates the full invoicing flow, from invoice creation and delivery to payment collection and bookkeeping. Features include automated reminders, credit‑control, integration with accounting systems, and support for direct payments and auto‑giro. The service is offered as a SaaS product with a free trial and is designed for companies of all sizes, from startups to large enterprises. Billecta emphasizes ease of use, speed, and compliance with Swedish financial regulations.

providers.name: Bloomberg ESG Products
providers.description: Bloomberg ESG Products provide environmental, social, and governance data, analytics, and scores to help investors assess sustainability risks and opportunities. Bloomberg collects ESG data from thousands of companies globally, offering ESG scores, climate data, green bond data, and sustainable finance analytics through the Bloomberg Terminal and API.

providers.name: Bloomberg Indices
providers.description: Bloomberg Indices are a comprehensive family of fixed income, equity, commodity, and multi-asset benchmark indices used by institutional investors worldwide. The Bloomberg Global Aggregate Bond Index, US Aggregate Bond Index, and related indices serve as key benchmarks for fixed income markets. Bloomberg provides index data, analytics, and constituent information through its Terminal and data delivery platforms.

providers.name: Bloomberg Sustainable Finance Products
providers.description: Bloomberg Sustainable Finance Products provide comprehensive data, analytics, and tools for sustainable investing, green bond markets, ESG integration, and climate risk assessment. Bloomberg serves as a key data provider for sustainable finance markets, offering green bond data, ESG scores, climate analytics, and impact measurement tools aligned with major regulatory frameworks including SFDR, EU Taxonomy, and TCFD.

providers.name: Calcupedia
providers.description: Calcupedia provides an extensive library of over 2,400 free calculators and converters that can be embedded on any website with a single line of code. The platform offers fully branded, customizable widgets without requiring developer effort, and includes AI-powered tools to create custom calculators. It serves businesses and developers looking to add interactive calculation functionality quickly and easily.

providers.name: Carpenter Technology
providers.description: Carpenter Technology Corporation is a U.S.-based producer and distributor of premium specialty alloys — including titanium alloys, powder metals, high-temperature stainless steels, tool steels, and soft magnetic alloys — serving the aerospace, defense, medical, transportation, energy, and industrial end markets. The company supports customers through technical product resources such as its Alloy Finder, alloy technical data sheets, conversion tables, and a member-only Customer Portal for order and account self-service, but does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Case Status
providers.description: Case Status is a Charleston, South Carolina legal technology company, founded in 2018 by Andy Seavers and Lauren Gulley, that builds an AI-powered client engagement, experience, and communication platform for modern law firms. It delivers a branded, mobile-first client portal (iOS and Android), a CMS-integrated secure messaging hub with 1:1, bulk, and automated options, AI-driven Client Intelligence (message urgency triage, response recommendations, case summarization, sentiment prediction, and translation across 140+ languages), and client satisfaction analytics such as NPS, Predictive NPS, and CSAT. Case Status integrates with leading case management systems including Clio, Litify, MyCase, Neos, Filevine, SmartAdvocate, Docketwise, PracticePanther, SmokeBall, CASEpeer, MerusCase, CoCounselor, Salesforce, NuLaw, Matterly, and Zapier, plus a Chrome extension for attorneys. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Techstars.

providers.name: CEIPAL
providers.description: Ceipal provides a unified talent platform that combines applicant tracking, vendor management, and workforce management with AI-driven sourcing, matching, and engagement. The solution serves staffing agencies, corporate recruiting teams, healthcare organizations, and global capability centers, offering modules for credentialing, invoicing, workflow automation, and analytics to accelerate hiring and improve talent lifecycle efficiency.

providers.name: Crow
providers.description: Crow is a Y Combinator (Winter 2026) company building an AI infrastructure platform that makes any web or mobile application AI-native. Instead of a simple chatbot, Crow embeds an agent that connects to a product's own APIs and MCP servers, executes workflows, navigates users between pages, and calls server-side and client-side tools from natural-language commands. Developers add Crow with a single script tag or the React SDK, point it at a REST API via OpenAPI or at an MCP server, and configure the agent in a sandbox. Crow also ships the Envoy CLI, which reads a backend codebase and auto-generates and deploys an MCP server, plus a headless client and React UI component library (Widget and Copilot). Crow is initially positioned for commercial real estate but the platform applies to any software product.

providers.name: Ctrl
providers.description: Ctrl (Ctrl, Inc., a Delaware corporation) is an AI-powered workspace for revenue and sales teams that consolidates the tools and data a rep needs — CRM, email, calendar, and messaging — into a single actionable view. Founded in 2021 by Omri Sagzan and Aviv Nahum and based in Tel Aviv and London, Ctrl automates the manual work of updating records across apps such as HubSpot, Salesforce, Google Workspace, and Slack, and helps teams codify and replicate their winning sales playbooks. The company raised a $9M seed round led by LocalGlobe and Earlybird in 2023 and was acquired by Sana Labs in October 2024. Ctrl is a UI/workspace product surfaced as an Earlybird portfolio company; it publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or SDKs.

providers.name: Dropsuite
providers.description: Dropsuite, now a NinjaOne company, is a cloud backup, archiving, and recovery platform built for managed service providers (MSPs) and their small-to-midsize business customers. It provides automated backup and one-click restore for Microsoft 365, Microsoft Entra ID, Google Workspace, email, and website/database data, plus long-term email archiving with legal hold, eDiscovery, and journaling for compliance. Partners manage tenants through a multi-tenant portal and can automate provisioning, reporting, and reconciliation through a partner REST API gated to Direct Partners and Distributors (credentials issued in the Partner Portal under Settings -> API Settings). Dropsuite was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and profiled in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Edyoucated
providers.description: Edyoucated is a German SaaS company offering an AI-powered corporate learning and skills-management platform for mid-to-large enterprises. The product combines a learning management / learning experience system (central management of training, mandatory compliance training, seminar administration, AI-assisted content creation, blended learning, and learning analytics) with skills management (skill cataloging, assessments, gap analysis, expert identification, and career guidance) to give organizations a common language for skills and personalized learning pathways. It also offers consulting for custom skill-taxonomy development. Customers include Deutsche Bahn, BASF, Shopware, and Finanz Informatik. Edyoucated is a portfolio company of Earlybird Venture Capital. As of this profile the company publishes no public developer/API surface, developer portal, OpenAPI, or documentation.

providers.name: Fullseam
providers.description: FullSeam builds AI agents for corporate accounting and finance operations teams, automating the manual work that happens outside traditional accounting software. Its agents handle accounts receivable (following up on payments, generating requested documentation, and entering invoices into customer AP portals), accounts payable (extracting invoices from multiple sources, matching them against purchase orders and contracts, chasing vendors for missing information, and categorizing expenses before posting to the general ledger), cash application, and reconciliation. FullSeam integrates with existing systems including QuickBooks, Xero, NetSuite, Sage, Bill, Stripe, HubSpot, Salesforce, and PandaDoc rather than requiring a platform migration, flagging exceptions with full context for human review and maintaining audit logs for compliance. Founded by the team behind TaxProper (acquired by Opendoor), FullSeam is a Y Combinator Winter 2026 company.

providers.name: Kroll Bond Rating Agency
providers.description: Kroll Bond Rating Agency (KBRA) is a full-service credit rating agency founded in 2010 by Jules Kroll and headquartered in New York, with offices in Dresher PA, Frederick MD, Chicago, Dublin, London, and Tokyo. KBRA is registered with the U.S. SEC as a Nationally Recognized Statistical Rating Organization and with ESMA and the UK FCA through its Irish and UK entities. It has issued 96,000+ ratings covering $4.78 trillion of rated issuance across ABS, CMBS, RMBS, structured credit, corporates, financial institutions, funds, insurance, project finance, public finance, and sovereigns. KBRA distributes ratings and analytics commercially through the KBRA Analytics product family — Ratings Feed, Credit Intelligence, Direct Lending Deals, Premium, Credit Profile (KCP), and Financial Intelligence (KFI). KBRA publishes no public API or developer portal; machine access is contract-gated and delivered as bulk feeds over email/FTP/SFTP, through the Snowflake Marketplace, or via Bloomberg, Aladdin, and FactSet.

providers.name: marginfi
providers.description: marginfi is a decentralized borrowing and lending protocol built on the Solana blockchain by mrgn labs. Users lend supported Solana tokens to earn yield and borrow against supplied collateral, with account-health, e-mode, liquid staking token (LST), and leveraged looping (mrgnloop) products layered on top of the core mrgnlend market. marginfi exposes no hosted REST API — developers integrate on-chain through the marginfi-v2 Solana program using the official TypeScript SDK (marginfi-client-v2, mrgn-common) and the Rust (CLI) SDK, with an early-alpha Python SDK (marginpy) and a Rust CPI interface crate also published. It was surfaced through the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Multicoin Capital and Pantera Capital.

providers.name: Marlo Technologies
providers.description: Marlo is a maritime ERP platform for dry bulk, tanker, and commercial shipping companies, unifying chartering, voyage management, finance, banking, and compliance in a single system. Operators use Marlo to plan charters, track voyage operations and cargo, model voyage P&L and cashflow, run valuations and credit scoring, manage loans and covenants, hold multi-currency accounts with FX transfers and corporate cards, and handle sanctions screening, emissions tracking, and CII rating management. Marlo is a Techstars-backed company and holds SOC 2 (AICPA) certification. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Techstars and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this pass the company exposes a customer web application (app.marlo.co) but publishes no public developer API, API documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Pothos
providers.description: TypeScript-first GraphQL schema builder with a plugin system for Prisma, Relay, federation, simple objects, and code-first type-safe schema construction without code generation.

providers.name: Project Honey Pot
providers.description: Project Honey Pot operates a collaborative anti‑spam network that tracks online fraud and abuse. By deploying “honeypot” traps on participating websites, it gathers data on malicious IP addresses, email harvesters, and spammers. The collected intelligence is made available via a public HTTP:BL DNS‑based API, allowing website owners and security tools to query the reputation of IPs in real time. The service aims to reduce spam, phishing, and other abusive activities across the web through community‑driven data sharing.

providers.name: Pulse Labs
providers.description: Pulse Labs is an AI-powered user experience research platform, founded in 2017, that helps product, design, and UX research teams gather and analyze real-world user feedback. The platform combines surveys, moderated and unmoderated interviews, task-based evaluations across web, mobile, smart devices, and automotive, and naturalistic observations, alongside its FlightRecorder SDK for embedded in-app feedback and session replay on iOS, Android, Web, React, and Flutter. Participant recruiting is powered by the proprietary Pulse Voices panel. Backed by Google, Amazon, Bezos Expeditions, Techstars, and Madrona Ventures, Pulse Labs emphasizes privacy, ethical AI, and enterprise-grade security including ISO 27001 certification and GDPR compliance. Pulse Labs does not currently publish a public REST API or OpenAPI; its developer-facing surface is the FlightRecorder embedded SDK and GitBook product documentation.

providers.name: RealtyFeed
providers.description: RealtyFeed, a Realtyna company, is a real estate data platform that distributes MLS listing data to brokers, agents, IDX website builders and data vendors. Its MLS Router API is a RESO-certified Web API (OData) at api.realtyfeed.com, authenticated with OAuth2 client credentials issued through the RealtyFeed Dashboard (data vendors get access through a separate invitation-only dashboard). It serves Property, Member, Office, OpenHouse, PropertyRooms, Media, metadata and lookup resources in either RESO or RealtyFeed output, plus geo and history endpoints, and publishes documentation (authentication, searchable fields, error handling, rate limits, changelog) and a public Postman collection. RealtyFeed also offers MLS On The Fly IDX widgets.

providers.name: ReturnGO
providers.description: ReturnGO provides a sustainable returns and exchanges management platform for eCommerce brands. Their open API enables automated return processing, warranty handling, exchange management, and tracking, helping companies turn post‑purchase interactions into revenue while reducing waste. The service integrates with major eCommerce tools and offers a white‑label solution for branded return portals.

providers.name: Runway Financial
providers.description: Runway Financial provides a modern financial platform offering banking, payments, and credit services for businesses and consumers. Founded with backing from leading venture firms, the company focuses on integrating seamless API-driven solutions to enable real-time transaction processing, account management, and financial analytics. Their suite includes account opening, fund transfers, card issuance, and compliance tools, all accessible via robust RESTful APIs designed for developers. Runway Financial aims to democratize financial services through open APIs, fostering innovation across fintech ecosystems.

providers.name: SKYNETLAB
providers.description: SKYNETLAB offers Cortex, a patent‑pending semantic memory infrastructure that provides persistent, model‑independent AI context. It enables AI systems to retain information across conversations, acting as a long‑term memory layer for large language models. Available as a ChatGPT connector, Cortex aims to reduce forgetting in AI applications and improve continuity of user interactions.

providers.name: Thunkable
providers.description: Thunkable is a no-code, AI-powered platform for building native iOS and Android mobile applications through a visual drag-and-drop designer, a block-based logic editor, and conversational AI prompts. Creators assemble screens and app logic without writing code, and connect their apps to external services using the built-in Web API blocks (HTTP GET/POST/PUT/DELETE against any REST endpoint), realtime databases, cloud storage, maps, media, push notifications, and payment providers such as Stripe. More than 5 million users across 185 countries have created over 11 million apps on the platform. Note that Thunkable itself does not publish a first-party developer REST API, OpenAPI specification, or SDK for programmatically managing Thunkable projects; its "API" surface is the in-app Web API component used to consume third-party APIs from within apps built on Thunkable.

providers.name: TickTick
providers.description: TickTick is a productivity platform offering a to‑do list, calendar, habit tracker, and Pomodoro timer. It helps individuals and teams organize tasks, schedule events, track habits, and collaborate across devices. The service provides AI‑assisted task creation, real‑time sync, and integrations via MCP, CLI, and OpenAPI APIs for developers to automate workflows.

providers.name: Tulip Interfaces
providers.description: Tulip is a manufacturing operations platform that enables frontline operations teams to build apps, connect machines and devices, and analyze production data without code. The Tulip REST API provides programmatic access to apps, tables, connectors, stations, automations, and analytics, supporting integration with ERP, MES, and industrial equipment on the shop floor.

providers.name: TVbeat
providers.description: TVbeat is a London-based, Techstars-backed advertising technology company whose platform unifies linear television and streaming (CTV) advertising operations into a single system. It lets media owners and buyers forecast, plan, transact, optimize, and measure campaigns across audiences, yield, and operations, supporting multi-currency transacting (ratings, spots, impressions, and outcomes) and modern buying models — Direct, Programmatic, Self-Serve, and AI-driven — across both traditional linear spots and streaming inventory. TVbeat publishes a complete first-party API reference for its analytics API — three query endpoints signed with a custom TVBEAT-HMAC-SHA256 scheme, with two draft-04 JSON Schemas and example responses — in its own GitHub organization at github.com/tvbeat/public, but the API root it names (api.tvbeat.com) no longer resolves in public DNS and the document has not been modified since 2017. TVbeat ships no OpenAPI, SDK, CLI, MCP server or agent card, and its current documentation portal at docs.tvbeat.com is credential-gated.

providers.name: UnitedMasters
providers.description: UnitedMasters is an independent music distribution platform founded by Steve Stoute in 2017 and backed by Alphabet, Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), and Apple. Artists distribute music to 150+ streaming services while keeping full ownership of their master recordings, with real-time royalty payouts, Blueprint AI artist development tools, analytics, and brand and sync licensing partnerships with the NBA, ESPN, TikTok, and other major brands. UnitedMasters does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: Uplight
providers.description: Uplight is a Boulder, Colorado energy technology company formed in 2019 from the merger of Tendril and Simple Energy and expanded through the acquisitions of EnergySavvy, FirstFuel, Ecotagious, EEme, and DERMS/VPP provider AutoGrid (closed February 2024). It sells software to electric and gas utilities and retailers in North America, Europe, and Asia rather than to consumers, covering energy efficiency and electrification marketplaces, home energy reports, rate engagement, demand response, distributed energy resource management (DERMS), virtual power plants, and a utility data lake with analytics. In the United States value chain Uplight sits on the utility side of the meter as a vendor and orchestration layer between the utility, its customers, and connected devices, and it publicly states support for OpenADR, IEEE 2030.5, Modbus, DNP3 and other SCADA protocols for DER control. Its API posture is honestly closed — a Developer Platform exists and is marketed to utilities and ecosystem partners, the documentation portal at docs.uplight.com serves a public landing shell but every Documentation and API Reference path redirects to a ReadMe login, and the production gateway at api.uplight.com answers anonymously only with HTTP 401 and a bearer-token error. No consumer usage-data API, no open market data, no downloadable OpenAPI, and no Green Button or ESPI reference could be found. Uplight is a software vendor, not a regulated data holder, so no consumer data mandate applies to it.

providers.name: Zeew
providers.description: Zeew is a European (Estonia-based) white-label, no-code delivery-platform provider that lets businesses launch on-demand delivery marketplaces and apps in days. Its platform powers food, grocery, pharmacy, retail, and home-services delivery with connected customer, vendor, and driver apps plus an admin dashboard, sold as SaaS subscriptions or purchasable source code under a reseller / white-labeling program. Zeew runs a backend API host (api.zeew.eu) that serves its white-label apps, but as of mid-2026 publishes no public, self-serve API reference, OpenAPI specification, developer portal, or webhook catalog; integration is delivered through the managed platform. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company.

providers.name: 1Social
providers.description: 1Social enables publishing to major social networks directly from AI chat interfaces like ChatGPT and Claude. One message to your AI agent is sent to Instagram, TikTok, YouTube Shorts, LinkedIn, X, Bluesky, Threads and Facebook, with each caption automatically trimmed to fit. No dashboard, no copy‑paste, and scheduling is handled server‑side. The service respects your tokens, never stores them, and provides engagement metrics per network.

providers.name: Actualyze AI
providers.description: Actualyze AI is an enterprise AI governance and management company building tools that give organizations the visibility and control they need to adopt AI at scale without slowing their teams down. Founded by Rafi Khardalian (CEO) and Sean Lynch (CTO) — veterans of building and operating distributed systems at global scale — the company designs for regulated industries from day one, embedding compliance, defense-in-depth data protection, comprehensive audit logging, and continuous monitoring into the platform rather than bolting it on. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Agent Request Desk
providers.description: Agent Request Desk provides a free MCP server that helps AI agents report and diagnose failures when accessing external sites. It captures blocked URLs, missing data, and error reasons, offering private reports without requiring accounts. The service aggregates public issue data, supports multiple client integrations (Claude, Cursor, VS Code, n8n), and supplies pointers to official APIs or datasets when available. Operated by Patrick Hussey in the UK, it aims to improve agent reliability and transparency.

providers.name: Agnikul Cosmos
providers.description: Agnikul Cosmos Private Limited is an Indian aerospace manufacturer and commercial launch service provider founded in 2017 and incubated at the National Centre for Combustion Research and Development at IIT Madras, Chennai. It builds Agnibaan, a configurable small-lift orbital launch vehicle powered by Agnilet — a single-piece, fully 3D-printed semi-cryogenic rocket engine — and flies it from Dhanush (ALP-01), India's first privately built launchpad, at Satish Dhawan Space Centre. On 30 May 2024 its Agnibaan SOrTeD suborbital demonstrator became the first vehicle to fly from a privately built launchpad in India. Agnikul publishes NO API for its launch business: launch is sold per kilogram through an HTML enquiry form, with no developer portal, no OpenAPI and no mission or manifest API anywhere. What it does publish is a genuine, hand-authored corporate /llms.txt and /llms-full.txt about the launch programme, and — on its Cosmos Store merchandise storefront at shop.agnikul.in — a live, anonymous agent-commerce surface: a /.well-known/ucp merchant profile implementing the Universal Commerce Protocol 2026-08-25 and two Model Context Protocol endpoints offering fourteen catalog, cart, checkout, order and policy tools.

providers.name: AI Clearing
providers.description: AI Clearing is an AI-native construction progress tracking and quality control company founded in 2020, headquartered in Austin, Texas with an R&D center in Warsaw, Poland. Its CORE platform ingests drone imagery, ground-level mobile capture, CAD/BIM models and project schedules (including Primavera P6) and returns automated progress, productivity and quality analytics through interactive dashboards, a 3D digital twin and an agentic assistant (Clara), serving contractors and asset owners across solar, pipelines, transmission, highways, railways and airports. As of this profiling round the company publishes no public developer program, API reference or machine-readable contract: the CORE application at core.aiclearing.com is a customer-only single-page app behind a Cloudflare bot challenge, and docs.aiclearing.com does not answer public requests.

providers.name: Alchemix
providers.description: Alchemix is a self-repaying DeFi protocol that allows users to take out interest-free, non-liquidating loans against yield-bearing collateral. Users deposit assets such as ETH, DAI, USDC, or USDT into yield-bearing vaults, and the generated yield automatically repays the loan over time. The protocol issues synthetic alAssets (alUSD, alETH) representing future yield, and provides a Transmuter mechanism to stabilize alAsset prices by gradually exchanging alAssets for underlying collateral. Alchemix operates on Ethereum Mainnet, Optimism, and Arbitrum, with V3 in active development targeting 90% LTV and Meta-Yield Tokens.

providers.name: aMember
providers.description: aMember provides a self‑hosted membership and subscription software solution called aMember Pro. It enables website owners to sell memberships, subscriptions, digital products, and services directly from their own servers, supporting over 237 payment systems, multiple languages, and extensive integration options. The platform includes features such as affiliate programs, helpdesk, newsletters, licensing, and detailed reporting, catering to businesses of all sizes.

providers.name: Anotepad
providers.description: Anotepad provides a free, fast online notepad that autosaves as you type, requires no sign‑up, and lets you download notes as PDF or Word. It supports plain and rich‑text editing, sharing, and easy note management.

providers.name: anymailmcp
providers.description: anymailmcp provides a hosted email MCP (Model Context Protocol) server that connects any IMAP mailbox and CalDAV calendar to AI assistants like Claude, ChatGPT, Grok, and Vibe. It enables AI to read, draft, send emails, and manage calendars directly from chat, offering a free tier for a single mailbox with 150 calls per month and paid plans for higher usage. The service encrypts passwords, supports many IMAP providers, and integrates calendar via CalDAV, making AI‑driven email handling seamless and secure.

providers.name: Archive
providers.description: Archive is a brand-owned resale and recommerce technology platform, founded in 2021, that lets forward-thinking global brands launch and scale profitable, sustainable resale businesses. Its circularity platform spans branded recommerce storefronts, peer-to-peer marketplaces, trade-in (online and in-store), take-back, warranty and repair, a resale warehouse management system (WMS), a unified product catalog, a dynamic pricing engine, and analytics — reclaiming supply through returns, past-season inventory, consumer listings, and in-store trade-ins. Archive serves 50+ brands across 10+ countries, including The North Face, lululemon, Peloton, New Balance, Dr. Martens, Fjällräven, Oscar de la Renta, Hanna Andersson, and Faherty. The company is backed by Bain Capital Ventures and Lightspeed Venture Partners (with Energize Capital leading its $30M Series B), and has raised $54M to date.

providers.name: Asking
providers.description: Asking provides a unified customer support platform integrating WhatsApp, Instagram, email, and chat into a single inbox. Businesses can manage conversations across multiple channels, assign owners, and reply with context, improving response efficiency and customer satisfaction. The service offers features like multi-channel messaging, team collaboration, automated workflows, and analytics, targeting small to enterprise-level companies seeking streamlined support operations.

providers.name: Astelia
providers.description: Astelia is an AI-native exposure management and vulnerability management company whose platform helps security teams find and fix the reachable fraction of their vulnerabilities. Using agentic AI and read-only integrations, Astelia maps network topology, extracts the technical requirements an exploit actually needs, and correlates reachability with network context to surface which vulnerabilities are truly exploitable by an attacker. Rather than ranking issues on probability scores alone, it delivers attack-path visualization, coverage-gap analysis, and evidence-based remediation guidance tailored to each organization's environment. Astelia is backed by Index Ventures and documents its security posture in a public trust center (SOC 2 Type 2, ISO/IEC 27001:2022, HIPAA, GDPR). This API Evangelist profile enriches the company as a network lead; the product surface is enterprise SaaS with no public API published at this time.

providers.name: Aura
providers.description: Aura is an all-in-one consumer digital-safety company that protects individuals and families from identity theft, financial fraud, scams, and online threats. Its subscription service bundles credit and identity monitoring with up to millions in identity-theft insurance, suspicious-transaction alerts, dark-web monitoring, a privacy assistant that removes personal data from data brokers, parental controls and safe-gaming alerts, an encrypted vault and password manager, spam-call protection, a VPN, and antivirus. Aura is a direct-to-consumer product with no public developer API; this profile captures its identity, security posture, and compliance surface. Backed by Accel, Cowboy Ventures, General Catalyst, and Partech.

providers.name: Axflow
providers.description: Axflow provides AI tooling for the future, offering a platform that integrates large language models, agents, and AI-driven workflows. The service focuses on enabling developers and enterprises to build, deploy, and manage AI-powered applications with ease, featuring customizable pipelines, tool integrations, and collaborative features.

providers.name: Beem
providers.description: Beem is a consumer fintech mobile app (trybeem.com) offering instant cash advances of up to $1,000 through its Everdraft feature with no credit check and no interest, alongside personal loans up to $100,000, high-yield savings accounts paying up to 5% APY, AI-powered budgeting, credit building, cashback rewards, identity-theft protection, and insurance products. It supports non-traditional income (gig, freelance, government benefits) and can transfer funds to Cash App or a bank account. Backed by Techstars and used by more than five million people, Beem is consumer-facing and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal at this time. Added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile.

providers.name: big xyt
providers.description: big xyt AG (now branded simply xyt, with big-xyt.com redirecting to xyt.one) is an independent, majority employee-owned market data analytics firm headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, Germany. It sells tick-data-driven market intelligence covering equities, ETFs, listed derivatives, FX, and fixed income across 120+ venues, processing 12bn+ messages per day with roughly ten years of history at nanosecond precision and market-by-order granularity. Products include the Liquidity Cockpit (market share and liquidity analytics), Transaction Cost Analysis against its SMART benchmark, pre-trade cost modeling, a Datashop of analysis-ready datasets and APIs, and an xyt AI natural-language query layer. Three API products are publicly named - the big xyt API, Liquidity Cockpit API, and TCA API - but their reference documentation sits behind a login at docs.big-xyt.com (HTTP 403 unauthenticated), and access is sales-gated via a book-a-demo motion with no self-serve signup, public pricing, or public OpenAPI.

providers.name: Bilg
providers.description: Bilg provides a shared context platform for teams and AI agents, enabling collaborative knowledge bases, prompt sharing, and integrated tooling. The service offers a unified workspace where users can store, search, and manage prompts, code snippets, and documentation, with AI-powered assistance to streamline workflows. It supports connections to Claude, Claude Desktop, Cursor, and other MCP clients, allowing seamless integration into existing development pipelines. The platform emphasizes security, privacy, and team collaboration, making it suitable for enterprises and developers seeking to enhance productivity through AI-driven knowledge management.

providers.name: Binti
providers.description: Binti builds cloud-based, mobile-friendly software for child welfare and foster care agencies, offered as a modular Comprehensive Child Welfare Information System (CCWIS) covering licensing, placements, case management, intake, investigations, eligibility, payments, and family finding & engagement. Since 2017 it has scaled to serve over 450 government agencies across 34 states and Washington, DC, including statewide implementations, and supports roughly half of the nation's child welfare system. Binti exposes a private, bi-directional integration API so agencies can connect its modules to their existing systems of record; the platform is HIPAA-compliant with a Vanta-hosted Trust Center. Binti is headquartered in Oakland, California and is a portfolio company of Cowboy Ventures. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Blocks
providers.description: Blocks is a cloud cost-optimization service that guarantees up to 20% savings on AWS spend by aggregating the purchasing power of hundreds of companies into group-buying negotiations, then layering automated cloud management on top. Its AI-powered DevOps agent, Major Tom, continuously monitors connected AWS accounts through read-only billing access, surfaces cost-saving and security findings in Slack, and can propose Terraform fixes without requiring root or code access. Onboarding is a one-click read-only AWS cost-data integration with no long-term contracts and no infrastructure changes. Blocks is backed by Speedinvest and is profiled in the API Evangelist network; it currently exposes a marketing and product surface rather than a public developer API.

providers.name: Bloomberg Tradebook
providers.description: Bloomberg Tradebook is an electronic brokerage and agency trading platform offering execution services across global equities, futures, options, and foreign exchange. Founded in 1996 as a Bloomberg LP subsidiary, Tradebook provides algorithmic trading, direct market access, and transaction cost analysis (TCA) via FIX protocol connectivity and integration with Bloomberg Terminal workflows.

providers.name: Built
providers.description: Built (Built Technologies) is an AI-powered real estate and construction finance platform that connects capital and information across the construction lending ecosystem. It serves banks, credit unions, private credit firms, owners, developers, and general contractors with construction loan administration, deal origination and underwriting, project financials, invoice and lien-waiver management, compliance tracking, and payments. Founded over a decade ago and headquartered in Nashville and New York, Built operates on one of the largest connected datasets in real estate finance and integrates with Procore, Sage Intacct, Yardi, QuickBooks, Encompass, nCino, and DocuSign. It is backed by Fifth Wall and Index Ventures. This profile was enriched from Built's public developer and trust surfaces; Built publishes an integrations directory, identity/SSO, a status page, and a trust center, but does not expose a public REST API or OpenAPI.

providers.name: canienter-com
providers.description: canienter-com is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: mcp-registry) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.

providers.name: CARET Legal
providers.description: CARET Legal provides cloud‑based legal practice management software designed to streamline case handling, automate workflows, and integrate billing, document management, and client communication. The platform serves law firms of all sizes, offering features such as case management, reporting and analytics, secure document storage, and mobile access, all hosted securely in the cloud.

providers.name: Cartesi
providers.description: Cartesi is a Linux-based optimistic rollup protocol that lets developers build decentralized applications by running rich off-chain computation inside a sandboxed Linux virtual machine. The core of the stack is the Cartesi Machine, a deterministic RISC-V emulator that boots a real Linux userland so dApps can be written in any language (Rust, Go, Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, C++) using familiar libraries, then settle results on Ethereum and other EVM chains through Cartesi Rollups smart contracts. Cartesi Rollups 2.0 is the current major version, packaging an application-specific rollup as the combination of the Cartesi Machine, the Cartesi Rollups Node middleware (Rust + Go), and a set of Solidity rollup contracts that handle settlement, consensus, and data availability. The DAVE permissionless fraud-proof system provides Stage-2 trust minimization, while the Cartesi CLI (the successor to Sunodo) packages scaffolding, build, and local devnet workflows. Cartesi is stewarded by The Cartesi Foundation and the CTSI token governs the network. Cartesi is fully open source under Apache-2.0 and LGPL-3.0 licenses on github.com/cartesi; there is no proprietary SaaS product, but the Rollups Node ships several developer-facing surfaces — the Rollup HTTP API used by application backends, the Inspect HTTP API for read-only queries from frontends, a GraphQL reader for advance-state inputs / outputs / vouchers / notices / reports, and a JSON-RPC node API for operations.

providers.name: Clipboard Health
providers.description: Clipboard Health (now branded simply "Clipboard", at clipboardworks.com) is a U.S. healthcare workforce marketplace that connects workplaces — long-term care facilities, home health and hospice agencies, hospitals, dental practices, and travel assignments — with vetted, independent professionals to fill open shifts. Workplaces post shifts and Clipboard matches, credentials, schedules, and pays qualified workers, with the platform handling documentation, compliance, and instant pay for pros. The company reports serving more than 6,500 workplaces and over a million workers nationwide. Backed by Initialized Capital and IVP, it was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company. Clipboard Health publishes no public consumer API; its public developer surface is limited to open-source TypeScript utility libraries on npm (the @clipboard-health scope, from github.com/ClipboardHealth/core-utils) and a minimal RFC 9116 security.txt.

providers.name: CO2 AI
providers.description: CO2 AI is an enterprise sustainability platform that helps organizations measure, reduce, and report carbon emissions across their entire value chain. It combines trustworthy emissions data, AI-powered workflows, and supply-chain collaboration to baseline and track Scope 1, 2, and 3 corporate footprints, compute audit-ready product carbon footprints (PCF) at scale across thousands of SKUs (PACT, TfS, PEF, ISO aligned), engage suppliers for primary data, and build decarbonization plans ranked by Marginal Abatement Cost. Backed by Partech and surfaced to the API Evangelist network as a climate-sector company profile. No public developer API is published as of this enrichment pass; the profile captures the company's security, trust, and legal surface.

providers.name: Colainsight
providers.description: COLA Insight provides a Social Security COLA calculator that separates forecasts, partial inflation data, and official decisions, exposing index values, linking claims to their origins, and explaining limitations. The site is designed for quick answers while offering audit‑ready data records, methods, limitations, and sources. It operates without charge, may display advertising, and is not affiliated with any government agency.

providers.name: Continuous
providers.description: Continuous provides a quote-to-cash and revenue recognition platform that integrates Salesforce and NetSuite. Their solutions include a control lifecycle logic layer, usage metering, and advanced deal structuring for CPQ. The company offers products, services, and support to help enterprises automate financial processes and improve revenue operations.

providers.name: Countries GraphQL API
providers.description: Countries GraphQL API is a free, public GraphQL API that provides structured information about countries, continents, and languages around the world. Created by Trevor Blades, it draws from the Countries List dataset and the provinces npm package, returning data such as capital cities, currencies, languages, and AWS region mappings for every country.

providers.name: CyberCube
providers.description: CyberCube is a cyber risk analytics provider for the insurance industry — brokers, insurers, reinsurers and cyber ILS investors — translating cyber risk into quantified financial impact. Its product line spans Account Manager (single-risk underwriting), Portfolio Manager (portfolio aggregation and catastrophe loss modeling), Broking Manager, Exposure Manager, SPoF Intelligence (digital supply-chain single points of failure) and the Industry Exposure Databases. CyberConnect is the company's API layer, marketed as a way to deliver CyberCube models, insights and signals into a customer's own underwriting, exposure-management and capital-modeling workflows, spanning catastrophe risk management, risk scoring, financial loss modeling, reinsurance modeling, SPoF intelligence, risk intelligence and threat modeling. The CyberConnect reference and the Atlas documentation portal sit behind a customer login, and the production API host answers unauthenticated requests with an AWS API Gateway authentication challenge.

providers.name: Distroless
providers.description: Distroless images by Google contain only the application and its runtime dependencies, stripping out package managers, shells, and other OS-level utilities to minimize attack surface and image size. The smallest variant (gcr.io/distroless/static-debian12) is roughly 2 MB. Distroless ships base images for static binaries, glibc-based binaries, C/C++, Java (17, 21, 25), Node.js (22, 24), and Python 3, with multi-architecture support including amd64, arm64, arm, s390x, ppc64le, and riscv64. Adopters include Kubernetes, Knative, Tekton, and Teleport.

providers.name: dv01
providers.description: dv01 is an "InvestorTech" data and analytics platform for the structured finance and consumer-lending markets, part of Fitch Group. It aggregates, standardizes, and validates loan-level data across asset classes (RMBS, auto, student loans, personal loans, buy-now-pay-later) and delivers it, along with reporting and surveillance tooling, to issuers, lenders, and investors. Products include Data Direct, Data Management, DealStudio, Securitizations, Tape Cracker, and portfolio/market surveillance. dv01 publishes no public developer REST API or OpenAPI; data is delivered into client environments via Snowflake Data Share, BigQuery, SFTP, and S3. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Ribbit Capital and enriched with verified public identity, compliance, and domain-security signals.

providers.name: Ethyreal Bio
providers.description: Ethyreal Bio is a Cambridge, Massachusetts clinical-stage biotechnology company founded in 2024 and headquartered at 700 Technology Square, developing precision therapies for thyroid diseases with high unmet need. It emerged from stealth on 10 June 2026 with $101 million in combined Series A and Series B financing — the Series A co-led by Atlas Venture and Medicxi alongside Nandi Life Sciences and Checkpoint Capital, the Series B led by Avoro Capital. Its lead program ETHY-001 is a monoclonal antibody that blocks autoantibody-mediated activation of the thyroid stimulating hormone receptor (TSHR), the shared pathogenic driver of Graves' disease and thyroid eye disease; it is formulated for subcutaneous administration with half-life extension technology for infrequent dosing, and first-in-human trials were planned for the second half of 2026. Ethyreal Bio publishes no developer program, no product API, no SDKs and no OpenAPI definition of its own. The only machine-readable surface on ethyrealbio.com is the WordPress REST API (wp/v2) that the company website exposes at /wp-json/, which serves its press releases, corporate pages, leadership and board-of-directors profiles, media library, taxonomies and site search as JSON. The OpenAPI documents in this repository were derived mechanically by API Evangelist from that route-discovery descriptor.

providers.name: Feroot
providers.description: Feroot Security is a Toronto-based cybersecurity company providing AI-powered client-side (browser) security and compliance automation for websites and mobile apps. Its platform gives organizations visibility into the third-party JavaScript, trackers, cookies, and data flows running in the browser, and automates compliance with PCI DSS 4.0.1 (requirements 6.4.3 script inventory and 11.6.1 tamper detection), HIPAA, GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, and 50+ global regulations. Products include DXComply (privacy compliance and consent auditing), PaymentGuard (PCI DSS 4.0.1 automation for payment pages), and DXSecure (real-time client-side script security against formjacking, Magecart, and data exfiltration). Feroot is SOC 2 Type 2 certified and a PCI Security Standards Council Associate Member. Backed by Y Combinator, True Ventures, Haystack, and Stonemill Ventures.

providers.name: Globacap
providers.description: Globacap is a London-based private capital markets technology company, founded in 2017, that builds workflow-automation software-as-a-service for issuance, share register management, ongoing administration, transferability and settlement of private securities. Its platform is used by securities exchanges, securities firms, private banks and asset managers to run primary placements and secondary liquidity events, and the company states its technology has supported 200+ primary placements, matched and settled $800m+ of secondaries and administered $30bn+ in private markets assets. Globacap operates an FCA-regulated UK entity and a US-registered broker-dealer and alternative trading system. In November 2025 Apex Group agreed to acquire the company; the change of control completed in early 2026 and Globacap technology now sits inside Apex Group's digital/tokenisation initiative alongside Tokeny. As of this profile the public globacap.com site has been reduced to a single acquisition announcement page and Globacap publishes no public developer program, API reference or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Ironlane
providers.description: Ironlane provides an AI inference routing platform that connects applications to over 70 model providers via a single API. It enables users to set business priorities such as price, latency, EU residency, or reliability, and automatically routes requests to the optimal provider, offering failover, cost monitoring, and performance optimization. The service includes a unified gateway, health monitoring, and detailed usage reporting, simplifying AI integration for developers.

providers.name: Leah
providers.description: Leah, formerly ContractPodAi and legally ContractPod Technologies Limited, is a London-headquartered enterprise agentic AI company that unifies contract lifecycle management, legal transformation, procurement, and finance operations into a single autonomous system. Its Leah Agentic OS platform provides skills-based orchestration, agentic workflows, a natural-language app builder, a library of domain-specific legal, contracting, procurement, and finance agents, and the Leah Maestro enterprise orchestrator. Leah is a five-time Gartner CLM Visionary, is SOC 2 Type II and ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certified, and is used by enterprises including PwC, KPMG, Philips, Alaska Airlines, MUFG, and Cushman & Wakefield. Leah ships pre-built connectors and describes open REST APIs for enterprise integration, but maintains no public developer portal or published API reference — API access is unlocked through the enterprise contract.

providers.name: LegalOS
providers.description: LegalOS is an AI-native U.S. immigration law practice based in San Francisco and backed by Y Combinator (Winter 2026 batch). Founded by Matthew Asir (CEO), Rachel Asir (COO) and Claire Jutabha (CTO), the company pairs proprietary legal software with licensed immigration attorneys to prepare employment-based visa and green-card petitions — H-1B, L-1A, L-1B, O-1 and TN visas, plus EB-1A, EB-1C and EB-2 NIW green cards. AI agents draft petition narratives, assemble supporting evidence and anticipate USCIS objections, with every filing reviewed by a licensed attorney before submission. LegalOS is delivered as a service through a customer web application at app.legalos.ai; as of this profile it publishes no public developer API, SDKs, developer portal or machine-readable API artifacts.

providers.name: mockAPI
providers.description: mockAPI.io is a hosted mock API service that lets developers create custom REST endpoints, define resource schemas, and generate fake data for testing and prototyping web and mobile applications. Users define resources in a web UI and mockAPI provisions a fully working REST endpoint with CRUD semantics, custom response codes, and seed data so teams can prototype against realistic API behavior without standing up a backend.

providers.name: Pave
providers.description: Pave is an AI-native compensation management platform that helps organizations make data-driven pay decisions. It combines real-time market benchmarking (compensation data sourced from 9,000+ companies), automated market pricing and salary-range building, merit-cycle and compensation-planning workflows, an employee-facing total rewards portal, and visual offer letters into one system. Pave connects to HRIS, ATS, equity-management, and performance-management systems to create a single source of truth for an organization's compensation ecosystem. Pave does not currently publish a public developer API or developer portal; its integration surface is inbound connectors to systems of record.

providers.name: Pimjo
providers.description: Pimjo, operating under the brand Aymo AI, offers an all‑in‑one AI platform for teams, providing access to leading large language models such as Claude, GPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, Grok, and Seedream. The platform includes tools for text summarization, paraphrasing, paragraph generation, SEO title creation, YouTube hashtag generation, speech writing, song lyric composition, and more. It features a private, secure workspace for collaborative AI‑assisted brainstorming, model comparison, and result sharing, targeting teams seeking integrated AI capabilities across multiple use‑cases.

providers.name: Pipe Network
providers.description: Pipe Network is a decentralized storage and content-delivery network built on Solana, marketed as "Firestarter" storage. It offers content-addressed (Blake3) object storage with client-side AES-256-GCM and post-quantum (Kyber-1024 / Dilithium5) encryption, deterministic public URLs of the form /{account}/{hash}, prepaid-USDC billing funded via Solana Pay, and first-party TypeScript / Python / Rust SDKs plus a Rust CLI. The SDKs ship native agent- framework tool adapters (OpenAI, Anthropic, LangChain, LlamaIndex, Vercel AI SDK, Cloudflare AI Workflows, AutoGen, CrewAI) and x402 machine-to-machine payment support. Backed by Multicoin Capital.

providers.name: Quilter
providers.description: Quilter is a physics-driven AI platform that automates printed circuit board (PCB) placement and routing. Using reinforcement learning, it converts a schematic into multiple fabrication-ready layout candidates in hours instead of weeks, validating each against physical constraints through Physics Rule Checks (impedance control, differential pairs, power nets, bypass capacitors, keepouts, and stackup rules). Quilter supports Altium, Cadence Allegro, Siemens Xpedition, KiCAD, and OrCAD formats and handles boards of roughly 100-1,000 components with 2,000-5,000 pins to route. It is delivered as a hosted web application (app.quilter.ai) with a startup program and a free tier; there is no public developer API, SDK, or CLI surface at this time.

providers.name: Remitly
providers.description: Remitly is a Seattle-based digital financial services provider for immigrants and their families, operating a global cross-border remittance and money-movement network across more than 170 countries. Beyond its consumer money-transfer app, Remitly runs "Remitly for Developers" (Remitly Access), a gated enterprise partner API that lets businesses embed international payouts, cross-border payments, and locally relevant disbursement options into their own products, along with open-source "Connected Experiences" mobile/web SDK components. Remitly is a regulated money services business: FinCEN-registered, licensed as a money transmitter across all 50 U.S. states, and registered with FINTRAC in Canada. Added to the API Evangelist network as a fintech company profile and enriched with identity, domain-security, and compliance artifacts.

providers.name: SeekOps
providers.description: SeekOps Inc. is an Austin, Texas emissions-measurement company that detects and quantifies methane and carbon dioxide from industrial facilities using drone-mounted laser spectroscopy. Its SeekIR sensor suite applies tunable diode laser absorption spectroscopy (TDLAS) originally developed at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory to search for methane on Mars, hardened for terrestrial energy operations. SeekOps sells measurement as a service — Leak Detection and Quantification (LDAQ) surveys flown over upstream and midstream oil and gas sites, offshore platforms, landfills, biogas digesters and renewable natural gas facilities — and delivers the results through two software surfaces: Celsius, a cloud analytics and reconciliation-reporting dashboard, and FASTR, a real-time telemetry view. Founded in 2017, the company has surveyed facilities across six continents and is backed by Equinor Ventures and OGCI Climate Investments. Its software is customer-only: both Celsius and FASTR sit behind authentication and SeekOps publishes no public developer program, API documentation or machine-readable contract.

providers.name: Step CI
providers.description: Step CI is an open source API testing and monitoring framework that uses YAML-based workflows to define and run automated API test scenarios. It supports REST, GraphQL, gRPC, tRPC, and SOAP protocols in a single unified testing framework. Step CI is language-agnostic, self-hosted, and integrates with all major CI/CD platforms.

providers.name: Stockholm University
providers.description: Stockholm University (Stockholms universitet) is a public research university in Sweden and one of the country's largest, with roughly 33,000 students across four faculties. It operates no public developer portal, no API gateway and no first-party documented API: api.su.se, data.su.se and developer.su.se do not resolve, and www.su.se/api returns 404. What the institution genuinely runs and serves anonymously is narrow — a Shibboleth SAML2 identity provider at idp.it.su.se whose entity metadata is published by the university and registered in the SWAMID federation (and so in eduGAIN), the Bolin Centre Database research data repository on bolin.su.se minting its own DataCite DOIs under prefix 10.17043 since 2014, and a SiteVision REST sitemap on www.su.se that indexes every course syllabus in the education archive. Its two harvestable research surfaces are both tenancies rather than SU engineering: the DiVA OAI-PMH endpoint at su.diva-portal.org is operated by the DiVA consortium at Uppsala University Library, and su.figshare.com is a Figshare deployment. This profile previously credited Stockholm University with eleven APIs that were all one Figshare contract at api.figshare.com/v2; those contracts and everything derived from them have been removed and the two repository relationships recorded as tenant surfaces instead.

providers.name: Table22
providers.description: Table22 is a subscription commerce and growth platform built specifically for food & beverage businesses. It enables restaurants, wine shops, wineries, butchers, bakeries, specialty grocers, and retailers to launch and grow subscriptions, clubs, memberships, pre-orders, and product drops that generate predictable recurring revenue beyond their four walls. The full-service platform combines branded storefronts, an order management system, white-glove fulfillment coordination, automated lifecycle marketing and CRM, five-star consumer support, and AI tools for hospitality. Over 1,000 merchants across 40 U.S. states use Table22, representing $100M+ in revenue impact. Pricing is success-based (15% revenue share, no upfront or setup fees). Table22 is a sales-led SaaS with no public developer API; this profile captures its identity, website surface, and machine-readable llms.txt.

providers.name: Trezy
providers.description: Trezy is a Franco-Dutch fintech SaaS (Trezy SAS, founded 2021 in Paris by Quentin Lacointa) offering AI-driven cash flow management for small and medium businesses across Europe, the US, and Canada. It connects to 2,000+ banks via PSD2/Open Banking to deliver real-time cash position, automatic AI transaction categorization, 95%-accurate 12-month cash flow forecasting, real-time P&L, 27+ financial KPIs, supplier cost analysis, and OCR-based document management from a single platform starting at a free tier. Trezy also offers dedicated plans for external CFOs (DAF) and accounting firms, and integrates with QuickBooks Online and Pennylane. Backed by Seedcamp and Playfair Capital (with Kima Ventures and Discovery Ventures) in a €3M seed round. Trezy publishes an llms.txt corpus and an /.well-known/ai-plugin.json manifest but does not expose a public developer API.

providers.name: Tryton
providers.description: Tryton is an open-source three-tier ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning) platform built on Python and PostgreSQL, designed for companies of any size. It provides REST APIs for managing a comprehensive suite of business modules including financial accounting, inventory and stock management, purchasing, sales, production, and project management. The REST API supports standard CRUD operations (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE) with JSON responses, user application authentication, context headers for localization, pagination via Range headers, and domain filtering via query parameters. Tryton is licensed under GPL v3 and free to use.

providers.name: Tutor Intelligence
providers.description: Tutor Intelligence builds AI-powered robotic workers for industrial and logistics operations, delivered as robots-as-a-service. Its flagship Cassie palletizing robot handles material-handling tasks — palletizing, depalletizing, and case picking — in warehouses and factories without facility retrofits, and a humanoid robot, Sonny, is slated for late 2026. The company pairs on-robot autonomy with a human-in-the-loop teleoperation and data model, priced per robot-hour with no long-term contracts, and is backed by Union Square Ventures. No public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface is published as of this profiling; the company's public GitHub organization hosts internal tooling and open-source forks rather than a first-party product API.

providers.name: Uptake
providers.description: Uptake Technologies is a Chicago-based industrial AI and predictive-maintenance software company founded in 2014 by Eric Lefkofsky and Brad Keywell. Its SaaS platform ingests telematics, sensor, fluid-analysis and work-order data from heavy commercial fleets and industrial assets, then applies machine-learning failure models — backed by an Asset Strategy Library of roughly 800 equipment types and tens of thousands of failure modes acquired with Asset Performance Technologies in 2018 — to predict component failure before it happens. Products include Uptake Fleet and Radar (predictive maintenance alerts), Compass (work-order data cleansing), Fusion (operational-technology data to cloud) and Scout (rules-based alerting), delivered through the fleet.uptake.com web application, a Geotab Marketplace add-in, and a customer-provisioned REST API gateway at api.uptake.com. Bosch announced its acquisition of Uptake in March 2026.

providers.name: Weilliptic
providers.description: Weilliptic provides infrastructure for autonomous systems, offering a stack of primitives such as WeilChain, Autos, Writ, Pensieve, WeilStream, and Receipts. The platform enables secure identity, scoped authority, tamper‑evident memory, event streaming, and verifiable receipts for AI agents and decentralized applications.

providers.name: Acorns
providers.description: Acorns is a micro-investing and personal finance platform that helps everyday Americans grow their wealth through automated round-up investments, diversified portfolios, retirement accounts, high-yield savings, and financial wellness tools. The Acorns Partner API enables authorized third parties to access Acorns user data on behalf of users via OAuth 2.0.

providers.name: AdsGPT
providers.description: AdsGPT is an AI-powered advertising platform that creates, launches, and optimizes ad campaigns across Google, Instagram, TikTok, LinkedIn, and more. Users simply describe their product or provide a URL, and AdsGPT generates creatives, copy, targeting, and budgets, continuously optimizing spend for maximum ROI. The service supports multiple brands, offers free and paid plans, and integrates with major ad networks, providing a unified dashboard for campaign management and performance insights.

providers.name: Agenlify
providers.description: Agenlify is a directory that helps individuals and small teams choose AI agents for specific tasks. It catalogs over 470 AI products across categories like research, building, content creation, data analysis, automation, and customer support. The site provides detailed reviews, pricing, setup limits, and source links, aiming to simplify the selection process for AI tools.

providers.name: AI Backtester
providers.description: AI Backtester provides free AI-powered backtesting for crypto trading strategies, allowing users to describe strategies in plain English and receive detailed performance reports instantly.

providers.name: Aizon
providers.description: Aizon is a B2B SaaS manufacturing-intelligence platform for GxP pharmaceutical manufacturers and CDMOs. It turns process data into AI-driven recommendations to increase yield, reduce deviations, and prevent batch loss without replacing existing MES, LIMS, ERP, or historian systems. The platform spans four connected products: Aizon Execute (intelligent electronic batch records), Aizon Unify (a GxP manufacturing data platform / lakehouse), Aizon Predict (operationalized ML for yield optimization, CPV, and predictive quality), and Aizon Agentic Studio (a natural-language application and dashboard builder). Aizon runs single-tenant on AWS with ALCOA++ data integrity, 21 CFR Part 11 e-signatures, and a GxP model lifecycle, and exposes a RESTful API to customers. Offices in San Francisco, USA and Barcelona, Spain.

providers.name: Alexis
providers.description: AlexisHR offers an AI‑powered all‑in‑one HR platform that simplifies people operations, boosts productivity, and provides instant HR access via a chatbot. The solution reduces administrative overhead, improves employee experience, and streamlines tasks such as performance reviews, onboarding, and time‑off management.

providers.name: AMBOSS
providers.description: AMBOSS is a Berlin-based (AMBOSS SE) digital medical knowledge platform used by medical students, physicians, educators, and healthcare institutions worldwide.
