Its products include PointOne Time (automatic cross-device time capture with AI-generated narratives), PointOne Review (pre-bill review with AI markup and collaboration), and PointOne Intelligence (time analytics and resource-allocation insights), along with automatic enforcement of Outside Counsel Guidelines. The platform syncs with billing systems including Aderant, Clio, Filevine, QuickBooks, Actionstep, Elite 3E, Surepoint, MyCase, and LeanLaw, and serves 200+ law firms. PointOne is backed by Bessemer, Y Combinator, General Catalyst, and 8VC. No public developer API is currently published; integrations are delivered as pre-built connectors.

providers.name: PropTrack
providers.description: PropTrack is an Australian property data, analytics, and automated valuation business, part of REA Group. It supplies residential property data, an industry-leading AI-powered Automated Valuation Model (AVM), the PropTrack Home Price Index, and market insights drawn from more than a trillion property data points across some twelve million Australian residential properties. Its raw data is sourced from public records (State/Territory land titles offices, Valuers General, and Geoscape Australia) and proprietary sources including the realestate.com.au listing portal. PropTrack exposes this through a developer program of REST APIs — covering address suggestion and matching, property and listing data, sold-transaction search (including point-and-radius queries), automated valuations, and market metrics — documented on a hosted Stoplight developer portal and secured with OAuth 2.0. The APIs are aimed at banks, lenders, brokers, proptech platforms, and other enterprise customers integrating Australian property intelligence.

providers.name: Revion
providers.description: Revion builds an AI-powered operating system for automotive retail service operations. Its voice-first platform lets dealership technicians dictate repair information hands-free, automatically structuring their speech into repair orders, multi-point inspections, and service recommendations in real time so shops can service more vehicles and capture more high-margin work. Revion is a Winter 2026 Y Combinator company based in New York City, operating across US and EU regions. As of this profile Revion is an early-stage product company with no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this entry captures its public identity, security posture, and web properties for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Saama
providers.description: Saama (Saama Technologies, Inc.) is a Campbell, California life-sciences technology company that builds AI-powered clinical analytics software for biopharmaceutical sponsors and CROs. Its platform ingests, curates and animates clinical trial data through products including the Data Hub, Smart Data Quality (SDQ), Operational Insights, Patient Insights, Source to Submission (S2S) and the BRAIN family (BRAIN SDTM, BRAIN SCE, BRAIN Visualization, BRAIN Consortium), alongside a set of modular Clinical AI Agents announced in 2025. Saama states its platform offers 40-plus pre-built connectors and that its agents are "connected via APIs", but as of this profile the company publishes no public developer portal, API reference or machine-readable specification - technical documentation and the support portal both sit behind a customer login.

providers.name: Sainapse
providers.description: Sainapse, built by Bayestree Intelligence, is a unified, explainable AI engine for customer support, outreach, and operations that is embedded directly in an enterprise's environment. It connects to existing integrations to source real-time data for autonomous resolution, grounds every response in verified sources of data, and can act as an agent copilot (next best actions, suggested responses) or as an autonomous agent. Sainapse learns from human-in-the-loop corrections and evolving business rules, supports 220+ integrations, and is offered as a hosted service or deployed on-premises. It publishes SOC 2, HIPAA, ISO 27001, and GDPR compliance. Sainapse is an enterprise, demo-led product with no public self-serve API, developer portal, or machine-readable specification at this time.

providers.name: SCADA
providers.description: SCADA (Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition) is an industrial control system architecture used to monitor and control industrial processes, infrastructure, and facility-based equipment. It is widely used in manufacturing, energy, water treatment, oil and gas, transportation, and other critical infrastructure sectors to collect real-time data from remote sensors and control equipment. Modern SCADA systems increasingly expose REST APIs, OPC-UA endpoints, and MQTT brokers for integration with enterprise systems, cloud platforms, and AI/ML workloads.

providers.name: SimpleTix
providers.description: SimpleTix provides an online ticketing platform for attractions, farms, festivals, and events. It offers customizable ticket sales, season passes, and integration with payment processors, aiming to reduce fees compared to competitors. The service includes a manager portal, support resources, and pricing plans for various organization sizes.

providers.name: SKU IQ
providers.description: SKU IQ provides inventory synchronization solutions for small to medium businesses, connecting point‑of‑sale (POS) systems with eCommerce platforms. Their platform automates stock updates, prevents overselling, and consolidates order views across channels like Shopify, TikTok Shop, BigCommerce, and more. SKU IQ offers tiered pricing plans and a free trial, aiming to reduce manual data entry and operational errors for retailers.

providers.name: Soundful
providers.description: Soundful provides AI-generated music for brands, creators, and enterprises. Their platform offers scalable, royalty‑free tracks created with ethically trained AI, enabling users to quickly generate custom soundtracks for marketing, video, podcasts, and more. Soundful’s service includes a free tier for hobbyists, paid plans for teams, and enterprise licensing, with features like unlimited track generation, style libraries, and direct download options. The company emphasizes copyright‑safe music, brand‑centric sonic identity, and collaborative tools for producers.

providers.name: StatCounter
providers.description: StatCounter provides web analytics services that help website owners track visitor behavior, traffic sources, and engagement in real time. Their platform offers features such as heatmaps, session replay, click fraud detection, and detailed reporting, catering to both small sites and enterprise customers. With a focus on ease of use, StatCounter delivers actionable insights without requiring extensive setup, supporting integration via a paid API for developers to build custom reports and applications.

providers.name: Sudoswap
providers.description: Sudoswap is a minimal, gas-efficient automated market maker (AMM) protocol for NFTs that facilitates NFT-to-token swaps using customizable bonding curves. It supports ERC-721 and ERC-1155 NFTs alongside ETH and ERC-20 tokens. Liquidity providers can create single-sided buy/sell pools or dual-sided trade pools to earn fees. Developers interact with the protocol through smart contracts (LSSVMPair, VeryFastRouter, bonding curve contracts) and off-chain indexing services such as The Graph subgraph and the Defined/Codex data API. Sudoswap v2 is deployed on Ethereum mainnet, Arbitrum, Base, Berachain, Sanko, and other EVM-compatible networks.

providers.name: Superduper
providers.description: Superduper (formerly SuperDuperDB) is an open-source Python framework for building database-integrated AI agents and applications directly on top of existing databases - MongoDB, SQL databases, Snowflake, and Redis - without separate vector stores or ETL. It supports semantic / vector search, RAG, transformer and PyTorch model integration, LLM serving, and distributed ML workflows. The commercial side, Superduper Agents, is an enterprise AI agent orchestration platform for BI and data operations, distributed via the Snowflake Marketplace and self-hosted enterprise installs.

providers.name: TOPdesk
providers.description: TOPdesk is a Netherlands-based service management vendor offering an ITSM and Enterprise Service Management platform used by IT, facilities, HR, and customer service teams for incident management, change management, asset management, self-service portals, and shared service workflows. The TOPdesk REST API uses application password authentication (basic auth) and exposes resources for incidents, changes, assets, persons, operators, and locations for building integrations against on-premises and SaaS TOPdesk environments.

providers.name: Uber Freight
providers.description: Uber Freight is a digital freight brokerage platform providing 24/7 access to truckload freight with instant quoting and booking, real-time shipment visibility, lane management, and carrier network pricing. Its REST APIs enable shippers and TMS platforms to generate price quotes, tender loads, cancel tenders, and automate facility scheduling — all backed by a network of 50,000+ carriers across the U.S. and Europe. API access uses OAuth 2.0 client credentials and requires approval of the freight.loads scope through the Uber developer portal.

providers.name: Valdera
providers.description: Valdera is the AI-powered sourcing and procurement platform for chemicals, ingredients, and raw materials, matching buyers with vetted global suppliers across a database of 400K+ suppliers and 1.7M+ unique chemistries. Buyers get supplier discovery, RFQs, and negotiation in one place; suppliers receive relevant inbound RFQs and fulfill orders on the platform. Valdera is a web platform, not an API provider — it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Volusion
providers.description: Volusion is an all-in-one e-commerce platform that provides merchants with a REST API for managing online store products, categories, customers, orders, shipping, and inventory across Volusion-hosted stores. API access is available on Business and Prime plans.

providers.name: Waiv
providers.description: Waiv is a Paris-based AI precision-testing company spun out of Owkin (formerly Owkin Dx) that builds clinically validated, AI-powered diagnostic tests for oncology and digital pathology. Its products — RlapsRisk BC (breast-cancer distant-relapse risk), the MSIntuit Suite (MSI/dMMR pre-screening in colorectal, gastric and endometrial cancer), BRCAura RUO (gBRCA pre-screening) and TLS Detect — read routine H&E whole-slide images to accelerate biomarker detection, outcome prediction and treatment-response assessment. The tests are delivered through Destra, an AI-native digital pathology platform that lab and clinician users reach in the browser and that laboratories can wire into an existing IMS/LIS through the Destra API. RlapsRisk BC and MSIntuit CRC hold dual CE-IVD marking under the EU IVDR. Waiv raised $33M led by OTB Ventures and Alpha Intelligence Capital, with Serena, Karista and SistaFund participating, and later closed $35M total with CRB Health Tech. The Destra API is advertised on the product page but is sales-gated — there is no public developer portal, reference, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: wallabag
providers.description: Wallabag is an open-source, self‑hostable read‑it‑later application that lets users save web articles to read later across devices. It offers features like import from Pocket, extensions, mobile apps, and a web interface, emphasizing privacy with no ads or tracking. The project is community‑driven, providing documentation, API access, and regular releases.

providers.name: whistle
providers.description: Tractive sells GPS tracking and health monitoring devices for dogs and cats. The smart trackers provide real‑time location, virtual fences, health insights, bark and scratch monitoring, and waterproof designs for pets of various sizes. Tractive markets these products directly to pet owners worldwide.

providers.name: Zilch
providers.description: Zilch is a London-headquartered "buy now, pay later" and ad-subsidised payments network founded in 2018, and one of the United Kingdom's most prominent BNPL brands. Rather than integrating at each retailer's checkout, Zilch is deliberately merchant-agnostic: consumers apply in the Zilch mobile app, receive a virtual (and physical) Mastercard, and can Pay-in-3, pay over six weeks, or Pay-now-and-earn-cashback anywhere Mastercard is accepted, online or in-store, through Apple Pay and Google Pay wallets. Because Zilch reaches merchants over the open Mastercard card rails and relies on partners such as Mastercard for card issuing and Checkout.com as its payments processor, it does not operate a public merchant-integration or developer platform the way a PSP or open-banking provider does. As of this review Zilch publishes no developer portal, no API reference, and no downloadable OpenAPI/Swagger specification; its public surface is a consumer marketing site, a help centre, and a customer sign-up/login app. This profile therefore records Zilch's verified public web properties honestly and carries no API entries, because none are publicly documented.

providers.name: Aident Loadout
providers.description: Aident Loadout provides a unified gateway for AI agents to securely access over 1,000 third‑party applications. Users connect each app once, then agents can invoke actions across services without handling raw credentials. The platform offers built‑in skills, balance management, and a dashboard for monitoring usage, aiming to simplify AI‑driven workflows in enterprise and developer contexts.

providers.name: AIReiter
providers.description: AIReiter provides a unified AI API platform offering text, image, and video generation across multiple leading models such as Claude, GPT, Gemini, VEO3, and Seedance. It supports asynchronous job handling, transparent credit‑based pricing, and OpenAI‑compatible endpoints, enabling developers to integrate multimodal AI capabilities with a single API key and billing system. The service includes model‑specific channels, webhook callbacks, and a developer console for API key management.

providers.name: AirWise Solutions
providers.description: AirWise Solutions is a Tulsa, Oklahoma drone operations software company founded in 2021. Its airwiseOS platform covers the full mission lifecycle for public safety and critical infrastructure teams: pre-flight planning and FAA authorizations including LAANC, real-time in-flight airspace awareness fusing ADS-B, Remote ID, RF, radar and weather data, and post-flight data, analytics and compliance. Products include Flight Manager, Nexus and UASidekick. The airwiseOS API exposes flight planning, real-time tracking, airspace restrictions and UTM coordination, and its documentation sits behind a developer-account sign-in.

providers.name: American Electric Power
providers.description: American Electric Power (AEP) is one of the largest electric utilities in the United States, delivering electricity to more than 5.6 million customers across 11 states through its regulated utility subsidiaries including AEP Ohio, AEP Texas, Appalachian Power, Indiana Michigan Power, Kentucky Power, Public Service Company of Oklahoma, and Southwestern Electric Power Company. AEP operates the nation's largest electricity transmission network spanning over 40,000 miles and maintains approximately 31,000 megawatts of generating capacity.

providers.name: Ancient8
providers.description: Ancient8 is a gaming-focused Ethereum Layer 2 blockchain built on the Optimism OP Stack with Celestia for data availability, designed to power Web3 gaming experiences at scale. The network is EVM-equivalent, so developers deploy Solidity smart contracts and dApps using standard tooling (Hardhat, Remix, thirdweb) against a public Ethereum JSON-RPC interface. Ancient8 Mainnet uses chain ID 888888888 with ETH as its gas currency, complemented by a Celestia-backed testnet, native and third-party bridges (Meson, Relay), block explorers (Routescan, Blockscout/A8Scan), a faucet, staking, and a vault. The programmable surface exposed to integrators is the JSON-RPC endpoint over HTTPS and WebSocket. Backed by Pantera Capital and surfaced into the API Evangelist network from its venture portfolio.

providers.name: Angle Health
providers.description: Angle Health is a San Francisco-based, AI-native health insurance company offering full-stack, level-funded group health plans for small and mid-sized employers. Its platform pairs rapid, firm, bindable quoting with a modern benefits-administration experience that integrates with 100+ payroll and HRIS systems, a member care team, iOS/Android mobile apps, and pharmacy benefits (AngleRx). Angle also runs a partner API platform that lets quoting platforms, broker technology providers, and MGAs generate fully underwritten, firm, bindable level-funded quotes in minutes, along with automated proposal generation and member health scorecards with risk and cost-driver analysis. Developer documentation lives in an access-on-request partner portal.

providers.name: Apache Log4j
providers.description: Apache Log4j is a versatile, industrial-grade Java logging framework composed of an API, its implementation, and components to assist deployment for various use cases. It is part of the Apache Logging Services project. Log4j is a Java library distributed as Maven artifacts and is consumed via its Java API rather than over the network; no public HTTP/REST surface is published.

providers.name: Apache Parquet
providers.description: APIs and tools for working with Apache Parquet, the open source columnar storage format for efficient analytics workloads. This index covers the format specification along with the major language implementations.

providers.name: AppLaunchFlow
providers.description: AppLaunchFlow provides a store‑ready app store and Google Play assets platform, offering AI‑powered screenshot, icon, video, and mockup generation tools. It helps developers create marketing assets, manage ASO copy, and integrate with ChatGPT via MCP. The service includes pricing plans, a blog, and a developer API for automating asset creation.

providers.name: Applied Industrial Technologies
providers.description: Applied Industrial Technologies, Inc. (NYSE: AIT) is a Cleveland, Ohio industrial distributor and technical solutions provider, founded in 1923, serving MRO and OEM customers across North America, Australia, New Zealand and Singapore. It distributes bearings, power transmission products, fluid power components, industrial rubber products, linear motion components, specialty flow control, tools and related supplies, and operates engineered fluid power and automation businesses alongside its distribution network. Its customer-facing storefront is applied.com, an SAP Commerce site; the company runs an Azure API Management gateway at api.applied.com but publishes no public developer program, API reference or machine-readable contract.

providers.name: Apprentice
providers.description: Apprentice (apprentice.io) is an AI-native manufacturing platform for the life sciences, delivering Tempo Manufacturing Cloud — a GxP-compliant SaaS suite that unifies a Manufacturing Execution System (MES), Laboratory Execution System (LES), Augmented Work Instructions (AWI), and the Tandem collaboration/guest layer across pharmaceutical, biotech, and cell-and-gene-therapy sites. Tempo digitizes batch records, recipe authoring, and quality data from raw materials to finished goods, and exposes a RESTful Apprentice Public API (7.4+) for integrating Tempo data and metadata with external systems. The platform is SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001:2022 certified and validated to FDA 21 CFR Part 11. Backed by ICONIQ Capital. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline from public surfaces; the Public API reference is gated to customers via their delivery lead / CSM.

providers.name: Arbor Biotechnologies
providers.description: Arbor Biotechnologies is a next-generation gene editing company founded in 2016 by Feng Zhang, David Walt, David Scott and Winston Yan, and headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts. Its proprietary AI- and machine-learning-guided discovery engine has produced a toolbox of programmable DNA editors spanning knockdown, nuclease excision and compact reverse-transcriptase editing, aimed at functionally curative genomic medicines. The wholly-owned pipeline is focused on liver disease (ABO-101 for primary hyperoxaluria type 1 and ABO-103, both LNP-delivered and partnered with Chiesi Group) and CNS disease (ABO-202, ABO-203 and ABO-204 for ALS, plus ABO-206, all AAV-delivered), alongside collaborative ex vivo cell therapy programs run with Vertex, Allogene, Edigene and Chiesi. Investors include ARCH Venture Partners, Ally Bridge Group, Temasek, TCG and the Samsung Life Science Fund. Arbor operates no product or developer API and publishes no developer portal, SDKs or API documentation; its corporate site does serve the standard WordPress REST API anonymously, which makes its press releases, site pages and taxonomies machine-readable.

providers.name: Bark
providers.description: Bark is a digital safety and parental-controls company that helps families keep children safer online and in the real world. Its AI-powered platform monitors texts, email, social media, web browsing, and 30+ apps across more than 20 content categories, flagging potential issues such as online predators, cyberbullying, self-harm, and adult content, and pairs that monitoring with screen-time management, app blocking, web filtering, and GPS location alerts. Bark ships as an app for existing iOS and Android devices as well as purpose-built hardware including the Bark Phone, Bark Watch, and Bark Home.

providers.name: Bespoke Post
providers.description: Bespoke Post is a New York City direct-to-consumer men's lifestyle retailer founded in 2011 by Rishi Prabhu and Steven Szaronos. It sells curated menswear, gear and home goods through a free-to-join membership: members answer an onboarding quiz, are offered a personalized monthly "Box of Awesome" shipment they can preview, swap or skip, and buy at member pricing. Alongside third-party independent brands the company operates its own labels, including Line of Trade and Fieldworth (apparel), Halfday (travel), Wren (outdoor), Ash and Fir (home and fragrance) and Marcellin (kitchen and bar). Bespoke Post publishes no public developer portal, API documentation or machine-readable specification. It does run an internal storefront API under /api/ on its own domain and - unusually for a retailer - names eight of those paths in robots.txt with explicit Allow directives for AI agents including GPTBot, ChatGPT-User, OAI-Searchbot, ClaudeBot, anthropic-ai, PerplexityBot, meta-externalagent and cohere-ai, while disallowing /api/ to every other agent.

providers.name: BMLT.app
providers.description: BMLT.app provides a full‑stack, open‑source solution for managing Narcotics Anonymous meetings. It offers a BMLT Server backend that synchronizes meeting lists instantly to front‑end applications such as Crouton, Bread, and Yap. Since its first alpha release in May 2009, BMLT has grown to host over half of the world’s known NA meetings, supporting dozens of servers, zones, regions, areas, groups, and tens of thousands of meetings. The platform enables service bodies to keep meeting information up‑to‑date across multiple apps, fostering community coordination and accessibility.

providers.name: BotSociety
providers.description: Botsociety is a tool to design, preview, and prototype conversational interfaces — chatbots and voice assistants — before they are built. Its API lets applications retrieve the content of a design (messages, intents, variables, and integration data) at runtime, so bot content can be updated in the design tool without redeploying bot code. The API exposes design retrieval plus a legacy apisociety 2.0 surface for managing conversations, messages, and variables, authenticated with a user id and a public API key sent as request headers. Botsociety, backed by 500 Global, is winding down ("working on a new direction") and its API host is presently unreachable; the artifacts in this repo are reconstructed from the official first-party npm client and public API documentation. Surfaced originally as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched into the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Build
providers.description: Build is an AI-native operating partner for the built world, pairing autonomous AI agents (its "Dougie" platform) with deep domain expertise to accelerate commercial real estate and infrastructure development. The platform automates mission-critical development workflows including site selection, due diligence, underwriting, investment-committee memos, test-fit analysis, market and zoning research, environmental diligence, and ESG reporting. Build serves institutional clients across data centers, industrials, energy, power, office, telecommunications, mixed-use, hotels, and multifamily. Backed by Index Ventures; profiled in the API Evangelist network. Build is a services company and does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Capacity
providers.description: Capacity provides a unified CX automation platform that leverages AI agents to automate, assist, analyze, and engage customers across voice, chat, SMS, email, and web channels. Founded in 2017 and part of the Equity.com incubator, it serves over 20,000 organizations, handling billions of automated interactions. The platform offers AI knowledge orchestration, real‑time agent assist, analytics, outbound campaigns, and industry‑specific solutions, aiming to reduce support costs and improve customer experiences.

providers.name: Carbon Data Solutions
providers.description: Carbon Data Solutions builds carbon.talent, a skills‑assessed data and AI talent platform, and carbon.iq, a data‑maturity and AI readiness platform for data teams globally. The company provides AI‑driven hiring tools and data readiness assessments, serving enterprises worldwide.

providers.name: Chargezoom
providers.description: Chargezoom provides an AI‑powered autonomous accounts receivable (AR) platform that automates the entire invoice‑to‑cash cycle. Their solution combines AR outreach, payment processing, and customer portal features into a single graph‑based system, reducing manual work and exceptions for enterprises. With integrations for major accounting software, credit‑card vaults, and recurring billing, Chargezoom helps businesses accelerate cash flow, improve collection rates, and deliver a seamless payment experience for both B2B and B2C customers.

providers.name: Cipherome
providers.description: Cipherome provides the COMPASS data analysis platform for healthcare and life‑science research. It transforms raw clinical, genomic and biobank data into clean, structured datasets, enables cohort definition, statistical analysis, AI model training and automated reporting, all through an intuitive no‑code GUI. The platform accelerates research by handling data extraction, transformation, exploration and visualization, letting scientists focus on insights rather than data wrangling.

providers.name: Citation File Format
providers.description: The Citation File Format (CFF) is a human- and machine-readable YAML schema for providing citation metadata for software and datasets in source code repositories. A CITATION.cff file at the root of a repository declares authors, version, DOI, release date, and reference metadata, enabling consistent academic attribution across publishing and discovery platforms. CFF is governed as an open community standard with a published JSON Schema, a guide, and a maintained schema repository on GitHub. Native integrations include GitHub citation display, Zenodo software publishing, and the Zotero browser plugin. Tooling includes cffinit for authoring, cffconvert for conversion to BibTeX/RIS/CodeMeta/EndNote formats, and the cff-validator GitHub Action for CI validation. The current schema version is 1.2.0.

providers.name: Cobalt
providers.description: Cobalt provides an AI‑powered offensive security platform that delivers continuous penetration testing as a service. Their solution combines human‑led expertise with automated testing, integrating with development workflows to identify and remediate vulnerabilities across web applications, APIs, mobile apps, and cloud environments. Cobalt’s platform offers flexible credit‑based pricing, real‑time reporting, and integrations that help organizations embed security into the software development lifecycle.

providers.name: Conduit
providers.description: Conduit provides an agentic procurement hub connecting businesses with over 13,000 merchants without fees. The platform monitors supply lines, ranks alternate suppliers, and enables agents to place orders within set limits, automating restocking and procurement workflows. It offers tools like MCP connectors, pipes, and a yard for managing vendor relationships, aiming to reduce risk and streamline B2B purchasing.

providers.name: Context Studios
providers.description: Context Studios is an AI-native development studio based in Berlin, offering AI agents on MCP, Claude, and GPT integrated into workflows. They deliver production‑ready MVPs within weeks, focusing on custom software, React, TypeScript, and AI integration services for enterprises.

providers.name: Databand
providers.description: DBND (Databand) is an open-source Python framework — a library, a set of APIs, and a CLI — for building, tracking, and observing data pipelines across data ingestion, preparation, ETL/ELT, and machine-learning workflows. It collects pipeline metadata (runs, metrics, dataframes, schemas) to give data-engineering teams a system of record for runs and to detect pipeline failures and data quality issues before they hit downstream consumers. The DBND SDK integrates with Apache Airflow, Apache Spark, Databricks, dbt, and IBM DataStage. Databand was acquired by IBM in 2022 and is now IBM Databand, part of IBM's data observability offering; the open-source DBND SDK remains published on PyPI and GitHub under the databand-ai organization.

providers.name: DatePhotos AI
providers.description: DatePhotos AI provides AI‑generated dating profile photos for platforms like Tinder, Bumble and Hinge. The service uses advanced generative models to create natural‑looking, high‑quality images that help users improve their first impression and increase match rates. It offers a web dashboard, mobile apps, and integrations, with features such as multiple style generations, realness scoring, and privacy controls. The company emphasizes data protection and user consent, and its platform is available globally.

providers.name: Dayuse
providers.description: Dayuse is a global online marketplace for daytime hotel bookings, letting travelers reserve 3-to-5-star hotel rooms by the hour or for a microstay during the day rather than for an overnight stay, at discounts of up to 75% off the nightly rate. Founded in France in 2010, the platform connects consumers with more than 9,000 partner hotels across roughly 29 countries, with use cases spanning remote work, layovers, wellness and spa access, and privacy. Hoteliers join through the Dayuse partner network and manage daytime inventory via the partner portal. Dayuse is backed by Partech and is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile; no public developer API is currently published, so this profile captures identity, partner surface, and domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Decker AI
providers.description: Decker AI provides real‑time Korean stock market signals, trading strategies, and market data via a public REST API. The platform offers live briefings, watchlists, and AI‑driven insights for KRX listings, delivering JSON payloads for signals, positions, and market state. It also hosts an MCP server exposing tool integrations and webhook notifications.

providers.name: EarlyFrame
providers.description: EarlyFrame provides a stateful edge webhook orchestration platform with a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server. It intercepts raw webhook payloads, transforms them into structured JSON, de‑duplicates, applies conditional routing, and fans out to Discord, Slack, Telegram and custom APIs. The service offers tiered plans, including a free sandbox, and supports AI‑agent integration via JSON‑RPC MCP.

providers.name: F6S
providers.description: The API Design Management Platform powering the world's leading API first companies.

providers.name: Granted
providers.description: Granted is an AI-plus-human healthcare navigation service that helps consumers reduce medical bills and manage health insurance. The platform detects billing errors (duplicate line items, up-coding, incorrect charges), finds unadvertised financial-assistance programs, negotiates discounts, optimizes insurance benefits, and manages claims communication across more than 1,300 insurance companies and patient portals. It runs on a success-based model that is free to use, charging only when it saves the user money (capped at $300 per bill or 10% of savings). Granted is a Forerunner Ventures portfolio company operating in the consumer health / medical-billing sector. It publishes a consumer web and iOS app rather than a public developer API.

providers.name: greytHR
providers.description: greytHR provides an AI‑first full‑suite HRMS and payroll platform serving over 33,000 companies across 30+ countries. It automates recruitment, onboarding, attendance, leave, payroll, performance management and compliance, offering a unified employee record and AI‑driven assistance (NAVOS) to simplify HR operations for enterprises of all sizes.

providers.name: HelloVerify
providers.description: HelloVerify is India's leading background verification (BGV) and employee screening company, delivering fast, accurate, and compliant primary-source verification for employment, education, healthcare credentialing, immigration, and enterprise workforce programs. The platform has completed 20M+ verifications for 2000+ organizations across 120+ countries, offering AI-powered background checks, customer KYC with identity and liveness, vendor due diligence (Certifier), and instant messaging-based verification (HelloV). HelloVerify operates an audited information-security and compliance program (ISO/IEC 27001, ISO/IEC 27701, ISO 9001, ISO 22301, Cyber Essentials, GDPR) and serves regulators, enterprises, SMBs, and applicants worldwide. Added to the API Evangelist network as a dcvc portfolio company; no public developer API surface is currently published.

providers.name: INBOTIQA
providers.description: INBOTIQA is a UK-based fintech whose flagship product, YUDOmail, is an Intelligent Business Email and shared-mailbox management platform for high-volume group inboxes at banks, BPOs and financial-services operations teams. YUDOmail layers over Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace to turn incoming emails into assigned, trackable tasks with ownership, due dates, SLA tracking, machine-learning triage and sentiment analysis, audit trails and analytics, without replacing the underlying email platform. It deploys in the cloud or on-premises, integrates with Symphony chat and Microsoft Teams, and is used across KYC, FX, collateral, settlements and trade-support functions. INBOTIQA was a 2019 Barclays Accelerator (powered by Techstars) company.

providers.name: Infinera
providers.description: Infinera is a vertically integrated optical networking and DWDM transport equipment vendor, known for its in-house photonic integrated circuits, coherent optical engines (ICE), XR optics, and the GX, Groove, and FlexILS system lines used by carriers, cloud/internet-content providers, and enterprises to build high-capacity transport networks. Infinera was acquired by Nokia (completed in 2025) and now operates as part of Nokia Optical Networks. Network programmability is delivered through open transport-networking standards (ONF TAPI, OpenConfig, gNMI/gNXI, NETCONF/YANG) and infrastructure automation (a published Terraform provider and an Ansible collection) rather than a single proprietary REST API.

providers.name: InvestCloud
providers.description: InvestCloud is a wealth-management technology company that provides an AI-driven digital wealth platform connecting advisors, financial institutions, asset managers, TAMPs, RIAs and investors across the full investment lifecycle. Its product surface spans front-office advisor and client solutions, a wealth data platform ("Digital Warehouse") that aggregates custodial, market and portfolio data, managed account solutions including the Advisor Programs List (APL) and Private Markets Account, post-trade processing and settlement, revenue management, and the NaviPlan and RetireUp financial planning products acquired with Advicent. InvestCloud markets a developer platform — branded "Wealthsqope Digital Developer" — offering web-service APIs, embeddable widgets, code recipes, client libraries and application API keys, but that platform and its reference documentation sit entirely behind a portal login, and no machine-readable API contract is published publicly.

providers.name: Issa
providers.description: Issa Compass is a software platform that simplifies Thailand visa applications, operated by Issara Platforms Pte. Ltd. (Singapore) and Issa Systems Co, Ltd. (Bangkok). The platform helps users identify which Thai visa they qualify for and manages the end-to-end application process: a two-minute eligibility questionnaire, document verification and pre-qualification checks, real-time tracking of requirements against thousands of criteria, and a money-back guarantee if a pre-qualified application is rejected. Supported visa types include the Destination Thailand Visa (DTV), Long-Term Resident (LTR), Retirement, Spouse, and Student visas. Issa is a portfolio company of 500 Global. There is no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Jackett
providers.description: Jackett provides a proxy server that translates queries from various torrent clients into a unified API, allowing users to search and retrieve torrent tracker results across many sources. It supports a wide range of trackers, offers configuration options, and can be self‑hosted via Docker or native installations on Windows, Linux, and macOS. The project is open‑source and maintained on GitHub, with active community contributions and documentation covering installation, usage, and API endpoints.

providers.name: Kindsight
providers.description: Kindsight provides fundraising intelligence platforms that help nonprofit organizations unlock opportunities through AI‑powered insights, integrated data, and modern fundraising tools. Their suite includes prospect research, CRM integrations, online giving, and analytics, serving sectors such as education, healthcare, and community foundations. Kindsight aims to enhance fundraising efficiency and effectiveness with data‑driven decision making.

providers.name: Metacritic
providers.description: Metacritic is a review aggregator that collects critic and user scores for games, movies, TV shows, and music, computing a weighted Metascore for each title. The Metacritic API (provided via Fabric Origin / IVA / Gracenote) gives programmatic access to Metascores, user scores, individual critic reviews, publication details, and entertainment rankings for movies and television. Unofficial community-built wrappers also expose game, movie, and TV data from Metacritic's public backend.

providers.name: modelpricewatch-com
providers.description: Model Price Watch provides a neutral, verified reference for LLM API pricing, tracking live token prices, context windows, benchmarks, and price history for hundreds of models across dozens of providers. The site offers a sortable table, detailed model pages, and an API for programmatic access to pricing data, aiming to help developers compare and choose LLM services efficiently.

providers.name: moodytiger
providers.description: moodytiger is a technology-driven, design-led activewear brand for kids, offering leggings, shorts, tees, skirts and outerwear for boys and girls. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners, its direct-to-consumer storefront runs on Shopify at moodytiger.com. The store has no bespoke first-party developer API, but it does expose a modern agent-native commerce surface: a published Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP, ucp.dev) MCP shopping endpoint, an /agents.md agent-instructions document mirrored at /llms.txt, and Shopify Customer Account OIDC discovery under /.well-known/. This profile captures those verifiable agent and well-known surfaces.

providers.name: Neko Health
providers.description: Neko Health is a Swedish preventive-healthcare company founded in 2018 by Daniel Ek and Hjalmar Nilsonne. It designs, engineers, and assembles its own full-body scanning hardware in Stockholm and operates clinics across Sweden, the UK (London, Manchester, Birmingham) and, following a $700M Series C, the United States. The roughly 60-minute Neko Health Scan is a non-invasive, radiation-free examination that captures millions of data points across the skin, heart, blood, and circulation in a single visit, feeding a consumer patient app. Neko exposes no public third-party developer API; its only public machine surface is a Duende IdentityServer OIDC provider (account.nekohealth.com) that authenticates the patient application. This profile was surfaced as a venture-portfolio lead and enriched from Neko's public web and identity surface.

providers.name: Novakid
providers.description: Novakid is an online English language school for children aged roughly 4-12, founded in 2017 by Max Azarov and Dmitry Malin, incorporated in the United States and operating as a fully remote company with a head office in London. It delivers 25-minute one-to-one and small-group video lessons with native and near-native speaking teachers through a proprietary gamified virtual classroom, on a curriculum aligned to the CEFR framework, and sells directly to parents as a subscription across Europe, Latin America, the Middle East and Asia. Novakid is a direct-to-consumer education product: as of this profile it publishes no developer portal, no API reference, no SDKs and no machine-readable API contract of any kind, and its production API host serves a blanket robots.txt disallow.

providers.name: Phyllo
providers.description: Phyllo provides APIs that give developers access to public and consented social data across 25+ platforms, enabling influencer discovery, brand safety vetting, social listening, background verification, and financial services such as income assessment and visa checks. Their platform consolidates multiple social media sources into a single API, offering tools for creator tools, identity verification, content publishing, and AI-driven insights, aimed at influencer marketing, PR agencies, and financial institutions.

providers.name: Provus
providers.description: Provus (Provusinc) is an agentic AI Configure, Price, Quote (CPQ) platform built specifically for services organizations — professional services, consulting, and asset-based services firms. The platform turns unstructured inputs such as emails, RFPs, and call notes into structured, accurate services quotes, and runs a set of AI agents (Quote Optimizer, Deal Predictor, Proposal Response, Deal Rescue, and Provus Admin) that monitor deals, optimize pricing, assess risk, and protect margin. Provus ships two products — CPQ Express for growing teams and Enterprise Services CPQ for large organizations — with native connectors to Salesforce, HubSpot, Kantata, NetSuite, and DocuSign. It is backed by Norwest Venture Partners and reports managing over $5B in enterprise services revenue across customers including Thoughtworks, Trace3, and Prolifics. Provus does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal; integration is delivered through native prebuilt connectors and a Salesforce AppExchange managed package, and product help documentation is hosted on a Document360 knowledge base at docs.provus.ai that 302s the entire site to a login. Provus names an internal "Profet API" in its published sub-processor list, but that service is not documented, versioned, or reachable publicly.

providers.name: Quatrix (Maytech)
providers.description: Quatrix, operating under the Maytech brand, provides secure file transfer, automated data acquisition, and compliant data sharing solutions for enterprises across industries such as finance, healthcare, and media. Their platform offers SFTP hosting, secure file sharing, large‑file transfers, and data rooms, emphasizing PCI compliance and robust security features.

providers.name: Seeed Studio
providers.description: Seeed Studio is a global IoT hardware enabler offering a wide range of open‑source hardware, development boards, sensors, and modules. Founded in 2010, it supports makers, startups, and enterprises with products like the Wio Terminal, Grove system, and reComputer series, plus a comprehensive wiki, community forums, and developer resources. The company emphasizes rapid prototyping, open‑source collaboration, and end‑to‑end solutions from hardware to cloud services.

providers.name: ShopShops
providers.description: ShopShops is a livestream commerce marketplace for authenticated pre-owned luxury and designer goods — handbags, jewelry, watches, accessories, and shoes sold through live shopping events and an online store. Buyers shop curated secondhand inventory with authentication (via Entrupy), buy-now-pay-later (Afterpay / Shop Pay), and return assurance (Seel). The storefront runs on Shopify and publishes a live agent-commerce surface: a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) merchant profile, an MCP endpoint for agent-driven catalog search and buyer-approved checkout, an OIDC/OAuth2 Customer Account API, and an llms.txt describing how AI shopping agents may transact with the store.

providers.name: skuit-ai
providers.description: SKUit provides instant, validated Bills of Materials (BOMs) for networking equipment such as switches, routers, transceivers, licences and power. Users describe their deployment—data center, campus, edge, or telco—and the platform assembles the right parts, leveraging expert‑reviewed knowledge and AI‑driven workflows. It supports major vendors including Cisco, Arista, Juniper and more, delivering accurate BOMs in minutes rather than days.

providers.name: SkyFoundry
providers.description: SkyFoundry, founded in 2009 and headquartered in Glen Allen, Virginia, develops SkySpark, an analytics and informatics platform that connects, stores, analyzes, and visualizes data from smart devices, automation and control systems, meters, and sensors to "find what matters" in large equipment and facility datasets. SkySpark automatically detects issues, patterns, deviations, faults, and cost-reduction opportunities across intelligent buildings, industrial, agriculture, energy, government, and healthcare facilities, and has been applied to over 15,000 buildings spanning more than a billion square feet. SkySpark is a native Project Haystack server: external applications integrate through the Haystack HTTP REST API (ops such as read, hisRead, hisWrite, pointWrite, watchSub/watchPoll, eval, commit, and nav) with Zinc, JSON, Trio, and CSV data formats, and authenticate using the Haystack SCRAM (SHA-256) handshake with bearer authTokens. The company sells through a network of 140+ OEM, systems-integrator, and value-added-distributor channel partners rather than a self-service public SaaS.

providers.name: Source Beauty
providers.description: Source Beauty is an online beauty and wellbeing marketplace serving Egypt, selling skincare, makeup, fragrance, hair care, body care, K-beauty and wellness/supplement products from hundreds of local Egyptian and international brands. The consumer-facing storefront (sourcebeauty.com) offers curated brand pages, bundles and gift sets, promotional offers, bilingual English/Arabic shopping, and free shipping on qualifying orders. Source Beauty is a 500 Global portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass the company operates a direct-to-consumer e-commerce website only and publishes no public developer program, API, SDKs, or technical documentation.

providers.name: Standard Industries
providers.description: Standard Industries is a privately-held global industrial company headquartered in New York City and tracing its origins to 1886. The company operates a portfolio of building solutions, performance materials, logistics, real estate, and investment businesses, with more than 20,000 employees and approximately $11 billion in annual revenues. Standard Building Solutions includes GAF (North America's largest roofing manufacturer), GAF Energy (Timberline Solar nailable solar shingles), BMI Group (Europe's largest pitched and flat roofing manufacturer, with brands including Braas, Monier, Icopal, Wolfin, and Redland), Siplast (specialty roofing and waterproofing for iconic structures), SGI (mining and mineral processing), Schiedel (flue, stove, and ventilation systems), and Standard Logistics. Performance Materials is anchored by W. R. Grace & Co., which produces catalysts, engineered materials, process technologies, and fine chemicals. Standard Investments deploys capital across public equities and early-to-growth venture investments. Winter Properties is a vertically integrated real estate firm with more than 100 years of history in New York City. Standard Industries does not publish a public developer API or developer portal at the corporate level; technology integration with customers and partners is handled inside the individual operating companies (most notably GAF and Grace).

providers.name: Tebi
providers.description: Tebi is a hospitality management platform that unifies point-of-sale, payments, and back-office operations for restaurants, bars, cafes, bakeries, quick-service venues, and events. The system connects front-of-house service to back-office administration in a single product spanning Point of Sale, Kitchen Display System, Reservations, integrated card Payments (with invoicing and split-bill), QR ordering, inventory management, CRM, recipe management, and AI-driven insights. Tebi is priced on a revenue-based subscription (the first EUR 10k of monthly revenue is free, each additional EUR 10k costs EUR 20/month) with no long-term contracts, and it bundles its own payment processing with transparent per-transaction fees. The company is backed by Index Ventures. Tebi does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or a developer portal; this profile captures its production identity, help center, changelog, status page, and security posture as surfaced by the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: tradeos-xyz
providers.description: TradeOS provides an AI‑powered reasoning engine for financial markets, enabling traders and institutions to build autonomous trading agents that analyze charts, data, and strategies without coding. The platform integrates market data, technical indicators, and large language models to deliver explainable, 24/7 AI decision support across stocks, commodities, FX, and crypto. TradeOS offers a marketplace, pricing plans, and extensive documentation for building and deploying custom agents.

providers.name: Vela
providers.description: Vela is an AI scheduling assistant from Y Combinator's Winter 2026 batch that handles the ambiguity that breaks scheduling. Added to any email thread or messaging conversation, it negotiates on the user's behalf — reading context, proposing meeting times across timezones, following up with participants, detecting calendar conflicts, rescheduling, and sending invites once scheduling is finalized. It works across Gmail, Outlook, Slack, Teams, WhatsApp, SMS, and phone, and is used by enterprise recruiters coordinating thousands of multi-party interviews a week as well as executives who need white-glove coordination at scale.

providers.name: Wolf
providers.description: Wolf (fromwolf.com) is a white-label, multi-tenant staffing and gig-work platform that lets staffing companies run their own branded on-demand workforce. Its API coordinates job seekers, clients, campaigns (client orders), shifts, tenders (a seeker's request to work a shift), applications, timesheets, availability, notifications, and in-app chat — everything needed to build a client- or worker-facing staffing interface on top of the Wolf backend. Each tenant runs on its own database and authenticates with a tenant key plus a platform API key or per-user authentication token. Wolf was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and profiled by the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: 3DOptix
providers.description: 3DOptix provides native‑cloud optical prototyping and optical bench simulation software. Their platform offers design‑studio tools, AI‑assisted optical design, OptiTwin and TrueScene beta programs, and a suite of simulation widgets, catalog, filter finder, and API integration for developers to embed optical design capabilities into applications. The company serves industries such as imaging, academia, and engineering with cloud‑based solutions and extensive documentation, tutorials, and support resources.

providers.name: Afilio
providers.description: Afilio (Afilio - Gesellschaft für Vorsorge mbH) is a Berlin-based digital provision platform ("Vorsorgeplattform") that helps German families prepare for emergencies, care situations, and death. Through a paid membership, users create legally valid advance directives (Patientenverfügung), healthcare powers of attorney (Vorsorgevollmacht), and wills (Testament), and maintain a digital inventory of documents and assets. A central emergency card gives doctors and relatives 24/7 access to critical medical and provision information, and Afilio also assists with care-level (Pflegegrad) applications and expert consultation. Over four million families use the GDPR-compliant service. Afilio is a consumer (B2C) platform and does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile captures its public product, legal, and security surface. Backed by Speedinvest.

providers.name: Anduin
providers.description: Anduin (Anduin Transactions) is a private-markets technology company that digitizes investor onboarding and fund operations for venture capital, private equity, and hedge funds. Its platform replaces paper-based subscription workflows with electronic fund subscription documents, secure data rooms, investor data management, an engagement hub, an integration hub, automated data extraction, and e-signature. The company reports 1,305+ funds served, $244B+ capital raised, and 74,000+ investors subscribed. Anduin publishes no public developer API or OpenAPI; this profile captures its public company, trust, and security surfaces (Trust Center, RFC 9116 security.txt, and domain-security posture). Backed by 8vc; surfaced to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead and enriched by the pipeline.

providers.name: Arine
providers.description: Arine is a San Francisco-based healthcare technology company that operates an AI-driven medication intelligence and comprehensive medication management platform for health plans, government payors and risk-bearing provider organizations. The platform ingests pharmacy and medical claims, clinical, cost, quality, behavioral and social-determinants-of-health data, then applies machine learning and clinical decision logic to surface medication-related gaps in care and generate targeted, just-in-time interventions, member education materials and prescriber communications. Arine packages this as four solutions — LUMINATE (high-risk member management), RESONATE (prescriber analytics), ELEVATE (Star Ratings and quality improvement) and ELEVATE MTM (medication therapy management) — delivered as a SaaS portal running in AWS. The Arine Platform holds HITRUST Risk-based 2-year (r2) certification. Arine ships no public developer program: its API gateway at api.arine.io is closed to anonymous callers and its product documentation portal at docs.arine.io sits behind customer authentication, so no machine-readable API contract is publicly available.

providers.name: Attivo Networks (SentinelOne)
providers.description: Attivo Networks was a pioneer in identity threat detection and response (ITDR), cyber deception, and Active Directory attack protection. SentinelOne acquired Attivo Networks in 2022 and folded its technology into SentinelOne Singularity Identity, part of the AI-powered Singularity security platform spanning endpoint (EDR/XDR), identity, and cloud security. There is no standalone public Attivo API; programmatic access is delivered through the SentinelOne management console REST API (v2.1), which is scoped to a customer's console URL rather than a public developer portal. This API Evangelist profile tracks the combined entity's public security, trust, disclosure, and compliance surface: a published RFC 9116 security.txt, a HackerOne-hosted bug bounty, and a SafeBase trust center carrying SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001/27017/27018, FedRAMP, and TX-RAMP certifications.

providers.name: Belk
providers.description: Belk is a privately-held American department store chain headquartered in Charlotte, North Carolina, serving the southeastern United States. The company sells clothing, handbags, jewelry, beauty products, and home goods. Belk operates an omnichannel retail model with physical stores and an online marketplace. Supplier and marketplace integrations are handled via EDI through value-added networks, with order management integration available through Rithum (formerly CommerceHub) and other channel management platforms. Belk publishes no public HTTP API, developer portal, OpenAPI or SDK: the only integration contract it publishes is the mandatory X12 4030 EDI supplier program (850/856/810/820/824/855/860 and more), documented as PDF implementation guides and routed through a VAN.

providers.name: Bloomberg Index Solutions Limited (BISL)
providers.description: Bloomberg Index Solutions Limited (BISL) is the entity that administers Bloomberg's fixed income and multi-asset indices, including the Bloomberg Global Aggregate Bond Index and other benchmark indices. BISL provides index data, calculations, and licensing for asset managers and financial institutions using Bloomberg indices as benchmarks or for financial product construction.

providers.name: Bloomberg Instant Messaging
providers.description: Bloomberg Instant Messaging (IB) is a secure, compliant messaging platform embedded in the Bloomberg Terminal and accessible via Bloomberg Anywhere. It enables real-time communication between financial professionals globally, with message archiving, compliance monitoring, and integration capabilities. Bloomberg also provides B-Chat for broader enterprise messaging connectivity.

providers.name: Bloomberg Message
providers.description: Bloomberg Message is the core messaging service within the Bloomberg Terminal ecosystem, enabling financial professionals to communicate securely through the Bloomberg IB (Instant Bloomberg) messaging system. It provides a compliant, archived communication channel for trading desks, asset managers, and financial institutions to exchange information, research, and trade-related messages.

providers.name: Bloomberg Query Language (BQL)
providers.description: Bloomberg Query Language (BQL) is a proprietary query language for accessing, filtering, aggregating, and computing on Bloomberg's financial data universe. BQL enables users to write flexible data requests that go beyond standard API fields, supporting derived calculations, time series expressions, and complex filtering of securities and data points. Available in the Bloomberg Terminal, Excel Add-in, and via API.

providers.name: Boldfit
providers.description: Boldfit is an Indian direct-to-consumer fitness and sportswear brand selling workout equipment (pull-up bars, resistance bands, massage guns, yoga mats and lifting gear), performance footwear (running, trekking, walking, cricket and badminton shoes) and athletic apparel for men and women. The brand positions itself around fitness and performance, partnering with athletes, and sells primarily to the Indian market through a Shopify-hosted online store at boldfit.com. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. Boldfit does not run a public developer program or API; the only programmatic surface is the Shopify Customer Account OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect layer exposed on the storefront.

providers.name: Branding Brand
providers.description: Branding Brand is a Pittsburgh-based digital and mobile commerce technology company that has built native apps, progressive web apps, and websites for enterprise retailers for more than fifteen years. Its public developer surface is the open-source Flagship and Flagship Code React Native toolkits — a configuration-as-code framework with reusable commerce components, commerce data adapters, analytics/CMS modules, and a CLI — published under the @brandingbrand npm scope. The company also offers Shipcode, an AI-assisted no-code platform for building digital commerce experiences. Branding Brand is backed by Insight Partners. It publishes no public REST API or OpenAPI; this profile catalogs its open-source packages, CLI, and developer resources.

providers.name: Brickway
providers.description: Brickway provides a LEGO® and alt‑brick collection and build tracker app. Users can track sets from wish‑list to built, monitor minifig counts, scan sealed boxes, and share collections with family. The service offers a 14‑day free trial and a subscription for full features, supporting iOS, Android, and web platforms.

providers.name: Bstow
providers.description: Bstow is a fintech-for-good startup whose flagship product, Cheerful Giving, lets nonprofits and their supporters raise money through spare-change round-up donations, recurring gifts, and branded campaign pages. Backed by 500 Global, Bstow's Cheerful Giving product now operates as part of the Goodworld social-impact platform (goodworldnow.com), which layers on giving forms, events, peer-to-peer and workplace/payroll giving, text engagement, and an impact CRM. The platform documents webhooks and partner integrations (Salesforce, Stripe, PayPal, Klaviyo, Zapier, Fundraise Up) but does not publish a public, self-serve API reference or OpenAPI specification; API access is arranged directly with the vendor through a sales-gated developer portal. This profile was surfaced from the 500 Global portfolio and enriched by the pipeline.

providers.name: BuzzSearch
providers.description: BuzzSearch provides AI‑powered tools to discover ad angles on Reddit and TikTok, tracking brand visibility across ChatGPT, Gemini, and Google AI Overviews. It monitors rankings, sentiment, and citations in real time, helping marketers improve their outreach and measure impact across major social platforms.

providers.name: Caya
providers.description: Caya (Caya GmbH, Berlin) is a German intelligent document processing (IDP) company whose Document Automation Suite digitizes, classifies, and routes business documents end to end. Its core capabilities are Post Scan (physical mail intake with OCR and automatic classification), Document Extractions (AI-powered structured data extraction), and Document Automations (rule-based routing and distribution into downstream systems). Caya connects to 100+ tools across accounting, ERP, HR, cloud storage, and e-signature, and hosts data in a high-security Frankfurt data center. It is certified and compliant against ISO 27001, GDPR/DSGVO, DORA, GoBD, and German HGB/AO retention rules, with a public Vanta-hosted trust center. Surfaced as an HV Capital portfolio company and enriched into the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Cermati
providers.description: Cermati (PT Agregasi Cermat Indonesia) is a fintech aggregator offering a platform for loans, credit cards, insurance, investments and gold products in Indonesia. It provides consumers with information and access to thousands of financial products, and offers API access to product data for developers. Registered with OJK, it operates via its website https://www.cermati.com and mobile app.

providers.name: Concourse
providers.description: Concourse builds AI agents for corporate finance teams. Its platform lets finance, accounting, and data teams query financial data in natural language, generate board and investor reporting with commentary, and run forecasts and scenarios against real-time data. Concourse connects natively to financial and operational systems including QuickBooks, NetSuite, Ramp, Snowflake, Salesforce, HubSpot, Stripe, Brex, Rippling, Gusto, BigQuery, and Databricks, and says it cuts manual finance work by over 75%. The company is SOC 2 Type II certified and backed by CRV, raising a $12M Series A alongside general availability. This profile was surfaced from a VC portfolio and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Conduitly
providers.description: Conduitly provides a platform that connects and automates data flow between business applications. It enables companies to integrate various SaaS tools, automate repetitive tasks, and streamline workflows without manual data entry. By offering a wide range of integrations across HR, payroll, sales, marketing, and more, Conduitly helps businesses reduce busywork, improve efficiency, and focus on core activities. The service includes customizable automation, a marketplace of pre-built connectors, and tools for building custom integrations, aiming to accelerate work and eliminate duplicate data entry.

providers.name: D Fetcher
providers.description: D Fetcher provides a simple web calculator and open JSON API to estimate how long you need sun exposure to achieve a target vitamin D dose. It uses real‑time UV index data, location lookup, skin type, body surface area and age to compute minutes of sunlight needed. The service is free, CORS‑open, and requires no API key, making it easy to integrate into health apps, wearables, or personal dashboards.

providers.name: Demystdata
providers.description: Demystdata provides an external data management platform that enables businesses to ingest, store, and orchestrate data from multiple sources. The platform offers APIs for data ingestion, transformation, and retrieval, supporting compliance and privacy controls. Founded in 2026, Demystdata serves enterprises seeking scalable data pipelines and governance.

providers.name: Dinilu
providers.description: Dinilu is a supplier of quality promotional products and printed matter from the Far East. They offer a quick quotation tool for customized items, with competitive pricing, quality control, shipping and delivery to customers' doors. The company operates online, providing a range of branded products, including temporary tattoos, playing cards, rolling papers, and first aid supplies, catering to businesses seeking promotional merchandise. Their site includes product catalogs, RSS feeds, and contact information, reflecting a comprehensive e‑commerce platform for promotional and printed goods.

providers.name: Dinilu Promotional & Printed Products
providers.description: Dinilu Promotional & Printed Products is a Guangzhou‑based trading company offering a wide range of custom promotional items, printed matter, branded merchandise and disposable gifts sourced from the Far East. Customers can obtain online quotations, calculate costs and delivery times quickly, and benefit from worldwide shipping, quality control and competitive pricing. The company was founded in 2024 and serves global businesses seeking reliable promotional product solutions.

providers.name: DolarApp
providers.description: DolarApp — rebranded to ARQ in March 2026 — is a Latin American cross-border fintech founded in Mexico in 2022 by former Revolut operators Fernando Terres, Zach Garman and Alvaro Correa. It gives consumers and businesses in Mexico, Argentina, Colombia and Brazil digital dollar (USDc) and euro (EURc) accounts, US ACH/wire receiving details, international cards accepted in 180+ countries, interbank-rate FX conversion, bulk supplier and contractor payouts, corporate cards with spend controls, and investment and credit products. It reports roughly two million users and is backed by Sequoia Capital, Founders Fund, Brevan Howard Digital, Y Combinator and Kaszek. DolarApp/ARQ runs a private API host at api.dolarapp.com for its own mobile and web applications but publishes no public developer program, documentation or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Duco
providers.description: Duco is an AI-powered operational data automation platform for financial services. It helps banks, asset managers, brokers, asset servicers and market infrastructure firms normalize, validate and reconcile any data in the cloud — cutting the time spent on manual data work, reducing operational risk and accelerating front-, middle- and back-office processes. The no-code platform ingests data from any source (including unstructured documents via Adaptive Intelligent Document Processing), then transforms, matches, reconciles and publishes it with full audit and control. Duco's Agentic Workspace layers agentic AI over these operations so agents can handle repetitive extraction, matching and exception-labelling work under human oversight. Use cases span securities and derivatives reconciliation, ETD clearing, OTC confirmations, custody, cash accounts, crypto holdings and transaction/regulatory reporting (EMIR, CFTC, MiFID II, ASIC, MAS, T+1). Customers include HSBC, Deutsche Bank, ING, Santander, Northern Trust and Fidelity Digital Assets. Duco is backed by Insight Partners.

providers.name: EarnUp
providers.description: EarnUp is a San Francisco-based financial-wellness fintech that automates consumer debt paydown and savings. Using patented technology and predictive analytics, its platform lets people schedule and automatically make payments toward mortgages, auto loans, student loans, and other personal debt, and save for life events. EarnUp sells engagement and AI-advisor tooling to lenders, mortgage servicers, credit unions, employers, unions, and financial professionals, and reports that more than three million people have used the platform. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Bain Capital Ventures, this is a company profile in the API Evangelist network; EarnUp publishes no public developer API, so enrichment is limited to identity and security posture.

providers.name: Elisity
providers.description: Elisity is a San Jose-based cybersecurity company (founded 2019, backed by Insight Partners) that builds an AI-powered, identity-based microsegmentation platform for Zero Trust security. Elisity discovers, classifies, and continuously monitors every user, workload, and device, then enforces dynamic least-privilege policies to stop lateral movement, without agents, new hardware, or network changes, by leveraging the Cisco, Arista, and Juniper switches organizations already own. The platform centers on Elisity IdentityGraph (real-time asset visibility enriched from sources like Active Directory, CrowdStrike, and Armis), a Dynamic Policy Engine, lightweight Virtual Edge container software that syncs policy to existing infrastructure, and the Cloud Control Center admin portal. Its product API and Open Connector integration API are documented inside the authenticated Cloud Control Center rather than a public developer portal. Elisity is used by Fortune 500 healthcare systems, manufacturers, and pharmaceutical firms for IoMT, OT/ICS, and enterprise segmentation.

providers.name: Ermeo
providers.description: Ermeo (rebranded Causeway Field) is a French connected-operator / field-operations SaaS platform that lets industrial and field teams digitize paper procedures into dynamic, interactive workflows for inspections, maintenance, and interventions. Operators complete pre-built interactive forms on mobile, capture equipment and report data in the field in real time, and operational managers monitor all field work from a central console. Ermeo exposes a REST API secured with OAuth 2.0 so customers can connect their information systems (CMMS, MES, EDM) to import and synchronize equipment, forms, and reports and enrich the data collected in the field.

providers.name: Findoctave
providers.description: Findoctave (operating as Octave) is a mental health care provider offering virtual and in-person therapy across 20+ U.S. states. Services include individual, couples, and family therapy, DBT, and specialized centers of excellence for perinatal and postpartum health, LGBTQIA+ (queer resiliency), trauma, and women's emotional health. Octave is in-network with major insurers (Aetna, Blue Shield of California, BCBS plans, Health Net, and others) and publishes a therapist directory, cost calculator, and getting-started flow through its consumer website. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Felicis and added to the API Evangelist network; Octave exposes no public developer API, so this profile is a company identity record rather than an API listing.

providers.name: Fresha
providers.description: Fresha is a marketplace and business-management platform for the beauty and wellness industry — salons, barbershops, spas, medspas and independent professionals. Consumers discover and instantly book appointments across 120+ countries (over one billion appointments booked), while businesses run scheduling and calendar, client management, point of sale, integrated card and online payments, automated messaging (SMS, WhatsApp and email) and marketing. Fresha is subscription-free for businesses, monetizing through payment processing, marketing add-ons and new-client marketplace fees, and is backed by investors including Partech and KKR. Fresha does not currently publish a public developer API or developer portal; its public engineering footprint is the open-source @fresha Web API tooling on GitHub (OpenAPI lint, diff and codegen).

providers.name: gjalla-io
providers.description: Gjalla.io is a technology company focused on providing innovative solutions in the IoT and data analytics space. Founded to bridge the gap between complex data streams and actionable insights, Gjalla.io offers a suite of APIs that enable developers to integrate real-time device telemetry, analytics dashboards, and automated reporting into their applications. The platform emphasizes scalability, security, and ease of integration, supporting a wide range of industries including smart manufacturing, environmental monitoring, and logistics. With a commitment to open standards and developer-friendly documentation, Gjalla.io aims to empower businesses to harness the power of connected devices and data-driven decision making.

providers.name: HAMAMA
providers.description: Hamama is a West Sacramento, California consumer-products company that makes it easy to grow fresh microgreens at home. Founded by two MIT-trained mechanical engineers, Hamama sells self-watering microgreen grow kits and its signature pre-seeded "Seed Quilts" (non-GMO, mostly Certified Organic) that sprout edible greens in 7-10 days with nothing more than a single addition of water, no soil, pesticides, or fertilizer required. The company sells grow kits, ceramic trays, Seed Quilt refills, green-onion and mushroom kits, and accessories directly to consumers through its Shopify storefront, offers flexible subscribe-and-save refill plans, and supports growers with Growing Guides, recipes, a rewards program, and a Grow Coach customer-support team.

providers.name: Juno Chat
providers.description: Juno (junocompanion.com), operated by SharedGenes, Inc., is a Y Combinator-backed (P26) consumer digital-health startup building an AI personal health assistant for the 1B+ people living with chronic illness. The Juno mobile app (iOS and Android) builds a longitudinal health profile through conversation, biometrics, and medical history to deliver personalized symptom guidance, automated symptom tracking by text or voice, trigger-pattern identification, and appointment-ready reports for clinicians. It supports conditions including fibromyalgia, long COVID, POTS, ME/CFS, EDS, endometriosis, lupus, and MS, and is informed by research from Oxford and UCL plus 1,000+ patient interviews. Founded in 2025 by Marshall Gould (CEO) and Isaac Tolley (CTO); HIPAA-aligned infrastructure with no health data sold. Juno also publishes Juno Open Health Tools, an MIT-licensed remote MCP server at https://juno-health-tools.vercel.app/api/mcp with five read-only, consent-gated tools that turn a user's non-identifying health notes into non-diagnostic appointment-preparation material; it is listed in the official MCP Registry and archived on Zenodo (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21730086). Juno publishes no REST API or SDK.

providers.name: Kiwibot
providers.description: Kiwibot — legally Kiwi Campus, Inc., and rebranded to Robot.com in October 2025 — builds and operates fleets of autonomous sidewalk delivery robots, warehouse logistics robots, quadruped and humanoid platforms, and robot-mounted advertising units. Founded in Berkeley, California in 2017 by Felipe Chavez and Jason Oviedo out of a UC Berkeley campus food-delivery pilot, the company reports more than 1.7 million completed real-world autonomous tasks for campus dining, retail, grocery and enterprise customers across the United States, Canada, Colombia, the United Arab Emirates and Saudi Arabia, and acquired mobile-advertising firm Nickelytics in 2023. Its B2B delivery platform is exposed as an API-key-gated REST service on a Google Cloud Endpoints gateway at api.kiwibot.com — historically integrated by ordering partners such as Shopify and Ordermark — but the company publishes no developer portal, no public API reference, and no machine-readable contract; access runs through the sales/demo form. Its autonomy team publishes substantial first-party open source ROS 2 tooling from the github.com/kiwicampus organization.

providers.name: Lighten
providers.description: Lighten Platforms, Inc. is a San Mateo, California healthcare AI company building an AI-native platform for clinical evidence curation from electronic health record (EHR) data. Its 360° EHR Curation Platform reasons over unstructured clinical notes together with structured records to reconstruct complete patient journeys, applying clinically validated quality assurance at the variable, patient, and cohort level rather than relying on model accuracy metrics alone. On top of that curation layer Lighten delivers Apps & Insights for patient finding and HCP targeting, longitudinal patient journeys, and market intelligence, plus a "Beyond Claims" offering that integrates curated EHR signal with claims data for broader coverage. The company serves life sciences, health systems, data and analytics consultancies, and investors, and was founded by Xinkun Nie, PhD. Lighten publishes no public developer API program, SDKs, or developer documentation as of this profile.

providers.name: Lightning Labs
providers.description: At Lightning Labs, we develop software that powers the Lightning Network.
