Our open source, secure, and scalable Lightning systems enable users to send and receive money more efficiently than ever before. We also offer a series of verifiable, non-custodial Lightning-based financial services. We bridge the world of open source software and the next-generation of bitcoin financial software.

providers.name: Liveu
providers.description: LiveU is a provider of cloud-based, IP-bonded live video contribution, production, and distribution technology for broadcasters, sports, news, public safety, and enterprise. Its portfolio spans field encoders (the LU-series and the Q Era LU900Q), the LiveU Central cloud management platform, LiveU Studio and Nexus production tools, the LiveU Matrix distribution grid, DataBridge and LU-LINK connectivity, and the LiveU Solo streaming line. LiveU pioneered bonded-cellular transmission that aggregates multiple LTE/5G, Wi-Fi, and satellite links into a single reliable, low-latency video feed. This profile was surfaced as a venture-capital portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; LiveU publishes marketing, support, and training surfaces but no public developer portal, OpenAPI, or open API documentation was found - the LiveU Central API is available to customers behind authentication.

providers.name: Maisa
providers.description: Maisa is an enterprise agentic-AI company whose platform, Maisa Studio, lets non-technical teams build, deploy, and manage "Digital Workers" — AI agents that automate complex, regulated, end-to-end business processes. Its proprietary Knowledge Processing Unit (KPU) and Chain-of-Work approach combine large and small language models to deliver deterministic, auditable, hallucination-resistant execution rather than probabilistic responses, making it regulator-ready from day one. Maisa targets highly regulated verticals — banking and financial services, insurance, manufacturing and supply chain, and engineering/infrastructure — with an employee-based pricing model instead of per-token API billing. Maisa also exposes a developer REST API at api.maisa.ai (API-key authenticated via X-API-Key) with capabilities (compare/extract/summarize over text and media), models (embeddings, rerank), a KPU run endpoint, a file-interpreter (PDF/DOCX/HTML/image/audio), and Mainet search — with official first-party Python and Node SDKs both named "maisa"; the Maisa Studio product and the docs portal (docs.maisa.ai) sit behind an AWS Cognito login. Backed by Creandum and ForgePoint, Maisa has raised a $25M seed round and been named a Gartner front-runner in agentic AI. This profile was enriched from Maisa's public marketing surface, llms.txt, and the official open-source SDK repositories.

providers.name: Maloja
providers.description: Maloja is an open-source, self-hosted music scrobble database that lets users collect and analyze their listening habits. It provides charts, artist association insights, and customizable images without relying on external music services. Users can run it via Docker or Podman, configure API keys for Last.fm or Spotify, and integrate with existing scrobble clients through a standard-compliant API. The project emphasizes privacy, data ownership, and simplicity, offering manual scrobbling and proxy capabilities.

providers.name: MTN OPS
providers.description: MTN OPS is an American-owned outdoor performance nutrition and lifestyle brand founded in 2014 and headquartered in Fruit Heights, Utah. The company develops, manufactures, and sells energy and nutrition supplements (pre-workout, protein, hydration, creatine, and energy bars) alongside apparel and gear for hunters, tactical professionals, military, and outdoor athletes, running a "Conquer Hunger" program that donates one meal for every order placed. MTN OPS is a direct-to-consumer, internet-first retailer operating on the Shopify platform and is backed by Norwest Venture Partners. It publishes no bespoke developer API; the only machine-readable surfaces on its domain are the Shopify New Customer Accounts OIDC discovery documents and a Shopify-generated agent-commerce llms.txt. This profile was surfaced as a Norwest portfolio lead and enriched from the provider's live public surface.

providers.name: Orionis Biosciences
providers.description: Orionis Biosciences is a privately held biotechnology company headquartered at 950 Winter Street in Waltham, Massachusetts, with a research site in Ghent, Belgium, co-founded by Niko Kley and Jan Tavernier. It develops precision medicines across three modalities — small molecule molecular glues built on its Allo-Glue platform, conditional and cis-targeted cytokines built on its A-Kine platform, and multi-specific cell engagers built on its MCE platform — combining disease biology, immunology, chemistry, protein engineering, computational science and machine learning at genome scale. Its lead A-Kine program ORB-011, an attenuated cis-targeted interferon immunotherapy, has entered Phase 1. Orionis has run multi-year molecular-glue discovery collaborations with Genentech (2023, and a 2025 expansion with $105M upfront and more than $2B in potential milestones) and Novartis (from 2020, expanded in 2026 with $40M upfront and up to $1.4B in milestones). Orionis Biosciences publishes no developer program, no product API and no OpenAPI of its own; the only machine-readable surface on orionisbio.com is the WordPress REST API (wp/v2) that serves the company newsroom, corporate and platform pages, leadership and scientific-team profiles and the media library as anonymously readable JSON, alongside a WordPress Abilities API (wp-abilities/v1) registry that is present but authentication-gated.

providers.name: ottobot-agency
providers.description: OttoBot Agency provides contractor-focused website design and local SEO services. It delivers managed sites, lead routing, and checkout-backed onboarding with transparent pricing and proof‑driven performance metrics. The platform offers a free fit‑check, showcases portfolio examples, and integrates analytics, SEO hygiene, and ongoing support. Plans include website launch, hosting, lead routing, analytics, and monthly support, with higher‑tier options adding recurring SEO and faster cadence.

providers.name: Raindrop.io (bookmarks)
providers.description: Raindrop.io is an all‑in‑one bookmark manager that lets users save, organize, and sync bookmarks across devices and browsers. It offers collections, tags, highlights, AI‑assisted search, and integrations with services like Dropbox, Google Drive, and various browsers. The platform provides a web app, desktop apps, and mobile apps, supporting collaboration, backup, and public sharing of bookmark collections. Raindrop.io emphasizes security with SSL, VPC‑protected architecture, and no ads or trackers.

providers.name: Raphael AI
providers.description: A free, no-signup AI image and video generator (text-to-image, image-to-image, image editing, outpaint, background removal, text-to-video, image-to-video) that aggregates multiple underlying models (Nano Banana, Seedream, GPT Image, Veo, Kling and more). Currently exposes an llms.txt product/marketing index but no public API, MCP server, or agent skills; the provider states a public API is planned for the near future.

providers.name: runlane-run
providers.description: Runlane is a web‑based task tracker designed for solo developers and AI‑assisted coding agents. It lets developers capture ideas, create project backlogs, and delegate work to Claude Code or other agents. The platform offers a free tier with AI credits, supports multiple languages, and provides a clean, minimalist UI for managing many projects in one place.

providers.name: Self
providers.description: Self (Self Financial, Inc.) is a fintech platform that helps people build credit, savings, and access to cash through a small set of consumer financial products. Its Credit Builder Account pairs a small installment loan with a locked savings deposit and reports on-time payments to all three major credit bureaus; the Self Secured Credit Card requires no credit check, and Rent & Bills Reporting and Self Cash round out the lineup. Self serves several million members and is a Techstars portfolio company. It is a consumer-facing product with no public developer API or documentation surface at this time; this profile captures the company's public identity, security posture, and compliance certifications.

providers.name: Seneca
providers.description: Seneca is a microservices toolkit for Node.js that uses a pattern-matching approach to message handling. It provides transport independence, allowing services to communicate over HTTP, TCP, or message queues without changing business logic. Seneca emphasizes simplicity and composability through its plugin-based architecture.

providers.name: Sketch
providers.description: Sketch is a digital design tool for Mac providing a REST API for managing workspaces, documents, libraries, components, prototypes, and share links in the Sketch cloud collaboration environment. The Cloud REST API (api.sketch.cloud/v1) supports Personal Access Token and OAuth 2.0 authentication, enabling workspace member management, document access, and SCIM provisioning for enterprise identity workflows.

providers.name: Strategic Blue
providers.description: Strategic Blue is a UK-headquartered cloud FinOps company founded in 2010 by Dr James Mitchell, a former commodities trader. It specialises in AWS rate optimization through commitment management, delivering Reserved Instance and Savings Plan savings of up to 40-45% without lock-in, forecasting burden, or technical compromise. Strategic Blue treats cloud like a commodity, applying price-risk-management techniques from financial markets to optimize AWS discounts. Its Automate service serves commercial enterprises while Accelerate serves the UK public sector. The company operates on a least-privilege model, accessing only cost and usage metadata and never customer cloud environments. It is ISO 27001, ISO 9001, and ISO 14001 certified, CSA STAR and Cyber Essentials registered, and an AWS Advanced and Google Cloud Premier partner.

providers.name: University of Tartu
providers.description: The University of Tartu is Estonia’s leading research university, founded in 1632. It ranks among the top institutions in the Baltic region, offering a wide range of undergraduate, graduate, and doctoral programs across sciences, humanities, and social sciences. The university emphasizes research, international collaboration, and innovation, contributing significantly to education and knowledge advancement in Europe.

providers.name: US Arctic Research Commission
providers.description: The US Arctic Research Commission is an independent agency that provides recommendations and advice to the President and Congress on Arctic research and policy. The Commission works to promote research that improves our understanding of the Arctic environment and its impact on global climate change, as well as the Arctic's role in national security and economic development. The Commission publishes research goals, working group resources, and policy documents at arctic.gov.

providers.name: USAA
providers.description: USAA (United Services Automobile Association) is a Fortune 100 financial services group offering banking, investing, and insurance products exclusively to people and families who serve, or have served, in the United States military. USAA does not publish a first-party public developer portal or downloadable API specifications. Third-party access to member financial data is delivered through consumer-permissioned open-banking aggregators — Plaid, Mastercard Open Banking (formerly Flinks), and BankSync — using OAuth 2.0 tokenized authorization rather than shared credentials. USAA is an active member and board participant of the Financial Data Exchange (FDX) and helps shape the FDX API standard for secure open finance data sharing in the US.

providers.name: 9am Health
providers.description: 9amHealth (join9am.com) is a US virtual cardiometabolic clinic delivering specialized care for type 2 diabetes, obesity/weight loss, high blood pressure, and high cholesterol entirely from home. Founded in 2021 in San Diego by mySugr co-founders Frank Westermann and Anton Kittelberger, the company pairs at-home lab test kits, asynchronous and synchronous telehealth visits with obesity specialists, pharmacists, dietitians, and behavioral health experts, mail-order pharmacy for prescriptions including GLP-1 receptor agonists, and optional connected devices such as continuous glucose monitors into individualized care plans. It sells direct to individuals and through employers, health plans, and pharmacy benefit managers. 9amHealth is a consumer and enterprise telehealth brand and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation program; this profile captures its public web identity for the API Evangelist network. Backed by Speedinvest.

providers.name: AgentRoam.ai
providers.description: AgentRoam.ai provides travel eSIMs that can be purchased with stablecoins and cryptocurrencies. The platform offers a range of data plans for over 130 countries, allowing users to buy, activate, and manage eSIMs instantly via email QR codes. It targets travelers seeking flexible, cashless connectivity, featuring AI‑ready checkout, crypto payments, and a developer-friendly MCP skill for integration.

providers.name: Arch Network
providers.description: Arch Network is Bitcoin-native financial infrastructure and a computation environment that lets developers build DeFi and capital-markets applications — lending, yield, trading, and structured products — with settlement kept local to Bitcoin. It executes programmable smart contracts (written in Rust) over Bitcoin UTXOs using a specialized virtual machine and threshold-cryptography (FROST/ROAST) validator security, and exposes a JSON-RPC API with first-party TypeScript and Rust SDKs, a CLI, and an AI agent kit. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Multicoin Capital.

providers.name: Back Office
providers.description: Back Office, Inc. operates Finally (finally.com), a Miami-based fintech that provides a unified, AI-powered bookkeeping, accounting, and finance suite for growing small and medium-sized businesses. The platform combines automated bookkeeping and ledger management, accounts payable and bill pay, expense management, corporate cards with built-in controls, invoicing, payment processing, payroll across 150+ countries, and credit monitoring, with AI agents that classify transactions, reconcile accounts, close the books, and prepare audits. Founded in 2018 and trusted by over 3,500 companies, Finally publishes a SOC 2 trust center but does not currently expose a public developer API or developer portal; this profile tracks its identity, web properties, and security posture in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Backflip Ai
providers.description: Backflip AI provides an AI copilot for 3D design, enabling users to create parametric CAD models with full feature trees directly in their favorite CAD packages. The platform aims to lower the steep learning curve of traditional CAD tools by offering a foundation model that generates editable designs, supporting rapid prototyping and engineering workflows for creators and professionals alike.

providers.name: Bariendo Inc.
providers.description: Bariendo Inc. is a venture‑backed technology company identified in the API Evangelist harvest backlog. While the stub entry provides basic corporate metadata, no public website, documentation, or API endpoints have been verified for Bariendo. The company appears to lack an active online presence under its own domain, and attempts to resolve https://bariendo.com redirect to an unrelated site, suggesting the domain is not owned by the company. Consequently, no API specifications, developer portals, or other technical resources are currently available for profiling.

providers.name: Belly
providers.description: Belly provides a customer loyalty and marketing automation platform for small and medium businesses. Founded in 2011, Belly offers a customizable loyalty program that integrates with point-of-sale systems, delivers analytics, and helps businesses engage customers through rewards, campaigns, and personalized experiences. The service is used by retailers, restaurants, and other consumer‑facing brands to build lasting relationships and gather actionable insights.

providers.name: Boompop
providers.description: Boompop is a corporate event management and planning SaaS platform that helps companies organize offsites, conferences, team gatherings, and other business events. The platform pairs AI-powered planning tools that generate briefs, agendas, and logistics with hotel and vendor sourcing (AI-powered RFPs and rate negotiation), guest and RSVP management, itinerary and event websites, budget and expense tracking, and 24/7 AI messaging. Tiers range from a free Starter plan through a per-event Pro plan to Full Service white-glove planning with a dedicated expert. Boompop was named the 7th fastest-growing software company on the 2025 Inc. 5000 list. It is SOC 2 certified and GDPR compliant, and offers passwordless login plus Google and Microsoft single sign-on. Boompop is backed by Wing Venture Capital. Boompop does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or API documentation.

providers.name: BridgeDays
providers.description: BridgeDays is a free online planner that helps users turn a few days of leave into long breaks by finding bridge days around public holidays for over 200 countries. It offers calendar export, customizable vacation preferences, and a widget for travel businesses, all without cost. The service is built as a web application accessible worldwide.

providers.name: CareRev
providers.description: CareRev is a healthcare workforce management and on-demand labor marketplace that connects hospitals and health systems directly with local, credentialed clinical professionals — registered nurses, LPN/LVNs, CNAs, surgical and ER techs, medical assistants, respiratory therapists, phlebotomists and mental health techs — without a traditional staffing agency in the middle. Facilities post open shifts from their existing scheduling and HR systems and vetted clinicians browse, claim and self-schedule them in the CareRev mobile app, while CareRev handles credential verification, compliance and payment. The product line spans the CareRev Marketplace (external on-demand talent), IRP+ (internal resource pool control and float-pool visibility for a health system's own staff) and Smart Rates (dynamic rate modeling to control labor spend). CareRev is certified by The Joint Commission under its Health Care Staffing Services program and serves more than 650 facilities across the United States. Integration with a facility's VMS, scheduling and workforce-management stack (including UKG Dimensions via the UKG Connect Technology Partner Program) is delivered through private, partner-scoped API connections; CareRev publishes no public developer portal, API documentation or machine-readable API contract as of this profiling pass.

providers.name: CarMax
providers.description: CarMax (NYSE: KMX) is the largest retailer of used cars in the United States, operating an omnichannel business that spans brick-and-mortar stores, carmax.com online purchasing, home delivery, financing, appraisals, and trade-ins. CarMax does not publish a public developer portal, but its engineering organization operates an extensive internal API program built around distinct API roles (Data Access Layer, Business Logic Layer, Server-Driven UI, Backend for Frontend). Public-facing APIs documented by the CarMax Engineering Blog include a Store Locations API and a Vehicle Inventory API, and CarMax has publicly discussed a Server-Driven UI API that controls vehicle search filters across web and mobile. Partner and syndication integrations are handled case by case rather than through a self-service portal.

providers.name: Cazoomi
providers.description: Cazoomi provides a Salesforce and NetSuite focused iPaaS called SyncApps, enabling two-way integrations without code between CRM, marketing, and ERP systems. The platform syncs data across Salesforce, NetSuite, Zoho, Mailchimp, HubSpot, Constant Contact and more, automating data flow, reducing manual entry, and improving reporting. It offers a free trial, various pricing plans, and extensive documentation for setup and security.

providers.name: Charles Proxy
providers.description: Charles Proxy is an HTTP proxy and HTTP monitor that enables developers to view all HTTP and SSL/HTTPS traffic between their machine and the Internet, including requests, responses, and HTTP headers. It supports SSL proxying, bandwidth throttling, AJAX debugging, AMF inspection, breakpoints, content rewriting, and traffic recording for API debugging, testing, and development workflows on Windows, macOS, and Linux.

providers.name: Climeworks
providers.description: Climeworks AG is a Swiss carbon dioxide removal company founded in 2009 as an ETH Zurich spin-off by Christoph Gebald and Jan Wurzbacher. It designs, builds and operates direct air capture (DAC) plants that filter CO2 out of ambient air through an adsorption-desorption cycle and then permanently mineralize it underground with storage partners such as Carbfix in Iceland - the Orca and Mammoth facilities. Through Climeworks Solutions it also sells risk-mitigated carbon removal portfolios that blend its own DAC removals with certified third-party suppliers, delivered within seven years of purchase and tracked by corporate buyers in an online customer platform. Climeworks is a supplier of carbon removal rather than a software vendor: it publishes no public developer portal, no API documentation and no machine-readable API contract, and its removals reach programmatic buyers through third-party carbon marketplaces instead.

providers.name: Cloudian
providers.description: Cloudian offers object storage products such as HyperStore, HyperScale AIDP, and HyperIQ for enterprises, government agencies, and service providers. Its solutions provide S3‑compatible, on‑premises and hybrid cloud storage for AI workloads, data lakes, backup, and ransomware protection. The company targets sectors including financial services, healthcare, education, and telecommunications.

providers.name: Code Summary
providers.description: Code Summary provides a platform that synthesizes source code repositories into structured, reviewed knowledge systems. It offers hosted documentation, AI‑agent context, and team workflow tools, enabling developers to generate, edit, and publish living documentation that stays in sync with code changes. Users can start a free trial, explore pricing plans, and integrate the service with their repositories for continuous knowledge updates.

providers.name: Crinkl
providers.description: Crinkl is a verified commerce protocol that turns everyday receipts into cryptographic proofs, allowing users to earn Bitcoin rewards via the Lightning Network. The platform offers a receipt scanning app, a web portal, and developer APIs to integrate verified spend data into financial services, aiming to create a tokenized economy of real-world purchases.

providers.name: CyberGRX
providers.description: CyberGRX is a third-party cyber risk management platform — the Global Risk Exchange (GRX) — that helps organizations assess, monitor, and reduce risk across their vendor and supplier ecosystem. It combines a shared library of standardized vendor risk assessments with analytics for inherent and residual risk, control gaps, and findings. CyberGRX was acquired by ProcessUnity in 2023 and is now delivered as the ProcessUnity Global Risk Exchange. It exposes a versioned REST API (v1, bulk-v1, v2) authenticated with an account API token passed in the Authorization header, including a Bulk API that returns an entire third-party ecosystem — residual risk, control scores, and findings — in a single request, plus first-party Python examples and Go/Splunk connectors.

providers.name: CyberVadis
providers.description: CyberVadis is a Third-Party Cyber Risk Management (TPCRM) platform that runs evidence-based cybersecurity assessments of vendors and suppliers at scale. Its assessment methodology maps to global frameworks and standards including NIST, ISO 27001, DORA, NIS2 and GDPR, producing standardized security ratings, prioritized improvement plans, and continuous monitoring with external attack surface management (EASM). CyberVadis pairs a managed assessment service with a self-service platform offering SSO, unlimited users, and API/GRC integrations (for example ServiceNow) so organizations can embed third-party risk workflows into existing systems. Part of the EcoVadis group and backed by Partech. The platform exposes an enterprise, contract-gated API (a monitored "API Integrations" component on its public status page) but publishes no open developer portal, OpenAPI, or SDK.

providers.name: EIS Group
providers.description: EIS Group (EIS Ltd) is a United States core-systems vendor for insurance, founded in 2008 out of Exigen Insurance Solutions and headquartered in San Francisco, California. EIS sells the EIS Platform and EIS OneSuite — a cloud-native, microservices core suite covering customer management, policy administration, billing, and claims — across group benefits, property and casualty / general, protection, life and annuities, and pet insurance. EIS markets itself as API-first and claims thousands of open REST APIs (1,100 digital APIs announced in 2019, 9,000+ claimed for OneSuite) fronted by the EIS DXP API middleware, but none of that surface is public. There is no self-serve developer portal on eisgroup.com; the documentation host docs.eisgroup.com answers HTTP 401 behind an HTTP Basic realm named "EIS Group Users", so the entire API reference is a customer/partner login wall. No OpenAPI, Swagger, GraphQL, AsyncAPI, or public Postman collection could be retrieved. The only public code EIS ships is two open-source GitHub repositories (kraken-rules, ui-render), which are libraries rather than APIs. ACORD is attested only indirectly — an analyst evaluation hosted on eisgroup.com states the system integrates using "web services, APIs, RESTful APIs, ACORD and certified ACORD" — with no ACORD artifacts, AL3 mappings, or IVANS/agency-download detail published. What EIS does publish is a substantial certification posture — a certified MACH Alliance membership (Microservices, API-first, Cloud-native SaaS, Headless) and a full ISO stack covering 27001, 27701, 22301, 27017, 27018, 27035-1, 12207, 15288, 25000 and ISO/IEC 42001, which EIS announced in June 2025 as the first cloud-native insurance core platform provider to obtain. One first-party package is public, eis-ui-render on npm. This is the canonical United States core-systems posture — the APIs exist and are sold, but they are reachable only through a licensed implementation.

providers.name: Flexport
providers.description: Flexport is a digital freight forwarder and logistics platform that orchestrates global ocean, air, ground, and customs operations for shippers.

providers.name: Forus
providers.description: Forus (formerly Tandem) is an AI-powered healthcare technology company operating a network that connects physicians, pharmacies, payers, and biopharmaceutical companies to accelerate patient access to prescribed medicines. Its platform automates the administrative work between a clinical decision and treatment initiation: insurance prior authorization, AI-generated denial appeals, financial-assistance enrollment, benefit verification, and pharmacy fulfillment routing. Forus is embedded in physician workflows across most U.S. zip codes and is SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA compliant. It offers no public developer API, OpenAPI spec, or SDKs; this profile captures the company's public web, trust, and security surface.

providers.name: Frame Security
providers.description: Frame Security is an AI-powered human risk management and security awareness platform that defends organizations against human-targeted attacks such as phishing, deepfakes, and social engineering. Frame generates personalized security awareness training in 70+ languages, hyper-realistic email, voice, and video phishing and deepfake simulations built from an organization's own context, employee risk scoring with targeted interventions, automated phishing triage of reported suspicious emails, and cross-platform reporting and integrations. The company is backed by Index Ventures and raised a $50M round in 2026.

providers.name: Hackernoon
providers.description: HackerNoon is an independent technology publishing platform and community CMS, founded in 2016 by David Smooke and headquartered in Edwards, Colorado. It operates a free, open library of more than 150,000 practitioner-authored, human-edited technology stories from 35,000+ contributing engineers, covering AI, software engineering, Web3, cybersecurity, startups and science, and serves roughly 3-4 million monthly readers. The company builds and open-sources the publishing software behind the site — the Chowa collaborative editor, the Pixel Icon Library, the HackerNoon pixel font and the Editing Protocol — and monetises through business blogging credits, targeted ads, newsletters and AI content licensing. HackerNoon publishes no public API: probed on 2026-08-22, it serves no OpenAPI, GraphQL, MCP or A2A surface. Its machine-readable surface is a content and AI-access one — an llms.txt, a per-crawler robots.txt policy, RSS feeds and sitemaps — with a "live content feed API" advertised in llms.txt as coming in Q3 2026 and not yet shipped.

providers.name: HealthJoy
providers.description: HealthJoy is a Chicago-based employee-benefits engagement, healthcare navigation, and cost-containment platform founded in 2014, which markets itself as a "Benefits Operating System" (BOS) for employers and benefit consultants. It unifies fragmented health benefits into a single member-facing app combining Joy AI — a 24/7 AI assistant trained on each client's benefits plan — with a licensed human healthcare concierge team, provider search with cost scores and quality ratings, prescription savings, medical bill review, and an intelligent steerage engine that routes members to high-value, fair-priced care. Employers and consultants get a client dashboard reporting engagement, utilization, savings, and ROI. HealthJoy reports 1,800+ client companies and 1.25M+ members. It publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API contract; integrations with benefits-administration and TPA vendors (e.g. Employee Navigator) are delivered as managed eligibility/census data feeds set up by its implementation team rather than as a self-serve API.

providers.name: Hearth
providers.description: Hearth is a business-management platform for residential home-improvement contractors and trades professionals. It bundles customer financing (a marketplace of 18+ lenders with $0 dealer fees), quotes and estimates, digital contracts and e-signature, invoicing and payments, client management, and scheduling, together with Harper, a 24/7 AI receptionist that answers calls, handles follow-ups, and creates social content. Hearth serves 16+ residential contracting verticals including roofing, HVAC, plumbing, landscaping, fencing, and flooring, and is backed by 8vc.

providers.name: HSBC USA
providers.description: HSBC USA is the United States arm of HSBC Holdings plc, operating principally through HSBC Bank USA, N.A., a nationally chartered bank supervised by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC). After exiting mass-market domestic retail banking in 2022 — selling its East Coast branches and national online deposit business to Citizens and its West Coast branches to Cathay Bank — HSBC refocused its US operations on global wholesale, commercial and corporate banking, global banking and markets, and wealth management for internationally connected clients. On the open-finance front, HSBC USA does not publish a US-specific first-party developer program; public API access is provided through HSBC's group-wide corporate and institutional Developer Portal (developer.hsbc.com), whose transaction-banking API products serve US wholesale clients but require registration and login to reach the actual API reference and specifications. There is no publicly downloadable OpenAPI, and consumer-permissioned data access for remaining US accounts is mediated through third-party aggregators rather than a documented first-party consumer data-sharing API.

providers.name: iECURE
providers.description: iECURE is a clinical-stage genetic medicines company developing variant-agnostic, in vivo targeted gene insertion therapies for rare, life-threatening inherited metabolic diseases, with an initial focus on urea cycle disorders and other neurometabolic conditions of the liver. The company takes its name from iecur, the Latin word for liver, and was founded on the translational gene therapy research of James M. Wilson, M.D., Ph.D., advancing its pipeline in partnership with the University of Pennsylvania Gene Therapy Program. Its lead candidate, ECUR-506, pairs a dual-AAV delivery approach with Precision BioSciences' ARCUS nuclease to insert a functional copy of the OTC gene into the genome of infants with neonatal-onset ornithine transcarbamylase deficiency; it is in the OTC-HOPE study and has received FDA Orphan Drug, Rare Pediatric Disease, Fast Track and RMAT designations plus EU orphan designation, with clinical trial clearances in the United States, United Kingdom, Australia and the EU. Discovery-stage programs target citrullinemia type 1 and phenylketonuria. iECURE has raised roughly $115 million across a $50 million Series A in 2021 and a $65 million Series A-1 in 2022 from Versant Ventures, OrbiMed, Novo Holdings, the Qatar Investment Authority, LYFE Capital and Double Point Ventures. iECURE runs no developer program and publishes no product API, developer portal or API documentation. The only machine-readable surface reachable without credentials is the WordPress REST content API behind iecure.com, catalogued here.

providers.name: Invitae
providers.description: Invitae — operated as Labcorp Invitae / Labcorp Genetics since Labcorp acquired select Invitae assets out of the company's 2024 Chapter 11 — is a United States medical genetics and healthcare-technology company providing clinical-grade hereditary and somatic genetic testing across oncology, women's health, cardiology, neurology, pediatrics, and rare disease. Its laboratory is CLIA-certified and CAP-accredited, and it publishes a HIPAA Notice of Privacy Practices and state laboratory licensure. Clinicians order tests and receive results through a web portal with licensed genetic counseling and the Gia digital assistant. Invitae publishes no API: contract discovery across every Invitae host found no developer portal, no OpenAPI, no GraphQL endpoint, no MCP server, no A2A agent card, no FHIR CapabilityStatement, no SMART-on-FHIR configuration, no webhooks, no client SDK and no /.well-known document. api.invitae.com resolves but returns a blanket nginx 403 for every path, and the developer, docs and fhir subdomains do not resolve at all. The company's public GitHub organization is genuine but consists of forks of upstream bioinformatics projects, not first-party specifications or libraries.

providers.name: LaunchNotes
providers.description: LaunchNotes is a release communication platform for sharing changelogs, roadmaps, and deprecation notices. The platform helps product, engineering, and customer-facing teams coordinate launches, communicate releases, and notify customers about deprecations through a structured publishing workflow and an extensible API.

providers.name: LiveScore MCP
providers.description: MCP server for real-time football scores, fixtures, team stats and player data. Connect Claude, Cursor or any AI agent to 1000+ leagues worldwide. Free under fair use; full commercial access $100/month.

providers.name: MassTransit
providers.description: MassTransit is a free, open source distributed application framework for .NET that makes it easy to create applications and services that leverage message-based, loosely-coupled asynchronous communication for higher availability, reliability, and scalability.

providers.name: Matchaful
providers.description: Matchaful is a premium Japanese matcha brand selling single-origin, organically-grown ceremonial matcha from Shizuoka, Japan — ground to order, pesticide-free, and third-party tested under its Farm-to-Whisk program. It sells direct-to-consumer through a Shopify storefront and runs physical cafes, and is a Techstars portfolio company. Matchaful publishes no traditional developer REST API or OpenAPI, but its Shopify storefront exposes a live agent-commerce surface: an /llms.txt and /agents.md agent instruction set, a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP, ucp.dev) merchant profile at /.well-known/ucp, a first-party MCP shopping endpoint at /api/ucp/mcp, and Shopify Customer Account OIDC/OAuth discovery documents served under the store domain.

providers.name: Maxwell Financial
providers.description: Maxwell is an end-to-end mortgage-origination technology and services company serving banks, independent mortgage banks, and credit unions. Its platform spans a customizable borrower Point of Sale, a Lender Hub for loan officers (pipeline, application processing, document validation, underwriting, and pricing), Business Intelligence analytics, and outsourced services including Maxwell Fulfillment (processing, underwriting, closing), Maxwell Diligence (QC and due diligence), and Private Label Origination. The product is a hosted SaaS delivered through login-gated lender and borrower hubs with a public documentation hub; it does not publish an open, versioned developer API.

providers.name: Mentor Graphics
providers.description: Mentor Graphics was a leading electronic design automation (EDA) software vendor whose tools span integrated-circuit design and verification, PCB and electronic-systems design, and manufacturing analysis. Battery Ventures held a position in the company. In 2017 Mentor Graphics was acquired by Siemens and its portfolio now ships as Siemens EDA (part of Siemens Digital Industries Software), including Calibre for physical verification and DFM, the Questa functional verification platform, and the Xpedition / PADS PCB design suites. The mentor.com domain now redirects to the Siemens EDA site. Siemens EDA delivers desktop and cloud-hosted engineering software and managed services; it does not publish a public developer REST API, OpenAPI definition, or self-serve developer portal, so there is no public API surface to enrich for this provider.

providers.name: Minoan
providers.description: Minoan provides a shoppable hospitality platform that enables property hosts and hospitality professionals to furnish and restock their spaces at insider prices. By aggregating premium brands and offering deep discounts, Minoan streamlines procurement, order tracking, and delivery, allowing users to earn commissions on showroom sales. The service is free to use with no membership fees, targeting Airbnb hosts, property managers, interior designers, and hotels seeking cost-effective furnishing solutions.

providers.name: MonkeyLearn
providers.description: Machine learning text analysis platform with REST APIs for sentiment analysis, keyword extraction, topic classification, and custom ML model training on text data. Now part of Medallia's experience management platform.

providers.name: MORE Health
providers.description: MORE Health, Inc. is a global digital health company headquartered in San Mateo, California, with offices in Boston, Houston, New York, Beijing, Shanghai, Chengdu and Guangzhou. It provides expert medical second opinions and cross-border telemedicine through its proprietary, cloud-based Physician Collaboration Platform, which lets a patient's treating physician and an expert specialist jointly review medical history, hospital records, lab results, DICOM imaging, pathology imaging and genetic testing, and co-develop a diagnosis and treatment plan over HIPAA-compliant video conferencing with translation in 129 languages. Product lines include Expert Medical Opinion, MORE Health for Kids, employee benefits for self-insured groups, a Medical Travel Concierge, mental health, Prodigy Fertility and hospital solutions for health systems seeking international patient reach. The company states it serves 6.2 million members across six continents and that its platform is ISO 27001 certified and GDPR- and HIPAA-compliant. MORE Health publishes no public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable specification of any kind; the platform is sold to patients, employers and hospitals as an end-user product.

providers.name: National Hockey League
providers.description: The National Hockey League (NHL) is the premier professional ice hockey league in North America, comprised of 32 franchises across the United States and Canada. The NHL produces the Stanley Cup playoffs and is one of the major North American professional sports leagues. The NHL does not publish an officially documented developer portal; the league operates undocumented JSON endpoints used by its first-party web and mobile apps (api-web.nhle.com) and provides advanced statistics through NHL EDGE. Commercial data feeds are licensed through SMT, Sportradar, and other approved partners.

providers.name: Native Instruments
providers.description: Native Instruments creates software and hardware for music production, DJing, and audio engineering. Their portfolio includes the Komplete suite, Maschine, Traktor, and a range of virtual instruments and effects, serving musicians, producers, and sound designers worldwide.

providers.name: Neutrino AI
providers.description: Neutrino AI provides AI-powered solutions for data analysis, automation, and predictive modeling. The company offers a suite of APIs that enable developers to integrate advanced machine learning capabilities into their applications, including natural language processing, computer vision, and time-series forecasting. Their platform focuses on scalability, security, and ease of use, targeting enterprises and developers seeking to leverage AI without building infrastructure from scratch. Neutrino AI is committed to responsible AI practices and provides comprehensive documentation and support for its services.

providers.name: NTT
providers.description: NTT (Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corporation) is a Tokyo-headquartered global technology and telecommunications group with roughly 340,000 employees and a 150-year history of innovation. The group operates through five business divisions — Consulting & IT Services, Mobile Solutions, Smart Tech, Consumer & Business, and Research & Development — and is anchored by major subsidiaries including NTT DOCOMO (Japan's largest mobile carrier), NTT Communications / NTT DOCOMO BUSINESS (enterprise cloud, network, and platform services), NTT DATA Group (global IT services and systems integration), NTT Ltd. (managed services), and NTT Research. NTT exposes a substantial developer surface through the NTT DOCOMO BUSINESS Developer Portal at developer.ntt.com, which catalogs enterprise APIs across Network (Arcstar Universal One, Flexible InterConnect, Global M2M), Cloud (Smart Data Platform, Enterprise Cloud 2.0), Voice, App (Safety Confirmation, Text & Language Analysis, Speech Recognition), Management (asset visibility, vulnerability), and Core (Authorization, Billing, API Log, Business Process, Service Order, Pay-per-use, Price, Organization, Personal Profile) categories. The group also publishes IoT APIs (Things Cloud) and a docomo Developer support portal at dev.smt.docomo.ne.jp. NTT's primary open source presence is the nttcom GitHub organization, which ships the Enterprise Cloud Python and Go SDKs (eclsdk / eclcloud), the eclcli command-line tool, Terraform providers for Enterprise Cloud 2.0 (terraform-provider- ecl) and Flexible InterConnect (terraform-provider-fic), the ksot network-IaC framework, the pola stateful PCE / PCEP library, the fluvia eBPF/XDP IPFIX exporter, and threatconnectome for SBOM-driven vulnerability management. NTT DATA additionally maintains regional GitHub orgs (NTTDATA, NTTDATA-EMEA, NTTDATA-DACH, NTTDATAInnovation, launchbynttdata, nttdata-oss) covering testing automation, Kubernetes plugins, and LLM observability tooling. NTT also drives the IOWN (Innovative Optical and Wireless Network) initiative, photonics and optical-quantum research, and responsible AI development across its R&D arm.

providers.name: ObjectBox
providers.description: ObjectBox is a high-performance, low-footprint, offline-first on-device database with built-in data synchronization and on-device vector search, designed for mobile, IoT, embedded, and edge computing applications. It is delivered as native language bindings (Java, Kotlin, C/C++, Go, Swift, Flutter/Dart, and Python) rather than a hosted REST API, giving apps ACID-compliant local persistence that works reliably offline and is described as up to 10x faster than SQLite. ObjectBox was the first on-device vector database on the market, targeting Edge AI use cases such as semantic search, recommendations, and retrieval-augmented generation, and offers optional bi-directional Data Sync between devices and the cloud, including a direct connector to MongoDB. Founded in Germany and backed by Techstars.

providers.name: Ohmconnect
providers.description: OhmConnect is a residential demand-response and virtual power plant company that turns household electricity flexibility into grid capacity. It alerts customers during "OhmHours" — windows when grid power is most expensive or carbon-intensive — and pays them cash, gift cards, and prizes for reducing or automating down their usage, then aggregates those reductions and sells them into wholesale energy markets. It serves California utility customers (PG&E, SCE, and SDG&E) and operates as a competitive retail electricity provider in Texas through OhmConnect Energy. OhmConnect runs a login-gated developer portal (developer.ohmconnect.com) secured with AWS Cognito OAuth2, but publishes no public API specification.

providers.name: Postcron
providers.description: Postcron is a social media scheduling and publishing tool that lets marketers, agencies, and small businesses plan, schedule, and automatically publish content across Instagram, Facebook, X (Twitter), LinkedIn, Pinterest, and TikTok from a single dashboard. It supports bulk uploading up to 1,000 posts from Excel or Google Docs, multi-account and team management, automatic image watermarking, a browser extension, and mobile apps for iOS and Android. Originally a Y Combinator / 500 Global-backed startup, Postcron is a consumer- and SMB-facing publishing product; it exposes an internal application API used by its own clients but does not publish a documented public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or a developer portal.

providers.name: Recurse
providers.description: Recurse ML is an AI-powered code review platform built for modern development workflows that lean on AI coding assistants like Cursor, Claude Code, and GitHub Copilot. It understands a whole codebase's context to catch subtle bugs, breaking changes, library/API misuse, and SQL query issues that tests and static analyzers miss, and returns actionable feedback with one-click fixes. Recurse ships as a GitHub App that reviews pull requests, an rml CLI for local and CI/CD review, and ReMCP, a Model Context Protocol server that turns Recurse into a self-healing quality gate AI agents call to fix their own mistakes. It advertises a zero data retention policy and is pursuing SOC 2 compliance.

providers.name: Remarcable
providers.description: Remarcable is an AI-powered procurement and materials-management platform built for MEP (mechanical, electrical, plumbing) trade contractors, distributors, and construction teams. It unifies purchasing, purchase-order and invoice processing, inventory and warehouse visibility, prefabrication workflows, and tool/equipment crib management into a single system, with AI-assisted smart search, document OCR, field note-to-order conversion, and invoice verification. Remarcable connects to accounting and ERP systems (QuickBooks Desktop and Online, Sage 50/100/300, Acumatica, Viewpoint Spectrum/Vista, Foundation, Procore, and more) plus supplier catalogs to automate data entry and reduce errors. The company reports 30,000+ active users and over $900M in monthly material purchases processed, is SOC 2 certified, and raised a $15M Series A led by Insight Partners. Remarcable does not currently publish a public developer API or SDK program; its integration surface is delivered through pre-built ERP and supplier connectors.

providers.name: Rheaply
providers.description: Rheaply is a circular-economy platform for enterprise asset lifecycle management. It gives organizations real-time inventory visibility, an internal reuse marketplace with approval workflows for reallocating surplus furniture, equipment, IT assets, and lab supplies, and sustainable disposition through a network of 3,400+ verified nonprofit and commercial partners. Rheaply helps companies, universities, and governments cut procurement costs, divert waste from landfill, track embodied-carbon savings, and run decommissioning and office move-outs. Backed by Techstars, the company operates a web application at app.rheaply.com. As of this enrichment pass Rheaply publishes no public developer/API program, SDKs, or OpenAPI surface.

providers.name: Rockstar Games
providers.description: Rockstar Games is an American video game publisher headquartered in New York City and a wholly-owned subsidiary of Take-Two Interactive Software (NASDAQ: TTWO). Best known for the Grand Theft Auto and Red Dead Redemption franchises, Rockstar operates online services for GTA Online and Red Dead Online, the Rockstar Games Launcher PC client, and the legacy Rockstar Games Social Club identity / authentication platform. Rockstar does not publish a public developer portal; its HTTP API surface is internal and consumed only by first-party clients (game executables, the Rockstar Games Launcher, and Rockstar's mobile companion apps). The most visible public-facing API is its OpenID Connect / OAuth 2.0 identity provider at signin.rockstargames.com, which exposes standard /connect/authorize, /connect/Token, /connect/introspect, and /.well-known/jwks endpoints. Grand Theft Auto VI is scheduled to launch on November 19, 2026 for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S and will include a "significant online mode" succeeding GTA Online.

providers.name: Second Front Systems
providers.description: Second Front Systems is a public-benefit, venture-backed software company that accelerates government access to emerging technologies for the world's democracies. Its 2F Suite delivers DevSecOps and continuous-accreditation tooling for defense and public-sector software teams: 2F Workshop (integrated security and compliance tooling for accredited development), 2F Game Warden (a fully accredited FedRAMP High and DoD ATO DevSecOps platform that fast-tracks commercial software to classified and unclassified government networks in roughly 90 days), and 2F Frontier (edge deployment to disconnected and denied environments). The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures. It exposes no public developer API; its primary technical surface is the Game Warden platform documentation, a compliance Trust Center, and a broad certification posture (FedRAMP, SOC 2, ISO 27001, CMMC, FIPS 140).

providers.name: Silicon Labs
providers.description: Silicon Labs (Silabs) is a fabless semiconductor company headquartered in Austin, Texas that designs silicon, software, and solutions for a more connected, IoT world. Its portfolio includes wireless connectivity SoCs and modules for Bluetooth, Bluetooth Mesh, Zigbee, Thread, Matter, Z-Wave, Wi-Fi, and proprietary sub-GHz protocols, along with 32-bit microcontrollers, sensors, and timing devices. Developers build on Silicon Labs hardware using the Simplicity Studio IDE, the Simplicity SDK (formerly Gecko SDK), the docs.silabs.com developer documentation, and the Silicon Labs Community. Silicon Labs is a hardware and embedded-software provider rather than a web-API vendor: its public developer surface is embedded C/C++ SDKs, tools, and reference examples on GitHub (github.com/SiliconLabs), not a hosted REST API — so this profile carries identity, developer-portal, and security signals rather than API specifications.

providers.name: Trass Games
providers.description: Trass Games is an a16z-backed independent VR game studio best known for Yeeps - Hide and Seek, a free-to-play social hide-and-seek and building game on Meta Quest, and Gods of Gravity, an arcade space RTS. The studio ships a Yeeps companion app for iOS and Android, sells plush, maker-kit, and apparel merchandise through Shopify storefronts at yeeps.com and godsofgravityvr.com, and runs a community licensing program for creators. Trass Games publishes no first-party developer API, but its storefronts expose agent-ready commerce surfaces including llms.txt, agents.md, a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) merchant profile, and a live storefront MCP endpoint.

providers.name: unremind-me
providers.description: UnRemind is a context‑aware reminder and task engine that delivers notifications only when they make sense for the user. By leveraging location, device, and calendar data, UnRemind waits for the right moment—such as being near a specific place or having free time—before firing a reminder. The platform offers geofenced triggers, AI‑powered assistance, and integrates with existing calendars and task managers, all while remaining ad‑free and privacy‑focused. Currently in private beta, UnRemind aims to enhance productivity without requiring users to abandon their preferred tools.

providers.name: usesignal-dev
providers.description: useSignal offers a suite of free, browser‑based tools that require no registration. Users can download video or audio from URLs, record screen or voice, compress and merge PDF files, generate QR codes, and format or beautify JSON data. All tools run client‑side, ensuring privacy and quick results, and are accessible via a clean web interface at usesignal.dev.

providers.name: Varnish Cache
providers.description: Varnish Cache is a high-performance HTTP accelerator and reverse proxy designed for content-heavy dynamic websites and APIs. It sits in front of web servers and caches HTTP responses to serve repeated requests without hitting the backend, dramatically reducing load and latency. Varnish is configured via VCL (Varnish Configuration Language), a domain-specific language for request/response policy, and managed through a CLI interface (varnishadm) and a set of command-line tools for logging, statistics, and monitoring.

providers.name: Vulcan Technologies
providers.description: Vulcan Technologies builds frontier AI for law and government, headquartered in Austin, Texas and founded in 2025. Its flagship product, Justinian, is a legal AI agent that runs on roughly 157 billion records of American law and policy — including 13+ billion court records, every municipal code, and federal and state statutes, regulations, and active legislative sessions — planning research, drafting work product, and verifying and citing every claim against source. A second product, Trajan, is a government AI concierge for citizen services such as permits, registrations, and license renewals. Vulcan is FedRAMP Ready, runs in AWS GovCloud (US), and serves customers including the Virginia Office of Regulatory Management, the U.S. Department of Education, and South Carolina agencies. The company raised a $10.9M seed round (October 2025) co-led by General Catalyst and Cubit Capital, with participation from Y Combinator, SV Angel, and others. Vulcan is a product/agent company and does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Waldo
providers.description: Waldo is a no-code mobile test automation platform for iOS and Android that lets any team member create, run, and maintain reliable end-to-end tests on a cloud of virtual devices (iOS simulators and Android emulators) with zero device setup. Its Scripting (Core) API exposes a W3C WebDriver and Appium-compatible endpoint at core.waldo.com so engineers can programmatically create sessions on cloud devices and drive native, hybrid, and mobile-web apps, capturing video replays, logs, and network calls. Build upload runs through a Go CLI, GitHub Actions, Bitrise, and a fastlane plugin. Waldo was acquired by Tricentis in July 2023 and is part of the Tricentis mobile testing portfolio.

providers.name: Wideframe
providers.description: Wideframe is a Y Combinator (Winter 2026) startup building an AI agent for video production that automates the work editors do outside the editing timeline. It searches, labels, organizes, and sequences raw footage across local filesystems and cloud storage, indexing large media libraries by meaning and outputting native, editable Adobe Premiere Pro (.prproj) sequences rather than synthetic video. Delivered as an Apple Silicon (M1+) desktop application, it targets brands, agencies, and professional editors who spend far longer preparing footage than actually cutting it. Wideframe currently ships as a consumer/product application with no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company lead.

providers.name: Adaptive
providers.description: Adaptive is an AI agent platform that lets individuals and teams automate workflows, build full applications, and run AI‑powered operations using plain‑language prompts. Users can connect tools like Gmail, Slack, Google Sheets, and Calendar, then describe outcomes to generate and deploy end‑to‑end solutions, from support inbox handling to custom dashboards and content creation.

providers.name: AdRadar
providers.description: Ad Radar (AdRadar MCP) is a remote Model Context Protocol server that lets AI agents search the public Meta Ad Library and TikTok Creative Center Top Ads, classify sales angles, and compute a 0-100 Winning Score.

providers.name: Agency Growth
providers.description: Agency Growth provides AI-powered agents that help marketing agencies automate content creation, client outreach, and revenue growth. Their platform offers tools for generating social media posts, videos, and carousels, as well as AI-driven lead generation and client retention solutions. The service includes a customizable Growth Plan, white‑label AI agents, and integrations with popular tools, aiming to boost agency efficiency and scale without hiring additional staff.

providers.name: Agentic Mermaid
providers.description: Agentic Mermaid turns agent prompts into beautiful, verified Mermaid diagrams with deterministic layout, 16 styles, 20 palettes, and output options including SVG, PNG, ASCII, and Unicode. It offers a library, CLI, and MCP integration for typed edits and layout JSON for coordinate-aware tools.

providers.name: AMI Paris
providers.description: AMI Paris is a French contemporary ready-to-wear fashion house founded in 2011 by Alexandre Mattiussi and headquartered in Paris, known for its "Ami de coeur" heart logo. It sells menswear, womenswear, and accessories direct-to-consumer through amiparis.com, an online store built on Shopify. The store exposes a real agent-commerce surface: a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP, ucp.dev) MCP endpoint advertised in /.well-known/ucp, a published /llms.txt and /agents.md with agent instructions, Shopify Customer Account OIDC/OAuth2 authentication, and read-only product/collection JSON endpoints. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of HongShan (Sequoia China) and profiled by the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Anonyome Labs
providers.description: Anonyome Labs provides identity protection solutions through its MySudo suite, offering tools such as password management, VPN, and secure digital identity for individuals and businesses. The platform enables developers to integrate identity protection via APIs and SDKs, supporting privacy, secure communications, and verifiable credentials across multiple industries.

providers.name: Antares Therapeutics
providers.description: Antares Therapeutics is a Boston- and South San Francisco-based precision medicine company developing small-molecule therapies against validated but previously undruggable targets in cancer and other serious diseases. Spun out of Scorpion Therapeutics following Eli Lilly's March 2025 acquisition of Scorpion, Antares launched in June 2025 with a $177 million Series A co-led by Omega Funds, Atlas Venture, Lightspeed Venture Partners, BVF Partners and Cormorant Asset Management. The company combines medicinal chemistry (proprietary compound libraries and next-generation mass spectrometry to find new chemical pockets), target biology (first-in-class preclinically validated targets and allosteric approaches to clinically validated ones), and predictive sciences (physics-based modeling, machine learning and molecular dynamics) to shorten discovery cycles. Its most advanced program is expected to enter the clinic in 2026, with multiple additional preclinical programs and discovery collaborations with Novartis, AstraZeneca and Pierre Fabre Laboratories. Antares is a private, preclinical-stage biotechnology company and publishes no public product API, developer portal or SDK surface.

providers.name: Arcserve
providers.description: Arcserve is a data protection, backup, and disaster recovery software vendor that helps organizations safeguard business-critical data across cloud, on-premises, and hybrid environments. Its Unified Data Protection (UDP) platform combines backup, replication, high availability, immutable storage, and AI-assisted ransomware detection, alongside SaaS Backup for cloud application data and Replication and High Availability (RHA) for continuous availability. Arcserve sells through MSPs, resellers, and direct channels with a usage-based pricing model. Programmatic surfaces are product-internal (a SOAP API for RHA scenario control and HTTP/PowerShell control of the UDP Console) rather than a public developer API program. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Arizona Solar Cost Calculator
providers.description: Arizona Solar Cost Calculator provides an online tool to estimate solar panel system costs in Arizona, incorporating the 25% state tax credit (capped at $1,000) and current federal credit information. Users input system size and price per watt to see installed cost, net cost after credit, and other details. The site also offers FAQs on tax credits, utility export rates, and battery considerations, serving as a resource for Arizona residents exploring solar installations.

providers.name: Ask10AI
providers.description: Ask10AI provides a cross‑model AI brand mindshare ranking platform that publicly verifies raw model responses. The service offers methodology insights, pricing details, and refusal logs, allowing brands to diagnose and improve their AI visibility across multiple large language models. Users can access rankings, methodology, insights, and pricing in both English and Chinese, with tools to share results via QR codes and social media.

providers.name: August
providers.description: August (August Home) makes Wi-Fi smart locks, keypads, doorbell cameras, and the August Connect bridge for keyless, app-controlled home entry. Founded in San Francisco and originally backed by Bessemer Venture Partners and Uncork Capital, August was acquired by Assa Abloy and its product line is now unified with Yale Home; the two brands share the August mobile app. August does not publish a public device-control API for consumers — third-party integrations rely on community-reverse-engineered endpoints or aggregators such as Seam, and Yale/August partners use the developer.august.com portal. Its august.com storefront (hosted on Shopify) does, however, expose an agent-native commerce surface: a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) merchant profile at /.well-known/ucp and a hosted shopping MCP server at /api/ucp/mcp for buy-for-me agents, alongside Shopify customer-account OpenID Connect discovery.

providers.name: Belden
providers.description: Belden Inc. designs, manufactures, and markets networking, connectivity, and cable products and solutions for industrial automation, smart buildings, and broadcast markets. The company delivers end-to-end signal transmission solutions for mission-critical applications, including industrial Ethernet infrastructure, cybersecurity, and IIoT connectivity. Belden's Hirschmann brand is a leading provider of industrial network switches and management software with CLI, SNMP, and REST API interfaces for network device management.

providers.name: BidDeed.AI
providers.description: BidDeed.AI provides AI‑powered foreclosure and tax deed intelligence across all 67 Florida counties. The platform offers real‑time property record searches, auction forecasts, zoning analysis, and automated alerts for investors and professionals seeking to acquire distressed real‑estate assets.

providers.name: Bookbub
providers.description: BookBub is a book-discovery and ebook-deals platform that connects a membership of over 10 million power readers with limited-time discounted ebooks, new releases, and preorders across major retailers (Kindle, Apple Books, Barnes & Noble, Kobo, Google Play) in the US, UK, Canada, and Australia. For readers it curates personalized daily deal alerts and recommendations; for authors and publishers it operates a partner side offering Featured Deals promotions, BookBub Ads (a self-serve display advertising platform), preorder and new-release alerts, author profiles, and free marketing tools, all managed through the Partner Dashboard. BookBub is backed by Bloomberg Beta. No public developer API is currently published; partner tooling is delivered through the web dashboard rather than a documented API surface.

providers.name: Branddock
providers.description: Branddock provides a platform that captures a brand’s identity once and distributes it to AI systems such as Claude, ChatGPT, and custom tools. It offers AI‑team collaboration, campaign text generation, web‑page creation, and brand‑score checking with explanations, ensuring nothing goes live without approval. The service includes templates, team workflows, and integrations with analytics and payment providers, aiming to keep brand consistency across AI outputs.

providers.name: Butterfly Network
providers.description: Butterfly Network develops handheld, portable ultrasound devices and a cloud‑based imaging platform that enable clinicians to capture, store, and share diagnostic images at the point of care. The company offers a suite of products including the iQ series of probes, AI‑assisted image analysis, and a subscription service for data management and tele‑medicine integration, serving hospitals, clinics, and veterinary practices worldwide.

providers.name: Cellarity
providers.description: Cellarity is a Somerville, Massachusetts based clinical-stage biotechnology company founded in 2017 inside Flagship Labs by Flagship Pioneering, which discovers medicines against the cell as a whole rather than a single molecular target. Its multi-omics, AI-powered platform is trained on tens of millions of single-cell transcriptomes to characterize disease as a shift in cell state and to design small molecules that course-correct that state back toward health. The company has raised roughly $294M across Series A, B and C rounds from Flagship Pioneering, BlackRock, The Baupost Group and Pictet Group, runs an active MASH collaboration with Novo Nordisk, and is advancing CLY-124 — a first-in-class globin-switching oral medicine for sickle cell disease — through a Phase 1 clinical study, alongside myelofibrosis and exploratory hematology programs. Cellarity publishes no product or developer API and runs no developer program; its only anonymously readable machine-readable surface is the WordPress REST API (wp/v2) that serves cellarity.com — news items, the drug-development pipeline, leadership and board profiles, event speakers, case studies, platform videos, media and site search — as JSON. Its scientific software is published as open-source research code in the github.com/Cellarity organization (DrugReflector, DILImap, MolRL), and its technical documentation site at docs.cellarity.com is a private Read the Docs Business instance behind SSO.

providers.name: Champions Oncology
providers.description: Champions Oncology (NASDAQ: CSBR) is a global preclinical and clinical oncology contract research organization (CRO) supporting pharmaceutical and biotech drug development from discovery through the clinic. It maintains a living bank of more than 1,400 patient-derived tumor models and primary hematological models, and offers proprietary in vivo and ex vivo platforms, next-generation sequencing (WES/RNASeq), quantitative and phospho-proteomics, flow cytometry, and other analytical assays. Its Lumin Bioinformatics platform is an integrated, no-code analytics and visualization solution built on precisely curated multi-omics oncology data assembled from over 12,000 cancer patients, exposing gene networks, molecular signatures, target discovery, and AI-driven predictive analytics to researchers. Champions was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Clearview AI
providers.description: Clearview AI is a U.S.-based facial recognition company providing identity verification, investigative search, and biometric matching services primarily to law enforcement, government agencies, and approved financial sector customers. The platform indexes publicly available images and exposes proprietary facial recognition technology through a controlled, customer-vetted developer surface. Public technical documentation of the API is intentionally limited; access is gated, and integrations are scoped through customer agreements with strict use-case, audit, and transparency requirements.

providers.name: Cobli
providers.description: Cobli provides a fleet management platform that combines video telematics, traditional telematics, and mobile applications to give operators real‑time visibility, reduce costs, improve driver safety, and optimize routes. The solution includes video‑based driver monitoring, AI‑driven analytics, fuel and maintenance tracking, and compliance tools, serving logistics companies and vehicle fleets across Brazil and Latin America.

providers.name: Comscore
providers.description: Comscore is a cross-platform media measurement and audience analytics company that provides a trusted, independent currency for planning, transacting, and evaluating media across digital, social, television, streaming/CTV, movies, and programmatic advertising. Its products measure audiences, brands, and consumer behavior for media buyers and sellers, spanning advertising effectiveness, CTV and video measurement, programmatic targeting (Proximic by Comscore), social intelligence, and box-office tracking. Comscore publishes first-party audience- measurement SDKs for Android, iOS/tvOS, and Flutter used to instrument content and apps, and maintains an ISO/IEC 27001-certified trust and security program. It does not currently expose a public self-serve REST API or developer portal.

providers.name: Dataify
providers.description: Dataify provides real‑time web data and AI training data platforms for enterprises and AI developers. It offers live webpage data, multimodal training datasets, and custom services supporting model training and intelligent agent development, empowering AI and business decision‑making.

providers.name: Dgraph
providers.description: Distributed graph database with a native GraphQL API, automatic type enforcement, real-time subscriptions, horizontal scaling, and built-in authorization directives.

providers.name: Director of National Intelligence
providers.description: The Office of the Director of National Intelligence (ODNI) leads intelligence integration across the United States Intelligence Community. The DNI serves as head of the IC, principal intelligence adviser to the President, and oversees and coordinates the foreign and domestic activities of the 18 IC elements. ODNI houses the National Counterterrorism Center, the National Counterintelligence and Security Center, the Office of Economic Security and Emerging Technologies, the Mission Integration and Policy & Capabilities directorates, and the IC Inspector General. ODNI publishes no developer program and no machine-readable specification of its own; its public content — newsroom press releases, remarks, interviews, the Annual Threat Assessment, the annual IC transparency reports, IC directives and NCTC counterterrorism guides — is served from a WordPress site at www.odni.gov whose REST API answers anonymously and is catalogued here.

providers.name: DoubleZero
providers.description: DoubleZero is a decentralized physical infrastructure network (DePIN) that builds and operates a global, permissionless, dedicated-fiber backbone for distributed systems like blockchains — delivering low-latency, high-throughput connectivity where milliseconds matter. Its two-ring architecture pairs edge-node filtering with private high-bandwidth transport, connecting Solana validators, RPCs, and market-data consumers directly to one another. The network is coordinated by onchain smart contracts on Solana and powered by the 2Z SPL token, which meters bandwidth access, rewards fiber and device contributors for measured performance, and drives stake delegation. Operators connect through the first-party `doublezero` CLI and `doublezerod` daemon. Founded by Austin Federa with Malbec Labs; backed by Multicoin Capital and Dragonfly Capital.

providers.name: EarthScope Consortium, Inc.
providers.description: EarthScope Consortium, Inc. is a university consortium dedicated to transforming global geophysical research and education. It operates NSF’s GAGE and SAGE facilities, providing data and tools for seismology, geodesy, and earth science research, and supports collaborative projects across academia and industry.

providers.name: ENDVR
providers.description: ENDVR provides a sell‑through enablement platform that connects brands, retailers, and frontline teams. The network powers real‑time product availability insights, digital education, sales incentives, consumer cashback, and display maintenance tools. Brands can activate stores for free, access pricing calculators, and integrate with mobile apps on iOS and Android. ENDVR aims to boost sell‑through in every door by offering data‑driven insights and collaborative tools for brand and retail teams.

providers.name: Fortuna Health
providers.description: Fortuna Health is a consumer-first Medicaid navigation platform that helps patients and members move through the Medicaid enrollment, recertification, appeals, and coverage-management processes end to end. Founded in 2023 and based in New York City, Fortuna consolidates the fragmented rules of the 50+ state and territory Medicaid programs — each with its own eligibility rules, documentation standards, and renewal timelines — into a single digital interface. The platform lets consumers connect accounts that auto-populate their filings, provides a virtual mailbox for state and health-plan communications, and sends text notifications for urgent, time-sensitive actions. Fortuna partners with health systems and managed care plans as middleware for the roughly $800B Medicaid ecosystem, and is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and Y Combinator.

providers.name: hanria-ai
providers.description: HANRIA provides a decision point for agent commerce, enabling verification of AI agents' identities, mandates, and payment eligibility before actions are taken. It offers a mandate check, runtime enforcement, independent review, and record carrying to ensure accountability and compliance. The platform protects users from unauthorized agent actions and maintains transparent audit trails.

providers.name: Little Spoon
providers.description: Little Spoon is a New York-based direct-to-consumer children's food and nutrition brand, founded in 2017, that delivers fresh, organic, stage-based meals, snacks and infant formula for babies, toddlers and kids on a subscription basis across the United States. Its product architecture maps to feeding stages — Formula, Babyblends purees, Biteables finger foods, Baby Puffs, Baby Cereal, Smoothies and YoGos, Lunchers, Plates and a snack line — with a frozen line sold exclusively through Target. The brand competes on ingredient transparency: a published No-No List of 100+ banned ingredients, EU-level food safety standards, 500+ toxin and contaminant tests, and 2000+ safety tests per batch of Formula. Little Spoon operates no public developer program and publishes no API contract; its storefront is a Next.js front end backed by an undocumented first-party JSON API at api.littlespoon.com. It does publish two machine-readable public artifacts — an llms.txt at the site root and an open-source React design system distributed as fifteen @littlespoon/* npm packages from the little-spoon-dev GitHub org.

providers.name: LottieFiles
providers.description: LottieFiles is the platform and open-source runtime ecosystem for Lottie and dotLottie — a lightweight, JSON-based vector animation format that ships motion on any platform as easily as a static asset. Rather than a hosted HTTP API, LottieFiles' developer surface is a family of first-party, Rust+WASM-powered "dotLottie" players and framework/native components (Web, React, Vue, Svelte, Solid, React Native, iOS, Android, Flutter), plus embeddable web components and design-tool plugins for Adobe After Effects, Figma, Canva, VSCode, Framer and Webflow, letting developers render and control animations client-side.

providers.name: Mesa
providers.description: Mesa is a Boulder, Colorado fintech that provides embedded electronic-invoicing, payments, and invoice-financing (early-payment) infrastructure for B2B supplier networks. Suppliers get paid early via ACH while Mesa automates repayment once the buyer settles. Mesa ships as drop-in embedded UI — a JavaScript SDK (MesaClient) that renders Mesa's onboarding, dashboard, and instant-payout flows in an origin-pinned iframe inside a partner's web app — backed by a Partner REST API for user authentication and invoice retrieval. Auth is via API keys (clientId/clientSecret) exchanged for a short-lived JWT, with optional OIDC (Okta, Azure AD, Google). Backed by Matrix Partners; SOC 2.

providers.name: Moxtra
providers.description: Moxtra (now operating as Moxo) is a contextual collaboration and customer engagement platform that lets businesses embed chat, video meetings, voice calls, file sharing, e-signature, digital workflows, and binder-based collaboration into their own mobile and web applications via SDKs and REST APIs. The Moxtra Developer Portal exposes 200+ REST API endpoints for managing users, binders (workspaces), messages, files, meetings, todos, and notifications.
