Authentication uses OAuth 2.0 access tokens issued against the Moxtra (or self-branded GroupHour) authorization server.

providers.name: Nowlun
providers.description: Nowlun is a digital freight-forwarding platform serving the Middle East and North Africa that lets businesses compare instant ocean-freight quotes from 30+ shipping lines, book FCL and bulk sea shipments, arrange inland trucking to and from ports, track cargo through transit, and handle customs clearance. Beyond its shipper-facing web application, Nowlun operates a live, OAuth-protected Model Context Protocol (MCP) server at https://nowlun.com/mcp, secured with RFC 8414 authorization-server and RFC 9728 protected-resource discovery (Authorization Code + PKCE, "mcp" scope). Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched into the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: OpenWrt
providers.description: OpenWrt is an open-source project that provides a fully writable filesystem for embedded devices, primarily routers. It offers a Linux-based operating system with a package manager, allowing users to customize firmware, add features, and improve performance. The community maintains extensive documentation, guides, and a developer portal, supporting a wide range of hardware platforms. OpenWrt’s mission is to empower users with flexible, secure, and up-to-date networking solutions.

providers.name: Peppyrus
providers.description: Peppyrus provides a free Peppol Access Point, enabling businesses to connect to the global e‑invoicing network. It offers both a test environment (https://api.test.peppyrus.be/v1) and a production API (https://api.peppyrus.be/v1) for seamless integration, along with a customer portal for managing invoices and licenses. The service is certified, developer‑friendly, and includes free and paid plans.

providers.name: Rent Manager
providers.description: Rent Manager is property management software with a REST API (WAPI12) for managing properties, tenants, leases, work orders, accounting, billing, and maintenance workflows for residential and commercial portfolios. The API provides both read and write access to the Rent Manager Online (RMO) database, enabling integration with 200+ PropTech partner solutions.

providers.name: Schrödinger
providers.description: Schrödinger is a New York-headquartered (NASDAQ: SDGR) computational science company that develops a physics-based and AI-driven molecular simulation platform used across drug discovery and materials science. Its flagship desktop modeling environment is Maestro (MS Maestro for materials science), which integrates a deep stack of computational tools — Glide (docking), FEP+ (free energy perturbation), Desmond (molecular dynamics), Jaguar (quantum chemistry), Prime (protein structure prediction), BioLuminate (biologics), LigPrep, QikProp, SiteMap, and WaterMap — together with the Schrödinger-maintained PyMOL visualization system. LiveDesign is the cloud-native enterprise design lab where chemists, biologists, and program teams collaborate on molecules, run computational workflows, and integrate experimental data; it exposes a snap-in API framework for connecting in-house and third-party tooling. The Schrödinger Python API (current release 2026-1) is the primary developer surface, providing programmatic access to molecular structures, Maestro automation, jobcontrol, Glide, FEP+, Desmond, Jaguar, MacroModel, Prime, BioLuminate, and LiveDesign integration (login, export, dataset and column management). Schrödinger also ships KNIME extensions, command-line drivers for every computational product, and maintains a meaningful open-source footprint on GitHub — including PyMOL, maeparser, coordgenlibs, sketcher, gpusimilarity, csmiles, and the fixed-data-table-2 React component. The business has two segments — software licensing to global pharma, biotech, and materials companies, and a co-developed and proprietary drug discovery pipeline. There is no public developer signup or self-serve REST API; access to the platform, Python API, and LiveDesign is gated through commercial licensing and the my.schrodinger.com customer portal.

providers.name: Scopio
providers.description: Scopio (Scopio LLC) is a New York-based global visual-content marketplace and creative-talent platform, founded in 2017 and backed by 500 Global. It connects businesses with a network of 25,000+ vetted photographers and visual artists across 172 countries and a library of more than three million authentic, diverse stock images that can be licensed under standard, extended, and editorial licenses. Brands including Disney, Microsoft, and Meta use Scopio to hire creative talent and source unique imagery, with AI used to sort, tag, title, and feature contributed work. Scopio operates as a consumer- and business-facing web and mobile marketplace (Shopify-hosted storefront plus iOS/Android artist apps); it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Simantic
providers.description: Simantic builds simulated hardware for embedded QA, modernizing embedded firmware development through hardware simulation designed for AI adoption in hardware engineering. Its platform emulates microcontroller (MCU) systems so engineers can inject sensor readings and observe how their firmware reacts over CAN, Ethernet, and BLE, running full firmware test suites in CI (for example GitHub Actions) on every push and pull request without physical boards. A Model Context Protocol (MCP) server lets AI agents step through firmware, inspect peripheral state, and replay scenarios against a simulated MCU, and a CLI drives simulations locally. Simantic offers private, self-hosted deployment so firmware and test data never leave a team's own servers. Founded in 2025, Simantic is a Y Combinator (Fall 2026) company.

providers.name: Sunlight
providers.description: Sunlight is an educational-spending platform that lets organizations fund learning for their people. Administrators create groups, invite registered or unregistered members, allocate a per-user education budget ("sunlight"), and let members place orders for courses, books and subscriptions from providers such as Amazon and Platzi, while an activity feed tracks what members join and buy. Its REST API is built on the JSON:API specification (media type application/vnd.api+json) with Bearer-token authentication, and exposes groups, group membership and invitations, per-user credit/budget transactions, orders, and activities. Sunlight was backed by Seedcamp and Speedinvest.

providers.name: Tabs3
providers.description: Tabs3 provides cloud‑based practice management software for law firms, offering integrated billing, accounting, case management, and reporting tools. Their platform helps legal professionals improve profitability, streamline workflows, and maintain compliance with trust accounting standards, serving thousands of firms worldwide.

providers.name: TriNet Group
providers.description: TriNet Group is a professional employer organization (PEO) providing small and midsize businesses with full-service human resources solutions including payroll processing, employee benefits administration, risk management, compliance, and HR technology. TriNet serves over 16,000 companies and 340,000 worksite employees across verticals including technology, financial services, life sciences, professional services, and nonprofits.

providers.name: Uare.ai
providers.description: Uare.ai is a consumer Individual AI platform founded by LivePerson founder Rob LoCascio that lets people build and own a personal AI trained on their own voice, knowledge, and experiences, organized by its proprietary Human Life Model across seven dimensions (Identity, World, Story, Mindset, Drive, Pattern, Growth). The company raised a $10.3M seed led by Mayfield and Boldstart Ventures in November 2025. Memberships are metered in Credits and include MCP tool integrations that connect an Individual AI to 1000+ applications, with iOS and Android apps alongside the web app at app.uare.ai. Uare.ai publishes no public developer API, API documentation, or SDKs as of July 2026.

providers.name: uni-msg-com
providers.description: uni-msg provides a WhatsApp bulk messaging platform with a unified inbox, AI conversation insights, a full REST API and webhooks, enabling users to connect their own numbers quickly without Meta approval, per‑message fees, or bans, and includes automation workflows, multi‑device support, and built‑in warm‑up controls.

providers.name: Vetcove
providers.description: Vetcove is a free purchasing and procurement platform for veterinary clinics and animal-health organizations that lets a practice shop every distributor and manufacturer at once. It consolidates accounts from suppliers such as Henry Schein, Patterson Vet, MWI, and Midwest Veterinary into one interface where staff compare live pricing and availability, place and track orders, and manage inventory across vendors without changing existing supplier relationships. The service is delivered as a web application and mobile app and is free to veterinary clinics and nonprofits. No public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal was found during enrichment; this profile captures the company identity and a probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: VitePress
providers.description: VitePress is a Vite and Vue powered static site generator widely used for developer documentation. It converts Markdown content into fast, beautiful documentation sites with support for Vue components embedded directly in Markdown pages. VitePress ships a polished default theme with built-in dark mode, mobile-responsive layout, full-text local search, Algolia DocSearch integration, internationalization, and automatic sitemap generation. VitePress is the official documentation framework used by Vue, Vite, Rollup, Pinia, and many CNCF and open source projects.

providers.name: Woebot Health
providers.description: Woebot Health is a clinical mental health company founded in 2017 by Dr. Alison Darcy that delivers an AI-powered, CBT-based conversational agent ("Woebot") for evidence-based mental health support. The company operates an enterprise (B2B) model, partnering with health systems, payers, employers, and providers to embed Woebot into existing care pathways and digital front doors. The Woebot Health Platform offers a partner API library for transmitting aggregated, validated patient-reported outcomes (PHQ-8/PHQ-9, engagement, satisfaction, topic modeling) into EMRs and value-based care workflows. The partner API is gated to enterprise customers — there is no public REST API, OpenAPI specification, or self-serve developer portal.

providers.name: Workit Health
providers.description: Workit Health is a 100% virtual addiction-treatment provider delivering telehealth care for opioid use disorder, alcohol use disorder, and kratom/7-OH dependence via mobile app and video visits with licensed clinicians. Care includes FDA-approved medications such as Suboxone (buprenorphine/naloxone) and naltrexone, recovery groups, and asynchronous care-team messaging, serving members across fourteen US states. Backed by Insight Partners and Lux Capital. Workit Health publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: American Gene Technologies
providers.description: American Gene Technologies International Inc. (AGT) is a privately held gene and cell therapy company founded in 2007 and headquartered in a 27,000 square foot laboratory and office at 9713 Key West Avenue, 5th Floor, Rockville, Maryland, across from the National Cancer Institute campus and the Johns Hopkins Shady Grove campus. AGT operates a proprietary lentiviral gene-delivery platform for the rapid development of cell and gene therapies against infectious disease, cancer and inherited disorders, and runs a Vector Production Facility and a Translational Science Laboratory on site. Its programs include AGT103-T, an autologous cell therapy aimed at a functional cure for HIV, a lentivirus vector-based gene therapy for phenylketonuria (PKU), and a gamma-delta T cell immuno-oncology program (ImmunoTox) targeting hepatocellular carcinoma and other solid tumors. AGT publishes no product API, no developer portal and no API documentation, and operates no developer program. The only machine-readable surface reachable without credentials is the WordPress REST content API behind americangene.com, catalogued in this profile — a read-only content surface exposing the company's gene therapy reference entries, patent portfolio, news releases, press coverage, blog, newsletters, advisory board, milestones, media library and video series as structured JSON.

providers.name: Apache Avro
providers.description: Apache Avro is a data serialization system that provides rich data structures, a compact binary format, and container files for storing persistent data. Avro uses JSON for defining data types and protocols, and serializes data in a compact binary format.

providers.name: Assured Allies
providers.description: Assured Allies is an insurtech company founded in 2018 by Roee Nahir and Afik Gal, headquartered in Boston with an office in Tel Aviv, that partners with long-term care insurance carriers to rebuild the LTC category around successful aging. Its platform combines data science, predictive analytics and human coaching across four solution lines — NeverStop Wellness (an integrated wellness and rewards program the company reports reduces claims by roughly 7%), Digital Underwriting (which it says closes policies in about 40 minutes), Product Development for carrier LTCI portfolios, and Distribution Excellence agent enablement. Two consumer-facing programs sit on top of the platform: NeverStop (neverstop.com) for the wellness-motivated 55+ market and AgeAssured (assured.care) for policyholders aging at home. The company raised a $42.5M Series B in 2023 co-led by FinTLV Ventures and Harel Insurance, reports $78M+ raised in total, and works with carriers and programs including EquiTrust and CalPERS Long-Term Care. As of this profile Assured Allies publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API contract; its member application backend is private and authenticated.

providers.name: Astrix Security
providers.description: Astrix Security is a cybersecurity company providing identity security for AI agents and non-human identities (NHIs) — the API keys, OAuth apps, service accounts, SSH keys, and MCP servers that fall outside traditional human IAM. Its platform lets enterprises discover a real-time inventory of every AI agent and NHI with business and risk context, secure them by remediating excessive privileges, misconfigurations, and abnormal or malicious activity, and deploy agentic AI safely via an Agent Control Plane that provisions short-lived, tightly scoped credentials. Founded by Alon Jackson and Idan Gour and headquartered in Boston, Astrix is backed by CRV, Bessemer Venture Partners, Menlo Ventures, F2, and Anthropic. The company was acquired by Cisco and ended standalone sales of new licenses effective June 30, 2026.

providers.name: Biomodal
providers.description: Biomodal (formerly Cambridge Epigenetix) is a Cambridge, UK genomics and epigenetics company whose duet multiomics solutions capture genetic and epigenetic information from a single low-input DNA sample in one experiment, giving researchers access to the six-base genome (the four canonical bases plus 5-methylcytosine and 5-hydroxymethylcytosine). Its products include the duet multiomics solution evoC and duet +modC library-prep assays, the biomodal CLI and duet post-sequencing pipeline (alignment, methylation quantification, and variant calling), and the modality XPLR analysis software. The technology is applied to cancer and liquid-biopsy research, neurodegenerative disease, aging, precision medicine, and non-invasive prenatal testing. Biomodal is a portfolio company of GV (Google Ventures) and was added to the API Evangelist network as a life-sciences provider profile.

providers.name: Blobr
providers.description: Blobr is an AI-powered Google Ads management platform that deploys specialized AI agents to automate campaign optimization, keyword management, ad copy improvement, and budget allocation. Originally founded as an API monetization and portal platform, Blobr has evolved into an AI teammate for Google Ads that helps agencies and advertisers automate the bulk of daily campaign management tasks. The platform features 50+ specialized AI agents that analyze accounts, generate recommendations, and implement approved changes directly to Google Ads.

providers.name: BracketView
providers.description: BracketView provides a privacy‑first online JSON workspace that lets users view, format, validate, query (JSONPath + jq), diff, and generate schemas directly in the browser. It offers multiple visualizations such as tree, graph, node cards, and nested tables, supporting nine UI languages. Optional AI‑assisted fixes, encrypted snapshots, and a webhook tester are available as paid features. The service also includes a downloadable Windows and Linux desktop app for offline use, ensuring data never leaves the user's device unless explicitly chosen.

providers.name: Braintrustbac9
providers.description: Braintrust is an AI infrastructure company offering a talent marketplace, AI interview software (AIR), and workflow automation (Nexus). It connects enterprises with 2M+ vetted professionals, provides AI‑powered recruiting, and builds AI tools for enterprise work. Founded in 2018, Braintrust delivers transparent pricing and compliance solutions for modern talent acquisition.

providers.name: Cape Analytics
providers.description: Cape Analytics (now part of Moody's) is a geospatial property intelligence provider that applies computer vision and machine learning to high-resolution aerial and satellite imagery, property records, and other novel data sources to produce inspection-quality condition and characteristic data for over 100 million residential and commercial structures across the United States and Canada. Its insights — roof condition and material, swimming pools, solar panels, accessory structures, tree overhang, wildfire and wind exposure, distance to hazards, and a proprietary Liquidity Score — are delivered to insurance underwriters, lenders, and real estate investors in under two seconds via API, batch/bulk files, an Automated Property Condition Report (aPCR), and a customer web portal, as well as through third-party platforms such as Guidewire and Duck Creek. Cape does not publish a public, self-service developer portal or open API specification; API access is provisioned to customers and partners through a gated onboarding flow.

providers.name: Care Leader Guide
providers.description: Care Leader Guide is a platform that provides curated guides and resources for individuals leading care work. It focuses on the challenges faced by care leaders, offering practical advice, best practices, and community support to help them navigate their roles effectively. The site includes articles, guides, and tools aimed at improving care leadership and fostering better outcomes for those they serve.

providers.name: CASE
providers.description: CASE (Clearance Adjudication Search Engine) provides a searchable knowledge base of Department of Homeland Security (DOHA) security clearance decisions dating back to 1996. Users can query outcomes, view statistics, and access citations for over 30,000 public clearance records. The platform offers descriptive analysis without predictions, supporting researchers, employers, and individuals seeking transparent clearance information.

providers.name: Centralize
providers.description: Centralize provides a relationship workspace for enterprise deal teams that builds account maps, org charts, and stakeholder maps from a company’s CRM, email, and call data. The platform offers AI‑driven insights and outreach recommendations, integrates with tools such as Salesforce, Slack, Gmail, and Gong, and includes security features like SOC 2 Type 2 compliance, SSO, and encryption. It is positioned for sales, customer success, and leadership teams to coordinate account collaboration and drive deal progress.

providers.name: CUTISS
providers.description: CUTISS AG is a Swiss late-stage clinical TechBio company headquartered at the Bio-Technopark in Schlieren, Zurich, founded in 2017 as a spin-off of the Tissue Biology Research Unit (TBRU) at the University of Zurich and the University Children's Hospital Zurich, and accelerated through Wyss Zurich. Its lead product, denovoSkin, is a first-in-class bioengineered, personalized dermo-epidermal skin graft grown from a small biopsy of a patient's own skin to treat large and deep skin defects in children and adults; it holds Orphan Drug Designation for burns from Swissmedic, the EMA and the FDA and is in late-stage clinical development. With CSEM the company built denovoCast, described as the world's first machine for automated production of personalized human skin tissue, funded in part by Innosuisse and EU Horizon 2020. CUTISS has raised roughly CHF 50 million and employs around 50 people. It is a therapeutics manufacturer, not a software vendor: it publishes no product API, no developer portal, no SDKs and no pricing. The only machine-readable API on its public host is the WordPress REST API behind cutiss.swiss, which serves the newsroom, blog, corporate pages, team directory, teams taxonomy and media library as JSON, read-only without credentials.

providers.name: Dalux
providers.description: Dalux, founded in 2005 in Copenhagen, Denmark, provides digital construction software including BIM viewers, field management, and asset management tools. It aims to make the construction industry more efficient and sustainable through digitalization, offering solutions for design, on‑site management, and facility operations, serving a global customer base across commercial, residential, healthcare, and infrastructure sectors.

providers.name: Dinilu Promotional & Printed Products
providers.description: Dinilu Promotional & Printed Products offers online quotations for promotional items, advertising specialties, branded merchandise, printed matter, disposables, logo gifts and customised products from China. They specialise in delivery across Europe with good prices, quality control, transport and delivery to your door, acting as factory, wholesaler and shipping company in one.

providers.name: diningco-co-uk
providers.description: DiningCo is a UK‑based online restaurant reservation and table‑booking platform that connects diners with a wide range of restaurants across the United Kingdom. The service allows users to search for venues, view menus, read reviews, and secure reservations in real time. DiningCo also offers restaurant partners tools to manage bookings, optimize seating, and integrate with point‑of‑sale systems. Founded to simplify the dining experience, the company provides a modern API for developers to access reservation data, restaurant listings, and customer insights, supporting both web and mobile applications.

providers.name: EasyKanban
providers.description: EasyKanban provides a free online kanban board with unlimited cards for personal work, freelancers, and small teams. It offers a calm, minimalist interface, real‑time collaboration, drag‑and‑drop, dark mode, and AI‑enhanced features in its Pro plan. The service is web‑based, requires no credit card to start, and aims to be a simple Trello alternative for focused productivity.

providers.name: EverTrue
providers.description: EverTrue is a donor experience and fundraising platform for nonprofit, higher-education, and healthcare advancement teams, serving more than 13,000 teams. Its product suite spans AI-driven prospect identification and research (Signal, DonorSearch), donor outreach and stewardship (ThankView personalized video, Pledgemine direct mail), and endowment reporting (Balance, Impact, ODDER). EverTrue integrates with advancement CRMs such as Blackbaud Raiser's Edge NXT via an automated data sync. EverTrue operates as a closed B2B SaaS: it runs internal REST APIs behind its iOS, Android, and single-page web applications but does not publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, or self-serve API program. Backed by Bain Capital Ventures and Techstars.

providers.name: Fairplay
providers.description: Fairplay is a Mexican fintech offering flexible, collateral-free business financing for e-commerce sellers, marketplaces, retailers, and wholesalers. Its products include revolving credit lines (MXN 2-30 million), invoice advances/factoring, and working-capital financing, underwritten from a company's sales and analytics data with offers issued in as little as 48 hours through a 100% digital process. Fairplay operates as a Sociedad Financiera de Objeto Multiple, Entidad No Regulada (SOFOM E.N.R.) under Mexican CNBV and CONDUSEF supervision and is ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certified for information security. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of QED Investors and Speedinvest. Fairplay serves financing and account data to customers through a private insights dashboard; no public developer API is currently published.

providers.name: Ferguson
providers.description: Ferguson is a Fortune 500 distributor of plumbing supplies, HVAC products, pipe, valves and fittings, waterworks, and building supplies serving professional contractors, residential homeowners, and commercial customers across the United States. Ferguson runs an Enterprise API program on Google Apigee, published through the Ferguson Developer Portal, that lets approved partners and software providers pull product availability and cost data and submit purchase orders electronically. Access is granted only to organizations that complete Ferguson's partner review and approval process, and the API catalog and its Swagger documentation are not readable without credentials.

providers.name: Gannett
providers.description: Gannett Co., Inc. is a diversified media and digital marketing solutions company and the publisher of USA TODAY and a network of more than 200 local daily newspapers across the United States. It now presents its corporate identity as USA TODAY Co. — www.gannett.com 301-redirects its corporate pages to www.usatodayco.com, and investors.gannett.com resolves to investors.usatodayco.com. Through the USA TODAY Network and LocaliQ, its digital marketing services arm for small and medium-sized businesses, Gannett delivers news, audience and advertising technology. Gannett publishes no developer portal, no API reference and no machine-readable API contract: developer.gannett.com and developer.usatoday.com both redirect to consumer sites, and no OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, GraphQL, MCP or A2A surface is served on any of its hosts. What it does publish machine-readably is a publisher-side control surface — an RFC 9116 security.txt, a Global Privacy Control signal, an llms.txt on localiq.com, and a 958-line robots.txt that denies the major AI crawlers site-wide while re-allowing a commercial subset of shopping, money and sponsor-content paths.

providers.name: GovWell
providers.description: GovWell is a cloud-based AI operating system for modern local and county government, used by municipal and county agencies across 40+ U.S. states to digitize and automate civic services. The platform replaces paper and legacy systems with online workflows for permitting, licensing, planning and zoning, and code enforcement, and layers on AI capabilities including AutoCheck, which automatically reviews applications for errors and missing documentation before submission, and a 24/7 AI Community Assistant that answers resident questions. GovWell serves both government staff, who manage plan reviews, inspections, applications, payments, and renewals, and applicants and contractors, who submit and track requests through a self-service jurisdiction portal. The company is backed by Insight Partners and is an Esri partner. GovWell does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or a .well-known discovery surface; this profile captures its identity and public trust/security posture.

providers.name: Howden Group
providers.description: Howden Group Holdings is a London-headquartered, employee-owned international insurance intermediary founded in 1994, operating across retail insurance broking (Howden), specialty and reinsurance broking (Howden Re / Howden Specialty), and managing general agency underwriting (DUAL). Its home market is the United Kingdom and the Lloyd's of London subscription market, with lines of business spanning property and casualty, specialty, credit and political risk, marine, cyber, employee benefits, and reinsurance. Howden's API posture is partner-gated and honestly recorded as such: no developer subdomain resolves (developer/developers/docs/api.howdengroup.com all fail DNS) and no /developers, /api or /partners path exists on howdengroup.com. What Howden does operate is real but private broker-to-carrier integration — HowdenCAP's Tepfin X structured credit placement application holds direct bilateral APIs with insurers (Allianz Trade, AXA XL, Mosaic), and in July 2025 Howden went live with ACORD GRLC digital accounting and invoicing standards over ACORD Solutions Group's ADEPT gateway with retail insurer partner Hiscox. None of that surface is self-serve, documented publicly, or accompanied by a downloadable OpenAPI definition. The only public web surfaces are marketing pages and login walls. Howden does publish two real machine-readable web artifacts — an RFC 9116 security.txt at www.howdengroup.com naming security@howdengrp.com, and an llms.txt overview blurb mirrored across the Howden Re and DUAL brands — plus a robots.txt Content-Signal directive permitting AI training, search and AI input use of its public content.

providers.name: Joy
providers.description: Joy offers a subscription-based parenting club that provides expert‑backed toolkits, 24/7 human support, personalized insights, and 1:1 video consultations for parents in the United States. Members can track daily baby activities, access resources on feeding, sleep, behavior, and receive exclusive discounts on family products.

providers.name: Lendio
providers.description: Lendio is a small business lending marketplace that connects businesses with funding through a network of 75+ lenders. The platform offers a REST API for submitting loan applications, checking eligibility, connecting businesses with lenders, and managing loan products. Lendio provides Embedded Financing for service providers to integrate loan marketplace functionality, Intelligent Lending software for banks and lenders, and a Loan Performance Tracking API for high-volume lenders submitting bulk data records.

providers.name: LevelUp
providers.description: LevelUp (SCVNGR, Inc. d/b/a LevelUp) was a Boston-based mobile payments and customer-loyalty platform whose REST API let point-of-sale systems and e-commerce applications accept LevelUp payments, issue QR-code order tokens, manage merchant locations, and run merchant-funded loyalty and credit campaigns. The platform shipped first-party C#, Ruby and Java SDKs plus packaged point-of-sale adapters for Aloha, Micros 3700, Dinerware and Agilysys InfoGenesis. LevelUp was acquired by Grubhub in 2018 and the platform API is now RETIRED: the developer portal, API reference, sandbox and production hosts have all been decommissioned and thelevelup.com redirects to grubhub.com. This profile is a historical record reconstructed from LevelUp's surviving first-party open-source SDKs and package feeds.

providers.name: Literati
providers.description: Literati is an Austin, Texas based children's book company founded by Jessica Ewing that operates three connected consumer and school businesses: personalized monthly Book Clubs for Kids that ship five curated books matched to a child's reading level and interests starting at $11.95 per month, Clubs for Classrooms for teachers, and a school book fair business (in-person and online) run through the OpenBook coordinator dashboard at openbook.literati.com and the year-round Literati Store, which returns a share of proceeds to participating schools. The company draws on 150+ publishers, combines expert curation with data science to personalize book selection, and reports more than one million books donated to Title I schools and underserved communities since 2019. Literati publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or SDKs; its public technical surface is limited to consumer and school-facing web applications, iOS and Android apps, and an RFC 9116 security.txt vulnerability-reporting contact.

providers.name: LiveAction
providers.description: LiveAction is a network observability and intelligence platform that provides visibility and monitoring across physical, virtual, cloud, and SD-WAN infrastructure. Its product family includes LiveNX (network performance monitoring using flow, API, SNMP, and cloud telemetry), LiveWire (network forensics and packet capture), LiveSP (monitoring for service providers), and Omnipeek (protocol analyzer), alongside AI-driven operations offerings. LiveAction's products expose product-embedded REST APIs authenticated with API tokens for automation and integration; there is no public hosted developer API or OpenAPI specification, as the APIs run on customer-operated deployments and the reference is served in-product. LiveAction is part of BlueCat Networks and a portfolio company of Insight Partners.

providers.name: Lovys
providers.description: Lovys is a European digital neo-insurance provider offering flexible, subscription-based cover for home (habitation), smartphone, and pet insurance, designed to be managed entirely online and adjusted month to month. Beyond its direct-to-consumer product, Lovys operates a Partner API (the "Lovys Partner API") that lets resellers and platforms embed insurance into their own experiences: creating and managing real-time quotes, retrieving plans, pricing and coverage options, capturing and managing customer data, enabling policy purchase and activation, and handling the policy lifecycle, updates, and renewals. The Partner API is fronted by Azure API Management and authenticated with OAuth2 via Microsoft Entra ID / Azure Active Directory B2C. The public developer portal (docs.lovys.com) documents getting-started, onboarding, quoting, purchase, and end-to-end partner guides alongside an API reference covering account, customer, quote, basket, orders, payments, policies, and reference-data resources.

providers.name: Mimic
providers.description: Mimic is an enterprise cybersecurity company building ransomware and AI-threat defense based on "Known-Good Enforcement" at the kernel level. Its SaaS platform models a system's authorized state and blocks unauthorized modifications, detecting ransomware in fractions of a second to deflect attacks before they can encrypt data or damage infrastructure, and providing rapid-recovery technology that restores in seconds-to-minutes rather than days. Product lines include Ransomware Defense, AI Shield (Guard/Patch/Trace) and Agentic AI Governance. Founded in 2023 and headquartered in Palo Alto, California, Mimic raised a $27M seed and a $50M Series A led by GV (Google Ventures) and Menlo Ventures, with Ballistic Ventures, Team8, Wing Venture Capital and Shield Capital participating; former Mandiant CEO Kevin Mandia joined its board. The platform is enterprise/government-facing (sold via demo, no public developer API) and is aligned with GDPR, SOC 1 & 2, IL4/IL5 and holds FedRAMP Ready status. Added to the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio lead.

providers.name: My AI
providers.description: My AI Inc. is the company behind Me Protocol, a universal open rewards infrastructure that lets brands issue, redeem, and swap loyalty rewards across a decentralized cross-brand ecosystem through a single API integration. Founded in 2022 by Robert Wesley and Paul Oamen and backed by 500 Global, the protocol combines an EVM smart-contract layer (Sepolia, Hedera, Base, Polygon), a hosted Platform-as-a-Service REST API, and embeddable SDKs — an AI agent chatbot widget plus drop-in React and inline payment components — so merchants can plug frictionless open rewards into web and agent-driven storefronts for the emerging AI Agent Economy.

providers.name: mypinpal-com
providers.description: Pinpal, built by Portfoliobox Stockholm AB, offers simple AI‑enabled note‑taking, project, and to‑do apps hosted in the EU. Founded in 2012 in Stockholm, the company serves about 30,000 paying customers, emphasizing privacy, plain‑Markdown data, and no AI training on user content.

providers.name: Nameko
providers.description: Nameko is a microservices framework for Python that provides tools for building, testing, and running services. It supports RPC over AMQP, HTTP endpoints, WebSocket connections, and timer-based workers, with built-in dependency injection and a testing framework that allows services to be tested in isolation or integration.

providers.name: Origin Financial
providers.description: Origin (Blend Financial Inc. DBA Origin Financial) is a personal finance platform built around an SEC-regulated AI financial advisor, combining spending tracking, budgeting, investing, tax filing, estate planning, and couples money management in one app, and offering employers a financial wellness benefit. Account connections run through partners including Plaid, MX, and Mastercard. Origin is a consumer and employer product with no public developer API surface today.

providers.name: OT Fabric
providers.description: OT Fabric (otfabric.io) builds open-source, MIT-licensed, pure-Go protocol libraries, command-line tools and Dockerized interoperability test suites for industrial operational technology (OT): Modbus, OPC UA, BACnet/IP, IEC 60870-5-104, IEC 61850, Siemens S7, OpenADR, OCPP, DNP3, IEEE 2030.5, EtherNet/IP, PROFINET, CANopen on CAN bus and KNX, plus SunSpec Modbus and IEC 61850 information models and Sparkplug B over MQTT. Its stated goal is 'unified data for industrial operations': breaking down OT data silos so industrial data is easy to discover, access and use across systems, sites and teams. It publishes libraries and CLIs rather than a hosted web API.

providers.name: Own (OwnBackup)
providers.description: Own (formerly OwnBackup, now Own from Salesforce) is a SaaS data protection platform that provides backup, recovery, archiving, sandbox seeding, and data security and compliance for cloud applications including Salesforce, Microsoft Dynamics 365, and ServiceNow. Founded in 2015 and acquired by Salesforce in 2024, Own helps organizations protect and manage the data held in their business-critical SaaS systems against loss, corruption, and compliance risk. Own is delivered as a managed product rather than a public developer API platform: it operates a public system status page and a trust center listing its security certifications (SOC 2, ISO 27001/27701, FedRAMP, HDS, GDPR, HIPAA/HITECH) and a published vulnerability disclosure policy, but does not currently publish an open, self-serve REST/OpenAPI developer surface.

providers.name: Packback
providers.description: Packback is an AI-powered instructional platform for higher education and K-12 that delivers real-time, formative feedback on student discussion and writing. Its products - Questions/Discussions, Writing and Deep Dives, and Originality - embed into a school's LMS through the IMS Global LTI standard rather than a public REST API.

providers.name: pagepenny-com
providers.description: PagePenny provides a low‑cost PDF and image generation API that renders templates into PDFs, PNGs, and social images for a penny per render. Users can send JSON data with a chosen template to receive invoices, receipts, reports, or custom graphics instantly via a simple HTTP POST. The service offers a free tier with 100 renders per month and paid usage at $0.01 per render. Documentation, pricing, and a live demo are available on the site, and an API key can be obtained after login.

providers.name: Parsyl
providers.description: Parsyl Inc. is a Denver, Colorado based technology-enabled cargo insurance company for perishable and temperature-sensitive supply chains, with an office in London and underwriting capacity placed at Lloyd's of London. It pairs IoT temperature and condition sensors with a data platform that turns shipment telemetry into risk insight, and sells that insight back as connected marine cargo insurance products — ColdCover cargo insurance, stock throughput, excess stock, legal liability, a small-business program, and the cargo market's first parametric spoilage policy. Customers include food, seafood, pharmaceutical, vaccine and semiconductor shippers, plus global health programs such as Africa CDC and PFSCM. Parsyl runs a Data Partner Program that ingests telemetry from third-party monitoring vendors (Berlinger, Copeland, Roambee, Sensitech, Tive) and offers custom API integration so customers can pull their own systems' data into the Parsyl Platform. The API surface is real but is documented only to authenticated customers at docs.parsyl.com; no OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, MCP server or agent card is published publicly.

providers.name: Paycom
providers.description: Paycom provides cloud‑based human capital management (HCM) software, offering payroll, talent acquisition, time tracking, and HR management solutions for businesses of all sizes. Their platform integrates payroll processing, employee self‑service, benefits administration, and compliance tools, delivering a unified experience for employers and employees. Paycom emphasizes automation, real‑time data, and a user‑friendly interface to streamline workforce management and reduce administrative overhead.

providers.name: Polaris Industries
providers.description: Polaris Inc. (NYSE: PII), long known as Polaris Industries, is a Minnesota-based global manufacturer of powersports and off-road vehicles. Its portfolio spans RANGER, RZR, Polaris XPEDITION and GENERAL side-by-sides, Sportsman ATVs, snowmobiles, Slingshot moto-roadsters, military and commercial off-road vehicles, Aixam quadricycles, Goupil electric utility vehicles, and Bennington and Godfrey pontoon and deck boats. Its connected-vehicle platform, RIDE COMMAND, ships in-dash navigation and vehicle telematics to riders as an end-user product. Polaris completed the separation of Indian Motorcycle and the sale of a majority stake to Carolwood LP on 2 February 2026. Polaris publishes no public API, developer portal or machine-readable specification; the only credentialed integration surface a member of the public can find is the dealer portal at polarisportal.com, which authenticates against an Auth0 tenant.

providers.name: Polotno
providers.description: Polotno provides a powerful, open-source canvas library for building design tools and visual editors directly in the browser. It offers a flexible, component‑based architecture, extensive customization options, and a rich set of pre‑built UI elements, enabling developers to create sophisticated graphic applications without reinventing core drawing functionality. The library is actively maintained, supports modern web standards, and integrates seamlessly with React, Vue, and other frameworks, making it a versatile choice for both startups and enterprise projects seeking high‑performance, client‑side design capabilities.

providers.name: PremiaLab
providers.description: PremiaLab is a portfolio performance and risk analytics platform for institutional investors — asset owners, asset managers, and consultants who collectively manage roughly $20 trillion in assets. Its platform provides a quantitative strategy database of more than 7,000 single- and multi-asset systematic (QIS) strategies from 18 leading investment banks, position-based risk analytics (stress tests, sensitivities and VaR across asset classes), the proprietary Premialab Pure Factors model for decomposing market risk premia, independent price verification with daily index-level reconciliation, and standardized QIS Index futures offered in partnership with Eurex. PremiaLab exposes a client-facing REST API at api.premialab.com that is protected by an OAuth2 / OpenID Connect authorization server; API access is provisioned for institutional clients rather than through self-service developer signup. This profile was surfaced as a Balderton Capital portfolio company and enriched from PremiaLab's public web and authentication surface.

providers.name: Scott Foresman
providers.description: Scott Foresman was a leading elementary educational publisher for PreK through Grade 6 across all subject areas. Founded in 1896, the company became part of Pearson PLC in 1996. In 2019, Pearson spun off its U.S.-based K-12 courseware business, which was rebranded as Savvas Learning Company in 2020. Scott Foresman's iconic educational content — including the "Dick and Jane" reading series and basal reading programs — now lives under the Savvas Learning brand. No public developer API is currently available.

providers.name: Segura
providers.description: Segura provides a comprehensive Identity Security Platform that secures privileged access, endpoint privilege management, multi‑cloud identity security, DevOps secrets management, certificate lifecycle, and remote access. It serves enterprises across industries, offering audit, compliance, and threat detection capabilities, with a focus on reducing risk and simplifying access governance.

providers.name: SendJim
providers.description: SendJim provides a direct mail marketing platform that helps home service businesses automate their outreach. It offers features like campaign playbooks, predictive targeting, and integrations with popular tools such as Jobber, ServiceMinder, and Housecall Pro. Users can schedule webinars, access case studies, and explore pricing options, all aimed at simplifying marketing and increasing revenue for service‑based companies.

providers.name: Singpass
providers.description: Singpass is Singapore’s national digital identity platform that enables residents to securely access government services, sign documents, and share verified personal data with businesses. It provides authentication, MyInfo data pre-fill, and digital signing capabilities, supporting over 2,700 services across more than 800 agencies, and aims to simplify and secure everyday transactions for citizens and residents.

providers.name: Software
providers.description: Software is a technology company focusing on delivering software solutions across various industries. The company provides a suite of APIs for integration, data access, and automation, targeting developers and enterprise customers. Detailed information about its offerings, platform capabilities, and developer resources can be found through its official channels.

providers.name: Software Mansion
providers.description: Software Mansion is a custom software development and consultancy firm specializing in mobile apps, React Native, Elixir, low‑latency streaming, full‑stack web applications, and on‑device AI computing. They are a founding member of the React Foundation and have award‑winning products such as Partiful. Their services include product development, consulting, and open‑source contributions to the React Native ecosystem.

providers.name: Soundboks
providers.description: Soundboks is a Danish consumer-electronics company that designs and manufactures loud, durable, battery-powered Bluetooth party speakers (Soundboks 4, Soundboks Mix) plus companion products such as Lightboks party lights. Products are sold direct-to-consumer through a Shopify-powered storefront and controlled with a companion iOS/Android app that supports wireless playback and multi-speaker pairing (TeamUp). Soundboks does not publish a first-party developer API or SDK; its only programmatic surface is the Shopify Customer Account API (OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect) exposed on its own store domain via the standard Shopify discovery documents, which is what this enrichment pass captured.

providers.name: Southwest Gas
providers.description: Southwest Gas Holdings is a natural gas distribution company that purchases, distributes, and transports natural gas for customers in Arizona, Nevada, and California. As a Fortune 1000 utility company headquartered in Las Vegas, Nevada, Southwest Gas serves over 2 million customers through its regulated utility segment and also operates Centuri Group, a full-service utility infrastructure services company.

providers.name: Sudowrite
providers.description: Sudowrite is an AI writing platform built specifically for fiction and creative writers, used by 300,000+ authors from debut novelists to bestselling professionals. Its fiction-trained Muse AI model, alongside Story Bible (AI-powered character, worldbuilding, plot, and style memory), First Draft chapter drafting, and tools like Write, Rewrite, Describe, Expand, Brainstorm, and Canvas, helps writers draft, revise, and develop stories faster without sacrificing their voice. Sudowrite also offers a 1,000+ plugin marketplace, multi-model support (Sudowrite Muse, Claude, GPT, Gemini), and web plus iOS/Android apps. Named "a salvation" by The New Yorker and featured in The New York Times, The Verge, Time, and Wired. Sudowrite publishes no public developer API; the surface here is its consumer product, docs, and support properties.

providers.name: Superpower
providers.description: Superpower is a consumer preventive-health and longevity membership that provides an annual comprehensive blood draw across 100+ biomarkers, AI-driven result interpretation, biological age scoring, personalized action plans, and a care team, delivered through web and mobile apps. As of the catalog date Superpower does not publish a public or partner developer API; this catalog documents the product surface honestly rather than fabricating endpoints.

providers.name: ThousandBirds
providers.description: Thousand Birds builds AI agents that are fully debuggable, offering a TypeScript runtime called Chidori. The platform records every LLM call, tool invocation, and side effect, enabling step‑by‑step replay of agent runs. Users can debug production failures, trace execution, and integrate with tools like Tael for observability. The open‑source project emphasizes deterministic agents, reproducible debugging, and seamless integration with modern AI workflows.

providers.name: Town
providers.description: Town is a personal AI assistant that works across email, calendar, Slack, docs, WhatsApp, and the web. Users connect their accounts and Town — through a personal agent called a "Townie" — learns how they work, then suggests and runs automated "routines" (meeting briefs, email drafting, follow-ups, scheduling) on their behalf. Founded by Jean-Denis Greze (former Plaid CTO) and Tony Vincent (former Google product/AI lead), Town raised a $55M Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz (June 2026) with Forerunner Ventures, First Round, Alt Capital, and Conviction participating. Town publishes no public developer program: the product is fully auth-gated, api.town.com is a Convex backend deployment rather than a public API, and its robots.txt carries explicit Content-Signal declarations restricting AI training on its content.

providers.name: Tracxn
providers.description: Tracxn provides technology and data intelligence for venture capitalists, private equity firms, investment banks, and corporations, helping them track innovative companies and emerging sectors worldwide. Their platform aggregates comprehensive company information, market trends, and analytics to support investment decisions and corporate development strategies.

providers.name: Ubitricity
providers.description: Ubitricity is a Berlin-based electric vehicle charging company and wholly-owned subsidiary of Shell, best known for integrating EV charge points into existing street infrastructure such as lampposts and bollards. It operates the UK's largest public on-street charging network, with further networks in Germany and France, providing charge point hardware (Simple Socket lamppost units, AC and DC chargers), a managed charging platform built on the Open Charge Point Protocol (OCPP), and Pay-As-You-Go driver charging. The company does not currently publish a public developer API or developer portal.

providers.name: Voiio
providers.description: Voiio is a German employee assistance and work-life balance platform, positioning itself as "#1 in Work-Life-Balance" in the German market. The platform provides employee support across all life stages (family planning, childcare, eldercare, personal wellness, career support) through digital services, coaching, live lectures, expert referrals, and a 24/7 accessible portal. Integration with employer systems is available via Magic Links (authenticated deep-link URLs) and a white-label customization approach. No public REST API or developer portal has been identified; integrations are enterprise-contract based.

providers.name: 98point6 Technologies
providers.description: 98point6 Technologies is a Seattle-based digital health software company, founded in 2015, that builds and licenses a cloud-based virtual care platform to health systems, payers and virtual care providers. After selling its own care-delivery division in 2023 it operates purely as a licensed software provider. The platform combines an AI-driven Automated Assistant for patient intake and visit documentation, a web-based Clinician Console with automated clinical decision support, and a white-labeled patient application, covering both asynchronous and real-time (messaging, audio, video) care. It advertises HL7 and FHIR based EMR integration with Epic and Cerner, SSO for patient login, and an SDK for building a fully branded patient experience, but that integration surface is delivered under a licensing agreement, so no developer portal, API reference or machine-readable specification is published publicly.

providers.name: Ableton
providers.description: Ableton is a Berlin‑based company that creates software, hardware, and learning platforms for music creation and performance. Founded in 1999, Ableton develops the flagship DAW Live, as well as instruments like Push, Move, and Note, and offers extensive educational resources, community support, and a global user base of musicians, producers, and educators.

providers.name: Acadia Healthcare
providers.description: Acadia Healthcare Company, Inc. (NASDAQ: ACHC) is a Franklin, Tennessee-based Fortune 1000 behavioral healthcare provider operating a national network of acute inpatient psychiatric hospitals, specialty substance use disorder treatment facilities, residential treatment centers, and outpatient comprehensive treatment clinics across the United States. It is a clinical services operator rather than a software company: as of August 2026 it publishes no developer portal, no API reference, and no machine-readable contract of any kind. A MuleSoft CloudHub gateway is deployed at api.acadiahealthcare.com, but every anonymous path on it returns an empty-body HTTP 404, and the developer host previously recorded here (developer.acadiahealthcare.com) does not resolve. Not to be confused with Acadia Pharmaceuticals (NASDAQ: ACAD), an unrelated company.

providers.name: Aervivo
providers.description: Aervivo, Inc. is a San Diego, California company founded in 2020 that sells the Aervivo Connectivity Platform, a cloud operating system paired with the Aervivo Hybrid Edge ecosystem of fiber and fixed-wireless networking equipment (AerHub, AerSwitch). It lets multifamily property owners, fiber overbuilders, WISPs and incumbent ISPs deploy and operate community-wide gigabit managed WiFi without a full fiber build, bundling a virtualized core network with cloud-based OSS and BSS. Aervivo publishes no developer portal, API reference or machine-readable contract; its partner surface is a Salesforce Experience Cloud portal behind a login at portal.aervivo.com, and the only anonymous machine surface on its own hosts is the Wix Site MCP endpoint its marketing site serves.

providers.name: AgentPay
providers.description: AgentPay provides a marketplace of 34 pay-per-call APIs on the Base blockchain, allowing developers to integrate tools that settle payments in USDC without requiring an account or API key. The platform offers bundled credit packs, transparent pricing, and a simple token‑based authentication model, targeting Web3 developers seeking on‑demand functionality.

providers.name: Aitho
providers.description: You know your material. The hard part is delivering it when the room is watching. Aitho keeps your words in front of you as you speak (a voice-following teleprompter), moves your slides with you, keeps your notes private, and gives you a grounded private answer when a question comes.

providers.name: Akorda
providers.description: Akorda was a contract intelligence and contract lifecycle management (CLM) startup that applied artificial intelligence and natural language processing to accelerate contract negotiation, review, and management for legal and procurement teams. Backed by Bloomberg Beta, the company built machine-learning tooling to surface risky clauses, benchmark contract language against standards, and streamline the redlining and approval workflow. Akorda has since been acquired and absorbed into LegalSifter: its former domain (akorda.com) now redirects to legalsifter.com, and no independent Akorda product, developer portal, or public API remains. This profile is retained as a network lead and reflects the acquisition rather than a live, standalone API provider.

providers.name: Almanac Leie1
providers.description: Almanac Labs, Inc. (almanac.io) is a San Francisco-based productivity company building an async collaboration platform positioned as "the fastest wiki and workflow tool ever built." Almanac consolidates a team's documents into an organized single source of truth, pairing a modern doc editor with version control, structured review/approval workflows, and reusable templates. Founded in 2017 and backed by General Catalyst, the company also ships the Almanac API (V1, private beta) for programmatic workspace management — importing files, moving files and folders, listing workspace users and groups, reading and updating document properties and access, and managing document and folder metadata. This profile was surfaced as a General Catalyst portfolio lead and enriched from Almanac's public marketing, developer help, changelog, and legal pages.

providers.name: ALPNAI
providers.description: ALPNAI is a Swiss‑based SaaS platform that provides economic and performance analysis for AI agents. It offers tools such as Spend Proof, Latency Lab, and Quality Gate to measure cost per successful task, latency, and quality thresholds. Users can compare configurations, generate audit reports, and integrate the service via its API. The product is developed in Geneva by Frederic Pure and targets developers and teams deploying AI agents.

providers.name: Arch Coal
providers.description: Arch Coal was a St. Louis-based producer and marketer of metallurgical and thermal coal, renamed Arch Resources in 2020. In January 2025 Arch Resources merged with CONSOL Energy in a merger of equals to form Core Natural Resources, Inc. (NYSE: CNR), headquartered in Canonsburg, Pennsylvania. The combined company operates the Pennsylvania Mining Complex, Leer, Leer South, West Elk, Black Thunder, and other mines across six U.S. states with 5,000+ employees, and holds stakes in East Coast marine export terminals. Core Natural Resources does not publish a public developer API. Its external digital surface is a corporate website at corenaturalresources.com plus a separate investor relations portal, both serving HTML and PDF only — the investor portal's /rss and /feed paths were probed on 2026-07-25 and every one returns HTML, not XML. Machine-readable company data is available only through third-party channels, namely the SEC's own EDGAR APIs.

providers.name: Ardoq
providers.description: Ardoq provides an intelligent enterprise architecture platform that streamlines IT portfolios, reduces technical debt, and manages risk through real-time insights and AI-enhanced modeling. The platform enables dynamic, data-driven architecture, integrates with numerous tools via APIs, and supports collaboration across people, processes, and technology.

providers.name: Arga Labs
providers.description: Arga Labs provides testing infrastructure for AI agents and agent-facing software. Its platform spins up isolated, resettable sandboxes wired to stateful "digital twins" of third-party services — Stripe, Slack, GitHub, Salesforce, Notion, Discord, Google Drive, Jira, Box, Dropbox, Gmail, Google Calendar and more — so teams can run browser-agent tests, per-PR preview environments, and CI validation without hitting real APIs, exhausting rate limits, or mutating production data. Developers drive it from a web app, a REST API at api.argalabs.com, the arga CLI, official Python and TypeScript SDKs, and a hosted MCP server that lets coding agents (Cursor, Claude Code, Codex) provision twins and query validation runs directly from the editor.

providers.name: Army National Guard
providers.description: The Army National Guard is a reserve component of the United States Army that serves both the nation and individual states in times of need. Operating under the dual authority of the federal government and the fifty state governors, the Army National Guard provides trained and ready soldiers for overseas military operations, domestic disaster relief, homeland security, and civil support missions. Its primary data and digital services are focused on recruiting, career management, benefits administration, and public outreach. The National Guard Bureau (NGB) coordinates federal operations and maintains administrative systems under Title 10 and Title 32 of the United States Code.

providers.name: Basata
providers.description: Basata is a Phoenix-based healthcare AI company building the operational layer for American medical practices. Its AI agents automate back-office administrative work — processing patient referrals, answering phone calls 24/7, and managing faxes and patient communications — while integrating with existing EHR systems so clinical staff can focus on patient care instead of paperwork. Founded in 2024 by Kaled Alhanafi (CEO, formerly Lyft and Cruise), Chetan Patel (co-founder and president, formerly Medtronic), and Vivin Paliath (co-founder and CTO), Basata raised a $21M Series A led by Basis Set Ventures with Cowboy Ventures and PHX Ventures participating (~$24.5M total). The platform is marketed as fully HIPAA-compliant and the company publishes a SOC 2 attestation. Basata does not currently expose a public developer API or documentation surface; this profile captures its public identity and web properties.

providers.name: Ben
providers.description: Ben (thanksben.com) is an AI-native global employee benefits and rewards platform for enterprises. It unifies benefits eligibility rules, policy configuration, employee enrollment and access, spend and compliance dashboards, and rewards/recognition into a single system spanning 140+ countries, replacing fragmented regional benefits tooling. Customers include Moet, Henkel, Virgin, Zalando, Deliveroo, and Octopus Energy. Ben is backed by Seedcamp and was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company; it publishes no public developer API today, so this profile captures the company's identity and its public security and trust surface (RFC 9116 security.txt, a Vanta-hosted Trust Center, and probed domain security).

providers.name: Better Health
providers.description: Better Health (Better Health Supplies) is a modern, direct-to-consumer medical supplier that ships home medical supplies for chronic conditions straight to patients' doorsteps. The company covers diabetes and continuous glucose monitors (CGMs), incontinence, urology and self-catheterization, ostomy, and wound care categories, carrying leading brands and pairing product fulfillment with insurance-benefit navigation and one-on-one peer and clinical support. Better Health operates a Shopify-based storefront at joinbetter.com plus an education-focused community blog, and is backed by General Catalyst. It is cataloged in the API Evangelist network as a healthcare company profile; it publishes a consumer commerce experience rather than a first-party developer API, so this record captures its public web, security, and identity surface.

providers.name: BetterUp
providers.description: BetterUp is an enterprise Human Transformation Platform that combines human and AI-powered coaching, grounded in behavioral science and enterprise data, to help organizations develop leaders, managers, and their broader workforce. Founded by Alexi Robichaux, BetterUp serves 750+ enterprise customers including Google, Salesforce, Moderna, and Workday, with a network of 4,000+ coaches across 70+ countries. The platform delivers leadership development, manager effectiveness, AI coaching, and workforce resilience programs. BetterUp is HR-tech / organizational-development software and exposes no public developer API; platform integration is delivered through packaged enterprise connectors (Workday, Salesforce, Slack, Microsoft Viva, SAP SuccessFactors, Degreed) plus HRIS and SSO provisioning. Sector: hr-tech.

providers.name: Blue Crane Works
providers.description: Blue Crane Works is a Hamilton, Ontario based digital agency that designs, builds, and operates websites and custom business applications. They offer managed website services with pricing starting at $189 per month, focusing on SEO-friendly, AI‑compatible sites that integrate with tools like ChatGPT and Copilot. Their services include design, development, hosting, domain management, email routing, and ongoing visibility updates.

providers.name: Blueprint Studio
providers.description: Blueprint Studio provides design and development services for founders and companies. It creates apps, websites, brand identities, and launch videos, offering both project‑based work and a monthly subscription with unlimited requests and revisions. The studio handles UI/UX design, web and mobile development, and ongoing maintenance.

providers.name: Brandize
providers.description: Brandize is an AI-powered logo generator that creates professional, vector SVG and high‑resolution PNG logos instantly. Users can generate custom brand identities with a one‑time purchase, receiving full commercial rights without subscriptions, watermarks or attribution. The service offers a simple web interface, fast generation, and a library of design styles to suit startups, small businesses, and creators.

providers.name: Brightseed
providers.description: Brightseed is a bioactives and AI company founded in 2017 (San Francisco, CA, with operations in Durham, NC) that uses its Forager AI platform to map the compounds in plants to human biological pathways and health benefits. Forager draws on a proprietary dataset the company describes as the world's largest — 21 million bioactive compounds and hundreds of biological receptors spanning 23 health areas — combining high-resolution omics, high-throughput robotics and machine learning to predict which natural compounds confer a benefit and where to source them at commercial scale. Hummingbird, launched in 2026, layers an agentic AI system on top of Forager to carry partners from discovery through development. Brightseed sells discovery services (Bioactive Profiler, Bioactive Ingredient Finder) and market-ready ingredients (Bio Gut Fiber, Bio Meta Control, Bio Gut Core) to food, supplement and health-science companies. Brightseed publishes no product or developer API for Forager or Hummingbird — those are sold as enterprise engagements through a contact form. The single machine-readable surface the company operates is the WordPress REST API (wp/v2) behind its corporate site at www.brightseedbio.com, which exposes anonymous read access to posts, pages, categories, tags, users, media, comments, search, taxonomies, types and statuses, plus authenticated write operations via WordPress application passwords. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline from that live surface.

providers.name: Camber
providers.description: Camber is a healthcare revenue cycle management (RCM) and medical billing software platform purpose-built for specialty care providers, including ABA (applied behavior analysis) therapy, physical therapy, and ENT and allergy clinics. The platform automates the full claims lifecycle — creation and submission, pre-submission scrubbing and eligibility verification, payment posting and reconciliation, and denial management and prevention — using a rules engine and AI trained on billions of dollars in real claims data, combined with human review where judgment matters. Founded in 2021 (Y Combinator W21, rebranded from Juniper Behavioral Health to Camber), the New York-based company is backed by Craft Ventures, a16z, and Y Combinator, and processes over a million claims annually for hundreds of specialty care providers across all 50 states.

providers.name: Catena
providers.description: Catena (Catena Labs) is building a regulated banking and governance platform for AI agents. The platform gives agents verified identities, custodial and non-custodial accounts, fiat and stablecoin payment rails across ten chains, yield on idle assets, and policy-enforced spending controls. For the humans and businesses deploying those agents it is a control plane: set policy, cap spending, restrict counterparties, audit every movement, and halt activity when needed. Agents access the platform through an API, a CLI, an MCP server, and a Skills framework. Founded by Sean Neville (CEO) and Matt Venables (CTO) - both Circle co-founders and creators of USDC - Catena has filed for a National Trust Bank charter with the OCC and raised $48M total ($30M Series A co-led by a16z crypto and Acrew, with QED, Coinbase Ventures, General Catalyst, Breyer Capital, IDG Capital, Oak HC/FT, and Pillar).

providers.name: Chainlink
providers.description: Build hybrid smart contracts with Chainlink

providers.name: Code4rena
providers.description: Code4rena (C4) is a competitive smart-contract security auditing platform that connects Web3/DeFi projects (sponsors) with a global community of security researchers (wardens) through time-boxed competitive audits and ongoing bug bounties. Sponsors fund an audit, wardens compete to surface vulnerabilities, and judges rate severity, validity, and quality to distribute awards via a ranked-curve incentive model. Over five years the platform ran 512+ audits, engaged 16,600+ researchers, and surfaced 26,898 findings including 1,607 high-severity vulnerabilities. Code4rena announced it is winding down operations, seeing active competitions and bounties through to completion. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a paradigm portfolio company; the platform is web/app-based with GitBook documentation and does not publish a public REST/GraphQL API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Complir
providers.description: Complir is the AI infrastructure for product compliance, described by the company as "Vanta for physical products." Its AI agents map product data, analyse compliance risks, generate audit-ready documentation, and track regulatory changes across every market a brand sells in - covering GPSR, ESPR, EPR, REACH, RoHS, PPWR, EUDR, CE/UKCA marking, Digital Product Passports and 100+ other frameworks across 40+ markets. The platform maps each SKU to its regulatory requirements, produces translations, labels, warnings, declarations of conformity and technical files, verifies marketing claims, and offers native Adobe Illustrator/InDesign plugins plus a natural language interface for querying compliance data. Founded in 2024 (Gustav Bang, Marc Kaa Brejner, Tine Kuhnel) and part of Y Combinator's Spring 2026 batch, Complir monitors 100,000+ products for international retailers including Flying Tiger Copenhagen, Konges Sloejd, Matas and COOP.

providers.name: Coursera
providers.description: Coursera is a global online learning platform offering courses, specializations, professional certificates, and degrees. The Catalog API provides public, read-only access to courses, instructors, partners, and categories; the Affiliate API supports partner programs.

providers.name: Daily Harvest
providers.description: Daily Harvest is a direct-to-consumer health food delivery company. It sells organic, ready-to-prepare frozen foods — smoothies, oat bowls, elixirs, protein, and boosters — that customers order on daily-harvest.com (a Shopify storefront) and receive shipped frozen to their door, with no subscription required. Daily Harvest is a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners. It publishes no first-party developer API; its only public programmatic surface is the Shopify Customer Account API OIDC/OAuth2 authorization layer exposed at account.daily-harvest.com.

providers.name: Documint
providers.description: Documint is a programmatic document generation platform with a template editor, REST API and integrations with major CRMs and automation tools (HubSpot, Airtable, Zapier, Make). Documents are generated by merging user-supplied JSON data into pre-built templates; data is not stored on Documint servers. The REST API is published on the Platinum plan.

providers.name: Dragonboat
providers.description: Dragonboat provides an agentic product development lifecycle (PDLC) platform that uses an active ontology to orchestrate strategy, portfolio, and execution across product teams. It offers headless APIs, MCP integration, and tools for product managers, CPOs, and CTOs to automate workflows, gain real‑time insights, and adapt to changing market conditions. The platform integrates with Jira, Azure DevOps, Salesforce, Slack, and Teams, enabling AI agents to act on product data and drive outcomes at scale.

providers.name: Driver
providers.description: Driver turns your phone into an AI dash cam with free HD recording that flags risky moments and saves every trip to the cloud on iPhone and Android. The flagship Driver app provides safety coaching, community‑sourced road intelligence, and partners with fleets and mobility platforms to deliver smarter roads. It records every trip, flags risky moments, and stores video in Driver Cloud, offering free plans for drivers and paid options for families, driving schools, and fleets.

providers.name: FastAPI
providers.description: FastAPI is a modern, fast (high-performance), web framework for building APIs with Python 3.7+ based on standard Python type hints.

providers.name: First Data (Fiserv)
providers.description: First Data was a global payment technology solutions company providing merchant transaction processing, financial institution services, and prepaid services before merging with Fiserv in 2019. Legacy First Data API products including Payeezy, Bolt, and Commerce Hub are now part of the Fiserv developer portal.

providers.name: Fixie
providers.description: Fixie, now operating as Ultravox, builds real‑time speech‑native voice AI platforms. The company provides developer‑friendly APIs that enable fast, natural conversational experiences, offering primitives for voice agents, pricing tiers, and extensive documentation. Backed by Redpoint Ventures, Ultravox focuses on research and product development to accelerate speech‑to‑speech AI capabilities.

providers.name: Forte Labs
providers.description: Forte builds on-chain compliance and economic tooling for games and Web3 applications. Its flagship developer product, the Forte Rules Engine, is an open-source EVM protocol that lets developers define powerful, flexible, and composable on-chain policies — for regulatory compliance, risk management, and token-economy design — without hardcoding rules into their smart contracts. The engine centers on policies, rules, trackers, and calling/foreign contracts, ships client contracts for the ERC20/721/1155/721A token standards, and is consumed through a TypeScript SDK. Forte was founded in 2019 and is backed by Andreessen Horowitz, Battery Ventures, Griffin Gaming Partners, and Canaan. This profile catalogs Forte's public developer surface — Rules Engine documentation, SDK, and GitHub organization.

providers.name: Harbin Institute of Technology
providers.description: Harbin Institute of Technology (HIT, 哈尔滨工业大学) is a public technical research university in Harbin, Heilongjiang, China, founded in 1920, administered by the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, and a member of the C9 League, with additional campuses at Weihai and Shenzhen. HIT operates NO public developer programme, no API documentation, no developer portal and no API key issuance of any kind, and this profile should be read as recording that absence. Its one institution-operated machine-readable surface is a Shibboleth SAML 2.0 identity provider at idp.hit.edu.cn, scoped to hit.edu.cn — genuinely HIT's own engineering, though the metadata document it publishes is the unedited Shibboleth template and expired in 2020. Every other machine-readable surface is a tenancy on Elsevier Pure running under HIT's own hostname (scholar.hit.edu.cn): a live and anonymously harvestable OAI-PMH endpoint carrying the OpenAIRE CERIF 1.2 profile, RSS feeds of publications and researcher profiles, and a Pure web services API that is credential-gated and whose contract belongs to Elsevier, not to HIT. The data in those surfaces is HIT's; the contracts are not.

providers.name: Horizon Media
providers.description: Horizon Media is the largest independent media agency in the United States, founded in 1989 by Bill Koenigsberg and headquartered at 75 Varick Street in New York with offices in Los Angeles and Toronto. The agency employs roughly 2,300+ people, is ranked the third largest US media agency by COMvergence, and manages an estimated $8.7 billion in billings. Horizon operates a portfolio of specialty units (Horizon Next for performance, Blue Hour Studios for social/creator, Night Market for retail media, Scout Sports for sponsorship via Horizon Sports & Experiences, and the WHY Group for cultural insights) and runs a proprietary data and AI stack anchored by the Blu platform. In 2025 Horizon formed Horizon Global, a 50/50 US joint venture with Havas positioned at roughly $20 billion in combined billings, merging Blu with Havas Converged into a shared platform branded BluConverged, and is also building Horizon OS (Open Sphere) as an orchestration layer over the programmatic ad-tech stack. In June 2026 Horizon launched an agentic integration layer around Blu — a set of Blu audience APIs, MCP endpoints and agent-based integration points that ad-tech, media-owner and martech partners can build on — but that surface is partner-gated: Horizon publishes no developer portal, no API reference, no OpenAPI or other machine-readable contract, no SDKs in any public registry, and its GitHub organization has zero public repositories. The only route to the API is the corporate contact form. All platforms documented here are proprietary systems reachable through a commercial partnership rather than open developer APIs.

providers.name: HyperWrite
