The solution offers a universal API and DSL to automate data flows, supports both cloud and on‑premise deployments, and includes tools for pricing, stock management, and custom business rules. It targets agencies, SaaS providers, and businesses seeking to streamline operations without building individual connectors for each system.

providers.name: DivestMe
providers.description: DivestMe buys stuck private positions for $1 under a counter‑signed sale agreement. A flat $150 covers the documentation, providing a dated sale your accountant can work with. The service documents a real, counter‑signed sale of a defunct private position, offering Asset Sale Agreements and Certificates of Completion with SHA‑256 integrity hashes. It does not determine tax eligibility or provide legal advice, leaving those decisions to the holder and their advisors.

providers.name: Dockwa
providers.description: Dockwa provides marina management software connecting boaters and marinas. Their platform offers tools for reservations, contracts, customer communication, and occupancy optimization, serving a network of over 300,000 boaters and numerous marinas worldwide.

providers.name: dryos-ai
providers.description: Dryos AI operates a data marketplace delivering real-time and historical energy, weather, and property datasets via a unified API. It aggregates streams from multiple sources such as ERCOT, MISO, PJM, and SPP, providing over 135 live data streams covering power prices, demand, generation, forecasts, and property information. The platform offers a no‑code workspace, open-source tools, and free public access without requiring accounts, enabling developers and AI agents to integrate and analyze the data effortlessly.

providers.name: Dubai Real Estate Data
providers.description: Dubai Real Estate Data provides open market analytics for Dubai property transactions, offering data on sales volumes, price indexes, rental yields, mortgage statistics, and area‑specific insights. The platform aggregates official DLD open data and presents it through dashboards and downloadable datasets for developers, analysts, and investors.

providers.name: Dylibso
providers.description: Dylibso, Inc. is the company behind Extism, the open-source, cross-language framework for building with WebAssembly (Wasm). Its focus is AI-driven application extensibility: giving developers an off-the-shelf, secure-by-default, fully sandboxed plug-in system that is "just a library import away" and runs almost anywhere, with idiomatic Host SDKs for JavaScript, Python, Rust, Ruby, Go, .NET, PHP, Java, C/C++, OCaml, Haskell, Perl, and Zig. Beyond Extism, Dylibso builds Chicory (a native pure-JVM WebAssembly runtime) and Turbo MCP (formerly mcp.run / XTP), a standards-compliant, self-hosted Model Context Protocol gateway and management platform with OIDC identity integration and audit controls. Dylibso is backed by Felicis.

providers.name: Finaloop
providers.description: Finaloop is a real-time, ecommerce-native bookkeeping and accounting platform for direct-to-consumer (DTC) and multichannel brands. It replaces QuickBooks/Xero, human bookkeepers, and integration tooling with automation plus a team of ecommerce accounting experts, delivering always-current financials. Finaloop continuously syncs sales, returns, fees, reimbursements, inventory movements, COGS, and banking across 60+ ecommerce, marketplace, payment, banking, lending, and 3PL integrations (Shopify, Amazon, TikTok Shop, Walmart, PayPal, Stripe, Chase, ShipBob, and more) to produce real-time P&L, balance sheet, and cash-flow statements, inventory analytics, and tax services. Finaloop exposes no public developer API; its APIs are internal connectors to source platforms, so this profile is identity- and posture-focused rather than spec-bearing.

providers.name: Finsweet
providers.description: Finsweet is a Webflow development, design, and product agency offering a range of services including web development, SEO, CRO, AI automation, integrations, and HIPAA‑compliant applications. They provide tools, components, and consulting for Webflow users, with a focus on enterprise solutions, multilingual sites, and custom web apps, supporting industries such as fintech, healthcare, and education.

providers.name: Forecastr
providers.description: Forecastr is a startup financial planning and forecasting platform, founded in 2018 in Louisville, Kentucky, that helps founders and finance teams build investor-ready financial models, track cash flow and runway, plan headcount, budget expenses, and run what-if scenario analysis. It pairs cloud-based forecasting software (a spreadsheet-style formula builder, pre-built templates, drag-and-drop dashboards, and shareable live models) with fractional CFO services, and keeps actuals current through accounting integrations with QuickBooks Online and Xero. Forecastr is an API consumer of those accounting platforms rather than a public API provider; it publishes no developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDKs at this time.

providers.name: General Motors
providers.description: You can reach customers in their cars using GMs powerful, in-vehicle platform. Our tools can provide access to close to 200 data points, allowing you to monitor vehicle data in real-time to deliver the content that matters, when it matters. Create an account now to start developing amazing in-vehicle experiences for your customers.

providers.name: Hearth Display
providers.description: Hearth Display provides a household organization platform that grows with families, helping parents manage toddler routines, teen schedules, chores, calendars, and family communication through a digital display and companion app. The solution adapts to every season of family life, offering customizable views, reminders, and integration with smart home devices to keep the household running smoothly.

providers.name: Helical
providers.description: Helical turns your data into biological intelligence for target identification and biomarker discovery. Your models and the intelligence they capture stay yours. Helical provides a virtual AI lab for drug discovery, enabling users to teach biological foundation models with proprietary data, run target and biomarker workflows, and assess cross-species translation with evidence to prioritize experiments.

providers.name: HireArt
providers.description: HireArt is a workforce management platform that helps enterprises source, employ, and manage their contingent workforce - contract workers, freelancers, and staffing vendors - through a single self-serve system. Its products span Employer of Record (EOR), on-demand sourcing and recruitment, a Vendor Management System (VMS), worker classification and compliance (1099 vs. W-2 with indemnification), program management, and freelancer management. Customers include Toyota Research Institute, Zoox, Via, Scale AI, Dropbox, Meta Quest, Carta, and Rover. HireArt was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network; it does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation at this time.

providers.name: Houm
providers.description: Houm (Houm Technologies SpA) is a Chilean proptech operating a digital real-estate brokerage and rental-management marketplace across Chile, Mexico and Colombia, with operations in Santiago, Viña del Mar, Concepcion, Bogota and Ciudad de Mexico. Founded in 2018 by Benjamin Labra and Nicolas Knockaert, the company lets owners list, rent and sell apartments and houses without a guarantor (sin aval), guarantees on-time rent payment to the owner even when the tenant does not pay, and runs a network of freelance field agents ("Houmers") who photograph, show and manage properties. Its ReV pricing algorithm (houm.com/cl/algoritmo-precio) values a property online, and it also runs an investor product and a broker exchange (Houm Aliados / Canje Corredores). Houm raised a $35M Series A in 2021 led by Goodwater Capital. As of this profile Houm publishes no public developer program, API reference or machine-readable contract; its production backend at api.houm.com answers 403 to every anonymous request and carries no published documentation.

providers.name: Hubble Protocol
providers.description: Hubble Protocol is a Solana-based decentralized finance (DeFi) protocol that lets users borrow the USDH stablecoin against multiple crypto collateral assets (SOL, mSOL, stSOL, ETH, BTC and more) with interest-free, fixed-fee loans held open for unlimited time. The protocol pairs a Stability Vault, a Peg Stability Module, a hybrid liquidation model, and native yield on deposited collateral. Developers integrate with Hubble on-chain through its Anchor programs (IDLs published on GitHub) and the open-source "@hubbleprotocol/hubble-sdk" TypeScript client, which exposes borrowing market states, HBB staking and USDH stability-pool data, user loans, treasury and circulating-supply metrics, and peg-stability swaps. Hubble published security audits (Arcadia, Kudelski, Smart State, Sec3) and runs a funded bug-bounty program; its core contributors later built Kamino Finance.

providers.name: Integral
providers.description: Integral (Integral Development Corp.) is a technology provider for institutional currency and digital-asset trading. Its cloud-native, API-first platform delivers liquidity aggregation, execution management, pricing engines, distribution, risk management, settlement, and market data across foreign exchange, CFDs, precious metals, and crypto. Integral serves banks, institutional and retail brokers, precious-metals businesses, and crypto trading firms, and is SOC 2 Type II certified with connectivity over FIX, ITCH, and proprietary REST and WebSocket APIs. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel, Electric Capital, and General Catalyst.

providers.name: Kriya Therapeutics
providers.description: Kriya Therapeutics, Inc. is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company founded in 2019 that designs, develops and manufactures one-time AAV gene therapies for chronic diseases that affect large patient populations, rather than for ultra-rare indications alone. It is headquartered at 1219 Shiloh Glenn Drive in Durham, North Carolina, inside Research Triangle Park, with additional operations in Palo Alto, California, and has raised more than $900 million across Series A ($80M, 2020), Series B ($100M, 2021), Series C (over $430M including a $150M extension, 2022-2023) and Series D ($320M, September 2025). Its pipeline spans three therapeutic areas: ophthalmology (geographic atrophy, thyroid eye disease including KRIYA-586), metabolic disease (Type 1 diabetes, MASH/NASH, an investigational AAV-FGF21 program) and neurology (trigeminal neuralgia, added through the 2022 acquisition of Redpin Therapeutics). The company operates a vertically integrated engine that pairs computational product design with in-house GMP manufacturing — the same unit operations from 1L research scale through 50L, 500L and 3,000L bioreactor scale, with Akta chromatography purification, vial filling and in-house analytical characterization of critical quality attributes. It was selected for the FDA PreCheck Pilot Program in June 2026. Kriya Therapeutics runs no developer program and publishes no product API, no developer portal and no API documentation; the only machine-readable surface reachable without credentials is the WordPress REST content API behind kriyatherapeutics.com, catalogued here.

providers.name: Mirza
providers.description: Mirza is a public benefits infrastructure platform that helps government agencies, health plans and MCOs, health systems, and employers enroll people in social safety-net programs (Medicaid, SNAP, WIC, childcare subsidies, and more) and keep them covered as eligibility rules change. It matches individuals to 200+ benefits across all 50 states, verifies eligibility from existing data rather than paperwork, prevents disenrollment through early exemption detection, and generates audit-ready compliance documentation including H.R.1 Medicaid community-engagement support. Mirza integrates with existing eligibility systems rather than replacing them. Founded in 2020 by Siran Cao and Mel Faxon; backed by 500 Global and others.

providers.name: Money You're Owed
providers.description: Money You're Owed publishes plain-English US consumer money-recovery help — free official-route checklists (unclaimed property, airline refunds, EITC, medical bills, property tax) and one-time-purchase self-help kits such as Deposit Defender and DenialFix — and exposes its source-cited fact catalog to AI assistants through two free, anonymous, read-only agent surfaces: a remote MCP server at mcp.moneyyoureowed.com with a single answer_money_question tool, and an A2A 1.0 agent whose card is served from agent.moneyyoureowed.com. There is no REST API, SDK or developer program; the machine surface is agent-native by design.

providers.name: NameSilo
providers.description: NameSilo is a domain registrar and web services provider offering domain registration, hosting, email, and SSL solutions. NameSilo exposes a Domain API enabling programmatic domain search, registration, and management via HTTPS GET requests with XML or JSON responses, plus an MCP server for AI agents.

providers.name: NiKang Therapeutics
providers.description: NiKang Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company headquartered at 200 Powder Mill Road, Building E500, Wilmington, Delaware, founded in 2017 to discover and develop innovative small molecule medicines that help patients fight cancer. The company works from deep insights into disease biology and molecular pathways and applies structure-based drug design to targets long considered difficult to drug, spanning both inhibitor and targeted-protein-degradation modalities. Its lead programme, NKT2152, is an orally bioavailable allosteric HIF2alpha inhibitor in Phase 1/2 for clear cell renal cell carcinoma, VHL disease and other solid tumours; NKT3964 is a first-in-class selective CDK2 degrader in Phase 1 for advanced or metastatic solid tumours; NKT5097 is a first-in-class dual CDK2/4 degrader, also in Phase 1; and a KRAS G12D small molecule programme sits in discovery and IND-enabling work. NiKang raised a $10 million Series A in December 2017, a $50 million Series B in September 2020 and a $200 million Series C in May 2021, and has partnered its chemistry with Erasca on SHP2 and with Pfizer, Hansoh and Roche on HIF2. NiKang Therapeutics runs no developer program and publishes no product API, developer portal, API reference or machine-readable specification of its own. The only machine-readable surface reachable without credentials is the WordPress REST content API behind www.nikangtx.com, which is catalogued here — 210 registered routes across 17 namespaces, of which the anonymously readable read-only content families are described in openapi/.

providers.name: Noda
providers.description: Noda (formerly Infogrid) is an agentic AI platform for commercial real estate building operations. It functions as an always-on AI virtual building engineer that connects to a portfolio's building management systems (BMS), IoT, weather, and utility data, continuously detects faults and energy waste, identifies root causes, generates quantified savings recommendations, and executes authorized setpoint and load adjustments — tying every action to measured, audit-ready ROI. The platform processes 100M+ data points daily and reports 15-25% annual energy reduction across deployed assets. Trusted by owners and operators of 400M+ square feet including Hilton, JLL, CBRE, Macerich, Cousins, DivcoWest and Salesforce. ISO 27001 certified and hosted on AWS in the United States. Backed by Northzone. Noda exposes no public developer API; onboarding is enterprise/demo-based.

providers.name: Nolla Health
providers.description: Nolla Health is a Norway-born, AI-powered telehealth and dermatology company that entered the U.S. market with a $4.5M seed round led by General Catalyst and set up its headquarters in New York City. After treating more than 50,000 patients in Europe and becoming one of Norway's top-five medical apps, Nolla launched an AI-guided skin and acne care platform across 40+ U.S. states. The service pairs proprietary AI symptom assessment with clinician-in-the-loop oversight: patients complete a guided chat, a licensed U.S. medical provider reviews and approves every diagnosis and prescription, and topical medications are shipped directly to the patient. Nolla operates as a consumer-facing product (per-consultation and a monthly subscription) rather than an API provider, and publicly states HIPAA and GDPR compliance.

providers.name: Olyns
providers.description: Olyns is a Silicon Valley company, founded in 2019, that operates an AI-powered reverse vending and retail media network built around the Olyns Cube — a self-serve kiosk that accepts beverage containers and rigid plastic packaging, uses computer vision to identify and sort each item at the point of deposit, pays the consumer their deposit (CRV) refund electronically, and carries a 55-inch screen that Olyns sells as digital-out-of-home advertising inventory. Cubes are placed with supermarkets, big-box retailers, pharmacies and gas stations, and the advertising side is sold both directly and programmatically through Screenverse. Olyns ships consumer and operations software — a mobile/web wallet app at app.olyns.com and a self-service ad portal at ads.olyns.com — but publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable contract of any kind.

providers.name: Poloniex
providers.description: US based digital asset exchange

providers.name: Privyr
providers.description: Privyr is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: vc-portfolio; backed by crane-venture-partners) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.

providers.name: RefleXion Medical
providers.description: RefleXion Medical is a privately held therapeutic oncology company headquartered in Hayward, California, founded in 2009 by Sam Mazin and Akshay Nanduri around the biology-guided radiotherapy (BgRT) concept conceived at Stanford University in 2007. The company designs, manufactures and commercializes the RefleXion X1 radiotherapy platform and SCINTIX biology-guided radiotherapy, which uses onboard PET detectors to sense emissions from an injected radiopharmaceutical and autonomously direct external-beam radiotherapy delivery with sub-second latency. The RefleXion X1 received FDA clearance for SRS, SBRT and IMRT in 2020, and SCINTIX therapy was FDA cleared in February 2023 for treating tumors in the lung or bone arising from primary and metastatic cancer. RefleXion has raised more than $500 million from investors including TPG's The Rise Fund, KCK Group, PSP Investments, Sofinnova, Pfizer Ventures and Johnson & Johnson Innovation. RefleXion is a medical device manufacturer rather than a software vendor and publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: REST
providers.description: REST (Representational State Transfer) is an architectural style for designing networked applications, defined by Roy Fielding in his 2000 doctoral dissertation. REST uses stateless communication, standard HTTP methods (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH), and resource-oriented URLs to provide scalable, cacheable, and loosely coupled interfaces. It has become the dominant approach for building web APIs, forming the foundation of modern API design principles and tooling ecosystems.

providers.name: Rite Aid
providers.description: Rite Aid is one of the nation's leading drugstore chains, providing prescription drugs, health and beauty aids, and convenience items. Rite Aid supports vendor integrations through EDI (Electronic Data Interchange) and B2B services, and offers digital health tools including an AI health assistant, pharmacy services, vaccination record management, and preventive health screening programs.

providers.name: Saaras
providers.description: Saaras provides cloud‑native API gateway and service‑mesh solutions built on Kubernetes. Their EnRoute Gateway offers high‑performance traffic management, security, observability, and dynamic routing for modern cloud applications. Saaras also delivers Istio‑based subscriptions, FIPS‑validated distributions, and consulting services to help enterprises adopt API management at scale.

providers.name: SAIB & Co.
providers.description: SAIB (Save & Co.) is a Seoul-based Korean intimate cosmetics and wellness brand focused on female empowerment, offering premium condoms and solid feminine cleansing products made with proprietary, health-conscious ingredients such as CranProB. The brand donates 10% of sales revenue to campaigns supporting gender equality and women's rights. SAIB sells direct-to-consumer through a Cafe24-hosted storefront (saibnco.com); its only programmatic surface is the Cafe24 Unified Commerce Platform (UCP) storefront, which exposes an OpenID Connect discovery document and an OAuth 2.0 / OIDC storefront API for this mall. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and enriched into the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: SanDisk
providers.description: SanDisk, a Western Digital brand, is a leading manufacturer of flash memory products including memory cards, USB flash drives, solid-state drives, and embedded storage solutions. SanDisk provides developer SDKs for integrating iXpand storage devices into iOS applications, enabling third-party app developers to access and manage iXpand Flash Drive storage through the Lightning interface. Western Digital also maintains the My Cloud Home platform with RESTful APIs for building off-device cloud storage applications.

providers.name: Savvly
providers.description: Savvly is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of techstars and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Seatti
providers.description: Seatti is a hybrid-workplace management platform that helps organizations run desk, room, and parking booking, track real office occupancy and utilization without hardware sensors, manage visitor check-ins, and coordinate team presence. It integrates deeply with Microsoft Entra ID, Outlook, and Teams, and serves 100+ companies across 30+ countries including OSRAM, Sartorius, and IKB. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Partech (Applicative SaaS) and enriched in the API Evangelist network; no public developer API surface was found at enrichment time.

providers.name: Section
providers.description: Section provides an Enterprise AI Training & Adoption Platform that helps organizations measure, guide, and scale AI adoption. Their solutions include AI transformation planning, personalized coaching, workflow automation, and agentic enterprise workshops. The platform offers tools for leadership coaching, AI strategy support, and hands‑on consulting to accelerate AI initiatives across the enterprise.

providers.name: Sequence
providers.description: Sequence is a usage-based billing, pricing, and revenue orchestration platform for B2B SaaS and other recurring-revenue businesses. It turns product usage and negotiated contract terms into automated billing schedules, invoices, credit notes, and quotes, backed by a metering engine for usage events and usage metrics, plus revenue recognition and integrations to ERP/CRM, tax, and payment providers. The REST API (production base https://eu.sequencehq.com) uses HTTP Basic authentication with a Client ID and Client Secret, date-based API versioning (for example sequence-version 2024-07-30), and signed webhooks for event notifications. A Sandbox environment (https://sandbox.sequencehq.com) mirrors production for testing.

providers.name: Simpatico Project
providers.description: Simpatico Project (유쾌한프로젝트, Yukwaehan Project Co., Ltd.) is a Korean B2B mental-wellness startup, backed by 500 Global, whose product Clify (클라이피, "Climb & Clarify") is an AI-based integrated mental-care and Employee Assistance Program (EAP) solution for individuals and companies. Clify uses a patented multimodal algorithm to fuse Face & Voice biosignals — blood-flow changes, micro-expressions and voice characteristics — into a roughly one-minute mental-state diagnosis (stress, anxiety, depression, burnout) that it claims exceeds 90% accuracy, and rolls the results up into an organization insight dashboard for HR (company-wide mental trends, high/low-risk teams, usage). Personal mental data is processed on-device and de-identified so it is never shared with the employer, and the company states it holds ISO 27001. Product surfaces include FAV (the Face & Voice AI diagnosis engine), an EAP counseling center, and the Clify organization-insight analytics. The public presence (clify.co.kr, an imweb-built marketing and account site) exposes no developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or webhook surface at this time.

providers.name: Stack Health
providers.description: Stack Healthcare (stackhealthcare.com) is a health-insurance fintech offering affordable, flexible coverage for small businesses and their teams. Operating as a technology company rather than a bank, Stack acts as a HIPAA Business Associate to employer-sponsored health plans, processing Protected Health Information for enrollment and benefits administration, and partners with Stripe for payments and Celtic Bank for issuing commercial cards. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of 8vc and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Stack publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or documentation surface — the product is a waitlist-gated web application — so this profile captures the identity, security, and compliance posture that is publicly verifiable.

providers.name: Stance
providers.description: Stance is a direct-to-consumer apparel brand best known for expressive, performance-oriented socks, plus underwear and related apparel sold under the "Feel good, do good" tagline. The company operates a Shopify-hosted online storefront at stance.com with licensed collaborations (MLB, NBA, Disney, and others). Stance publishes no developer product API; its only public machine-facing surface is the Shopify Customer Account API (OpenID Connect / OAuth 2.0) exposed for customer sign-in at account.stance.com. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Bond Capital and Shasta Ventures and enriched from live probes of its public well-known discovery documents and storefront pages.

providers.name: Strands Agents
providers.description: Strands Agents provides an open-source toolkit for building, deploying, and managing production AI agents. It offers a modular harness, SDKs for multiple languages, sandboxing, evaluation tools, and a marketplace of integrations. The platform enables developers to compose complex multi-agent systems, enforce policy, and monitor performance, aiming to accelerate AI agent adoption in real-world applications.

providers.name: Synthetic Sciences
providers.description: Synthetic Sciences is a Y Combinator-backed AI research lab building foundation models for scientific discovery. Its flagship product, Atlas, is an agent-first research graph and infrastructure layer for autonomous science: durable typed nodes (hypotheses, experiment plans, recorded runs, evidence, decisions) linked into a shared, forkable map that humans and AI agents read and write directly over a REST API and the @synsci/atlas CLI. Atlas bundles a Library for indexing and grounded search over repos, docs, papers, and datasets, a cross-provider GPU compute marketplace, GEPA-based optimization and refereed autoresearch, and nine agent Skills. The lab also ships two open-source (Apache 2.0) projects: OpenScience, a model-agnostic AI workbench that runs the full research loop, and Delphi, a self-hosted MCP server that gives coding agents semantic context over code, papers, and HuggingFace datasets.

providers.name: taktile
providers.description: Taktile is an agentic decision platform for financial institutions that combines AI speed with human oversight to automate and optimize high-stakes decisions across banking and insurance. Its Decision Engine, AI Agent Manager, Case Manager, and Context Layer power onboarding and KYC, credit underwriting, AML and fraud investigation, claims processing, and insurance underwriting. Teams design, test, deploy, and monitor decision flows and AI agents through a no-code studio backed by real-time APIs (the Taktile API and Flow API), with enterprise-grade infrastructure, data integrations, and governance controls.

providers.name: Ten Little
providers.description: Ten Little is a direct-to-consumer children's footwear and essentials brand that designs healthy, non-toxic shoes for babies and kids. Its APMA-approved shoes use a proprietary TenForm Fit System — wide, foot-shaped toe boxes and flexible zero-drop soles grounded in medical and biomechanical research — to support natural movement and healthy foot development at every size and stage, and to accommodate AFO/SMO orthotics and braces. The brand sells online through a Shopify storefront and publishes no first-party developer API; the only API surfaces reachable on its domain are Shopify's platform-level Customer Account OIDC/OAuth and MCP endpoints.

providers.name: Terex
providers.description: Terex Corporation is a global manufacturer of aerial work platforms and materials processing equipment. Terex provides digital telematics solutions through its MyTerex platform and Connect by Terex for remote diagnostics, fleet management, and predictive maintenance of construction and industrial equipment.

providers.name: UMB Bank
providers.description: UMB Bank, National Association is the primary banking subsidiary of UMB Financial Corporation (Nasdaq ticker UMBF), a Kansas City, Missouri financial services holding company. UMB is a commercial bank operating under a national (federal) bank charter supervised by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC), with roughly $70 billion in assets following its 2025 acquisition of Heartland Financial and branches across the central United States. It offers personal, commercial, and institutional banking, including asset servicing, corporate trust, and healthcare (HSA) services. UMB runs a partner-facing open-banking and Banking-as-a-Service (BaaS) program through its Institutional & Fintech Banking group, exposing REST APIs across risk & compliance, customer onboarding, accounts, information (statements/check images), and cash management. Access is partner-gated through a consultation and contracting process — there is no public self-serve developer portal, no publicly downloadable OpenAPI/Swagger specification, and no published FDX or CFPB 1033 posture. Consumer-permissioned account data is reached primarily through the Plaid aggregator rather than a first-party public API.

providers.name: University of Canterbury
providers.description: University of Canterbury (Te Whare Wananga o Waitaha) is a public research university in Christchurch, Aotearoa New Zealand. It operates no public developer programme, no developer portal and no published, self-serve API: everything machine-readable it runs is infrastructure for a purpose other than being an API product. What is genuinely institution-operated and genuinely readable is narrow — the UC Research Repository (a self-hosted DSpace 7 on ir.canterbury.ac.nz) serves a live OAI-PMH 2.0 interface with thirteen metadata formats, and three Shibboleth Service Providers on canterbury.ac.nz hosts publish valid SAML 2.0 metadata as members of Tuakiri, the New Zealand Access Federation. The rest is gated rather than absent: a CA API Gateway 9.0 answers on api.canterbury.ac.nz with no routed public service, a self-hosted GitLab serves an authenticated v4 API to the College of Engineering, and the DSpace REST API sits behind a Cloudflare bot challenge. The institution's research data repository and its identity provider are both tenancies on other people's platforms — Figshare and REANNZ's Tuakiri Hosted IdP respectively — and are recorded here as relationships, not as University of Canterbury contracts. This profile was corrected on 2026-08-30: eleven entries previously listed under this institution were a single Figshare API v2 contract, split by tag, and have been removed.

providers.name: Urban SDK
providers.description: Urban SDK is a geospatial AI and data analytics company serving the public sector, delivering hourly road-speed and traffic data, analytics, and AI tools that help cities, counties, and transportation agencies prioritize issues, pinpoint trends, and act on traffic management, public safety, emergency response, and infrastructure planning. A Techstars portfolio company based in Jacksonville, Florida, Urban SDK delivers its data through a web platform and automated Workflows reports rather than a public API, and currently publishes no developer documentation or client SDKs.

providers.name: Valera Health
providers.description: Valera Health is a Brooklyn, New York based virtual behavioral health provider delivering therapy, psychiatry, group therapy, comprehensive Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT), suicide care and youth support programs to adults and children through an in-house clinical team, a care-coordinator model and a patient mobile app. It is a care-delivery organization rather than a software vendor: revenue comes from commercial insurance, Medicaid and Medicare reimbursement, and the clinical record and patient portal run on third-party health IT (the patient portal is operated by NextGen Healthcare at pxpportal.nextgen.com). As of this profile Valera Health publishes no developer program, no public API reference, and no machine-readable contract of any kind; its only externally addressable API host, api.valerahealth.com, is the private backend for its own patient application.

providers.name: Volt
providers.description: Volt is a desktop application (Mac, Windows, and Chrome) that supercharges WhatsApp for professionals and sales teams — turning long voice notes into readable transcripts and summaries, scheduling messages, adding keyboard-first navigation, organizing chats into focused workspaces, and sending personalized broadcasts. Message content stays under WhatsApp's end-to-end encryption and never passes through Volt's own servers. For agents and AI models, Volt runs an authenticated remote Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that exposes WhatsApp contacts, chats, messages, groups, and lists as tools. Volt is backed by 500 Global, EQT Ventures, and IVP.

providers.name: VuMedi
providers.description: VuMedi (Vumedi, Inc.) operates a video education platform for physicians and other healthcare professionals. Founded in 2008 and headquartered in Oakland, California, with offices in Saint Louis Park, Minnesota and Zagreb, Croatia, the platform aggregates a library of long-form educational videos, webinars, conference coverage and case discussions contributed by key opinion leaders and academic medical centers across more than twenty-five clinical specialties. Physicians use it to watch surgical technique videos, follow live and on-demand webinars, discuss cases with peers and presenters, and stay current on clinical evidence. The company monetizes through industry partnerships with pharmaceutical and medical-device brands rather than a subscription paywall. As of August 2026 VuMedi publishes no public developer program, API documentation, machine-readable API contract, SDKs or MCP server; its public surface is the consumer web application, an iOS app, and a set of static marketing and policy pages.

providers.name: Wonder Workshop
providers.description: Wonder Workshop (GitHub org "playi", originally Play-i) is an educational technology company that makes the Dash, Dot, and Cue programmable robots and the Make Wonder K-8 coding and robotics learning platform, used by more than 40,000 schools across 65 countries. Its developer surface is a set of official SDKs that give granular realtime control of the physical robots' sensors and actuators over Bluetooth Low Energy: WonderPy (Python, on PyPI), @wonderworkshop/wwjs (JavaScript, on npm), and an iOS/Android robot framework shipped in the playground sample-app repository. There is no HTTP/cloud REST API, OAuth, or webhook surface; integration happens locally over BLE. Backed by GV.

providers.name: Workwell Technologies
providers.description: Workwell Technologies, Inc. is a Carlsbad, California workforce management company backed by Battery Ventures, best known for its uAttend cloud-connected time and attendance platform and uPunch punch clocks. uAttend pairs biometric time clocks (fingerprint, facial recognition, RFID, voice control) with cloud software for time tracking, scheduling, overtime alerts, and optional payroll processing for small businesses. The WorkWell Technologies API exposes employee, timecard, and punch data from uAttend accounts over HTTPS with API-key authentication, supporting payroll and HRIS integrations.

providers.name: Ximplifi
providers.description: Ximplifi provides specialized accounting, tax, and financial services tailored for short-term vacation rental property managers. Leveraging automated bookkeeping, revenue tracking, and compliance tools, Ximplifi helps owners and managers streamline their finances, reduce manual effort, and stay audit‑ready. The firm serves U.S. vacation rental businesses, integrating with popular platforms to deliver accurate reporting, tax filing assistance, and actionable insights for growth.

providers.name: aceRNA Technologies
providers.description: aceRNA Technologies Co., Ltd. is a Japanese biotechnology venture founded in April 2018 to commercialize the RNA design technology ("RNA Switch") developed in the synthetic RNA biology laboratory of Prof. Hirohide Saito at Kyoto University. An RNA Switch is embedded into a messenger RNA so that expression of the therapeutic transgene is gated by the activity of a specific microRNA inside the cell, letting a treatment act only on the cell type and cell state that is diseased. The company applies the platform across mRNA medicines, cell therapy and gene therapy, co-develops with partners (an agreement with Nitto Denko was announced in December 2021), and closed a JPY 960M Series B in May 2024 led by DCI Partners. It is headquartered at the University of Tokyo Entrepreneur Plaza. aceRNA runs no developer programme and publishes no API reference, OpenAPI or SDK; the only machine-readable surfaces on its domain are the Wix-platform llms.txt and Site MCP endpoint, both captured here.

providers.name: ADOR Diagnostics
providers.description: ADOR Diagnostics is an in-vitro diagnostics (IVD) company developing syndromic multiplex molecular diagnostics for infectious disease, headquartered in Guidonia Montecelio, Italy with operations in Israel and Cyprus. Its NATlab platform pairs a bench-top modular analyser with a disposable all-included microfluidic cartridge to run fully automated sample-to-answer testing of crude clinical specimens in roughly 30-60 minutes, detecting up to 100 multiplexed targets per sample. The assay chemistry is a patented isothermal rolling circle amplification (RCA) protocol read by a proprietary carbon array sensor embedded in the cartridge, rather than PCR, and the system is aimed at small and mid-sized laboratories, doctor offices, point-of-care and near-bed testing, rural labs and mobile care units. The company markets an optional connectivity feature linking NATlab units across sites for geographic mapping of results and outbreak detection, but publishes no technical documentation for it. ADOR is a diagnostics instrument and assay manufacturer, not a software vendor: it operates no developer program, publishes no public API, SDK or machine-readable API contract, and the only machine-readable surfaces on its own host are an llms.txt and the Wix-platform site MCP endpoint that llms.txt advertises.

providers.name: AppBoard
providers.description: AppBoard is a free product discovery platform that helps creators launch, rank, and grow their software through community engagement. It offers a REST API for product discovery, allowing searches, trending data, and category vocabularies. The service provides free API keys, rate limits, and aims to surface great software without gatekeepers.

providers.name: AppTail
providers.description: AppTail provides mobile app analytics, market intelligence, and ASO tools to help developers and marketers understand app performance, track competitor metrics, and optimize app store visibility. The platform offers comprehensive dashboards, AI‑generated recommendations, and real‑time data on downloads, revenue, and user engagement across iOS and Android ecosystems.

providers.name: ASR Memory
providers.description: ASR Memory provides an MCP memory server that lets multiple AI tools share a common memory store. Users can save up to 1,000 memories for free, enabling AI agents to retain context across sessions. The platform offers API keys, a dashboard, and supports tools like Claude, Codex, and Gemini. It emphasizes privacy, with raw content stored and optional summaries for search.

providers.name: Astral
providers.description: Astral (Astral Software Inc.) builds high-performance developer tools for the Python ecosystem, written in Rust. Its products are uv, an extremely fast Python package and project manager that replaces pip, pip-tools, pipx, poetry, pyenv, twine, and virtualenv; Ruff, an extremely fast Python linter and code formatter; and ty, a fast Python type checker and language server. Founded by Charlie Marsh (creator of Ruff) and backed by Accel, Caffeinated Capital, and angel investor Guillermo Rauch, Astral ships open-source command-line tooling distributed via PyPI, crates.io, npm, and Homebrew. In March 2026 Astral agreed to join OpenAI as part of the Codex team.

providers.name: Atria
providers.description: Atria provides site intelligence for teams and AI, offering AI‑driven analysis of land acquisition, zoning, permitting, and feasibility studies across the United States. Their platform scores sites, aggregates parcel data, and enables agents to query the Atria MCP server for detailed insights, supporting developers, consultants, and government agencies in making data‑informed decisions.

providers.name: AutoNation
providers.description: AutoNation is the largest automotive retailer in the United States, operating over 250 new and used vehicle franchises along with collision centers, parts and service operations, and AutoNation USA used-vehicle stores. The company sells vehicles across most major OEM brands and provides digital retail, financing, and service scheduling capabilities through its website and mobile applications.

providers.name: Ava
providers.description: Ava is a consumer financial-technology company that helps people build credit and reduce the cost of debt. Its products include the Ava Credit Builder Mastercard (a no-interest card usable at approved subscription merchants), a Save & Build secured savings loan, and rent and utility payment reporting to the three major U.S. credit bureaus (TransUnion, Equifax, Experian). Ava operates as a mobile app on a subscription model and partners with regulated banks and lenders (including Patriot Bank, N.A. and Pier Lending) to deliver its products. This profile was surfaced as a Greylock portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Ava is a consumer app and does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Bevel
providers.description: Bevel is a consumer digital-health application, built by Finerpoint, Inc., that acts as an AI-powered "connected health coach." It consolidates and interprets health data from wearables (Apple Watch, Oura, Garmin, Amazfit) and lab providers (Labcorp, Quest, LifeLabs) into a single view, scoring daily strain, sleep, recovery, stress/energy, nutrition, cycle, biological age and strength training. Its "Bevel Intelligence" layer delivers conversational, research-backed guidance, personalized workout plans and daily check-ins. Bevel is a mobile-first consumer product with no publicly documented developer API; this profile captures its public web, support, roadmap and legal surface. Backed by General Catalyst.

providers.name: Burlington Stores
providers.description: Burlington Stores, Inc. (NYSE: BURL) is a US national off-price department store retailer offering brand-name clothing, footwear, accessories, baby products and home decor at everyday low prices across more than 1,200 stores. Burlington operates no public developer program: no OpenAPI, GraphQL, gRPC, SOAP or event contract is served on any host it controls. Its one documented machine-to-machine surface is ASC X12 version 4010 EDI for merchandise vendors and freight carriers, and unusually for a retailer of this size the implementation guides are fully public — seventeen transaction-set PDFs plus a GS1-128 shipping label companion report, readable without a login at burlington.com/vendors/edi. The runtime behind them, the Gateway Vendor Management Suite, is invite-only.

providers.name: Carecloud
providers.description: CareCloud (NASDAQ: CCLD, formerly MTBC) is a cloud-based healthcare technology company serving 45,000+ providers with an integrated platform spanning electronic health records (EHR), practice management, revenue cycle management (RCM), patient experience tools, and AI-driven clinical documentation (cirrusAI). Its Connector product delivers healthcare interoperability with FHIR and C-CDA data exchange across labs, EHRs, immunization registries, and diagnostics. CareCloud is Drummond-certified ONC Health IT and Surescripts-certified, publishes HIPAA compliance content, and operates a developer portal (AWS API Gateway) at developer.carecloud.com. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners and enriched in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Carputty
providers.description: Carputty provides flexible auto financing solutions, offering consumers real-time, transparent lines of credit for vehicle purchases. Their platform enables users to pre‑qualify for loans without impacting credit scores, choose financing terms, and manage the process online. Carputty aims to simplify car ownership by delivering clear, fast, and user‑friendly financing options, backed by proprietary valuation tools and a mission to rewrite industry rules.

providers.name: Certa
providers.description: Certa (operated by Opinr, Inc. d/b/a Certa) is an AI-native third-party risk management (TPRM) and compliance platform that unifies the full third-party lifecycle — onboarding, due diligence, contract management, continuous compliance monitoring, and offboarding — in a single no-code system. Founded by Jag Lamba and headquartered in Saratoga, CA, Certa serves Fortune 500 companies (Honeywell, Uber, Mars, Box, Quantcast) across 120+ countries and 17 languages. The platform covers all risk domains — operational and resilience, infosec and cyber, compliance and legal, financial and credit, reputational, geopolitical, and ESG and ethical risk — via its Studio no-code process designer, Certa Connect (130+ native integrations), and embedded AI agents. Certa was named a Leader in the inaugural 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Third-Party Risk Management Tools. External integration is available through an enterprise external API surfaced from the platform; no public OpenAPI or developer portal is published as of this profile.

providers.name: Chefaa
providers.description: Chefaa is Egypt's leading digital pharmacy and pharmacy-benefits platform, founded in 2017 and headquartered in Cairo. Its GPS-enabled, AI-powered consumer app connects more than 1.5 million monthly users with a nationwide network of over 1,500 partner pharmacies, letting patients upload, order, schedule, and refill both insured and non-insured prescriptions with home delivery, medication reminders, and pharmacist chat support. On the B2B side Chefaa operates a full-stack supply layer for pharmacies and corporates — including Chefaa Supply (direct procurement with deferred payment and consolidated delivery) and the Makhazen pharmacy-supply app — plus the Chefaa Prime subscription for SMEs and consumers. Chefaa is a 500 Global portfolio company. This profile is maintained by the API Evangelist network; Chefaa publishes consumer and B2B web/mobile products but does not expose a public developer API program, so the enrichment below is limited to its public web, security, and domain surface.

providers.name: Clockspring
providers.description: Clockspring is a technology company specializing in precision timing components and synchronization solutions for industrial automation, robotics, and consumer electronics. Founded to address the growing demand for reliable, high-performance clock mechanisms, Clockspring offers a suite of APIs that enable developers to integrate real-time timing data, device health monitoring, and predictive maintenance capabilities into their applications. The company emphasizes robust security, extensive documentation, and developer-friendly tools to accelerate integration and foster innovation across sectors.

providers.name: Comply365
providers.description: Comply365 is an enterprise SaaS provider of operational content, safety, and training management software for highly regulated, safety-critical industries including airlines, defense, rail, and MRO (maintenance, repair, and overhaul). Its AI-powered platform unifies three mission-critical products: ContentManager365 for authoring, managing, and distributing controlled operational documentation and manuals; SafetyManager365 for safety reporting, investigation, and root-cause analysis; and TrainingManager365 for workforce readiness and compliance training. Comply365 helps regulated operators shorten document change cycles, maintain regulatory compliance, and connect frontline teams to the current, approved content they need. The company is an Insight Partners portfolio company and is an ISO 27001 and ISO 9001 certified organization.

providers.name: Crossover
providers.description: Crossover is a global recruitment platform that connects top 1% talent with AI‑first remote full‑time job opportunities. It offers a sophisticated matching system, productivity monitoring tools like WorkSmart, and serves over 70 leading tech companies. The service includes hiring solutions for enterprises and career resources for job seekers, positioning Crossover as a leading marketplace for remote work.

providers.name: dearovo-com
providers.description: dearovo-com is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: mcp-registry) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.

providers.name: Deblock
providers.description: Deblock is a fintech company offering a hybrid financial app that combines a fully licensed current account with a French IBAN and a Visa debit card alongside a self-custodial (non-custodial) crypto wallet, so customers hold their own private keys while spending fiat and crypto in everyday life. Founded by former Revolut and Ledger team members and registered with France's AMF as a digital-asset service provider, Deblock lets users buy, sell and swap crypto through an integrated exchange, earn interest on their current account balance, and round spare change up into Bitcoin. Its consumer product is delivered as a mobile app under the tagline "Own Your Money"; Deblock does not currently publish a public developer API, portal, or documentation. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network from the Speedinvest venture portfolio.

providers.name: Donuts
providers.description: Donuts (now operating as Identity Digital, following the 2022 merger of Donuts Inc. and Afilias) runs the world's largest portfolio of new generic top-level domains (gTLDs) — more than 280 extensions such as .email, .guru, .social, .live, and .restaurant. As a wholesale domain registry it provides DNS infrastructure, domain-name security, premium-domain services, and rights-protection tooling to the accredited registrars and resellers who sell domains to end customers. Its programmatic surface is registry-oriented and partner-facing: an EPP (Extensible Provisioning Protocol) interface for domain provisioning, a HTTP Reports API that delivers weekly domain and billing report files (CSV.gz over HTTP basic auth), and a Registrar Portal. There is no public REST/OpenAPI developer surface.

providers.name: Easol
providers.description: Easol is an experience commerce platform for creators of festivals, adventure and travel operators, entertainment venues, and multi-day events. Its all-in-one system combines a branded website builder, booking and ticketing, packages and upsells, global payments and on-site POS, marketing and CRM, operations analytics, AI support agents, and creator capital/funding, letting experience businesses move beyond rigid legacy ticketing systems and sell and scale on their own platform. Plans range from Easol Stride (from $250/month) to a custom-priced Easol Pro tier. Easol does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal; this profile captures its public commercial, support, security, and status surfaces, and is backed by Tiger Global.

providers.name: Genesis AI
providers.description: Genesis AI is a physical-AI company building a universal robotics foundation model and a full-stack platform for general-purpose robots. Founded in 2024 by Zhou Xian and Théophile Gervet, it emerged from stealth in July 2025 with $105M in seed funding from Eclipse, Khosla Ventures, Bpifrance, HSG, Eric Schmidt, and Xavier Niel. Its stack spans the GENE vision-language-action foundation model (GENE-26.5), the Eno general-purpose robot, and Genesis World, a multi-physics simulation platform that generates synthetic training data and is developed in the open as the `genesis-world` Python package. The company is pre-product with customer deployments targeted for the end of 2026; its primary public developer surface today is the open-source Genesis simulation stack on PyPI, GitHub, and Read the Docs rather than a hosted web API.

providers.name: Gradescope
providers.description: Gradescope, a Turnitin company, is an assessment and grading platform for paper-based, digital, and code assignments used across higher education and K-12. It does not publish a generally available public REST API; programmatic integration is delivered through LTI 1.3 / LTI Advantage (roster and grade sync with Canvas, Blackboard, Brightspace/D2L, Moodle, and Sakai) and a documented autograder framework for code assignments. A first-party public API for courses, assignments, submissions, and grades is a published feature request but is not yet generally available.

providers.name: Hawthorne
providers.description: Hawthorne is an internet-first men's personal care and grooming brand founded in 2016 in New York City (a Techstars alum, later Series B). It sells personalized, long-lasting fragrance and grooming products — cologne, deodorant, body wash, face and hair care — tuned to a customer's body chemistry and lifestyle through an onboarding quiz and a smart-subscription model built around its "Surround Scent" technology. The direct-to-consumer storefront at hawthorne.co runs on Shopify and exposes a modern agent-commerce surface: a published /llms.txt and /agents.md, Shopify Customer Account OpenID Connect discovery, and a live Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) MCP endpoint so AI shopping agents can search the catalog, build a cart, and complete a buyer-approved checkout.

providers.name: HubSync
providers.description: HubSync is an AI-powered, end-to-end tax and accounting workflow platform built for CPA firms, founded in 2019 by John McGowan and headquartered in Franklin, Tennessee. The SaaS platform unifies the engagement lifecycle in one interface: engagement letter generation and tracking, tax organizers and prepared-by-client data collection, document management, e-signature (including IRS Form 8879), batch federal and state extensions, tax return breakup and delivery, e-file status tracking, web-based tax workpapers, firm analytics dashboards, and integrated bill-and-pay. Its HubSync Halo layer adds agentic AI orchestration across those stages. HubSync publishes an llms.txt and states that it ships a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server and bi-directional API integrations with CCH Axcess/ProSystem fx, Thomson Reuters GoSystem/UltraTax and SurePrep, but it publishes no public developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI description or endpoint documentation — the entire integration surface is provisioned per customer firm.

providers.name: iwebdevelopment-com
providers.description: iWebDevelopment, trading as Codex Connectors B.V., provides a platform that automates bookkeeping by integrating with major accounting systems (Exact Online, AFAS, Twinfield, Multivers) and e‑commerce platforms (WooCommerce, Shopify, Magento, Lightspeed, CCV Shop, Prestashop, Shopware, Amazon, Bol). The service offers AI‑driven assistants, real‑time financial insights, and a suite of modules for payments, tax validation, currency conversion, and CRM integration, all built on ISO‑27001 certified infrastructure.

providers.name: Jellyfish
providers.description: Jellyfish is a software engineering intelligence (SEI) platform that turns data from developer tools — issue trackers (Jira, Linear, Azure Boards), source control and CI/CD (GitHub, Azure DevOps), and AI coding assistants (Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Amazon Q, Gemini Code Assist) — into productivity and business-impact insights for R&D leaders. The platform measures AI adoption, engineering allocation, and delivery across the software development lifecycle through a Data Hub, extensible dashboards, and AI-assisted custom queries. Jellyfish is an enterprise, demo-gated product with no public self-service API; data access is delivered through the product and its integrations rather than a documented developer API. Backed by Accel, Insight Partners, and Wing Venture Capital.

providers.name: Koloma
providers.description: Koloma is a Denver, Colorado based natural (geologic) hydrogen exploration and production company founded in 2021 by Pete Johnson and Tom Darrah, PhD, with a research laboratory in Columbus, Ohio. The company applies subsurface geoscience, proprietary data and data-driven exploration methods — airborne geophysics, passive acoustic and magnetotelluric surveys, and lab characterization of rock, liquid and gas samples — to locate and produce naturally occurring hydrogen generated by serpentinization deep within the Earth. Koloma operates in the United States and internationally, including Koloma Australia and exploration operations in the Philippines, and is backed by Amazon Climate Pledge Fund, Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Khosla Ventures, Mitsubishi Heavy Industries and United Airlines. Koloma publishes no public developer platform, API documentation or SDKs; its only machine-readable agent surface found in this pass is a Wix-platform Model Context Protocol endpoint plus an llms.txt served from the Koloma California regional site.

providers.name: lastlookdata-com
providers.description: LastLook Data provides financial market data APIs tailored for AI agents, offering real-time treasury yields, mortgage rates, foreign exchange, macro indicators, cryptocurrency prices, and company fundamentals. Access is managed via x402 micropayments on Base, eliminating the need for API keys, subscriptions, or minimum usage requirements. The service delivers up-to-date data sourced from FRED and other providers, enabling agents to integrate financial insights directly into their workflows without friction.

providers.name: LetMeShip
providers.description: LetMeShip provides a B2B shipping platform that simplifies multi‑carrier shipping, customs, and logistics for European businesses. Their Shipping API enables developers to integrate rate calculation, label generation, and shipment tracking across numerous carriers, supporting parcel, document, and pallet shipments both domestically and internationally.

providers.name: Meal Ticket
providers.description: Meal Ticket provides an end‑to‑end profitability management platform for foodservice distributors, suppliers, and restaurants. Their TrackMax+ solution helps businesses optimize pricing, rebates, and margins across the supply chain, delivering real‑time analytics and actionable insights to improve financial performance.

providers.name: Mosaic
providers.description: Mosaic is a North American brand experience agency with global reach, and one of the pillar agencies of Acosta Group. It works across four service lines — experiential marketing, B2B corporate experiences and events, integrated commerce and shopper programs, and field sales and marketing — plus third-party labor, assisted selling, retail merchandising, sales training, retail execution and surge staffing for retail, B2B and CPG environments. With roots in Toronto and Dallas and offices in Jacksonville, Mosaic says it has spent more than 35 years building brand experiences designed to drive awareness, engagement, conversion and behaviour change. Mosaic publishes no developer program, API documentation or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: NeuroFlow
providers.description: NeuroFlow is a Philadelphia-based behavioral health technology company that gives payers, health systems, provider groups and federal agencies the infrastructure to identify and manage behavioral health risk at scale. Its IntegrateBH platform pairs patient-facing mobile and web applications with measurement-based care and screening workflows, clinical dashboards, care-coordination tooling and population-level behavioral health analytics. The platform reaches customers through EHR and partner integrations — including Epic (App Orchard / Epic Showroom) and the Xealth digital-health ecosystem — over a session-authenticated REST API served from neuroflowlive.com/api/. NeuroFlow publishes no public developer portal: a Swagger document exists at /api/swagger.json on every environment, but it returns HTTP 401 "Please log in to continue" to anonymous callers, so the contract is customer-only.

providers.name: Pretto
providers.description: Pretto is a French online mortgage brokerage (courtier en credit immobilier) operated by FINSPOT SAS, founded in 2016 and headquartered in Paris. It runs a digital platform that lets borrowers simulate a home loan, compare rates across more than 125 partner banks, assemble a financing file and be accompanied by a human credit expert through to signature, and it publishes a transparent, non-negotiable fee schedule instead of the bank-funded commission model used by most French brokers. Pretto also operates Pretto Galaxie, a B2B network that opens the same technology stack — semi-automated file assembly, an embeddable loan simulator, a client portal, a commission dashboard and a back-office service — to independent brokers, and Pretto Search, a consumer property-search product priced against real borrowing capacity. FINSPOT is registered with ORIAS (17000916) as a banking/payment-services and insurance broker and is supervised by the ACPR. As of this pass Pretto publishes no public developer program: the api.pretto.fr host serves its API reference behind HTTP Basic auth and the developers.pretto.fr ReadMe hub is deactivated.

providers.name: RemoteLock
providers.description: RemoteLock provides a cloud-based smart access control platform that enables property owners and managers to control doors, locks, and credentials across multifamily, vacation rentals, and commercial properties. Their API allows developers to integrate lock management, schedule access, and receive real-time events via webhooks, supporting a wide range of hardware and software integrations.

providers.name: Ridecell
providers.description: Ridecell is an AI-powered asset intelligence and orchestration platform for automotive leasing, fleet, and finance companies. Its five intelligence modules (Client, Spend, Supplier, Asset, and Operational Intelligence) and the "Maya" AI agent monitor fleets, flag invoice overcharges, track garage/supplier performance, optimize vehicle remarketing and residual value, and resolve idle-vehicle inefficiencies. The platform processes 12M+ events daily across 500K+ assets, 100+ connected systems, and 14+ countries. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Initialized Capital. Ridecell does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDK; this profile captures its public information, security, and compliance surfaces.

providers.name: Sensel
providers.description: Sensel is a Sunnyvale, California touch-input company founded in 2013 by Ilya Rosenberg and Aaron Zarraga, building high-resolution force-sensing hardware — the Morph pressure-sensitive input device and the force-sensing touchpad technology shipped in laptops such as Lenovo's ThinkPad X1 Titanium Yoga. Its developer surface is not a web API: the Sensel API is an open-source, MIT-licensed C library (LibSensel) that talks to Sensel devices over USB/serial, published at github.com/sensel/sensel-api with C, C#, Python, Arduino, Processing, Max and Pure Data bindings and documented at guide.sensel.com. Sensel's intellectual property, physical assets and trademarks were acquired by Cirque Corporation (an Alps Alpine company), and sensel.com now 301-redirects to cirque.com/sensel.

providers.name: Speak
providers.description: Speak (Speakeasy Labs, Inc.) is an AI-powered language learning application focused on spoken fluency rather than grammar drills or vocabulary memorization. Its proprietary "Speak Method" has learners study real phrases, practice them across contexts, and then apply them in back-and-forth conversation with an AI tutor that gives real-time pronunciation and fluency feedback. Speak teaches Spanish, French, Korean, Japanese, Italian, German, and Chinese, plus English for non-English speakers, and offers B2B language training for organizations across Korea, Japan, Spain, Taiwan, and France. The company is backed by Accel and the OpenAI Startup Fund and partners with OpenAI. Speak runs a production application backend at api.usespeak.com (an OAuth2/OIDC issuer) but does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDKs; the surfaces below were discovered from the company's public well-known and llms.txt endpoints.

providers.name: Sportwey
providers.description: Sportwey is a Mexican SaaS platform that digitizes and automates the operations of sports organizations across multiple segments — tournaments and leagues, training academies, and sports facilities. It provides team management, scheduling, results and statistics, attendance and membership tracking, payments, class scheduling, court and field reservations, and referee coordination. The company reports more than 10,000 organizers and 2.3 million players using the platform, delivered through dedicated player and referee apps and a manager back office. Sportwey is a portfolio company of 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass it publishes no public API, developer portal, or API documentation.

providers.name: Tobii
providers.description: Tobii is the global leader in eye tracking and attention computing, headquartered in Danderyd, Sweden and listed on Nasdaq Stockholm. Its developer offering centers on the Tobii Pro SDK — Python (tobii-research), .NET, C and Matlab bindings for streaming gaze and eye-tracking data from Tobii's screen-based and wearable eye trackers — together with the Tobii Pro Glasses 3 API (with official g3pylib Python and .NET client SDKs) and XR / consumer game-integration developer kits. Tobii's technology serves scientific and behavioral research, UX, healthcare, XR/VR, automotive driver monitoring and PC gaming markets.

providers.name: Uhnder
providers.description: Uhnder is an Austin, Texas fabless semiconductor company founded in 2015 that designs the S80 and S81 77 GHz 4D digital imaging Radar-on-Chip (RoC) for automotive ADAS and automated mobility. Its Digital Code Modulation (DCM) approach on a 28nm RF CMOS process replaces analog FMCW radar with a software-defined sensor, and each RoC ships with an ASPICE-qualified Software Development Kit carrying ready-to-integrate software APIs, on-chip user algorithm support and system tools for Tier-1 and OEM radar stacks. Uhnder is a chip supplier rather than a web-API provider: the SDK and its APIs are embedded interfaces delivered under a commercial customer relationship, and the company publishes no public developer portal, documentation host or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Venice
providers.description: Venice is an enterprise privileged access management (PAM) platform built for the AI era, delivering zero standing access across human, machine, and AI-driven identities. Founded by Rotem Lurie (CEO) and Or Vaknin (CTO) and operating out of Tel Aviv and New York, Venice discovers and controls privileged access across the enterprise and removes standing privileges entirely, so that only the right identities reach critical systems and only for the moments they should. The company emerged from stealth in February 2026 with $33M in funding led by IVP with participation from Index Ventures. As an early-stage security vendor it publishes a marketing site, blog, and a public trust center, but does not yet expose a public developer API surface.

providers.name: Vishay Intertechnology
providers.description: Vishay Intertechnology is one of the world's largest manufacturers of discrete semiconductors (diodes, rectifiers, MOSFETs, optoelectronics, selected ICs) and passive electronic components (resistors, inductors, capacitors). Vishay components are used in automotive, industrial, computing, consumer, telecommunications, military, aerospace, and medical applications. Component data is accessible via distributor APIs (Octopart/Nexar, DigiKey) and Vishay's own Parts Library (VPL) tool.

providers.name: Vulcan Technologies
providers.description: Vulcan Technologies provides AI agents for government and legal professionals. Its Justinian platform offers an AI knowledge worker tool backed by a large database of U.S. laws, regulations, court cases, fiscal data, and health information, accessible via email, Slack, and Teams. The Trajan AI concierge is a public‑facing service that automates permits, licenses, applications, and regulatory queries for businesses and citizens on government websites.

providers.name: Xpedeon
providers.description: Xpedeon is a construction-specific ERP platform from Algorithms Software Pvt Ltd (30+ years in construction software), serving general contractors, specialist contractors, housebuilders and developers, engineer-to-order manufacturers, and off-site manufacturers across the UK, India, the GCC, and the US. The cloud platform covers construction finance and accounting, job costing and CVR, contract and subcontractor management, procurement, inventory and supply chain, plant and equipment, warehouse management, HR and payroll, CRM, and a mobile app for site teams, and is ISO 27001, 27017, 27018, 27701 and SOC 2 certified. Xpedeon publishes no public API, developer portal, or integration documentation, but does publish an llms.txt. Backed by Norwest Venture Partners.

providers.name: Zip Security
providers.description: Zip Security is a cloud-based security, IT, and compliance platform that automates identity management, device management (MDM for macOS, Windows, iOS, and Android), and endpoint threat detection for small and mid-sized businesses. It unifies tools such as Microsoft Intune, Jamf, and CrowdStrike behind a single dashboard, deploying frameworks, policies, and controls that are continuously enforced to help teams reach SOC 2, HIPAA, ISO 27001, CMMC, and PCI readiness, often within two weeks. Zip Security is backed by General Catalyst. This profile currently exposes no public developer API; it is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile.

providers.name: Zone & Company
providers.description: Zone & Co (Zone & Company) is a NetSuite-native financial operations software vendor whose SuiteApp suite automates the back office across five product families - Quote to Cash (ZoneBilling billing and revenue recognition, ZonePayments Stripe integration), Procure to Pay (ZoneProcure, ZoneCapture, ZoneApprovals), Treasury (ZoneLiquidity cash forecasting, ZoneReconcile), Payroll Management (ZonePayroll, Employee Portal), and Record to Report (ZoneReporting on Power BI, Data Warehouse, ZoneExtract, Solution 7). The products are delivered as native Oracle NetSuite SuiteApps distributed through the SuiteApp Marketplace rather than as a standalone public developer API. Backed by Insight Partners.

providers.name: 4DReplay
providers.description: 4DReplay is a media technology company that builds multi-camera, time-slice ("bullet-time") video capture and replay systems for live sports, entertainment and events. Arrays of roughly 50 to 120 synchronized cameras — locked to within 1/10,000 of a second — are processed in real time to produce any-angle replay highlights within seconds of a play and deliver them to broadcast, mobile and OTT audiences. The product line spans 4DReplay (premium broadcast instant replay), 4DReplay+ / 4DLive (5G-based interactive multi-view live streaming with speed, angle and tracking overlays), and 4Dist, a browser-based interactive OTT platform that adds automated AI motion and swing analysis for academies, coaches and players. Founded in 2012 by Hongsu Jung and headquartered in San Mateo, California, with offices in Seoul and Tokyo, the company has worked with ESPN, NBC, CBS, FOX Sports, the NBA, MLB, NHL, the PGA Championship and the Olympics. As of August 2026 4DReplay publishes no public developer API, SDK, or machine-readable API contract; its surfaces are broadcast integrations and the consumer/operator 4Dist web and mobile apps.

providers.name: Advise Insurance
providers.description: Advise Insurance is the Medicare distribution business of Advise Health Holdings, a Bloomington, Indiana company founded in 2018 by Sherman Rogers that raised a $100M growth round led by Oak HC/FT in March 2021. It operates as a Medicare concierge agency — unbiased plan comparison and enrollment help for seniors, plus managed-care growth support for physician practices — and its operating brand today is Bloom (bloomthrives.com), the Medicare telesales, quoting, enrollment and health-activation business Rogers launched in 2007. Bloom sells the Ascend platform (Ascend Quote & Enroll, Ascend Broker, Health Activations) to national and regional health plans on a white-label basis. As of 2026-09-09 the company publishes no developer portal, no API documentation and no machine-readable API contract; adviseinsurance.com no longer serves a site of its own and resolves into the bloomthrives.com WordPress multisite.

providers.name: AgentNX
providers.description: AgentNX provides AI-driven voice agents for enterprise and government operations, offering pilot-first pricing, secure data handling, and customizable workflows. Their platform demonstrates controlled demos, integrates with Deepgram for transcription, and supports regulated environments with FedRAMP path and NIST mapping.

providers.name: Amazon Music
providers.description: Amazon Music is a streaming service offering on-demand music, playlists, and podcasts. It integrates with Amazon devices and provides a catalog of millions of songs, personalized stations, and offline listening. The service is part of Amazon’s ecosystem, available via web, mobile apps, and Alexa-enabled devices, and supports subscription tiers for ad‑free listening and high‑fidelity audio.

providers.name: AppGoblin
providers.description: AppGoblin provides free and paid mobile app marketing tools, offering B2B intelligence on app rankings, SDK usage, ad creatives, and growth trends. Their platform lets users track install estimates, monitor keyword performance, analyze SDK stacks across millions of Android and iOS apps, and access detailed reports on ad networks and product analytics. Targeted at app marketers, ASO teams, and competitor researchers, AppGoblin delivers real‑time insights, data exports, and customizable dashboards to inform acquisition strategies and market analysis.

providers.name: AppScreenshots
providers.description: AppScreenshots provides a free, easy‑to‑use online editor for creating app store screenshots and mockups. Users can upload app captures, apply device frames, backgrounds, multi‑language support and AI‑assisted layouts, then export PNGs or ZIPs. The service supports iOS App Store, Google Play, Huawei AppGallery and Chrome Web Store, offering free core editing with paid plans for batch translation, AI workflows and premium templates. It targets developers and designers needing quick, professional‑looking store listings.

providers.name: Armadaai
providers.description: Armada.ai provides edge computing solutions with hardware and software platforms such as Leviathan, Galleon, Atlas, Bridge, and Marketplace. The company builds ruggedized mobile data centers and GPU‑as‑a‑service offerings for industries including oil & gas, defense, public sector, manufacturing, mining, and telecommunications. Their products enable scalable AI workloads at the edge, combining high‑performance compute with remote monitoring and management.

providers.name: Armorcodeinc
providers.description: ArmorCode is the independent control plane where AI agents help find, prioritize, and fix vulnerabilities across apps, cloud, infra, and AI. It offers a unified exposure management platform integrating risk graphs, agentic workflows, and compliance tools for enterprises.

providers.name: ArtifactBridge
providers.description: ArtifactBridge provides an AI‑driven collaborative platform where agents propose changes to governed documents and human reviewers approve them, ensuring attribution, version history, and secure management of shared knowledge across teams. The service integrates with tools like Claude, ChatGPT, and Codex, offering a unified library for documents, skills, and AI‑generated proposals, all governed by robust security and compliance policies.

providers.name: Axion
providers.description: Axion (formerly Axion Ray) is an AI platform for manufacturing quality intelligence that helps global manufacturers detect, diagnose, and resolve product quality and warranty issues faster. It unifies customer, service, field, and telematics data to deliver early problem detection, root-cause analysis, and improvement tracking, reducing warranty costs and investigation time. Customers include Daikin, Harley-Davidson, SharkNinja, Cummins, and Schneider Electric. Founded by Daniel First, Axion has raised Series A (led by Bessemer Venture Partners) and Series B (led by Salesforce Ventures). Axion is an enterprise SaaS product with no publicly documented API or developer platform at this time; this profile captures its company identity, legal, and security/compliance surface.

providers.name: Blooming Health
providers.description: Blooming Health is an AI-powered, omnichannel care-management and community-engagement platform for healthcare and social-services organizations.
