The company serves more than 52,000 Canadian organizations — including Sun Life, National Bank of Canada, Via Rail, Lightspeed, and Samsung — connecting employees and their families with multidisciplinary care teams of nurses, physicians, and mental health specialists. Dialogue is a consumer-facing digital health application; it does not currently publish a public developer API or OpenAPI surface.

providers.name: DivvyDiary
providers.description: DivvyDiary provides a personal dividend calendar platform that helps investors track current and future dividend payments across global stocks and ETFs. Users can create portfolios, receive notifications, and visualize cash flow, while the service offers extensive data on dividend dates, amounts, and yields. The platform includes features such as calendar export, mobile alerts, and integration with financial tools, aiming to strengthen shareholder culture through transparent dividend tracking.

providers.name: Double the Donation
providers.description: Double the Donation provides a platform that simplifies corporate matching gifts, volunteer grants, and payroll giving for nonprofits. Their service automates the collection, verification, and submission of matching gift requests, helping organizations increase donor contributions and streamline compliance. The company offers integrations with major fundraising and CRM tools, a searchable matching gift database, and resources such as guides, webinars, and case studies to educate nonprofits on maximizing corporate giving opportunities.

providers.name: Dragonfly
providers.description: Dragonfly is a modern in-memory datastore built for performance and scalability, designed as a drop-in replacement for Redis and Memcached with improved efficiency and throughput. Dragonfly uses a multi-threaded, shared-nothing architecture to deliver significantly higher throughput with lower latency than Redis. It is fully compatible with Redis and Memcached APIs, requiring no code changes to migrate existing workloads.

providers.name: drobek
providers.description: drobek is an open-source, self‑hosted vibe‑coding hosting platform that lets AI agents build small web apps directly via its MCP. Users can connect Claude Code, Cursor, or Codex, write files, preview builds, and publish apps. The service offers a hosted instance at drobek.app and a fully open‑source core under AGPL‑3.0 for self‑hosting, with documentation, API keys, and integration guides for agents.

providers.name: earmarkIQ
providers.description: earmarkIQ is an AI‑powered budgeting application targeting UK professionals. It connects to all major UK bank accounts, providing a personal money coach that tracks spending, suggests bill switches, and helps users meet savings goals. The app is free to download on iOS and offers insights to optimise cash flow, aiming to simplify financial management for busy professionals.

providers.name: Farmers Business Network
providers.description: Farmers Business Network (FBN) is a farmer-to-farmer ag-tech network serving 117,000+ member farms across the U.S. and Canada. Its membership platform pairs the FBN Direct inputs marketplace with seed and farm analytics, crop marketing, agricultural financing, and Norm, an AI agronomy advisor. FBN exposes these as member-facing web and mobile product surfaces; it does not publish a public or partner developer API.

providers.name: Games24x7
providers.description: Games24x7 is a Mumbai-headquartered Indian online skill-gaming company founded in 2006 by Bhavin Pandya and Trivikraman Thampy, operating consumer real-money and casual gaming platforms rather than a developer API business. Its portfolio spans RummyCircle (online rummy), My11Circle (fantasy cricket, football, kabaddi and ludo) and Wowzy (a three-dice ludo variant), backed by Tiger Global, The Raine Group and Malabar Investment. The company publishes engineering writing on distributed systems, Cassandra, Amazon Aurora, ksqlDB and React Native through its Resources section, runs the TechXpedite accelerator, and maintains a small public GitHub organization (games24x7-opensource) plus one first-party npm package for AI-assisted Appium test automation. As of August 2026 it publishes no developer portal, no API documentation, no machine-readable specification, and no partner or affiliate API of its own.

providers.name: Graftcode
providers.description: Graftcode (Graftcode S.A.) builds an integration-free development layer: the Graftcode Gateway (gg) exposes the public classes and methods of a service written in Python, .NET, Java, JavaScript, Go, Ruby, PHP or C++ and lets other applications install a strongly-typed client (a Graft) through their own package manager, communicating over the binary Hypertube protocol instead of REST or gRPC. The gateway also serves the Graftcode Vision explorer and automatically exposes an MCP endpoint so AI agents can call the hosted methods. Graftcode publishes no public HTTP API or OpenAPI contract of its own.

providers.name: Grailed
providers.description: Grailed is a peer-to-peer online marketplace for buying, selling, and discovering luxury, designer, vintage, and streetwear fashion for both men and women. Founded in 2013 and owned by GOAT Group, the platform lets independent sellers list clothing, footwear, accessories, and jewelry while Grailed facilitates the transaction, offering digital listing verification by trained moderators, purchase protection on qualifying orders, secure third-party payment processing (card, PayPal, Apple Pay, Klarna), and a community trust and seller-rating system. Grailed does not publish a public developer API; it exposes a consumer web and mobile experience, an agent-facing /llms.txt, and a RFC 9116 security.txt with a bug bounty program. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Index Ventures and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Intaker
providers.description: Intaker provides AI‑powered client intake software for law firms and local businesses, converting more leads with chat, texting, and automation so every inquiry is answered in seconds across every channel.

providers.name: Jobandtalent
providers.description: Jobandtalent is an AI-powered workforce marketplace that connects companies with reliable staff for temporary and permanent roles across logistics, warehousing, manufacturing, retail, and hospitality. Its platform combines a worker-facing mobile app for finding shifts and jobs with an employer-facing business platform for recruitment, shift planning, attendance management, and performance coaching. Founded in Spain and backed by Atomico, Jobandtalent operates across Europe, the US, and Latin America. This API Evangelist profile tracks the company's public developer, security, and compliance surface; the company publishes no public developer API at this time.

providers.name: Kick (kick.com)
providers.description: Kick (kick.com) is a live streaming platform that enables creators to broadcast video content to audiences worldwide. It offers features such as real-time chat, channel subscriptions, and monetization tools. Kick positions itself as a community-focused alternative to larger streaming services, emphasizing creator control and audience interaction. The platform supports a variety of content categories, including gaming, music, and talk shows, and provides resources for developers through its API and documentation.

providers.name: Kimpton AI
providers.description: Kimpton AI is an AI-native investment research platform for institutional portfolio managers at hedge funds, mutual funds, and sustainable equity funds. It ingests market data, SEC filings, 13F holdings, earnings, and a fund's own investment mandates and research documents, then generates daily trade proposals with citations grounded in the fund's actual holdings — keeping human managers in control of every final decision. The platform connects to custodians and OMS/portfolio systems (or accepts direct uploads) to sync positions and P&L, aggregates mandates and research in a document vault, and integrates market-data partners FactSet, Tiingo, Massive, and Plaid. It is a managed service for professional investors and does not currently expose a public developer API. Backed by Y Combinator.

providers.name: KITRO
providers.description: KITRO is a Swiss company founded in 2017 in Zurich that helps professional kitchens measure and reduce food waste through AI-powered automation. Its KITRO TARE device pairs an IoT scale with a camera and computer vision to automatically identify, weigh and categorize discarded food with no change to kitchen workflow, feeding a cloud analytics dashboard that surfaces waste trends by time, item and station, compares performance across properties, and exports reports for sustainability and EU food-waste compliance reporting. KITRO serves hotel groups and resorts, hospitals and care homes, corporate canteens, universities and schools, and river and ocean cruise operators in 20+ countries, with customers including Marriott, Hyatt, TUI BLUE, Pestana, 25hours Hotels and Sydney Opera Bar. KITRO publishes no public developer API, SDKs or developer portal — the only customer-facing software surface is the authenticated dashboard at my.kitro.ch — but it does publish an llms.txt agent-readable company description at www.kitro.ch/llms.txt.

providers.name: Kixeye
providers.description: KIXEYE Inc. is a video game developer and publisher founded in 2009 and headquartered in Victoria, British Columbia, with staff across Canada and the United States. KIXEYE creates, develops, and publishes massively multiplayer online real-time strategy (MMORTS) games for browsers, tablets, and smartphones, including Battle Pirates, War Commander, War Commander: Rogue Assault, and Rise of Firstborn. An early innovator in the free-to-play genre, KIXEYE operates long-lived live-service game worlds with monthly events, alliances, and competitive leaderboards for millions of players worldwide. KIXEYE is part of the Stillfront Group. KIXEYE publishes no public developer program or partner API; its api.kixeye.com host is a private game-services backend that exposes an OpenID Connect discovery document and JWKS for token verification. The company does maintain a public GitHub organization of open-source infrastructure libraries (chassis, kixmpp, janus, scout) used to build its own cloud services.

providers.name: La Trobe University
providers.description: La Trobe University is a public research university headquartered in Bundoora, Melbourne, Victoria, Australia, founded in 1964 and ranked #217 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. La Trobe operates no public, self-service API product and publishes no OpenAPI, AsyncAPI or GraphQL description of its own. Its single institution-operated API host, api.latrobe.edu.au, is an Azure API Management developer portal (CNAME ltu-api-prod-apim.developer.azure-api.net) that redirects every unauthenticated path to /signin, with no public catalogue, documentation or sign-up. Everything else that looks programmable under the La Trobe name is a vendor platform running under an institutional tenancy: the open-access repository OPAL (opal.latrobe.edu.au, CNAME figshare.com) and its alias researchdata.latrobe.edu.au are Figshare; the course handbook (handbook.latrobe.edu.au) is CourseLoop, whose backend at cf-api-ap-southeast-2.prod.courseloop.com refuses unauthenticated calls; library discovery and resource management are Ex Libris Primo and Alma; the Shibboleth identity provider at aaf.latrobe.edu.au is operated by the Australian Access Federation under La Trobe's own domain, entityID and scope. What La Trobe genuinely holds in its own name is registry identity — a DataCite membership with the DOI prefix 10.26181 over 47,824 DOIs, Crossref member 11371, ROR 01rxfrp27, and the AAF/eduGAIN SAML entity that federates its staff and students. That is the honest footprint: institutional identity and stewardship, not institutional engineering.

providers.name: Lettria
providers.description: Lettria provides advanced natural language processing APIs that extract semantic information from French text. Their services include entity extraction, sentiment analysis, relationship detection, and text classification, enabling developers to build intelligent applications such as chatbots, content moderation tools, and data analytics platforms. Lettria’s platform is designed for scalability and offers both RESTful endpoints and SDKs for multiple programming languages, supporting high-volume processing with robust performance and compliance with data privacy standards.

providers.name: Lightyear
providers.description: Lightyear operates a low‑cost investment platform that lets personal and business customers trade stocks, funds, ETFs, bonds, money‑market funds and crypto, and earn 2.46 % APY on a high‑yield Savings balance. The service is provided in the UK and across the EU, is regulated by the FCA and the Estonian Financial Supervision Authority, and uses BlackRock and J.P. Morgan custodians for asset protection.

providers.name: Mentlio
providers.description: Mentlio provides engineering intelligence and token optimization for AI workloads. Their platform measures AI usage locally, reduces token waste, and keeps prompts and source code on-device. By offering detailed insights into AI costs, performance, and ROI, Mentlio helps teams understand and control AI spend, improve efficiency, and ensure data privacy. The service includes research, documentation, and integrations, targeting enterprises seeking to optimize AI adoption and reduce operational expenses.

providers.name: Native Security
providers.description: Native Security is a cloud security control plane that unifies security posture and enforcement across AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, and OCI. The platform translates security intent expressed in natural language into enforceable architectural controls, shifting teams from reactive detection toward proactive, secure-by-design defense using built-in cloud security primitives. Capabilities include multi-cloud policy enforcement from a single definition, automated organization topology discovery and mapping, architectural segmentation and perimeter enforcement, AI-agent guardrails through architectural boundaries, and compliance automation with audit readiness. Native Security is backed by General Catalyst. As of this profile the company exposes no public developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI surface; product documentation and the application console sit behind authentication.

providers.name: Oasis Security
providers.description: Oasis Security is an enterprise Non-Human Identity Management (NHIM) and agentic access management platform that discovers, governs, and secures non-human identities — service accounts, API keys, secrets, certificates, and AI agents — across cloud and on-premises environments. The platform focuses on understanding access intent rather than static roles, enabling enterprises to adopt AI and automation securely at scale. Oasis targets enterprise security teams through a sales-led (demo-request) motion rather than a self-service developer product, and does not publish a public API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal; its product documentation is a login-gated knowledge base.

providers.name: oti-labs-com
providers.description: OTI Labs provides a Domain Intelligence API that aggregates WHOIS, DNS, SSL, subdomain enumeration, and email security data into a single REST endpoint. The service enables developers and security professionals to retrieve comprehensive domain signals in one call, supporting use cases such as threat intelligence, brand monitoring, and automated security workflows. Powered by the Osiris Technical Institute, OTI Labs offers a free tier with 1,000 requests per month and MIT-licensed source code, positioning itself as a versatile tool for AI agents and security tooling.

providers.name: OXIO
providers.description: OXIO is a Telecom-as-a-Service (TaaS) platform that lets brands, enterprises, and fintechs launch and operate their own branded mobile networks (MVNOs) through a single API, without building traditional telecom infrastructure. Its API-first platform unifies multiple carriers behind one integration and layers on no-code service creation (BrandVNO), AI-driven subscriber and network intelligence (BrandIQ), and multi-carrier connectivity (OXIO Network). Developers use OXIO's RESTful APIs and sandbox for programmatic line and subscription management, payments, fraud detection, and CRM/ERP synchronization. OXIO was surfaced as a portfolio company of Multicoin Capital (its GitHub org carries Stellar blockchain SDK forks) and enriched from its public web surface; the full developer documentation is gated behind authorized-customer access.

providers.name: Paperplane
providers.description: Paperplane is an AI sales-productivity tool (Y Combinator W23, backed by Bloomberg Beta) that automatically takes notes on sales calls and keeps a rep's CRM up to date. It connects to a team's calendar and to conversational intelligence and call-recording tools such as Gong and Chorus, transcribes and analyzes each call, then writes the results back to Salesforce — updating opportunity fields, notes, and action items so sales teams spend less time on manual CRM data entry and stay on top of their deals. The product is organized around opportunities, calls, and notes, with integrations for Google Calendar, Gong, Chorus, and Salesforce. Paperplane appears to have wound down: Y Combinator lists the company as Inactive (and now describes it as a credit risk management platform for builders' merchants, so it pivoted at least once before stopping), its marketing site presents no TLS certificate, its application host returns a Vercel 402 DEPLOYMENT_DISABLED, and its API host is an Envoy ingress that 404s every path with an empty body. Two surfaces remain live: a GitBook documentation site — which is an unfilled starter template carrying GitBook's own placeholder copy, last updated three years ago — with an llms.txt index, and a Clerk-hosted OpenID Connect identity instance at clerk.paperplane.ai that still serves real OIDC and RFC 8414 discovery documents. There is no public developer API, OpenAPI definition, SDK, MCP server, or agent card.

providers.name: Relativity Space
providers.description: Relativity Space is an aerospace manufacturer building Terran R, a reusable medium-to-heavy lift orbital launch vehicle produced with the company's proprietary Stargate metal 3D printing platform in Long Beach, CA. The company sells launch services - dedicated and rideshare payload missions to LEO and GTO - to government, commercial, and telecommunications customers. Relativity Space does not publish a public developer API; its developer-facing artifact is the Terran payload user's guide (mission integration documentation), not a programmatic interface.

providers.name: SecureLayer7
providers.description: SecureLayer7 provides penetration testing and offensive security services, offering AI‑driven autonomous pentesting, on‑premise API scanning, and comprehensive red‑team assessments. Their platform continuously monitors and attacks APIs, web applications, cloud resources, and infrastructure to uncover real‑world exploits, delivering detailed remediation reports and integrations with JIRA, Slack, and CI/CD pipelines. Trusted by fintech, SaaS, enterprise, and critical infrastructure sectors, SecureLayer7 combines over a decade of research with a modern CTEM framework to protect evolving attack surfaces.

providers.name: SecurityPal
providers.description: SecurityPal AI is a cybersecurity assurance management platform that pairs AI agents with certified human experts to automate security questionnaires, vendor risk assessments (TPRM), audit response preparation, Trust Center management, and broader GRC workflows for regulated industries including healthcare, financial services, technology, and manufacturing. The platform advertises 700+ native integrations (Salesforce, Okta, Jira, Slack, Microsoft Teams, HubSpot, Zendesk, Google Workspace, and more) and offers three service tiers (Basecamp self-serve AI, Summit AI-plus-concierge, and Everest fully managed). SecurityPal is a Craft Ventures portfolio company. No public developer API or documentation is published at this time; this profile captures the company identity, public web properties, domain-security posture, and Trust Center.

providers.name: Sprout.ai
providers.description: Sprout.ai is an AI-powered insurance claims automation platform (InsurTech) that eliminates manual work in claims processing — automating routine claim decisions while equipping handlers with smart tooling. Its layer combines document intelligence (extracting and structuring data from claims documents, reports and photos), policy validation against coverage terms, fraud and anomaly detection, and end-to-end claims resolution across Health, Life & Disability, Motor & Auto, Home & Property, and Commercial lines of business. Sprout.ai sells to insurers and enterprise partners rather than through a self-service developer program, so there is no public API, developer portal, or SDK; this profile captures the company's identity and its published security, privacy, and compliance posture.

providers.name: StorSimple
providers.description: StorSimple was a Santa Clara, California hybrid cloud storage company founded in 2009 by Ursheet Parikh and Guru Pangal. Its appliances combined primary storage, tiered cloud archiving, deduplication, compression, and encryption behind iSCSI/SMB interfaces, backed by $31.5M from Index Ventures, Redpoint Ventures, Ignition Partners, and Mayfield Fund. Microsoft acquired StorSimple in November 2012 and folded it into Azure as Azure StorSimple (8000 series physical and virtual arrays, plus the StorSimple Data Manager). The product is managed through Azure Resource Manager under the Microsoft.StorSimple resource provider and its REST API. Azure StorSimple reached end-of-life in December 2022 and is out of support; Microsoft directs customers to Azure File Sync and Azure Files.

providers.name: Topline Pro
providers.description: Topline Pro is an AI-powered business management platform for local and home service professionals in the United States — contractors, landscapers, painters, roofers, cleaners, and other owner-operated service companies. It provides AI-generated websites, local marketing and online discovery, lead capture with automated follow-up, AI-assisted customer communication, appointment and job scheduling, and invoicing with automated payment collection. Topline Pro is backed by Forerunner Ventures and Northzone. As of this enrichment pass it exposes no public developer API, SDK, gRPC, AsyncAPI, or /.well-known discovery surface; it does publish an llms.txt at its marketing domain that describes the platform for AI agents.

providers.name: TrueLook
providers.description: TrueLook provides construction site security and intelligence through high-definition cameras, AI-driven analytics, and a cloud platform that delivers live video, time-lapse documentation, PPE detection, and automated alerts. The solution integrates with construction management tools such as Procore, offering remote monitoring, incident reporting, and data-driven insights for owners, contractors, and insurers.

providers.name: Trust Token
providers.description: TrustToken, founded in San Francisco in 2017 and rebranded as Archblock in November 2022, builds infrastructure for moving institutional funds and real-world assets onto blockchain rails. The company created the TrueUSD (TUSD) stablecoin and the TrueCurrencies family, and launched TrueFi, an on-chain under-collateralized lending protocol governed by the TRU token. Today Archblock operates a marketplace and fund-tokenization platform for institutional capital at app.archblock.com, with smart contracts, audits, and bug bounty programs published through its trusttoken GitHub organization. Backed by a16z, Founders Fund, BlockTower, and Morgan Creek.

providers.name: University Startups
providers.description: University Startups is an AI-powered transition planning management platform built for special education teams. The platform helps teachers create IDEA-compliant IEP transition plans in under 10 minutes, audits plans against 11 IDEA Indicator 13 criteria in under 90 seconds, generates SMART-format IEP goals, and engages students with disabilities in building their own transition plans, alongside a college and career readiness curriculum and internship simulator. A Techstars portfolio company serving United States school districts including NYC Public Schools; no public developer API surface is published.

providers.name: Upp.
providers.description: Upp. is a technology company providing a unified platform for managing and optimizing digital experiences across multiple channels. The service offers APIs that enable developers to integrate user engagement tools, analytics, and personalization features into their applications. Backed by Bonfire Ventures, Upp. focuses on delivering scalable solutions for businesses seeking to enhance customer interactions and drive growth through data-driven insights and automation.

providers.name: uxcontinuum-com
providers.description: Continuum (uxcontinuum.com) is an AEO agency and fractional CTO service provider that partners with founders and business owners to build, ship, and maintain software products. They offer services such as MVP building, ship‑check, ship‑fix, user acquisition, sprint planning, and pricing strategy. The company emphasizes AI‑driven recommendations, continuous product support, and a senior partner model to ensure long‑term success for client ventures.

providers.name: VIPKid
providers.description: VIPKid (Beijing Dami Technology Co., Ltd. / 北京大米科技有限公司) is an online language-education company founded in 2013 that connects children with English teachers over one-to-one live video lessons, and runs a global teacher-marketplace side (VIPTeacher) alongside consumer learning brands including Lingo Bus, VIPKID AI 双师智学, VIPKID 国际教育 and the Dino parent-child reading rooms. The product is delivered entirely as consumer web and mobile apps and a teacher portal; VIPKid publishes no public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable contract of any kind.

providers.name: Yoona.ai
providers.description: Yoona.ai is an enterprise agentic-AI platform for product innovation, originally built for the fashion industry. It creates an adaptive "Enterprise Twin" of a brand by connecting PLM, ERP, e-commerce and market data into a single intelligence layer, then uses AI agents to autonomously generate product designs, optimize assortments and validate sell-through. Capabilities include text-to-image and sketch-to-design generation, trend and data analysis, and a Sales Confidence Algorithm. Integration with a customer's stack (Shopify to SAP) is offered via a flexible REST/GraphQL API, but that API is delivered as an Enterprise-tier custom integration — there is no public self-serve API, developer portal, or OpenAPI specification published as of this enrichment pass. Backed by Techstars.

providers.name: Yubi
providers.description: Yubi (formerly CredAvenue) is an Indian debt and credit technology company operating a full-stack digital marketplace that connects enterprises, lenders, and investors across India's credit ecosystem. Its product suite spans Yubi Loans for corporate borrowing, Yubi Co.Lend for bank/NBFC co-lending partnerships with one-time API integration, Yubi Pools for securitisation and ABS deal-making, Yubi Invest for fixed-income and debt investing, and Yubi Flow for supply-chain financing. Founded in 2020 and headquartered in Chennai, the company reached unicorn status in 2022 and exposes self-serve APIs for co-lending and loan-origination data exchange through its developer portal at developer.go-yubi.com. This profile was seeded from the Lightspeed Venture Partners portfolio and enriched from Yubi's public web surface.

providers.name: Zunoy
providers.description: Zunoy provides a cloud‑based platform for real‑time data integration, API management, and analytics. It enables businesses to connect, orchestrate, and monitor APIs across hybrid environments, offering features such as traffic routing, security policies, and detailed usage insights. The platform targets developers and enterprises seeking scalable API solutions with robust monitoring and governance capabilities.

providers.name: AaDya Security (Judy Security)
providers.description: AaDya Security, founded in 2019 by Raffaele Mautone and rebranded in 2023 around its product as Judy Security, sells an all-in-one AI-driven cybersecurity platform to small and midsize businesses, schools, non-profits and public-sector buyers, almost entirely through MSP and MSSP partners. The Judy platform bundles endpoint detection and response, DNS filtering, a password manager, a cloud SIEM and XDR ("Blue Team"), automated compliance management and reporting, secure and passwordless authentication, and security awareness training behind a single Control Center. The company publishes no developer program, no public API reference and no machine-readable API contract; its documented API surface is outbound only - configuration guides for pushing Judy Portal tickets into ConnectWise PSA and Datto Autotask using those vendors' APIs. It does operate a public Atlassian Statuspage for the platform.

providers.name: Aerwave
providers.description: Aerwave is a Dallas, Texas managed Wi-Fi provider founded in 2019 that builds and operates fiber-backed, property-wide wireless networks for multifamily apartment communities and student housing. Its HomeWiFi platform gives each resident a private, VLAN-isolated network with individual encryption and instant-on gigabit service without a rented router, while property owners and managers get a SaaS portal for network management, resident onboarding and support. Aerwave publishes no public developer program or API documentation; the machine-readable surface it does serve is an llms.txt and a live, anonymous Model Context Protocol endpoint on its marketing site, both provided by its Wix hosting platform.

providers.name: Agilemd
providers.description: AgileMD is a clinical decision support company that embeds real-time predictive analytics and evidence-based clinical pathways directly into hospital electronic health record (EHR) workflows such as Epic and Cerner. Its FDA-cleared eCART Clinical Deterioration Suite continuously scores patient risk from nearly 100 real-time variables — labs, vital signs, and nursing assessments — to help care teams recognize deteriorating patients earlier, while its Clinical Pathways product standardizes evidence-based order sets, documentation, and protocols across care settings. AgileMD is used across 400+ hospitals by more than 150,000 clinical users and has processed millions of patient encounters. The company is backed by Y Combinator, MATTER, and Rock Health.

providers.name: AMPAworks
providers.description: AMPAworks builds AI-powered smart-shelf inventory management for healthcare and defense supply chains. Its platform pairs computer-vision cameras and rolling kiosks that image inventory to auto-count stock in real time with software that tracks supplies 24/7, automates reordering, and gives teams live visibility to prevent stock-outs. The company reports outcomes such as $15M in cost reduction, 25,000 hours saved on hand counting, and 72% fewer stock-outs across more than 28 healthcare and operational organizations. Backed by 500 Global, AMPAworks operates from offices in Santa Monica CA, Buffalo NY, Hackensack NJ, and Ann Arbor MI.

providers.name: Assured
providers.description: Assured provides an AI‑powered platform that streamlines provider credentialing, payer enrollment, and network management for health systems, digital‑health companies, and multi‑specialty groups. The solution automates credentialing committee readiness, reduces enrollment time to under 48 hours, and offers tools such as NPI and PECOS lookup, licensing, and roster management. Backed by Kindred Ventures, Assured aims to simplify compliance and accelerate onboarding across the healthcare ecosystem.

providers.name: Autrady
providers.description: Autrady audits trading strategies. Upload the signals behind a bot, a paid newsletter or your own backtest, and Autrady tests whether they beat the market after trading costs and allowing for luck. 14 days free with no card, then €19 a month including VAT.

providers.name: Avant Arte
providers.description: Avant Arte is a global online art marketplace for discovering and collecting limited edition prints, sculptures and digital works produced in close collaboration with leading contemporary artists. Founded in the Netherlands, the platform works directly with 250+ artists on exclusive editions and release "draws", offering authentication, custom framing, gift cards, and expert collector support. It surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners and Prosus Ventures in the marketplaces sector. Avant Arte does not publish a public developer API; this profile has been enriched from its public web, security, and organizational surfaces.

providers.name: Baxus
providers.description: BAXUS is a peer-to-peer marketplace for buying, selling, trading, and storing fine and rare wine and spirits, built on the Solana blockchain. Founded in 2021 by Tzvi Wiesel and based in Woodland Park, New Jersey, BAXUS authenticates physical bottles and holds them in climate-controlled vaults, then tokenizes each as an NFT that serves as a digital certificate of ownership and provenance. Beyond the marketplace and Vault, BAXUS operates the BoozApp collection app, an open-source AI whiskey sommelier agent (BOB), and Whisky-Goggles AI bottle recognition. Its backend API at services.baxus.co powers bottle search, marketplace listings, and user bar collections. Backed by Multicoin Capital.

providers.name: Blackberry
providers.description: BlackBerry Limited is a Canadian intelligent security software and services company headquartered in Waterloo, Ontario, and listed on the NYSE and TSX as BB. Once known for its smartphones, BlackBerry today builds embedded and cybersecurity software for enterprises and governments. Its portfolio spans QNX (a real-time operating system for automotive and embedded/IoT systems), Cylance AI-driven endpoint protection, BlackBerry UEM (Unified Endpoint Management), BlackBerry AtHoc critical event management and mass notification, BlackBerry SecuSUITE secure voice and messaging, BlackBerry Workspaces secure file sharing, and the BlackBerry Dynamics secure mobility platform. Developers integrate with these products through REST APIs and SDKs, including the BlackBerry UEM Web Services REST API, the BlackBerry AtHoc API (v2, REST with OpenID Connect / OAuth 2 auth), and the BlackBerry Dynamics SDKs for iOS, Android, Cordova, and React Native. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead and enriched by the pipeline from BlackBerry's public developer surface.

providers.name: BoostedChat
providers.description: BoostedChat provides AI‑powered conversational agents that engage leads instantly on WhatsApp, Messenger and Instagram. The platform offers proactive, personalized conversations that convert, with features like automated follow‑ups, scheduling, and multi‑channel support. It aims to make every customer feel like the only one, helping businesses increase engagement and sales through intelligent chat automation.

providers.name: Brightfield
providers.description: Brightfield is an extended-workforce intelligence company whose TDX (Talent Data Exchange) and TDX AI platform give enterprises data, automation, and precision over contingent-labor and statement-of-work (SOW) spending across 100+ countries. Products include Rate Intelligence, Rate Card Manager, SOW Rate Insights, SOW Quality and Risk Analytics, Supplier Scorecard, and an ROI Dashboard, built on transaction-level data from 700+ companies and $500B+ of global spend. Founded and led by CEO Jason Ezratty and headquartered in Washington, DC, Brightfield is backed by Sapphire Ventures. The product is delivered as a login-gated SaaS application; no public developer API or documentation surface is published at this time.

providers.name: CAVA
providers.description: CAVA Group, Inc. (NYSE: CAVA) is a Washington, D.C.-headquartered Mediterranean fast-casual restaurant company that operates the CAVA brand, serving customizable bowls, pitas, salads and sides built on house-made dips, spreads and dressings. Alongside its restaurants CAVA runs a consumer packaged goods line sold in grocery stores, a digital ordering and delivery channel, a catering business at catering.cava.com, and the CAVA Rewards loyalty program delivered through its iOS and Android apps. The company listed on the New York Stock Exchange in June 2023 and reports an in-house technology program — CavaCore, its data platform, and CAVA Current, a restaurant operating system. CAVA publishes no public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable API contract; its public machine-readable surface is limited to an RFC 9116 security.txt and a published llms.txt.

providers.name: Centre for Sight
providers.description: Centre For Sight is a UK‑based private eye‑care provider offering premium laser eye surgery, cataract surgery, glaucoma treatments and a wide range of ophthalmology services across multiple locations. Established in 1996, it operates over 95 centres in the UK and internationally, delivering advanced technology and specialist care to patients. The organisation also runs a charitable trust supporting eye health initiatives.

providers.name: Chamade
providers.description: Chamade provides a voice and chat gateway for AI agents, enabling integration with meetings, phone calls, and direct messages across platforms such as Teams, Zoom, Google Meet, Discord, Telegram, Slack, WhatsApp, Nextcloud Talk, and SIP. Users can drive the service via MCP or REST APIs, attach LLM providers like OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, or Mistral, and customize audio handling with hosted STT/TTS or their own stack via WebSocket. The platform offers flexible deployment and comprehensive communication capabilities for AI-driven interactions.

providers.name: CheapCADTools
providers.description: CheapCADTools provides browser‑based parametric CAD tools for designing timing pulleys, roller‑chain sprockets, involute gears, worm gears, bevel gears and planetary gear sets. All generators are live, built to ISO, DIN and ASME standards, and output STL, STEP, DXF or SVG files for 3‑D printing or CNC cutting. The service offers a free tier with limited downloads and paid per‑download pricing, aiming to make precise gear design accessible without installing heavyweight CAD software.

providers.name: Cleanly
providers.description: Cleanly was a US-based on-demand laundry and dry-cleaning startup (backed by 500 Global and Y Combinator) that has since rebranded and now operates as ByNext at bynext.co. ByNext is an app-based, on-demand laundry, dry cleaning, and home cleaning pickup and delivery service operating 7 days a week (8am-8pm) with 24-48 hour turnaround across metro markets including New York City, New Jersey, the Washington D.C. area, and Los Angeles. Booking is handled through its iOS and Android apps with real-time driver tracking, pay-per-pound or subscription pricing, and free pickup and delivery. Cleanly/ByNext exposes no public developer API surface; this profile captures the company's public web and consumer-app footprint. The original cleanly.com domain now redirects to bynext.co.

providers.name: Codenotary
providers.description: Codenotary provides cognitive cybersecurity solutions that monitor, secure, and govern AI agents and autonomous workflows across enterprise environments. Their platform offers real‑time observability, policy enforcement, cost optimization, and compliance for AI‑driven tools, helping organizations prevent rogue AI behavior, data leakage, and security incidents. With products like AgentMon and AgentX, Codenotary enables continuous oversight of millions of agent interactions daily, delivering actionable insights and automated remediation for modern AI‑centric operations.

providers.name: ComplyBridge
providers.description: ComplyBridge is a compliance operating system for regulated financial services firms operating in the European Economic Area — banks and credit institutions, electronic money institutions, crypto-asset service providers, payment institutions, and investment firms. The SaaS platform automates the operational compliance workload that would otherwise sit with an outside law firm or an in-house compliance team: wizard-driven license and authorisation packs (License Builder), regulatory policy generation (Policy Studio), a natural-language regulatory Copilot, obligation tracking and audit logs (Compliance Dashboard), repository scanning against the rulebook (Code Compliance), KYB intake and a director/officer/UBO Data Room, and an EU Whistleblower Directive channel (Confide). Coverage spans MiCA, PSD2/PSD3, EMD2/EMD3, MiFID II, DORA, GDPR, and the AML/CFT framework (AMLD5/6, AMLR/AMLA). Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and enriched into the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Cox Communications
providers.description: Cox Communications is a leading American telecommunications provider offering broadband internet, cable TV, and phone services for residential and business customers. Cox provides REST APIs for account management, service configuration, network diagnostics, and customer portal integrations across its broadband, cable television, and voice service platforms.

providers.name: DigiLens
providers.description: DigiLens Inc. is a Sunnyvale, California company that designs and manufactures holographic waveguide optics and augmented reality display systems for extended reality (XR). Its Crystal Waveguides are produced with a proprietary photopolymer material set, inkjet printing and a holographic contact-copy process rather than etching, and are supplied to partners including Samsung, Corning, Panasonic, Sony, Continental, Mitsubishi Chemical and Goertek for smartglasses, automotive head-up displays, smart helmets and avionics head-up guidance. DigiLens also ships ARGO, a standalone, rugged enterprise AR headset running DigiOS — an Android-based operating system with voice UI, gaze and scroll-wheel interaction, projector control and Microsoft Intune MDM certification. Developers build for ARGO in Unity or Android Studio on top of the DigiOS SDK and Qualcomm Snapdragon Spaces, with samples published in the digilens-ar GitHub organization and documentation on the DigiLens developer portal. DigiLens has raised a Series D led by Samsung Electronics at a valuation above $500M.

providers.name: Dow Inc. (formerly The Dow Chemical Company)
providers.description: Dow Chemical, now operating as Dow Inc., is a global materials science company headquartered in Midland, Michigan. Dow develops innovative products and solutions across three segments - Packaging and Specialty Plastics, Industrial Intermediates and Infrastructure, and Performance Materials and Coatings - serving packaging, infrastructure, mobility, and consumer applications.

providers.name: Duchamp
providers.description: Duchamp (뒤샹) is a competitive advertising analysis tool that aggregates Meta ads for competitors, providing daily updates on new, paused, and long-running ads. It offers AI‑enhanced insights via Claude Code·Codex MCP, delivering ad copy, landing pages, keyframes, and transcription data for deep market research.

providers.name: EnergyX
providers.description: EnergyX (Energy Exploration Technologies, Inc.) is a critical-materials technology company founded in 2018 by Teague Egan and headquartered in Austin, Texas, with operations in Texarkana, Antofagasta in Chile, and San Juan, Puerto Rico. It develops direct lithium extraction (DLE) technology — a modular, brine-agnostic flow sheet combining adsorbents, solvent extraction and its own selective membranes under the GET-Lit platform — together with SoLiS lithium-metal battery technology and NUKE-it membranes for lithium-6/7 isotope separation and nuclear fuel-cycle applications. The company produces lithium hydroxide, lithium carbonate and lithium dihydrogen phosphate, holds a large patent portfolio, and controls lithium resources in Chile and the United States including the Black Giant project. EnergyX is a materials and process-technology company rather than a software vendor: it publishes no developer program, no API documentation, no SDKs and no developer portal. The only machine-readable interface it exposes is the WordPress REST content API behind its corporate website at energyx.com, which is captured here for discovery purposes and is anonymously readable but read-only.

providers.name: Free Barcode Generator Online
providers.description: Generate EAN-13, UPC-A, Code 128, QR Code and 20+ barcode formats online for free. Create single or bulk barcodes with no signup required. The service offers a simple web interface and API for developers to integrate barcode generation into applications without registration.

providers.name: Hula Earth
providers.description: Hula Earth is a Munich-based environmental technology company providing real-time biodiversity monitoring. It combines solar-powered, maintenance-free Hula BioT IoT sensors with AI-powered species detection, satellite-based Earth Observation, and the Hula Platform dashboard so organizations can monitor, manage, and report on biodiversity at landscape scale. Hula Earth serves renewables (solar and wind), agriculture, nature conservation, and urban development, turning environmental uncertainty into operational confidence and compliance-ready reporting.

providers.name: Imagen
providers.description: Imagen (Imagen Technologies) is an AI-enabled, sub-specialized diagnostic imaging partner for independent practices, hospitals, and health systems. It combines in-clinic imaging equipment, FDA-cleared AI algorithms, and a 24/7 teleradiology network of fellowship-trained, board-certified specialists to deliver rapid, accurate radiology interpretations, plus advanced analytics for care-gap identification. Imagen operates across 23 states, serving roughly 3.5 million patients, and is backed by GV and Threshold Ventures. The company publishes a security program covering SOC 2 Type II, the HITRUST CSF, and HIPAA. Imagen Technologies exposes no public developer API surface at this time. (Note the distinct namesake company Imagen AI, imagen-ai.com, an AI photo-editing product that does publish an API and SDK.)

providers.name: kissdomain
providers.description: kissdomain is a Berlin‑based domain registration provider operating under 1blu business GmbH. It offers domain names for business customers with personal support, focusing on reliable DNS management, SSL provisioning, and flexible contract terms. The service targets enterprises seeking professional domain services, emphasizing security, local German support, and integration with 1blu’s broader hosting solutions.

providers.name: Koltin
providers.description: Koltin is a Mexican health membership company serving older adults, aimed at people aged roughly 50 to 84 and at the adult children who want to protect their parents and grandparents. Koltin is explicit that it is not an insurer and does not sell traditional policies: it packages access to private medical care, preventive follow-up, and financial protection against costly illness or accident into a membership. The membership pairs a major-medical expense insurance product operated and issued by BBVA Seguros Salud with preventive medicine — longevity assessments, an integrated medical check-up, video consultations, and continuous follow-up — plus a social community program (painting, tai chi, film discussion, dance). It operates across CDMX, Estado de Mexico, Guadalajara, Monterrey, Queretaro, Puebla, Guanajuato, Cuernavaca, Merida, and Veracruz, and publishes a member portal, a hospital network directory, and an extensive Spanish-language blog on aging and preventive health. Koltin is a 500 Global portfolio company. It publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API specification; it does publish a first-party llms.txt describing the site for language models.

providers.name: Litmos
providers.description: SAP Litmos is a cloud-based learning management system (LMS) with a REST API for managing courses, learning paths, user enrollment, completions, assessments, and training compliance reporting. The API enables organizations to automate user provisioning, synchronize training data with HR and CRM systems, manage teams, and retrieve completion records for compliance workflows.

providers.name: Moltbook
providers.description: Moltbook is a social network built exclusively for AI agents, enabling them to share, discuss, upvote content, and interact in a community. The platform welcomes human observers and provides a dedicated space for AI-driven conversations, fostering collaboration and knowledge exchange among intelligent agents.

providers.name: MOSN
providers.description: MOSN (Modular Open Smart Network) is a cloud-native network proxy written in Go, open-sourced by Ant Group. It serves as a Service Mesh data plane and can function as L4/L7 load balancer, API gateway, and cloud-native ingress, with multi-protocol support including HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, and gRPC.

providers.name: NATIX
providers.description: NATIX Network is a decentralized physical infrastructure (DePIN) network building what it calls the world's largest on-street camera network to power Physical AI, autonomous driving, and real-time mapping. Drivers use the Drive& smartphone app and the VX360 plug-and-earn smart camera for Tesla to collect, validate, anonymize, and monetize multi-camera dashcam footage, earning $NATIX token rewards. NATIX packages the resulting data into training datasets, edge cases, and OpenScenario/OpenDrive simulation scenarios for AI and mapping customers, and runs an on-chain token economy with staking, governance, and xNodes. As of 2026 it reports 2.89M+ registered drivers and coverage across 33 countries. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio company; enrichment confirms NATIX publishes no public REST/GraphQL developer API — the surface is consumer apps, an on-chain token, and a proprietary partner Vision SDK.

providers.name: Pendulumlife
providers.description: Pendulum (pendulumlife.com) is a direct-to-consumer probiotics and metabolic-health company founded by PhD scientists from Johns Hopkins, Harvard, Berkeley and Stanford. It sells next-generation probiotic supplements such as Metabolic Daily, Akkermansia, Glucose Control (a medical probiotic clinically shown to improve A1C in type 2 diabetes) and Polyphenol Booster. Surfaced as a portfolio company of felicis and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. Enrichment finding: the site is a Shopify-hosted storefront and Pendulum publishes no first-party developer API, SDKs, or documentation; the only machine surface is Shopify's platform customer-account OIDC discovery endpoint.

providers.name: Petfolk
providers.description: Petfolk is a Charlotte, North Carolina based veterinary care company that operates a network of modern, company-owned pet care centers across the US Southeast and Texas, paired with a consumer mobile app. Founded and led by veterinarian Dr. Audrey Wystrach, Petfolk provides primary and wellness care, sick and urgent care, dentistry, surgery, spay and neuter, vaccinations and diagnostics for dogs and cats, delivered under a "gentle handling" clinical model with seven-day-a-week hours and published, transparent pricing. The Petfolk iOS and Android app lets pet parents book in-person or virtual appointments, message their care team around the clock, request medications and access their pet's medical records; a paid PetfolkCare membership layers on 24/7 veterinary support and per-visit savings. The company raised a $40M Series B in October 2023 led by Movendo Capital, with White Star Capital and Idea Farm Ventures participating. Petfolk is a consumer veterinary services operator, not an API provider: as of this profiling pass it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI/GraphQL contract, SDKs or MCP server. It does publish a hand-authored llms.txt at the site root, which is the company's only machine-readable, agent-facing surface.

providers.name: pixharvest-com
providers.description: PixHarvest provides a WhatsApp‑based quoting solution for printing shops in Singapore and Malaysia. By loading a price table once, the service automatically generates finished quotations for every WhatsApp enquiry within minutes, streamlining order handling and reducing manual effort. The platform targets small‑to‑medium print businesses seeking fast, automated price responses via a popular messaging channel.

providers.name: Pometry
providers.description: Pometry provides institutional intelligence solutions, offering a library of tools that model organizational data across finance, operations, and transformation initiatives. Their platform includes capabilities such as chat, explorer, toolkit, and memory, enabling enterprises to build live models of how their organization works and derive actionable insights for programme delivery, technology optimisation, financial reporting, and client intelligence.

providers.name: Pricerunner
providers.description: Pricerunner is a product price-comparison platform founded in 1999 and owned by Klarna since 2022 (operated by Klarna Technologies AB). It helps shoppers compare prices and products across thousands of retailers in 13 countries (Sweden, Denmark, the UK, Norway, USA, Germany, Austria, Finland, France, Ireland, Italy, the Netherlands and Spain). Pricerunner markets a product-and-price-data API for retailers and businesses covering product search, competitor analysis, price history and automatic price matching across roughly 126 million daily-updated prices, but access is gated behind a sales contact form, with no public developer documentation, OpenAPI specification, or self-serve onboarding published.

providers.name: Pumble
providers.description: Pumble is a free business communication tool that offers team chat, voice calls, and file sharing in a single platform. It is designed for small to medium-sized businesses to improve internal collaboration with features like channels, direct messages, integrations, and searchable message history. The service emphasizes simplicity, security, and cross‑platform availability, supporting web, desktop, and mobile clients.

providers.name: Rapchat
providers.description: Rapchat is a mobile-first music creation platform for artists, rappers, singers, and producers, founded in 2014. Creators use the Rapchat iOS and Android apps to find professionally-produced beats from top producers, record studio-quality vocals with effects and audio filters, write lyrics, join music challenges, collaborate, and share finished songs with a creator community. The platform reports 15M+ creators, 100M+ tracks, and over one billion plays, and offers free web-based artist tools (rap name generator, lyric generator, rhyme finder, BPM mood guide) alongside Free, Premium, and Pro subscription tiers. Rapchat is a portfolio company of 500 Global. As of this profile the company exposes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; its /api endpoint is an internal application backend (HTTP 403).

providers.name: rubiic-com
providers.description: Rubiic is an AI‑powered creative platform that enables users to generate videos, graphics, GIFs, and animations through conversational prompts. Users can think out loud, try a direction, and change their mind, with free signup credits and paid credit packs or a subscription plan. Rubiic integrates with coding agents via its MCP, supporting Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, and VS Code, offering step‑by‑step setup and copyable configurations. It positions itself as a creative partner from idea to finished media.

providers.name: SendCutSend
providers.description: SendCutSend is a rapid custom manufacturing service offering online sheet metal fabrication, laser cutting, waterjet cutting, CNC machining, CNC bending, tapping, hardware installation, and finishing across 175+ materials, with instant online pricing from uploaded STEP or DXF files and parts delivered in as little as a few days. Customers quote, configure, and order parts through the app.sendcutsend.com web application. The company reached a $1.01B valuation following a $110M investment co-led by Sequoia, Paradigm, and Patrick and John Collison. SendCutSend does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile captures its public web, pricing, and content surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Shopventory
providers.description: Thrive by Shopventory is inventory management, catalog control, and reporting software for small and medium-sized retail, restaurant, and hospitality businesses. Founded in 2012 out of a San Diego boutique and a graduate of the Techstars Boulder accelerator, Shopventory syncs stock, sales, and cost-of-goods data across multiple locations and sales channels, and integrates with Square, Shopify, Clover, BigCommerce, WooCommerce, and QuickBooks Online. The platform offers barcode scanning, purchase-order automation, demand forecasting, bundles and component-level tracking, price-tag printing, and advanced custom reporting. The company operates as Thrive by Shopventory (thrivemetrics.com). Its former public developer API (apidocs.shopventory.com) is no longer resolvable, so this profile captures the company's live web, support, and integration surface plus probed domain-security posture rather than a public API specification.

providers.name: Skootar
providers.description: Skootar is a Thai on-demand courier, messenger, and logistics platform serving Bangkok, its surrounding provinces, and Chonburi. It offers same-day document delivery, cheque and bill collection, parcel shipping, business food delivery, and on-demand pickup-truck and moving jobs across a fleet of motorcycles, cars, and trucks, all with real-time tracking. Orders can be placed 24/7 through the website, the mobile app, or an API intended for high-volume businesses to wire delivery ordering into their own back-office systems. Skootar reports more than 130,000 business customers, 26,000+ drivers, and 9.2 million+ completed deliveries over 12 years, and is backed by 500 Global. No public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, or SDK is published; API access is arranged through its business/enterprise channel.

providers.name: Skopenow
providers.description: Skopenow is an open-source intelligence (OSINT) platform built to modernize digital investigations. Founded in 2015 and backed by Techstars, it fuses public records, consumer data, crime data, news, and online content with AI-powered fraud and threat-detection models to generate intelligence reports on entities, uncover and visualize networks between people and organizations, and surface operational risks. Its product suite spans Grid, Pre-Check, Workbench, Link Analysis, and Rabbit, serving global security, insurance, government, law enforcement, legal, and media teams — more than 1,500 organizations, including a fifth of the Fortune 500. Skopenow ships as a login-gated web application rather than a public developer API.

providers.name: SKUPLUGS
providers.description: SKUPlugs provides a no‑code solution to sync inventory, products and orders across major POS and e‑commerce platforms such as Lightspeed, Square, Loyverse, Zoho, Shopify, WooCommerce, Amazon and Walmart. Users can connect their POS, configure mappings, and automate inventory synchronization without writing code, benefiting from a 15‑day free trial and multi‑channel support.

providers.name: Snappy
providers.description: Snappy is a corporate gifting platform that lets businesses send curated gifts, branded swag, and recipient-choice collections to employees and customers. Beyond its web app, Snappy publishes a developer API suite that embeds gifting into CRMs, HRIS platforms, and marketing-automation tools, triggering gifts from business events such as recognition moments, loyalty milestones, and sales-pipeline events, with budget controls and approval workflows. It also ships Slack and Microsoft Teams integrations. Backed by GGV Capital; sector hr-tech / corporate gifting.

providers.name: Spiber
providers.description: Spiber Inc. is a Japanese biotechnology and advanced-materials company founded in 2007 and headquartered in Tsuruoka, Yamagata Prefecture, Japan. Spiber develops Brewed Protein materials — structural proteins produced by precision fermentation of plant-derived sugars using engineered microbes, then spun into fibers, resins, and films as animal-free, petroleum-free alternatives to silk, wool, cashmere, leather, and synthetic polymers. The company operates fermentation plants in Japan, Thailand, and the United States and supplies apparel, outdoor, automotive, and consumer brands, alongside a research program in synthetic biology, polymer science, and life-cycle assessment. Spiber is a materials manufacturer rather than a software vendor and publishes no developer program, developer portal, SDKs, or product API; the only machine-readable HTTP surface it serves is the read-only WordPress REST content API behind its corporate website.

providers.name: Spire Maritime
providers.description: Spire Maritime (Spire Global) delivers satellite and terrestrial AIS vessel data - global ship positions, static vessel characteristics, voyage and destination data, port events, and predicted ETAs. The flagship Maritime 2.0 service is GraphQL-first at a single endpoint (https://api.spire.com/graphql, Bearer token auth), with a separate raw-TCP AIS stream for real-time message delivery in NMEA 0183 format. Access is enterprise / contact-sales. NOTE - following Spire Maritime's acquisition by Kpler, these APIs are being migrated/discontinued; new integrations are directed to developers.kpler.com.

providers.name: Sunbird
providers.description: Sunbird provides Data Center Infrastructure Management (DCIM) software that helps organizations monitor, manage, and optimize their data center assets and operations. The platform offers tools for asset tracking, capacity planning, energy management, environmental monitoring, and security analytics, supporting both colocation and government data centers. Sunbird’s solutions enable real‑time visibility, automated workflows, and detailed reporting to improve efficiency, reduce risk, and lower operational costs across complex data center environments.

providers.name: Tawkify
providers.description: Tawkify is a US personalized matchmaking service that pairs paying clients with a trained human matchmaker rather than offering a self-service dating app. Founded in 2012 and headquartered in San Francisco, the company screens and hand-selects introductions from a network of several million singles, arranges curated first dates, and collects structured feedback after each match. Packages are sold by consultation through a client experience specialist instead of a published price list. Tawkify operates a consumer web application at app.tawkify.com for onboarding, profiles and match feedback, but publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable contract of any kind; its engineering surface is entirely internal.

providers.name: TelevisaUnivision (Univision Communications)
providers.description: TelevisaUnivision (formerly Univision Communications) is the world's leading Spanish-language media company, operating television networks (Univision, UniMás, TUDN, Galavisión), the ViX streaming platform, Uforia audio platform, and a suite of advanced advertising technology solutions. The company serves advertisers and media partners through programmatic ad platforms, first-party audience data, and content partnerships rather than a public developer API.

providers.name: Tem
providers.description: Tem (Tem-Energy Limited) is a UK-based energy technology company building AI-native transaction infrastructure for a modern energy market. Its RED platform is a modern utility that removes wholesale market markups to cut business electricity costs by up to 30%, provides transparent line-by-line billing from half-hourly meter data, and gives generators fairer earnings with renewable-energy traceability across 6,000+ sites. Backed by a February 2026 GBP 55M Series B led by Lightspeed Venture Partners. The customer-facing platform runs at app.tem.energy behind an OIDC login; the platform API at api.tem.energy is a private AWS API Gateway with no publicly documented developer surface at the time of profiling.

providers.name: TenneT
providers.description: TenneT is a leading European transmission system operator (TSO) responsible for high‑voltage electricity grids in the Netherlands and Germany. It ensures reliable, secure power supply, drives the energy transition, and provides market platforms for electricity trading. The company focuses on sustainability, grid expansion, and digital innovation to support a low‑carbon future.

providers.name: The Business of Fashion
providers.description: The Business of Fashion (BoF) is an authoritative digital media and intelligence company founded by Imran Amed in 2007, serving the global fashion and luxury industry. It publishes news, analysis, case studies and industry data, and operates subscription products including BoF Professional membership, BoF Insights research reports, events and online courses. Backed by Index Ventures. BoF publishes no public developer API; this profile captures the company's public web, subscription and legal surface plus a domain-security probe.

providers.name: Toonimo
providers.description: Toonimo is a digital adoption platform (DAP) that overlays personalized, interactive on-screen guidance onto enterprise software and websites. Using patented voice, text-bubble, and visual-cue walkthroughs, Toonimo guides end users and employees through onboarding, self-service, and complex workflows to increase conversions, accelerate software adoption, and reduce support costs. It layers on top of platforms such as Salesforce, SAP SuccessFactors, Workday, ServiceNow, Oracle Cloud, Microsoft Dynamics, Coupa, and SharePoint, and enables subject-matter experts (not just developers) to build and maintain adoption content. Toonimo is a marketing/product company backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners; it does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: TwinStrand Biosciences
providers.description: TwinStrand Biosciences is a Seattle, Washington genomics company founded in 2015 by Jesse Salk and Michael Schmitt that develops and commercializes Duplex Sequencing, an error-corrected next-generation-sequencing chemistry licensed from the University of Washington that independently tracks both strands of an individual DNA molecule and compares them, cutting sequencing error rates from roughly 1-in-100 to below 1-in-10,000,000 per nucleotide and making ultra-rare mutations detectable. The company sells DuplexSeq assay kits — a Mutagenesis Assay for genetic toxicology in human, rat and mouse models, an AML MRD Assay for minimal residual disease in acute myeloid leukemia, and a customizable assay — each paired with a proprietary cloud analysis pipeline that turns raw Illumina reads into duplex-consensus sequences, variant calls, mutation frequency, SBS spectra and assay quality metrics. That analysis software is not a public API: it is hosted on the DNAnexus platform and reachable only by customers through a DNAnexus project. TwinStrand publishes no developer portal, no API reference and no OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, GraphQL or Postman artifact of its own, and the api., docs. and developer. subdomains of twinstrandbio.com do not resolve. The only machine-readable surface on twinstrandbio.com is the WordPress REST API at /wp-json — 349 routes across 18 namespaces — whose wp/v2 content collections are anonymously readable and serve the company publication index, patent estate, conference posters, news releases, events, team profiles, pages and media library as JSON. Its public code lives in the github.com/twinstrandbio organization, which holds a single reference-data repository and no client libraries. The DuplexSeq Mutagenesis Assay business has since been transferred to Scantox, and Exact Sciences holds an exclusive license to the Duplex Sequencing technology.

providers.name: Unmind
providers.description: Unmind is a workplace mental health platform that supports employees, develops leaders, and strengthens organisational performance through therapy, coaching, manager training, crisis care, an Employee Assistance Programme (EAP), wellbeing content, insights and assessments, and Nova, an AI wellbeing coach. Customers include Uber, MLB, Samsung, British Airways, Diageo, and the NHS. Unmind publishes no public developer API; api.unmind.com is a private Apollo GraphQL backend serving its own apps.

providers.name: Valid.it
providers.description: Valid.it (Validit.ai) is an AI-based fraud prevention SaaS that lets enterprises, governments, and financial institutions validate users' statements remotely and in real time through a standard smartphone, laptop, or tablet camera. Its patented physio-behavioral AI combines computer vision, signal processing, and PPG bio-signal analytics to detect deepfakes, synthetic identities, and deceptive intent across onboarding, KYC/AML, insurance claim verification, security vetting, and HR screening — delivered as a standalone web-based solution or via API integration. A Techstars portfolio company; no public developer portal or API documentation is published.

providers.name: VendorPM
providers.description: VendorPM is a PropTech procurement and vendor-lifecycle-management platform for the commercial real estate industry, unifying vendor credentialing, compliance screening, eTendering/eBidding, procurement, and contract management under a single login. Its marketplace connects property managers with a network of 50,000+ vendors to fulfill building services and contracts of all sizes, while an AI Procurement CoPilot surfaces recommendations and a Yardi Voyager ERP integration syncs vendor compliance and profile data. VendorPM serves 100+ property management groups and 6,000+ buildings across the US and Canada. This profile was surfaced as a Bessemer Venture Partners portfolio company; VendorPM exposes no public self-serve developer API — its Yardi/ERP integration is provisioned through a Customer Success Manager.

providers.name: Vroom
providers.description: Vroom, Inc. is a Houston-based automotive technology company that operated as an online used vehicle retailer offering no-haggle pricing, nationwide home delivery, and digital financing. In January 2024 Vroom ceased direct-to-consumer e-commerce vehicle sales and pivoted to focus on its two B2B subsidiaries — United Auto Credit Corporation (UACC), a non-prime automotive finance lender serving 7,300+ dealerships, and CarStory, an AI-powered analytics and digital retail services platform processing over 7 million vehicle listings per day. The company exited Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in January 2025. Current API-adjacent services include the UACC dealer portal for financing origination and the CarStory analytics platform for inventory appraisal, promotion, and profit tracking — both available to dealer partners under negotiated B2B agreements.

providers.name: Workrise
providers.description: Workrise - which returned to its original RigUp brand in September 2024 - is an Austin-based source-to-pay platform for the energy industry, combining vendor management, contingent workforce staffing, bid management, capital management, and field-service payments for upstream and midstream oil and gas operators. Backed by a16z and Founders Fund. The company publishes no public developer portal or API documentation; platform access is through accounts.rigup.com (OpenID Connect via Auth0), and its engineering org open-sources utilities at github.com/rigup.

providers.name: Zenchef
providers.description: Zenchef provides an all‑in‑one restaurant management platform that handles reservations, table management, payments, guest communication, and analytics. Their SaaS solution helps restaurants reduce no‑shows, fill last‑minute tables, and improve revenue through integrated booking, AI‑driven tools, and a guest‑facing app. The platform serves individual venues and groups, offering customizable branding, multi‑location oversight, and a marketplace of integrations for POS, marketing, and loyalty systems.

providers.name: 7 Cups
providers.description: 7 Cups (7cups.com) is an on-demand emotional health and online therapy service founded in 2013 and backed by Y Combinator. It connects people seeking support with a network of trained volunteer listeners for free, anonymous one-on-one chat, and matches members with licensed therapists and social workers for paid online therapy delivered by messaging, audio, or video. The platform also runs peer community forums, group support chat rooms, and self-help "growth path" content. 7 Cups operates across 189 countries in 140 languages with hundreds of thousands of trained listeners. It is a consumer web and mobile product rather than an API-first developer platform; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record and carries no public API at this time.

providers.name: AMMP
providers.description: AMMP (AMMP OS) is a distributed energy monitoring and operations platform for operators of commercial and industrial (C&I) solar and battery-storage portfolios. It unifies visibility across multi-vendor fleets, pulling data directly from more than 30 manufacturer cloud platforms and its own AMMP Edge data logger, and layers on monitoring, alerting, stakeholder reporting, commercial (SLA/cost) tracking, and customizable dashboards. AMMP OS monitors over 10,000 sites across 35+ countries and emphasizes vendor independence and ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certified security. Surfaced as a portfolio company of point-nine and enriched by the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Angular Material
providers.description: Angular Material is the official Material Design component library for Angular applications, maintained by the Angular team at Google. It provides over 30 accessible UI components implementing Material Design 3 (M3) with design tokens, a theming system based on CSS custom properties, and the Angular Component Dev Kit (CDK) with behavior primitives for custom component development. Angular Material is published on npm as @angular/material and @angular/cdk.

providers.name: Archrock
providers.description: Archrock (NYSE: AROC) is the premier provider of natural gas compression services and equipment to customers in the oil and natural gas industry throughout the United States. The company operates a large fleet of compression equipment and provides contract operations and aftermarket services.

providers.name: Aska Charge
providers.description: Aska Charge provides a cloud‑based CSMS platform for operators of electric vehicle charging stations. The service offers real‑time monitoring, remote OCPP command control, billing integration with Stripe, multi‑brand white‑labeling, and a roaming hub for revenue sharing among operators. It supports both B2B operators and fleet managers, with features like automated tax invoicing, power‑distribution without civil works, and customizable pricing plans. The platform is SaaS, GDPR‑compliant, and available in Spanish and English, targeting hotels, parking facilities, fleets, installers, and municipalities.

providers.name: Base Power
providers.description: Base Power (Base Texas REP, LLC, PUCT License #10338) is an Austin, Texas home energy company that pairs an installed home battery (40–80 kWh) with retail electricity service across Texas and Illinois. The battery powers a home automatically during outages with no manual switch and helps lower the energy bill: batteries charge when grid demand is low and send power back to the grid when demand is high (grid-balancing), and that grid revenue helps keep member energy rates low. Base can be the retail electricity provider with or without a battery, works with existing solar, and serves the Oncor, CenterPoint, AEP Texas, TNMP, CoServ, GVEC, Farmers Electric, and El Paso Electric areas in Texas plus ComEd in Illinois. Led by CEO Zach Dell and co-founder Justin Lopas; named to the TIME100 Most Influential Companies (2026); backed by Andreessen Horowitz, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Addition, Bond Capital, Ribbit Capital, and Spark Capital. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Base publishes no public developer API.

providers.name: BaseThread
providers.description: BaseThread provides a shared context platform for AI tools used by teams, enabling saved prompts, clipboard history, and markdown notes across macOS applications. It integrates with major AI assistants like Claude, Cursor, and ChatGPT, allowing automatic read/write of decisions, activity, and tasks. The service offers a free beta with no credit card required and scales with per-seat pricing for larger teams. Features include product integrations, engineering and design solutions, and comprehensive security and privacy controls.

providers.name: Bestever
providers.description: Bestever is an AI-powered ad generation platform that helps brands create thousands of video and image ad variations at scale. It integrates with major ad platforms, pulls performance data, and uses generative AI to produce on‑brand creative assets, offering tools for competitor analysis, data‑driven optimization, and workflow automation for agencies and marketers.

providers.name: Blackcloak
providers.description: BlackCloak provides digital executive protection and personal cybersecurity services, safeguarding high‑profile individuals and enterprises from deepfake scams, impersonation, and cyber threats. Their platform offers monitoring, threat detection, and response tools tailored for executives, families, and high‑net‑worth individuals, combining technology and expert guidance to mitigate personal and corporate risk.

providers.name: Bootify
providers.description: bootify-io is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: mcp-registry) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.

providers.name: BrandVane
providers.description: BrandVane provides AI‑driven SEO research tools that let small businesses and agencies discover keywords, compare competitors, and plan content directly within AI assistants like ChatGPT, Claude, or Codex. Their platform offers transparent pricing starting at $29/month, with cost estimates shown before each run, and integrates free tools and paid plans to enhance visibility and content strategy.

providers.name: BrowsingBee
providers.description: BrowsingBee provides a remote browser connector that lets Claude and ChatGPT browse the internet, search web pages, read PDFs, and extract data. Users can access any page without installing software, with a free tier of 300 pages per month.
