providers.description: Stable Audio (by Stability AI) is a generative audio model for music and sound-effect generation. The Stability Developer Platform exposes Stable Audio 2.5 endpoints alongside image, video, and 3D generation. Pricing is credit-based at 1 credit = $0.01; Stable Audio 2.5 generations are reported at $0.20 per generation regardless of duration.

providers.name: Switchyards
providers.description: Switchyards is a membership-based neighborhood work club — a 24/7 network of coffee-shop-style workspaces built for focused solo work close to where members live. Each club pairs a bustling cafe with quiet library spaces for deep work, plus bookable phone booths and meeting rooms, free locally roasted coffee and organic tea, and fast internet. Membership runs about $100/month for unlimited access across all locations, and the company is expanding from its Atlanta roots into neighborhoods across the Southeast and beyond. Switchyards is backed by Bullpen Capital and does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: The Black Friday Agency
providers.description: The Black Friday Agency offers a free AI Recommendation Readiness Audit that evaluates whether a business is understandable, verifiable, recommendable, and usable by AI systems. It helps small and midsize businesses improve AI visibility through a plain-English diagnostic covering eight readiness categories.

providers.name: Upwage
providers.description: Upwage is an AI interview platform that helps employers hire faster and more fairly with lower turnover. Its emotionally intelligent AI interviewer conducts 24/7 multilingual candidate screening, scoring competencies consistently to reduce bias in high-volume hiring across retail, healthcare, logistics, and staffing, with ATS integrations including Ashby, Greenhouse, iCIMS, Lever, SmartRecruiters, and Workday. Founded by Diana Tsai and Greg Call and backed by Bloomberg Beta, Upwage publishes a SOC 2 Type 2 trust center with third-party bias audits, but no public developer API surface yet.

providers.name: Vertical Bar
providers.description: Vertical Bar Inc. builds CrossCheck, a DevOps and operations-visibility platform for NetSuite environments. CrossCheck gives NetSuite teams configuration tracking, change management and deployment safety: environment snapshots, comparisons and restore, automated record-and-replay regression testing that catches issues before production, AI-assisted error analysis with fix suggestions, and process mining to surface workflow delays and inefficiencies. Vertical Bar also offers managed services and industry-specific solutions for medical device, food and beverage, chemical, and aerospace and defense manufacturers, plus the FieldTrail browser extension for NetSuite field customization. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched from its public web surface.

providers.name: Wenrix
providers.description: Wenrix is an AI infrastructure company for the travel industry, providing embedded AI that helps Online Travel Agencies (OTAs) and Travel Management Companies (TMCs) drive revenue and operational efficiency from search through post-trip servicing. Founded in 2017 and backed by Insight Partners, Wenrix processes roughly $12 billion in annual air volume across 60+ global OTAs and TMCs. Its platform is delivered as three API-first products: FareSight, a predictive price-assurance engine that optimizes pricing across EDIFACT, NDC, GDS, aggregators, and low-cost carriers at both search and post-booking stages; FlexEngine, a flight-flexibility solution offering short- and long-term flexibility, refund guarantees, and price-lock through a single API; and DeepFlow, a post-booking servicing automation layer that automates cancellations, refunds, and changes at 93%+ automation rates and is available as either an API or an MCP (Model Context Protocol) Server. Wenrix operates from offices in Tel Aviv, New York, and Barcelona.

providers.name: Xtime
providers.description: Xtime is Cox Automotive's service experience platform for franchised auto dealerships, combining online appointment scheduling, service-lane check-in, multi-point vehicle inspection, customer communications, service marketing, and payments into one fixed-operations workflow. Part of Cox Automotive since 2014 alongside Dealertrack, VinSolutions, Kelley Blue Book, and vAuto, Xtime integrates with DMS and dealer-website partners through the Cox Automotive ecosystem; it publishes no public self-serve API or developer portal, with partner integration handled via the Cox Automotive Integration Platform.

providers.name: Yieldify *
providers.description: Yieldify is a website personalization and conversion rate optimization (CRO) platform for ecommerce brands, founded in 2013 in London by Jay Radia and backed by investors including GV (Google Ventures). Its SaaS platform delivers targeted on-site messaging, customer-journey personalization, and A/B testing to lift conversion and revenue. Yieldify was acquired by Publicis Groupe in January 2023 and folded into Epsilon, where it is now sold as Epsilon Accelerate; yieldify.com redirects to the Epsilon Accelerate product page and the legal entity behind the platform is Zeus Enterprise Ltd, trading as Yieldify. Delivery is entirely client-side: a customer-specific JavaScript tag placed before the closing head tag (directly, or via Google Tag Manager, Tealium, Shopify theme.liquid or Recharge checkout) renders a documented library of on-site experience components — overlays, notifications, banners, sticky and embedded experiences, toasters, carousels, countdown timers, lead-capture forms — configured from the Yieldify Conversion Platform at convert.yieldify.com, with a typed dynamic-expression language for personalized copy and client-side yieldify_impression/click/close/form_submit events pushed into the customer's own GA4 property. There is no public developer API: probing every Yieldify host on 2026-08-13 found no OpenAPI, GraphQL, MCP, A2A card, webhooks, SDK, CLI or developer portal, the status page at status.yieldify.com has been deactivated, and no pricing is published anywhere.

providers.name: 1F3EA
providers.description: 1F3EA is a market district for AI agents, offering a read‑only public API that lets agents browse aisles, view stores, and retrieve marketplace data such as listings, events, and treasury fees. The site runs on a Vercel‑hosted domain and provides endpoints like /api/me, /api/window, and various public read‑only resources. Humans can view documentation pages such as /about, /help, /city-bridge, /terms, /privacy, /support, and /treasury, while agents interact via the API without authentication. The platform enforces payment of $1 USDC per merchant listing and logs all transactions publicly.

providers.name: A-Team
providers.description: A-Team is an AI Application Platform that enables users to design, build, deploy, govern, and operate complete AI-powered applications. It supports multiple large language models including OpenAI, Anthropic, Ollama, and SGLang, and can run in the cloud, on managed services, or on‑premises. The platform offers low‑code skill creation, tool integration, governance policies, and runtime monitoring, allowing enterprises to create AI teams that automate tasks across email, messaging, documents, and more.

providers.name: Abacum
providers.description: Abacum is an AI-native financial planning and analysis (FP&A) platform built for CFOs and finance teams to connect financial data, automate planning and reporting, and align cross-functional teams. It unifies budgeting and forecasting, headcount and revenue planning, scenario modeling, investor and board reporting, and P&L / balance-sheet / cash-flow roll-ups, with 700+ prebuilt integrations across ERP and accounting systems (NetSuite, Sage Intacct, QuickBooks, Xero, Dynamics 365), HRIS and payroll (Workday, Rippling, BambooHR, Gusto, Deel), CRM (Salesforce, HubSpot), billing (Stripe, Chargebee, Maxio), and data warehouses (Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks). An Excel connector and embedded workflows keep planning models and actuals in sync. Abacum surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Creandum and Scale Venture Partners.

providers.name: AETumi
providers.description: AETumi provides an AI-native 3D web platform offering production‑ready Three.js, WebGL components, interactive scenes, and AI‑generated prompts for designers, developers, and agencies. The service includes a library of templates, 3D scenes, and components across industries such as fashion, automotive, e‑commerce, and finance, with pricing plans for individuals and enterprises.

providers.name: Agent Couch
providers.description: Agent Couch provides an MCP (Multi-Client Protocol) server that enables agents across various AI tools like Claude, Codex, Cursor, and others to communicate in shared messaging rooms. It offers seamless integration without sign‑up forms, supporting installation via command‑line tools and configuration files. The platform focuses on secure, real‑time agent collaboration, handling messages, attachments, and room management, while exposing a simple MCP endpoint at https://mcp.agentcouch.dev for client integration.

providers.name: Agrofy
providers.description: Agrofy is a Latin American agribusiness technology company founded in 2015 in Rosario, Argentina, operating the region's largest online marketplace for agricultural inputs, machinery, farmland, vehicles and services. The company runs three business units — Agrofy Market (the marketplace, live in Argentina and Brazil with country storefronts across Bolivia, Chile, Colombia, Paraguay, Peru and Uruguay), Agrofy News (an agricultural news publication) and Agrofy Pay (payments, credit and financing for agribusiness transactions). Agrofy markets a partner integration program, Agrofy Developers, for sellers who want to automate listings and lead management inside the marketplace.

providers.name: Aira Technologies
providers.description: Aira Technologies is an AI-defined networking company founded in 2019 and headquartered in Saratoga, California, building machine-learning and generative-AI software for mobile network operators. Its platform, Naavik, is marketed as an Adaptive Intelligence Framework for the Radio Access Network, combining an Intent Manager that turns natural language into network actions, AppGen for no-code telecom application generation, a reasoning agent for anomaly detection and root-cause analysis, a telecom-specific AI/ML hub and a knowledge graph. Earlier work includes RANGPT, a GenAI utility for RAN observability, analysis, control and automation demonstrated with Broadcom and Tech Mahindra, and an AI-based channel estimation and prediction xApp. The company is a member of the O-RAN Alliance, the AI-RAN Alliance and TM Forum, and raised a $14.5M Series B from AT&T Ventures, Intel Capital and In-Q-Tel. Aira sells to operators through a demo and sales motion and publishes no developer program, no API documentation, no SDKs and no public specification for Naavik or RANGPT. The only machine-readable interface reachable at aira-technology.com is the WordPress REST content API behind the corporate website, captured here for discovery purposes; it is anonymously readable and read-only.

providers.name: Albertinvent
providers.description: Albert Invent builds Albert OS, an AI operating system for chemists and R&D teams that unifies electronic lab notebooks, structured molecular-level experimental data, chemical drawing, and safety/compliance data (safety data sheets for roughly 400,000 substances) with chemistry-trained AI models built on a foundation of 15 million molecular structures. The platform helps materials, formulation, and specialty-chemical teams capture proprietary experimental data and accelerate discovery, training custom predictive models on each customer's own chemistry. Albert Invent is a scientific R&D / developer-tools SaaS company backed by Homebrew; its APIs and developer surface are not publicly documented (product documentation at docs.albertinvent.com is access-gated).

providers.name: Apron
providers.description: Apron is a London, UK-based financial technology company that helps small business owners, accountants, and bookkeepers automate supplier payments, payroll, expenses, and payment collection. The platform captures invoices, batches and pays bills directly from a business bank account, and reconciles transactions in real time with accounting software such as Xero and QuickBooks Online. Founded by Bogdan Uzbekov (an early Revolut operator), Apron serves more than 10,000 businesses and is an FCA-authorised Electronic Money Institution (firm reference 1004915), ISO 27001 certified, and regulated under the UK Payment Services Regulations 2017 and Electronic Money Regulations 2011. Apron does not currently publish a public developer API; it integrates as a consumer of the Xero and QuickBooks accounting APIs.

providers.name: Archer Aviation
providers.description: Archer Aviation is a U.S. eVTOL aircraft company developing Midnight, a piloted four-passenger all-electric aircraft designed for rapid back-to-back urban flights of roughly 20-50 miles with a ~10 minute charge between trips. Archer is pursuing FAA Type Certification and operates through commercial and defense business lines. Key partnerships include Stellantis (contract manufacturing at Archer's Covington, Georgia facility), United Airlines (launch routes including the Manhattan-Newark corridor), and a Launch Edition program in the United Arab Emirates with Abu Dhabi Aviation. Archer also has a dedicated defense division (Archer Defense) developing hybrid VTOL platforms with Anduril and supporting U.S. government missions. The company trades on the NYSE under ACHR.

providers.name: AtoB
providers.description: AtoB is a fleet payments platform for the trucking and transportation industry, offering fuel cards, spend-management controls, driver payouts, and trip credit to fleets of every size. Its cards work across a nationwide fuel network with truck-stop discounts, granular purchase controls (fuel-only, category/MCC restrictions, per-transaction and daily limits), telematics-aware fraud prevention, and reporting that supports IFTA fuel-tax and expense compliance. AtoB also runs partner programs for factoring companies, freight brokers, and merchants, and exposes a private Partners API used by telematics and fleet-management integrations (for example Fleetio and Oxmaint) to sync cards, drivers, vehicles, and settled fuel transactions. AtoB was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bloomberg Beta and General Catalyst; this profile has been enriched from public web sources.

providers.name: Balloon
providers.description: Balloon is a research-backed team collaboration and decision-making platform built to eliminate groupthink and give quieter voices a psychologically safe way to contribute. Its core workflow, called a "flight," is a two-stage, partly anonymous process in which a leader poses a question, team members submit ideas ("balloons") and discuss them, and the group then evaluates and "pumps" the strongest ideas on merit, surfacing a Balloon Score that shows consensus and buy-in. Balloon ships 150+ expert-authored flight templates across 25 business areas and supports asynchronous, time-zone-independent participation, positioning itself as a replacement for status and ideation meetings (the company cites a 70% reduction in meeting time and that ~80% of information shared is new to the organization). Founded by Amanda Greenberg and Noah Bornstein, Balloon is backed by 500 Global and other investors, with an advisory board including Adam Grant, Amy Edmondson, and Daniel Pink. It is a SaaS web application (app at balloon.app) with no public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: BevSpot
providers.description: BevSpot is a Boston-based food and beverage inventory management platform for restaurants, bars, and hospitality groups. The web application streamlines back-of-house operations including inventory counting, ordering, invoice management, recipe and menu costing, and sales-driven analytics. BevSpot ingests point-of-sale data through integrations with more than a dozen POS systems (Toast, Square, Clover, Lightspeed, SpotOn, NCR Aloha, Upserve, Brink, Lavu, and others), plus accounting and vendor connections (QuickBooks, Microsoft Dynamics GP, Ottimate, Fintech, US Foods, Sysco). It is a portfolio company of Bain Capital Ventures. BevSpot does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its public web, commercial, and security surface.

providers.name: Brightline
providers.description: Brightline is an award-winning pediatric mental health practice delivering therapy, psychiatry (including medication management), and psychological testing for children and adolescents up to age 18, using an evidence-based, family-focused model that begins with a structured diagnostic evaluation. It treats anxiety, OCD, ADHD, disruptive behavioral disorders, depression, trauma, grief, and autism-spectrum symptoms via in-person clinics in New York and telehealth across NY, NJ, CT, MA, and WA, and operates BrightLife Kids, a free California state-funded behavioral health program for families with children up to age 12. Surfaced as a portfolio company of GV and Threshold Ventures; Brightline is a consumer/clinical healthcare provider with no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Buildforever
providers.description: BuildForever is a consumer software company building products that feel personal, magical, and deeply human. Its first product, Extra (extra.email), is a free AI email app for iPhone, Mac, and Gmail that automatically organizes the inbox into smart categories, summarizes what matters in a daily digest, cleans up subscriptions and unwanted senders, answers natural-language questions about your mail, and drafts replies in your own tone. Founded and led by CEO Naveen Gavini (formerly SVP/CPO at Pinterest), BuildForever is backed by Abstract Ventures, Felicis, and DST Global, with angel investors including Ben Silbermann, Guillermo Rauch, and Paul Buchheit. The company does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile captures its consumer product surface and identity.

providers.name: CACI International
providers.description: CACI International provides information technology, professional services, and managed solutions to U.S. federal government agencies in the defense, intelligence, homeland security, and civilian markets. The company delivers expertise and technology across C3I, cyber, digital solutions, enterprise IT, mission support, space, and spectrum superiority domains.

providers.name: Chain of Title
providers.description: Chain of Title provides launch-time provenance for Solana tokens, recording over three million token launches from creation transactions. It offers an API to retrieve detailed launch records, including claimed metadata, transaction data, and on-chain documents. The service also includes brand protection alerts and detailed provenance reports for token launches, supporting developers and brands in blockchain forensics and token verification.

providers.name: Clara
providers.description: Clara provides seamless digital formation services for companies, offering incorporation, equity management, data room, and visa solutions across multiple jurisdictions. The platform serves startups, investors, SMEs, and legal advisors with tools for company formation, equity management, data room access, and specialized visa programs such as ADGM, DIFC, BVI, Cayman, and Golden Visa. Clara also offers pricing transparency, partner integrations, and a knowledge hub to help businesses navigate legal and financial processes efficiently.

providers.name: Cofertility
providers.description: Cofertility is a human-centered fertility and family-building platform built around an egg-sharing model. Through its Split program, women can freeze their eggs at no cost when they donate half of the retrieved eggs to another family who cannot otherwise conceive; its Keep program offers self-funded egg freezing at a discount where members retain all of their eggs. On the family-building side, Cofertility matches intended parents (including LGBTQ+ families and single parents) with fresh and frozen egg donors, working with 225+ clinic partners nationwide and a donor community spanning 270+ ethnicities. Founded by Lauren Makler, the company operates a consumer web platform (match.cofertility.com) plus an extensive fertility education library. It is a consumer health company with no public developer API or programmatic surface at this time; this profile captures its public web properties and posture.

providers.name: Collective
providers.description: Collective is an all-in-one financial back-office platform built for self-employed entrepreneurs, solopreneurs, and businesses-of-one. It bundles S Corp formation and election, bookkeeping, payroll (as a Gusto partner), business and personal tax preparation and filing, quarterly tax planning, and a dedicated accounting team into a single membership. Roughly 12,000 members use Collective to optimize self-employment taxes, with members reporting average annual business-tax savings around $10,000. Collective is a private fintech company backed by General Catalyst, Kindred Ventures, and QED Investors. It currently exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this profile captures its public web, security, and compliance footprint for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Coople
providers.description: Coople is a technology-driven workforce solutions provider that connects businesses with flexible, skilled talent across various sectors such as healthcare, retail, logistics, hospitality, and office environments. Their platform enables companies to quickly find, hire, and manage temporary staff, offering services like payrolling, workforce planning, and compliance support. Coople leverages a smart digital platform to streamline recruitment, onboarding, and workforce management, helping businesses adapt to fluctuating labor needs while providing workers with flexible job opportunities.

providers.name: customs.dog
providers.description: customs.dog provides a web application that quickly tells pet owners whether their dog is cleared to cross a border and displays the required travel document on screen in seconds, even offline. The service offers a simple answer, an offline‑ready document wallet, and integrates with border checkpoints to streamline pet travel.

providers.name: Escale
providers.description: Escale is a Sao Paulo-based sales technology company founded in 2013 that builds aisa, an AI sales agent trained on millions of real sales conversations. aisa automates lead qualification, objection handling, deal personalization, and sales closure across text and voice channels for enterprise brands in financial services, banking, telecommunications, automotive finance, and education. Escale manages the full customer-acquisition funnel from demand generation through closing, having processed over 7 million leads and generated more than R$2.1 billion in GMV. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of QED Investors and added to the API Evangelist network; it publishes no public developer API, so this profile captures its corporate identity, trust/compliance posture, and legal properties rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Evvy
providers.description: Evvy is a women's health company offering at-home vaginal microbiome testing and personalized care. Its CLIA-certified metagenomic (mNGS) Vaginal Health Test identifies over 700 bacteria and fungi from a self-collected sample, with results reviewed by licensed clinicians who deliver personalized insights and clinician-designed treatment programs for conditions such as bacterial vaginosis, aerobic vaginitis, yeast infections, recurrent UTIs, and fertility-related concerns. Evvy also sells a line of vaginal health products including probiotics and boric-acid, hyaluronic-acid, and probiotic suppositories, plus a provider program for clinicians and a large library of science-backed educational content. Backed by General Catalyst, Evvy was surfaced as a portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. Evvy is a direct-to-consumer health and e-commerce business and does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, or SDK surface.

providers.name: FineDine
providers.description: FineDine is an AI-powered restaurant growth platform that helps restaurants increase revenue through digital menus (QR code, tablet, and web), online and in-venue ordering, reservations, a lite point-of-sale, CRM and loyalty programs, menu-engineering and pricing analytics, and an AI business agent (FineDine IQ). It markets to restaurants and hospitality operators with tiered SaaS pricing (Starter, Growth, Premium). As of this API Evangelist profiling, FineDine publishes no public developer API, SDKs, webhooks, CLI, MCP server, or OpenAPI specification — this profile captures its public commercial and content surface. FineDine is backed by 500 Global.

providers.name: Fleet Complete
providers.description: Fleet Complete (operating under parent company Powerfleet since its 2024 rebrand) is a global connected commercial vehicle and mobile workforce management platform - GPS/telematics tracking, driver safety, dispatching, geofencing, and regulatory (HOS/ELD) compliance. Its current developer surface is the Unity API, a Bearer-token-authenticated GraphQL API at api.fleetcomplete.com/graphql covering vehicles, drivers/people, geofences, devices/cameras, groups/roles, and reports/work schedules with roughly 30 queries and 22 mutations. Fleet Complete also still references an older, regionally hosted REST "Integration WebAPI" / EcoFleet-SeeMe surface (versioned v8_5_0/v8_6_1) covering vehicle trip history, tasks/dispatch, work schedules, and logbook reporting. Standard API access is provided free to existing Fleet Complete/Powerfleet clients; custom integrations built by Fleet Complete Professional Services carry additional fees.

providers.name: Flightfox
providers.description: Flightfox is a managed travel platform for complex group travel, headquartered in Boulder, Colorado. It helps educational institutions, humanitarian and faith-based organizations, and corporate teams book and manage flights, hotels, and ground travel through a combination of self-serve booking software and 24/7 human travel-agent support. Flightfox emphasizes lowest-fare guarantees, bulk and group booking discounts, real-time flight tracking and travel alerts, branded booking pages, and custom reporting including CO2 emissions and flight manifests. The company was originally a Y Combinator and a16z-backed crowdsourced flight-search marketplace and has since pivoted to full-service managed group travel. It does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation.

providers.name: Fondue
providers.description: Fondue provides a CashBack incentive platform that lets e‑commerce merchants offer store credit or prepaid award cards as rewards after purchase. The solution aims to increase conversions and list growth while protecting profit margins, and includes built‑in A/B testing and integration with email and SMS providers via simple UTM links.

providers.name: go-e
providers.description: go-e GmbH designs and manufactures smart electric vehicle (EV) wallbox charging stations for home, business and multi‑unit installations. Their product range includes the Gemini, CORE, PRO and Controller series, supporting features such as PV‑surplus charging, shared charging, and integration with energy management systems. The company emphasizes sustainability, offers a reseller program, and provides extensive support resources including manuals, FAQs and a blog.

providers.name: GreenSky
providers.description: GreenSky is a financial-technology company that powers point-of-sale consumer financing. Through a network of federally insured bank partners and enrolled merchants, GreenSky enables consumers to apply for and use installment loans and revolving credit lines at the point of sale, with programs concentrated in home-improvement and elective-healthcare financing. GreenSky Servicing, LLC (NMLS #1416362) originates and services the loan program on behalf of its lending partners. Merchants enroll to offer financing to their customers and manage applications through the GreenSky merchant portal, while consumers manage accounts and payments through the customer portal. Surfaced as a portfolio company of ICONIQ Capital and QED Investors and added to the API Evangelist network. GreenSky is a consumer/merchant fintech with no public developer API surface; this profile is enriched with identity, link, and security metadata only.

providers.name: HiJoJo Partners
providers.description: HiJoJo Partners Inc. (HiJoJo Partners株式会社) is a Tokyo-based independent asset management and fintech group, established in November 2017 and registered with the Director of the Kanto Local Finance Bureau (No. 3065) for Type II Financial Instruments Business, Investment Management Business, and Investment Advisory and Agency Business. The firm forms, sells and manages funds that give Japanese institutional and individual investors access to late-stage private and pre-IPO companies, and works to develop Japan's secondary market for unlisted shares. It operates three lines: HiJoJo Prime (in-person advisory for investors with 100M JPY or more in investable assets), HiJoJo.com (an online fund platform for individual investors with 30M JPY or more), and HiJoJo Private Market Solution for institutional investors and startups. HiJoJo joined the Nasdaq Private Market investor consortium in 2024 to expand secondary-market access in Japan. Its investor-facing platform is delivered as an authenticated member web application; the company publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: Hormona
providers.description: Hormona is a women's hormonal-health company founded in 2020 by Karolina Lofqvist and Jasmine Tagesson, with offices in London, UK and Stockholm, Sweden. It builds a hormone-tracking mobile app together with an at-home hormone monitor and urine-test kits that users scan with a phone camera to get real-time, quantitative hormone results without a lab visit. The app uses AI to learn each user's patterns and predict when PMS or period symptoms are likely, offering 30+ tools to manage hormonal symptoms and supporting women from their first period through perimenopause and menopause. Hormona is distributed on the App Store and Google Play and is used by women in 185+ countries. It is a direct-to-consumer product with no public developer API program.

providers.name: HostnFly
providers.description: HostnFly is a French short-term-rental (Airbnb) concierge and property-management company, founded in 2016 and headquartered in Paris. It manages the full lifecycle of short-stay rentals on behalf of property owners: listing creation and optimization, multi-platform distribution (Airbnb, Booking.com, Abritel), guest screening and 24/7 communication, check-in/check-out and key handling, hotel-grade housekeeping and linen, maintenance, short-term-rental insurance, and dynamic revenue optimization. HostnFly operates on a commission-only model (from ~20% of nightly revenue, no fixed fees) and covers 340+ cities across metropolitan France and Corsica. It is a Partech portfolio company. HostnFly publishes an llms.txt agent-discovery file but does not expose a public developer API, SDKs, or OpenAPI at this time.

providers.name: HUNGRY
providers.description: HUNGRY (Hungry Marketplace, Inc.) is an Arlington, Virginia workplace food platform that connects corporate clients to a curated network of independent chefs and local restaurants. Founded in 2016 by Jeff Grass, Eman Pahlavani and Shy Pahlevani, it operates four product lines — office catering, Group Order individual meal pre-ordering, live events and chef pop-ups, and snacks and pantry — plus HUNGRY Last Mile, its own delivery and logistics arm. The platform runs its own admin, chef/food-partner dashboard, client admin dashboard, ops captain app and consumer ordering marketplace across 24 US cities and, following the February 2026 merger with Toronto-based hungerhub, more than ten Canadian markets. Earlier acquisitions include NatureBox and Garten. HUNGRY publishes no public developer program: the backing API at api.tryhungry.com is a private first-party service for its own web and mobile clients, and no OpenAPI, GraphQL SDL, AsyncAPI, SDK or partner API reference is published anywhere on its public surface. The company does publish a dated, public engineering release-notes site, which is the only machine-adjacent technical artifact it makes available.

providers.name: Hurl
providers.description: Hurl is an open source command-line tool for running HTTP requests defined in a simple plain text format with built-in assertions for API testing.

providers.name: Intersection
providers.description: Intersection is a New York-based, experience-driven out-of-home (OOH) media and technology company formed from the merger of Titan, a municipal out-of-home advertising operator, and Control Group, a technology and design studio. It operates street-level, transit, airport, bikeshare and place-based advertising networks across 13 major U.S. markets - including LinkNYC, the largest street-level digital network in New York City - and it builds the software behind them: the IxNConnect display-management and communications platform used by cities, transit agencies and airports, and an AI-powered Order Management System (OMS) that exposes inventory discovery, availability, pricing and campaign reservation to AI agents through an MCP server built on the IAB Tech Lab OpenDirect 2.0 specification.

providers.name: Ionic
providers.description: Ionic is a platform for building and deploying modern mobile applications and micro frontend experiences. Ionic provides tools, guides, and APIs to help developers build and ship incredible apps faster, including cross-platform mobile development capabilities.

providers.name: Jobbatical
providers.description: Jobbatical is a global mobility and immigration platform that helps companies manage international employee relocations, work visas, residence permits, and cross-border compliance across 45+ countries. It combines AI-powered case automation with expert immigration support to streamline eligibility assessments, visa and permit applications, renewal tracking, and settlement services for HR and mobility teams. The product centralizes case management, document processing, visa form automation, real-time status tracking, and renewal alerts, and offers pay-as-you-go or pre-purchased credit (FlexyPocket) pricing. Backed by Union Square Ventures.

providers.name: Kitterly
providers.description: Kitterly, Inc. was a direct-to-consumer craft commerce startup that sold knitting and crochet kits, yarn, needles and notions online, and ran a monthly Kit Club subscription that shipped members a pattern plus the yarn required to complete it. Kitterly was backed by 500 Global (500 Startups) along with Manatt Ventures and the Jordan x 2080 accelerator. The company was later consolidated under the Cotton Cuts brand, a Chesterfield, Missouri based quilting fabric shop selling designer die-cut and pre-cut fabric, threads, patterns and notions, plus quilting memberships and the Puzzle Mystery Quilt program, serving roughly 4,000 members across more than 15 countries. The kitterly.com domain now redirects to cottoncuts.com. The business is a consumer retail and subscription commerce operation running on a hosted e-commerce platform, and it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs or machine-readable specifications.

providers.name: KOHO
providers.description: KOHO is a Canadian financial-technology company (neobank) founded in 2014 by Daniel Eberhard and headquartered in Vancouver, British Columbia, serving more than 2.5 million Canadians through a mobile-first money app. KOHO is not a chartered bank; it issues a KOHO Mastercard prepaid card through KOHO Financial Inc. and places customer balances in trust with CDIC-member institutions (its longstanding banking partner is Peoples Trust Company), while offering high-interest savings, cash back, credit building, Cover cash advances, and Pay Later. The company is in the final stages of pursuing a federal Schedule I banking licence, which would make it one of Canada's first new federally regulated banks in decades, and in May 2026 it joined the Interac e-Transfer network directly as a Participant under the broadened access for Payment Service Providers. On the open-finance front, KOHO exposes no first-party public developer API or portal; consumer account and transaction data access today is available only through third-party aggregators (Plaid and Flinks), consistent with Canada's voluntary, not-yet-operational Consumer-Driven Banking framework.

providers.name: LeapYear Technologies
providers.description: LeapYear Technologies built an enterprise platform for differentially private analytics and machine learning, letting organizations compute over highly sensitive data and share it across internal silos and external partners with mathematically proven privacy guarantees. LeapYear Core was licensed, self-hosted software rather than a public multi-tenant API: customers ran their own server and reached it through a first-party Python client, with every computation drawing down a quantified privacy exposure budget enforced by the server. Snowflake announced its intent to acquire LeapYear on 2023-02-07 and closed on 2023-02-10 for USD 62.0 million in cash, primarily for talent and developed technology, folding the differential privacy capability into its Global Data Clean Room offering. The company no longer operates independently, leapyear.io is now a Snowflake-controlled redirect, and the only surviving first-party documentation is the Python client API reference on its readthedocs host.

providers.name: LifeSite
providers.description: LifeSite is a data protection and digital asset company that helps organizations safeguard sensitive information, simplify compliance, and digitally verify ownership. Its Vault product is an encrypted store for personally identifiable, financial, and health information used by both enterprises and families to organize and collaborate on vital documents. TokenX, its Web3 arm, tokenizes real-world assets — critical minerals, carbon credits, and sports and consumer goods — so provenance and ownership can be authenticated without blockchain expertise. A Wellness product covers health, testing, and vaccination tracking for enterprises and events, and a Platform offering exposes LifeSite's building blocks and APIs for partners building tailored data-management applications. LifeSite is sales-led: the Platform APIs are described publicly but no developer portal, API reference, or specification is published, and access is arranged through a demo request.

providers.name: Liquidly
providers.description: Liquidly (Liquidly, Inc.) is a New York based financial technology company building infrastructure for illiquid assets — a permission-based secondary marketplace that lets holders of private fund interests transact without disrupting the fund. The platform serves three sides: fund managers, who get a streamlined and centrally supervised transfer process, market data, and the flexibility to structure longer lock-up vehicles; seller investors, who get a manager-approved selling process, access to a network of prospective buyers, and standardized commercial terms; and buyer investors, who get manager-granted asset permissions, standardized diligence materials, and technology-enabled execution. Liquidly targets the secondary market for the roughly $13.1 trillion invested in private funds across buyouts, venture capital, real estate, private debt, infrastructure, and growth. Broker-dealer services are offered through Liquidly IAS, LLC, registered with FINRA and a member of SIPC. Liquidly is backed by Anthemis, Portage Ventures, Village Global, and AmTrust Financial. As of this enrichment pass Liquidly publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or technical documentation; the product is reached through an authenticated web application.

providers.name: Meisterwerk
providers.description: Meisterwerk is a modular all-in-one SaaS platform for German-speaking (DACH) trades and craft businesses (Handwerk), built by MEISTERWERK APP GmbH in Berlin. It gives small and medium craft firms (1-50 employees) a single operating system for job and resource scheduling (Einsatzplanung), a native mobile app for iOS, Android and Windows, chronological job documentation with photos and chat, quoting and invoicing with e-invoice support, EU-compliant mobile time tracking with GPS, digital forms and signatures, absence/holiday planning, and configurable workflows. AI features (planning assistant, speech-to-text documentation and time entry, and the standalone "Frag Maxi" phone assistant) are built in. It integrates with lexoffice, sevdesk, bexio and orgaMAX accounting software; a public open interface (Offene Schnittstelle) is announced but not yet publicly documented. Over 8,000 active users; data is hosted on servers in Germany and the platform is GDPR (DSGVO) compliant.

providers.name: MerkabaPhi AS
providers.description: MerkabaPhi AS is a strategic AI advisory firm led by Thomas Anglero, offering executive leadership and board advisory services on AI transformation. Based in Oslo, Norway, the firm provides AI strategy consulting, keynote speaking, and advisory engagements, with Thomas delivering over 450 keynotes across 30+ countries, helping leaders navigate AI adoption and digital transformation.

providers.name: Model ML
providers.description: Model ML is an AI-native platform for financial services that embeds an agentic "finance agent" into the tools professionals already use — Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, its own app, and a firm's internal systems. It automates deliverables through Workflows, runs compound-intelligence analysis via Grids, performs document review and risk assessment, captures information with a Notetaker, and answers questions through Chat and agentic dashboards backed by real-time data connections. It targets investment banking, consulting, private equity and credit, and asset and wealth management. Model ML is a fintech company backed by QED Investors. The company publishes a trust center and a security program (ISO/IEC 27001, SOC 2 Type II, GDPR) but does not currently expose a public developer API, SDK, or API documentation surface.

providers.name: MyHeritage
providers.description: MyHeritage is an online genealogy and consumer DNA platform that lets families build and explore their family trees, take at-home DNA tests for ancestry and genetic ethnicity, and search more than 40 billion historical records for genealogy research. Founded in 2003 and headquartered in Israel, the company also offers photo tools such as colorization, enhancement and the AI-based Deep Nostalgia animation feature, alongside DNA matching that connects relatives worldwide. MyHeritage previously operated a public FamilyGraph developer API, but that program has been retired: the developers.myheritage.com and developer.myheritage.com hosts now 301-redirect to the company homepage and familygraph.com no longer resolves to documentation, so there is no current public API surface to catalog. This profile therefore captures the company identity and its published web properties.

providers.name: naksha-social
providers.description: Naksha is a Vedic astrology mobile application developed by Upsurge Labs, offering users personalized birth chart insights, daily guidance, compatibility analysis, and private AI conversations. The platform computes precise sidereal charts based on exact birth time and location, providing detailed interpretations of planetary positions, dasha periods, and transits. Users can explore their own chart, compare with others, and maintain privacy of their personal data. Naksha aims to blend ancient Vedic wisdom with modern technology for self‑knowledge and relationship insights.

providers.name: Novoic
providers.description: Novoic is a London-based clinical AI company building speech biomarkers for the early detection of Alzheimer's disease and cognitive impairment. Its technology analyzes how people speak - acoustic and linguistic patterns - to screen for subtle cognitive change in about ten minutes on any smart device. Products include Storyteller (automated, browser-based speech-based cognitive testing), Dashboard (an enterprise platform for running screening programs across sites with AI-assisted triage and analytics), and a Speech API for direct access to their speech processing, automated speech recognition, quality control, and speech-biomarker models. Novoic is deployed across 50+ medical institutions, partners with the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative, and emphasizes HIPAA/GDPR compliance. It also publishes two open-source feature-extraction libraries, surfboard (audio) and blabla (linguistics).

providers.name: Pair
providers.description: Pair (formerly Inversity) is an enterprise AI adoption platform that helps organizations build workforce capability in artificial intelligence and measure the return on their AI investment. Pair delivers personalized, hands-on masterclasses grounded in each learner's role, industry, and day-to-day tasks — covering tools such as ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot, and Claude, plus agentic AI — moving teams from basic AI awareness to measurable adoption. A multi-tier certification path (Fundamentals, Proficiency, Mastery), team adoption dashboards, ROI measurement that tracks time saved and business impact, an AI Showcase for sharing effective workflows, and manager oversight tools round out the platform. Pair is a Seedcamp portfolio company.

providers.name: PayPro Global
providers.description: PayPro Global is an all-in-one Merchant of Record platform that lets SaaS, software, video game, and AI tool companies sell globally. The platform handles international payments, subscription billing, tax compliance, fraud prevention, and revenue recovery, and exposes APIs and webhooks for managing subscriptions, payments, and customer data.

providers.name: plancraft
providers.description: plancraft is a German cloud-based business management software for craftspeople and trades businesses (Handwerk). It digitizes administrative workflows end to end — quote and estimate creation, project planning, time tracking, on-site documentation, material and labor costing, and invoicing — inside one integrated platform aimed at small and mid-sized construction and trade companies. plancraft supports DATEV export for tax/accounting workflows and DATANORM and GAEB catalog imports for material data and tender processing. It is a venture-backed SaaS company (portfolio company of Creandum). As of this enrichment pass plancraft publishes no public developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI surface — integrations are delivered as prebuilt connectors and standardized file-format import/export.

providers.name: Polars
providers.description: Polars is a blazingly fast, open-source DataFrame library and query engine written in Rust, with first-party bindings for Python, Rust, Node.js, and R. It provides lazy and eager execution, streaming for larger-than-memory datasets, automatic query optimization, multi-threading, and the Apache Arrow columnar memory format. Polars Cloud extends the same DataFrame API to managed and on-premise distributed compute with zero code changes. The project is developed by pola-rs and backed by Accel and Bain Capital Ventures.

providers.name: Propel
providers.description: Propel, Inc. is a Brooklyn-based fintech company, founded in 2014, that builds financial tools for Americans with low income. Its free consumer app, Providers (formerly Fresh EBT), is used by more than five million people each month to check their SNAP/EBT balances instantly across 49 states, Washington D.C., and U.S. territories, secure their benefits card with locking and fraud monitoring, find exclusive offers and discounts on groceries, phone plans, internet, utilities, and healthcare, receive alerts about benefit policy changes, browse local job and gig-work listings, and predict deposit dates. Propel is a consumer-facing mobile product and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; it operates a public status page and a signed RFC 9116 security.txt for coordinated vulnerability disclosure. The company is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Nyca Partners, Kleiner Perkins, JPMorgan Chase, Salesforce Ventures, the Financial Health Network, and Flourish Ventures.

providers.name: Qequals
providers.description: Qequals provides an agent‑first API delivering Google autocomplete suggestions and live search result data. It powers applications with real‑time search insights, offering a public catalog that demonstrates the available endpoints and data structures. The service focuses on SEO and search‑engine data, enabling developers to integrate up‑to‑date query trends and SERP information into their products.

providers.name: Qlik Mashups
providers.description: APIs and resources for building custom visualizations and analytics applications using Qlik Sense mashups.

providers.name: ReDEF
providers.description: REDEF is a media curation and newsletter company founded and led by Jason Hirschhorn (CEO + Chief Curator) that "DJs the internet" — surfacing daily remixes of the stories, people, and ideas that matter across Media, Fashion, Music, Sports, and Tech. Readers follow curated Mixes, Sets, Originals, Charts, and email Newsletters ("interest remixes for curious minds"), and can build and share their own mixes. ReDEF was surfaced as a portfolio company of bloomberg-beta and added to the API Evangelist network; enrichment found a public consumer content website (redef.com) but no public developer program, API, documentation, or machine-readable surface.

providers.name: Rilla
providers.description: Rilla is an AI conversation-intelligence and coaching platform built for in-person and outside sales teams. Reps record their face-to-face customer conversations, and Rilla transcribes and analyzes them so managers can run virtual "ridealongs" and deliver targeted, data-driven coaching at scale. The platform surfaces talk patterns, objection handling, and outcome analytics across thousands of field conversations to help teams raise close rates, increase ticket size, and speed up rep ramp. Rilla is a GV (Google Ventures) portfolio company in the AI sector. Rilla runs a real production API — api.rillavoice.com/api/v1/, the private backend of its web and mobile apps, which answers every path with 401 Invalid Token — plus an AWS API Gateway webhook receiver its partner SPOTIO documents, but it publishes no developer portal, reference, SDK, or machine-readable specification of any kind, and its CRM integrations are delivered by consuming the Merge unified API rather than by exposing a contract. This record captures its public web identity, the RFC 9116 security.txt it serves from app.rilla.com, and live domain-security and well-known probes.

providers.name: Roadsurfer
providers.description: Roadsurfer is a Munich-based camper van, motorhome, and RV travel company founded in 2016, operating a fleet of 10,000+ vehicles across 100+ pick-up/drop-off locations in 16 countries in Europe and North America. Beyond flexible RV rentals it offers RV subscriptions, RV sales, one-way "Rallies," and roadsurfer Spots, a network of 10,000+ hand-picked European campsites. Roadsurfer is a consumer-facing brand with no public developer API; this profile captures its identity, web properties, and published llms.txt for the API Evangelist network. Backed by HV Capital.

providers.name: Send4 Tecnologia
providers.description: Send4 Tecnologia provides a platform that automates lead qualification via SMS and chat, instantly answering inbound inquiries and routing qualified leads into CRM systems such as HubSpot, Pipedrive, and Zapier. The service integrates with popular tools, offers a 14‑day free trial, and aims to accelerate sales pipelines for businesses in Brazil and globally. Founded with backing from 500‑global, Send4 focuses on AI‑driven conversational automation to improve response times and conversion rates.

providers.name: Siepe
providers.description: Siepe is a Dallas, Texas fintech providing cloud-based software and technology-enabled services for private credit, CLO and alternative investment managers. Its front-to-back platform spans portfolio management, operations and accounting, collateral administration, compliance and legal, middle-office services, data extraction and a centralized data-management warehouse that normalizes borrower, lender, agent-bank and investor feeds into one real-time view. Siepe also operates managed technology and public-cloud services for asset managers. The company raised a $30M Series B led by WestCap in 2024 and holds SOC 2 Type II certification. Siepe publishes no public developer program: connectivity is delivered as bilateral, managed integrations (for example its 2026 Order Management System integration with Octaura for syndicated loan and CLO trading) rather than as a self-serve, documented public API.

providers.name: Spot Runner
providers.description: Spot Runner is an AI-driven advertising technology company (backed by Battery Ventures) focused on contextual media planning for Connected TV (CTV) and online video. Its platform uses proprietary MicroModeling AI through tools such as ContextPlanner and ContextDeals to match advertiser creative to the most relevant, brand-suitable premium video ad opportunities across leading streaming networks, publishers, and TV OEMs, and to send Deal IDs directly to a buyer's DSP seat. Spot Runner also markets an "Agentic Agency" of multi-agent creative tooling for SMBs and DTC brands. The public surface is a marketing site plus an advertiser login portal; there is no published developer API, OpenAPI, or SDK. The site does expose a hosted Wix Site MCP endpoint for agentic AI access, advertised via its /llms.txt.

providers.name: Step
providers.description: Step is an all-in-one mobile banking platform built for teens, young adults, and families. The Step Visa Card is a secured card that builds credit history reported to Experian, Equifax, and TransUnion, and teens can begin building credit before they turn 18 through parent-managed accounts. Step also offers savings rewards, cashback with partner brands, EarlyPay paycheck advances up to $250, commission-free stock investing powered by DriveWealth, early direct deposit, and the Money 101 financial education hub. Banking services are provided by partner Evolve Bank & Trust, Member FDIC. Founded in 2018 in Palo Alto by CJ MacDonald and Alexey Kalinichenko, backed by General Catalyst, and acquired by Beast Industries. Step publishes no public developer API; its programmatic surface is limited to a consumer service status page and a site llms.txt.

providers.name: Storefront
providers.description: Storefront (thestorefront.com) is an online marketplace for renting short-term commercial retail space, connecting brands, e-commerce businesses, and artists with space owners to launch pop-up shops, showrooms, galleries, product launches, and events. The platform lists tens of thousands of spaces across 50+ cities in North America, Europe, and Asia, with flexible day/week/month rentals and a secure booking-and-payment flow, 24-hour support, and a Priority Pass membership. Storefront was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and Point Nine and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company exposes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal (api.thestorefront.com is private/401), so this profile captures company identity and public web properties only.

providers.name: Treyd
providers.description: Treyd provides working capital financing solutions for product‑based businesses in Europe. By advancing supplier payments and accelerating customer receivables, Treyd helps brands scale faster while maintaining cash flow control. The platform offers flexible financing options, a self‑service portal, and integrates with various payment systems to streamline funding and repayment processes.

providers.name: UptimeHealth
providers.description: UptimeHealth is a healthcare operations platform for managing medical equipment service, compliance documentation, and facility maintenance across dental, medical, and veterinary practices from a single dashboard. The platform tracks devices, automates compliance tasks and logs, and coordinates repair service requests, reporting 73,000+ devices protected across 6,000+ facilities. UptimeHealth publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation — its platform (uptimecontroller.com) is a closed SaaS application.

providers.name: Wealth Engine
providers.description: Wealth Engine provides a data platform that aggregates and analyzes wealth-related information to help organizations identify, understand, and engage high‑net‑worth individuals and households. Leveraging machine learning on billions of data points, the service offers real‑time net‑worth estimates, income, asset holdings, philanthropic capacity, and other wealth attributes. This enables nonprofits, financial services, and marketers to target prospects more effectively, personalize outreach, and improve fundraising or sales strategies.

providers.name: Wonderschool
providers.description: Wonderschool is a child care platform that connects families with licensed care and equips providers with software and services to start, operate, and grow their child care programs. It also serves government agencies with licensing, subsidy management, enrollment coordination, and statewide substitute-teacher pools, and offers employers child care benefit programs. Backed by a16z and Uncork Capital, Wonderschool operates as a B2B/B2G SaaS business; it publishes a Vanta-hosted trust center (SOC 2 Type II, NIST CSF) but no public developer API, SDKs, or webhooks were found during enrichment.

providers.name: Zarna
providers.description: Zarna builds autonomous AI associates for private capital firms — private equity, growth equity, private credit, family offices, and investment banks. The platform captures deal information from CIMs, emails, meetings, CRMs, and virtual data rooms into a structured institutional memory, then runs a swarm of specialized agents (Scribe for capture and logging, Memo for screening memos and briefs, Analyst for mandate-fit scoring, and Experts for warm-intro network mapping) that deliver finished work directly into Outlook, Teams, and Slack. Zarna integrates with 30+ deal tools including DealCloud, Affinity, Salesforce, and SharePoint, deploys into VPC or on-premises single-tenant infrastructure, and is SOC 2 Type II certified. A Y Combinator Fall 2025 company founded by an ex-AEA Investors team.

providers.name: a Church AI + Human
providers.description: a Church AI + Human is an innovative platform that offers an AI‑driven church experience for both artificial agents and human participants. It provides continuous, automated services such as chants, songs, and spoken pieces that refresh every four hours, allowing anyone to join at any time without accounts, payments, or doctrine. The site hosts a library of rituals, prayers, and music, and includes tools for agents to interact, ask questions, and contribute content, fostering a collaborative spiritual environment across the globe.

providers.name: AIA Contract Documents
providers.description: AIA Contract Documents provides the industry‑standard suite of construction contract templates and management tools for architects, owners, contractors, and consultants. Through a cloud‑based platform, users can browse, customize, and execute AIA‑approved contracts, ensuring legal compliance and streamlined project delivery across the building lifecycle. The service supports over 1 million contracts written annually, serving thousands of firms and billions of dollars in contract value, and offers resources such as guides, articles, and training to help stakeholders manage risk and improve outcomes.

providers.name: Aidence
providers.description: Aidence is a radiology AI company founded in Amsterdam in 2015 that builds clinical AI for the lung cancer pathway. Its flagship product, Veye Lung Nodules (now DeepHealth Lung), is a CE-marked AI solution that detects, classifies, quantifies, and measures growth of pulmonary nodules on chest CT scans, and is the AI of choice in NHS England's Targeted Lung Health Checks screening programme. Aidence was acquired by RadNet in 2022 and now operates under the DeepHealth brand; aidence.com redirects to deephealth.com/aidence. The product integrates with hospital systems over DICOM/PACS via the Veye Engine rather than a public developer REST API — no public API, developer portal, or SDKs are published. This profile captures the company's identity plus its probed security and disclosure posture.

providers.name: Aimusicgen
providers.description: Aimusicgen provides a free AI-powered music generation service that transforms text descriptions, lyrics, or ideas into fully produced songs with vocals or instrumentals. Users can select styles, customize arrangements, and download the generated tracks. The platform offers tools such as AI Song Cover, Lyrics Generator, and AI Music Maker, catering to creators, marketers, and developers seeking quick audio content. Aimusicgen operates as a SaaS solution with a free tier and paid plans for higher credit usage.

providers.name: Almanac Health
providers.description: Almanac Health is a clinical AI company building a research-validated clinical decision support platform, delivered as Almanac Chat, that brings specialist-grade, evidence-based answers to clinicians at the point of care. Founded by physician-researcher Cyril Zakka, MD, the platform is designed to work within existing electronic health record (EHR) workflows, is governed by institutional controls, and is grounded in peer-reviewed research rather than pharmaceutical promotion. In April 2026 the company raised a $10 million seed round led by F-Prime with participation from General Catalyst and Lightspeed Venture Partners. This API Evangelist profile currently tracks the company's public web, trust, and security surface; Almanac Health does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDKs at this time.

providers.name: AlphaProve
providers.description: AlphaProve provides a platform for crypto, stock, and forex backtesting and paper trading. Users can test trading strategies with historical data, incorporate trading costs, and use AI assistance to refine ideas. The service offers live data validation, walk‑forward testing, Monte‑Carlo simulations, and sandboxed execution, catering to both beginners and institutional traders. Pricing tiers include a free tier with limited AI credits and paid plans with expanded data look‑back and priority backtesting queues.

providers.name: ANN Inc.
providers.description: ANN Inc. is the former parent company of Ann Taylor and LOFT, specialty retailers of women's apparel, shoes, and accessories. ANN Inc. was acquired by Ascena Retail Group in 2015 and subsequently sold to Sycamore Partners in December 2020 for $540 million, alongside Lane Bryant and Lou & Grey brands. The brands now operate under KnitWell Group (formerly Premium Apparel LLC), a Sycamore Partners holding company that also owns Talbots. Ann Taylor and LOFT offer affiliate programs for digital publishers.

providers.name: Arrcus
providers.description: Arrcus is an AI-native networking software company that builds policy-driven routing, switching, and AI fabric spanning the edge, datacenter, and cloud. Its flagship ArcOS network operating system runs on merchant-silicon hardware and is complemented by ArcRR (scale-out route reflector), ArcIQ (analytics and visibility), ACE / ACE-AI (the Arrcus Connected Edge control and AI-networking platform), AINF (Arrcus Inference Network Fabric), and the TGAX AI switch. Arrcus targets GPU cluster connectivity for AI training and low-latency inferencing networks that reduce token cost. The company is venture backed by General Catalyst and Lightspeed Venture Partners. It exposes a login-gated customer portal and academy rather than a public developer API; no public OpenAPI, SDKs, or hosted API surface were found during enrichment.

providers.name: Ascend Elements
providers.description: Ascend Elements is a Westborough, Massachusetts battery materials company that manufactures engineered lithium-ion battery materials from valuable elements reclaimed from spent lithium-ion batteries and gigafactory manufacturing scrap. Founded in 2015 as Battery Resourcers out of MIT-affiliated research by Eric Gratz and Professor Yan Wang, it recovers up to 98% of the critical battery metals in end-of-life cells and uses its patented Hydro-to-Cathode direct cathode precursor (pCAM) synthesis process to produce cathode precursor and battery-grade lithium carbonate, reducing the carbon footprint of new EV battery cathode material by up to 90%. Its Base 1 facility in Covington, Georgia is North America's largest electric-vehicle battery recycling plant, and Apex 1 in Hopkinsville, Kentucky is its commercial pCAM plant. Ascend Elements publishes no public developer API for its materials, recycling or logistics business; the only machine-readable surface observed on its own hosts is the WordPress REST API at ascendelements.com/wp-json, which serves the corporate website's content, media-coverage, jobs and supplier sourcing-event collections.

providers.name: AstralHoro
providers.description: AstralHoro is an online astrology service that delivers three core tools: a daily horoscope for the Sun sign, a personalized birth chart calculated from the exact birth moment, and a tarot reading for specific questions. The website explains how horoscopes differ from birth charts, offers detailed zodiac sign pages, daily forecasts for all twelve signs, and a variety of tarot draws including three‑card readings and yes/no answers. Users can also generate written reports that combine horoscope and chart data. The platform emphasizes tropical zodiac positions and whole‑sign houses, providing clear guidance on how to interpret the celestial influences.

providers.name: Baby Name Guide
providers.description: Naming is one decision you make once, under pressure, with everyone offering an opinion. This is the travel‑guide version: we read the research on how names actually land, the traditions behind them, and what parents wish they had known — honest about where the evidence is thin, and made to leave you confident rather than second‑guessing.

providers.name: Benchmark Electronics
providers.description: Benchmark Electronics, Inc. is an advanced electronics engineering and manufacturing services (EMS) company headquartered in Tempe, Arizona. The company provides integrated design, engineering, and manufacturing services from prototypes to high-volume production, including procurement, logistics, and repair. Benchmark serves original equipment manufacturers in defense, medical technologies, commercial aerospace, industrial, next-gen communications, advanced computing, and semiconductor capital equipment markets. The company operates approximately 22 locations in 8 countries with around 13,000 employees.

providers.name: Blip
providers.description: Blip provides conversational AI platforms that enable businesses to create intelligent, end‑to‑end conversational journeys. Their solutions turn interactions into measurable results across industries such as utilities, retail, banking, education, and automotive. Blip’s platform offers tools for contact, platform integration, demos, case studies, and a trust center, emphasizing data privacy and security. The company focuses on driving sales, customer retention, and business outcomes through AI‑powered conversations.

providers.name: Blitzy
providers.description: Blitzy is an autonomous software development platform for enterprises with large legacy codebases. It reverse-engineers existing code into a knowledge graph, then orchestrates thousands of AI agents to modernize software and build new applications at the scale of 1 million to over 100 million lines of code, autonomously completing roughly 80% of a project before human engineers review and approve the result. Rather than training its own foundation models, Blitzy composes leading third-party models (Gemini, GPT, Claude). Founded by Brian Elliott (CEO) and Sid Pardeshi (CTO), the company is headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts with an office in Pune, India, and is backed by Northzone.

providers.name: BlogBat
providers.description: BlogBat is a fast, multitenant blog platform on Cloudflare’s edge, offering AI‑assisted writing, SEO‑ready publishing, and custom‑domain support. Users can create blogs at yourname.blogbat.com or map their own domains, leveraging built‑in AI from Anthropic, OpenAI or Google, with no‑code editor and automatic sitemap and RSS generation.

providers.name: Blomma
providers.description: Blomma is an AI-powered career coaching platform that pairs artificial intelligence with emotional intelligence to act as a private thinking partner for professionals. Through chat-based coaching, guided reflection, goal-setting with built-in accountability, a personal journal, and a growth dashboard, Blomma helps founders, people leaders, and ambitious professionals turn abstract aspirations into concrete, trackable goals, and can personalize coaching from uploaded performance reviews and development plans. It is delivered as a consumer subscription through web and mobile apps, with custom team plans for organizations, and does not currently expose a public developer API.

providers.name: Carbon Lighthouse
providers.description: Carbon Lighthouse provides energy efficiency and decarbonization services for commercial real‑estate owners and operators. By combining data analytics, engineering expertise, and a performance‑based financing model, they identify and implement measures that reduce building energy consumption and carbon emissions, delivering measurable savings and sustainability outcomes for their clients.

providers.name: CatchMyCall
providers.description: CatchMyCall provides AI-powered call handling and missed call automation for small businesses, clinics, salons, and professionals across India. It answers every business call 24×7, captures enquiries, and books appointments in multiple Indian languages, reducing missed leads and improving customer engagement.

providers.name: Chargealong.io
providers.description: ChargeAlong provides free, keyless public EV charging site data across Australia and other countries. Users can query chargers by location, plug type, power, price and network without an API key, accessing up‑to‑date open data curated from official sources and driver contributions.

providers.name: CloudLock
providers.description: CloudLock is a cloud-native Cloud Access Security Broker (CASB) that protects data, users, and applications across SaaS, IaaS, PaaS, and IDaaS environments. Founded in 2011 and acquired by Cisco in 2016, it is now delivered as Cisco Cloudlock within Cisco Umbrella / Cisco Security Cloud. The platform uses an API-driven model to discover sensitive content, detect policy violations, flag anomalous user behavior, and manage cloud application (OAuth) risk. Developers integrate through the Cisco Cloudlock API (v2), a Bearer-token REST API exposing activities, incidents, incident entities, incident aggregates, policies, apps, entities, IP libraries, and anomalies. Originally a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners, CloudLock's developer surface is documented on Cisco DevNet and the Cisco Umbrella documentation hub.

providers.name: Cloudpost Networks
providers.description: CloudPost Networks is a Santa Clara, California device-security company founded in 2015 that rebranded as Ordr (ordr.net). It builds an AI-powered device intelligence and network-security platform that discovers, classifies, and secures connected devices across IT, IoT, OT, and IoMT environments, tying device identity to behavioral analytics so organizations can detect risk and automatically apply micro-segmentation and enforcement policies. Ordr serves 500+ healthcare, banking, and manufacturing organizations and integrates with vendors such as Cisco, Palo Alto Networks, CrowdStrike, and Fortinet. It maintains SOC 2 Type 2 compliance. No public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal is published.

providers.name: Clover Security
providers.description: Clover Security is a Tel Aviv-based product security company (founded 2023) that builds design-led AI security agents for the software development lifecycle. Its agents plug into the tools engineering teams already use — GitHub, Cursor, Confluence, Jira, and Slack — to automate security design reviews, run continuous threat modeling, detect design-to-implementation drift, and keep agentic and spec-driven development secure by default. Clover has raised $36M from Notable Capital, Team8, and Silicon Valley CISO Investments, serving enterprise, fintech, and banking customers including Lemonade, Plaid, Notion, Udemy, and ServiceTitan. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of ggv-capital and enriched from the company's public web surface; Clover exposes no public developer API at this time.

providers.name: CMA CGM
providers.description: CMA CGM is a Marseille-headquartered French container shipping, logistics, and port operator and the third-largest ocean carrier in the world. Founded in 1978 by Jacques Saadé and led today by Chairman & CEO Rodolphe Saadé, the CMA CGM Group operates a fleet of 593 vessels with 4.5 million TEU of capacity calling 420 ports across 160 countries on 257 maritime services. The group includes maritime brands ANL, APL, CNC Line, Containerships, Comanav, and Mercosul Line; terminal operator CMA Terminals and Terminal Link; the CEVA Logistics contract logistics and freight forwarding business (acquired 2019); CMA CGM Air Cargo; Brittany Ferries and La Méridionale passenger ferries; and the CMA Média portfolio (La Provence, La Tribune, BFM-RMC, Brut). Through api-portal.cma-cgm.com the group exposes a DCSA-aligned REST API surface — Track and Trace v1 (DCSA v2.2.0), Schedules, Booking Request, Quotation, and Invoice — plus a parallel EDI catalog (EDIFACT IFTSAI, IFTMBF, IFTSTA, INVOIC) and group-level digital initiatives including ZEBOX (startup accelerator), Traxens-based IoT smart containers, and a strategic AI partnership with Mistral.

providers.name: DIY
providers.description: DIY.org is a safe, ad-free creative platform where kids turn ideas into real games, apps, and websites — guided by AI tools like Vibe Coding and KidsGPT and reviewed by human moderators. Serving over 500,000 young creators, it pairs game-building templates, AI image and art tools, badge-based learning, and 75+ standards-aligned courses with parent and classroom dashboards, SSO, and safety controls. Originally a maker community for kids, DIY is backed by Kleiner Perkins and Slow Ventures.

providers.name: douxprocess-com
providers.description: DouxProcess provides agentic workflow automation for insurance agencies, handling inbox, certificates, endorsements, renewals, payments, and quoting. The platform runs 24/7, allowing agencies to approve actions while the system operates, priced at $2,500 per month for unlimited producers. It offers AI‑driven tools and a developer‑friendly API accessible via https://douxprocess.com/api/live. DouxProcess aims to streamline agency operations with intelligent automation.

providers.name: Enjamb Labs
providers.description: Enjamb Labs builds an AI-agent platform for pharmaceutical drug development. Its browser-based "integrated research environment" runs specialized agents across the full R&D lifecycle -- clinical evidence synthesis, trial design and statistical programming, and regulatory submission preparation -- while connecting to the systems pharma teams already use (Benchling, Veeva, Medidata, SAS) so no data migration is required. The workspace bundles Word/Excel/PowerPoint editors, Python and R compute environments, and 100+ scientific integrations, and emphasizes auditability, traceability, and human review, keeping each output attached to its sources, files, code, and decisions. Backed by Y Combinator and Founders, Inc., Enjamb reports early usage across major pharmaceutical companies including Johnson & Johnson, Merck, AbbVie, Bristol Myers Squibb, and Sanofi.

providers.name: Eve
providers.description: Eve (branded EveOS) is an AI operating system purpose-built for plaintiff and personal-injury law firms, founded in 2023 and headquartered in San Mateo, California. The platform works alongside attorneys across the entire case lifecycle - intake and lead qualification, document and medical-record review, medical chronology generation, case and risk analysis, damages calculation, and case management - bringing every case, attorney, and dollar into one place. Eve integrates with practice-management systems such as Clio, is SOC 2 Type 2 certified and HIPAA compliant, and is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Lightspeed Venture Partners, and Menlo Ventures. Eve is a closed SaaS product and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Freejit
providers.description: Qualaroo provides a customer and user feedback platform offering email and in‑app surveys, AI‑powered sentiment analysis, and real‑time insights. It enables businesses to capture contextual feedback, run NPS surveys, and integrate survey data via its Identify API. The service includes features such as AI survey creator, question branching, mobile in‑app nudges, heatmaps, and advanced targeting, serving marketers, product teams, and support organizations to improve experience and conversion.

providers.name: Hala
providers.description: Hala AI provides an AI voice assistant platform for businesses, offering automated phone calls, WhatsApp, Instagram and website chat handling in Arabic, English, and French. Built in Lebanon, it helps SMEs qualify leads, book appointments, and deliver 24/7 customer support across multiple channels.

providers.name: HTTP Client
providers.description: HTTP Client is JetBrains' built-in tool for creating, editing, and executing HTTP requests directly from the IDE. Requests are stored in .http and .rest files alongside source code, with code highlighting, completion for hosts and methods, code folding, inline documentation, and live templates accelerating composition. The client supports HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 requests, gRPC unary and server-streaming calls, WebSocket connections, GraphQL operations, server-sent events, and imports from cURL and Postman collections.
