providers.description: Selency is the leading European online marketplace for vintage furniture and second-hand home decor. Founded in Paris in 2014 (formerly Brocante Lab), it connects individual sellers and professional antique dealers with buyers around a curated catalog of more than 300,000 unique pieces: Scandinavian, art deco, mid-century, 20th-century and contemporary design, lighting, mirrors, rugs and decorative objects. Selency acts as a trusted third party, editorially validating each listing and arranging specialized furniture delivery across Europe. It is a B Corp certified consumer marketplace with French, UK and Netherlands storefronts. No public developer API is offered.

providers.name: Silo Finance
providers.description: Silo Finance is a decentralized, non-custodial lending protocol built around isolated money markets. Each market pairs a single collateral asset with a borrowable asset in its own risk silo, so the failure or manipulation of one asset cannot cascade into unrelated markets — the isolation model that distinguishes Silo from pooled lenders. The protocol is delivered as onchain smart contracts (Silo V1, V2 and V3) deployed across Ethereum and other EVM chains, with an application at silo.finance, developer and protocol-architecture documentation at docs.silo.finance, third-party security audits, and an open GitHub organization publishing the contracts, subgraph and indexer. Silo Finance is backed by Electric Capital and is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a DeFi lending provider.

providers.name: Superfeedr
providers.description: Superfeedr provides a real-time feed API that pushes RSS and Atom updates instantly via PubSubHubbub. It enables publishers and subscribers to deliver content as soon as it changes, offering a simple Push API for developers, content publishers, and application teams.

providers.name: Tealet
providers.description: Tealet is a wholesale tea marketplace that connects independent tea growers and family farms directly with retailers and businesses. Buyers browse, trace, and order specialty teas sourced from family farms and cooperatives across 8 countries and 15 growing regions, with grower profiles, farm videos, subscription ordering, and a wholesale request flow that emphasize transparency and direct trade from source to cup. Tealet originated in Hawaii and is backed by 500 Startups and Blue Startups. The company operates a consumer/B2B web storefront with account sign-up, newsletter, and blog; it does not currently publish a public developer API, documentation, SDKs, or an MCP server.

providers.name: Thames Water
providers.description: Thames Water is the UK’s largest water and wastewater company, serving 16 million customers across London and the Thames Valley. It provides water supply, wastewater treatment, and related services, focusing on sustainability, community, and environmental stewardship.

providers.name: The Cirqle
providers.description: The Cirqle provides an AI‑powered influencer marketing platform that connects brands with creators to run performance‑driven campaigns. Its end‑to‑end solution includes creator discovery, AI‑generated briefs, automated contracts, rights management, and detailed ROAS forecasting. By integrating with major ad and e‑commerce networks, The Cirqle enables brands to turn organic creator content into scalable advertising, offering real‑time reporting, affiliate tracking, and a marketplace for creator‑driven ads. The platform aims to maximize ROI for advertisers while simplifying workflow for creators.

providers.name: TIFIN
providers.description: TIFIN is a Boulder, Colorado based fintech company founded in 2018 by Dr. Vinay Nair that builds AI-driven wealth technology for financial advisors, RIAs, broker-dealers, asset managers and insurance firms. Its platforms span TIFIN.AI (an agentic operating system consolidating the group's AI businesses for wealth and asset management workflows), TIFIN Wealth (investment proposal, risk-capacity and client-personalization tooling that integrates with Fidelity, BNY Pershing, Black Diamond, Salesforce, Wealthbox, Redtail, Orion and iRebal), TIFIN AMP/AG for asset-manager distribution intelligence, TIFIN Give for charitable giving accounts, TIFIN @Work for workplace financial wellness, and Magnifi, an AI investing assistant. TIFIN incubated 55ip (sold to J.P. Morgan) and Paralel, and announced a joint venture, TIFIN.AI, with J.P. Morgan Asset Management. The company states its AI capabilities are available as APIs that plug into existing wealthtech stacks, but publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable contract; access is gated behind a "Get access" request form.

providers.name: Tofu
providers.description: Tofu offers AI‑driven candidate fraud detection, deepfake detection, and resume screening for recruiting and security teams. The platform connects to an applicant tracking system (ATS) and flags identity theft, impersonation, synthetic identities, deepfakes, and proxy interviewers across the hiring funnel. It provides a Fraud API and Deepfake API for platforms and a Chrome extension for recruiter verification.

providers.name: TranZak
providers.description: TranZak is an African fintech platform headquartered in Douala, Cameroon, providing REST APIs for mobile money collections, merchant payments, bulk disbursements, bill payments, and SMS services across sub-Saharan Africa. The platform bridges banked and unbanked populations by supporting MTN Mobile Money, Orange Money, and CEMAC bank networks, with sandbox and production environments, webhook notifications, and support for up to 2,000 recipients in a single bulk payment request.

providers.name: Trelora
providers.description: Trelora is a technology-driven, full-service discount real estate brokerage founded in Denver, Colorado and now operating as part of HomeSmart. It lets people buy and sell homes for a low, transparent fee instead of the traditional percentage-based commission, helping sellers save thousands of dollars and offering buyers cash-back rebates of up to several thousand dollars at closing. Trelora pairs salaried, non-commissioned real estate agents with an online platform and IDX-powered property search across markets including Colorado, Washington, and other U.S. states, and publishes a real estate blog, glossary, and city-level market reports. Originally a Techstars-backed startup, Trelora is consumer-facing and does not currently expose a public developer API.

providers.name: Tripitaca
providers.description: Tripitaca is a Kenya-based travel and hospitality booking marketplace where travelers get the best deals when they travel and where property owners list their properties. The platform lets travelers receive offers from hosts and hotels, while hosts create curated packages and special offers, see travelers interested in their area, and make them offers. Coverage spans destinations including Nairobi, Mombasa, Nakuru, Kisumu, and Maasai Mara safari experiences. Backed by 500 Global.

providers.name: Tungee
providers.description: Tungee (Guangzhou Tungee Technology Co., Ltd., 探迹科技) is a Chinese AI sales-intelligence company backed by Qiming Venture Partners. Its Tungee AI Sales Cloud covers the full B2B sales cycle -- AI prospecting over a 300M+ company knowledge graph, inbound capture, outreach via call center, SMS, and email, and an AI CRM -- plus a Sales GPT agent line, a mobile app, and a DingTalk edition. The group also operates Futern, an international B2B leads product, and reports 50,000+ customers. Tungee publishes no public developer portal or API documentation.

providers.name: UK Met Office
providers.description: The UK Met Office is the United Kingdom’s national weather service, providing weather and climate data, forecasts, warnings and scientific research. It offers public weather services, data APIs, and expertise to support businesses, government and the public in understanding and responding to weather and climate change impacts.

providers.name: Umrahme
providers.description: Umrahme is a consumer online travel platform from the Traveazy Group focused on the Umrah pilgrimage, letting pilgrims across the GCC, UK, US, Europe, and Egypt book complete Umrah packages as well as individual hotels in Makkah and Madinah, Haramain high-speed train tickets, ground transfers, holiday add-ons, and travel eSIMs. The company is an Accel portfolio company and operates a companion B2B portal for travel agents, mobile apps on iOS and Android, and a travel-guide blog, but publishes no public developer or API program.

providers.name: Uplevel
providers.description: Uplevel is an engineering intelligence platform for enterprises — an operating system for engineering transformation that helps leaders see team performance clearly, solve root causes, and sustain improvement in the AI era. The platform pulls data from existing tools and uses machine learning to produce engineering metrics and actionable insights: DORA metrics, time allocation and ML issue classification, deep-work and interruption measurement, developer-experience metrics, and AI-impact analysis, framed by the company's WAVE framework of engineering KPIs. Founded in 2018 and led by CEO Joe Levy, Uplevel is backed by Norwest Venture Partners, Madrona Ventures, and Voyager Capital. Uplevel serves enterprise customers such as Xactly, Accolade, Braze, Avalara, and Qualtrics; it operates an internal API behind the product (api.uplevelteam.com, AWS API Gateway) but publishes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Varagesale
providers.description: VarageSale is a community-based online marketplace for buying and selling used items locally, founded in 2012 by Montreal teacher Tami Zuckerman and programmer Carl Mercier and headquartered in Toronto, Ontario. Members join a local community, verify their identity, and buy and sell with verified neighbors through native iOS and Android apps and the web, with communities across North America and beyond. Backed by Sequoia Capital and Lightspeed Venture Partners, VarageSale was acquired by VerticalScope in 2017, with online auction company MaxSold assuming operational control in early 2026. It is a direct-to-consumer marketplace and does not publish a public developer API, so this record captures its identity, web properties, and domain-security posture.

providers.name: VentureBeat
providers.description: VentureBeat is a leading technology news and media company covering artificial intelligence, enterprise technology, gaming, and the business of innovation. Founded in 2006 and based in San Francisco, VentureBeat does not offer a public developer REST API but provides content access via RSS feeds and content licensing. Its editorial coverage spans AI, machine learning, cloud computing, cybersecurity, and digital transformation for business leaders and technologists.

providers.name: VWR International (Avantor)
providers.description: VWR International, now part of Avantor, is a global distributor of laboratory supplies, chemicals, equipment, and services for the life sciences, pharmaceutical, biotechnology, and research industries. With over 180 years of history, VWR serves more than one million customers in over 30 countries. The company operates as Avantor's distribution and procurement platform, providing laboratory consumables, reagents, instruments, and cold chain solutions. VWR/Avantor offers e-procurement integrations and eProcurement APIs to support laboratory supply chain automation for enterprise customers through EDI, OCI/PunchOut, and catalog integration.

providers.name: Zervant
providers.description: Zervant is an online invoicing and billing platform for freelancers, sole traders, and small businesses. It lets users create, send, and manage estimates and invoices online, automate recurring invoices and payment reminders, track time and expenses, and get paid online across free and paid subscription tiers. Founded in Espoo, Finland and now part of the Ageras group, Zervant is a Northzone portfolio company. No public developer API is currently documented — this profile captures the company identity and a domain-security probe.

providers.name: 550wai-cn
providers.description: 550W AI (550W AI实验室) provides AI‑powered tools for content creators to automatically remove subtitles from videos, erase watermarks from images and videos, compress images, and more. The platform offers a public Open API that enables developers to integrate subtitle removal, watermark removal, image compression, asynchronous task polling, and webhook callbacks into their applications. Services are accessible via web, WeChat mini‑program, and desktop clients for macOS and Windows, supporting both single‑image and batch processing with before‑after comparison and automated workflows.

providers.name: AEG Fuels
providers.description: AEG Fuels (Associated Energy Group, LLC) is a Miami, Florida-based global aviation fuel supply, logistics and trip-support company that has served commercial air carriers, business and general aviation operators, FBOs and government aircraft since 1988. It arranges jet fuel uplifts at more than 3,000 locations across 197 countries and layers ancillary services on top of supply: flight support (flight planning, ground handling, overflight and landing permits, on-site supervision, coordination of third-party services), fuel management for airlines, tax recovery and VAT exemption, a Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) program, marine fuel and land fuel, the Carnet fuel card, the AEG Rewards loyalty program, and the AEG Connect network for FBOs and bulk fuel distribution. Customers transact through the company's own MILO ordering platform - a browser client portal at app.aegfuels.com and iOS/Android apps for quoting, ordering, authorizing and reviewing fuel transactions. As of this profile AEG Fuels publishes no public developer program, API reference or machine-readable contract; the digital surface is an end-user product, not a platform.

providers.name: AgentIndex
providers.description: AgentIndex is a curated directory of over 3,000 open-source AI agents, MCP servers, and agent frameworks. Updated daily, it provides reviews, selection guides, and detailed listings to help users discover and compare AI tools across categories. The platform also offers insights into MCP server implementations and community-driven rankings, serving developers, researchers, and enterprises seeking the best AI solutions in 2026.

providers.name: AngularJS
providers.description: AngularJS (Angular.js, version 1.x) is the original Angular JavaScript framework for building dynamic single-page web applications, created by Google. It introduced MVC patterns to front-end development with two-way data binding, dependency injection, directives, filters, services, and controllers. AngularJS reached End of Life on December 31, 2021 and is no longer actively maintained. Developers should migrate to the modern Angular framework (v14+).

providers.name: Askli
providers.description: Askli provides AI‑powered user research, enabling product teams to validate ideas, features, and customer needs by conducting real‑user interviews moderated by artificial intelligence. The platform offers quick checks, pricing plans, and integrations, delivering evidence‑based insights to guide development decisions and reduce assumptions.

providers.name: Atomic CSS
providers.description: Atomic CSS is a utility‑first CSS framework that lets you combine the first letters of CSS properties into concise class names, enabling you to style any element instantly. It works without any configuration or build step – just write classes and see results immediately. The framework emphasizes a minimal, class‑only approach, turning CSS property names into short, memorable utilities for rapid development.

providers.name: Avatr Technology
providers.description: AVATR Technology (Chongqing) Co., Ltd. (阿维塔科技) is a Chinese premium intelligent electric-vehicle manufacturer headquartered in Chongqing, founded in 2018 as a joint venture in which Changan Automobile and CATL are the two largest shareholders and Huawei supplies the smart-cockpit and advanced driver-assistance stack. Its vehicles — the AVATR 11 and 12, the volume 06 and 07 (battery-electric and range-extended), and the limited 011 and 012 — are built on the jointly developed CHN smart-EV platform, a six-layer architecture spanning the mechanical, energy, electronic/electrical architecture, vehicle operating system, vehicle function application and cloud big-data layers. AVATR produced 73,606 vehicles in 2024 and sells through mainland China plus overseas markets including Hong Kong, Singapore, Thailand, Sri Lanka, the UAE and Qatar, with design and engineering offices in Shanghai and Munich. AVATR is a vehicle manufacturer, not a software vendor: www.avatr.com is a marketing and configurator site with no developer portal, no public API, no SDK and no machine-readable specification. The only live agent surface anywhere on an AVATR hostname is platform-provided — the official Hong Kong site runs on Wix and exposes the Wix Site MCP endpoint plus a Wix-generated llms.txt over its public marketing content.

providers.name: Beducated
providers.description: Beducated is an online platform offering 150+ courses on sex and relationships, providing safe, inclusive education for adults of all orientations and genders. It aims to improve sexual skills and confidence through expert-led video tutorials and interactive exercises, fostering better intimacy and personal growth.

providers.name: Blockit AI
providers.description: Blockit AI provides an AI‑powered scheduling assistant that automates calendar management, meeting coordination, and time‑zone handling for individuals and teams. Leveraging natural language understanding, Blockit can parse conversational requests, suggest optimal meeting times, and integrate with major calendar platforms. The service targets productivity‑focused users and enterprises seeking to reduce the friction of scheduling, offering a free tier and paid plans with advanced features such as team collaboration, analytics, and custom integrations. Backed by Sequoia Capital, Blockit aims to become the go‑to virtual assistant for time management.

providers.name: Cactosaa16
providers.description: Cactosaa16, operating as Cactos, is a Finnish startup delivering smart battery energy storage systems for commercial and grid‑scale applications. Their platform optimises energy use, shifts consumption to low‑price periods, and enables participation in electricity markets, helping customers reduce costs and increase resilience.

providers.name: Canopy Aerospace
providers.description: Canopy Aerospace & Defense delivers specialized materials and components for aerospace, defense, space launch, maritime, and power sectors. They provide advanced additive manufacturing, rapid prototyping, and engineered solutions that enable platforms to perform faster, cooler, and quieter, supporting mission success through innovative, reliable, and scalable production.

providers.name: Cars24
providers.description: Cars24 (CARS24 Services Private Limited) is one of India's largest auto-tech companies and an online marketplace for buying and selling used cars, operating across India, the UAE, and Australia. Founded in 2015 and headquartered in Gurgaon, Haryana, Cars24 is an RBI-registered NBFC that combines a used-car transaction platform with financing, insurance, and vehicle-management services. Its offerings include buying and selling pre-owned cars with 300+ point inspections, fixed transparent pricing, warranties, and doorstep delivery; AI-driven used-car valuation; new-car discovery; traffic challan checking and payment; pre-delivery inspections across 220+ cities; vehicle history and service-history reports; car scrapping; FASTag recharge; and used-car loans, loan-against-car, and personal-loan products through Bikes24, Insure24, and related brands. Cars24 is backed by SoftBank Vision Fund and 500 Global. It is a consumer platform and does not publish a public developer API; this profile captures its identity, agent-facing llms.txt, and security posture.

providers.name: Change.org
providers.description: Change.org is an independent, nonprofit-owned social-change platform where anyone can start, sign, and win petitions. With over 500 million users worldwide, it lets people launch campaigns on social, political, and community issues, collect signatures, engage decision makers, and reach the media to drive real-world outcomes. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Slow Ventures and profiled in the API Evangelist network. Change.org's historical public developer/petitions API has been deprecated and is no longer maintained; no first-party OpenAPI, SDK, or hosted MCP server is currently published.

providers.name: Cicada
providers.description: Cicada Securities, LLC is a financial technology company revolutionizing the bond markets in Emerging Markets. It operates an Alternative Trading System (ATS) focused on local-currency-denominated government bonds in Mexico (M Bonos, UDI Bonos, and Cetes), enhancing liquidity and facilitating all-to-all access in an anonymous trading environment through central limit orderbook and request-for-quote protocols. Cicada Securities, LLC is an SEC-registered broker-dealer and FINRA member, and Cicada SEF, LLC is an applicant for swap execution facility registration with the CFTC. The company offers a trading platform, live pricing data, and a programmatic API for direct access to LatAm local-currency rates market liquidity, backed by 500 Global.

providers.name: ClawShow
providers.description: ClawShow provides advanced electronic signature solutions (AES, eIDAS art. 26) tailored for schools, training institutions, and SMEs. Their platform enables creation and management of school contracts, training agreements, quotes, and client contracts, hosted in France with unlimited users per enterprise plan. The service emphasizes compliance, security, and ease of use for French private schools and professional services.

providers.name: Collective Medical
providers.description: Collective Medical is a full-continuum, real-time care collaboration network for healthcare, connecting hospitals, health systems, post-acute providers, health plans, and payers so care teams can coordinate around complex, high-risk, and vulnerable patients across the entire patient journey. Founded in Utah and backed by Bessemer Venture Partners and Kleiner Perkins, the platform is known for its real-time event notifications, ADT-based care-coordination alerts, and shared clinical insights used by emergency departments and care-management teams. Collective Medical was acquired by PointClickCare in 2020 and is now fully integrated into PointClickCare; its former developer, login, support, and legal surfaces are served through PointClickCare properties (developer.pointclickcare.com and pointclickcare.com). This profile tracks the Collective Medical brand within the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Connect-RPC
providers.description: Connect is a slim framework for building browser-friendly and gRPC-compatible HTTP APIs from Protocol Buffer schemas. Servers built with Connect speak the Connect protocol, gRPC, and gRPC-Web simultaneously, while clients can switch between protocols without changing code. Connect provides type-safe SDKs for Go, TypeScript/JavaScript, Swift, Kotlin, and Python, plus the Buf-generated `protoc-gen-connect-*` code generators. The project is open source under the Apache 2.0 license and is maintained by Buf.

providers.name: Cosmiccloud
providers.description: Cosmiccloud provides an auto‑DevOps platform that enables developers to deploy, scale, and monitor applications across multiple cloud providers with minimal effort. Their solution offers a no‑code backend, automated release and rollback, logging, DNS integration, and comprehensive monitoring, targeting startups and small‑scale companies seeking to reduce operational overhead and accelerate delivery.

providers.name: Credi2
providers.description: Credi2 GmbH is a Vienna, Austria based fintech that operates a white-label, cloud-native embedded lending platform enabling banks, card issuers, and merchants to launch Buy Now Pay Later (BNPL) and installment financing products under their own brand. The modular platform covers five financing products - pay per invoice (14-day BNPL), split pay (3-12 month installments up to EUR 5,000), installment loans (up to EUR 50,000 over 84 months), revolving credit lines, and subscription financing - and handles the full lifecycle including core banking operations, credit and risk management, servicing, and collections. Use cases span eCommerce and point-of-sale financing, subscription payments, installment-on-cards, and cash loans, with omni-channel integration and go-live in weeks. Credi2 is ISO 27001 and ISO 27701 certified and is backed by Speedinvest.

providers.name: Crowdbotics
providers.description: Crowdbotics, now operating as CoreStory, provides an AI‑powered platform that modernizes and maintains software applications. It offers tools for code analysis, automated refactoring, and full‑stack development, helping enterprises accelerate digital transformation while reducing technical debt.

providers.name: Daxko
providers.description: Daxko provides cloud‑based software solutions for YMCAs, community centers, and other nonprofit fitness organizations. Its platform includes membership management, facility scheduling, payments, marketing automation, and analytics, helping operators streamline operations and improve member experiences. Daxko serves a broad range of clients across the United States, offering integrated tools for clubs, gyms, and wellness programs.

providers.name: Ellevest
providers.description: Ellevest is a women-founded, women-led wealth management and financial planning firm dedicated to closing the gender wealth gap. The platform delivers personalized investment management and comprehensive financial planning for high-net-worth individuals, families, and institutions, with services including portfolio management, retirement and estate planning, tax strategy, and cash flow analysis. Ellevest leverages REST-based internal APIs for portfolio management, financial coaching, banking operations, and personalized investment goal tracking, with third-party account connectivity available through Open Banking aggregators such as Plaid.

providers.name: energyaisolution-com
providers.description: EnergyAI provides AI‑driven decision support for residential energy choices, offering tools for solar, weatherization, EV charging, battery storage and heat pump planning. Users can obtain personalized quotes, incentive information, and evidence‑based recommendations, while agents can call the platform to retrieve estimates and compliance data. The service emphasizes transparency, human review options, and integrates with energy‑related data sources to help people and their agents make informed energy decisions.

providers.name: EV24
providers.description: EV24 provides a comprehensive platform for electric vehicle (EV) charging management, offering solutions for charging station operators, fleet managers, and businesses. Their services include a partner portal, open API integrations, white‑label charging solutions, hardware, payment terminals, and a mobile app, enabling scalable EV charging networks and monetization opportunities.

providers.name: Expedock
providers.description: Expedock is a digital business process outsourcing (BPO) and document-automation company for the logistics and freight-forwarding industry. It pairs AI-powered document automation products (FCL/LCL accounts-payable automation, monthly statement automation, and commercial invoice and packing-list data entry) with tech-enabled remote teams supported by operations managers and QA specialists. Freight forwarders, 3PLs, and supply-chain operators use Expedock to digitize shipping documents, automate back-office workflows, and scale operations without scaling headcount. Customers include Maersk, Gebrueder Weiss, and large shippers such as Nike, Adidas, Coca-Cola, and Shell. Expedock is backed by Insight Partners. The company operates a Digital BPO offering and document-automation product suite; it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API reference documentation.

providers.name: Finley (Concord)
providers.description: Finley (Concord) is Finley Technologies, a cloud-based loan administration and debt-capital-management platform for credit funds, banks, and private credit operators. The software digitizes 200+ credit-agreement fields and covers loan servicing (KYC, money movement, notice delivery), portfolio and borrowing-base monitoring, syndicated-loan management, and backup / credit administration, plus Finley AI for automating calculations, compliance checks, and notices. Finley is backed by Bain Capital Ventures and is delivered as a hosted web application at app.finleycms.com with product documentation at docs.finleycms.com. No public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDK is published at this time.

providers.name: FTI Consulting
providers.description: FTI Consulting is a global business advisory firm (NYSE: FCN, Fortune 1000) working in corporate finance and restructuring, economic consulting, forensic and litigation consulting, strategic communications and technology (e-discovery and information governance). Engagements are bespoke professional services; the firm publishes no public developer program, API reference or machine-readable contract. The only agent-facing document it serves is an llms.txt site index on www.fticonsulting.com.

providers.name: Fundraising Report Card
providers.description: Fundraising Report Card provides nonprofit analytics and reporting tools that deliver metrics such as donation growth, donor retention, donor lifetime value, and churn. The platform offers one‑click dashboards for fundraising performance, helping organizations track and improve their fundraising efforts with clear, actionable insights.

providers.name: Gecko Robotics
providers.description: Gecko Robotics is a Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania based AI and robotics company that inspects and manages critical physical infrastructure. Its wall-climbing, aerial and submersible robots capture full-coverage ultrasonic, visual and other sensor readings from boilers, pressure vessels, tanks, pipelines, ship hulls and decks, which are fused with facility records and operational data inside Cantilever, the company's AI-powered operating platform for the built world. Cantilever quantifies corrosion rates, predicts remaining asset life and prioritizes capital and maintenance decisions for customers across defense, power, oil and gas, steel, pulp and paper, mining and advanced manufacturing. Cantilever is delivered as a closed, authenticated enterprise SaaS at cantilever.app; Gecko Robotics publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs or self-serve API program, and integrations are arranged through the company directly.

providers.name: Geniebook
providers.description: Geniebook is a Singapore-based educational technology company (Geniebook Pte Ltd, incorporated 2016) offering an AI-powered online learning platform for primary, secondary, and JC students. Its product suite includes GenieSmart (AI-personalised worksheets generated from a library of 300,000+ MOE syllabus-aligned questions, using algorithms co-developed with A*STAR), GenieClass (live and recorded online classes taught by experienced teachers), and GenieAsk (real-time moderated teacher chats for after-school academic support), plus a CAMPUS physical-tutoring offering and PSLE/JC preparation programmes. Geniebook serves more than 220,000 students across Singapore, Vietnam, Malaysia, and Indonesia, and is backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners. It is a consumer (B2C) learning application delivered via web and mobile apps; no public developer API is published.

providers.name: Green Hills Software
providers.description: Green Hills Software is a privately held embedded software company founded in 1982 by Dan O'Dowd and Carl Rosenberg and headquartered in Santa Barbara, California. It builds safety- and security-certified real-time operating systems (INTEGRITY, INTEGRITY-178 tuMP, u-velOSity), embedded hypervisors (INTEGRITY Multivisor, u-visor), optimizing C/C++/Ada/Fortran compilers, the MULTI and AdaMULTI integrated development environments, the TimeMachine back-in-time debug suite, the DoubleCheck static analyzer, the Green Hills Probe hardware debugger, and networking, file-system and USB middleware. Its customers ship these components inside aerospace, defense, automotive, medical, industrial, rail, telecommunications and consumer devices. Green Hills is a toolchain and operating-system vendor rather than an API provider: the programmable interfaces it ships are in-product C/C++, POSIX and MULTI-Python scripting APIs delivered with a licensed installation and documented in manuals distributed with the product, and its technical support portal at support.ghs.com requires an account. No public web API, developer portal, or machine-readable API description was found on any Green Hills host during enrichment.

providers.name: Hapi
providers.description: hapi is a rich, configuration-centric framework for building web applications and APIs in Node.js. It provides a powerful plugin system, built-in input validation with Joi, authentication strategies, caching, cookie handling, and a focus on security and reliability for enterprise-grade applications.

providers.name: Harmonya
providers.description: Harmonya is a New York- and Tel Aviv-based product intelligence company for consumer packaged goods manufacturers and retailers. Founded in 2021, it reads live product listings, pack and label copy, manufacturer specs, syndicated feeds and consumer reviews, and turns them into normalized product attributes at the UPC level — claims, ingredients, flavors, pack, dietary positioning and measured nutrition values — plus demand themes and consumer-voice signals layered on top. The platform ships as four modules (Demand Intelligence, Consumer Intelligence, Attribute Intelligence and Product Catalog) delivered through a tenant web application at app.harmonya.com and as an enriched product feed into a customer's PIM, data lake and analytics stack. Harmonya publishes no public developer portal, API reference or machine-readable contract; access runs through a sales conversation and an Auth0-protected tenant.

providers.name: Hilltops IT
providers.description: Hilltops IT, operating as ConnectIt Software Development, provides integration and add‑on solutions for business software systems such as QuoteWerks, Sage, Microsoft Dynamics, and Monday.com. Based in the UK, they deliver bespoke development, migration, and support services to improve efficiency and profitability for their clients.

providers.name: Hippocratic AI
providers.description: Hippocratic AI builds safety-focused generative AI agents for non-diagnostic healthcare tasks, powered by its Polaris constellation architecture. Polaris 5.0 is a multi-trillion-parameter constellation of specialized models clinically validated by U.S.-licensed clinicians. Hippocratic AI sells agents such as Nurse Co-Pilot and AI Front Door to health systems, payors, and life-sciences organizations through enterprise sales rather than a self-service public API.

providers.name: HowLongToBeat
providers.description: HowLongToBeat is a game completion time database that tracks how long it takes to finish thousands of video games. Community-sourced data provides average completion times across multiple play styles including main story, main story plus extras, completionist, and all styles. The site is owned by IGN Entertainment (Ziff Davis) and does not publish an official public API; all programmatic access relies on community-built wrappers that query the website directly.

providers.name: Indinero
providers.description: Indinero is a Finance-as-a-Service (FaaS) provider that combines professional accountants, tax experts, and fractional CFOs with AI-accelerated workflows to deliver outsourced accounting, bookkeeping, business tax preparation, payroll, 409A valuations, and on-demand financial support. Founded in 2009 and backed by 500 Global, the company serves startups through $500M+ revenue businesses across technology, SaaS, ecommerce, healthcare, construction, crypto, professional services, and non-profits, integrating primarily with QuickBooks Online and NetSuite. Indinero is SOC 2 compliant and delivers its services through a client portal (the indinero Exchange) rather than a public developer API.

providers.name: Joomla
providers.description: Joomla is a free and open-source content management system (CMS) built in PHP that includes a built-in REST API for managing core content types. The Web Services API provides JSON endpoints for articles, categories, contacts, banners, menus, modules, tags, fields, and user accounts. Authentication is handled via Bearer tokens with optional HMAC security, and every endpoint requires authentication unless explicitly marked public. Joomla is maintained entirely by volunteers and released under the GNU General Public License.

providers.name: Keepit
providers.description: Keepit is a SaaS backup and recovery platform providing independent cloud-to-cloud data protection for Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, Salesforce, and other SaaS applications.

providers.name: LabDoor
providers.description: Labdoor is an independent San Francisco-based supplement testing company that buys top-selling vitamins, supplements, protein powders and energy drinks off retail shelves and online stores and sends samples to FDA-registered analytical laboratories for chemical analysis of active ingredients and potential contaminants. It grades every product on Label Accuracy, Product Purity, Nutritional Value, Ingredient Safety and Projected Efficacy, then publishes the resulting rankings, scores and expert reports for free so consumers can compare products, and it funds that testing through retail sales and through Labdoor Enterprise certification and custom-testing services sold to manufacturers. Labdoor publishes no public developer API, SDKs, developer portal or API documentation as of July 2026.

providers.name: Legion Security
providers.description: Legion Security is a browser-native AI SOC analyst that learns a security team's real workflows from inside the browser and then helps execute and automate them in phases: Learning Mode captures and maps how analysts actually work, Guided Mode runs those workflows with a human in the loop, and Autonomous Mode takes over the steps the team has signed off on. The platform targets alert triage, investigation, and evidence gathering in the security operations center, positioning agentic AI as a dependable teammate rather than a black box, with every captured insight visible and every action explainable. Legion Security operates a SafeBase trust center and publishes SOC 2 Type 2, ISO/IEC 27001:2022, ISO/IEC 42001:2023, HIPAA, and CSA STAR Level 1 compliance documentation. The company is seed-stage and backed by Accel; it publishes no public developer API at this time.

providers.name: Liftopia
providers.description: Liftopia is a consumer marketplace for advance-purchase ski and snowboard lift tickets, letting travelers browse and buy discounted day tickets and multi-day passes at hundreds of ski areas across the United States, Canada, Europe, South America, Japan, Australia and New Zealand. The site is organized by region, state and destination with dated availability and 1-8 day ticket search, and carries an affiliate program for partners. Liftopia's engineering organization operates on GitHub as Catalate Commerce, Inc., and the site footer points to Spotlio. As of this profile Liftopia publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI definition or client SDKs.

providers.name: LinkPeek
providers.description: Real-time website screenshot service that captures, stores, serves, and refreshes webpage snapshots via a simple GET-based image API. Give it a target URI and it returns a screenshot image.

providers.name: Lula (maintenance)
providers.description: Lula provides end-to-end residential property maintenance for property managers, offering a vetted network of over 9,000 professionals, flat‑rate pricing, and coordinated work order management across more than 350,000 properties in 50+ U.S. markets. Their platform integrates with major property management systems and delivers real‑time job tracking, AI‑driven intake, and quality assurance, aiming to simplify maintenance operations for landlords and managers.

providers.name: Magic
providers.description: Magic is an embedded-wallet and authentication platform offering passwordless login (magic links, OAuth, WebAuthn, SMS) plus white-label Embedded Wallets and Server Wallets. Primary surface is the Magic SDK; an Admin REST API exists for user lookup, token validation, and metadata.

providers.name: Matplotlib
providers.description: Matplotlib is a comprehensive open source library for creating static, animated, and interactive visualizations in Python. It provides a MATLAB-like interface via pyplot and an object-oriented API for full customization of publication-quality figures and plots.

providers.name: Mattilda
providers.description: Mattilda is a financial management platform for private educational institutions across Latin America, operating in Mexico, Colombia, and Ecuador. It automates tuition collection and payment processing, offers tuition advances that guarantee schools receive full monthly tuition on the first day regardless of family payment rates, and provides academic operations and admissions tools under its Algebraix product line. Families can pay through multiple channels, including WhatsApp. Mattilda operates under the oversight of Mexico's financial authorities CNBV and CONDUSEF and is backed by QED Investors. Mattilda does not currently expose a public developer API, SDKs, or documentation portal; this profile captures the company's public identity, status page, and Vanta-hosted trust center.

providers.name: PassimPay
providers.description: PassimPay provides a B2B crypto payment gateway enabling businesses to accept cryptocurrency payments across over 74 coins with no hidden fees. It offers instant conversion to EUR, automated AML checks, low‑cost USDT TRC20 fees, and fast withdrawals to cold wallets. Serving more than 530 merchants, it processes over $4 billion monthly, delivering 99.99% uptime and detailed reporting tools for sectors such as retail, real‑estate, advertising, healthcare, and renewable energy.

providers.name: Pearly
providers.description: Pearly provides dental practice billing and revenue cycle management automation software. Its platform streamlines patient billing, accounts receivable, payment plans, letter automation, and integrates with practice management systems. Pearly serves DSOs, group practices, and private dental offices, offering online payments, reporting, and AI‑driven insights to improve cash flow and reduce administrative overhead.

providers.name: Plans
providers.description: Plans (plans.app, formerly lun.energy) is a climate-technology company focused on decarbonising the built world. It removes the friction that stands in the way of transitioning homes to low-carbon energy faster, letting professionals capture building data on a mobile device, analyze it, and produce retrofit / energy plans — "capture, analyze, plan, all in your pocket." A web platform (platform.plans.app) and a Chrome extension support the workflow, and the product is offered across English, Danish, and French markets. Plans is backed by Partech. No public developer API has been identified during enrichment; the platform is a login-gated single-page application and the site exposes no OpenAPI, SDKs, docs, or developer portal.

providers.name: Plink
providers.description: Plink is a personalized commerce and card-linking platform that turns everyday payment transactions into intelligent, permission-based savings and engagement experiences for banks, merchants, and consumers. Its technology enriches transactions in real time, applying business rules and automated actions across payments, digital banking, and customer engagement, and exposes an API that lets any payment network make its transactions "smart" while keeping consumers anonymous. Plink says it has personalized over 700 million transactions and reaches 350+ banks, hundreds of thousands of merchants, and 10+ million consumers through an invitation-only network. The company operates a merchant/business portal and a consumer savings program (Fancoins) built on a PCI-compliant, tokenized card-linking structure.

providers.name: PlotBox
providers.description: PlotBox is a deathcare management platform for cemeteries, crematories, and funeral homes. Founded in Northern Ireland, its cloud SaaS combines records management, interactive digital cemetery mapping, financial and trust-fund management, work orders, scheduling, and family-facing records portals to help deathcare providers run compliant, efficient operations. PlotBox serves over 2,000 facilities globally, is hosted on Microsoft Azure, and holds ISO 9001 and ISO 27001 certifications. The company does not currently publish a public developer API or developer portal.

providers.name: Prenda
providers.description: Prenda, Inc. is a Mesa, Arizona education technology company that makes it possible for an adult to open and run a K-8 microschool — a tight-knit learning community of roughly five to ten students — out of a home, studio, or office. Founded by Kelly Smith out of the Prenda Code Club he started at a public library in 2013, Prenda opened its first microschool in January 2018 and now supports more than 1,000 "guides" running microschools for nearly 10,000 learners across multiple US states, funded largely through school-choice and education savings account programs. The product is a plug-and-play software platform bundled with curriculum, training, and coaching: guides use it to manage enrollment, run adaptive diagnostic assessments in math and reading, track learner progress against Prenda's four-mode "connect, conquer, collaborate, create" learning day, process payments, and publish a marketing site for their school. Prenda is venture-backed, having raised a $20M round led by 776 in 2022. The platform is closed and end-user facing — Prenda publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable contract of any kind. Its only public developer surface is the Prenda Design System, an open-source MUI v6 React component and icon library published from the prenda-school GitHub organization.

providers.name: PyTorch
providers.description: APIs and resources for PyTorch, an open source machine learning framework for tensor computation and deep learning developed by Meta.

providers.name: Red Points
providers.description: Red Points operates an AI-powered brand protection and anti-counterfeiting platform used by businesses to detect and remove counterfeits, unauthorized sellers, fake websites, social media impersonation, and digital piracy across more than 5,000 marketplaces, social networks, and app stores. Its software combines automated detection with enforcement and takedown workflows, domain monitoring, gray-market and unauthorized-seller blocking, ad-fraud detection, and revenue-recovery and litigation services. Red Points was surfaced as a portfolio company of Northzone and added to the API Evangelist network; it does not expose a public developer API or documented API surface as of this enrichment pass, so this profile captures the company's public web, legal, security, and llms.txt footprint rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: ShiftMed
providers.description: ShiftMed is a McLean, Virginia healthcare workforce technology company operating an on-demand clinician marketplace and AI-powered open shift management platform for hospitals, health systems, skilled nursing facilities and post-acute providers. It matches credentialed W-2 CNAs, LPNs and RNs to open shifts, and markets an API that lets a facility tap that clinician network directly from its own scheduling stack. The API surface reaches customers through workforce-management partner integrations — UKG Pro Workforce Management (formerly UKG Dimensions), symplr Smart Square, QGenda, Smartlinx and Attendance on Demand — alongside file-based SFTP feeds. ShiftMed publishes no public developer portal, documentation, specification or SDK; API access is arranged through a workforce consultation.

providers.name: Skan
providers.description: Skan AI is an enterprise process-intelligence and agentic-AI platform that observes how work actually happens across desktop, web, mainframe, legacy, VDI, and office applications without integrations, then distills those observations into a "context graph of work" that powers AI agents to execute complex business processes. The platform layers Observation, Distillation, Context (Agent Operating Procedures), Agents, and Control, and ships as Process Intelligence, Engineering Intelligence, and an AI Agent Builder. Skan serves financial services, insurance, healthcare, high tech, and energy/utilities with in-environment processing so customer data never leaves the enterprise perimeter. Backed by Bloomberg Beta and surfaced into the API Evangelist network from that portfolio. Skan is an enterprise SaaS product; it exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDKs — its documentation portal is gated and its architecture is described as cloud-native and API-first for in-product integration only.

providers.name: SolveBio
providers.description: SolveBio is a platform for biomedical and genomic datasets that lets developers query, harmonize, and automate bioinformatics workflows over curated reference data through a REST API and first-party client libraries (Python, JavaScript, Ruby, and R). SolveBio has been rebranded to QuartzBio, a Precision for Medicine company: the solvebio.com website now redirects to quartz.bio, the legacy API is served as the QuartzBio EDP REST API on per-customer instance hosts, and the SolveBio SDKs are being deprecated in favor of the quartzbio packages (Python client end of maintenance 2026-03-31). Surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and enriched from its public GitHub organization and package registries.

providers.name: Sound Agriculture
providers.description: Sound Agriculture is an Emeryville, California agriculture company founded in 2013 by Eric Davidson and Travis Bayer that sells nature-based crop nutrition products to row-crop growers through an independent dealer network: SOURCE, a foliar-applied soil activator that stimulates soil microbes to supply nitrogen and phosphorus; BLUEPRINT, an arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi inoculant; and INFLECT. It also runs an on-demand breeding program that tunes plant gene expression epigenetically without editing DNA. Sound Agriculture is not a software company and publishes no developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable contract; its only authenticated surface is a Salesforce Experience Cloud dealer portal at dealerportal.sound.ag.

providers.name: SQL
providers.description: SQL (Structured Query Language) is the ANSI/ISO standard language for managing and querying relational databases. SQL defines the interface for creating, reading, updating, and deleting data in relational database management systems (RDBMS). Database connectivity standards including ODBC (Open Database Connectivity) and JDBC (Java Database Connectivity) expose SQL capabilities as programmatic APIs, enabling applications to connect to and interact with SQL-compliant databases. Major implementations include MySQL, PostgreSQL, Microsoft SQL Server, Oracle, SQLite, and many others.

providers.name: Strella
providers.description: Strella is an AI-powered customer research platform that automates qualitative research at scale. It runs AI-moderated interviews with adaptive questioning, auto-generates discussion guides, recruits participants from an 8M+ global panel or a company's own customers, supports 46+ languages, and synthesizes insights and video highlights within hours instead of weeks. Research types span exploratory research, concept testing, usability testing, market research, and customer journey mapping. Strella is backed by Bessemer Venture Partners. No public developer API or SDK surface is currently published; this profile captures the company identity, security posture, and product changelog.

providers.name: Turion Space
providers.description: Turion Space is an Irvine, California aerospace company founded in 2021 (Y Combinator S21) that designs, builds and operates DROID maneuverable spacecraft for space domain awareness, non-earth imaging and in-orbit servicing, alongside the STARFIRE software platform for mission planning, autonomous tasking and command-and-control across Turion and third-party constellations. Its customer-facing surface is the STARFIRE dashboard at starfire.turionspace.com, backed by a first-party REST API gateway at api.app.turionspace.com that issues per-user API keys and meters imagery tasking and Starfire NEXUS jobs against a Stripe-billed credit balance. The company publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable specification; the entire contract sits behind the STARFIRE customer login.

providers.name: ulehla-dev
providers.description: Ulehla-dev is the personal brand and professional portfolio of Ondřej Úlehla, a full‑stack developer and AI engineer based in Prague. He builds fast, well‑crafted software products, ranging from client‑side applications to cloud‑native back‑ends, and shares his work, projects, and insights through open‑source repositories, blog‑style markdown profiles, and a public API catalog. The site showcases his technical expertise, open‑source contributions, and offers machine‑readable documentation for developers and AI agents.

providers.name: Vector.ai
providers.description: Vector.ai, now operating as Raft (raft.ai), is an AI-powered logistics automation platform for freight forwarders, customs brokers, and trade finance teams. The Raft Intelligence Engine layers organization data, contextual LLMs, orchestration, and specialized governed agents to automate document processing, invoice matching, data extraction, and exception handling across supply chain operations, reporting 20M+ tasks completed by AI agents and 5M+ shipments processed annually. Raft publishes no public developer API; the platform is an enterprise application that integrates with customers' TMS and ERP systems.

providers.name: Web Shop Manager
providers.description: Web Shop Manager provides a cloud‑based platform that enables merchants to create, manage, and scale their online stores with integrated inventory, order processing, payment gateways, and analytics. The solution offers customizable storefront themes, multi‑channel sales support, and robust APIs for developers to extend functionality, automate workflows, and integrate third‑party services. Targeted at small to medium‑size businesses, it aims to simplify e‑commerce operations while delivering a seamless shopping experience for end‑customers.

providers.name: Whip Media Group
providers.description: Whip Media is a SaaS company powering the global media and entertainment industry through its AI-native Helix platform, which connects content licensors and licensees across the rights-to-royalties value chain. Helix spans supply-chain modules for licensees (avails management, contract management, royalties processing) and distribution modules for licensors (asset order management, performance tracking, revenue recognition), plus AI-powered Title Management for metadata enrichment and standardization. Customers include NBCU, Warner Bros. Discovery, Paramount, Sony, and Lionsgate. The company publishes an SEO llms.txt and reports SOC 1 and SOC 2 Type II audits for a sixth consecutive year, but does not expose a public developer portal or documented API. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of IVP.

providers.name: Zensurance
providers.description: Zensurance is a Toronto-based digital commercial insurance brokerage founded in 2016 that sells small-business and freelancer coverage online across every Canadian province, placing risk with Canadian carriers rather than underwriting it. Its book is commercial property and casualty — general and commercial general liability, professional liability and errors and omissions, cyber liability, directors and officers, commercial property, commercial auto, builder's risk, and a long tail of trade- and profession-specific packages — sold through a quote-to-bind web flow marketed as an instant online price with licensed broker support and claims advocacy behind it. It sits in the thin digital-broker layer beneath Canada's Big-Few carrier oligopoly, in a market with no open-insurance mandate — OSFI supervises federally-regulated insurers prudentially while FSRA, the AMF, and the other provincial regulators own market conduct, and Consumer-Driven Banking excludes insurance outright. Its API posture reflects that. Zensurance publishes no public, self-serve developer portal, no reference documentation, and no downloadable OpenAPI, Swagger, GraphQL, or AsyncAPI definition. The company's partnership page advertises "seamless API integrations and co-branded white-label tools" for distribution partners, but the only route to that surface is a partnership application form — the integration is partner-gated and privately negotiated. A first-party host at api.zensurance.com answers on the public internet (HTTP 200, returning a bare version string, with a /health endpoint) but it is the undocumented backend for Zensurance's own quoting and policy application, not a published product API. No ACORD, AL3, ACORD XML, NGDS, or agency-management-system integration claim appears anywhere on the company's public web properties. The one machine-addressable surface the company does publish for automated consumers is an llms.txt at www.zensurance.com/llms.txt — a 178KB marketing index of its pages, blog posts, and FAQs (which inadvertently lists its zenstage.wpengine.com staging host rather than the production domain). It describes insurance products for AI assistants; it documents no API.

providers.name: zhihuo-net
providers.description: zhihuo-net is currently a placeholder entry in the API Evangelist network. The company was identified from the MCP registry harvest but no public website, documentation, or API endpoints could be verified. Attempts to resolve https://zhihuo.net/ redirected to an unrelated site, and no alternative domain or developer portal was found. Consequently, the profile contains minimal information and serves as a stub for future enrichment when authoritative sources become available.

providers.name: 24Symbols
providers.description: 24Symbols is a digital reading subscription service, often described as a "Spotify for books," giving readers unlimited access to a catalog of more than 500,000 e-books across Spanish, English, German, Italian, Portuguese, and French for a flat monthly fee. Founded in Madrid and backed by Seedcamp, the platform lets subscribers read on smartphones, tablets, e-readers, and the web, build personal bookshelves, track reading progress, and follow other readers and authors through its social reading community. Alongside its consumer premium plan, 24Symbols offers B2B "reading space" solutions that let hotels, telecoms, media outlets, educational institutions, and loyalty or employee programs license library access for their audiences. The company operates as a consumer- and business-facing subscription product and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or partner integration surface; this profile captures its verifiable identity and public web properties.

providers.name: AdWhispr
providers.description: AdWhispr is an AI‑powered marketing agent that discovers competitors' winning ads, clones them for your brand, and launches campaigns across Meta, TikTok, Google and X. It provides a chat‑driven interface, prompt cookbook, and automation tools for ad research, creative generation, and real‑time campaign management, empowering marketers to accelerate performance and reduce creative costs.

providers.name: Agentmemory
providers.description: Agentmemory provides a persistent memory layer for AI coding agents, enabling teams to capture, retrieve, and govern agent session data across workflows. The platform supports Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and OpenAI agents, offering features like hybrid recall, review before share, and memory actions. It includes a marketplace for memory packs, pricing plans for teams, and integrates with MCP tools to ensure secure, governed memory for AI-driven development.

providers.name: AI-Translators.com
providers.description: AI-Translators.com provides a professional AI-powered translation platform offering text, document, website, photo, and video translation services in over 100 languages. The service emphasizes privacy, does not store user data for training, and offers a free tier with limits plus paid plans. It supports real-time conversation mode and integrates with various tools, aiming to break language barriers worldwide.

providers.name: AIGE
providers.description: AIGE provides an AI-powered image and video studio that enables creators to generate characters, films, brand designs, and marketing assets from simple text prompts. The platform offers tools for AI image generation, video creation, digital twins, and brand consistency across campaigns, with integrations for Claude, Cursor, and popular creative tools. It includes a marketplace of models, pricing plans, and a developer portal for building custom workflows.

providers.name: Aiwyn
providers.description: Aiwyn is a practice-automation platform built for modern accounting and CPA firms, unifying payments, practice management, client experience, and tax into a single relationship-centered system. Aiwyn Payments automates invoicing, card and ACH collection, and reconciliation; Aiwyn Practice covers time, billing, project management and resource planning; Aiwyn Experience delivers a unified client portal for engagement letters and secure document exchange; and Aiwyn Tax adds AI-assisted tax preparation. The company serves 800+ firms and raised $113M from KKR and Bessemer Venture Partners. This profile was surfaced as a Bessemer portfolio company; Aiwyn publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or SDK surface at this time, so enrichment is limited to identity, its published llms.txt, and probed domain security.

providers.name: AppGenie
providers.description: AppGenie is a distinguished B2B-oriented IT service provider specializing in Salesforce, AWS, Azure and DevSecOps solutions. They help businesses transition to cloud platforms, optimise applications, and deliver custom software, consulting and staffing across Australia, New Zealand and India. Over 20 years of experience underpin their Salesforce ISV and consulting partnership, offering integration, migration and managed services.

providers.name: ApplyBoard
providers.description: ApplyBoard is a study-abroad application platform that simplifies the international education journey by connecting students, recruitment partners, and partner schools on a single platform. Students explore and apply to more than 1,500 global universities and colleges across Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, Ireland, Australia, and Germany, with supporting services spanning financial products, English-language test vouchers, and accommodation. ApplyBoard also operates ApplyProof, a document-verification and trust product. The company does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI definition, or SDK; its programmatic surface (including ApplyProof) is partner-gated. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and profiled in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Atari
providers.description: Atari is one of the founding brands of the interactive entertainment industry, originally established in 1972, and today operates as a global video game and consumer-hardware company. It publishes classic and modern titles, manufactures the Atari VCS console and retro hardware (Atari 2600+, Atari 400 Mini), licenses its catalog and brand, and sells games, collectibles, and merchandise through its official online store at atari.com. Atari does not publish a general-purpose public REST API; its developer surface is limited to Atari VCS content-submission guidance (developers email vcs@atari.com and use the VCS submission portal) and legacy HTML5 Atari Arcade SDK libraries on GitHub. This profile was surfaced as a Mayfield portfolio company — a nod to Mayfield's foundational 1970s venture investment in Atari — and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: BabyList
providers.description: Babylist is the leading universal baby registry and a baby-focused commerce and content company for growing families. Because the registry is universal, parents can add any product from any store — including Amazon, Target, and Etsy — to a single list. Babylist has grown into a full ecosystem spanning the Babylist registry, the Babylist Shop, Babylist Health (insurance-covered breast pumps), Babylist Money (family financial planning), expert product guides, and a flagship Los Angeles showroom. More than 10 million people shop with Babylist every year. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global and norwest-venture-partners and added to the API Evangelist network; Babylist runs no public developer API, but it does publish an llms.txt agent surface and an OpenID Connect discovery document.

providers.name: Barnir Hired
providers.description: Barnir Hired provides AI‑powered job fit analysis for technical roles. It helps candidates and hiring teams quickly assess fit by analyzing resumes, job descriptions, and public profiles without storing data. The service offers a free trial and paid plans, delivering detailed playbooks, interview strategies, and personalized feedback. Founded by a veteran technical go‑to‑market professional, Barnir Hired leverages proprietary methodology and domain expertise to improve hiring outcomes.

providers.name: BestEOR.co
providers.description: BestEOR.co provides a comprehensive comparison of employer-of-record (EOR) and global payroll providers, offering detailed per-employee pricing, country coverage, and owned-entity model analysis. The site aggregates data on top providers, enabling businesses to evaluate options based on cost, features, and compliance across multiple jurisdictions. It serves HR professionals and companies seeking to outsource payroll and employment responsibilities worldwide.

providers.name: Betterplace01b9
providers.description: Betterplace01b9 is a learning platform that provides AI‑powered tools for educators to create, deliver, and experience courses. It offers a suite of services including instant course generation, adaptive learning, and a marketplace for instructors. The platform aims to make education more accessible, scalable, and personalized for learners worldwide.

providers.name: Bhaptics
providers.description: Bhaptics creates advanced haptic technology, offering wearable haptic suits, vests, and accessories that enable developers to integrate tactile feedback into games, VR experiences, and other interactive applications. Their platform provides SDKs, APIs, and developer tools to control haptic patterns, synchronize with audio and visual cues, and deliver immersive sensations across a range of devices.

providers.name: Bluejay Therapeutics
providers.description: Bluejay Therapeutics, Inc. was a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered in Redwood City, California, developing treatments for viral hepatitis and liver disease. Its lead asset, brelovitug (BJT-778), is an investigational monoclonal antibody targeting the surface antigen shared by the hepatitis D and hepatitis B viruses; it received U.S. FDA Breakthrough Therapy designation for chronic hepatitis delta and reported a 100% virologic response at week 48 in its Phase 2 monotherapy study before entering the AZURE-2 global Phase 3 trial. The company also advanced a proprietary TLR9 agonist (cavrotolimod), a liver-targeted HBV transcript inhibitor (BJT-628) and a liver-targeted fatty acid synthase inhibitor (BJT-188) toward a combination regimen aimed at functional cure of chronic hepatitis B. Mirum Pharmaceuticals agreed to acquire Bluejay Therapeutics in December 2025 and completed the acquisition on 26 January 2026; the corporate site now serves a single acquisition notice redirecting readers to mirumpharma.com. Bluejay Therapeutics never ran a developer program — no product API, no developer portal, no API documentation, no SDKs, no GitHub organisation and no package-registry presence. The only machine-readable surface reachable without credentials is the WordPress REST content API behind bluejaytx.com, catalogued here. That surface is notable for outliving the web site it belongs to: the marketing page tree was deleted in the teardown, but the REST API and the post archive still serve all 35 press releases and publication notices from 2021 through 2025 with full text.

providers.name: Boardroom Bob
providers.description: Boardroom Bob is an AI‑powered strategy consulting service for solo founders and small teams. It offers a library of 19 proven business frameworks – such as SWOT, Porter’s Five Forces, BCG Matrix and decision‑making tools – that users can apply via an interactive web form. The platform generates structured analyses, diagrams and actionable recommendations, with a strict truthfulness policy that flags unknown information instead of fabricating data. Free users get limited monthly analyses, while paid plans unlock unlimited use and premium support. Boardroom Bob also provides an MCP server for AI agents like Claude and Cursor to run the frameworks directly.

providers.name: bolttech
providers.description: bolttech is a global insurtech running an embedded insurance exchange that connects insurers, distribution partners and customers. It operates a developer portal (Apigee integrated portal) with a free mock-data sandbox; the API catalogue and specifications are behind partner login.

providers.name: Braid Social
providers.description: Braid Social, Inc. is a venture-backed startup that has run two products under the Braid name. It launched as a creator-economy, direct-to-fan engagement platform — founded by former Facebook product designer Matthew Cahill and software engineer Chris Piro — letting creators build customizable landing pages that consolidated their work across the web (blog posts, videos, podcasts, and commerce links), collect fan phone numbers, and reach followers directly through SMS, push notifications, and mailing lists, with link tracking and cross-platform analytics. It raised a $6.8M seed round in August 2023 led by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) with Initialized Capital. The original domain braid.ai is now a domain-for-sale listing at atom.com and braid.social no longer resolves. The same legal entity now ships "Braid Teams" at trybraid.io (mirrored at braidsocial.com) — an AI-powered employee-engagement copilot that runs inside Slack, automating icebreakers, games, polls, events, reminders, leaderboards, and engagement reporting for distributed teams, on a free / $5-per-user Premium / contact-us Enterprise plan. Braid Teams is a Slack-app product with no public developer program: no developer portal, no documentation, no OpenAPI, no SDKs, and no GitHub organization. The only machine surface is the private application backend at core.trybraid.io, which answers {"status":"ok"} at its root and 404s every spec, docs and /.well-known/ path. The homepage states the product is "Currently not accepting new users" and the Slack install endpoint returns HTTP 500.

providers.name: CADDi
providers.description: CADDi is a Tokyo-headquartered manufacturing-technology company that builds an AI Data Platform for industrial manufacturers. Its two products, CADDi Drawer and CADDi Quote, aggregate scattered 2D engineering drawings and supply-chain data into a single searchable asset, offering keyword and drawing-similarity search, automatic extraction of dimensions, text and shapes, and AI-assisted quotation and sourcing. The platform serves procurement, engineering, sales, production, quality, and leadership teams across automotive, robotics, and precision-machinery sectors, and connects to ERP, CAM, CAD, and quality systems via batch and CSV imports. CADDi was surfaced as a portfolio company of Atomico and DCM Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. It does not currently publish a public developer API or SDK.

providers.name: CHANGELOG.md (Keep a Changelog)
providers.description: CHANGELOG.md is a community convention for a human-readable, Markdown- formatted file at the root of a project that records notable changes between versions. The leading specification is "Keep a Changelog" by Olivier Lacan, which defines a stable, opinionated set of section headings (Added, Changed, Deprecated, Removed, Fixed, Security) and recommends pairing with Semantic Versioning (SemVer). The format is widely adopted across open source and enterprise projects as the de facto way to document API and software releases in a way that is readable by humans and parseable by tooling.

providers.name: Citead
providers.description: Citead provides a Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) SaaS platform that evaluates web content for citation by AI models. Users paste a URL and receive a score across five criteria, with actionable recommendations to improve AI retrievability. The service offers tiered pricing, operates in French and English, and targets content creators, marketers, and SEO professionals seeking better visibility in ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google AI Overviews.

providers.name: Context.ai *
providers.description: Context (context.ai) is a unified enterprise AI platform for building, deploying, and improving AI agents at scale. The product is organized into modular components: a Workspace for authoring agent workflows in plain English, an Engine with 800+ connectors and IdP-brokered identity, Unify as a knowledge/institutional-context repository, and Evals for rubric-based quality scoring. It is model-agnostic (Claude, GPT, Gemini, Kimi, or open weights) and offers hosted, VPC, on-prem, or air-gapped deployment. The company originated as a GV (Google Ventures) and Theory Ventures backed product-analytics-for-LLMs startup and now operates as an enterprise agent platform used by teams including Qualcomm, Stripe, and Palantir. This repo carries no public developer/API surface: the provider publishes no OpenAPI, SDKs, MCP server, or developer documentation, so most machine-readable artifacts are not applicable.

providers.name: Continuum
providers.description: Continuum (gocontinuum.ai) is an AI-powered platform that automates B2B returns, warranties, and repairs for distributors and manufacturers. It handles the post-sales workflow end to end through four solution hubs: a Customer Hub with self-service warranty and return portals, a Warehouse Hub for one-click receiving, inspection and dispute processing, a Vendor & Finance Hub for automated vendor engagement and accounts-receivable management, and a Manufacturer Warranty Hub for warranty claim automation. The company reports outcomes such as a 70% reduction in returns labor cost, a 30% increase in profitability, and an 8% reduction in customer churn. Continuum integrates with major distribution ERP systems (Infor, NetSuite, Epicor, Oracle, Acumatica). Based in Chicago, it is seed-funded and backed by Cowboy Ventures. Continuum is SOC 2 audited and publishes a public trust center. No public developer API or documentation is available at this time.

providers.name: Cortico
providers.description: Cortico (Cortico Health Technologies) is a Vancouver, British Columbia based healthcare connection platform, founded in 2019, that links patients, medical clinics, and health records across Canada and the United States. Its patient-engagement suite layers online booking, automated appointment reminders, secure two-way patient messaging, digital intake forms, telemedicine, specialist e-referrals, payments, and AI-driven administrative automation on top of the electronic medical records (EMRs) clinics already run — most notably a supported two-way integration with OSCAR EMR through that system's REST/SOAP web services, plus SMART on FHIR contextual launch and robotic process automation (RPA). Cortico is SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified and compliant with HIPAA, PIPEDA, and PHIPA. Cortico consumes EMR and FHIR interfaces rather than publishing its own public developer API: as of this review there is no public developer portal, API reference, or FHIR CapabilityStatement, and integration is delivered through a partnership and onboarding model rather than self-serve API access.

providers.name: Cyclone Machining Co.
providers.description: Cyclone Machining Co. is a prototype and R&D machine shop located in Grand Rapids, Michigan. They offer five-axis CNC machining, precision finishing, TIG fabrication, and a range of manufacturing services for low‑quantity and custom parts, serving industries such as aerospace, automotive, and medical device development. The company emphasizes rapid prototyping, high‑quality engineering, and in‑house capabilities to turn designs into functional components.

providers.name: Dejbox (Refectory)
providers.description: Dejbox is a French corporate-catering company founded in Lille in 2015 by Adrien Verhack and Vincent Dupied, acquired by the Carrefour Group in January 2020 and since rebranded as Refectory (refectory.fr). It delivers prepared, seasonal meals to employees of companies located in the peripheral zones of major French cities via a digital canteen (click-and-collect precommande before 10:30) and connected self-service fridges, controlling 100% of its value chain through its own Manufactures and a national network of 23 logistics hubs. Originally surfaced as a Partech portfolio company, it operates in Bordeaux, Grenoble, Lille, Lyon, Nantes, Paris and other French cities. Its consumer platform runs on a public OAuth2/OIDC identity server (customers.refectory.fr) and an API gateway (gateway.refectory.fr).

providers.name: Diagon
providers.description: Diagon is a California-based industrial equipment sourcing company building Albus, an equipment intelligence platform for manufacturing buyers and sellers. Buyers search across millions of industrial equipment listings, compare models, specifications, pricing and availability, and connect directly with sellers; sellers publish AI-powered catalogs, reach qualified buyer demand, and see live equipment searches in real time. Diagon indexes manufacturing equipment products, suppliers and service providers, bringing hardware, services and financing into a consolidated procurement experience. Founded by a team out of Tesla, Bright Machines, Rivian and Snackpass, and backed by Anthemis under its data, tech and infrastructure thesis.
