By posting a clearly scoped ticket, organizations can receive solutions from external AI agents and automatically verify and pay out upon successful completion, streamlining workflow and focusing internal resources on higher‑value work.

providers.name: Artera Decisionrisk Analysis
providers.description: Artera Decisionrisk Analysis, operating as ArteraAI, provides personalized precision medicine and AI-driven cancer therapy solutions. The company offers a multimodal AI platform for clinicians and patients, including diagnostic tests for prostate and breast cancer, and supports HIPAA-compliant data handling. Artera aims to improve outcomes through advanced analytics and regulatory‑approved medical software.

providers.name: Banzaiinternational
providers.description: Banzaiinternational, operating as Banzai, provides data‑driven demand generation solutions through a platform that includes webinar hosting, video creation, and audience engagement tools. The company helps marketers boost event registrations, generate leads, and measure ROI with products like Demio, OpenReel, and its own Banzai suite. It serves B2B customers seeking to improve pipeline conversion and customer engagement across digital channels.

providers.name: Beket AI
providers.description: Beket AI provides AI visibility audit services that evaluate how large language models such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Microsoft Copilot, Google AI Overviews and Google AI Mode describe a business, flag inaccuracies, and suggest automated on‑site fixes. The platform offers a free one‑time audit and paid subscription plans for continuous monitoring, content generation and reporting.

providers.name: Bilance
providers.description: Bilance is a budgeting app that connects to over 2,300 European banks, automatically syncing transactions and organizing them into budgets. Available on iOS and Android, it helps users track spending, set financial goals, and gain insights into their money habits across multiple currencies and banks.

providers.name: Blocks
providers.description: Blocks is an AI‑native training platform for endurance athletes. It lets you build and visualise structured intervals, sync every ride, and train with an assistant that reads your real data – cycling, running, swimming and strength. The service offers a free tier and premium plans, integrates with Strava and intervals.icu, and provides an MCP server for Claude and other AI agents.

providers.name: CalmLoop
providers.description: CalmLoop is a calm task manager offering daily focus, a morning email summary, and MCP access for AI assistants. Built by Algoza Solutions OPC Private Limited, it emphasizes distraction‑free productivity, honest pricing with a free month trial, and clear data practices. The platform provides a simple interface for planning, focus zones, and task tracking without push notifications or hidden fees.

providers.name: Calo
providers.description: Calo is a food-tech company founded in Bahrain in 2019 that operates a personalized meal-subscription and delivery service. Nutritionist-designed, chef-prepared meals are portioned to each customer's health goals and lifestyle, with 80+ new meal options rotated weekly and flexible pause/cancel anytime. Built by chefs, nutritionists, and software engineers around proprietary nutritional algorithms, Calo has expanded to seven markets across the GCC and beyond (Saudi Arabia, United Arab Emirates, Kuwait, Qatar, Bahrain, and Oman), ordered through its consumer apps. Calo is backed by 500 Global. It is a consumer-facing product with no public developer API or documented client SDKs.

providers.name: canopyapi-co
providers.description: Canopy API provides developers with real-time Amazon product data, including pricing, reviews, and sales estimates, via REST, GraphQL, and MCP interfaces. The service offers a single API key to access comprehensive product information without the need for web scraping, supporting AI agents and applications. It targets developers building e‑commerce tools, price‑tracking services, and market analysis platforms, delivering up to 100 free requests for new users and scalable plans for higher volume.

providers.name: ChannelMeter
providers.description: ChannelMeter is a creator management and payments platform for multi-channel networks, agencies, and brands. Founded in 2012 and headquartered in San Francisco, it provides an all-in-one suite for creator discovery, onboarding, contract management, analytics, and automated global payouts. Its Creator Pay product moves money to creators across 21+ currencies and 50+ countries, and Creator Cash offers cash advances to creators. ChannelMeter reports having processed over $1B in payments to more than one million creators, working with Stripe and Fifth Third Bank for financial services. The company is backed by 500 Global.

providers.name: Charune
providers.description: charune-com is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: mcp-registry) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.

providers.name: City National Bank
providers.description: City National Bank is a national bank chartered in the United States and a wholly owned subsidiary of Royal Bank of Canada (RBC) since 2015, headquartered in Los Angeles, California and known historically as "the bank to the stars" for its deep roots in the entertainment industry. With roughly $98 billion in assets, it is an FDIC-insured, super-regional institution offering personal, business, and private banking, wealth management, treasury management, and capital markets services, with industry expertise across entertainment, healthcare, real estate, technology, and law. City National operates as CN Bank in Florida. It runs NO first-party public developer portal or documented public API: developer.cnb.com and developers.cnb.com do not resolve and api.cnb.com returns 404. Consistent with the voluntary, fragmented US open-finance model, consumer-permissioned account data is reached through third-party aggregators (Plaid, MX, Finicity, Akoya) rather than a direct City National API. As a covered depository institution it falls under the emerging CFPB Section 1033 Personal Financial Data Rights rule, but no City-National-specific 1033 or FDX participation posture is publicly documented. Its Canadian parent RBC runs a separate developer portal (developer.rbc.com) under a different charter that does not expose City National Bank APIs.

providers.name: Cometa
providers.description: Cometa (getcometa.com / cometaedu.com) is a Mexican education technology company that provides an operating system for private schools. More than 500 private schools in Mexico use Cometa to run and automate their operations across a set of integrated modules: Cobranzas (tuition collections with WhatsApp and email payment reminders and dashboards), Tienda en linea (an online store for uniforms, materials and services with vendor management), Admisiones y Reinscripciones (admissions and re-enrollment workflows), Comunicaciones (AI-assisted, multi-channel family communications with engagement analytics), Calificaciones (grade entry and SEP-compliant report cards and digital credentials), and Gestion Escolar (attendance, incident logging and administrative workflows). Cometa is a 500 Global portfolio company. It was surfaced as a stub in the API Evangelist network for enrichment; as of this pass Cometa publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API documentation surface.

providers.name: Connexion
providers.description: Connexion is an open source Python framework that automatically handles HTTP requests based on OpenAPI specifications. Connexion 3 provides AsyncApp, FlaskApp, and ConnexionMiddleware as primary entry points, with built-in routing, request and response validation, parameter parsing, security enforcement, content negotiation, error handling, lifespan, and Swagger UI integration. Connexion takes a contract-first, design-first approach: the OpenAPI specification is the source of truth and Python handlers are resolved from operationId or via configurable resolvers.

providers.name: Context Awesome
providers.description: Context Awesome provides an MCP server offering over 8,500 curated awesome lists and more than 1.5 million vetted resources for AI agents. It aggregates community‑curated collections across technology domains, enabling agents to recommend high‑quality tools, libraries, and resources instead of random search results. The platform supports browsing, submitting lists, and integrates with GitHub and other developer tools.

providers.name: ContextGem
providers.description: ContextGem provides an AI-powered platform for extracting structured data from unstructured text using large language models. It offers pipelines for aspect extraction, concept identification, and decision modeling, enabling developers to integrate advanced natural language understanding into their applications. The documentation includes quickstart guides, installation instructions, and extensive examples for building extraction pipelines and leveraging supported LLMs.

providers.name: Cowboy
providers.description: Cowboy is a Brussels-based mobility company that designs and manufactures premium connected electric bicycles for urban commuting. Its lineup — the Cruiser, Cruiser ST, Cross, and Cross ST — pairs a lightweight frame with removable batteries, integrated GPS tracking, crash detection, and its proprietary AdaptivePower motor assistance, all managed through the Cowboy mobile app. The company sells direct-to-consumer and through a network of 125+ service centers and mobile technicians across 40+ European cities, complemented by leasing, business, and student programs. Backed by Index Ventures, Cowboy operates a Shopify-based storefront and a connected-bike app platform; it does not publish a public developer API. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead and enriched with the company's real identity, legal, support, and security surfaces.

providers.name: DoubleDutch
providers.description: DoubleDutch was a San Francisco mobile event technology company backed by Bessemer Venture Partners. Its Developer Platform (DDDP) let event organizers and third-party developers build React Native extensions that install into any DoubleDutch event app, with a Firebase-backed data layer, a UI component library, an admin/CMS client, and a command-line interface — all published as official @doubledutch npm packages. DoubleDutch was acquired by Cvent in 2019 and its technology now lives under Cvent's mobile event apps product; www.doubledutch.me redirects to Cvent. The developer surface (GitHub org, the doubledutch.github.io documentation site, and the npm packages) remains published but is unmaintained. There is no public REST OpenAPI — the platform is a client-side extension SDK rather than a hosted web API.

providers.name: Edufund
providers.description: EduFund is an Indian fintech platform that helps parents plan and invest for their children’s education costs. It offers fixed‑deposit, mutual‑fund, and loan products, along with AI‑driven calculators and counselling services to optimise long‑term education savings.

providers.name: Eero
providers.description: eero makes home mesh Wi-Fi systems that are simple, powerful, secure, and reliable. eero pioneered home mesh wifi and sells products for homes, businesses, service providers, pro installers, and communities, including the eero Pro 7, eero PoE 7, and eero Signal, plus the eero Plus subscription for enhanced security and multi-network management. Devices are managed through the award-winning eero app and are deployed across 27+ countries. eero LLC is based in San Francisco, CA and is an Amazon company. eero does not publish a public developer API or first-party SDK; the eero app communicates with a private, unpublished backend.

providers.name: Equipboard
providers.description: Equipboard is a community-sourced music-gear discovery platform where musicians, producers, and DJs find the equipment behind the music. Members browse the gear their favorite artists play — guitars, effects pedals, synthesizers, DAWs, plug-ins, microphones, drum machines, and keyboards — build and share their own rigs and gear lists, read and write reviews, and follow buy-links to retailers. Equipboard is built by musicians for musicians and monetizes primarily through affiliate relationships (including the Amazon Associates Program). Recent product work adds album- and track-level gear attribution. The company is backed by 500 Global. Equipboard does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile is maintained by the API Evangelist network and enriched from Equipboard's public web surface.

providers.name: Fieldpoint
providers.description: Fieldpoint is an enterprise field service management (FSM) platform built for commercial contractors and service organizations across HVAC, electrical, fire inspection, security, medical equipment, and technology verticals. The platform covers the full service lifecycle including quoting, work order management, scheduling and dispatching, mobile technician apps, inventory tracking, service contracts, project costing, and customer management. Fieldpoint exposes an open REST API known as the Fieldpoint Data Transfer Service (FPDTS) that enables custom integrations with ERP, CRM, accounting, payroll, and workforce management systems. The platform ships pre-built connectors for Microsoft Dynamics GP/365, NetSuite, QuickBooks, Salesforce, WorkMarket, AvaTax, and more, while the FPDTS API allows enterprises to build bespoke integrations with any additional back-office system.

providers.name: Fintua
providers.description: Fintua provides a comprehensive platform for indirect tax compliance, offering solutions for VAT registration, e‑invoicing, VAT recovery, and global payment integration. Their services include consultancy, data transformation, audit review, and a suite of tools to help businesses manage VAT obligations across multiple jurisdictions, supported by a resource library, webinars, and a community of tax experts.

providers.name: Fluxx
providers.description: Fluxx is a cloud grants management platform for foundations, government agencies, corporations, and nonprofits, covering the full grant lifecycle from funding announcement through pre-award applications, post-award payments, and measurement and evaluation. Fluxx Grantmaker includes a RESTful API (REST API v2) available to customers for building custom integrations with financial, CRM, and business-intelligence systems. The API is exposed per-client on each customer's own Fluxx instance under https://{client}.fluxx.io/api/rest/v2, is authenticated with OAuth 2.0 credentials created in that instance, and is driven by a dynamic, instance-specific data model whose reference documentation is generated at /api/rest/v2/doc for each deployment. Because the surface is per-instance and gated behind an authenticated customer deployment, the endpoints below are honestly modeled from Fluxx's documented REST v2 conventions rather than pulled from a single public reference.

providers.name: Fortell
providers.description: Fortell develops clinically proven AI hearing aids that provide superior speech clarity in noisy environments. The company leverages advanced AI algorithms and scientific research to enhance hearing experiences for users, offering personalized solutions and a modern approach to auditory health.

providers.name: Funding Societies
providers.description: Funding Societies (known as Modalku in Indonesia) is Southeast Asia's largest unified SME digital finance platform, founded in 2015 and operating across Singapore, Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand and Vietnam. It provides small and medium-sized enterprises with business financing — term loans, micro loans, revolving credit lines, invoice and trade financing — and offers retail and institutional investors the ability to fund those loans for a return. The group is licensed and regulated in its markets and is backed by investors including SoftBank Vision Fund, Sequoia, and SoftBank Ventures Asia. Funding Societies does not currently publish a public developer API or SDK program; this API Evangelist profile captures the company's public web properties and security posture. It will be upgraded if and when a public API surface is published.

providers.name: GitStart
providers.description: GitStart provides AI‑powered coding agents that help development teams turn vague tickets into detailed specifications, generate merge‑ready pull requests, and automate code quality checks. Their platform includes Ticket Studio for transforming tickets, Accelerate for delivering production‑ready PRs, and GitSlice for fine‑grained security controls. Serving forward‑thinking companies, GitStart aims to streamline development workflows, reduce technical debt, and improve code quality through a hybrid of AI agents and human oversight.

providers.name: Goodweek
providers.description: Goodweek provides an AI management platform that enables enterprises to securely deploy, monitor, and govern AI models across their organization. The platform offers centralized model storage, usage analytics, policy enforcement, and integration capabilities, helping teams work faster, smarter, and safer with AI. It serves various use cases from inbox filtering to financial forecasting, emphasizing visibility, control, and compliance for AI deployments.

providers.name: Grotto AI
providers.description: Grotto AI is an AI sales-coaching platform purpose-built for the multifamily apartment leasing industry. Founded by former EvolutionIQ leaders Nick Deveau (CEO) and Ben Epstein (CTO), Grotto delivers real-time call guidance, tour and call coaching, and prospect-lifecycle support across email and text that help leasing agents handle objections, book tours, and convert more leads to recover net operating income and asset value. The platform works alongside multifamily systems such as Entrata, Funnel, and Yardi and is used by operators including Weidner Apartment Homes and Hillpointe. Grotto is SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27701 certified and Fair Housing compliant. It is backed by ICONIQ. Grotto does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; it is a demo-led enterprise SaaS product.

providers.name: Haulest
providers.description: Haulest, operated by Panaweb LLC (Dover, Delaware), publishes moving-cost ranges, route facts, reviewed movers, mover licence checks, moving guides and checklists for the US, Canada and the UK, and exposes them to AI assistants through a no-auth remote MCP server at https://haulest.com/mcp with eight tools including estimate_moving_cost, find_movers and request_moving_quotes. Haulest is not a carrier and does not operate trucks.

providers.name: Heven AeroTech
providers.description: Heven AeroTech (formerly Heven Drones) is a Dulles, Virginia headquartered manufacturer of hydrogen fuel-cell powered, runway-independent unmanned aircraft systems built for defense, national security and public safety missions. Founded in 2019, the company designs its own hydrogen propulsion stack and ships six named airframes — Raider, Z1, H2D55, Refueler, Atlas and Urban X — marketed on multi-hour endurance, low thermal and acoustic signature, and rapid payload and hydrogen-tank swaps. The Z1 is listed as a Blue UAS Select platform and the H2D55, Raider and Z1 are advertised as NDAA compliant. Heven operates sites in Dulles VA, Bingen WA, Mevo Carmel Israel and Mumbai India, and raised a $100M Series B led by IonQ. Heven AeroTech is a hardware manufacturer: it publishes no public developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable contract.

providers.name: Hole19
providers.description: Hole19 (Stat Track Technologies Lda) is a golf app for iOS, Android, and smartwatches used by 4.8M+ golfers across 42,000+ golf courses in 200+ countries. It provides GPS rangefinder distances, digital scorecards, shot tracking, performance statistics, an Otto AI game assistant, and a WHS handicap calculator, plus social features such as LivePlay live leaderboards and a social feed. The company also ships CORE Golf, a practice app with structured plans and 100+ drills, and operates a worldwide golf course directory, a golf glossary, and The 19th Hole magazine. The core app is free with two subscription tiers, Premium and Intelligence. Hole19 does not publish a public developer API; this profile captures its public web, legal, support, and llms.txt surface.

providers.name: Intermedia
providers.description: Intermedia is a cloud communications company serving over 145,000 businesses with an AI-powered platform spanning voice, video conferencing, chat, SMS, contact center, business email, productivity, file sharing, security, and archiving. The Intermedia Extend API platform exposes Voice, Meeting, Analytics, Address Book, and Contact Center APIs for embedding communications into CRMs, ERPs, ticketing systems, and custom business applications.

providers.name: Jobvite
providers.description: Jobvite, part of Employ Inc., is an applicant tracking system (ATS) and recruiting platform that helps enterprises source, hire, and onboard talent. The platform combines candidate relationship management, recruitment marketing, branded career sites, and onboarding workflows. Jobvite provides REST APIs that facilitate real-time data exchange in JSON for candidate records, requisitions, applications, and the Onboard New Hire endpoint.

providers.name: Junk King
providers.description: Junk King is a professional junk removal and hauling franchise operating across the United States and Canada as part of the Neighborly family of home service brands. Through locally owned and operated locations, Junk King provides full-service junk removal, self-service dumpster rental, and dumpster bag pickup for residential and commercial customers, handling appliance and furniture removal, estate and property cleanouts, construction debris, yard waste, and e-waste. The company emphasizes eco-friendly disposal, recycling, donating, and reusing as much collected material as possible. Junk King offers free estimates, same-day service in many markets, and online, phone, and text-based booking. It is a portfolio company associated with Norwest Venture Partners and is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile; Junk King publishes no public API or developer platform.

providers.name: Kinema
providers.description: Kinema is a social cinema platform and independent film distribution service. It empowers independent filmmakers to release, control, and get paid for their films through global distribution, partner-driven and live screenings, and direct-to-audience streaming, with ownership retention, transparent weekly payouts, and real-time earnings dashboards. Hosts and community builders get screening software and event tools to turn any space into a movie house, in person or online, while audiences discover independent films and attend virtual or in-person screenings, directly supporting filmmakers through ticket and rental purchases.

providers.name: Kubectl
providers.description: kubectl is the official command-line tool for Kubernetes, used to deploy applications, inspect resources, and manage clusters via the Kubernetes API.

providers.name: LeaseLock
providers.description: LeaseLock is an insurtech platform for rental housing that replaces the traditional cash security deposit with lease insurance. Its Zero Deposit program embeds coverage into the lease through a signed addendum, removing thousands of dollars of move-in cost for residents while protecting owners and operators against unpaid rent and damage. LeaseLock Shield applies AI to ledger data, market trends and lease profiles to underwrite risk, and LeaseLock Central gives property teams a portal for claims, support tickets and training. Founded in 2016 and headquartered in Dallas, Texas, the company says it integrates with all major property management systems, but publishes no public developer API, developer portal, API reference or client SDKs — integration is arranged as a managed engagement. Its public engineering output is two open-source PostgreSQL extensions, pgasync and pgflow.

providers.name: Letswork
providers.description: Letswork is a Dubai-headquartered flexible workspace booking platform that lets members work from coworking spaces, cafes, hotels, meeting rooms, private offices and creative studios through a single credit-based monthly membership with no long-term contract. Founded in 2019 by Omar AlMheiri and Hamza Khan, the platform covers 1030+ workspaces across 63+ cities in 18+ countries, serving 80,000+ members across the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Egypt, Pakistan, Europe and Sub-Saharan Africa. The product ships as iOS, Android and web apps with one-tap check-in, day passes, hourly meeting-room booking, a private-offices marketplace, and team plans that add a shared credit pool, admin dashboard and usage analytics for hybrid companies. Letswork publishes no public developer API or developer portal; it does publish a first-party llms.txt canonical fact set for AI assistants.

providers.name: Levo
providers.description: Levo provides an AI‑powered API security platform that protects both traditional APIs and emerging AI‑driven services. The solution offers runtime visibility, threat detection, red‑teaming, and governance across the entire application stack, integrating with CI/CD pipelines and supporting compliance for industries such as banking, insurance, healthcare, and retail. Levo’s platform unifies API and AI security, delivering real‑time risk insights, automated policy enforcement, and detailed reporting to help organizations secure complex, dynamic micro‑service architectures and AI models.

providers.name: LiqPay
providers.description: LiqPay is a Ukrainian payment platform operated by PrivatBank that provides REST APIs for accepting card payments, creating hosted payment pages, processing subscriptions, managing refunds, sending invoices, and conducting card-to-card transfers. It supports Mastercard, Visa, Apple Pay, Google Pay, and Privat24 wallets across 120+ countries, with full fiscalization (RRO) support for Ukrainian merchants.

providers.name: Livsn Designs
providers.description: Livsn Designs is a Techstars-backed outdoor apparel brand that makes durable, minimalist technical clothing (its Flex Canvas pants and multi-use travel and hiking apparel) sold direct-to-consumer from a Shopify storefront at livsndesigns.com. It publishes no first-party developer API or documentation portal. Its only programmatic surface is the agent-commerce layer Shopify serves on the merchant's own domain: a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) shopping MCP endpoint for agent-driven checkout, a Shopify Customer Account OIDC/OAuth2 authorization server, and an llms.txt / agents.md agent-instructions document. This profile captures that real agent surface; there is no bespoke API to catalog.

providers.name: Llama
providers.description: Llama is Meta's family of open-weight large language models, available for download, self-hosting, and via Meta's hosted Llama API for chat completions, text generation, and embeddings. The ecosystem also includes the open-source llama-models, llama-stack, and PurpleLlama safety projects on GitHub.

providers.name: Lootex
providers.description: Lootex is a Web3 infrastructure and AI application development company with eight years in the blockchain space, backed by 500 Global. It built a multi-chain NFT marketplace (Seaport protocol with aggregator support), the Lootex Studio minting tool, the Biru social platform, and Lootex Plus (an API and SDK offering to mint, trade, and integrate NFTs into apps and games). Its core marketplace infrastructure — a NestJS backend and Next.js frontend with blockchain event indexing and Web3 wallet authentication — is published as open source under Apache-2.0. Lootex is now sunsetting its consumer products (marketplace, Studio, and Biru wind down on 2026-04-04; assets stay in users' own non-custodial wallets) and pivoting to full-stack AI/Web3 development partnerships and open-source contributions.

providers.name: Medusa (TV)
providers.description: Medusa (TV) is an open-source automated video library manager designed for TV show enthusiasts. It continuously monitors your favorite series for new episodes, automatically downloading, organizing, and renaming them according to your preferences. Built with Python, it integrates with popular indexers, download clients, and media servers, providing a seamless experience for keeping your collection up to date without manual effort.

providers.name: Mottu
providers.description: Mottu is the leading motorcycle-rental ecosystem in Latin America, founded in 2020 in Sao Paulo, Brazil by Rubens Zanelatto. It rents motorcycles to gig and delivery couriers who lack access to traditional credit, bundling insurance, maintenance, 24-hour support and financial services (Mottu Pay) so workers can earn income through food delivery, e-commerce and last-mile logistics. Mottu has verticalized the value chain, running its own assembly line, parts and service network, and fleet-management software, and offers white-labeled last-mile delivery (Mottu Entregas) to more than 1,000 retailers across 100+ cities in Brazil and Mexico. Backed by QED Investors, Mottu has raised over US$150M. It operates as a consumer and B2B mobility/fintech app and does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Mutual of Omaha
providers.description: Mutual of Omaha is a Fortune 500 mutual insurance and financial services company headquartered in Omaha, Nebraska, providing life, disability, dental, vision, critical illness, accident and long-term care insurance, Medicare supplement and Medicare Advantage plans, annuities, retirement services, mortgage lending and investment products to individuals, employers and groups across the United States. Its Workplace Solutions unit runs an API integration program for group and voluntary benefits — Plan Setup, Evidence of Insurability and Enrollment — but those APIs are delivered through benefits administration platform partners such as ADP Workforce Now, bswift, Employee Navigator and PlanSource rather than through a public developer portal, and no machine-readable contract is published.

providers.name: National Health Service
providers.description: The National Health Service (NHS) of England publishes a catalogue of APIs for health and care providers, including the Ambulance Data Submission FHIR API used to submit ambulance data to the NHS Data Processing Service (DPS) for analysis and review by NHS England and ambulance trusts.

providers.name: NEURA Robotics
providers.description: NEURA Robotics is a German deep-tech company building cognitive and humanoid robots for industry, business, and everyday life. It develops robots such as the 4NE-1 humanoid and the MAiRA, MiPA, LARA, and MAV cognitive cobots, powered by its proprietary AI system AURA. Its Neuraverse ecosystem is a connected platform and app marketplace that links robots, developers, and partners so AI models, applications, and hardware come together to make the robots smarter. NEURA Robotics is backed by HV Capital. As of this profile the company exposes no public, documented developer API: neuraverse.com is a gated single-page application portal, and no OpenAPI, developer documentation, or well-known discovery endpoints are published on its public surface.

providers.name: novusmcp-se
providers.description: Novus MCP connects Fortnox accounting software with AI assistants like ChatGPT and Claude, enabling businesses to query their bookkeeping data via conversational interfaces. Operated by AMR Intelligence Sweden AB, the service emphasizes secure data handling, GDPR compliance, and flexible AI integration, offering a 30‑day open‑return policy and agency‑level support for agencies and enterprises.

providers.name: On Me
providers.description: On Me is a San Francisco digital gifting company that sells wallet-native, multi-brand eGift cards organised by hobby and interest rather than by single retailer. Founded by former Google product managers Darragh Meaney and Sitar Harel, it emerged from stealth in December 2024 with a five-year Mastercard partnership and $1.7M in pre-seed funding led by Lerer Hippeau and Focal VC. Recipients add a gift to Apple Wallet or Google Wallet and tap to pay across a curated category of brands, and senders can attach photos, video and GIFs. A business portal supports corporate gifting, campaigns and bulk sends. On Me markets a forthcoming Gifting API for programmatic rewards, incentives and webhooks, but as of this pass no public API reference, base URL, or machine-readable specification is published — access runs through a "talk to a specialist" sales conversation.

providers.name: One Auto API
providers.description: One Auto API provides comprehensive automotive data APIs for vehicle lookup, valuations, retail pricing, and more across the US, UK, and Europe. Their platform offers over 100 API methods covering car images, mileage checks, specifications, electric vehicle data, registration lookup, service history, and valuation, all accessible via a single subscription and monthly invoice. Designed for developers, product managers, and dealers, the service includes bulk report building, VRM360 insights, and consultancy services, backed by multiple data providers.

providers.name: Ontruck
providers.description: Ontruck is a Spanish road-freight technology platform that connects shippers (cargadores) with a network of professional carriers (transportistas) for full-truckload and less-than-truckload pallet, package, and parcel transport across Spain, France, and wider Europe. Shippers get instant AI-driven pricing, automated carrier assignment, real-time traceability, and digital documentation through service tiers (Economy, Flex, Express); carriers get access to freight loads with dynamic pricing and 24/7 support. Ontruck also packages its stack as "Ontruck AI Tech" — an AI pricing engine, AI routing engine, a predictive incident system, and a forecast/capacity planner — offered as transport-management software. The company operates a marketing and customer web surface plus an in-product shipper/carrier application; it publishes no public developer/API portal, OpenAPI, or SDKs at this time.

providers.name: Open Bank Project
providers.description: Open Bank Project (OBP) provides an open-source API platform enabling banks and fintechs to build, manage, and secure open banking APIs. It offers a sandbox, compliance tools, and developer resources to accelerate integration with PSD2 and other standards, fostering innovation across financial services.

providers.name: Perfios
providers.description: Perfios is a Bangalore, India-headquartered financial technology (SaaS) company providing an AI-driven operating system for banks, NBFCs, fintechs, and insurers, serving over 1,000 financial institutions globally. Its platform spans four product families: Perfios Analyse (bank statement, ITR, GST, payslip, credit-card and financial-statement analysers), Perfios Verify (KYC/KYB, video KYC, liveness detection, OCR, digital signature and onboarding via OneSDK), Perfios Lens (portfolio monitoring, PFM, credit assessment memos, due diligence), and Perfios Protect (document tamper detection, deepfake detection, and insurance fraud detection). Perfios also runs a digital public infrastructure (DPI) stack for Account Aggregator FIU/FIP roles. Its data-aggregation, decisioning, and verification capabilities are delivered to partners programmatically; public developer documentation is gated behind partner access. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners.

providers.name: Pinokio
providers.description: Pinokio is an open-source desktop application — self-described as an "AI Browser" — that acts as a 1-click launcher for any open-source AI project. Built by independent developer Cocktail Peanut (cocktailpeanut), Pinokio packages a terminal, package managers (Conda, Homebrew, Pip, NPM), and a graphical UI into a single MIT-licensed desktop app for macOS, Windows, and Linux with NVIDIA, AMD, and Apple Silicon GPU support. Users install AI apps with one click from a curated "Discover" directory of 160+ vetted scripts spanning image generation, video generation, text-to-speech and voice cloning, large language models, 3D generation, music and audio generation, and face swap. Pinokio is driven by a JSON-based scripting language designed to be both human and machine readable, with primitives like shell.run, fs, input, log, jump, hf (Hugging Face), notify, browser, and json that let publishers describe install and launch flows declaratively. Each script is sandboxed under ~/pinokio with isolated paths and Python virtual environments, and featured scripts must transfer ownership to the Pinokio Factory GitHub organization for admin review. Pinokio is purely client-side open source — there is no public REST API, no hosted commercial offering, and no developer SDK beyond the local script syntax and the desktop app itself.

providers.name: PlayStation
providers.description: PlayStation, a brand of Sony Interactive Entertainment, is a leading global provider of interactive entertainment hardware, software, and services. It offers the PlayStation consoles, a vast library of games, subscription services like PlayStation Plus, and a developer ecosystem. The company engages millions of players worldwide through innovative gaming experiences, community features, and a robust digital marketplace.

providers.name: Posha
providers.description: Posha (formerly Nymble) is a consumer robotics company that makes an autonomous countertop kitchen robot which cooks fresh, home-style meals from raw ingredients across 1,000+ recipes. The device combines robotics, computer-vision cameras, automated heat, timing and stirring control, and culinary AI, paired with an iOS/Android companion app for real-time monitoring and recipe control. Backed by Accel, Posha is a consumer hardware and appliance product with a companion mobile app; it does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or webhook surface. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead and enriched with real, verifiable public properties.

providers.name: Project Auxo, Inc.
providers.description: Project Auxo, Inc. operates the capabilities.txt initiative, an open convention allowing websites to publish a simple, human‑readable file that declares the actions they can perform. This enables agents to discover and invoke site capabilities such as support ticket creation, inventory checks, and other services via a well‑known location, fostering interoperable, agent‑centric web interactions.

providers.name: PSD Citywide
providers.description: PSD Citywide is a SaaS provider of enterprise asset management (EAM) and public-sector software for North American municipalities and government organizations. Its integrated Citywide platform spans asset management, maintenance and work-order management, GIS integration (ESRI-powered mapping), permitting, planning and licensing with citizen portals, multi-year budgeting and forecasting, facility/space management (Spaces), and a field mobile app, alongside asset-management advisory and grant services. The homepage references a "robust API" for integration and customization, but no public developer portal, API reference, SDKs, or GitHub organization were found during enrichment; end-user product documentation is published in a HappyFox-powered help center. Added to the API Evangelist network via the norwest-venture-partners portfolio.

providers.name: RESTful
providers.description: Representational State Transfer (REST) is an architectural style for designing networked applications using stateless HTTP communication and uniform interfaces. RESTful describes systems and APIs that conform to the REST constraints: client-server separation, statelessness, cacheability, layered system, uniform interface, and (optionally) code-on-demand. This index covers the RESTful design paradigm including maturity models, API design patterns, documentation formats, and key reference implementations.

providers.name: SS&C Geneva
providers.description: SS&C Geneva is an enterprise-grade fund accounting and portfolio management platform for asset managers, hedge funds, and fund administrators. Geneva supports NAV calculation, trade processing, investor accounting, position management, and regulatory reporting across multi-asset portfolios including equities, fixed income, derivatives, and alternative investments.

providers.name: StartEngine
providers.description: StartEngine is a Los Angeles based online private-market investment platform that lets everyday investors buy equity in startups and pre-IPO companies, and lets founders raise capital under Regulation Crowdfunding, Regulation A+ and Regulation D. The company operates StartEngine Capital, its FINRA-registered funding portal; StartEngine Private, a fund vehicle for later-stage pre-IPO companies; a secondary marketplace for trading eligible private shares; and StartEngine Secure, an SEC-registered transfer agent and cap-table management service sold to issuers on a published monthly plan. StartEngine publishes no public developer API, SDK, webhook catalog or developer portal - its public engineering output is an internal design-system npm scope, agent examples, and Ethereum security-token standards work (the ERC-1450 reference implementation).

providers.name: Subsplash
providers.description: Subsplash is an all-in-one church and ministry engagement platform - custom mobile and TV apps, websites, media hosting and delivery, online giving, and church management (People, Groups, Events, Volunteers). Subsplash publishes a REST developer API (OAuth 2.0, hosted on core.subsplash.com) for programmatic access to media, giving records, people, groups and messaging, and event registrations. Access is gated - full API documentation is released only after submitting the developer documentation-access form, and API credentials (Client ID / Client Secret) must be provisioned by a Subsplash representative on a qualifying paid plan (Pro / Enterprise). Because the documented endpoint surface is behind that gate, the APIs listed here are modeled from Subsplash's public product, support, and integration material rather than transcribed from an open reference, and are flagged endpointsModeled.

providers.name: tablethis-ai
providers.description: TableThis provides a shared database platform for AI‑built internal applications, offering typed tables and Markdown documentation that teams can collaborate on. It enables developers to connect large language models like Claude or Codex to a central data store, allowing AI assistants to read, write, and update information with version history and access controls. The service is free to start with 100 MB of storage and no credit card required, targeting teams that want to build internal tools powered by AI without managing infrastructure.

providers.name: Talk-A-Bot
providers.description: Talk-A-Bot is a Budapest-based, Techstars-backed enterprise chatbot company building compliance-first conversational AI for regulated industries including banking, healthcare, government, retail, and HR. Its platform emphasizes "zero hallucination" answers grounded only in verified knowledge bases, full conversation logging and audit trails, EU-based infrastructure with on-premise deployment options, and daily human review. Products include an FAQ Chatbot, an Agentic Chatbot, FeedbackHub, and the CHEQ internal-communications assistant, deployed across web, mobile, Messenger, and Viber. The company markets an API-first architecture for integrating with customer systems (CRM, ERP, payments, ticketing, HR) but publishes no public self-serve developer API, OpenAPI, or SDK; engagement is full-service. Compliance posture spans HIPAA, DORA, the EU AI Act, GDPR, and PCI DSS.

providers.name: Tenneco
providers.description: Tenneco is a global manufacturer of automotive components and systems, including clean air, powertrain, and ride performance systems for OEM and aftermarket markets. Through its DRiV aftermarket division, Tenneco serves mechanics, distributors, and retailers with digital catalog and parts lookup capabilities.

providers.name: The Clearing House (RTP)
providers.description: The Clearing House (TCH) is a U.S. banking association and payments company owned by many of the largest commercial banks. It operates three core payment systems: CHIPS (large-value wire clearing), the EPN automated clearing house (ACH), and the RTP network, the private-sector real-time payments rail it launched in 2017 as the first new U.S. payments infrastructure in decades. RTP is a 24/7/365 instant-payments scheme built on the ISO 20022 messaging standard, supporting immediate credit-push transfers up to $10 million with final settlement, plus Request for Payment (RfP), remittance data, and a UID addressing/directory lookup. TCH is the scheme operator for the U.S. market and competes with the Federal Reserve's FedNow service. Its API posture is documentation- and rulebook-first: TCH does not publish an open, self-serve public REST API or downloadable OpenAPI/Swagger specification. Instead it publishes ISO 20022 message specifications (pacs, pain, camt, remt) as PDFs, the RTP network operating rules, playbooks, and a technology-provider program. Real-time HTTP/JSON RTP APIs are surfaced to businesses by participating financial institutions (for example U.S. Bank) and registered technology providers that connect to the RTP network on their behalf.

providers.name: Thruster
providers.description: Thruster was a yield-first decentralized exchange (DEX) built natively on the Blast Ethereum Layer 2, offering Uniswap-style v2 and v3 concentrated liquidity AMMs, a stableswap AMM, and a token launchpad. Backed by Pantera Capital, the protocol shut down on July 29, 2025 after completing THRUST holder redemptions; its thruster.finance website is offline, while the GitBook documentation and the ThrusterX GitHub organization (Solidity contracts and audit reports) remain the surviving public record. No REST/HTTP API was published; the developer surface was on-chain smart contracts on Blast.

providers.name: Tigerconnect
providers.description: TigerConnect is a healthcare clinical communication and collaboration (CC&C) platform used by 7,000+ healthcare organizations to unify secure messaging, clinical collaboration, alarm management, physician and nurse scheduling, patient engagement, nurse call, and pre-hospital care-team coordination on one activation layer. It integrates with 200+ medical devices and EHR systems and adds an AI orchestration engine (CareConduit) that routes alerts and workflows to the right clinical role at the right time. TigerConnect is recognized as a leader in the 2025 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Clinical Communications and Collaboration. The company publishes end-user product release notes, an SLA, and legal terms, but exposes no public developer API portal or OpenAPI at this time.

providers.name: TikTok Shop API
providers.description: TikTok Shop is TikTok's integrated e-commerce platform that lets sellers, creators, and partners list products, manage inventory and fulfillment, and sell directly within TikTok's live streams, short videos, and shop tabs. The TikTok Shop Open API (open-api.tiktokglobalshop.com) is a RESTful API that uses OAuth 2.0 authentication and enables developers to programmatically manage products, orders, fulfillment, returns, finance, promotions, and seller authorization across TikTok Shop's global marketplaces.

providers.name: UBS Bank USA
providers.description: UBS Bank USA (BUSA) is a Utah state-chartered industrial bank and FDIC-insured depository institution headquartered in Salt Lake City, Utah, established in 2003 and reporting roughly $122 billion in total assets. It is the primary US banking vehicle of UBS Wealth Management Americas, providing FDIC-insured deposit sweep programs, securities-based lending, mortgages, and credit cards almost exclusively to the high-net-worth and ultra-high-net-worth advisory clients of parent UBS Group AG. It is supervised by the FDIC, the Utah Department of Financial Institutions, and the CFPB. Unlike a fintech or a Banking-as-a-Service provider, UBS Bank USA exposes no first-party public developer API surface of its own; its services are delivered through UBS Financial Advisors rather than self-serve APIs. The only live UBS developer portal (developer.ubs.com) belongs to UBS Switzerland and serves Swiss and EU products (key4 mortgages, QR-bill, PSD2, TWINT, bLink, KeyPort/EBICS), not this US entity. US consumer-permissioned data access, where available, is mediated by third-party aggregators rather than a documented BUSA API.

providers.name: Urbia
providers.description: Urbia is a German online community and content platform for parents and families, covering fertility, pregnancy, birth, babies, and family life through expert-written magazine articles, active discussion forums, and planning tools. Founded in Cologne in 1998 and backed early by Earlybird Venture Capital, urbia.de is today part of the ELTERN family of parenting brands, operated by Funke Women, People & Family GmbH in Hamburg. Urbia does not publish a public API or developer program.

providers.name: Virool
providers.description: Virool is a native video advertising platform that distributes branded video content ("advertainment") across the web to help brands reach and grow targeted audiences. It pairs a proprietary data-management platform of roughly 450 million unique profiles for granular audience targeting with native video placement technology designed to minimize disruption to the user experience, and a real-time performance analytics dashboard that includes emotional insight tracking (eIQ). Virool serves advertisers and publishers through self-service campaign and monetization dashboards rather than a public developer API. The company was backed by 500 Global and a16z and has run campaigns for brands including Turkish Airlines, Under Armour, and WestJet.

providers.name: Visby Medical
providers.description: Visby Medical is a molecular diagnostics company that has miniaturized the gold-standard PCR laboratory onto a single-use, palm-sized point-of-care device, delivering lab-quality results in about 30 minutes without any instrument, sample transport, or lab infrastructure. Its consumer offering (sold direct at visby.com) is an FDA-authorized at-home women's sexual health test that detects Chlamydia, Gonorrhea, and Trichomoniasis, paired with same-day telehealth consultation on a positive result. Visby also builds point-of-care PCR platforms for clinical and respiratory pathogen testing. The company is backed by venture investors including Amplify Partners. This API Evangelist profile tracks Visby Medical as a company; the business is a hardware diagnostics and direct-to-consumer commerce operation and does not publish a first-party developer API, SDK, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: WeiMai
providers.description: WeiMai (微脉) is a Chinese healthcare technology company operated by Choice Technology Inc. and headquartered in Hangzhou. It runs an internet-based medical services marketplace and licensed internet hospitals (including Hainan WeiMai Internet Hospital) that connect patients with doctors for online consultation, pharmaceutical products, medical devices, and health-management service packages, delivered primarily through the WeiMai consumer mobile app. WeiMai also operates a partner-facing Open Platform (微脉开发平台) at openapi.myweimai.com that exposes a Swagger 2.0 API surface for approved integrators; the public specification is a minimal stub with no operations exposed without partner credentials. The company is backed by IDG Capital and was added to the API Evangelist network as a healthcare portfolio company.

providers.name: Worq
providers.description: WORQ is Malaysia's largest community-centric coworking space operator, backed by 500 Global, offering private offices, dedicated desks, hot desks, virtual offices, meeting rooms, event spaces, and day passes across twelve locations in Greater Kuala Lumpur and Selangor. WORQ publishes no public developer portal or API as of July 2026.

providers.name: Zomma
providers.description: Zomma (Zomma Labs) is a Y Combinator (Summer 2026) startup building AI agents that automate repetitive back-office operations for investment firms — hedge funds, asset managers, and fintech companies. Rather than integrating through traditional APIs, its computer-use agents perceive and operate existing portals, desktop applications, and PDFs the way a human would (clicking, reading, typing) to handle reconciliation, client onboarding, KYC, and investor reporting, with human approval required before any submission. Zomma also markets a developer-facing computer-use API ("plug Hermes, Claude, or your own agent into our API") that is currently waitlist / pre-general availability with no public specification, SDK, or documentation.

providers.name: コエカツ
providers.description: コエカツは無料でアンケートの作成・投票ができる日本のアンケートサイトです。ユーザーはログイン不要で投票でき、棒・円グラフで集計を確認できます。無料アカウント登録後にアンケートを作成・公開でき、集計データは自由に再利用可能です。

providers.name: AAVantgarde Bio
providers.description: AAVantgarde Bio is a clinical-stage biotechnology company headquartered in Milan, Italy, developing next-generation adeno-associated virus (AAV) gene therapies for inherited retinal diseases with high unmet need. Founded in 2021 by Prof. Alberto Auricchio, the company has built two proprietary vector platforms — dual hybrid and dual intein — that overcome the DNA cargo capacity limit of a single AAV vector by splitting a large expression cassette across two AAV8 vectors that recombine inside the target cell. Its lead programs are AAVB-081 for retinitis pigmentosa due to Usher syndrome type 1B (LUCE-1 Phase 1/2, the first dual AAV gene therapy tested clinically in an ocular indication) and AAVB-039 for ABCA4-associated Stargardt disease (CELESTE Phase 1/2), which holds FDA Fast Track and Orphan Drug designation. The company raised a EUR 61 million Series A and closed a USD 141 million Series B. AAVantgarde publishes no public API, developer program or machine-readable contract; this profile records what its public web surface actually serves.

providers.name: Aevia
providers.description: Aevia provides an AI companion service that lets users import their conversation histories from Claude and continue them with a personalized AI. The platform offers features such as automatic message generation, customizable interaction schedules, and data privacy controls, with a subscription model starting at $49 per month. It emphasizes user‑owned data, no credit‑card required for a 7‑day free trial, and tools for exporting and managing AI dialogues.

providers.name: Affogata
providers.description: Affogata provides an insights platform that transforms unstructured data into actionable, real‑time intelligence for research, product, data and AI teams. Their solution offers public benchmarks, AI‑ready data, and a managed API layer that enables enterprises to govern, audit, and integrate noisy data sources across industries, supporting use cases from market research to AI agent training.

providers.name: Agreable
providers.description: Agreable (아그레아블) is a South Korean direct-to-consumer brand-commerce company founded by Lim Seung-jin (임승진, "Jason Im") out of a reading-club community of the same name. It has run the frozen convenience-food platform Wingeat (윙잇, wingeat.com) since 2015, and in March 2022 renamed itself after that brand — the operating legal entity is now 주식회사 윙잇 (Wing Eat, Inc.) in Guro-gu, Seoul, and agreable.com and agreable.co.kr both redirect to career.wingeat.com. The company designs, contract-manufactures and fulfils its own private-label food brands — 윙잇Dining, 윙잇Made, 고른, 페이보잇, 랠리 and 방아당 — across more than 200 products. It is a consumer packaged-goods and retail operator, not a software vendor: it builds its storefront, ERP and fulfilment systems in house on private hosts and publishes no developer portal, no public API, no SDK, no machine-readable specification and no agent surface of any kind. Its GitHub organization, wingeat-inc, carries zero public repositories.

providers.name: Arbetsförmedlingen
providers.description: Arbetsförmedlingen is Sweden’s public employment service, offering job seekers access to job listings, career guidance, and support programs, while providing employers tools for recruitment and labor market analytics. The agency operates a comprehensive digital platform (arbetsformedlingen.se) with multilingual support, extensive statistics, and services for municipalities and partners, aiming to improve employment outcomes across the country.

providers.name: AuraCite
providers.description: AuraCite provides an analytics platform for Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) and AI Visibility Analytics. It tracks how large language models and AI search engines mention, describe, and cite brands, products, and companies. The service offers recurring measurements, source analysis, competitive benchmarking, and developer‑friendly workflows, including MCP‑ready integrations for programmatic data access. Pricing plans include a free brand check and paid packages for deeper insights.

providers.name: Axial Networks
providers.description: Axial Networks operates Axial (axial.net), a private deal network for mergers, acquisitions and capital raising in the North American lower middle market. Founded in 2010 and based in New York, the platform connects business owners, M&A advisors, private equity buyers, strategic acquirers and lenders around live sell-side and buy-side transactions, and publishes a public member directory, the Middle Market Review editorial forum, industry deal-activity dashboards and business valuation calculators. The member product runs at network.axial.net and product help documentation at guide.axial.net. Axial publishes an llms.txt orientation file for language models and a public status page, but ships no public API, SDK, webhook surface or developer program — the platform is delivered as an authenticated end-user application only.

providers.name: Beautiful Soup
providers.description: Beautiful Soup is a Python library for pulling data out of HTML and XML files, widely used for web scraping and screen scraping tasks. It provides a parse tree API with simple methods for navigating, searching, and modifying parsed HTML/XML documents. Beautiful Soup automatically handles encoding, supports multiple parsers (html.parser, lxml, html5lib), and integrates with CSS selectors via the Soup Sieve library. Current stable version is 4.14.3.

providers.name: BetterComp
providers.description: BetterComp provides a modern compensation platform that leverages AI and data integration to help companies price jobs, manage compensation structures, and make data‑driven pay decisions. The solution unifies HRIS data, market surveys, and internal pay logic, offering tools for range modeling, market pricing, reporting, and AI‑assisted decision making, aimed at improving speed, fairness, and strategic impact of compensation across organizations.

providers.name: Brainly
providers.description: Brainly is an education technology company founded in 2009 in Krakow, Poland (originally Zadane.pl) and now headquartered in New York City. It operates the world's largest online learning and homework-help community, a gamified, crowdsourced social-learning network where students, parents, and teachers ask and answer academic questions with verified answers from peers, educators, and Brainly's proprietary AI. As of 2025 the platform serves over 350 million monthly users across roughly 35 countries and has evolved from a community Q&A product into an agentic AI Learning Companion spanning homework help, AI tutoring, test prep, and classroom participation. Brainly is a consumer subscription business (Brainly Plus); it publishes no official public developer API — this profile captures its public web, security, and policy surface.

providers.name: Bruce
providers.description: Bruce is a curated professional intro network for licensed real estate, mortgage, title & escrow, and insurance professionals, built by Tanda Technologies, Inc. and founded by Jesse Chor. Rather than a directory, review site, or CRM, Bruce verifies each member's license and role, then lets them log intros and build a portable, verifiable track record. The Bruce Card is each member's living profile — stats, deals, intros, and market rank — that replaces the resume and the "trust me" claim with a sharable credential. Bruce also runs an AI-hosted editorial publication at blog.bruce.bot that profiles verified members in interview-style stories. Backed by Initialized Capital; surfaced into the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company.

providers.name: Catalina Crunch
providers.description: Catalina Crunch creates high‑protein, low‑sugar snacks and cereals, founded by a Type 1 diabetic to fill a market gap for nutritious, low‑sugar options. The brand now offers a broad portfolio of snacks, cereals, granola, and chocolate bars, emphasizing protein and fiber while minimizing sugar, and provides online shopping, subscriptions, and retail locations across the US.

providers.name: CD Baby
providers.description: CD Baby is an independent music distribution and publishing administration service for songwriters, performers, and independent record labels. Founded in 1998 and now part of Downtown Music Holdings under Virgin Music Group, CD Baby services over 50 million music assets from creators in hundreds of countries across six continents. The platform distributes music to 150+ digital service providers including Spotify, Apple Music, YouTube, Pandora, Tidal, TikTok, Amazon, Shazam, and Deezer, and is a flagship member of YouTube's Preferred Distributor Program plus a preferred partner with Apple and Spotify. Services include digital distribution, physical CD and vinyl manufacturing, publishing administration, cover song licensing, sync licensing through CDB Boost, YouTube and social monetization, performing rights organization (ASCAP, BMI, SOCAN) registration assistance, and promotion tools via SymphonyOS, HearNow, Show.co, Managed Ads, Groover, Laylo, and Internet Radio Airplay. Pricing is a one-time fee ($9.99 single, $14.99 album) with artists retaining over 90% of earnings. CD Baby has paid out more than $1 billion to artists. CD Baby has no public developer API, SDK, or open-source release; all distribution and reporting workflows are exposed only through the artist member portal at members.cdbaby.com.

providers.name: Certinia
providers.description: Certinia (formerly FinancialForce) is a Salesforce-native ERP, Professional Services Automation (PSA), and revenue-management suite delivered as managed packages that run inside a customer's Salesforce org. Its programmatic surface is not a standalone public REST product; it is a set of global Apex service classes (and legacy SOAP APIs) - Revenue Management, Billing Central, PSA, Accounting/ERP, Supply Chain, and Services CPQ - invoked on the Salesforce platform against Certinia managed-package objects. Certinia automates revenue recognition to ASC 606 and IFRS 15, subscription billing, project and resource management, and accounting. Access is gated - it requires a provisioned Salesforce org with the relevant Certinia managed package installed and the appropriate permission set or profile assigned. The endpoints documented here are modeled from Certinia's public Apex API developer references; they are not called against a public, unauthenticated HTTP base URL.

providers.name: Chengfengtechnology
providers.description: Shanghai Chengfeng Technology Co., Ltd. provides water monitoring and testing solutions, including unmanned vessels, buoy stations, and data platforms. Established in 2008, the company offers ISO‑certified products and services worldwide, focusing on environmental monitoring, water quality analysis, and integrated hardware‑software systems.

providers.name: CielStay
providers.description: CielStay provides a free AI-powered index for direct booking homes, aggregating over 90,000 properties for short‑term, seasonal, or long‑term stays. Users can search by preferences, location, or through their own AI agents, accessing listings across all channels without intermediary fees. The platform aims to simplify vacation rentals by offering transparent, AI‑enhanced discovery and direct booking options.

providers.name: civops-io
providers.description: civops-io is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: mcp-registry) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.

providers.name: Coinshift
providers.description: Coinshift is a non-custodial, multi-chain onchain treasury management platform for startups, DAOs and crypto-native organisations, founded in 2021 as MultiSafe and built on top of Safe (Gnosis Safe) multisig accounts. The application unifies portfolio tracking across ERC-20 tokens and NFTs, multi-signature proposal and transaction workflows, mass and recurring payouts, contact and label management, CSV transaction export and cash-flow reporting, plus embedded dApp integrations for Aave, CoW Swap, 1inch, LI.FI, ParaSwap, Hedgey, Request Finance and Superfluid money streams, with Slack and Discord signing notifications. Coinshift also issues onchain yield assets — csUSDL, an ERC-4626 vault receipt token for USDL deposited into the Coinshift USDL Morpho Vault, csUSDC, the SHIFT governance token, and the iUSPC institutional credit product. Coinshift publishes no public developer API: the documentation at docs.coinshift.xyz is entirely end-user product and asset guidance, with no developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI, GraphQL schema or webhook catalog.

providers.name: Converseon
providers.description: Converseon provides AI‑powered natural language processing solutions that help enterprises extract actionable insights from unstructured data such as social media, news, and voice‑of‑customer content. Their platform offers trusted model governance, customizable and pre‑built models, and a suite of analytics tools to improve data quality, enable predictive intelligence, and support market research workflows. Converseon serves sectors including finance, consumer goods, and public relations, delivering scalable, secure, and compliant AI services.

providers.name: Culture Biosciences
providers.description: Culture Biosciences is a South San Francisco TechBio company that builds cloud-connected bioreactor systems and bioprocess development services for cell culture. Its platform pairs automated single-use bioreactors (250mL bench-scale and 5L, plus the Stratyx mobile bioreactor) with Console, a cloud-native software product for real-time monitoring, experiment management, data analytics, and remote collaboration. Through its Nexxys services group the company runs clone/strain/construct screening, process characterization, process development, and bioprocess modeling and simulation for customers working on synthetic biology, protein therapeutics, and viral vectors. Culture Biosciences lets teams outsource and scale bioreactor experiments without scaling their own lab infrastructure. Backed by DCVC, Northpond Ventures, Synthesis Capital, S32, and Cultivian Sandbox Ventures. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; the company operates the Console cloud platform but does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, SDKs, or developer documentation.

providers.name: Cypherium
providers.description: Cypherium is a permissionless Layer-1 blockchain built to bridge centralized (CeFi) and decentralized (DeFi) finance and bring real-world assets on-chain at scale. It runs CypherBFT, a hybrid consensus that pairs GPU proof-of-work committee election with HotStuff Byzantine Fault Tolerance for near-instant finality, and is EVM/Solidity compatible (EVM chain ID 16166). Products include CypherLink (cross-ledger notary), Cypherium Connect (bank integration plugin, marketed as ISO 20022 compliant), the Cypherium Validator, and Cypherium ID (decentralized identity). Developers integrate through an Ethereum-style JSON-RPC node API (eth/web3/net/ personal/miner/txpool/admin namespaces over HTTP, WS and IPC) and a Coinbase Rosetta API implementation for exchange and wallet integration. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Pantera Capital and enriched into the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: DesarrolloMCP
providers.description: DesarrolloMCP offers a Spanish-language course on Model‑Centered Programming (MCP), teaching developers how to design servers that effectively leverage AI models. The curriculum includes 32 lessons covering the 2026‑07‑28 specification, with free basic content and paid advanced (10 €) and expert (25 €) tracks. It aims to empower creators to decide what to build and how to structure code for optimal model usage.

providers.name: DonateStock
providers.description: DonateStock is a platform that enables donors to contribute publicly traded stock, cryptocurrency, and other assets to charitable organizations quickly and tax-efficiently. By allowing donors to avoid capital gains tax and receive larger deductions, it benefits both donors and nonprofits. The service also offers tools for financial advisors and donors to manage charitable giving, featuring a marketplace of causes, educational resources, and a secure transaction process.

providers.name: Easy Metrics
providers.description: Easy Metrics provides a warehouse performance management platform that unifies operational, labor, and financial data into a real‑time view. It helps align execution with financial outcomes, driving measurable performance across the network. The solution includes OpsFM®, labor management, profit management, professional services, and data integrations, targeting leadership, operations, and finance roles.

providers.name: Ember
providers.description: Ember.js is a productive, battle-tested JavaScript framework for building modern web applications. It includes Ember CLI for scaffolding and builds, a best-in-class router with async data loading, the Ember Data layer, a three-level testing framework, the Glimmer rendering engine, and a six-week release cycle that emphasizes stability and easy upgrades through automated codemods.

providers.name: Entelo
providers.description: Entelo is an AI-powered talent-sourcing and recruiting-automation platform for finding, engaging, and hiring candidates using predictive analytics, diversity-aware search, and candidate-engagement tooling. Entelo was acquired and is now delivered as "Entelo Recruit" within Rival (rival-hr.com), an AI-powered HR orchestration suite spanning recruiting, workflow, learning, and performance. Its former domain entelo.com now 301-redirects to Rival. No public developer portal, API reference, or OpenAPI is currently published for the Entelo/Rival Recruit product.

providers.name: Farmo
providers.description: Farmo makes remote monitoring and automation simple and effective. We provide solutions for agriculture, industrial and smart city applications using mobile and satellite technologies. We deliver the data you need to take action and boost efficiency.

providers.name: FeezBack
providers.description: FeezBack is an Israeli open-banking fintech, founded in 2016, that builds the technological infrastructure and consumer products enabling financial players to compete in Israel's open-banking ecosystem. Its products cover account-to- account payment initiation (direct bank payments with no card-processing fees integrated into sales and point-of-sale flows), aggregated financial data for underwriting and risk assessment, and financial analysis for investment portfolio and risk allocation. FeezBack holds a Bank of Israel financial information service provider (AIS) license and a payment initiation (PIS) approval, and is ISO 27001 certified for information security. The company describes an API-based integration model for partners but publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or SDKs at this time.

providers.name: Fidocure
providers.description: FidoCure is a translational precision-medicine service for canine cancer, developed by One Health Company and backed by a16z. It combines next-generation genomic sequencing of a dog's tumor at a CLIA-certified (human-grade) lab with tumor profiling and an AI-driven data platform to identify cancer-driving mutations, then recommends personalized targeted therapeutics that veterinarians can prescribe. FidoCure has guided treatment for thousands of dogs across roughly 1,350 clinics and maintains the largest proprietary canine cancer dataset, underpinning peer-reviewed research with Stanford, the Broad Institute, Tufts, and the University of Georgia. FidoCure operates as a veterinarian-facing clinical service rather than a public developer API; this profile captures its public identity, portal, and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Firsthand
providers.description: Firsthand provides an AI‑powered Brand Agent platform that enables marketers and publishers to deliver personalized, real‑time brand experiences across web, paid media, and other consumer touchpoints. The platform combines Lakebed™ data‑rights management with custom brand agents to dynamically share expertise while protecting content. Backed by Radical Ventures, Firsthand helps brands build direct, trusted relationships with consumers through intelligent, context‑aware interactions.

providers.name: Five Lives
providers.description: Five Lives is a health-technology company building evidence-based digital tools for dementia prevention and brain health for adults aged 50 and over. Founded by former Peak brain-training leaders Xavier Louis (CEO) and Sylvain Piquet (COO), the fully remote company operates two consumer mobile apps: Five Lives Brain Health, a prevention app available since 2021 with cognitive tests, brain games, and lifestyle tracking across five pillars (nutrition, sleep, physical activity, mood and social connection, and mental stimulation); and Five Lives Care, an evidence-based memory and autonomy programme for people aged 60+ launched in January 2026 and developed with leading memory centres in the UK and France. Its work draws on the FINGER study and the Lancet Commission's modifiable dementia risk factors, with research partners including the University of Oxford, Trinity College Dublin, the FINGER Brain Health Institute, Dementias Platform UK, and the Gerontopole d'Ile de France. Backed by Speedinvest. Five Lives does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Fortinet
providers.description: Fortinet is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Fortinet API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: Foundation
providers.description: Foundation Software provides construction accounting software designed for contractors, offering job costing, payroll, invoicing, vendor payments, and financial reporting in a unified cloud-based system. The platform enables real-time visibility into project expenses, streamlines payroll processing, and supports CPA tools, helping construction businesses manage finances from anywhere.

providers.name: GetApp
providers.description: GetApp is a free online resource that helps small businesses find, compare, and choose the best business software for their needs across hundreds of categories.

providers.name: Harbor Global
providers.description: Harbor Global is a global professional-services firm delivering technology, operations, strategy, and intelligence consulting to law firms, corporate legal departments, and government legal teams. Its practice areas span legal-technology and operations (application management, process automation, AI enablement), strategic advisory, intelligence and research/library services, and vendor governance, delivered by a global team of specialists. Harbor has grown through acquisitions such as iTrain (UK legal-technology training and AI enablement) and CE Global Partners (HCM/HR and payroll transformation). It is a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners. Harbor Global is a services company and does not publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for company identity and discovery.

providers.name: Housewhisper
providers.description: HouseWhisper (legal name Real Estate Productivity, Inc.) is a Seattle-based AI platform for real estate teams and brokerages, founded by former Zillow executives. It acts as a 24/7 AI teammate that automates the full lead lifecycle through personalized voice and text conversations: a Lead Engine that re-engages and revives cold database contacts, a Rules Engine that routes leads to the right agent with fallback escalations, and an AI Teammate that handles CRM updates, follow-ups, scheduling, reminders, and administrative busywork by call or text. It connects to real estate CRM, dialer, and calendar systems via API keys with no data migration, integrating with Follow Up Boss, Sierra Interactive, kvCORE, MoxiWorks, Salesforce, Lofty, HubSpot, and others. Pricing is outcome-based (a small monthly platform fee plus referral fees on closed deals). HouseWhisper has raised roughly $10M in seed funding led by Mayfield. The company does not currently publish a public developer API, documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: IgGenix
providers.description: IgGenix, Inc. is a clinical-stage antibody discovery and development company in South San Francisco, California, founded in 2019 on work from Stephen Quake's laboratory at Stanford in collaboration with allergy clinician-researcher Kari Nadeau. Its SEQ SIFTER platform uses single-cell RNA sequencing to capture the rare IgE-producing B cells circulating in allergic patients' blood, then re-engineers those sequences into fully human, high-affinity, allergen-specific IgG antibodies designed to block the allergic cascade before it starts. Lead program IGNX001 is a human IgG4 monoclonal antibody for peanut allergy, in the Phase 1 ACCELERATE Peanut trial, with discovery programs against alpha-gal syndrome, nsLTP allergens and atopic dermatitis autoantigens. The company has raised roughly $75M across seed, Series A and a $40M Series B. IgGenix publishes no product or developer API and no developer program; the only machine-readable surface on iggenix.com is the WordPress REST API (wp/v2) served at https://iggenix.com/wp-json/, which returns the company's press releases, peer-reviewed publications, conference abstracts, careers post type, pages, media library, taxonomies and site search as anonymous JSON. The OpenAPI definitions in this repository were derived mechanically from that route index; IgGenix publishes none of its own.

providers.name: Incluyeme
providers.description: Incluyeme.com is a Latin American social enterprise, founded in 2013 by Gabriel Marcolongo, working toward the social and labor inclusion of people with disabilities.
