Its open-source World Engine is a Python inference library that loads Waypoint world models and LoRA adapters from HuggingFace to generate playable, promptable worlds locally or in the browser. Founded by Louis Castricato (CEO) and Shahbuland Matiana (Head of Mathematical Research), both formerly of CarperAI and Stability AI, the team operates openly and publishes its infrastructure as public open-source repositories. Overworld does not currently expose a hosted REST API; its primary developer artifact is the first-party world_engine Python SDK.

providers.name: Parasoft
providers.description: Parasoft provides automated software testing solutions that help development teams improve code quality, accelerate release cycles, and ensure compliance with industry standards. Their portfolio includes tools for static code analysis, unit testing, API testing, and runtime error detection across a wide range of programming languages and platforms. Parasoft serves industries such as aerospace, automotive, finance, and healthcare, offering both on-premises and cloud-based solutions to meet diverse testing needs.

providers.name: persimmonhq-com
providers.description: Persimmon provides a brand‑intelligence MCP (Machine‑Consumable Product) for AI agents, delivering deterministic momentum indexes, strategic reads, and evidence‑backed competitive context. Users can query brand signals, receive structured strategic arguments, and access a public MCP registry. The platform offers free early‑access reads and paid tiers for strategists and teams, emphasizing data‑driven, auditable insights without fabricating scores.

providers.name: Pillar
providers.description: Pillar is an Italian construction-technology company, founded in 2025 and headquartered in Milan, building what it calls the operating system for the construction industry (il sistema operativo per l'edilizia). Its cloud platform unifies the back office of building firms (imprese edili) — invoicing (fatturazione), cash-flow management (flussi di cassa), bank reconciliation, quotes and estimates (preventivi), procurement, job and project cost control (gestione commessa), and delivery notes and site work reports (DDT e rapportini) — alongside on-site safety (Pillar Sicurezza) and an AI layer (Pillar AI) that automates data entry in real time, including inputs captured from the job site over WhatsApp. Pillar is backed by Earlybird Venture Capital and today reaches customers through a book-a-demo model rather than a public self-serve signup or a developer-facing API; no public API, SDK, or developer documentation surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Playbite
providers.description: Playbite is a free mobile arcade app - "an arcade in your pocket" - built by Digital Media Technology SL and backed by 500 Global. The app offers an ever-expanding library of simple, casual games spanning multiplayer, rhythm, puzzle, matching, relaxing, and racing categories, with over 500,000 players who play games and earn rewards. The service is free to users and monetized through non-intrusive advertising. Playbite is a consumer-facing mobile gaming product distributed through the Apple App Store and Google Play; it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal, so this profile captures its company identity, public web properties, and domain security posture rather than an API surface.

providers.name: Please
providers.description: Please (Please Platforms) is an AI-powered "thinking" reminders application for iOS that lets people capture a thought, a link, or an image with zero effort, then automatically enriches each reminder with additional context and surfaces intelligent, connected suggestions so nothing gets missed. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of General Catalyst and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead. Please ships a consumer mobile product and publishes no public developer platform, API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Prixtel
providers.description: Prixtel is a French mobile virtual network operator (MVNO) founded in 2004 by David Charles and headquartered in Aix-en-Provence. It is known for "forfaits flexibles" — mobile plans whose monthly price moves automatically between published tiers according to the data a subscriber actually consumed, with the ceiling known in advance — and it rides the SFR (historically also Orange) radio network rather than owning spectrum. Prixtel serves roughly 300,000 to 500,000 subscribers, reported about EUR 63.5M revenue in 2024, and was acquired by Altice France, the owner of SFR, in June 2021 for approximately EUR 415M while continuing to trade under its own brand; the Serena venture attribution that surfaced this profile is therefore a realized exit rather than a current holding. Prixtel publishes no public API, no developer portal, no SDK, no webhook catalog, and no machine-readable contract of any kind. Its only first-party software distribution is an end-user iOS/Android app for consumption tracking, invoices and line management; api.prixtel.com is that app's private backend and returns HTTP 404 on every probed path, including its own root.

providers.name: Qanoniah
providers.description: Adalah for IT Systems LLC operates Qanoniah, a Saudi Arabian legal technology platform that enables companies to access, understand, and act on the latest and most accurate legal information and procedures in seconds. The AI-driven service targets legal and compliance teams across Saudi Arabia. Backed by 500 Global, the company is tracked in the API Evangelist network; no public API or developer surface has been discovered to date.

providers.name: QiDZ Holding
providers.description: QiDZ Holding operates theQapp (formerly QiDZ), a consumer mobile platform that helps families discover, compare, and book activities, entertainment, and dining experiences across the United Arab Emirates and the wider Middle East (Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Riyadh, Jeddah, Eastern Province, Manama, and Cairo). The app curates theme parks, water parks, indoor play areas, sports and creative classes, kid-friendly restaurants, camps, staycations, museums, and birthday and event packages, and offers a Q-Club membership with exclusive promo codes and discounts. Backed by 500 Global, QiDZ is a B2C mobile experience distributed through the Apple App Store and Google Play; it exposes no public developer API, developer portal, or machine specification, so this profile captures its identity and a domain-security probe rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: ReelData AI
providers.description: ReelData AI builds artificial intelligence software for land-based aquaculture, helping recirculating aquaculture system (RAS) fish farms maximize growth, minimize costs, and reduce risk across smolt, post-smolt, and on-growing production. Its integrated AI suite includes AI Smart Feeding (ReelAppetite), which monitors real-time population appetite to optimize feed and cut waste; AI Biomass Monitoring (ReelWeight), a non-intrusive biomass estimation tool returning results within hours; and AI Cameras (ReelVision), dual-function cameras for fish-behavior monitoring, feed counting, and standard IP camera use. Additional tools cover stress monitoring (ReelStress) and early disease detection (ReelHealth). ReelData is a Techstars portfolio company serving major operators including Samherji, Atlantic Sapphire, Kingfish Company, and Salmon Evolution. As of this enrichment pass the company exposes no public developer portal, API, or SDK surface; its products are delivered as on-site AI hardware and software rather than a self-serve API.

providers.name: Refyne
providers.description: Refyne is an Indian financial wellness platform and the country's first earned wage access (EWA) provider, letting employees draw a portion of their already-earned salary before payday at 0% interest through their employer's payroll. Founded in 2020 and backed by QED Investors, Refyne serves 500+ organizations across 23 industries and more than 8 million employees, and operates additional products including RuPay credit cards, the MoneyGuru financial-literacy service, and an employee privilege/discount club. The company operates under RBI compliance and holds ISO 27001 and SOC 2 certifications. Refyne is primarily a B2B2C mobile and payroll-integrated platform and does not publish a public developer portal or API at this time; this profile captures its public identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Res
providers.description: Res (ResQ) is an AI-powered operations platform for the service economy, connecting restaurants, hospitality groups, and facilities-management teams with vetted trades vendors to manage repair-and-maintenance work orders end to end. The platform covers work-order intake and dispatch, vendor sourcing and communication, invoicing and payments, and reporting across trades such as HVAC, plumbing, refrigeration, and electrical. Backed by Homebrew and surfaced through the API Evangelist network, ResQ operates a web and mobile SaaS product; it publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI definitions, SDKs, or webhook surface at this time, so this profile captures company identity, website properties, and probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: ScaleFlux
providers.description: ScaleFlux is a semiconductor and systems company, founded in 2014 and headquartered in Milpitas / San Jose, California, that designs enterprise NVMe SSD controllers, computational storage drives and CXL memory products. Its FX-series SoC controllers (SFX 3016, FX 5016) embed transparent hardware compression, so drives such as the CSD 2000, CSD 3000 and CSD 5000 series present substantially more logical than physical capacity while offloading compression and data-shaping work from the host CPU. The company also ships non-compressing NSD drives and CXL memory expansion silicon aimed at AI, cloud and database infrastructure. ScaleFlux is a hardware vendor rather than a web-API provider: it publishes no public REST, GraphQL or webhook API. Its programmable surface is the NVMe standard command set plus the vendor-specific "sfx" extensions shipped as an upstream plugin in linux-nvme/nvme-cli (sfx-nvme), together with kernel driver and utility packages distributed through packagecloud.io.

providers.name: Scoutbee
providers.description: Scoutbee is an AI-powered supplier discovery and procurement intelligence platform that helps enterprise buyers instantly find, vet, and connect with trusted suppliers. Founded in 2015 in Berlin, Germany, Scoutbee uses large language models, knowledge-graph technology, and a global supplier network to power supplier discovery, sourcing project execution (Streamline), and a centralized supplier data foundation (DeepSee), surfaced through the Scoutbee Intelligence Platform. Its AI gives procurement, sourcing, and category-management teams recommendations for suppliers matched on qualifications, risk, certifications, sustainability, diversity, cost, and experience. Scoutbee integrates with SAP Ariba guided sourcing and, following its October 2025 acquisition by Coupa, is being embedded into the Coupa Supplier Portal. Scoutbee does not currently publish a public developer API or documentation portal; this profile captures its public identity and web surface.

providers.name: Shakers
providers.description: Shakers is a Spanish technology platform — "the house of freeworking" — that connects enterprises with vetted, top-tier freelance developers and digital professionals. Its AI-powered products include Shakers AI (a copilot for project scoping and talent matching), Talent Insight (profile and skills analysis), Shakers Verified (technical verification of freelance profiles), and AI Interviews (automated candidate assessment). The platform serves 450+ enterprise clients including Telefónica, EY, BBVA, Microsoft, and HP across a community of 10,000+ tech freelancers. Backed by Partech, Shakers was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company profile; as of this enrichment pass it publishes a consumer web platform but no public developer or API surface.

providers.name: Shiftboard
providers.description: Shiftboard provides workforce management and scheduling solutions, now part of UKG. Their customers are listed on the UKG site, indicating integration into a broader human capital management platform. Shiftboard’s technology helps organizations manage employee shifts, compliance, and labor costs, leveraging AI-driven scheduling and analytics.

providers.name: Sighten
providers.description: Sighten was a San Francisco software company, backed by Obvious Ventures, that built a cloud platform for the residential and commercial solar industry — covering system design, proposal generation, sales, and financing workflows used by solar installers, dealers, and finance providers. The Sighten business was acquired (by GoodLeap) and folded into EverBright; the original sighten.io domain now redirects to goeverbright.com. EverBright operates as a residential solar and home-battery financing platform, connecting homeowners with local installers through lease and Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) products and the MyEverBright monitoring portal. No public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation is published for the Sighten or EverBright brand; a partner-facing platform (engine.goeverbright.com) and a protected API host (api.goeverbright.com, HTTP 401) exist but are not publicly documented. This profile records the company's current, honest public surface after enrichment.

providers.name: Sketchdeck.ai
providers.description: SketchDeck.ai is a B2B SaaS company whose flagship product, LIFT, is AI-powered material takeoff and counting software for the structural steel fabrication and erection industry. LIFT analyzes uploaded blueprints and shop drawings to automatically extract quantities and generate Bills of Materials, with claimed 95-99% accuracy and up to an 80% reduction in takeoff time so estimators can complete bids in minutes rather than hours or days. The platform adds revision management and exports data to industry estimating programs; the company reports more than $25 billion in projects bid through LIFT to date. SketchDeck.ai is a Techstars-backed startup. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a marketing and demo-request website only - there is no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable specification surface to catalog.

providers.name: Skillshare
providers.description: Skillshare is a New York City–based online learning community for creators, founded in 2010 by Michael Karnjanaprakorn and Malcolm Ong. The platform hosts thousands of on-demand video classes across creative disciplines — illustration, design, photography, animation, lettering, film, productivity, writing, and business — taught by working creators and industry professionals. Skillshare operates on a paid subscription model (Premium membership) that grants members unlimited access to the class catalog, project-based learning, and a discussion community where students submit class projects for feedback. The company has a teacher revenue-share program in which class creators are paid based on watch time and student enrollments, and runs Skillshare for Teams as a B2B offering for organizations to give employees access to the catalog. Skillshare does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, partner API, or SDK. The platform's programmatic surface is limited to internal web/mobile clients and an affiliate/marketing referral program; there is no documented developer portal, public webhook system, or third-party integration API for the Skillshare catalog, enrollments, watch-time, or teacher-payout data.

providers.name: SuppCo
providers.description: SuppCo is a consumer supplement tracking and optimization platform, describing itself as the world's first real supplement tracker and optimizer. Its iOS and Android app lets people log their supplement stack and get a personalized StackScore across quality, dosing, goal coverage, and nutrient levels, plus a TrustScore that rates products on 29 attributes. It is backed by a database of 160,000+ products, 20,000+ research studies, and 80+ expert protocols from functional-medicine practitioners. SuppCo is in open beta (free, with an optional Pro tier) and was acquired by Function Health. No public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal is currently published; this profile captures its public web, security, and legal surface. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Union Square Ventures.

providers.name: Tabz
providers.description: Tabz is a pharmacy commerce platform that provides payments, checkout, and invoicing solutions for manufacturers, mail‑order, compounding, specialty, and retail pharmacies. It enables seamless patient payment collection, integrates with pharmacy management systems, and offers APIs for building custom commerce experiences. Tabz aims to simplify the complex pharmacy payment ecosystem, supporting high‑cost medication workflows and improving checkout efficiency across the industry.

providers.name: Tailorbird
providers.description: Tailorbird is a CapEx orchestration platform for the multifamily real estate industry, replacing spreadsheet-based capital planning with AI-generated property intelligence. The platform produces unit-level as-builts, takeoffs, and interior models, runs renovation ROI and five-year capital plans, and tracks spend and budget variance in real time across apartment portfolios. Tailorbird ingests PCAs and property documents, integrates with major property-management ERPs including Yardi, RealPage, Entrata, and MRI via custom APIs and ELTs, and maintains SOC 2 Type II compliance. Founded in 2020 and based in Princeton, New Jersey, it serves 28 of the NMHC Top 50 operators and manages more than $2B in annual CapEx across over one million mapped units. It is a Bloomberg Beta portfolio company.

providers.name: Te Pari
providers.description: Te Pari designs and manufactures world‑leading livestock handling equipment in Oamaru, New Zealand. Their product range includes cattle yards, crushes, sheep handling systems, dosing guns, EID readers and weighing platforms, offering integrated solutions that improve safety, efficiency and profitability for farms. With over four decades of experience, Te Pari combines robust hot‑dip galvanised steel construction with modern technology to deliver durable, reliable equipment for the global agricultural sector.

providers.name: Teespring
providers.description: Teespring is a creator-commerce and print-on-demand platform, founded in 2011, that lets creators design, launch, and sell custom apparel and merchandise with no upfront cost or inventory, handling production, payment, and fulfillment on the creator's behalf. Backed by a16z, the company rebranded to "Spring" in 2021 and now operates as Amaze Commerce (part of Amaze Holdings): its consumer storefront lives at spri.ng while the creator/merchant SaaS platform runs at amazecommerce.com and amaze.co. As of this enrichment pass the company exposes no public developer API, developer portal, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, /.well-known discovery surface, or llms.txt; this profile therefore captures verified company identity and published site properties only.

providers.name: Tenkara
providers.description: Tenkara is an AI-powered operations and supply chain platform for material manufacturers across food, supplements, cosmetics, chemicals, beverages, and OTC products. The platform automates 75+ workflows spanning supplier sourcing and qualification, procurement, freight and logistics booking, order tracking, and compliance documentation (COA, SDS, and audit records), helping manufacturers find better suppliers faster, prevent delays, and run more efficient operations. Tenkara is backed by True Ventures.

providers.name: Terra
providers.description: Terra Security operates an agentic-AI-powered continuous offensive security (penetration testing) platform. Founded in 2024 and based in Tel Aviv, Terra runs a swarm of AI agents with a human-on-the-loop workflow that continuously validates every attack surface — web and internal applications, external and internal networks, and AI systems such as LLMs, copilots, MCP servers, and autonomous agents (AI red teaming). The platform compresses multi-week legacy pentests into hours, produces verified (low-noise) findings, and generates audit-ready evidence for SOC 2, ISO 27001, and HIPAA programs. Terra raised a $30M Series A led by Felicis in 2025. Terra publishes no public developer API; this profile captures the company's public web surface and security posture.

providers.name: TOCA Football
providers.description: TOCA Football, Inc. is a technology-enabled soccer experience and entertainment company headquartered in Costa Mesa, California, founded on the training methodology of former US international and Premier League player Eddie Lewis. It operates two businesses: TOCA Soccer, a network of indoor soccer training centers across the United States, Canada and Mexico offering private training, classes, clinics, camps, youth and adult leagues, tournaments and pickup play; and TOCA Social, a soccer-themed dining and entertainment venue brand. Its training centers pair a proprietary ball-delivery machine and digitalized smart targets with the MyTOCA player app, which tracks session performance, player cards, leaderboards and progress. TOCA is the official soccer training partner of Major League Soccer. TOCA publishes no public API, SDK, webhook or developer program: its software ships only as end-user consumer apps and in-venue systems.

providers.name: Tourlane
providers.description: Tourlane (Tourlane GmbH) is a travel planning company that creates personalized, custom multi-day trip packages. Travelers are paired with English-speaking, native-European destination travel experts for one-on-one consultations, free initial trip planning, complete booking management, and dedicated support throughout their trip, across destinations such as Italy, Greece, Ireland, Spain, Scotland, and France. Tourlane is a portfolio company of HV Capital. Sector: consumer travel. Tourlane publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal.

providers.name: TrackMan
providers.description: TrackMan A/S is a Danish sports-technology company (headquartered in Vedbaek, Denmark) that builds Doppler radar and optically tracked launch monitors, simulator software, and data platforms for golf, baseball, football, and US football. Its hardware lineage includes the TrackMan 4 outdoor/indoor launch monitor, TrackMan iO indoor launch monitor, the V3 stadium ball-tracking system used by every Major League Baseball club, and the portable B1 baseball launch monitor. On the software side TrackMan operates TrackMan Range (a connected driving-range platform), Virtual Golf 3 (the simulator rendering and gameplay engine), the TrackMan Golf App for performance and social play, TrackMan 360 for golf-club business operations, and a cloud data platform that aggregates measurements across products. TrackMan exposes several developer-facing surfaces — a TrackMan Cloud GraphQL API at api.golf.trackman.com/graphql for tournaments and facility data, the TrackMan Range REST API at docs.trackmanrange.com for range/bay/session integration, a device-local TM4 WebSocket protocol for receiving live shot measurements over LAN/UPnP from a TrackMan 4 unit, and the TrackMan Baseball Data API (Swagger-documented, OAuth-client + username/password) for ingesting V3 stadium and B1 portable measurements and media. The TrackMan public GitHub organization hosts internal Unity tooling rather than client SDKs, and most developer access is partner-gated through TrackMan Sports Solutions or the Golf B2B program. The commercial model is hardware sales plus tiered software subscriptions (TrackMan Range, TrackMan 360, V3 Cloud) sold direct to teams, leagues, ranges, and consumers.

providers.name: Verusen
providers.description: Verusen provides an AI‑powered MRO inventory optimization platform that helps manufacturers overcome data challenges to make better maintenance, repair, and operations decisions. Their solution offers tools such as ROI calculators, whitepapers, and a blog to educate users on spare‑part criticality, SLOB management, and inventory best practices.

providers.name: Vetted
providers.description: Vetted (formerly Lustre) is a San Francisco based AI-powered shopping research assistant that helps consumers find the best products and lowest prices. The service analyzes reviews and recommendations from trusted sources such as Reddit, YouTube, user reviews, and expert articles to surface the most recommended brands and products for a shopper's needs, then compares retailers to identify the best available price. Vetted is delivered as consumer iOS and Android mobile apps and a web experience, and is backed by Index Ventures. It exposes no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal at this time (api.vetted.ai serves the mobile apps as a private backend). This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub.

providers.name: Vistra
providers.description: Vistra Corp (NYSE: VST) is an Irving, Texas integrated retail electricity and power generation company and the largest competitive power generator in the United States, operating roughly 41,000-44,000 MW of natural gas, nuclear, coal, solar and battery storage capacity alongside a retail business serving nearly 5 million residential, commercial and industrial customers across 16 states and the District of Columbia through TXU Energy, Dynegy, Ambit Energy, Energy Harbor, Homefield Energy and U.S. Gas & Electric. Its home market is the United States, where it sits on both sides of the competitive value chain, a merchant generator selling into ERCOT, PJM, ISO-NE, NYISO, MISO and CAISO, and a retail electricity provider (REP) reselling that power to end customers. Its API posture is honestly none. No developer portal, no API subdomain and no machine-readable contract of any kind was found: developer., developers., docs., api. and data. on vistracorp.com do not resolve; /developers, /api, /docs, /data, /openapi.json, /swagger.json and /.well-known/openid-configuration all return 404; and TXU Energy's 758-URL sitemap contains no developer or API page. The United States has no consumer energy data mandate. Green Button is an NAESB/NIST ESPI standard adopted voluntarily, and TXU Energy appears on the US Department of Energy's list of "Utilities Committed to Implementing Green Button", a 2012-era commitment list and not evidence of a live endpoint. The only customer-data surface found is Download-My-Data-style export behind the TXU Energy MyAccount login, whose interval readings are themselves sourced from Smart Meter Texas, the shared ERCOT meter-data platform operated by the transmission and distribution utilities (Oncor, CenterPoint, AEP Texas, TNMP) rather than by Vistra. Because Vistra is a retailer and generator and not a wires company, the third-party interval-data API in its home Texas market belongs to Smart Meter Texas and not to Vistra. Vistra likewise publishes no open market or grid data of its own; ERCOT, the other ISOs/RTOs and the EIA publish the market data about Vistra's fleet. Both sides are therefore closed at the company boundary. Not to be confused with Vistra Limited (vistra.com), the unrelated corporate-services and fund-administration firm that does run a real API developer portal at devportal.vistra.com.

providers.name: Webersheim
providers.description: Webersheim is a German digital agency behind the alcometer.de project, offering a free, open-source blood‑alcohol calculator (Promillerechner) for the public and as a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for AI assistants. The service estimates blood‑alcohol concentration using Widmark’s formula, provides German drink‑driving limits, and includes tools for conversion and limits lookup, all without registration or authentication.

providers.name: 6Estates
providers.description: 6Estates provides enterprise AI solutions, offering a suite of agentic AI applications such as Document Agent, Lending Agent, and Financial Statement Agent. Their platform includes a token‑metered LLM inference service, a model hub, and tools for end‑to‑end workflow automation for lenders. Based in Southeast Asia, 6Estates delivers full‑stack AI from model deployment to decision making, targeting industries like finance, insurance, and enterprise analytics.

providers.name: Academia
providers.description: Academia (Academia.edu, Academia Inc.) is a San Francisco based platform for sharing and discovering academic research, founded in 2008 by Richard Price. Registered researchers upload papers, build public profiles, follow research interests and track readership analytics across a corpus of tens of millions of documents, and the company also runs the Academia journals program and sells Academia Premium subscriptions for advanced search, mentions, reader analytics and bulk PDF downloads. Academia publishes no public developer program, API reference or machine-readable specification; the /v0 JSON endpoints its own web client calls are explicitly disallowed to crawlers in robots.txt. It does publish an RFC 9116 security.txt with a named security contact and a disclosure posture, and a long per-crawler robots.txt that names AI and agent user-agents individually.

providers.name: Adagio Medical
providers.description: Adagio Medical, Inc. is a Laguna Hills, California medical device company and an operating subsidiary of Adagio Medical Holdings, Inc. (NASDAQ: ADGM). It develops catheter-based cardiac ablation systems built on its proprietary Ultra-Low Temperature Cryoablation (ULTC) platform and an emerging Pulsed Field Cryoablation (PFCA) platform, designed to create large, durable, transmural lesions for the treatment of ventricular tachycardia, atrial fibrillation and atrial flutter. Its CE-marked vCLAS Cryoablation System holds FDA Breakthrough Device Designation and is under U.S. evaluation in the FULCRUM-VT pivotal IDE study. Adagio Medical sells regulated physical devices to hospitals and electrophysiology labs; it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable contract. It does publish a coordinated product-security vulnerability disclosure policy.

providers.name: Alix
providers.description: Alix is an estate settlement service that pairs technology with human experts — Settlement Specialists, fiduciaries, CPAs, and probate attorneys — to execute the 150+ administrative, legal, financial, and tax tasks required to settle an estate after a death. It coordinates probate court filings, asset discovery (50-state unclaimed-property and federal life-insurance searches, hidden 401(k)s and bank accounts), estate bank-account and IRS EIN setup, creditor and debt negotiation, final personal (1040) and estate (1041) tax filings, property liquidation and estate sales, and the legally compliant distribution of funds to beneficiaries — while keeping the executor informed through a dedicated app. Alix charges a flat 1% of gross estate value (minimum $9,000, $2,500 initial deposit). Backed by Initialized Capital.

providers.name: Ambi Robotics
providers.description: Ambi Robotics is a Berkeley, California AI robotics company building parcel-sortation and induction robots for ecommerce, postal, and logistics workflows. Founded in 2018 as Ambidextrous Laboratories — a spin-out of UC Berkeley's Dex-Net Project led by Ken Goldberg — by Jeff Mahler (CTO), Stephen McKinley, David Gealy, and Matt Matl, with Jim Liefer (ex-Walmart, ex-UPS) as CEO. Its flagship products are AmbiSort A-Series (sort-to-sack small parcel sorting), AmbiSort B-Series (sort-to-gaylord parcel induction for middle-mile and reverse logistics), AmbiStack (mixed-case stacking for inbound and outbound), and AmbiVision (3D dimensioning, OCR, defect detection, and visual quality inspection). All robots run AmbiOS, the company's cloud-native "operating system for physical intelligence," comprising the AI Skill Suite (Sort, Stack, Kit, Pack, Induct apps), the PRIME-1 foundation model trained on millions of real-world operations, AmbiVision perception, AmbiAccess fleet management dashboard with heat maps and remote support, and a Sim2Real training pipeline that compresses model training by up to 10,000x. Ambi Robotics' primary commercial deployment is a $23 million expansion with Pitney Bowes, with AmbiSort A-Series and B-Series systems deployed across Pitney Bowes ecommerce hubs in the US (including the Stockton, CA hub that nearly doubled local-direct-delivery throughput in the 2021 peak holiday season, and middle-mile B-Series systems that sorted more than 3 million parcels within four months of deployment). Ambi Robotics does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or open-source release for AmbiOS, AmbiSort, AmbiStack, or PRIME-1; integration with customer WMS/WES systems is performed by Ambi's solutions team. The company's public GitHub org primarily contains forks of infrastructure tooling (Ray, trimesh, FCL, EIPScanner, tinygltf, rapier, jszmq, CVXPYgen, mongoose-delete) and internal CI/CD workflow utilities — no published API spec, SDK package, or developer documentation.

providers.name: America First Credit Union
providers.description: America First Credit Union is a federally chartered, NCUA-insured credit union headquartered in Riverdale, Utah, founded in 1939. With roughly $19 billion in assets, more than one million members, and about 124 branches across seven western states (Utah, Idaho, Oregon, New Mexico, Arizona, Nevada, and California), it is one of the largest credit unions in the United States. Like the vast majority of US credit unions, America First operates no public first-party developer portal and publishes no downloadable OpenAPI/Swagger specifications. It provides no self-serve, publicly documented API surface; consumer-permissioned account data access is handled through third-party data aggregators and its core banking provider rather than a direct first-party API. No public FDX participation or CFPB Section 1033 data-access posture is documented on its public website as of this bootstrap. This record is an honest identity profile with no fabricated API surface.

providers.name: Annex Cloud
providers.description: Annex Cloud is an enterprise loyalty and customer retention platform. Its Loyalty Experience Platform is built on a set of RESTful APIs that let brands enroll and manage loyalty members, issue and redeem points, track member activity and transactions, run referral (Refer A Friend) programs, and wire loyalty into commerce and marketing stacks. The APIs are documented publicly on a Redocly developer portal, but access is gated - credentials are provisioned per customer and the base host is tenant-specific. Authentication is JWT-based, created through the Tenant API, and prospective users are directed to "Contact your Customer Success Manager for assistance with API Connectors." No public self-serve signup, sandbox, or published pricing is offered; this is an enterprise, partner/customer-gated API.

providers.name: API Stack
providers.description: API Stack is a free, public directory and discovery platform for third-party API tooling, built and operated by Apideck B.V. as a tenant of its own Apideck Ecosystem marketplace platform. It catalogs 213 API tools and services across 46 published category pages spanning the whole API lifecycle: gateways, management, design, authentication, developer portals, documentation, specifications, testing, mocking, security, monitoring, analytics, billing, frameworks, linters and directories, with per-tool listing pages carrying descriptions, screenshots and outbound links so developers can shortlist and compare tooling. API Stack is a discovery surface rather than an API product: it publishes no developer portal, API reference, machine-readable contract, SDK, pricing page or terms of service of its own, and sits alongside Apideck's API Tracker, Open Banking Tracker and SaaS Blocks properties.

providers.name: Apna
providers.description: Apna is India's leading professional networking and job-search platform, headquartered in Mumbai, India. Job seekers use Apna to search and apply to jobs online for free, join profession and location-based community groups, build a professional profile, and prepare for interviews, while employers post job vacancies and hire quality candidates in as little as 48 hours. Apna is a portfolio company of Insight Partners. At the time of this profile Apna does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation; this entry captures its public identity and web properties.

providers.name: Applied Ev
providers.description: Applied EV is a Melbourne‑based mobility technology company developing autonomous electric freight and industrial vehicles. It offers a software‑defined platform with a proprietary Digital Backbone control system, enabling scalable autonomy for logistics, warehouse, and factory transport. The company provides hardware such as the Blanc Robot cabin‑less vehicle and a suite of power and control products, and partners with firms like Siemens, NXP, and Oxbotica to deliver end‑to‑end autonomous solutions.

providers.name: AppScreenStudio
providers.description: AppScreenStudio provides a free online App Store and Google Play screenshot generator for iOS and Android developers. Users can upload raw app captures, customize templates, and export store‑ready screenshots in all required sizes with a single click. The platform integrates AI agents like Claude, Code, and Gemini to assist design, and offers a large library of free and premium templates, serving over 9,400 developers and ASO specialists. It aims to simplify app store listing creation without needing design tools.

providers.name: Ara
providers.description: Ara (Ara Labs, Inc.) is a digital out-of-home (DOOH) advertising network that finances, installs, and operates rich-media displays across mobility, municipal, parking, and retail settings. It describes itself as the largest U.S. owner-operator of rideshare and taxi car-top digital billboards, running a long-term partnership with Uber alongside in-car, storefront, and parking/municipal kiosk screens. Ara owns the hardware and content-management operations under a monthly subscription model so fleet owners, retailers, parking operators and municipalities avoid cap-ex and operational overhead, and it also sells self-serve NYC taxi-top ad time by the hour or day. Its own site names Founders Fund, Coatue, Rosecliff Ventures, iHeart Media and Kellogg's as investors. Ara publishes NO public API, SDK, developer portal, documentation site or machine-readable specification. Contract discovery in August 2026 found a live private backend at api.arascreens.com (Ruby on Rails on Heroku) that answers every route with an HTTP Basic challenge, a React driver/operations application at app.arascreens.com, and a third-party signage CMS front end at cms.arascreens.com — all credentialed product infrastructure, none of it a developer offering. A second pass enumerated the full host inventory and added four more production hosts to the same finding: outdoor.arascreens.com (an SPA product page for the Ara O49 display), rts.arascreens.com (an unauthenticated Express service serving only its scaffold string), stationary.arascreens.com and assets.arascreens.com. Ara's marketing describes its CMS as "API-driven", meaning its own platform is programmatically operated and can integrate with a partner's existing signage stack — it is not an offer of a public API, and no key issuance, reference or access request mechanism exists anywhere on its surface.

providers.name: Arena Club
providers.description: Arena Club is a technology-first trading-card and collectibles platform founded in 2022 by entrepreneur Brian Lee and baseball Hall-of-Famer Derek Jeter, operating as Arenaclub.com, Inc. The company combines AI- and computer-vision-assisted card grading, an insured physical vault with 24/7 surveillance and climate control, a digital "Showroom" where collectors organize vaulted cards into collections, and an online marketplace for buying, selling and trading slabbed sports and trading-card-game cards. Members submit cards for grading and vaulting, browse and transact in the marketplace, open digital packs, and can retrieve physical cards from the vault on demand. Arena Club ships web and native iOS/Android apps but publishes no public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Arva
providers.description: Arva AI provides advanced artificial intelligence solutions for banking decisions, offering research-driven models that automate high‑risk financial processes such as fraud detection, compliance, and lending. Their platform delivers accurate, scalable AI agents that integrate into banking operations, trusted by regulated institutions worldwide. Arva’s technology aims to move critical decisions beyond human‑in‑the‑loop, enhancing efficiency and security across the financial sector.

providers.name: ASRM
providers.description: ASRM (AI Search Rank Monitor) provides AI visibility monitoring, allowing brands to track how often AI engines mention, cite, and recommend them. The service offers free scoring, tiered subscription plans (Solo $39/mo, Agency $149/mo, Agency Pro $349/mo), and a dashboard to improve AI search presence.

providers.name: Asserts.ai
providers.description: Asserts.ai is an observability intelligence platform for Prometheus and OpenTelemetry that automatically models the entities in your infrastructure and application metrics, applies golden-signal and SLO PromQL rules to surface anomalies, and correlates related failures into root-cause workbenches to cut mean-time-to-resolution. It also ships a Data Distiller for reducing metric cardinality and observability cost. Asserts was acquired by Grafana Labs in November 2023 and is now delivered as part of Grafana Cloud; its standalone website, docs, and GitHub organization are archived and no longer maintained.

providers.name: Astera Labs
providers.description: Astera Labs, Inc. (NASDAQ: ALAB) is a semiconductor company building purpose-built connectivity solutions for rack-scale AI and cloud infrastructure. Its Intelligent Connectivity Platform spans the Aries PCIe/CXL Smart DSP Retimers, Smart Cable Modules and Smart Gearboxes, the Taurus Ethernet Smart Retimers and Smart Redrivers, the Leo CXL Smart Memory Controllers, and the Scorpio Smart Fabric Switches, all managed by COSMOS (COnnectivity System Management and Optimization Software). COSMOS is the software layer of the platform: firmware modules on the devices plus platform-level libraries that run on hosts and baseboard management controllers, exposing what Astera Labs describes as a single standardized API for device discovery, configuration, security attestation, firmware update, telemetry, link diagnostics, RAS testing, scripting and fleet management. That API surface is an on-premises host/BMC SDK rather than a public web API: the COSMOS Developer Kit is offered through a "Contact Us" motion and the supporting application notes are released through a document-request form, so no public API reference or machine-readable specification is published.

providers.name: Auxilius
providers.description: Auxilius is R&D finance automation software for biopharmaceutical companies, purpose-built to manage clinical trial finances. The platform automates clinical expense accruals and financial close with built-in audit controls, tracks investigator grant spend by mapping patient-visit data to site contracts, and models and re-forecasts study spend as trial conditions change. It integrates with clinical (Medrio, Veeva), financial (Oracle NetSuite, Workday, SAP, QuickBooks), procurement (Coupa, Bill.com), and planning (Planful, Anaplan) systems, delivering variance analysis, automated reconciliation, and audit-ready role-based approval workflows. Auxilius is SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2 compliant and is used by 100+ biopharma companies. It is backed by Bain Capital Ventures. No public developer API is currently published.

providers.name: Azimuth GRC
providers.description: Azimuth GRC provides automated compliance management software that transforms complex regulatory requirements into clear, actionable guidance. Their platform, VALIDATOR, offers real‑time monitoring, audit automation, and curated legal content to help organizations maintain continuous compliance across industries. With features like ROI calculators, detailed reporting, and integration capabilities, Azimuth GRC serves enterprises seeking to streamline governance, risk, and compliance processes.

providers.name: Beszel
providers.description: Beszel provides a lightweight server monitoring solution that tracks CPU, memory, and network usage for Docker and Podman containers. It offers configurable alerts, multi‑user management with shared systems, OAuth/OIDC authentication, automatic backups to disk or S3‑compatible storage, and a REST API for integration. The software is released under the MIT License.

providers.name: Brandlive
providers.description: Brandlive provides a video streaming platform for businesses, enabling live town halls, video podcasts, on‑demand content, and interactive virtual events. Their solutions include BrandTV®, a streaming service, and Brandlive Studios for high‑production video creation. Serving enterprises such as Nike, Cognizant, Pfizer, and Shopify, Brandlive helps companies inject creativity into internal communications and external audiences, turning ordinary meetings into engaging, broadcast‑quality experiences.

providers.name: Bureau of Engraving and Printing
providers.description: The Bureau of Engraving and Printing (BEP) is an agency of the U.S. Department of the Treasury that designs and produces U.S. currency (Federal Reserve Notes), postage stamps, and other official U.S. government security documents. BEP offers a U.S. Currency Reader Program for the visually impaired and provides a mutilated currency redemption service.

providers.name: Butn
providers.description: Butn is an Australian embedded-finance company that funds business cashflow at the point of transaction, plugging invoice finance, outsourced credit terms, and supplier "pay now, settle later" directly into the platforms its business customers already use. Its funding products — Butn X (invoice finance to draw cash early against receivables), Butn Terms (outsourced buyer credit where Butn carries the risk), and Butn Pay (paying suppliers upfront in exchange for extended repayment) — are designed to be embedded into partner marketplaces, accounting tools, and B2B platforms such as MYOB, Salesforce, and FoodByUs rather than sold as a standalone destination. Butn sits in the spend / accounts payable and accounts receivable financing layer of Australia's payments market, where money movement rides the New Payments Platform and the banks opened by the Consumer Data Right. Its integration and embedding are delivered through private, partner-provisioned APIs: Butn markets "plug and play" embedding for partners but does not operate a public self-serve developer portal, publish downloadable OpenAPI/Swagger definitions, or expose openly documented API reference material as of this profile.

providers.name: BVI Crewed
providers.description: BVI Crewed offers luxury crewed catamaran charters in the British Virgin Islands. Customers can book hand‑picked yachts with professional crews, sailing to Tortola, Virgin Gorda, Jost Van Dyke and the full BVI. The service provides expert concierge matching, seamless booking, and a premium Caribbean sailing experience for leisure travelers seeking effortless island hopping and bespoke itineraries.

providers.name: Cajal Technologies
providers.description: Cajal Technologies (Cajal) is a San Francisco-based Y Combinator (W26) company scaling formal verification to accelerate scientific discovery. Its multi-agent system, Tau, collaborates to discover and verify new mathematical proofs in Lean, deploying AI mathematicians across high-impact applied domains starting with quantum computing and finance. Tau verifies compiled binaries with mathematical certainty down to the machine level. Cajal also partners with frontier AI labs and research institutes to improve their systems through datasets, evals, and RL environments, and open-sources tooling such as Talos, a Wasm interpreter written in Lean designed for reasoning.

providers.name: Cap'n Proto
providers.description: Cap'n Proto is an open-source binary data interchange format and capability-based RPC protocol specification originally created by Kenton Varda. Unlike Protocol Buffers, Cap'n Proto's in-memory representation is identical to its wire format, enabling zero-copy deserialization, incremental reads, random field access, and memory-mapped I/O. The reference implementation is in C++; a broad ecosystem of community-maintained bindings covers C#, Erlang, Go, Haskell, JavaScript/Node, OCaml, Python, Rust, C, D, Java, Lua, Nim, Ruby, and Scala.

providers.name: CarsMultiverse
providers.description: CarsMultiverse is an independent website that archives every version of vehicle recall notices, allowing users to see how safety authorities update information after announcements. It aggregates official recall data, provides searchable archives, and offers tools for tracking changes, without being a government authority. Sources are cited on each page.

providers.name: Casana
providers.description: Casana (Casana Care) is a Rochester, New York digital-health company building passive, in-home remote patient monitoring hardware. Its flagship Smart Seat (formerly the Heart Seat) is a toilet-seat replacement that captures vital signs — heart rate, heart-rate variability, blood-oxygen (SpO2), respiration rate, blood-pressure insights, and sit-to-stand power — during normal bathroom use, with no wearables, no daily charging, and explicitly no camera or microphone. Readings sync to companion iOS, Android, and web apps for patients, families, and caregivers. The company operates in the digital health, remote patient monitoring, and connected medical-device space and is backed by General Catalyst and Kaiser Permanente. As of this profile Casana publishes a consumer product, companion apps, and legal/privacy pages, but no public developer program, API, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Censinet
providers.description: Censinet provides purpose‑built solutions to reduce risk in healthcare organizations. Their platform offers third‑party risk management, enterprise risk oversight, systemic risk remediation, AI governance, and peer benchmarking to help healthcare providers secure data, comply with regulations, and improve cybersecurity maturity across the ecosystem.

providers.name: CertifiKit
providers.description: CertifiKit provides certificate of insurance (COI) tracking software that verifies subcontractor and vendor insurance certificates against user‑defined requirements. It automates collection, validation, and renewal alerts for general liability, workers’ compensation, auto, and umbrella coverage, targeting general contractors and property managers who manage multiple vendors.

providers.name: Corma
providers.description: Corma is a SaaS license and access governance platform for modern IT teams that automates SaaS discovery, access reviews, provisioning, and deprovisioning. Recognized in the 2025 Gartner Magic Quadrant for SaaS Management Platforms, Corma helps organizations centralize all applications in one place, identify shadow IT, and reduce software spend by 10 to 15 percent. Corma offers extensive native integrations with identity providers (Microsoft Entra ID, Okta, Google Workspace), HR platforms (Workday, BambooHR, Personio), financial tools (Spendesk, Qonto, Pennylane, Agicap), and productivity and business tools (Slack, Notion, Salesforce, HubSpot, Zendesk). A public developer API is not currently published.

providers.name: CreditPullEngine
providers.description: CreditPullEngine provides real‑time credit intelligence APIs that aggregate nationwide credit data into clean, actionable insights. Their platform serves fintechs, lenders, and debt‑settlement companies, offering products such as consumer reports, scoring models, and industry‑specific data. The service emphasizes compliance, security, and easy integration via RESTful endpoints, supporting developers with comprehensive documentation and sandbox environments.

providers.name: Dandelion Energy
providers.description: Dandelion Energy is a residential geothermal heating and cooling company that designs, engineers, and installs ground-source heat pump systems for homeowners and new-home builders. Its systems tap the earth's stable subsurface temperature to heat and cool homes year-round, cutting utility bills and carbon emissions versus conventional fossil-fuel HVAC. Dandelion delivers end-to-end service from ground-loop drilling through turnkey installation, and offers a leasing program that removes the upfront cost for buyers. The company reports thousands of installations across the United States. Backed by GV (Google Ventures), it operates in the frontier-tech and climate sector; it currently exposes no public developer API.

providers.name: Daniels AI Design Studio
providers.description: Daniels AI Design Studio is an intelligence design studio founded by Grover Daniels in Stowe, Vermont. It focuses on brand discovery intelligence, helping businesses be found, cited, and chosen. The studio offers AI‑driven design services, strategic branding, and market insight to empower clients in the digital era.

providers.name: DeHaat
providers.description: DeHaat (Green Agrevolution Private Limited) is one of India's largest full-stack agritech platforms, connecting smallholder farmers from "seed to market" through a phygital network of 11,000+ DeHaat Centres and 503 Farmer Producer Organisations across 12+ agrarian states. Founded in 2012 by IIT/IIM alumni, the platform serves 1.8 million+ farmers with agri-inputs (seeds, fertilizers, crop protection), AI-enabled crop advisory in multiple regional languages for 30+ crops, soil analysis, crop-health monitoring, market linkage for harvested produce, and agri-financing. Backed by Prosus Ventures and others, DeHaat operates a franchisee micro-entrepreneur model that raises farmer net incomes 30-50% while making procurement more predictable for buyers. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of prosus-ventures; the company publishes no public developer API portal or OpenAPI at this time, so enrichment is limited to identity, corporate link-properties, and security posture.

providers.name: Delphia
providers.description: Delphia (Delphia Technologies Inc., Toronto, Canada) is an AI-driven quantitative investment firm that puts alternative data to work in systematic trading strategies. Originally a consumer robo-advisor and data-reward token platform backed by a $60M Series A led by Multicoin Capital, Delphia pivoted in 2024 to institutional quant investing with its Oracle Alpha hedge fund and Tilt trend platform. As of this writing Delphia publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures the company identity plus its live security and well-known surfaces.

providers.name: Domo
providers.description: Domo is a cloud-based software company that specializes in providing business intelligence tools for organizations. Their platform allows businesses to gather, analyze, and visualize data from various sources in order to make more informed decisions. Domo helps companies streamline their data management processes and gain valuable insights into their operations, sales, marketing, and overall performance.

providers.name: Domusoinc
providers.description: Domusoinc, operating as Domuso, provides a multifamily rent payment platform that modernizes how property managers collect rent, manage resident payments, and boost cash flow through digital payments, rewards, and portfolio insights. The service offers paperless payments, centralized resident reporting, and analytics to improve collection efficiency and resident loyalty.

providers.name: Earnin
providers.description: Earnin (formerly Activehours) is a consumer financial technology company offering earned wage access (EWA) that lets workers tap the pay they have already earned before their scheduled payday. Its mobile app products include Cash Out (access earned wages up to $150/day and $1,000/pay period with no mandatory fees), Live Pay and the EarnIn Card, Early Pay, Balance Shield overdraft protection, credit monitoring, FDIC-insured Savings Jars, and an EarnIn Payroll offering for businesses. Earnin is a consumer app rather than an API platform; it publishes no public developer portal or API, but does operate a vulnerability-disclosure program (security.txt via Inspectiv) and a trust center. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z, Felicis, Matrix Partners, Ribbit Capital, and Trinity Ventures and profiled in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Enter
providers.description: Enter provides AI-powered agents that automate civil litigation processes for large Brazilian companies, reducing legal costs and improving case outcomes. Their platform reads documents, cross-references external evidence, detects fraud, and generates customized legal defenses, aiming to modernize the traditionally expensive legal workflow in Brazil.

providers.name: EQT
providers.description: EQT Corporation is the largest producer of natural gas in the United States, headquartered in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. It is a vertically integrated Appalachian Basin operator: upstream exploration and production, plus the interstate gathering and transmission pipelines it acquired with Equitrans Midstream in July 2024. EQT pairs production technology with environmental stewardship commitments, including a Scope 1 and Scope 2 net-zero target it reports as met ahead of its 2025 goal. EQT runs no developer program and publishes no API. Its only machine-readable public documents are the OpenID Connect discovery metadata of two Salesforce customer portals — infopost.eqt.com, the FERC-mandated Informational Postings site for its interstate pipelines, and customers.equitransmidstream.com — whose posting data renders client-side and is otherwise gated to registered customers. Not the Swedish firm EQT AB.

providers.name: Fileread
providers.description: Fileread provides an AI‑powered legal data intelligence platform that automates fact‑finding for litigation and investigations. By ingesting the full record of case materials, Fileread reads, analyzes, and cites every answer to its source, enabling lawyers to quickly locate relevant evidence, generate insights, and streamline discovery workflows. Backed by Gradient Ventures, the service combines natural language processing with a searchable knowledge base to improve accuracy and efficiency for legal teams.

providers.name: fizzl-eu
providers.description: Fizzl provides a suite of tools that enable AI agents to make and verify payments autonomously. By checking payments before an agent signs them and after responses, Fizzl ensures safe transactions across multiple payment networks without requiring API keys. The platform offers live services, a wallet, and a marketplace of over 50,000 paid endpoints, supporting AI-driven applications in finance, data retrieval, and more.

providers.name: Foodvisor
providers.description: Foodvisor is a French mobile nutrition platform whose app identifies food items from a photograph using computer vision and returns nutritional information — calories, macronutrients and portion estimates. Between 2023 and 2025 Foodvisor also sold that capability to developers as the Foodvisor Vision API, a commercial image-recognition and nutrition-analysis service documented at vision.foodvisor.io. That developer product has since been withdrawn: the Vision product page now returns HTTP 404, the documentation host no longer resolves in DNS, and the live site carries no API, developer or enterprise content. Foodvisor today publishes no machine-readable contract, no SDK, no MCP server and no /.well-known document, and operates as a consumer subscription app.

providers.name: Forterro
providers.description: Forterro is a pan-European industrial software company, founded in 2012 and headquartered in London, that provides enterprise resource planning (ERP) and specialised business software to the industrial mid-market. Built through a series of acquisitions, Forterro operates a portfolio of regional and vertical ERP brands - including Abas, Jeeves, Garp, Proconcept, Sylob, Silog, Myfactory, Orderwise, Clipper, 123Insight, BPSC, Helios, Proffix, Prodaso and its cloud-native Fortee product - alongside best-in-class point solutions such as warehouse management (WMS), point of sale (POS), material requirements planning (MRP) and business intelligence. The company serves more than 13,000 industrial businesses across manufacturing, warehousing, wholesale and retail from 40+ offices worldwide.

providers.name: grapecity-com-cn
providers.description: GrapeCity (葡萄城) is a professional software development technology and low‑code platform provider with over 40 years of technical accumulation. It focuses on software development technologies, empowering developers with a suite of controls, low‑code solutions, BI tools and services, offering one‑stop solutions that help enterprises improve development efficiency and innovate.

providers.name: Grover
providers.description: Grover is a Berlin-based consumer technology rental and subscription company that lets people rent smartphones, laptops, gaming consoles, cameras, smart home devices, and audio gear on flexible monthly plans ranging from one to twenty-four-plus months. With more than 500,000 active renters across the United States, Germany, Austria, Spain, and the Netherlands, Grover positions flexible tech access as a circular, subscription-based alternative to ownership, refurbishing and recirculating returned devices for resale. Grover is a consumer-facing service and does not currently publish a public developer portal or API; this profile captures its public identity and web properties for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Haven Energy
providers.description: Haven Energy is an Austin, Texas based residential clean-energy company that sells, finances, installs and operates home battery storage and solar systems, and then aggregates those systems into one of the largest virtual power plant (VPP) networks in the United States. Homeowners get an instant online quote, a fixed monthly payment over a ten-year term, end-to-end permitting and certified installation through Haven's Channel Partner network of local electricians, and ongoing remote monitoring. Haven then enrolls the installed batteries into utility and grid programs - California SGIP, PG&E, and Massachusetts ConnectedSolutions among them - so customers can monetize grid participation while utilities and community choice aggregators gain flexible local capacity. Founded in 2022 by Jeff Chapin, Philip Krim and Vinnie Campos, the company raised a $40M Series B in December 2025 led by Giant Ventures. Haven operates as a direct-to-consumer and utility-partner business; it publishes no public developer program, API, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Helm.ai
providers.description: Helm.ai is an AI software company for autonomous driving and robotics, founded in 2016 and headquartered in Redwood City, California. It develops camera-first perception, path prediction and end-to-end autonomy stacks — Helm.ai Vision and Helm.ai Driver — alongside the generative AI development and validation tools VidGen-3, GenSim-3 and WorldGen-1, all trained with its proprietary Deep Teaching unsupervised learning method. The software is licensed to automotive OEMs and Tier 1 suppliers (Honda, Volkswagen, Ambarella, NVIDIA, Qualcomm, Texas Instruments) as embedded, hardware-agnostic components for production vehicle programs rather than as a public developer API. As of 2026-08-22 the company publishes no developer portal, API reference, SDK, or machine-readable specification on any host it controls.

providers.name: Hometap
providers.description: Hometap is a Boston-based fintech founded in 2017 that offers homeowners a home equity investment (HEI) — an alternative to home equity loans and HELOCs. In exchange for a share of a home's future value, homeowners receive cash up front with no monthly payments, no interest, and no income or debt-to-income requirements, settling any time within a 10-year term via sale, refinance, or buyout. Homeowners manage their investment and track equity through the free Hometap Home Equity Dashboard. The company has helped more than 26,000 homeowners and completed over $1 billion in investments, and is backed by investors including General Catalyst. Hometap does not publish a public developer API or developer portal; this profile captures its public web properties and identity for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: IronPlanet
providers.description: IronPlanet is an online marketplace for buying and selling used heavy construction equipment and trucks across categories including construction, trucks, agriculture, mining, forestry, and oil and gas. The platform offers online auctions, buy-now listings, make-an-offer, sealed auctions, and on-site auctions, with detailed third-party inspection reports backed by its IronClad Assurance certification program. IronPlanet operates regional marketplaces for North America, Europe/Middle East, and Asia-Pacific and is part of the Ritchie Bros. (RB Global) family of businesses. This company was surfaced as a portfolio company of accel and kleiner-perkins and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; no public developer API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: JSW One
providers.description: JSW One Platforms is the digital B2B arm of India's JSW Group, operating a full-stack e-commerce and services platform for the country's manufacturing and construction MSMEs. It runs four connected businesses on one technology stack: JSW One Commerce (jswonemsme.com), a multi-brand marketplace for TMT bars, mild/hot-rolled/cold-rolled and structural steel, coated steel, wire rods, cement and bitumen sourced from certified mills; JSW One Homes (jswonehomes.com), a turnkey home-construction service with digital project tracking across fifteen Indian cities; JSW One Finance, the NBFC arm providing digital credit lines, channel financing and invoice factoring to MSMEs and retailers; and private brands JSW One TMT and One Helix. The platform reported FY25 gross merchandise value of INR 12,567 crore across more than 84,000 registered MSMEs, and raised INR 575 crore in a 2025 round led by the State Bank of India. JSW One publishes no public developer program, API reference or machine-readable contract; its customer-facing surfaces are the web marketplace and the JSW One MSME mobile apps. It does publish a maintained llms.txt on both of its consumer properties, plus an explicit AI/LLM bot-access policy on JSW One Homes.

providers.name: Kayako
providers.description: Kayako provides an AI‑powered help desk and customer support platform for SaaS businesses. Its solution combines ticketing, live chat, email automation, knowledge base, and shared inbox features, all enhanced with machine‑learning to route, suggest replies, and prioritize issues. Serving over 10,000 support professionals across 300+ companies, Kayako aims to reduce response times, improve CSAT, and lower support costs through intelligent automation and omnichannel experiences.

providers.name: Known
providers.description: Known is a voice-first, swipeless dating application founded in 2025 by Celeste Amadon and Asher Allen and headquartered in San Francisco, California. Instead of profiles, feeds, queues, and swiping, Known onboards users through a voice-AI interview and then sends one curated introduction at a time, with a 24-hour acceptance window on both sides. When both people accept, Known helps pick a restaurant that fits both sets of preferences and checks calendar availability, then collects a short post-date check-in to refine future matches. The company optimizes for in-person dates rather than engagement, and has raised $9.7M from Forerunner Ventures, NFX, and other investors. The product is iOS-only in the United States today, with waitlists for Android and for Apple users outside the US. Known publishes no public developer program, API, or SDKs; it does publish a first-party llms.txt describing the product for AI agents.

providers.name: Labcorp
providers.description: Labcorp helps patients, providers, organizations, and biopharma companies guide vital healthcare decisions every day. Labcorp supports HL7 / FHIR-based integration for laboratory orders and results exchange with electronic health record (EHR) systems, but does not publish a fully open public developer portal; access is granted through health-system and biopharma integration agreements.

providers.name: Last9
providers.description: Last9 provides a unified observability platform for developers, SREs, and AI agents, offering metrics, logs, traces, and APM in a single view with full visibility and cost control. The service aims to simplify monitoring and debugging across modern cloud environments, integrating with popular tooling and supporting automated insights.

providers.name: lastminute.com
providers.description: lastminute.com N.V. (SIX Swiss Exchange: LMN) is a European travel-tech group and the regional leader in dynamic holiday packages, operating an online travel agency portfolio that includes lastminute.com, Volagratis, Rumbo, Bravofly, Weg.de, Jetcost and Hotelscan alongside the Forward media/advertising business. The group sells flights, hotels and packaged travel across a global network, and runs an engineering organisation that publishes an open technology blog and a Stoplight-hosted API portal at developers.lastminute.com. That portal is a real partner-facing API surface, but its projects are not anonymously readable — API reference content sits behind a workspace sign-in, so lastminute.com currently exposes no public OpenAPI, SDK, or self-service developer onboarding path.

providers.name: Lens Protocol
providers.description: Lens Protocol is an onchain social graph and a developer platform for building social applications where users own their profile, content, and relationships. Originally launched on Polygon PoS, Lens has since evolved into Lens Chain — an L2 zkEVM rollup purpose-built for social — with the Lens v3 contracts redesigned around primitives like Accounts, Apps, Feeds, Groups, Graphs, and Actions. Developers integrate Lens through the Lens API (a GraphQL gateway over the indexed chain state), the Lens TypeScript SDK and React SDK, the underlying smart contracts, and an authentication layer that issues short-lived auth tokens after a SIWE-style signature. Lens powers social clients (Hey, Orb, Tape, Buttrfly), creator tools, and composable mini-apps that share the same onchain social graph.

providers.name: Lenus eHealth
providers.description: Lenus eHealth is a Copenhagen-headquartered health and fitness technology company that builds a coaching platform for online health and fitness coaches, positioning itself as a growth partner rather than a consumer fitness app. Coaching partners run their businesses through the Lenus web dashboard and branded consumer mobile apps: client onboarding and screening, training and nutrition programming, habit and progress tracking, in-app messaging, content delivery, subscription billing and business analytics. The company also operates Lenus Academy, a certified education program for online coaches, and in the United States offers a GLP-1 weight management program delivered with independent medical partner Beluga Health. Lenus operates from 20+ offices including Copenhagen, Berlin, London, Amsterdam, Stockholm, Madrid, New York and Toronto, and is backed by EQT Ventures. The platform is closed and invitation-based: as of July 2026 Lenus publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs or machine-readable API specifications, and access is available only to coaching partners under a partnership agreement.

providers.name: Locale
providers.description: Locale is a no-code workflow automation platform that lets operations, data, and engineering teams build, run, and monitor automated workflows without writing glue code. Its visual builder chains together apps and actions — HTTP requests, AI Actions, run-your-own code, email, Slack, PostgreSQL, Sendgrid, and Fireflies.ai — with flow controls such as conditional branching, delays, and list iterators, then passes data between steps to orchestrate real business processes. Workflows can be built, connected, debugged, and published from the Locale app, and the platform positions itself as an operational automation layer for teams that want internal alerting and process automation without a heavy engineering lift. Locale is backed by a16z. This profile was enriched from Locale's public documentation surface (docs.locale.ai); Locale publishes no first-party public REST API or OpenAPI at this time.

providers.name: Logstash
providers.description: Open source server-side data processing pipeline that ingests data from multiple sources, transforms it, and sends it to a specified destination. Part of the Elastic Stack.

providers.name: Lucem Health
providers.description: Lucem Health is a clinical-AI company founded in 2021 with Mayo Clinic Platform, backed by Mayo Clinic, Commure and Rally Ventures. Its Lucem Health Reveal programs apply clinically validated AI models to a health system's existing data to surface patients at elevated risk of serious or chronic disease — arrhythmias, colorectal cancer, liver disease, lung cancer and Type 1 diabetes — and deliver those insights into existing clinical workflows without changing how clinicians practice. The company also runs a Clinical AI SolutionOps practice that helps AI innovators and life-sciences organizations deploy, scale and commercialize models against provider data. Integration is delivered as a managed service into EHR, PACS and other clinical systems; as of 2026-08-25 Lucem Health publishes no public developer portal, API reference or machine-readable contract.

providers.name: MakerDAO
providers.description: MakerDAO is the decentralized autonomous organization behind the Maker Protocol, an Ethereum-based smart-contract system that lets anyone, anywhere generate the Dai (DAI) stablecoin by locking crypto collateral into Vaults. The protocol governs collateral types, stability fees, the Dai Savings Rate (DSR), collateral liquidation auctions, and oracle price feeds through on-chain governance by MKR token holders. Rather than a hosted REST API, developers integrate directly with the Maker Protocol smart contracts and through the official Dai.js JavaScript / TypeScript SDK, the multicall state-management library, and published developer guides. MakerDAO has since rebranded to the Sky Ecosystem (USDS / SKY). Surfaced as a portfolio company of Paradigm and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: MemVerge
providers.description: MemVerge is a memory and AI-infrastructure software company whose Memory Machine and Memory Machine Cloud (MMCloud) platforms virtualize and orchestrate memory and compute for AI, high-performance computing, and life-sciences workloads. MMCloud is operated through the OpCenter control plane and the first-party "float" command-line interface, which submits, migrates, checkpoints, and monitors containerized jobs across cloud and on-prem infrastructure, with spot-instance resiliency (SpotSurfer / WaveRider). MemVerge integrates with Nextflow, Snakemake, and Flyte through open-source plugins and SDKs published on its GitHub organization. Originally surfaced as a Lightspeed Venture Partners portfolio company, this profile is enriched from MemVerge's public documentation, CLI reference, and GitHub org.

providers.name: MicroTech Medical
providers.description: MicroTech Medical (Hangzhou) develops user-friendly diabetes glucose monitoring devices — blood glucose monitoring systems (BGMS), the AiDEX continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) system, the Equil patch insulin pump, a closed-loop artificial pancreas, point-of-care testing (POCT), and LinX. Its AiDEX API Platform (aidexapi.microtechmd.com) is a self-service developer portal that registers developers and issues API credentials for accessing blood glucose data resources from AiDEX CGM devices, with separate global and China regional endpoints. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners.

providers.name: Miyokos
providers.description: Miyoko's Creamery (miyokos.com) is a plant-based dairy company in the planetary-health sector, backed by Obvious Ventures, making vegan butter and cheese from cultured cashews, oats, and legumes. The company does not publish a first-party developer REST API; its digital surface is a Shopify-hosted storefront. That storefront exposes a genuine agent-commerce surface: a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) merchant profile at /.well-known/ucp, a hosted shopping MCP endpoint for search/cart/checkout, Shopify Customer Account OIDC/OAuth for identity, and an /llms.txt with agent instructions. This profile was enriched by probing that public surface.

providers.name: Nookly
providers.description: Nookly is a personalized children's content platform that helps the adults who care for a child — parents, teachers, therapists, and early-childhood organizations — turn their intimate knowledge of that child into custom stories, songs, visual schedules, social stories, emotion cards, and behavior supports. Grounded in social-emotional learning and behavioral science, it produces developmentally appropriate, COPPA/FERPA-compliant content for children ages 2-11, with particular value for neurodivergent kids (autism, ADHD, speech delays, anxiety, and sensory processing differences). Used across homes, classrooms, and clinics in 50+ states.

providers.name: OncoC4
providers.description: OncoC4, Inc. is a privately held, late clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered in Rockville, Maryland, founded in 2020, with subsidiaries in Nanjing, Guangzhou and Beijing, China, and Brisbane, Australia. The company discovers and develops novel biologics for the treatment of cancer, working across immune checkpoints including CTLA-4, CD24, PD-1/VEGF and the Siglec family, with monoclonal antibodies, bispecific antibodies, antibody-drug conjugates and CAR T-cell therapies. Its lead clinical candidate is gotistobart (BNT316/ONC-392), a next-generation anti-CTLA-4 antibody co-developed and commercialized with BioNTech under a strategic collaboration announced in March 2023. OncoC4 publishes no developer program, public API, SDK or developer documentation; its corporate website runs on the Umbraco CMS, which serves a default OpenID Connect / OAuth 2.0 discovery document and JWKS for CMS member authentication.

providers.name: Overstory
providers.description: Overstory provides AI-powered vegetation intelligence for electric utilities and grid operators.
