providers.description: AssessLane provides AI‑native team assessment tools that let organizations create, assign, and track knowledge‑check quizzes using any MCP‑compatible AI such as Claude or Cursor. Users can run a free 14‑day trial without a credit card, view sample assessments, and retrieve completion reports via the MCP interface. The platform offers per‑seat pricing starting at $3 per seat per month and supports unlimited quizzes and reporting.

providers.name: Atalaya
providers.description: Atalaya provides an AI‑powered work management platform for product managers and product teams. It enables teams to plan, prioritize, and execute projects using AI agents that translate natural‑language requests into actionable development plans, generate code, and automate testing. Users can create tasks, approve plans, and track progress without directly interacting with GitHub, leveraging large language models such as Claude Code and any MCP‑compatible assistant. The platform includes sprint boards, backlog management, automated code generation, and integration with communication tools, aiming to increase productivity and reduce manual coordination.

providers.name: Basebuild
providers.description: Basebuild Labs, Inc. builds Beams, an AI project manager for construction and real estate teams. The product automatically transcribes project meetings, tracks decisions and action items, and assembles a searchable knowledge base from those discussions, capturing information without requiring a bot to join the call. It is aimed at giving construction and real estate project teams real-time visibility and control over teams, projects, budgets, and finances. Basebuild is an early-stage Canaan Partners portfolio company based in Santa Monica, California, and this API Evangelist profile tracks its public-facing surface. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a marketing site and a product login only, with no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI definition, or documentation surface to catalog.

providers.name: bellwether-markets
providers.description: Bellwether Markets provides a unified API that aggregates prediction market data from major platforms like Kalshi and Polymarket. By normalizing disparate schemas into a single, developer‑friendly REST and MCP interface, it enables easy access to market listings, detailed market data, and cross‑venue arbitrage opportunities. The service offers free tier access with generous rate limits, supporting both real‑time data retrieval and integration into AI agents for automated trading strategies. Backed by YC and built after Polymarket’s acquisition, Bellwether aims to simplify the fragmented prediction market landscape for developers and traders alike.

providers.name: brainonbnb-com
providers.description: Brain On BNB AI (BOBAI) is a meme‑coin project on the BNB Smart Chain that provides a suite of open‑source, on‑chain tools and agents. It offers a public REST/MCP API, a DeFi agent that manages a PancakeSwap V3 position, a token‑price dashboard, a pool scanner, an AI‑driven agent marketplace (Brain Plaza), NFT buy‑drop, and various utility services. All code is open‑source on GitHub, and the platform emphasizes transparency with verifiable on‑chain data, no private keys, and read‑only access. The project’s website, documentation, and API references are hosted at brainonbnb.com.

providers.name: Brevis
providers.description: Brevis is a highly efficient ZK coprocessor and zkVM that empowers smart contracts to read from the full historical on-chain data across all supported blockchains and run customizable computations in a completely trust-free way. Developers build application circuits with the Brevis SDK (available in Go and TypeScript), implementing a Data Access Module to specify the historical blockchain data needed, an App Circuit for the computation logic, and an App Contract to receive ZK-verified or coChain-verified results on-chain. Brevis also operates ProverNet, an open marketplace for zero-knowledge proofs, and Pico, an open-source high-performance zkVM. Backed by Polychain.

providers.name: BrickTrack
providers.description: BrickTrack provides a cloud‑based investment property tracker that lets owners monitor equity, cash flow, rent and loans across their portfolio without using spreadsheets. The platform offers real‑time analytics, automated reporting, and tools for budgeting and forecasting, aiming to simplify property management for investors and landlords.

providers.name: Brim Financial
providers.description: Brim Financial is a Toronto-based Canadian fintech (founded 2017) that operates a fully-integrated, API-first credit-card Platform-as-a-Service (PaaS). It is not a chartered Schedule I or Schedule II bank; it describes itself as the only fintech in North America licensed to issue credit cards, and it delivers Credit-Cards-as-a-Service (CCaaS), loyalty/rewards, BNPL, and money-movement infrastructure to banks, credit unions, fintechs, and large brands (clients include Manulife Bank, Laurentian Bank, Canadian Western Bank, Affinity Credit Union, and Air France-KLM). Brim is registered under Canada's Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA) to Bank of Canada standards and was admitted to Payments Canada as a payment service provider, and has partnered with Mastercard to embed open-banking capabilities. Although Brim markets a comprehensive API-first platform, that API is delivered to enterprise/embedded-finance partners through a commercial onboarding relationship: as of this review there is no public, self-serve first-party developer portal, no downloadable OpenAPI/Swagger, and no operational consumer-driven-banking (open-banking) API, consistent with Canada's voluntary, not-yet-live open-finance framework.

providers.name: Bullrun
providers.description: Bullrun is a Zurich‑based fintech platform that helps investors find the cheapest UCITS ETFs for their chosen indexes. It provides a searchable comparison of ETFs by fee, domicile, payout, and trading venues, along with research on companies worldwide. The service is free, web‑based, and aims to simplify ETF selection for both retail and professional investors.

providers.name: Calensync
providers.description: Calensync provides a service to sync events across Google Calendar, Outlook, Microsoft 365, Apple iCloud and .ics links. It copies events between calendars, preserving details or marking them as busy, and offers per‑account pricing with a 7‑day free trial. The platform targets freelancers, consultants and teams needing to avoid double‑bookings, supporting multiple clients and personal calendars. It emphasizes privacy, with Google usage disclosure and clear terms of service and privacy policy pages.

providers.name: ClassPass
providers.description: ClassPass is a fitness and wellness marketplace that lets consumers book classes, gym visits, and spa/wellness experiences across a network of studios in a single app using a monthly credit subscription. On the supply side, ClassPass runs a partner integration platform - centered on a named "ClassPass Inventory API" - that lets studios and their scheduling/booking software (100+ platforms, including Mindbody, Vagaro, Zen Planner, and Eversports Manager) push live class schedules, availability, and pricing to ClassPass and receive bookings and cancellations back. The partner developer portal at developers.classpass.com requires an approved partner login (Auth0) to view the API specification document and run certification tests; ClassPass does not publish a public, unauthenticated API reference, OpenAPI file, or Postman collection. ClassPass is now part of Playlist, the group formed together with Mindbody and Booker.

providers.name: Cloudfabrixsoftware
providers.description: Cloudfabrixsoftware, now operating under the Fabrix brand, provides an AI-driven platform that enables enterprises to build, deploy, and manage autonomous agents across multiple domains. Their solutions span data fabric, observability, security, and workflow automation, empowering organizations to harness agentic AI for complex operational tasks and digital transformation.

providers.name: Conduct AI
providers.description: Conduct AI (conduct.ai) is an enterprise "AI operating system" that helps IT teams understand, operate, and transform their business software, starting with SAP and expanding across the wider enterprise stack. Its platform analyzes custom code to reveal dependencies and system relationships (Understand), automates software-development workflows from planning through deployment (Operate), and accelerates system migrations such as S/4HANA with automated analysis and code refactoring (Transform). The company markets outcomes like faster S/4HANA migration planning, reduced manual system analysis, and shorter change-implementation cycles. Conduct raised a $60M Series A and is backed by ICONIQ Capital. It publishes a marketing site, blog, and case studies but does not currently expose a public developer API, SDKs, or API reference documentation.

providers.name: Cooler Heads
providers.description: Cooler Heads Care, Inc. is a San Diego medical device company founded in 2018 by Kate Dilligan that makes Amma, an FDA-cleared Portable Scalp Cooling System (PSCS) used to reduce chemotherapy-induced hair loss. Amma circulates chilled fluid through a fitted cap to constrict scalp blood vessels and limit chemotherapy delivery to hair follicles, and is designed to be portable enough that patients can keep cooling outside the infusion chair. The company sells to infusion centers and oncology practices and publishes patient, provider, reimbursement and training material on its own site. It ships no developer API, SDK or public API documentation; its only machine-readable public surface is the Wix-platform site MCP endpoint and llms.txt served from its own host.

providers.name: Countable
providers.description: Countable was a civic-engagement technology company backed by Canaan Partners (seed, partner Joydeep Bhattacharyya) that built a digital platform helping citizens understand what Congress was doing in Washington and contact their elected representatives directly, later extending the same advocacy tooling to organizations and brands. As of this enrichment pass the Countable brand is no longer operating independently: both countable.com and countable.us HTTP 302 to https://www.myactionable.com/, the home of Actionable, a self-service advocacy campaign platform made by CSAG that offers petitions, pledges, lawmaker-message campaigns, supporter video collection, lead capture, polling and in-platform real-time campaign reporting on a $29.99/month self-service plan. No public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI definition, SDK, package, webhook catalog, MCP server or /.well-known discovery surface was found on either the legacy Countable hosts or the successor Actionable host during this pass.

providers.name: Coverdash
providers.description: Coverdash is a digital business insurance agency that provides fully‑digital, instant business insurance solutions for small and medium‑sized enterprises. Founded in 2022 and based in New York City, Coverdash offers a range of coverages—including General Liability, Workers’ Compensation, Cyber, Professional Liability, and Commercial Auto—through a streamlined online platform that connects businesses with top‑rated carriers, delivering quotes and policies in minutes without brokers or paperwork.

providers.name: Cyberpsyc
providers.description: CyberPsyc Software Solutions, operating as WellTrack Boost (now part of ProtoCall Services), builds self-guided, clinically-supported digital cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) tools for behavioral health and wellness. The platform lets users assess and understand their mental health on their own devices and schedule through MoodCheck mood tracking, the Zen Room, a Thought Diary, an Activity Scheduler, Fun and Achievement planning, and guided modules for stress, anxiety, and depression. WellTrack Boost is deployed by college counseling centers and certified community behavioral health clinics, offering institutional single sign-on through a SAML integration surface. No public developer REST API or OpenAPI is currently published.

providers.name: Feesable
providers.description: Feesable is a fintech infrastructure company providing embedded finance and debt capital management (treasury) tooling that connects platforms, lenders, and capital markets. Its Embedded Finance product delivers white-labeled loan origination infrastructure — KYC/KYB verification, credit decisioning, dynamic pricing, fraud detection, and servicing/collections — exposed through APIs, SDKs, and embeddable widgets so SaaS platforms, marketplaces, and B2B lenders can launch embedded lending without building fintech from scratch. Its Debt Capital Management (DCM Engine) product provides institutional-grade treasury management — credit facility modeling, covenant monitoring, borrowing-base calculations, and automated lender/regulatory reporting connected to live portfolio data. Feesable targets GCC markets with Shariah-compliant options and is a portfolio company of 500 Global. The developer surface (APIs, SDKs, sandbox keys, documentation) is partner-gated behind a partnership onboarding process rather than publicly self-serve.

providers.name: First Hawaiian Bank
providers.description: First Hawaiian Bank is Hawaii's oldest and largest financial institution, founded in 1858 and headquartered at First Hawaiian Center in Honolulu. It is a Hawaii state-chartered commercial bank and member FDIC, operating as the principal subsidiary of First Hawaiian, Inc. (NASDAQ ticker FHB), a publicly traded bank holding company. The bank serves consumer and commercial customers through roughly 57 branches in Hawaii plus locations in Guam and Saipan, offering deposit accounts, lending, wealth management, treasury/cash management, and merchant services. On the open-finance front, First Hawaiian operates no public first-party developer portal and publishes no downloadable OpenAPI/Swagger specifications; probes of developer.fhb.com, api.fhb.com, and fhb.com/en/developers returned no host or HTTP 404. Consumer-permissioned account data is reachable only through third-party aggregators (notably Plaid), not a direct bank API. No documented Financial Data Exchange (FDX) participation or published CFPB Section 1033 data-access posture was found as of this record. Its commercial online banking product (FHB Commercial Online, formerly OBC) is a traditional web application rather than a developer-facing API surface.

providers.name: Firstjob.me
providers.description: FirstJob (firstjob.me) is a Latin American employment platform founded in Chile in 2012 to improve working conditions for young professionals by connecting students and early-career candidates (0-2 years of experience) with entry-level jobs and internships at large employers. The platform lists 1,200+ active opportunities across engineering, administration, operations, and technology, maintains an employer directory, and runs networking events and webinars. It also operates related initiatives including Employers For Youth (EFY) and Best Internship Experiences (BIE) employer-ranking programs. FirstJob is a consumer-facing web platform used by more than 500,000 young professionals; it does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI/Swagger specification, SDKs, or a developer portal. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Fizz
providers.description: Fizz is a social platform built for college campuses, connecting students within their own school communities across 700+ campuses in the United States. Founded by Stanford students, Fizz gives verified students an anonymous, hyper-local feed to find their community and join the conversation, buy and sell through Fizz Marketplace, and engage under community values of being supportive, curious, honest, and brave. The platform is backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners and NEA. Fizz is a consumer mobile social app and does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation; this API Evangelist profile captures its public web, legal, and security surface for network discovery and monitoring.

providers.name: Fleetmatics
providers.description: Fleetmatics was a fleet management, telematics, and GPS vehicle tracking SaaS company whose Reveal platform tracked commercial vehicles, drivers, and mobile assets for small and mid-sized fleets. Founded in Dublin and later headquartered in Massachusetts, Fleetmatics IPO'd on the NYSE in 2012 and was acquired by Verizon in 2016 for about USD 2.4 billion, becoming the core of Verizon Connect. Its Reveal platform exposes a documented REST API and webhook suite - the Fleetmatics Integration Manager (FIM) / Reveal Integration Services APIs - covering vehicles, drivers, GPS positions and history, trips and segments, driver status and safety, hours-of-service logbooks, geofences (places), groups, and non-powered asset tracking. The API gateway still runs on Fleetmatics-branded hosts (fim.api.us.fleetmatics.com); access is gated to Reveal customers and approved integration partners who request Integration Manager and Reveal REST credentials before calling the documented endpoints. The Fleetmatics brand now redirects to Verizon Connect.

providers.name: Forage
providers.description: Forage provides free virtual job simulations and career preparation resources, partnering with top employers to offer hands‑on experience across industries such as finance, engineering, consulting, and cybersecurity. Users can explore simulations, build skills, and showcase their work to potential employers, while enterprises and educators access tailored programs for talent development and recruitment.

providers.name: Formic
providers.description: Formic is a Chicago, Illinois-based Robotics-as-a-Service (RaaS) company founded in 2020 by Saman Farid that delivers full-service industrial automation to American manufacturers on a pay-per-hour, fixed monthly subscription model with no capital expenditure. Formic specializes in end-of-line manufacturing operations — palletizing, case packing, and robotic pallet wrapping — and pairs deployed robots with a 24/7 remote monitoring, support, and field-service operation. The company's software stack includes Formic Core, an embedded operating system that abstracts motion, vision, sensing, and real-time coordination across heterogeneous industrial robot hardware (Fanuc, ABB, Kuka, Doosan) behind unified control interfaces; Formic Cortex; the Colony 2.0 fleet dashboard; FAST configuration tools; and Formic Production Intelligence (FPI), a manufacturer-facing analytics surface. Formic has raised more than $86M across rounds led by Lux Capital, Blackhorn Ventures, and other investors, and works through a network of 100+ system-integrator partners with 500+ systems deployed. Formic's revenue model is the RaaS subscription itself; there is no public developer API, no published SDKs, and no public customer-portal API documentation. Formic Core's "unified APIs" are internal abstractions used by Formic engineers and integrator partners to drive robot hardware — they are not exposed to manufacturers or third-party developers.

providers.name: GoSky AI
providers.description: GoSky AI Inc. is a Taipei-based no-code conversational marketing and social CRM platform that helps creators, brands, and enterprises automate customer engagement across Instagram, Threads, and Facebook Messenger. Founded in 2018, its product suite spans the GoSky AI Chatbot Platform (build no-code chat flows, capture leads, and auto-reply to comments and DMs in minutes), GoSky Loyal (a digital loyalty and membership points program), GoSky Ads (precision ad placement across Google, Meta, and Shopee), and GoSky AI Customer Service (generative-AI-powered 24/7 support). The company operates a hosted SaaS console at platform.goskyai.com and reports serving 400+ enterprises including Mercedes-Benz, VOGUE, and Lazada. GoSky AI is a portfolio company of 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass GoSky AI publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDKs, or developer documentation surface; this profile captures its public identity, web properties, and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Greenboard
providers.description: Greenboard is an AI-native compliance software platform for SEC- and FINRA-regulated financial institutions, consolidating communications archiving, employee compliance monitoring, marketing/advertising review, firm-wide compliance management, and third-party (vendor) compliance into a single system of action. It serves independent advisors, RIAs, hedge funds, private funds, and broker-dealers, automating regulatory workflows and reducing review times. Greenboard is a General Catalyst portfolio company. Its product is delivered as a hosted SaaS application; no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal is published at this time, so this profile captures corporate identity, trust/compliance posture (SOC 2 Type II), and domain security rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Greyparrot
providers.description: Greyparrot is a London-based AI waste analytics company that turns materials recovery facilities (MRFs) into data-driven operations. Its Greyparrot Analyzer uses computer-vision cameras mounted over waste conveyor belts to identify, count, and measure the composition of waste streams in real time, giving recyclers continuous visibility into what flows through their plant. The Greyparrot Sync product routes that analytics stream into existing operational control systems, ERP platforms, Power BI dashboards, and OEM sortation hardware (robotic arms, air-jet systems, balers, belt control), while Deepnest turns real-world recovery data into design feedback for packaging brands. Backed by Speedinvest, Greyparrot serves recyclers, equipment manufacturers, and consumer-goods companies working to raise recycling rates and automate compliance reporting. The company does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or OpenAPI definition; this profile captures its public web, product, and content surface.

providers.name: HEDNA
providers.description: HEDNA (Hotel Electronic Distribution Network Association) is a not-for-profit trade association founded in 1991 and headquartered in Forest Hill, Maryland, United States, that convenes the hotel distribution industry — hotel chains, GDS operators, OTAs, switches, channel managers, payment providers and connectivity vendors — around shared best practice for hospitality electronic distribution. It sits alongside rather than inside the distribution chain: it moves no inventory and processes no bookings, but its Disciplines (Connectivity, Content Distribution, Payments, Data & Analytics, Revenue Optimization) produce recommendation documents, and it co-authored the Open Payments Alliance Standards Specification with HTNG and OpenTravel. HEDNA publishes no developer portal, no API, and no machine-readable specification on hedna.org; every probe of developer./developers./docs./api. subdomains and of /developers, /api, /docs, /openapi.json, /swagger.json, /api-docs and /.well-known/ failed (DNS failure or HTTP 404). Its publications library, research reports and HEDNA U courseware are gated behind paid membership at members.hedna.org (HTTP 403 Cloudflare challenge unauthenticated) and pathlms.com/hedna. Honest posture: member-gated documents, no public API, no exit path published.

providers.name: Hoop
providers.description: Hoop is an AI retention agent for Shopify subscription brands, built by the founding team behind Trello and backed by Index Ventures. It plugs into a brand's helpdesk (Gorgias, Zendesk, or Kustomer), intercepts every subscription-cancellation ticket, and runs a tailored save conversation in the brand's voice: it asks why the subscriber wants to leave, then matches a retention offer (pause, plan swap, discount, or skip) to the stated reason and writes the accepted change back to the billing tool (Recharge or Skio) automatically. Hoop logs every cancellation reason, offer, and outcome so brands learn why subscribers churn, and lets teams A/B test save offers through plain-English policy changes rather than macros. It is an end-user SaaS application rather than an API provider — it consumes the Shopify, Gorgias, Zendesk, Recharge, and Skio APIs and exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation of its own.

providers.name: iCapital Network
providers.description: iCapital (Institutional Capital Network, Inc.) is a New York-headquartered financial technology company, founded in 2013, that operates the alternative investments marketplace and the operating infrastructure behind it. Its platform lets wealth managers, RIAs, family offices and institutional investors research, subscribe to, service and report on private markets funds, hedge funds, structured investments, annuities, model portfolios and separately managed accounts, while asset managers use it to distribute those products into the wealth channel. iCapital Marketplace advertises access to funds from 700+ asset managers and reports $945B+ in global platform assets. Around the marketplace sit Architect (portfolio construction and analytics), Data Solutions (alternative data management and consolidated reporting), Identity Solutions (KYC/AML), and iCapital DLT, an API-first distributed ledger platform built on the Canton Network. Integration with custodians, fund administrators, transfer agents and advisor platforms (BNY, Fidelity, Envestnet, Orion, Morningstar, Vestmark, TradePMR, GeoWealth, Ultimus, UMB) happens through SSO, embedded workflows and partner data integrations. As of the 2026-08-01 enrichment pass iCapital publishes no public developer portal, API reference, machine-readable API contract or client SDKs; API documentation is described as available to integration partners only, through the sales and technical-support organization.

providers.name: IRIS Software Group
providers.description: IRIS Software Group provides business software solutions for mission‑critical tasks across accounting, payroll, HR, education, financials and more. Their AI‑powered platforms help organisations manage finance, human resources, payroll and education operations efficiently, serving customers worldwide.

providers.name: Ivanti
providers.description: Ivanti is an IT asset management and security platform providing unified endpoint management, patch management, and IT service management. The Ivanti Neurons product family exposes REST APIs across People & Devices, MDM, ITSM, and Zero-Trust Access, alongside Endpoint Manager APIs for patch and software distribution.

providers.name: Jays
providers.description: JAYS is a Swedish consumer audio brand founded in 2006 by Jens and Johan, headquartered in Sweden and owned by the Northbaze Group AB. It designs and sells wireless and wired headphones, true-wireless earbuds, Bluetooth and multiroom speakers, and audio accessories, sold direct-to-consumer through a Shopify storefront at jaysheadphones.com. JAYS publishes no first-party developer API; its only machine-accessible surface is the Shopify-provided agent-commerce layer: a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) merchant profile with a hosted MCP shopping endpoint, Customer Account OpenID Connect / OAuth discovery documents, and an llms.txt. This profile was surfaced as a Creandum portfolio/commitment lead and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Jest
providers.description: Jest is a delightful JavaScript testing framework with a focus on simplicity. It works with projects using Babel, TypeScript, Node, React, Angular, Vue and more. Jest provides snapshot testing, parallel execution, built-in mocking, and code coverage out of the box.

providers.name: Julienne Bruno
providers.description: JULIENNE BRUNO is a London-based food company that creates, develops and produces naturally plant-based fresh cheeses. Its Collection 01 comprises Burrella, Superstraccia and Crematta - dairy-free, fermented products positioned as original foods in their own category rather than vegan imitations. Products are sold direct-to-consumer through a Shopify storefront and stocked at Ocado, Whole Foods, Planet Organic, Harrods and Selfridges, and featured on the menus of 800+ restaurants, pubs and cafes. Founded in 2020 and backed by Seedcamp, the brand and assets were later acquired by Harvey & Brockless (The Compleat Food Group). This is a consumer packaged goods company; it publishes no developer API - the profile is enriched from its public web surface.

providers.name: Juno
providers.description: Juno is a Brazilian B2B payments fintech, acquired by EBANX in October 2021, that provides a complete billing and payments platform for Brazilian companies. Founded in 2014 in Maringá, Paraná, Juno powers more than 35,000 small and medium businesses with online sales and collections via Pix, boleto bancário, boleto_pix, and credit cards, plus marketplace payment split, recurring subscriptions, and a digital business account (Conta Juno) with Banking-as-a-Service capabilities. Juno is a participant of the Brazilian Interbank Payments Chamber (CIP). The company exposes a public REST API v2 through the Juno Developer Academy at integracao.juno.com.br, secured with OAuth 2.0 client_credentials, plus HMAC-SHA256 signed webhooks and native mobile Direct Checkout SDKs for Android and iOS for PCI-safe card data encryption.

providers.name: KitchenMate
providers.description: KitchenMate is a Toronto-based autonomous retail and workplace food-service company that operates 24/7 unattended micro-markets built around two pieces of proprietary hardware, a checkout-free Smart Fridge that uses vision sensors to detect what a customer removes and bill them automatically, and induction-based Smart Cookers that heat chef-prepared entrees in seven to ten minutes. The kiosks are installed in workplaces, condominiums, schools, hospitals and other commercial locations, require roughly seven square feet plus standard electrical and network connectivity, and accept Visa, Mastercard, Amex, Apple Pay and Google Pay at the unit. A companion iOS and Android app carries loyalty rewards, dietary filters and meal feedback. The company has since rebranded its platform business as Micromart, which markets the same autonomous smart-store technology under the tagline "Be anywhere. Sell anything." across a stated 2,000+ locations in North America. KitchenMate publishes no public API, developer portal or SDKs; this profile captures its identity and probed security posture only.

providers.name: Konfig
providers.description: Konfig is an SDK and API documentation generator that turns an OpenAPI Specification or Postman Collection into production-ready client libraries, interactive reference docs, demos, and tutorials. It generates and publishes idiomatic SDKs across TypeScript/JavaScript, Python, Java, C#, PHP, Ruby, Go, Swift, Kotlin, Objective-C, and Dart, republishing them automatically whenever the spec changes, and adds spec linting and generated SDK tests to keep client libraries in sync across the API lifecycle. Konfig is driven from a CLI (konfig-cli) and a konfig.yaml config that calls Konfig's hosted generation backend - it is a developer-tooling platform, not a hosted public REST API of its own. Konfig was sunset in December 2024 and its full codebase was open-sourced (MIT) at github.com/konfig-dev/konfig; the marketing site, docs, and 491 generated SDK repositories at github.com/konfig-sdks remain online.

providers.name: Lara AI
providers.description: Lara AI is an AI agent for People and HR teams, built by SIGMA PEOPLE S.R.L. in Argentina and sold across Latin America. Lara talks to every employee in the messaging tools they already use — WhatsApp, Slack, Microsoft Teams and Google Chat — and covers five modules: Employee Experience (continuous listening, custom surveys and people analytics), Helpdesk (an AI help desk the company says automates over 80% of employee FAQs and requests), Onboarding (end-to-end automated flows for new hires), Comunicaciones (personalised, scheduled and segmented employee communications) and People Analytics (dashboards and reports built from people data). It integrates with HR platforms including SAP, BambooHR, Oracle, Buk, Humand, Mandu and Rex+, and targets retail, consumer goods, technology, consulting, banking and finance, education and manufacturing. Lara AI publishes a marketing site, a Spanish help centre and a real llms.txt, but no public API program — there is no developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI definition or SDK.

providers.name: Leta
providers.description: Leta is a pan-African logistics technology company founded in 2022 and headquartered in Westlands, Nairobi, Kenya, with operations across Kenya, Nigeria and South Africa. Leta builds an AI-driven delivery management platform that helps businesses move goods cheaper and faster while minimising climate impact: route optimization, automated dispatch and broadcast, live GPS track-and-trace, payment on delivery, fleet management, and delivery analytics. The platform is delivered as logistics SaaS plus on-demand and dedicated rider services, including an M-PESA business mini-app, and serves e-commerce, third-party logistics and courier, food and beverage, retail and consumer goods, and pharmacy and healthcare delivery operators. Leta is backed by Speedinvest.

providers.name: Lindus Health
providers.description: Lindus Health is a next-generation contract research organization (CRO) that runs clinical trials end to end for biotech and pharmaceutical sponsors. It pairs Citrus, an AI-assisted trial operating system connecting patient identification through final data capture, with centralized patient identification and enrollment (AI-powered EHR querying, digital pre-screening, centralized patient support), flexible site models spanning site-based, hybrid and fully virtual delivery, and integrated clinical services from protocol design through database lock. Its platform surface covers EDC, eSource, ePRO/eCOA, eConsent and CTMS. The company operates across the US, UK and Europe with APAC partnerships, employs over 160 staff, and works in cardiometabolic, respiratory, psychiatry, women's health and dermatology. Commercial engagements are performance-based with milestone pricing. Lindus Health publishes no public developer API, developer portal or API documentation; its public technical footprint is two open-source CDISC clinical-data repositories.

providers.name: Marand
providers.description: Marand Software (Marand d.o.o., Ljubljana, Slovenia) builds cloud-native Business Support System components for communications service providers, positioned as a vendor of TM Forum Open Digital Architecture (ODA) components. Its product line covers a Unified Product Catalog, 360 Customer / Inventory, CPQ, CRM, Multiservice Enterprise Billing, AI/ML solutions and custom software services. Marand's components implement the TM Forum Information Framework (SID) and expose TM Forum Open APIs; the company is a TM Forum Open API Gold certified member, holds Open API conformance certifications for TMF633 (Service Catalog Management, 2022) and TMF673 (Geographic Address Management, 2023), achieved "Ready for ODA" status in March 2024, and co-authored the TMF760 Product Configuration API with Orange and Amdocs as one of the first fifth-generation TM Forum Open APIs. Marand publishes no public developer portal, API reference or machine-readable specification of its own — its APIs ship inside licensed components deployed at operator customers, and the contracts they implement are the TM Forum specifications.

providers.name: Metra
providers.description: Metra provides GTFS API data for the Metra commuter rail system in the Chicago metropolitan area. The API is hosted at gtfsapi.metrarail.com and provides both RAW data and JSON for schedules, trips, stops, and real-time updates.

providers.name: NOBIL (Enova)
providers.description: NOBIL (Enova) provides a comprehensive API delivering real‑time and historical data on electric vehicle charging stations across Norway and other Nordic countries. The service offers information on station locations, availability, connector types, pricing, and operational status, supporting developers building EV navigation, fleet management, and energy‑grid applications. Data is sourced from public and private operators and is updated regularly to reflect changes in infrastructure and usage.

providers.name: nsave
providers.description: nsave provides individuals with personal multi‑currency accounts in USD, GBP and EUR that include real account details, ACH and wire information, and IBANs for SEPA. Users can receive payroll, invoices and other payments, send money to bank accounts or mobile wallets worldwide, and convert between the three currencies at real‑exchange rates with a transparent fee. The service is aimed at remote workers, freelancers and travelers who need cross‑border banking that traditional banks do not offer.

providers.name: NUnit
providers.description: NUnit is a unit-testing framework for all .NET languages. Initially ported from JUnit, the current production release has been completely rewritten with many new features and support for a wide range of .NET platforms. NUnit is a software testing framework, not a remote HTTP API service.

providers.name: OneHealthCompany
providers.description: The One Health Company is a Palo Alto veterinary precision-oncology company, best known for its FidoCure platform, that brings human-grade precision cancer medicine to dogs. FidoCure sequences a dog's tumor with next-generation DNA sequencing, matches the cancer-driving mutations to targeted therapies, and gives veterinarians an individualized treatment plan grounded in the world's largest proprietary canine cancer dataset (billions of data points across a network of more than 1,300 veterinary clinics). The company was founded in 2015 by Christina Lopes and Ben Lewis on the "One Health" thesis that treating cancer in companion dogs also advances real-world evidence for human oncology. It is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z bio), Y Combinator, Polaris Partners, Borealis Ventures, Lerer Hippeau and Tau Ventures. As of this profile the company exposes a consumer and veterinarian web experience (including a veterinarian login portal) but publishes no public developer API, SDK, or programmatic surface.

providers.name: OPC / 彼岸花开
providers.description: OPC / 彼岸花开 is a one-person company (OPC) operated by Lei Zhang in Hangzhou, China. Its agent-facing surface is a single A2A agent, "China On-Site Video Service": an agent (or a person) supplies a Google Maps link or coordinates for any place in China and Lei travels there and films about ten minutes of genuine, unscripted footage - streets, markets, temples, a family's old neighborhood - delivered by email as an MP4 for a fixed $50 USD (other requests at $50/hour, paid by Wise, Panda Remit or Remitly). The A2A agent card is served from the company's own domain at the legacy /.well-known/agent.json path and grades conformant against A2A 1.0.0; the JSON-RPC endpoint at /a2a/ is anonymous and live. It is an agent card in front of a human fulfilment service, not a software API: there is no OpenAPI, MCP server, SDK, developer documentation or developer signup. The site root hosts a separate login-gated Chinese consumer chat app (彼岸花开 · 花灵).

providers.name: Pallet
providers.description: Pallet builds an AI-powered logistics workforce: autonomous AI agents that automate supply chain operations for freight brokerages, freight forwarders, FTL and LTL carriers, warehouses, and shippers. Its agents handle end-to-end workflows from quoting through order entry, track-and-trace, billing, and customer service, integrating with existing TMS, WMS, email, and legacy applications. The Atlas product surfaces revenue opportunities across freight operations. Pallet is backed by Bain Capital Ventures and General Catalyst. No public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Placetel
providers.description: Placetel provides cloud-based telephone systems for businesses, offering features such as virtual phone numbers, call routing, voicemail, conferencing, and integrations with CRM tools. Their platform enables companies to manage communications over the internet with scalable, reliable services, supporting both domestic and international calling.

providers.name: Presto
providers.description: Presto Charging (Presto) is an electric-vehicle charging platform that aggregates access to 180,000+ public chargers across 20+ North American networks — including EVgo, ChargePoint, Blink, BP Pulse, and Flo — behind a single mobile app, payment method, and account. For drivers it offers price comparison, real-time charger availability, and a unified charging experience on iOS and Android. For fleets and enterprises it delivers charge management, granular usage data, and white-label products so operators can "manage charging like they manage fuel." For charging networks it drives utilization and station profitability. Presto exposes OCPI-compliant, mobile-first APIs and SDKs so fleet-solution and mobility partners can embed public charging — including Plug and Charge and Autocharge — under their own brand. Backed by Union Square Ventures.

providers.name: Quaise Energy
providers.description: Quaise Energy is a deep-geothermal energy company and MIT spinout, founded in 2018 by Carlos Araque and Matthew Houde out of a decade of millimeter-wave research by Paul Woskov at the MIT Plasma Science and Fusion Center. Quaise is developing millimeter-wave (MMW) drilling — using a gyrotron to vaporize rather than grind rock — to reach supercritical conditions several kilometers down, where temperatures approach 500 degrees C, and to convert existing fossil-fuel power stations to superhot geothermal baseload. The company drilled 100 meters with the technique at its Central Texas field site in 2025. Quaise is an energy and hardware company: it publishes no developer program, no public API, and no machine-readable API contract. Its only public web application is a levelized-cost-of-energy (LCOE) calculator whose full functionality sits behind an AWS Cognito login.

providers.name: Renovate
providers.description: Renovate is an Open Source, cross-platform dependency automation tool by Mend.io that automatically creates pull requests to keep software dependencies up to date. It supports over 90 package managers and language ecosystems including npm, PyPI, Maven, Docker, Helm, Go modules, Ruby Gems, NuGet, and more. Renovate runs as a CLI, Docker container, GitHub Action, or hosted cloud service (Mend Renovate App). It integrates with GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Azure DevOps, Gitea, Forgejo, and AWS CodeCommit. Configuration is done via a number of different locations in the repository: most commonly a `renovate.json` file in the repository root. The tool supports advanced scheduling, monorepo support, preset sharing, merge confidence scoring, and automatic replacement of deprecated packages.

providers.name: Rex
providers.description: Rex Inc, operating as Rex.fit (BabylonAI Inc.), is a Y Combinator (W23) health and fitness company building AI-powered, fully automated nutrition tracking. Its consumer products include Rex Nutribot, a WhatsApp AI nutrition coach; the Drop, a wearable AI camera pendant that detects meals and automatically logs calories, protein, carbs, and fats via computer vision; an AI body scanner; and personalized coaching with daily health reports. Rex also offers a white-label B2B nutrition-and-fitness AI that fitness chains and app builders integrate to add meal logging (photo, barcode, or text), recipe and meal-plan generation, workout logging, 3D body scans, and nutrition analytics under their own brand.

providers.name: Rivio
providers.description: Rivio provides an AI‑powered execution layer for procurement, helping enterprises automate sourcing, supplier management, and spend analytics. The platform combines machine‑learning insights with workflow automation to streamline purchasing decisions, reduce costs, and improve compliance across the supply chain. Backed by Gradient Ventures, Rivio targets B2B SaaS markets and integrates with ERP and finance systems.

providers.name: Rocket Lab
providers.description: Rocket Lab Corporation (Nasdaq RKLB) is an end-to-end space company providing launch services, spacecraft, satellite components, and on-orbit services. Its Electron rocket is the world's most frequently launched orbital small launch vehicle; the medium-lift Neutron rocket is in development. Rocket Lab Space Systems supplies Photon spacecraft, reaction wheels, star trackers, solar arrays, propulsion, separation systems, and composite structures to civil, national security, and commercial customers. Rocket Lab does not currently offer a public developer API.

providers.name: Sherpa
providers.description: Sherpa provides a travel requirements and eVisa platform that enables airlines, online travel agencies, and travel management companies to offer seamless eVisa services to their customers. The service aggregates visa information, automates application processes, and integrates with airline and OTA booking flows, helping travelers meet entry requirements quickly. Sherpa’s platform is trusted by leading airlines and travel brands worldwide.

providers.name: Silk Labs
providers.description: Silk Labs was an on-device artificial intelligence startup founded in 2015 by former Mozilla CTO Andreas Gal together with Chris Jones and Michael Vines, a team drawn from Mozilla's Firefox OS effort. The company's open-source Silk platform layered a Node.js runtime on Android so developers could build Internet of Things applications entirely in JavaScript, and it later shipped work on the "Sense" AI home camera focused on running real-time visual and audio recognition directly on the device. Silk Labs was backed by investors including 500 Global and was acquired by Apple in November 2018, after which it ceased independent operations; the silklabs.com domain is now parked on Apple nameservers. Its open-source Silk code, GitHub organization, and npm packages remain publicly available and are captured in this profile.

providers.name: Smile Digital Health
providers.description: Smile Digital Health (formerly Smile CDR) is a Toronto-based health interoperability software company and the commercial steward of the open source HAPI FHIR project (the world's most widely deployed Java implementation of the HL7 FHIR standard). Its flagship product, Smile CDR — marketed under the broader Smile Omni portfolio as the OmniVera Health Data Platform — is a FHIR-native clinical data repository and integration platform that ingests HL7 v2.x, CDA, CSV, JSON, XML, and FHIR payloads, normalizes them into FHIR (R4, R5, STU3, DSTU2), and exposes them through a hardened FHIR REST API, SMART on FHIR / OAuth2 / OIDC security, Bulk Data export, Subscriptions, MDM, Terminology Services, CQL-based Quality Measures, and a JSON Admin API. The platform is deployed on-prem and across AWS, Azure, and GCP, with HITRUST v9.4, SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, and ONC 2015 Edition certifications, and is used by 190+ global customers, including 30+ US payers running CMS Interoperability and Prior Authorization (CMS-0057-F) workloads on its CMS Suite. Adjacent Smile Omni product families include OmniCompli (regulatory compliance, including CMS Suite and CMS Concierge), OmniQ (digital quality measures / HEDIS, Intelligence Hub), and OmniConcierge (managed and professional services). The primary developer surface is the FHIR REST API, with per-endpoint auto-generated OpenAPI / Swagger UI at `{baseUrl}/swagger-ui/`, plus a separate JSON Admin API for cluster, module, user, audit, batch job, MDM, and OpenID Connect administration.

providers.name: Spring Health
providers.description: Spring Health is a New York City-based digital mental health company that sells a comprehensive mental healthcare benefit to employers, health plans, brokers, channel partners, and healthcare providers. Its platform combines a clinically validated assessment, AI-driven matching, and a curated provider network to deliver therapy, medication management, coaching, an Employee Assistance Program (EAP), critical-incident response, work-life services, and self-guided digital exercises through a unified member experience branded Spring Life. For health plans and providers, Spring Health offers Springworks — its enterprise care-coordination and care-management offering — alongside a generative-AI member-facing assistant called Guide and clinician-facing AI tooling. Customers include General Mills, Hearst, and Moda Health, and the company publishes outcomes, research, and ROI evidence on long-term cost savings of mental health benefits. Spring Health operates as a B2B2C benefit: it does not expose a public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or documented HTTP API. Integrations with HRIS, SSO, eligibility files, and health-plan partners are delivered through enterprise implementation rather than a self-service API, and its GitHub organization (github.com/SpringHealth) has no public repositories.

providers.name: Sprinto
providers.description: Sprinto is a security and compliance automation platform supporting SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, GDPR, PCI DSS, and more. Sprinto offers an API for building custom compliance and risk workflows; specific public reference docs are limited and require a customer login.

providers.name: Stepsize
providers.description: Stepsize AI provides automated Jira and Linear dashboards that generate themselves using AI. The platform offers AI‑generated reports, technical debt tracking, daily standup summaries, team sync updates, sprint and kanban reports, and executive summaries. It aims to keep software teams aligned by turning product development data into actionable insights, with a free first report and paid plans for deeper analytics. The company is backed by Crane Venture Partners and positioned as a tool for modern software engineering management.

providers.name: str8bat
providers.description: str8bat is a Bangalore, India based sports-technology company that builds a pocket-sized IoT sensor which attaches to a cricket bat and captures batting metrics in real time — bat speed, impact speed, back-lift angle, timing, sweet-spot placement and a 360-degree view of every shot. The sensor pairs with the str8bat mobile app (iOS and Android) to deliver instant, visual and actionable insights plus an AI cricket coach. The company reports 30,000+ active users, 6+ million shots recorded and operations across 350+ Indian cities and 14+ countries. str8bat is a consumer hardware and mobile-app company and publishes no first-party developer API; its str8bat.com storefront runs on Shopify, which exposes standard commerce discovery surfaces (customer-account OIDC and a Universal Commerce Protocol agent-commerce MCP endpoint).

providers.name: Swypex
providers.description: Swypex is an Egyptian fintech, founded in 2022 and headquartered at Smart Village in Cairo, that provides an all-in-one financial management platform for businesses. The platform bundles corporate cards, payments, invoice management, and working capital financing into one system, giving finance teams real-time visibility and control over company spend. Swypex launched Egypt's first approval-based corporate card, where each transaction's limit unlocks only after real-time review and approval by the company's finance team, and offers e-invoicing (with an Odoo integration) and Swypextend working-capital financing. Swypex is licensed by the Central Bank of Egypt and operates its card program in partnership with Visa and Mashreq Bank. It raised a $4M seed round led by Accel (Accel's first fintech investment in MENA), with Foundation Ventures and Raba Partnership. Swypex does not publish a public developer API; its products are delivered through web and mobile apps plus a small set of native integrations (Odoo, e-invoicing, Just2Pay).

providers.name: TraceLLM
providers.description: TraceLLM is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: g2-catalog) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.

providers.name: Trim
providers.description: Trim is a consumer fintech company founded in 2015 that built an automated personal finance assistant which finds and cancels unwanted subscriptions, negotiates bills such as cable and internet, and automates savings for its users. Trim was backed by Version One Ventures and was acquired by OneMain Financial; its former asktrim.com home now redirects to OneMain MyMoney (onemainmymoney.com), where the product lives on as a personalized money insights and expense tracking app. Trim/MyMoney is a consumer application and does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Udacity
providers.description: Udacity is an online tech-upskilling platform offering project-based Nanodegree programs, individual courses, and enterprise workforce development across Artificial Intelligence, Generative AI, Agentic AI, Data Science, Cloud Computing, Cybersecurity, Programming, Autonomous Systems, Product Management, and DevOps. Founded by Sebastian Thrun out of the Stanford CS221 free online AI course in 2011, Udacity pioneered the Nanodegree credential and partnered with industry leaders (AWS, Google, Meta, Microsoft, NVIDIA, Mercedes-Benz) to co-develop curriculum. In 2024 Accenture acquired Udacity for approximately $1B and folded the platform into LearnVantage, Accenture's enterprise learning and skilling business. Udacity reports 25M+ learners globally and remains best known for its Self-Driving Car, Deep Learning, and Generative AI Nanodegrees, with hands-on projects reviewed by human mentors and career services. Udacity does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal — enterprise customers integrate via Accenture LearnVantage sales channels rather than self-service APIs. Its public GitHub organization (github.com/udacity) hosts 1,100+ open-source classroom and course-content repositories (e.g. deep-learning-v2-pytorch, self-driving-car, cd13303-genai-c1-classroom) used as Nanodegree exercises, not as official platform APIs.

providers.name: UnifiedCRM
providers.description: UnifiedCRM is a Seedcamp-backed startup (2023 investment) building a unified sales hub for remote and hybrid teams — an AI-assisted CRM delivered as a web app and PWA at unifiedcrm.ai, with features observed in the application such as email processing, deal summarization, contact and company enrichment, and automated web research. The company currently publishes no public developer API, documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable specifications.

providers.name: Vroozi
providers.description: Vroozi provides an intelligent procure-to-pay platform that automates purchasing, invoice processing, and supplier collaboration. Their cloud‑based solution integrates with ERP systems like SAP, Oracle, NetSuite, and Microsoft Dynamics, offering features such as punch‑out catalogs, spend analytics, and a trusted supplier network. Vroozi aims to simplify procurement workflows, reduce manual effort, and deliver actionable insights for smarter spend management across enterprises.

providers.name: Wallet Studio
providers.description: Wallet Studio, built by Miss Moneypenny Technologies GmbH, is a no-code SaaS platform for creating, deploying, and managing Apple Wallet and Google Wallet passes. Aimed primarily at insurance carriers, it turns policy administration, claims, and CRM systems into wallet-based customer engagement channels reaching the four billion people who already carry a digital wallet, without replacing existing backend infrastructure. The platform offers visual pass editors with one-click publishing, prebuilt insurance templates, integrated automation, a REST API and webhooks for connecting to third-party systems, and authenticated links to portals and value-added services. Hosting is GDPR-compliant and the company describes the platform as certified for enterprise security standards. Backed by Earlybird, the company raised roughly EUR 7 million in 2025. There is no public developer portal, API reference, or OpenAPI specification; the REST API is provisioned per customer.

providers.name: World Data API
providers.description: World Data API provides a comprehensive suite of global data endpoints covering countries, regions, cities, currencies, languages, timezones, airports, airlines, holidays, and premium astronomy, business days, and travel data. The platform offers RESTful JSON APIs with extensive documentation, quickstart guides, authentication via API keys, and a developer portal for testing. It serves developers, businesses, and researchers needing reliable geographic and temporal data for applications, analytics, and integration.

providers.name: Zoox
providers.description: Zoox is an Amazon subsidiary developing a purpose-built, bidirectional, symmetrical robotaxi vehicle designed from the ground up for autonomous ride-hailing rather than retrofitted from a conventional car. The vehicle carries up to four riders in a carriage-style seating layout, has no steering wheel or pedals, and is engineered for dense urban operation. Zoox provides the autonomous driving stack, the vehicle hardware, and a consumer ride-hail app. Commercial robotaxi service has launched in Las Vegas and San Francisco, with expansion announced for Austin, Miami, Atlanta, and Los Angeles. Acquired by Amazon in 2020, Zoox does not publish a public developer API or open research dataset; its public surface is product, ride-experience, and safety content. This profile captures the company surface for API Evangelist reference.

providers.name: Acturis
providers.description: Acturis is a United Kingdom insurance software company founded in 2000 by David McDonald and Theo Duchen, operating the UK's leading multi-tenant SaaS platform for general insurance brokers, insurers and MGAs. The Acturis system covers commercial and personal lines broking, e-trade and digital distribution, policy administration, claims, document management, premium finance and accounting, and it builds and runs eight of the top ten UK insurer extranets. Acturis Group extends the platform into Germany, France and Canada (through the acquisitions of Power Broker and Brovada) and reports over 100,000 users across more than 40 countries. Its API posture is partner-gated and honestly not developer-facing: acturis.com markets an "API-enabled platform" and "API capabilities" but publishes no developer portal, no API reference, no OpenAPI or Swagger definition, and no self-serve onboarding. developer.acturis.com, developers.acturis.com, docs.acturis.com and api.acturis.com do not resolve, and /developers, /api, /developer and /integrations all return 404. Real integration happens through commercial agreements — insurer extranet and e-trade connections, the Polaris imarket digital-trading standards Acturis has traded on since 2005, and named bilateral work such as the Aviva claims Broker API launched in December 2024, which brokers enable through an Aviva Claims Service Manager or an Acturis Account Manager rather than through any public signup.

providers.name: Allcams
providers.description: Allcams is an adult live cam aggregator that indexes streams from multiple adult cam platforms, providing a unified searchable directory without hosting any content itself. The site offers age‑verification compliance, affiliate disclosures, and earns commission via referral links. It maintains legal compliance with U.S. 2257 record‑keeping, GDPR and CCPA, and provides a developer MCP server for AI agents. Allcams aims to keep listings honest by removing dead or duplicate entries and supporting multiple languages.

providers.name: Almured
providers.description: Almured provides an open agent-to-agent knowledge network that connects AI models and protocols across a decentralized platform. It enables agents to query expertise from a community of specialized agents, supporting multiple models like Claude, GPT, and Gemini, and protocols such as MCP, A2A, and REST. The service offers features like portable reputation, data export, and privacy controls, and is designed for quick, collaborative problem solving across diverse AI tools.

providers.name: Alwans
providers.description: Alwans, operating under the brand Foodics, provides a comprehensive cloud‑based restaurant management platform that streamlines point‑of‑sale, inventory, staff scheduling, and analytics for food‑service businesses. Founded in 2014 and backed by prominent investors, the company serves thousands of restaurants across the Middle East and beyond, offering integrations with payment gateways, delivery services, and third‑party apps. Their API enables developers to build custom extensions, retrieve sales data, manage menus, and automate operational workflows, fostering a vibrant ecosystem of partners and developers.

providers.name: AnswersNow
providers.description: AnswersNow is a virtual Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA) therapy provider for individuals with autism, delivering personalized, evidence-based care from board-certified behavior analysts (BCBAs) through its proprietary telehealth platform. Families access one-on-one therapy sessions, caregiver and parent training, and individualized treatment plans remotely, expanding access to ABA care in areas with limited in-person availability. AnswersNow accepts major insurance carriers including Medicaid, is BHCOE accredited and a CASP member organization, and was surfaced to the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio company. This profile has been enriched with company identity and domain-security posture; AnswersNow publishes a consumer web application (web.getanswersnow.com) but no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Associated Bank
providers.description: Associated Bank, N.A. is the primary banking subsidiary of Associated Banc-Corp (NYSE ASB), a nationally chartered commercial bank and the largest bank holding company headquartered in Wisconsin, based in Green Bay. With roughly $50 billion in total assets following the April 2026 acquisition of American National Corporation, Associated operates a full-service Midwest banking franchise of more than 200 locations across Wisconsin, Illinois, Iowa, Minnesota, Missouri and Nebraska, offering consumer, business, commercial and wealth-management services. Associated does not publish a first-party public developer portal or downloadable OpenAPI/Swagger specifications. Its digital banking runs on a core-provider stack (Jack Henry), and consumer-permissioned data access is delivered through third-party aggregators (Plaid, Tink/TrueLayer) rather than a direct first-party API. Its commercial treasury customers use the login-gated Associated Connect platform. No FDX participation or CFPB Section 1033 data-access posture is publicly documented as of this review.

providers.name: ATX Granite King
providers.description: ATX Granite King provides granite, quartz, and quartzite countertop services in Austin and Central Texas. Customers select from a live inventory of 299 slabs, which are templated, fabricated, and installed by the crew, with sink installation included. The company emphasizes flat, honest pricing per square foot and offers both standard and large‑scale projects.

providers.name: Avenue One
providers.description: Avenue One is a New York-based technology service platform and investment marketplace for institutional owners, buyers, sellers, lenders and borrowers of residential rental real estate. Founded in 2020, it connects institutional debt and equity capital to local operating partners and property owners across 21+ U.S. markets, combining proprietary property data, automated valuation, and a vetted partner network to find, finance, buy, renovate, lease, manage and sell single-family rental homes at scale. Its service lines span lending (bridge and SFR portfolio loans), strategy development, acquisitions, renovations, asset management, title and brokerage or dispositions. The company reports $2.2B+ of capital deployed. Its software runs as a private, login-gated product suite ("AvenueOS") for internal, builder, investor and partner users; no public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable contract is published.

providers.name: Ayebot
providers.description: Ayebot is an AI-powered business broker and deal engine for sell-side M&A in Singapore and Southeast Asia. It maps the buyer market, runs the process at machine speed, and keeps every number traceable. The judgement stays with the adviser. The platform is built by Aye Bot Pte. Ltd., offering AI-driven valuation, buyer matching, and advisory services to founders seeking exits.

providers.name: Beengo
providers.description: Beengo operates as Appfront (appfront.ai), an all-in-one restaurant engagement and eCommerce platform backed by 500 Global. The platform gives restaurants branded online ordering, dine-in scan-and-pay, loyalty and CRM, SMS/push/email marketing campaigns, gift cards and payments, branded native iOS/Android apps, and data analytics. It integrates with major point-of-sale systems (Toast, Revel, SpeedLine, Square, Clover, PAR/Brink, Oracle Hospitality MICROS, NCR) and third-party delivery (DoorDash, Postmates). No public developer program, OpenAPI, or API documentation is published at this time; this profile captures the company identity, web properties, and probed domain security posture.

providers.name: Befana
providers.description: Befana Gifting is a web‑based gifting platform that enables users to create, manage, and send personalized gifts. The application provides a gift workspace where users can organize orders, view pending gifts, and send gift references. Built on Vercel, the service offers a clean, browser‑based interface for gifting workflows and integrates with modern web technologies. While the site is primarily a single‑page app, it presents core gifting features without requiring account creation for browsing.

providers.name: Betr364d
providers.description: Betr is the world’s first real money gaming super app, offering daily fantasy, social sportsbook, social casino, and arcade experiences. Users can download the app to participate in real‑money gaming across a variety of sports and games, with high‑payout potential and a social community. The platform emphasizes responsible gaming and provides extensive help resources.

providers.name: Bitcoin.de
providers.description: Bitcoin.de is a German cryptocurrency exchange and marketplace offering buying, selling, and trading of Bitcoin and other digital assets. It provides a platform for users to manage crypto portfolios, access price data, and utilize P2P trading services. The company operates under regulatory oversight in Germany and aims to make cryptocurrency accessible to a broad audience.

providers.name: Blackboard
providers.description: Blackboard (now part of Anthology) provides Blackboard Learn LMS plus the Anthology product suite (Ally, Student). The Anthology Developer portal exposes REST APIs for Learn, Ally, and Student, with versions across the 3200, 3900, and 4000 series and ongoing backward compatibility.

providers.name: BloomNation
providers.description: BloomNation is a flower-delivery marketplace that connects consumers with independent local florists for same-day and next-day delivery of handcrafted floral arrangements across 40+ U.S. cities and the UK. Customers shop florist-designed bouquets for occasions such as birthdays, anniversaries, sympathy, and get-well, then pay with credit cards, Apple Pay, Google Pay, Amazon Pay, or Afterpay. Distinctive features include BloomSnap photo delivery confirmation and video message cards. BloomNation also runs a florist-facing SaaS side (point-of-sale, website, and order management, now part of Promenade) that powers member shops. This profile was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company; no public developer API or documentation program was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Certivity
providers.description: Certivity is a Munich-based RegTech company, founded in 2021, that operates an AI-native regulatory intelligence platform for regulated industries such as automotive, aerospace, and connected vehicles. Its product, Certivity Core, turns complex regulations, standards, and internal documents into structured, machine-readable, engineering-ready requirements with full traceability and real-time monitoring of legal changes across 50+ jurisdictions. The platform digitizes and structures regulatory content from publishers such as ISO, IEC, CEN, CENELEC, ASTM, UL, and SAE using a proprietary ingestion pipeline and a regulatory knowledge graph, and integrates directly into engineering workflows (including Jama Connect) via an official API. Backed by Earlybird, High-Tech Gruenderfonds, UVC Partners, and Almaz Capital, Certivity added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile and enrichment lead.

providers.name: Checkerspot
providers.description: Checkerspot is an Alameda, California biotechnology company, founded in 2016 and incorporated as a Public Benefit Corporation, that designs and produces functional fats and oils through precision fermentation of microalgae. Its biology-driven molecule licensing platform pairs algal strain development, an advanced analytical platform, bioinformatics, high-throughput screening, fermentation scale-up and downstream oil refining, built around the proprietary microbe Prototheca moriformis, which the company reports reaches over 80% oil content by dry cell weight. The commercial molecule portfolio includes a high sn-2 palmitate algal oil that mimics the triglyceride structure of human milk fat for infant nutrition, an Omega-7 (palmitoleic acid) algal oil, a designer high-oleic tropical-fat alternative to palm oil, and Algolein tG C18/80 for cosmetic formulation; earlier work commercialized algae-derived urethane composites through the WNDR Alpine outdoor brand. Checkerspot works through ingredient and manufacturing partners including AAK, Huvepharma and La Fabrique Vegetale, and closed a USD 55 million Series C led by ArrowMark Partners with participation from Cox Enterprises. It is a business-to-business ingredient and molecule licensing company rather than a software vendor: it operates a WordPress marketing site, publishes no developer portal, no API documentation, no SDK and no machine-readable API contract, and has no GitHub organization.

providers.name: Chegg
providers.description: Chegg is an American education technology company that provides direct-to-student learning services, including 24/7 homework and expert Q&A help, step-by-step textbook solutions, practice questions, and writing, grammar, and citation tools. Founded in 2005 and headquartered in Santa Clara, California, Chegg began as a textbook-rental marketplace and expanded into a subscription study-support platform (Chegg Study, Chegg Writing, Chegg Math Solver) plus tutoring and skills offerings. Chegg operates as a consumer web/mobile product rather than a developer platform: it exposes no public developer portal, published API, or SDKs at this time. Its public technical surface is limited to a coordinated vulnerability disclosure program on HackerOne and standard web security/policy pages. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Kleiner Perkins and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: China Southern Air Logistics
providers.description: China Southern Air Logistics Co., Ltd. (南航物流, CSAL) is the air cargo and logistics arm of China Southern Airlines, established in December 2018 and headquartered in Guangzhou. It combines the airline's freighter fleet with passenger belly capacity into an integrated air logistics network, and sells express (CZ Speed), standard, special cargo, whole-aircraft charter, intermodal truck and door-to-door products through its Tang (唐翼) online cargo system at cargo.csair.com, where agents and shippers book capacity, query freight rates, track air waybills, manage dangerous-goods accounts and request invoices. As of this profile the company publishes no developer program, no public API reference and no machine-readable specification; system-to-system integration is arranged bilaterally with agents and forwarders.

providers.name: Chronograph
providers.description: Chronograph provides cloud‑based portfolio monitoring, analytics, data management and reporting solutions for private equity and other private capital investors. Their platform automates data collection, valuation, ESG tracking and API connectivity, enabling limited and general partners to streamline portfolio oversight and investor communications.

providers.name: Cino
providers.description: Cino (getcino.com) is a European consumer fintech that offers the first shared virtual card that splits and pays a group bill at the same time. Members connect their existing debit or credit cards, create a group with configurable split ratios, and each person is charged only their proportional share at the moment of payment with no pre-funding required. The shared card works online and in person for one-off or recurring expenses, integrates with Apple Pay and Google Pay, supports per-transaction and monthly spending limits, and positions itself as a replacement for bill-splitting tools like Splitwise, Tricount, PayPal, and Tikkie. Cino is available across 29 European countries and is a portfolio company of Balderton Capital. This is a consumer mobile app with no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Clarity
providers.description: Clarity provides AI‑powered meeting transcription and note‑taking software that captures every detail of conversations, automatically generates follow‑up emails, action items, and insights. The platform integrates with popular CRMs, Slack, and email, offering customizable templates to extract targeted information from calls. Designed for sales, product, fundraising, recruiting, and other teams, Clarity helps users stay engaged during meetings while the AI records and organizes content, ensuring no important point is missed.

providers.name: Clearing
providers.description: Clearing (WTUK Limited trading as Clearing) is a cross-border financial infrastructure provider offering multi-currency accounts, global payments, cross-currency liquidity, and digital-asset settlement to businesses operating internationally. It is a regulated electronic money institution: authorised by the UK FCA under the Electronic Money Regulations (ref 900536), licensed by the Monetary Authority of Singapore as a Major Payments Institution (PS20200445), and registered with FINTRAC in Canada. This record was surfaced as a stub via VC-portfolio tagging (sector originally recorded as healthcare); on enrichment the clearing.com domain resolves to this fintech/payments company, and no public developer API surface was found.

providers.name: dopay
providers.description: dopay is a digital payroll platform operating in Egypt that lets employers register employees and disburse salaries in minutes through a single system, including permanent, temporary, and seasonal workers across construction, agriculture, hospitality, retail, healthcare, education, and manufacturing. Supervised by a bank and regulated by the Central Bank of Egypt, dopay digitizes cash-based wage payments and pairs core Salary Disbursement with an Early Pay earned-wage-access product that lets employees withdraw part of their salary before payday. Originally a Techstars-backed fintech focused on banking the unbanked, dopay is added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it publishes a business web app and login but no public developer API, portal, or documentation at this time.

providers.name: EaseCentral
providers.description: EaseCentral provides an employee benefits administration platform designed for insurance brokers and employers. The web‑based solution enables online enrollment, benefits plan management, compliance tools, and HR resources, serving thousands of businesses across the United States. It integrates with payroll, offers document libraries, and supports multi‑employer portals, aiming to simplify benefits administration for modern broker workflows.

providers.name: ECPRO
providers.description: ECPRO 電商博士, founded by 林克威, provides Taiwan website real‑price registration and the nation’s first e‑commerce media platform. It aggregates public website data, offering transparent insights into e‑commerce platforms, payment systems, advertising pixels, traffic, and company registration details. Users can query site technology stacks, compare competitors, and access free tools, reports, and AI‑assisted analysis, all aimed at making Taiwan’s e‑commerce landscape openly understandable.

providers.name: Enclave
providers.description: Enclave (enclave.ai) is an AI-powered application and cloud security platform that operates as an "agentic security engineer." It continuously builds a living model of an organization's attack surface across services and cloud providers, then autonomously triages and investigates vulnerability findings against known CVEs to determine real-world exploitability and reachability. Rather than flooding teams with signature-based noise, Enclave traces data flows to confirm whether a CVE is actually reachable, surfaces cross-service exploits that traditional scanners miss, and routes prioritized remediation plans with proof to the owning teams. Founded by veterans from Stripe, Box, VMware, Salesforce, and Yelp, the company is backed by 8VC and Marc Benioff. Added to the API Evangelist network and enriched from the company's public web surface; no public developer API is currently published.

providers.name: Exsited
providers.description: Exsited is a technology company that provides a platform for managing and optimizing digital experiences. The company focuses on delivering robust API solutions that enable businesses to integrate, automate, and scale their services efficiently. Exsited offers comprehensive documentation, developer tools, and support resources to facilitate seamless integration for developers and enterprises alike. Their mission is to empower organizations to innovate faster by providing reliable, secure, and well‑documented APIs that drive digital transformation across various industries.

providers.name: Extensity
providers.description: ExtensityAI is an AI research company building trustworthy, verifiable AI for enterprise environments through a neurosymbolic architecture that combines large language models with symbolic validation and knowledge-graph reasoning. Its flagship open-source framework, SymbolicAI, treats LLMs as programmable, differentiable primitives (Symbol objects) governed by Design-by-Contract validation, giving developers source-traceable, contract-enforced AI they can run on-premise with sovereign data control. The company also ships developer tooling including the ontoloom MCP server for building and exploring OWL 2 ontologies with AI agents. Backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners.

providers.name: EyeLights
providers.description: EyeLights is a French deep-tech company building augmented reality head-up display (HUD) technology for riders and pilots.
