providers.description: Desjardins Group (Mouvement Desjardins) is the largest cooperative financial group in North America, founded in 1900 in Lévis, Quebec by Alphonse Desjardins. It is a federation of caisses populaires (member-owned credit unions) rather than a share-capital chartered bank, comprising the Fédération des caisses Desjardins du Québec and its subsidiaries, the caisses in Quebec and the Caisse Desjardins Ontario Credit Union, regulated in Quebec by the Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF). It holds roughly CAD $470 billion in assets and serves more than 7.8 million members and clients with personal, business, wealth-management and insurance products. On open finance, Desjardins publishes no first-party public developer portal or downloadable API specification; developer.desjardins.com and other API-portal subdomains do not resolve, and consumer financial-data access is delivered today through third-party aggregators (Flinks, Plaid, Finicity, Tink) via screen-scraping/aggregator connectivity rather than a documented Desjardins API. Canada's Consumer-Driven Banking (open-banking) framework is legislated (Budget 2024/2025, overseen by the FCAC) but not yet operational; as a cooperative outside the Big Six, Desjardins may opt in to Phase 1 rather than being mandated.

providers.name: DZPage
providers.description: DZPage provides a comprehensive DayZ item database, interactive loot maps, a 3D map, and tools such as XML editors. All data is sourced directly from the real game files, offering over 4,700 items with detailed weapon stats, loot locations, and server tools. The platform also offers a free open REST API for developers to integrate DayZ data into their applications, without requiring accounts or paywalls.

providers.name: Ello
providers.description: Ello is a public-benefit AI education company building a 1:1 AI reading and math tutor for children ages 4-9. Its consumer app pairs proprietary child-speech recognition (trained on 100K+ hours of kids' audio) with generative AI and adaptive teaching agents to deliver personalized, sub-second, voice-based reading instruction grounded in the Science of Reading, plus a large catalog of leveled e-books, a "Storytime" create-your-own story feature, and parent progress reports. Recognized as one of TIME's Best Inventions of 2024 and backed by Y Combinator, Goodwater, Project A, and Homebrew, Ello is a consumer (B2C) product with no public developer API program at this time.

providers.name: Emeritus
providers.description: Emeritus is a global online education company that partners with more than 80 premier universities — including Wharton, MIT, Columbia, Harvard, Kellogg, and UC Berkeley — to deliver outcome-based executive education, professional certificates, and skill-development programs to over 500,000 learners worldwide. It operates across individual learners, enterprise/corporate training, and university-branded partnership programs, spanning topics such as AI and machine learning, data science, finance, leadership, and digital transformation through instructor-led online and blended formats. Emeritus is backed by Accel and the SoftBank Vision Fund. This profile was surfaced as a VC portfolio lead and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Emeritus publishes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Emtethal
providers.description: Emtethal is a Riyadh, Saudi Arabia based smart compliance and inspection management platform for the food service and hospitality sectors, backed by 500 Global. The platform automates inspection scheduling and distribution, provides custom checklists per facility type, captures photo documentation with automatic timestamps and GPS location, detects and categorizes violations automatically, and pushes real-time alerts for critical issues. It layers analytics and compliance reporting on top of an offline-capable mobile field-inspection app (iOS and Android) and AI-powered camera and sensor monitoring. Emtethal serves both individual food facilities and consulting firms managing multiple client sites, offering a 14-day free trial. There is no public API, developer portal, or documented developer surface at this time; this profile is an API Evangelist company lead maintained for enrichment and monitoring.

providers.name: Ent
providers.description: Ent is an intent-aware security platform for the enterprise that protects work as it happens. The company reads human, AI agent, and application activity in real time to understand intent and act at the moment of risk, rather than relying on after-the-fact logs and static policies. Ent is an early-stage security company backed by Felicis and surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; this profile captures its public web, legal, and security-disclosure surface. No public API, developer portal, SDKs, or OpenAPI have been published to date, so API and specification artifacts are not yet applicable.

providers.name: Glass Health
providers.description: Glass Health is a San Francisco-based clinical AI company founded in 2021 by Dereck Paul (CEO) and Graham Ramsey (Head of Product) that builds an AI clinical decision support (CDS) and ambient scribing co-pilot for physicians, nurse practitioners, physician assistants, residents, and medical students. The Glass platform combines large language model reasoning with curated, physician-reviewed clinical guidelines to generate ranked differential diagnoses, evidence-based assessment and plans, chart summaries, and direct answers to clinical questions ("Consult"), all delivered with inline citations. Glass also provides ambient scribing that listens during patient encounters and generates History and Physical notes, progress notes, discharge summaries, and patient-facing instructions, plus EHR integration via SMART on FHIR to pull demographics, problem lists, medications, laboratory values, vital signs, imaging, and encounter data into the workflow. Glass offers a tiered SaaS plan (Lite free tier, Starter at $20/month, Pro at $90/month, Max at $200/month) along with iOS and Android apps, and a public Glass Developer API ($250/month minimum, token-metered beyond the floor) that exposes the same clinical AI agent — Consult, Differential Diagnosis, Assessment and Plan, and Scribing endpoints — for third-party healthcare products. Glass is backed by Breyer Capital and graduated from Y Combinator's W23 batch, with roughly $6.5M in total disclosed funding. The provider does not publish an open OpenAPI specification or open-source SDKs; integration details are gated behind the developer portal and an enterprise contact at enterprise@glass.health.

providers.name: Glen
providers.description: Glen is a Y Combinator (Summer 2026) startup building a shared organizational learning and memory system for fleets of AI agents. The platform acts as a centralized store that every AI agent in a company can read from and write to, so that when one agent learns something the whole organization gains access to it. Glen preserves decisions, customer insights and operational procedures with full audit trails, applies role-based access control per observation at recall time, and connects to coding agents, PR assistants, bug bots and sales agents over the Model Context Protocol (MCP). It integrates with the tools where work already lives (code repositories, pull requests, issues, documentation and meetings) to give both agents and humans unified organizational context, aiming to eliminate knowledge silos, reduce new-hire ramp time and retain institutional knowledge through employee turnover. The company is pre-launch and operating a waitlist; its primary integration surface is an MCP server rather than a traditional REST API.

providers.name: Goose Insurance
providers.description: Goose Insurance Services Inc. is a Vancouver, British Columbia based digital insurance distributor — an app-first licensed agency and MGA rather than a carrier — that sells travel medical, Visitors to Canada, term life, whole life, final expense, critical illness, accidental death and dismemberment, hospital cash, kids and renters coverage through the Goose mobile "insurance super app". Founded in 2017 and licensed in British Columbia, Alberta, Saskatchewan, Manitoba, Ontario, Quebec (AMF firm registration 603913), New Brunswick and Nova Scotia, Goose underwrites nothing itself: every policy is placed with a partner carrier including AIG Canada, iA Financial Group, TuGo, IMG, MSH, American-Amicable, Teachers Life, Lloyd's of London and Sutton National. Its home market is Canada, with a US launch in 2020, and it sits in the thin digital-broker layer beneath the Big-Few Canadian oligopoly alongside Zensurance and APOLLO. Goose's API posture is closed: as of the 2026-07-25 review there is no public developer portal, no self-serve API documentation, no downloadable OpenAPI or Swagger, and no published ACORD, AL3 or agency-management-system integration. The only host that answers on the api. subdomain is a private Heroku-backed mobile-app backend that returns 404 at every probed path, and the only partner surfaces the company publishes are a marketing affiliate/referral program and a carrier-relationships page — quote, bind, issue and FNOL are all consumer-facing inside the app only.

providers.name: Icon Source
providers.description: Icon Source is a Denver, Colorado marketplace that connects brands, marketing agencies and universities with professional and college athletes for endorsement, appearance, speaking and social-media deals, including Name, Image and Likeness (NIL) engagements. Founded in 2018 by Chase Garrett, the platform lets brands search and filter verified athletes by location, interest, rate, audience size and demographics, build and send contracts, and pay athletes in-platform, charging a 10% transaction fee on each deal that is signed and closed. A companion product, Icon Suite (launched March 2022), gives universities NIL disclosure and compliance tooling. Icon Source is delivered strictly as an end-user product — a web application at prod.iconsource.app plus iOS and Android apps — and publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal or machine-readable contract of any kind.

providers.name: Jarmin
providers.description: Jarmin is a Y Combinator-backed company building autonomous "AI employees" for technical and operational roles — ML engineers, financial analysts, account executives, compliance analysts, data analysts, project managers, and paralegals. Rather than a single chatbot, Jarmin operates a system of proprietary agents, models, and automations that learn a role's responsibilities, connect to a company's internal systems and data sources, experiment with approaches, and run end-to-end workflows autonomously (with optional human approval at key decision points). For ML work this spans domain-specific feature engineering, model selection under constraints, hyperparameter optimization, and deploying production pipelines. Founded by engineers from Meta, Apple, AWS, Lockheed Martin, and JPMorgan Chase, Jarmin targets investment banking, fintech, and legal verticals. This profile was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio lead; at enrichment time Jarmin publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation surface.

providers.name: Kheiron Medical Technologies
providers.description: Kheiron Medical Technologies is a London-founded medical-imaging AI company best known for Mia (Mammography Intelligent Assessment), a deep-learning solution that supports radiologists in breast-cancer screening as an independent, concurrent, or triage reader. Founded in 2016 and backed by investors including Atomico, Kheiron now operates as part of RadNet's DeepHealth, whose portfolio spans breast, prostate, lung, brain, and thyroid imaging plus the Diagnostic, Operations, and TechLive suites. This API Evangelist profile tracks Kheiron/DeepHealth as a health-AI provider; the company exposes clinical products and enterprise integrations rather than a public self-serve developer API, so most machine-readable API artifacts are not applicable and this record captures its identity, security, and legal surface.

providers.name: Kinside
providers.description: Kinside is a modern child care marketplace that connects families with licensed child care providers by surfacing real-time availability across thousands of providers, helping parents find care in minutes rather than months. Beyond the consumer marketplace, Kinside serves child care providers with enrollment and scheduling tools, employers with child care benefit programs, and government agencies seeking community child care supply-and-demand data. Backed by Initialized Capital and Techstars, the company operates alongside UrbanSitter in the family-care benefits space. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network from venture-portfolio discovery; Kinside does not publish a public developer portal or API at this time, so this entry captures its public web, security, and identity surface.

providers.name: KLA
providers.description: KLA Corporation (formerly KLA-Tencor) is a leader in process control and process-enabling solutions for manufacturing wafers and reticles, integrated circuits, packaging, printed circuit boards and flat panel displays. KLA delivers advanced inspection tools, metrology systems, and computational analytics for the semiconductor industry. KLA does not publish a public developer portal or open API program; customer-facing software and tool APIs are provided to KLA customers under contract and are not publicly available.

providers.name: Layer
providers.description: Layer is a living digital art platform that curates code-based generative artwork and ultra-high-resolution video art for everyday display. Its developer surface is an artist-facing, first-party TypeScript SDK (a browser global, $layer) that lets creators declare customizable parameters, register a canvas for screenshot capture, and supply generated video previews back to Layer Studio, alongside published guidelines for generative and Ultra Res artwork. Layer is a portfolio company of Bloomberg Beta and Emergence Capital, added to the API Evangelist network and enriched from its public developer documentation. Layer exposes a client-side SDK rather than a public REST/HTTP API.

providers.name: Legora
providers.description: Legora is a Stockholm- and London-based legal AI company (formerly Leya) building a collaborative AI workspace for lawyers. The platform is centered on Legora aOS, an agentic operating system that connects information, communication, and the execution of legal work across Agent, Monitors, Lists, Legal Research, Tabular Review, Workflows, and the client-facing Portal, with Word and Outlook add-ins, an Editor, and a mobile app. Legora is sold to elite law firms and in-house legal teams via enterprise contracts; customers include Mannheimer Swartling, Goodwin Procter, Cleary Gottlieb, Linklaters, Bird & Bird, and HWL Ebsworth, with 400+ firms across 40+ countries. There is no public, self-serve developer API, SDK, or open-source release; integrations are arranged through enterprise sales and partnership engagements, and the platform runs on Azure OpenAI Service with SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, ISO 42001, GDPR, and HIPAA controls.

providers.name: Linguatrip
providers.description: Linguatrip is a language-education and language-travel company founded in 2014 and backed by 500 Global. It operates two connected businesses: a booking marketplace for accredited language schools abroad — covering course selection, accommodation, airport transfers and visa support across countries including the United Kingdom, Malta and the United Arab Emirates — and its own online English school offering 25+ self-paced courses, one-to-one tutoring, speaking clubs and exam preparation for IELTS, TOEFL, GMAT, GRE and SAT. It also provides higher-education placement consulting for US, UK and Canadian universities. Linguatrip publishes no public API, developer portal or SDKs; its surfaces are consumer web properties in four languages with pricing in 18 currencies.

providers.name: Linkett
providers.description: Linkett is a digital out-of-home (DOOH) analytics platform for digital signage and retail displays. A proprietary WiFi sensor mounted at the screen passively gathers audience data from nearby smartphones with no app required, and a hosted dashboard reports real-time campaign performance metrics such as impressions, dwell time, frequency and conversion rate, alongside demographic and behavioural insight, giving advertising agencies detailed client reporting and giving advertisers measurement they can tie back to return on ad spend. Linkett is a WestonExpressions Inc. company with offices in Toronto, Ontario and Mountain View, California, says it is used by 100+ digital out-of-home networks, and was surfaced through the 500 Global portfolio. It sells self-serve at $25 and $50 per month plus a one-time $130 hardware fee, with custom integrations offered only on a contact-sales enterprise tier. As of this enrichment pass Linkett publishes no public developer portal, API reference, SDK, or machine-readable API specification on any host it controls, and its marketing site is served behind a bot/CAPTCHA challenge that blocks automated retrieval of every path.

providers.name: Marker
providers.description: Marker is a writing tool for people who believe in writing — a calm, focused space for thinking and writing that acts as your partner and editor from first idea to final draft. Backed by Index Ventures, Marker sits in the future-of-work space and offers a distraction-free web application (my.marker.page) for drafting long-form writing. It is a consumer product web app: as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer API, SDKs, developer documentation, or /.well-known discovery surface, so this profile captures its identity and a live domain-security probe only.

providers.name: Minersai
providers.description: MinersAI applies artificial intelligence and machine learning to geoscience data for mineral exploration, mining operations, public geological authorities, and mining & minerals investors. Founded and run by geologists (CEO Tomi de Lophem, CTO Mason Dykstra) and backed by Speedinvest and the Creative Destruction Lab, MinersAI structures, cleans, QCs, feature-engineers, and standardizes geochemical, geophysical, and remote-sensing datasets, then applies anomaly detection, heatmap generation, dimensionality reduction, and geostatistical interpolation to surface high-potential exploration targets. Its "geologists-in-the-loop" approach keeps domain experts central rather than replacing their expertise. The platform is delivered as a gated web application (app.minersai.com); there is no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Mision Admision
providers.description: Misión Admisión is a Mexican education-technology company based in Mérida that prepares high school and university applicants for standardized admission exams such as EXANI I, EXANI II, PAA, and the UNAM, IPN, and UAM entrance tests. Its consumer web platform (misionadmision.com) delivers self-paced online courses, video lessons, interactive study capsules, thousands of practice questions, full-length exam simulators, live virtual and in-person classes, and the physical Sputnik smartbook guides. Founded in 2001 and online since 2015, the company is a seed-stage portfolio company of 500 Global. It is a consumer-facing EdTech platform and publishes no public developer API surface at this time; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for tracking and enrichment.

providers.name: ONEiO
providers.description: ONEiO is a managed integration service provider delivering IntegrationOps as a Service, providing cloud-based, automation-led integrations for enterprise IT that go live in weeks and evolve automatically.

providers.name: Outtake
providers.description: Outtake is an AI-powered digital risk protection (DRP) platform that autonomously detects and dismantles digital threats — brand impersonation, executive impersonation, fake domains, fraudulent ads, and dark-web activity — across 100+ platforms. Its agentic system combines an Entity Registry, Agentic Search, a Digital Reservoir of contextual intelligence, threat graphing / narrative intelligence, and adaptive takedown workflows to remove threats in hours rather than weeks. The company reports a 99.4% takedown-confirmation rate and a 14.4-hour average resolution time. Backed by CRV and ICONIQ Capital.

providers.name: Outverse
providers.description: Outverse is an enterprise "service AI operating system" from Outverse Limited, a UK company backed by Seedcamp and Wing Venture Capital. Its platform lets support and operations teams deploy governed AI agents across complex customer-service workflows — email, chat, voice, and API-driven actions — from a single control center. Teams define logic, policies, and human handoffs in natural language SOPs rather than rigid workflow builders, and get observability over every agent decision, tool call, workflow path, and escalation. Outverse integrates with existing CCaaS and CRM stacks (Salesforce, Freshdesk, Genesys, Twilio, Talkdesk) and offers voice agents that verify identity, retrieve data, apply policy, and resolve calls end to end. The company advertises SOC 2 and ISO 27001 certification and does not expose a public developer API at this time. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Seedcamp and Wing Venture Capital.

providers.name: Packhelp
providers.description: Packhelp is a European custom and wholesale packaging platform that lets businesses design, order, and warehouse branded packaging — boxes, mailers, bags, tubes, and accessories — through online design tools and a curated catalog of EU-based producers. Packhelp also markets "the first-ever API for packaging," a sales-gated set of web services that let 3PL, fulfillment, marketplace, logistics, and food-delivery platforms embed packaging quoting, ordering, and a drag-and-drop packaging editor directly into their own applications and whitelabel storefronts.

providers.name: Pentera
providers.description: Pentera is an AI-driven automated security validation (exposure validation) platform that lets organizations continuously test their security defenses through automated penetration testing, red teaming, and adversarial validation across internal networks, external attack surface, credentials, and cloud environments. The platform safely emulates real attacker techniques at scale to surface exploitable exposures, validate remediation, and prioritize risk. Pentera is enterprise/on-prem software consumed via its own console and a broad set of product integrations (SIEM/SOAR, ticketing, cloud, EDR, vulnerability management); it does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or developer portal. Pentera is backed by Insight Partners. Sector: cybersecurity.

providers.name: Pi Health
providers.description: Pi Health is an AI-native clinical trial technology company and contract research organization (CRO) building FICS, a unified operating system for oncology and global clinical trials. Its platform consolidates traditionally fragmented systems — Electronic Data Capture (EDC), Clinical Trial Management System (CTMS), electronic Trial Master File (eTMF), electronic Investigator Site File (eISF), and an EMR-to-EDC Orchestrator — into a single AI-validated master record spanning study startup through closeout. Pi Health pairs the platform with CRO services and a global research network with oncology sites across the US, Brazil, Australia, and India. As of this profile the company exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this remains an identity profile in the API Evangelist network awaiting a public API.

providers.name: PlanetSpark
providers.description: PlanetSpark is an Indian education-technology company headquartered in Gurugram, founded in 2017 by Kunal Malik and Maneesh Dhooper, that delivers live 1:1 online classes in public speaking, spoken English, creative writing, grammar, debating and vlogging to K-8 learners, along with mental and Vedic mathematics, abacus and school-excellence programmes, plus communication courses for working professionals. It sells directly to parents and learners through www.planetspark.in as a consumer subscription; it operates no public developer programme, publishes no API documentation or machine-readable contract, and its only external integration surface is an affiliate registration programme.

providers.name: Pop.in
providers.description: Pop.in is a consumer social gaming platform that connects people through real-time multiplayer games including Spades, Hearts, Dominoes, Liar's Dice, crosswords, Pop Quiz trivia, and Just Chatting. Delivered as iOS and Android apps plus a web play surface at play.pop.in, the service reports over 100M downloads and 20M active users with a 4.75+ average rating. The company is backed by 500 Global and was surfaced through its portfolio; it operates a purely consumer-facing product and publishes no public developer, API, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Preql
providers.description: Preql (preql.ai) is an enterprise data platform that automates data cleaning, reconciliation, and semantic modeling to deliver the trustworthy context layer that AI agents and business analytics depend on. Its agentic platform combines Agentic Semantic Modeling, Data Cleaning Agents, and AI-Powered Reporting to automatically resolve data mismatches, schema drift, and anomalies across ERP, CRM, HR, and expense systems without manual intervention, serving finance, operations, revenue, and executive decision-making at large enterprises. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners and Felicis, and added to the API Evangelist network. Preql does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or API reference; this profile captures its public company identity, help center, and web properties.

providers.name: Ray Browser
providers.description: Ray Browser is an AI-powered web browser that learns a user's interests and browsing habits to personalize their internet experience. It ships a built-in agent that can run web searches and automate tasks, a curated daily Discover feed, and Ray Studio for building custom tools and dashboards without writing code. The product is currently in public beta with a free Starter plan that grants weekly credits for its AI features. Ray Browser is a consumer product; as of this profile it does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network for tracking and enrichment.

providers.name: Saffron
providers.description: Saffron (trysaffron.ai) is a Y Combinator (Spring 2026) startup building an AI-native technical assessment platform for engineering hiring. Candidates build real features on a company's actual codebase using AI coding tools such as Claude Code inside a sandboxed environment, while Saffron captures every keystroke and AI interaction to score submissions against custom rubrics. It provides line-by-line attribution distinguishing human-written, AI-generated, and AI-modified code, and replaces traditional phone screens, take-homes, and on-site interview loops with a single AI-integrated assessment.

providers.name: Scoutzie
providers.description: Scoutzie is a Y Combinator-founded company (2012) led by Kirill Zubovsky. It launched as a curated marketplace connecting startups with top mobile designers and developers, operating from 2012 to 2020, and has since transformed into an AI-powered MVP (minimum viable product) development agency that builds and ships startup products in roughly two weeks. Today Scoutzie sells product-development services, an MVP Agent, founder training, and SEO consulting rather than a public developer API. It was surfaced through the a16z portfolio graph and enriched here as an API Evangelist network company profile.

providers.name: Selective Insurance Group
providers.description: Selective Insurance Group, Inc. (NASDAQ: SIGI) is a Branchville, New Jersey holding company whose insurance subsidiaries underwrite standard commercial lines, standard personal lines, and excess and surplus lines property and casualty insurance, plus flood insurance written through the National Flood Insurance Program's Write Your Own program. Coverage is distributed exclusively through independent insurance agents and brokers across the Eastern and Midwestern United States. Selective operates customer and agent self-service portals (MySelective, and the agent portal at customer1.selectiveinsurance.com) and supports policy, billing and claims download into agency management systems, but publishes no public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable API contract as of this profile.

providers.name: Slidebean
providers.description: Slidebean is a pitch deck and financial modeling platform for startup founders. It combines AI-powered presentation software that auto-designs investor-ready slides with professional pitch deck design services and financial modeling assistance for fundraising. Founders use Slidebean to build, refine, and share pitch decks, model their startup finances, and prepare for investor conversations. As of this enrichment pass Slidebean operates as a consumer/SMB SaaS product and does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or developer portal; its GitHub organization contains only forks and small internal JavaScript utilities.

providers.name: Smart Bricks
providers.description: Smart Bricks Holdings Limited operates Smart Bricks, an AI-powered real estate investment platform that uses proprietary foundational models and autonomous agents to help retail and institutional investors discover, underwrite, execute, and monitor property deals globally. Backed by a16z, Google, NVIDIA, Microsoft, Techstars, and 500 Global, the company automates deal sourcing, risk modeling across 1,000+ variables per opportunity, diligence, documentation, and portfolio intelligence. This profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; Smart Bricks currently publishes a consumer and institutional web application but no public API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: smilestory-ai
providers.description: SmileStory AI is a Korean AI-driven storytelling platform that offers REST API access for generating and managing personalized story content. The company provides tools for creators, integrates with large language models, and supports developers via a public API documented on its website. It operates under the SmileStory Group, with headquarters in Seoul, and maintains a GitHub organization for SDKs and examples.

providers.name: Spamhaus
providers.description: Spamhaus is an international non‑profit organization that tracks email spam and related cyber‑threats. It operates globally recognized blocklists such as the DNSBL, provides reputation data, and offers tools and services to help ISPs, email providers, and security teams protect their networks from spam, phishing, and malware. Through its research and data services, Spamhaus strengthens trust and safety across the internet.

providers.name: Standout
providers.description: Standout (standout.work) is an AI talent agent for tech professionals in the United States. Candidates run a CLI (`npx standout`) that assesses how they think, build, and debug to create a living, verified profile of capability rather than a resume. Standout matches candidates to hiring companies and brokers a direct introduction to the founder when a match looks right — no applications and no recruiter middle layer. It is free for candidates; companies pay only on a successful hire. Backed by Y Combinator.

providers.name: The Ladders
providers.description: Ladders (TheLadders.com) is a New York City based online job-search service founded in 2003 by Marc Cenedella that specializes in vetted executive and professional roles paying $100,000 or more per year. The subscription platform pairs a curated $100K+ job board with recruiter access, resume review and rewrite tools, AI-powered resume and LinkedIn optimization, and a daily career-news and advice product (Ladders News). It runs a consumer-facing web application with free Basic and paid Premium memberships and, as of this profile, publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or partner integration program.

providers.name: the2410-com
providers.description: The2410.com is a full-cycle SaaS and B2B development agency that builds, scales, and sells custom SaaS platforms, AI-driven business systems, and automation solutions, offering extended post‑launch support. It provides comprehensive full‑stack web development services, including consulting, product design, implementation, and ongoing maintenance for enterprises seeking digital transformation.

providers.name: Total Attorneys (Internet Brands)
providers.description: Total Attorneys is a legal marketing and lead-generation brand owned by Internet Brands. Originally a legal practice-management and client-intake SaaS backed by Bain Capital Ventures, the service was folded into the Martindale-Avvo network, and as of April 1, 2019 its attorney lead-generation offering transitioned to the Martindale-Nolo Pay Per Lead program. The totalattorneys.com site today markets pay-per-lead attorney marketing across practice areas such as bankruptcy, criminal defense, DUI/DWI, divorce, and personal injury. No public developer program or API is currently published.

providers.name: TrueCare24
providers.description: TrueCare24 is a nationwide care platform providing care professionals and services for home and business. Its offerings span in-home care, on-demand healthcare staffing, visiting nurses, behavioral health and counseling, and workplace health programs including flu vaccination, diabetes screening, and COVID-19 testing and vaccination services. A 500 Global portfolio company, TrueCare24 operates customer dashboards and a provider portal but publishes no public developer program or API.

providers.name: US Capitol Visitor Center
providers.description: The US Capitol Visitor Center (CVC) serves as the main entrance for visitors to the United States Capitol, providing resources and information to enhance the visitor experience. The Center offers guided tours of the Capitol building, allowing visitors to explore the historic rooms and learn about the legislative process. It also houses exhibits and educational materials that highlight the history and significance of the Capitol and its role in American democracy. The CVC operates under the Architect of the Capitol and offers free guided tours, specialty tours, virtual tours, and educational programs for students and visitors from around the world.

providers.name: Vastrm
providers.description: Vastrm is a custom-tailored menswear e-commerce company selling made-to-fit polo shirts with 24 different fits and sizes plus additional free adjustments, an online design-your-own configurator, corporate solutions for businesses, and a retail partners program. Vastrm is a Y Combinator and a16z-backed company tracked in the API Evangelist network; it operates a consumer storefront at vastrm.com and publishes no public developer or API surface.

providers.name: Webfleet
providers.description: Webfleet provides vehicle tracking and fleet management solutions, offering GPS tracking, driver safety, workflow optimization, compliance, sustainability, and maintenance tools for trucks, vans, cars, and assets. Their platform includes real‑time location, driver coaching, video telematics, route optimization, and integration with various industry services, serving businesses of all sizes across multiple sectors.

providers.name: Weee
providers.description: Weee! is America's largest online Asian grocery store and delivery platform, operating as a direct-to-consumer online supermarket serving major metropolitan areas across the United States. It curates and fulfills inventory through regional distribution centers and cold-chain logistics, bringing together products and ingredients commonly found in Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Vietnamese, Thai, Filipino, and Indian supermarkets. The storefront spans fresh produce, frozen meats, seafood, pantry staples, snacks, sauces, hot pot ingredients, beverages, and household essentials, accepts EBT/SNAP in eligible cities, and runs a multilingual experience (English, Chinese, Korean, Japanese, Vietnamese, Thai). Weee is backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners and the SoftBank Vision Fund. As of this profile Weee publishes no public developer API; this record captures its public web identity and AI-indexing (llms.txt) surface.

providers.name: Wizard
providers.description: Wizard is an AI-powered personal shopping agent for consumers. Shoppers describe what they want in natural language and Wizard searches across retailer websites, customer reviews, trusted editorial, and social content to return a tightly curated set of product recommendations, with direct checkout from retailers such as Amazon, Best Buy, Apple, and Target. The company is backed by Accel. As of this enrichment pass Wizard is a consumer-facing web/app product and exposes no public developer API, SDK, documentation, or well-known discovery surface (developer/docs/api subdomains and /.well-known/security.txt all return 404).

providers.name: Xpeng
providers.description: XPENG (Xiaopeng Motors) is a Chinese smart electric-vehicle company headquartered in Guangzhou that designs and manufactures smart EVs (G6, G7, G9, P7/P7+, X9, MONA M03) with in-house advanced driver-assistance and in-car software, listed on the NYSE (XPEV) and HKEX (9868). Surfaced as a portfolio company of hongshan and idg-capital. XPENG publishes no public developer API: its open platform (open.xiaopeng.com) is geo-restricted and account-gated, and no public API docs, specs, or SDKs were found.

providers.name: Ärikratt
providers.description: Ärikratt is a free, anonymous explorer of public Estonian company data, offering sector, regional, grant and procurement information. It presents only public company‑level data, each figure with unit, period and source, and never substitutes missing values with zero. Users can browse without an account; optional accounts provide free MCP keys. The service aggregates data from official registers, ensuring up‑to‑date facts for companies, sectors, regions, grants and public procurement.

providers.name: 24 FIX
providers.description: 24 FIX is the flagship consumer home-maintenance brand of 24 Solution Group (Thailand) Co., Ltd., founded in Bangkok in 2018 by six co-founders and now operating under the 24X umbrella brand. It runs an end-to-end property maintenance and home-solutions service rather than a matchmaking marketplace: air-conditioner cleaning and repair, washing-machine and appliance service, electrical and plumbing work, painting, cleaning, renovation and construction, delivered through an in-house managed ecosystem of more than 500 fixer teams and material vendor stores across Bangkok and the surrounding provinces, with expansion into Phuket and Singapore. The group fields four business lines — 24 FIX (consumer), 24 FIX for Business (commercial and facility maintenance, 500+ corporate customers), 24 House Solution, and 24 Projects (renovation and construction) — supported by an internal computerized maintenance management system that dispatches, tracks and quality-controls technician jobs. It raised a seed round in 2020, a pre-Series A from ECG Venture Capital in 2021, a 150 million THB Series A from Krungsri Finnovate, ECG Venture Capital and BCH Ventures in 2022, and a USD 5 million Series B from Wavemaker and Krungsri Finnovate in 2023. 24 FIX is a consumer and B2B services operator, not a software vendor: it publishes no developer portal, no API documentation, no SDKs and no machine-readable API contract, and the only /api/ path on its booking application is an internal Next.js route tree its own robots.txt disallows.

providers.name: Actifio
providers.description: Actifio is an enterprise data management company that pioneered "copy data management" (CDM) built on its Virtual Data Pipeline (VDP) technology, letting organizations capture a single physical copy of production data and instantly provision virtual copies for backup, disaster recovery, business continuity, test/dev, and analytics. Founded in 2009 and headquartered in Waltham, Massachusetts, Actifio was acquired by Google Cloud in December 2020. Its technology now underpins the Google Cloud Backup and Disaster Recovery (Backup and DR) service and Actifio GO, delivering SaaS backup and DR for Google Cloud and hybrid workloads. Actifio VDP exposes automation via a RESTful API and CLI on the appliance, but there is no public developer portal, OpenAPI/Swagger specification, or published client SDK.

providers.name: AgentLux
providers.description: AgentLux provides a platform for AI agents to showcase their capabilities, obtain a verifiable track record, and connect with clients through escrowed hires. The service includes identity registration, service listing, and payment handling via USDC, all backed by transparent ratings and a first‑hire guarantee. Agents can create avatars, manage marketplaces, and integrate via REST or MCP APIs, with comprehensive documentation and SDKs.

providers.name: Agreena
providers.description: Agreena is a Copenhagen-based agtech and climate finance company, founded in 2021, that helps farmers transition to regenerative agriculture and monetize the resulting soil-carbon outcomes. Its AgreenaCarbon platform combines farmer enrollment, a satellite-, AI-, and soil-sampling-based digital measurement, reporting and verification (dMRV) engine, and Verra-certified carbon credit issuance. Agreena also offers standalone remote-sensing products such as a field-boundary-detection API for agrifood supply-chain monitoring. The platform spans roughly 5 million hectares and 2,500+ farmers across ~20 European countries. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Anthemis and HV Capital and is being enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Agreena publishes no public developer portal or OpenAPI surface at this time.

providers.name: Ai²robotics
providers.description: Ai²robotics (智平方科技) is a global leader in the research, development, manufacturing, and services of general‑purpose intelligent robots. Founded in April 2023 and headquartered in Shenzhen, the company accelerates the adoption of AGI robots, aiming to make them as ubiquitous as smartphones. It offers the AlphaBrain Platform and other AI‑driven robotics solutions for industrial and commercial applications, with a focus on safety, scalability, and real‑world AI integration.

providers.name: AmlakIntel
providers.description: AmlakIntel is the property data layer for Claude and ChatGPT. It reads the Gulf’s official property registers and works the answer out, so you get the figure, the method behind it, how many records it came from, the window it covers and how wide the margin is. When the data is too thin to carry an answer, it says so.

providers.name: Arc (The Browser Company)
providers.description: Arc is a Chromium-based alternative web browser from The Browser Company, organized around Spaces, Profiles, Split View, Boosts (user-authored CSS/JS overlays), Easels, Notes, and Arc Search on mobile. Arc is primarily a consumer product without a broad public developer REST API. Developer surface area is limited to Developer Mode in the desktop browser, the underlying Chromium extension model, and user-created Boosts. The company has signalled that Arc's active product investment is winding down in favor of the successor product, Dia.

providers.name: Arcane Core
providers.description: Arcane Core provides a live tabletop role‑playing game (TTRPG) campaign display platform for game masters and players. It offers initiative tracking, character and map displays, player safety tools, and integration with streaming setups, enabling immersive online and tabletop sessions.

providers.name: Atalay AI
providers.description: Müşteri mesajını, teklifi, paylaşımı ve muhasebeyi yapay zekâ çalışanların hazırlar, onay sende kalır. Web sitesi, e-ticaret, e-Fatura aynı yerde. İşletmenizin Yapay Zekası. Mesajı, paylaşımı, teklifi ve muhasebeyi yapay zekâ çalışanları hazırlar; son söz senin.

providers.name: Athos
providers.description: Athos is a sports performance technology company founded in 2012 and based in Redwood City, California, that builds athletic apparel with embedded surface electromyography (EMG) sensors. Its garments and snap-on Athos Core module capture muscle activity, effort, and motion data, streaming it over Bluetooth to a mobile app and coaching dashboard so athletes, trainers, and sports scientists can measure muscular exertion, fatigue, and return-to-play readiness in real time. Athos is a consumer and team hardware brand with no publicly documented developer API; this profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners and enriched for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Audioknihy.cz
providers.description: audioknihy-cz is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: mcp-registry) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.

providers.name: Aunalytics
providers.description: Aunalytics provides AI agents and AI‑powered solutions tailored for financial institutions and IT departments. Their platform offers an intelligent data warehouse, analytics services, and a suite of AI tools that help banks, credit unions, healthcare providers, and government agencies streamline data processing, improve decision‑making, and automate routine tasks. By combining secure infrastructure with proprietary data models, Aunalytics enables organizations to make data AI‑ready and put it to work across a range of enterprise cloud services, backup, disaster recovery, and managed security solutions.

providers.name: Avenzo Therapeutics
providers.description: Avenzo Therapeutics is a biotechnology company focused on developing next‑generation oncology therapies. The firm aims to transform cancer treatment through innovative drug development, targeting solid tumors with validated targets. It maintains a pipeline of clinical trials and scientific research, and engages investors and partners to advance its mission.

providers.name: BEFOREVIBE
providers.description: BEFOREVIBE is an AI‑powered platform that designs app screens first, then generates a product requirements document (PRD) that guides code generation, enabling rapid development of applications. The service targets developers and AI builders seeking to accelerate UI design and implementation, offering a visual‑first workflow that translates designs into actionable specifications.

providers.name: Bitpart.ai
providers.description: Bitpart.ai provides a platform for creating immersive, AI‑driven virtual worlds. It offers tools such as the Bitpart Unreal Plugin, Archetypes, Coppola authoring tool, and the Aesop multi‑agent planner, enabling developers to build interactive characters and environments. The service includes documentation, tutorials, pricing plans, and a community hub, targeting game developers, simulation creators, and AI researchers.

providers.name: Bloomfire
providers.description: Bloomfire provides an AI‑first, headless platform for enterprise knowledge management. Their Governed Context for Enterprise AI unifies data, content, and AI models, offering modular services like Universal Connector Framework, Ontology Management, Content Guardrails, and AI‑driven search and summarization. The platform enables organizations to capture, curate, and retrieve enterprise context at scale, supporting use‑cases from conversational AI assistants to analytics and compliance. Bloomfire’s API‑first design lets developers integrate these capabilities into custom applications, driving intelligent insights across the enterprise.

providers.name: Bright Moments DAO
providers.description: Bright Moments is an onchain art organization and decentralized autonomous organization (DAO) that produces live, in-person (IRL) generative NFT minting experiences in cities around the world. Its flagship CryptoCitizens collection (10,000 Art Blocks-powered generative portraits by artist Qian Qian) was minted 1,000 at a time across ten cities including Venice CA (CryptoVenetians), New York, Berlin, London, Mexico City, Tokyo, Buenos Aires, Paris, Venice Italy, and the Metaverse. Holding a CryptoCitizen confers membership and governance rights in the Bright Moments DAO, which was founded on-chain in March 2021. Bright Moments also runs artist collaborations/residencies, a Golden Token minting mechanism, and display software for at-home viewing. It is not a traditional API provider: the public technical surface is Ethereum/Base smart contracts, a documentation site, a DAO portal app, and a public GitHub organization. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Union Square Ventures.

providers.name: BrightPlan
providers.description: BrightPlan is a San Jose, California based financial wellness company that sells a Total Financial Wellness platform to enterprise HR and benefits teams, combining a self-service digital financial planning application, an AI-powered financial wellness coach, and access to human CFP fiduciary advisors. BrightPlan LLC is an SEC-registered investment adviser, and the product is delivered to employees as an employer-sponsored benefit rather than as a self-serve consumer subscription. The employee experience runs at my.brightplan.com and web.brightplan.com with iOS and Android apps; employer value is framed around benefits engagement, retention, and measurable financial wellbeing. BrightPlan markets HRIS and benefits-system integration to employers but publishes no public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: Brokk
providers.description: Brokk (Brokk, Inc.) builds AI tooling for large codebases. Rather than a hosted REST API, Brokk ships open-source developer tools centered on "bifrost" — a Tree-sitter-backed multi-language static-analysis engine that gives coding agents structured code intelligence (symbols, definitions, references, call graphs, usage analysis) across 12 languages. Bifrost runs as a CLI, a workspace-aware language server (LSP), and a stdio MCP server, and is published to crates.io (brokk-bifrost) and PyPI (brokk-bifrost-searchtools). The company, founded by Jonathan Ellis (Apache Cassandra / DataStax) and backed by Mayfield, also ships the core Brokk application, the brokk-cli launcher, and Agent Client Protocol (ACP) tooling (anvil, mjolnir).

providers.name: Buildos
providers.description: Buildos provides construction project management software that centralizes bills of quantities, cost plans, site progress, inventory, and workforce management in a single web and Android platform. It enables contractors and quantity surveyors to streamline project data, reduce duplicate work, and improve budgeting and reporting across the entire construction lifecycle.

providers.name: Cash Flow Crescendo Inc.
providers.description: Cash Flow Crescendo Inc. operates Animation Machine, a web‑based service that converts HTML‑based animations and video files into polished MP4 or GIF outputs. It offers AI‑generated captions in 16 languages, AI voice‑over with 14 natural voices, a library of 500 000 royalty‑free tracks, 4K rendering, batch processing, and one‑click vertical Shorts creation. The platform runs entirely in the cloud, requires no installation, and provides a $5 per month flat‑rate subscription with unlimited renders and no per‑render fees. Users can upload HTML, Lottie, GSAP, CSS, Three.js, or existing video files, add music, captions, voice‑over, and branding, then download the final video. The service also includes an MCP server for AI agents such as Claude, ChatGPT, and Cursor.

providers.name: Charisma.ai
providers.description: Charisma.ai provides immersive conversational AI platforms for training, brand experiences, and interactive simulations. Their technology enables realistic dialogue scenarios, real‑time analytics, and cross‑platform integration for enterprises seeking high‑impact conversational outcomes. Based in Oxford, UK, Charisma.ai serves clients worldwide with award‑winning responsible AI systems and customizable SDKs for Unity, Unreal, and other environments.

providers.name: Chi Longevity
providers.description: Chi Longevity is a Singapore-based longevity medicine and healthy-aging clinic that focuses on biological-age optimization rather than reactive medicine, built on The Maier Method developed by co-founder Professor Andrea Maier. The practice combines precision health mapping (blood panels, genetic and cognitive testing, cardiovascular and metabolic analysis), flagship and specialised longevity programmes, cognitive and physical training, a branded NMN supplement, and ongoing support through health coaching, physician and dietitian consultations, and a client portal. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network; no public developer API is currently published, so this profile carries the company identity, domain-security posture, and published web properties rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Cityinnovate
providers.description: Cityinnovate, now operating under the brand Authorium, provides a no-code AI‑enabled platform for government operations. The solution streamlines procurement, contract lifecycle management, grants, legislative analysis, and budget requests, offering modular, configurable tools to improve transparency and efficiency in public sector projects. Built as a public benefit company, Authorium claims to manage over $50 billion in government projects and aims to reduce process times by up to 15 business days.

providers.name: Common Sense Machines
providers.description: Common Sense Machines (CSM) builds 3D world models with image-to-3D and 3D world simulation APIs aimed at games, robotics, and synthetic data. The CSM Cube product family released a single-click model pipeline with mesh-parts-based topology in early 2026. API access is bundled with mid-tier and enterprise CSM subscription plans.

providers.name: Comun
providers.description: Comun (Común) is a fintech company providing digital banking and money-transfer services designed for Latino immigrants in the United States. Through a bilingual (Spanish/English) mobile app, users open an FDIC-insured U.S. checking account with a valid national ID and no SSN required, get a Visa debit card, receive early direct deposit up to two days ahead of payday, and send international remittances to 17+ Latin American countries via the app or WhatsApp. Banking services are provided through Community Federal Savings Bank; remittance and P2P rails run on UniTeller and Cross River Bank. Comun is backed by Costanoa Ventures and Redpoint Ventures. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network from VC portfolio data; Comun operates as a consumer neobank and does not publish a public developer API surface.

providers.name: Covalto
providers.description: Covalto (formerly Credijusto) is a Mexican digital bank for small and medium-sized businesses, headquartered in Mexico City. It offers business and personal checking accounts, fixed-rate investment products, quick working-capital credit (Agil Covalto), factoring, leasing (arrendamiento), and fiduciary trust services (fideicomisos). Covalto acquired a regulated Mexican banking license, making it one of the first fintechs in Mexico to become a fully licensed bank. Its digital surface spans online banking, digital account opening, and a credit application flow. Covalto is backed by QED Investors. As of the latest review it publishes no public API developer portal; its developer documentation at docs.covalto.com is gated behind Google Identity-Aware Proxy for internal use.

providers.name: CSIDIA S.r.l.
providers.description: CSIDIA S.r.l. provides AI‑driven automation platforms that turn enterprise data into actionable decisions and actions. Based in Vignola, Italy, the company builds data and AI platforms designed for European compliance, offering tools for operational AI, governance, and integration across business processes.

providers.name: Daski
providers.description: Daski is a curated procurement marketplace for AI agents, offering services to discover, evaluate, buy, and manage domains, mailboxes, and company formation. It connects AI agents with essential digital infrastructure, providing a seamless platform for acquiring and managing online assets.

providers.name: Diplomètre
providers.description: diplometre-fr is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: mcp-registry) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.

providers.name: Douglas Elliman
providers.description: Douglas Elliman Inc. (NYSE: DOUG) is a residential real estate brokerage founded in 1911 and headquartered at 575 Madison Avenue, New York City. It is one of the largest brokerages in the New York metropolitan area and among the largest in the United States, with roughly 6,000 agents across New York, Florida, California, Texas, Colorado, Massachusetts, Connecticut, Nevada, New Jersey, Vermont, the Mid-Atlantic, and international outposts in France and Monaco. Its home market is the United States. In the value chain Douglas Elliman sits on the SELL side as a licensed brokerage and MLS participant — it consumes MLS listing data under IDX and broker agreements rather than originating a syndicated feed — and it extends into development marketing, property management, commercial brokerage, title and escrow (Douglas Elliman Title), relocation, and PropTech venture investment through New Valley Ventures. Its API posture is honest and thin: no developer portal, no published API documentation, no OpenAPI or OData $metadata contract, and no published access path of any kind. developer.elliman.com, developers.elliman.com, and docs.elliman.com all resolve to the marketing homepage via a wildcard catch-all rather than to a portal, and api.elliman.com exists as an IIS/ASP.NET host that returns HTTP 403 at its root with no documentation behind it. On RESO, Douglas Elliman Real Estate is listed as a Class D member (Brokers, Agents and Appraisers) on the RESO membership roster but does NOT appear in the RESO certified-organizations directory — it is a RESO member, not a RESO-certified data provider, and it publishes no Web API or Data Dictionary certification, no OData endpoint, and no UPI surface. The single public engineering artifact the company ships is a GitHub fork of a third-party .NET RETS client library, which is consumer-side evidence that Elliman pulls MLS data in rather than producer-side evidence that it exposes any.

providers.name: DXY
providers.description: DXY (丁香园) is China's leading digital healthcare technology company, founded in 2000 in Harbin and headquartered in Hangzhou. It operates a "D+C" dual strategy: a professional physician community and clinical toolset (drug reference "用药助手", clinical case database, medical education, and the "Insight" pharmaceutical data analytics platform) alongside consumer health services under the "丁香医生" (Dingxiang Doctor) brand. DXY also runs the Biomart / 丁香通 life-sciences supplies marketplace. Its Medical Data Open Platform (open.dxy.cn) exposes standardized healthcare data services — newly-approved drugs, drug SKU and drug search, disease search, and hospital/institution search — as REST/JSON APIs under api.dxy.cn for pharmaceutical, medical, and health-tech partners. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of dcm-ventures and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: elliat-nl
providers.description: Elliat is an independent developer brand operated by Martin Middel, specializing in JavaScript and XML technologies. Offering expertise in Fonto XML Editor, FontoXPath, and related standards, Elliat provides consulting, custom development, and open‑source tools such as an MCP server that makes Fonto documentation AI‑readable. The site showcases projects, a portfolio of XML‑related work, and contact information for hiring the developer.

providers.name: Epsor
providers.description: Epsor is a French fintech, founded in 2017, that manages employee savings and retirement plans (épargne salariale et retraite) for companies and helps them turn that benefit into an HR lever. A certified B Corp and mission-driven company, Epsor ranks among the top 10 employee-savings and retirement providers in France and serves more than 2,500 corporate clients. It targets HR, Compensation & Benefits, and Finance teams at mid-size and large French firms, combining a pedagogical, personalized saver experience, an open-architecture fund range (40+ funds from 15+ asset managers, with a strong ESG/SRI focus), and year-round support to run and promote the plan. Epsor is neither an asset manager nor a bank: it is the single point of contact for companies and their employees, and delegates account-keeping to Société Générale Securities Services (SGSS). Products span PEE, PER Collectif (PERECO), PER Obligatoire, intéressement, participation, abondement, and employee share ownership. Epsor exposes no public developer API; this profile captures its public identity and security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Glow
providers.description: Glow (glowing.com) is a women's health and reproductive-health technology company whose consumer mobile apps track periods, ovulation, fertility, pregnancy, and early baby development for a community of more than 25 million members. Its app suite spans Glow (ovulation and fertility), Eve by Glow (period tracking), Glow Nurture (pregnancy), and Glow Baby (infant development), and it layers AI-powered health insights through GlowGPT along with a Glow Premium subscription and a companion Glow Shop for hardware such as basal thermometers, test strips, and a smart breast pump. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Slow Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network, Glow is a consumer app business with no public developer program: no API portal, developer documentation, SDKs, or OpenAPI surface could be located during enrichment.

providers.name: Halter
providers.description: Halter is a New Zealand-founded agri-technology company that builds GPS-enabled, solar-powered smart collars for cattle paired with a mobile and web app, letting farmers set and move virtual fences, remotely shift and hold herds, and monitor animal location, behavior, heat and health without physical fencing or manual labor. The platform combines wearable IoT devices (including direct-to-satellite connectivity) with pasture-management and grazing-allocation tools for dairy and beef operations. Halter operates across New Zealand, Australia and the United States and is backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, Bond Capital and DCVC. No public developer API surface has been identified; this profile captures the company identity, web properties and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Harness (nonprofit giving app)
providers.description: Harness provides a recurring giving platform for nonprofits, enabling frictionless monthly donor subscriptions, retention dashboards, and automated stewardship. Their suite helps organizations launch, grow, and retain donors with easy-to-use forms and subscription‑economy‑style experiences, aiming to increase sustainable funding for charitable causes.

providers.name: Homebound
providers.description: Homebound is a tech-enabled, personalized homebuilder that pairs a proprietary software platform with a managed network of trade partners to build homes on a customer's lot, sell finished and in-progress inventory homes, and run disaster rebuild programs — most notably wildfire recovery in California. Homeowners track budget, schedule, documents, and construction progress through a Homeowner Portal. Backed by Fifth Wall, Forerunner Ventures, and GV, Homebound operates in the construction-tech sector. Homebound does not publish a public developer API or developer portal; its public engineering footprint is the homebound-team GitHub organization and the first-party open-source packages it publishes to the @homebound npm scope (the Beam design system, form-state, and truss). This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio lead and enriched from public company surfaces.

providers.name: Housable
providers.description: Housable is a California-focused proptech company that helps rental-property owners and operators develop Accessory Dwelling Units (ADUs) as a portfolio value-add strategy. Its platform manages ADU projects end to end — from concept and financial feasibility analysis through design, permitting, bidding, construction, and lease-up — and lets operators run many parallel developments across their properties at once, converting underused spaces such as leasing offices, garages, and parking areas into new rental units alongside ground-up ADU construction. Housable is an early-stage startup backed by Kindred Ventures and other seed investors. It is catalogued in the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: Inductive
providers.description: Inductive Bio is a New York-based AI drug discovery company building a virtual lab for small molecule optimization. It pairs medicinal chemists with AI to run millions of in silico ADMET experiments before synthesis. Its Beacon-1 models — trained on a pre-competitive, anonymized data consortium spanning thousands of drug programs — won consecutive first-place finishes in the 2025 Polaris/ASAP and 2026 OpenADMET blind ADMET prediction competitions, beating 370+ submissions including entries from Merck and NVIDIA. Products include the Compass software platform (accessible via API), the Indy AI chemistry assistant, the ADME-One high-throughput profiling service, and Embedded Experts. Founded in 2023 by Josh Haimson and Ben Birnbaum (both formerly Flatiron Health); SOC 2 compliant; backed by Obvious Ventures, a16z Bio+Health, Lux Capital, Bessemer Venture Partners, Character, and S32.

providers.name: Iris Telehealth
providers.description: Iris Telehealth is an Austin, Texas telepsychiatry company, founded in 2013, that delivers virtual behavioral health care to healthcare organizations rather than direct to consumers. It contracts psychiatrists, psychiatric nurse practitioners, LCSWs and LPCs to hospitals and health systems, community mental health centers, community health centers and FQHCs, and Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinics, covering pediatric through geriatric populations and low-acuity therapy through high-acuity psychiatry. Its service lines are Virtual Clinic (comprehensive care and behavioral health integration), On-Demand Services (24/7 emergency department psychiatry support), Scheduled Services (matched provider staffing), Bridge Clinic, and Iris Insights, an AI-enabled behavioral health analytics platform covering risk optimization, capacity management, a behavioral health command center and revenue cycle analytics. The company reports over 430 clinicians and over 210 partner organizations, and has been accredited by the Joint Commission for behavioral health care since 2019, earning recertification since. Its delivery model is deliberately technology-agnostic: Iris clinicians work inside each partner's existing EMR/EHR and e-prescribing tools over HIPAA-compliant video, so the integration burden sits with the partner's systems. Iris Telehealth publishes no public developer program, API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API contract, and operates no public GitHub organization.

providers.name: Item
providers.description: Item is an AI-native customer relationship management (CRM) platform, part of Y Combinator's Fall 2025 batch. It replaces the traditional CRM with an AI Assistant that handles daily work in plain language and customizable Agents that autonomously execute business processes across sales, support, and account management. Item connects to 100+ customer tools, gathers and enriches context automatically, discovers leads that match an ideal customer profile, and becomes a company's single source of truth for people, companies, and deals.

providers.name: JMock
providers.description: JMock is a library that supports test-driven development of Java code with mock objects. It provides an expressive API for defining expectations and mock behavior in unit tests, integrating with popular testing frameworks including JUnit. The most recent stable release is jMock 2.13.1.

providers.name: La Haus
providers.description: La Haus is a Latin American proptech company, founded in 2017 and headquartered in Medellín and Bogotá, Colombia, that operates the residential real-estate marketplaces lahaus.com (Colombia) and lahaus.mx (Mexico) together with an in-house brokerage. The platform lists de-duplicated, verified new-construction and resale housing from vetted developers, adds mortgage and down-payment simulators, buyer guides and an AI assistant, and takes buyers through negotiation and closing at no cost to the buyer. It has raised more than $135M in equity plus debt facilities from Kaszek, NFX, Acrew Capital, Greenspring Associates, SoftBank and Bezos Expeditions. La Haus publishes NO public developer portal, API documentation, SDK or machine-readable contract: the consumer sites are server-rendered applications whose /api/* paths are disallowed in robots.txt, and api.lahaus.com is a private AWS API Gateway that answers every anonymous request with MissingAuthenticationToken. Partner/portal syndication runs through access-controlled marketing feed integrations (Trovit). This profile therefore records the company's public web surface and security posture rather than an API surface.

providers.name: Lennar
providers.description: Lennar Corporation is a Fortune 500 company and one of the leading homebuilders of new homes for sale in the United States. Lennar operates an internal Azure-hosted API Management developer portal where Lennar developers and partners discover and consume Lennar Corporation APIs. Public OpenAPI artifacts have not been observed; access generally requires sign-in and partner approval.

providers.name: Medmonk
providers.description: Medmonk is a pharma market access platform that connects brand teams, healthcare providers, pharmacies, and patients on a single real-time infrastructure. It automates point-of-sale copay enrollment, benefit investigations, prior authorizations, financial assistance, hub workflows, and adherence tracking across specialty and rare-disease medications, reaching roughly 98% of U.S. pharmacy and buy/bill network connectivity. Medmonk states it exposes FHIR-compliant APIs to integrate with existing EHR, CRM, and pharmacy systems, and claims SOC 2, HIPAA, and GDPR compliance, though it publishes no public developer portal or API documentation. Founded in the Y Combinator W12 batch.

providers.name: MedThread
providers.description: MedThread is an AI-powered Health Information Management (HIM) platform built specifically for long-term and post-acute care facilities — skilled nursing facilities (SNFs), nursing homes, assisted living facilities (ALFs), and rehabilitation centers. The platform digitizes paper records with AI-powered scanning, runs continuous automated audits for documentation completeness and regulatory compliance, monitors CMS quality metrics (rehospitalization, pressure ulcers, antipsychotic use), and provides a compliance dashboard, provider portal, and patient-facing Personal Health Record (PHR). MedThread advertises FHIR compatibility and pre-built EHR integrations (Epic, Cerner, Allscripts, eClinicalWorks, NextGen, Meditech, athenahealth, Greenway, Practice Fusion) via a secure API. Techstars-backed and based in Miami, FL. No public developer portal, API reference, or OpenAPI specification is published at this time.

providers.name: Medzoomer
providers.description: Medzoomer is an on-demand prescription delivery platform that connects pharmacies, healthcare providers, and patients through a secure, HIPAA-compliant network of verified couriers. Founded in 2019 and headquartered in Tampa, Florida, the company handles last-mile medication logistics, including controlled substances (Schedule II-V), with tamper-evident packaging, FDA/TSA-approved envelopes, and real-time order tracking. Pharmacies and couriers operate through dedicated web and mobile applications, and the platform is backed by Techstars, UnitedHealthcare Accelerator, and other investors. Medzoomer operates a private pharmacy integration API but publishes no public developer documentation, SDKs, or OpenAPI at this time.

providers.name: MidFirst Bank
providers.description: MidFirst Bank is a federally chartered savings association (thrift) headquartered in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma, and owned by Midland Financial Co. Founded in 1982 with roots in Midland Mortgage from the early 1950s, it is the largest privately owned bank in the United States, with roughly $42 billion in assets and retail banking, private banking, commercial real estate lending, and nationwide mortgage servicing operations across Oklahoma, Arizona, California, Colorado, Nevada, Texas, and Utah. MidFirst does not operate a first-party public developer portal or publish downloadable OpenAPI/Swagger specifications. Its open-finance posture is aggregator-mediated: through its "Open Access" program, MidFirst adds direct API connections between its Business Online Banking platforms and consumer-permissioned data aggregators (Plaid, MX, Stripe, Intuit, Mastercard/Finicity, Envestnet Yodlee, and Morningstar), replacing screen scraping. There is no publicly documented first-party API surface, and no FDX participation or CFPB Section 1033 data-access posture is published on its site as of this review.

providers.name: Nave Bank
providers.description: Nave Bank is a digital-first business bank based in Puerto Rico, offering FDIC-insured deposit accounts, business savings, and business loans through an easy-to-navigate online and mobile banking platform. Its product surface centers on business checking ("Cuenta Nave Business"), interest-bearing savings, real-time payments, ACH and wire transfers, and mobile check deposit, with a bilingual (Spanish/English) experience and human customer support. Nave was surfaced as a portfolio company of Ribbit Capital and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Nave Bank publishes a consumer/business banking website and help center but no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation.

providers.name: Nix
providers.description: Nix (Nix Biosensors) develops wearable biosensor technology that analyzes sweat to deliver real-time hydration and electrolyte data. Its lightweight single-use biosensor patch continuously measures fluid and electrolyte losses and provides personalized hydration guidance to athletes, service members, and laborers. The company ships two consumer/enterprise offerings: Nix Solo, an individual app for self-monitoring hydration, and Nix Pro, a group-monitoring platform that lets coaches and supervisors track multiple users. Nix is a Techstars portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass it operates a direct-to-consumer commerce and mobile-app business with no public developer program, API documentation, or SDK surface.

providers.name: Numero
providers.description: Numero is an all-in-one donor database and call-time platform built for political campaigns at the federal, state, and local levels. It combines a fast, filterable donor CRM with auto-deduplication and pledge tracking, a mobile call-time dialer with one-click SMS, email, and voicemail follow-up plus virtual local numbers, prefilled one-click contribution forms with access to a large 1-click donor network, event and RSVP fundraising tools, and a deliverability-focused email platform. Campaigns use Numero to identify prospect donors, run efficient candidate call time, and raise money faster. Numero is backed by Initialized Capital. It currently exposes no public developer API surface; api.numero.ai serves the web application backend only.

providers.name: Oath
providers.description: Oath Soil Life is a US‑based company that offers products designed to replenish the soil microbiome, helping trees, lawns, and gardens thrive. Operating an e‑commerce storefront on Shopify, the brand markets soil‑health solutions and educational content to support sustainable gardening practices. The website provides a blog with gardening tips, a contact page for support, and clear terms of service and privacy policy. Oath aims to improve plant health through microbiome enrichment.

providers.name: Onlia
providers.description: Onlia is a Canadian digital insurance brokerage, operating as the registered business name of Onlia Agency Inc. and backed by Southampton Financial Inc. (the Southampton group of companies). It sells personal lines direct to consumers online and by phone — auto (car, motorcycle, ATV, snowmobile, trailer, motorhome), property (home, condo, tenant, landlord, second home, mobile home) and lifestyle lines (boat, pet, life, travel, seasonal) — plus group and bundle programs. Onlia does not underwrite; it places business with a panel of Canadian carriers disclosed publicly on its broker-disclosure page, including Aviva, Gore Mutual, Economical/Definity, Pembridge, Pafco, Echelon, Wawanesa, Unica, Forward, Premier, Facility Association (Intact) and APOLLO. Its home market is Canada, concentrated in Ontario, where market conduct sits with FSRA while OSFI supervises the federally-regulated carriers behind the policies. API posture, recorded honestly: Onlia publishes NO public developer portal and NO self-serve API. developer., developers., docs. and api. under onlia.ca do not resolve, and /developers, /api, /developer and /integrations on the marketing site all return 404. The only quote/bind/issue/FNOL surface is app.onlia.ca, a consumer-facing Angular single-page app running on a white-labelled Ignite Insurance policy administration platform whose backend is private to the app. The one "partner" page is a B2B marketing page inviting affinity discount partnerships by email, with no technical onboarding. No ACORD, AL3, ACORD XML or NGDS reference appears anywhere on the public site. The app's own bundle shows the private backend runs on MuleSoft Anypoint CloudHub ESB services (auto and home policy, authentication, documents, VIN/MVR, claims) plus an Ignite Insurance authentication service — real REST plumbing behind the SPA, but undocumented, uncredentialed and not offered to third parties, so no API entry is claimed here.

providers.name: Operator.io
providers.description: Operator.io provides an AI-powered chief of staff platform that automates email management, calendar scheduling, research, and follow‑ups across popular tools. Backed by Y Combinator, it integrates with Gmail, Outlook, Slack, Notion, GitHub, and more, offering plans starting at $10 per month. The service helps founders and operators streamline operations, improve productivity, and focus on high‑value tasks.

providers.name: Optivolt Labs
