The lola.com domain was previously the Boston-based corporate travel and expense-management startup founded by Kayak veterans Paul English and Bill O'Donnell (backed by Accel and GV, more than $80M raised) which wound down operations in 2021 with its technology acquired by Capital One; the domain now hosts this new consumer travel product. No public API or developer program is currently published — this profile captures the provider's public web and security posture.

providers.name: London House Exchange (Property Partner)
providers.description: London House Exchange, formerly Property Partner, is an FCA-regulated online platform that operates the world's only regulated exchange for individual residential, student and commercial properties. Founded in 2014 and now owned by US digital homeownership company Better, the platform lets retail investors buy fractional shares in professionally managed UK properties, earn monthly dividends from rental income, and trade those shares with other investors on a secondary market. It also offers property-backed mortgage bonds, an ISA, and bridging finance, with over £100m of fractionalised property assets under management and thousands of investors across more than 80 countries. It was surfaced as a Seedcamp portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. No public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Lower
providers.description: Lower is a U.S. direct-to-consumer mortgage lender and servicer (Lower, LLC, NMLS #1124061) offering home purchase loans, refinancing, and home equity products including conventional, FHA, VA, jumbo, and adjustable-rate mortgages, HELOCs, and cash-out options. Lower operates a mobile-first application experience with dedicated loan officers and conducts business in 47 states plus the District of Columbia. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and added to the API Evangelist network. Lower publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface at this time; this profile captures its public web, legal, and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Lumosity
providers.description: Lumosity is a consumer brain-training platform built by Lumos Labs that offers cognitive games and personalized daily workouts targeting memory, attention, problem solving, flexibility, and processing speed. The service adapts difficulty to individual performance, tracks progress over time, and is delivered through the web and iOS/Android mobile apps. Backed by Norwest Venture Partners, the company was surfaced through VC-portfolio discovery; probing its public surface found no developer portal, public API, or documented programmatic integration — it is a direct-to-consumer product with no API surface at this time.

providers.name: M&T Bank
providers.description: M&T Bank is a US super-regional bank holding company (M&T Bank Corporation, NYSE: MTB) headquartered in Buffalo, New York, operating through its national bank subsidiary Manufacturers and Traders Trust Company. With roughly $200 billion in assets it is one of the twenty largest US commercial banks, serving consumers, businesses, and institutional clients across the eastern United States, and it owns Wilmington Trust, its custody, fund-administration, and wealth arm. Unlike UK/AU open banking there is no single mandated contract in the US, so M&T's public API posture is split: it runs a real first-party Developer Portal / "API Store" at developer.mtb.com for institutional and wholesale clients (Banking & Treasury plus Wilmington Trust Custody APIs), gated behind Microsoft Entra login and Azure API Management subscription keys with per-product OpenAPI reference available only after authentication. Consumer-permissioned account data is shared through aggregators (Plaid) rather than a public first-party consumer API. No public FDX conformance or CFPB Section 1033 data-access API is documented on the portal at review time.

providers.name: Magic
providers.description: Magic, Inc. is a Y Combinator-backed virtual assistant company that matches busy professionals, executives, and entrepreneurs with dedicated, vetted human assistants rather than AI bots. Through its Magic Match screening (assistants drawn from the top 0.5% of applicants), Magic 24/7 backup coverage, and ongoing training, the service handles email and inbox management, calendar and scheduling, travel planning, customer support, research, data entry, and other recurring business and personal tasks. Magic is a consumer- and business-facing staffing/concierge service delivered through a web workspace; it does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or webhook surface at this time.

providers.name: Markt Pilot (aka MP)
providers.description: MARKT-PILOT GmbH is a German software company (registered in Beilstein, business address Stuttgart, with a US office in Chicago) that provides a unified pricing performance platform for industrial manufacturers. Its flagship product, MP ONE, combines an Intelligence Engine (real-time competitor and market data with AI-powered cross-reference part matching), a Decision Engine (cost-plus, market-based, and attribute-based pricing workflows), and a Performance Engine (portfolio, revenue, and margin analysis with executive dashboards). MARKT-PILOT serves 200+ manufacturers across agriculture, construction and mining, machine tooling, packaging, and industrial equipment, helping them move from static annual spare-parts pricing to dynamic, data-driven pricing. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Insight Partners. The company operates a marketing site, blog, and a hosted (Better Stack) status page, but publishes no public developer/API surface: no developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI, well-known discovery endpoints, or client SDKs were found during enrichment.

providers.name: Mayvenn
providers.description: Mayvenn is an Oakland, California beauty-commerce company that sells quality virgin human hair extensions, sew-in weave bundles, closures, frontals, and human hair wigs directly to consumers and through a network of more than 100,000 hair stylists. Founded by Diishan Imira and backed by a16z and 500 Global, Mayvenn pairs its hair products with a stylist-driven distribution model and a 30-day return policy, running its storefront on Shopify at shop.mayvenn.com. The company does not currently publish a public first-party developer API; this profile captures its web identity, security posture, and commercial link surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: memoryapi-org
providers.description: MemoryAPI provides a suite of AI‑powered agents that expose specialized functionality as paid API endpoints. Users can call agents for research, market data, legal analysis, health information, trading signals and more, paying per call with USDC via the x402 protocol. All agents run on‑chain under the ERC‑8004 standard, ensuring transparent accounting and accountability. The platform offers a single MCP (MemoryAPI Control Protocol) server that aggregates 36 agents, each accessible via standard HTTP calls. The service is hosted at memoryapi.org and includes sub‑services such as Shopping, Validator and Monitor.

providers.name: MerchantE
providers.description: MerchantE provides modern acquiring solutions for ISVs, PayFacs, ISOs, and merchants, powered by human insight. It offers a modern payment infrastructure built for builders, enabling faster integration and trusted transaction processing across multiple channels.

providers.name: Mintegral
providers.description: Mintegral provides AI‑powered mobile marketing solutions that help advertisers acquire, retain, and monetize users across gaming, subscription, and e‑commerce apps. Their platform offers app growth, retargeting, monetization, and creative studio tools, leveraging advanced AI to optimize ad spend and drive engagement. Mintegral serves global advertisers and publishers, emphasizing data‑driven growth and comprehensive campaign management.

providers.name: Moodle
providers.description: Moodle is the world's open source learning platform, used by educators and organizations to deliver online courses and learning experiences. The Moodle developer platform exposes a broad set of internal APIs for plugin and core development, plus a Web Services API that enables external systems to integrate with Moodle for users, courses, enrollments, grading, and more.

providers.name: Mophones
providers.description: Mophones (MoPhones) is a Nairobi, Kenya based fintech and recommerce company building accessible device-financing and re-commerce infrastructure for Africa, starting with premium refurbished smartphones from brands like Apple and Samsung sold with flexible weekly-installment and pay-on-delivery plans. The consumer storefront runs on Shopify at mophones.co and does not expose a first-party developer API; its only programmatic surface is the Shopify-provided agentic-commerce layer — a published Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) profile at /.well-known/ucp and a live UCP-over-MCP shopping endpoint at /api/ucp/mcp that lets buyer-approved AI shopping agents search the catalog, build carts, and complete Shop Pay checkouts. Mophones is backed by Speedinvest and was noted as the first African startup to secure NICE financing from STV.

providers.name: Motivo
providers.description: Motivo is the leading managed clinical supervision platform for behavioral health organizations. It connects pre-licensed and post-graduate mental health professionals with 1,500+ vetted clinical supervisors across all 50 states, enabling organizations to expand their workforce, reduce burnout, and meet licensure requirements. The fully-managed platform handles supervisor vetting, compliance and documentation, scheduling, HIPAA-compliant video sessions, and payment processing, and includes group supervision, peer consultation, webinars, and workforce-development resources. Motivo serves behavioral health centers, treatment facilities, health plans, and digital health companies. As of this profile Motivo publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; its platform is delivered as a managed SaaS product and it consumes third-party APIs (e.g. Google Calendar) internally.

providers.name: N-Drip
providers.description: N-Drip is an Israeli agritech manufacturer of gravity-powered micro-irrigation systems, led by Prof. Uri Shani, Israel's former Water Commissioner. Its patented drip system operates on gravity alone at under 0.87 PSI / 0.06 BAR, requiring no pumping station and no pressure-based filtration, and is positioned as a direct replacement for flood irrigation — which still accounts for roughly 85 percent of the world's irrigated agriculture and wastes an estimated 70 percent of the water it uses. Alongside the hardware the company ships N-Drip Connect, a sensor-and-app decision-support platform that measures root-zone water potential and available nitrogen, layers NDVI satellite imagery over the field, and issues irrigation and fertilization recommendations to growers. N-Drip technology is deployed in ten countries and five US states across 25 crop types including rice, corn, soybeans, potatoes, sugar cane, alfalfa and cotton, with a US production hub in Yuma, Arizona. N-Drip publishes no public developer program, API documentation, SDK or machine-readable API contract: N-Drip Connect is delivered strictly as a closed web and mobile application.

providers.name: Naver
providers.description: Naver Corp. is South Korea's largest internet company, operating the Naver search portal, Naver Webtoon, Naver Pay, Naver Maps, Naver Shopping, WORKS Mobile, and the LINE messenger platform (jointly with SoftBank via LY Corporation). Naver runs two distinct public developer surfaces: Naver Developers (developers.naver.com) which hosts Naver's classic Open APIs — Search (blog, news, book, encyclopedia, café, knowledge, web, image, shop, doc), Papago N2MT translation, Naver Login (OAuth 2.0), Naver Maps geocoding and static map, Datalab trend, CAPTCHA, and SmartEditor; and Naver Cloud Platform (www.ncloud.com) — Naver's IaaS / PaaS offering with Compute (Server, Container, Functions), Storage (Object, Block, File), Network (VPC, CDN+, Global Edge), AI (CLOVA Speech, CLOVA OCR, Papago, HyperCLOVA X), Maps, SENS (SMS / push messaging), Cloud Search, and Certificate Manager.

providers.name: Nonnatech
providers.description: Nonnatech is a New York-based remote patient monitoring (RPM) and virtual health company that provides HIPAA-secured technology and clinical services for healthcare providers. Its platform integrates biometric sensors and passive home devices to deliver real-time analytics, chronic condition management, and population health programs across hospitals, health systems, physician practices, payers, ACOs, home care, long-term care, and senior living communities. Nonnatech offers turnkey device ordering, EHR data integration, and optional clinical monitoring, with no upfront costs to providers and roughly 30-day implementation. Nonnatech is a 500 Global portfolio company. It does not publish a public developer program, API documentation, or developer portal.

providers.name: Northrop Grumman
providers.description: Northrop Grumman Corporation is a US global aerospace, defense and security company headquartered in Falls Church, Virginia, organized into four segments: Aeronautics Systems, Defense Systems, Mission Systems and Space Systems. It builds autonomous aircraft, strategic bombers and long-range strike weapons, missile defense and integrated battle command systems, radar and electronic warfare sensors, cyber and command-and-control mission software, solid rocket motors, and space vehicles and launch systems for US Department of Defense, intelligence-community, NASA and allied customers. It publishes no public developer program, API portal or machine-readable API contract; its external integration surfaces are the ADFS-authenticated OASIS supplier tools on myngc.com, available only to registered suppliers under contract.

providers.name: Nura Bio
providers.description: Nura Bio, Inc. is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered in South San Francisco, California, developing neuroprotective small-molecule medicines that halt neurodegeneration before it progresses. Conceived in 2018 by The Column Group together with scientific founders Steve McKnight, PhD and Marc Freeman, PhD, the company targets SARM1 — a neuronally enriched NAD hydrolase that acts as an axon-intrinsic metabolic sensor and central driver of axonal degeneration — on the thesis that intervening early in that pathway confers durable structural and functional neuroprotection across peripheral, central and ocular nervous-system disorders. Its pipeline is led by NB-4746, a first-generation oral, brain-penetrant, reversible orthosteric SARM1 inhibitor in a global Phase 1b/2a study in ALS, and NB-9402, a mechanistically differentiated second-generation oral, covalent, irreversible, allosteric inhibitor completing a Phase 1a healthy-volunteer study in 2026. Nura Bio launched publicly in January 2020 with a $73 million Series A, extended that round with $68 million to pass $140 million raised, and closed a $73.8 million Series B in June 2026 led by The Column Group with Euclidean Capital, Samsara BioCapital and Sanofi Ventures; Shilpa Sambashivan, PhD, a co-founder and its chief scientist, serves as CEO. Its science is published in NEURON and CELL REPORTS. Nura Bio runs no developer program and publishes no product API, developer portal, API reference, SDK or pricing. The only machine-readable surfaces reachable without credentials are a published llms.txt and the WordPress REST content API behind nurabio.com, which serves the news archive, site pages, people directory and media library as JSON — both catalogued here.

providers.name: ObserveIT (Proofpoint)
providers.description: ObserveIT was an insider threat management (ITM) vendor acquired by Proofpoint in 2019 and folded into the Proofpoint Insider Threat Management product line within Proofpoint's Information Protection portfolio. The platform provides endpoint visibility, user activity monitoring, session timelines, and data-loss detection across careless, malicious, and compromised users, correlating activity across endpoints, email, and cloud. Integration is delivered through webhooks that let SIEM and SOAR tools ingest alerts and automated exports to customer-owned AWS S3 storage; ObserveIT no longer operates as a standalone brand and publishes no public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, or self-service API documentation.

providers.name: Outpost Bio
providers.description: Outpost Bio builds frontier AI foundation models for the human microbiome. Its "lab-in-the-loop" platform pairs high-throughput wet-lab experiments with machine learning in a continuous cycle to predict how drugs and ingredients interact with microbial ecosystems, helping de-risk drug and ingredient R&D decisions around metabolism, toxicity, and efficacy. The company's public developer surface is the open-source Waypoint Python library and CLI (published to PyPI as waypoint-bio) plus gated Waypoint model checkpoints, the Atlas pretraining dataset, and the Compass benchmark suite on the Hugging Face Hub. Outpost Bio is a Seedcamp portfolio company and does not currently publish a hosted web API.

providers.name: PadSplit
providers.description: PadSplit is an Atlanta-based co-living marketplace that makes affordable housing accessible by connecting members seeking private rooms in shared homes with property owners who host them. The platform offers flexible weekly payments, fast move-ins, all-inclusive rent (utilities, wifi, and furnishings), member background screening, and a rewards program that helps residents build credit. PadSplit operates across multiple U.S. metros as a two-sided marketplace serving both members (renters) and hosts (property owners), and was backed by Techstars. The company has no public developer program, API, or documentation surface at this time; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: PB Health
providers.description: PB Health (PB Healthcare Service Pvt Ltd) is an India-based consumer healthcare network offering end-to-end care through a single app - online doctor consultations, hospital visits and admissions, lab tests and radiology scans, medicine ordering, diabetes and obesity management, preventive health packages, and structured home care and recovery. The platform spans top specialities including cardiology, gastroenterology, orthopaedics, pulmonology, internal medicine, gynaecology, ENT, paediatrics, and minimal-access and bariatric surgery, and helps families coordinate their complete health and insurance journey. PB Health is a consumer mobile application (iOS and Android) and website; it does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation.

providers.name: PeopleOne Health
providers.description: PeopleOne Health is a nationwide provider of value-based, employer-funded advanced primary care, delivering comprehensive physical and mental health services with no copays, deductibles, or coinsurance for members. Its model pairs dedicated care teams with a prevention-first approach to lower total cost of care for self-funded employers while improving member health outcomes, and it was named a 2024 Best Nationwide Primary Care Provider by the Validation Institute. Surfaced as a portfolio company of GV, PeopleOne Health operates as a healthcare services provider rather than an API platform: member access is delivered through a healow-based patient portal and a member portal, and no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer documentation is published.

providers.name: Perf.ai
providers.description: PerfAI is an autonomous agentic AppSec and auto-fix platform for AI-built apps, helping teams deliver privacy, security, and governance for APIs and applications.

providers.name: Phil
providers.description: PHIL (PHILRx) is a healthtech company operating a digital hub and direct-to-patient platform that helps pharmaceutical brands maximize prescription starts, insurance coverage, affordability, and medication adherence. Its all-in-one platform connects pharma manufacturers, patients, and healthcare providers to streamline the prescription access experience, run affordable direct-to-patient and cash-pay programs, and improve commercial performance across the medication access journey. PHIL is a portfolio company of Uncork Capital. As of this enrichment pass it exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this profile captures its identity and probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: Playabl
providers.description: Playabl is a no-code, conversational game creation platform that lets anyone build games and interactive experiences by chatting with AI. Operated by Replkt, Inc. and backed by Y Combinator, Playabl turns natural-language prompts into playable games across genres including sports, idle, brainrot, dopamine, and think/puzzle categories, with no coding required. The product is a consumer-facing web application (playabl.ai); as of this profile Playabl does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or technical documentation surface. This profile was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline from the company's public web presence.

providers.name: Plenna
providers.description: Plenna is a women's healthcare provider operating a network of integrated medical clinics across Mexico City, redefining health for women across every life stage. Its services span gynecology, maternity and prenatal care, fertility, menopause, contraception, gynecological surgery, psychology, nutrition, laboratory studies, vaccines and lactation support, delivered across six physical clinics (Tlalpan, Coapa, Del Valle, Polanco, San Angel and Satelite) and through Portal Plenna, a patient portal and iOS/Android mobile app for scheduling appointments, virtual consultations, test results, prescriptions and pregnancy tracking. Plenna is a 500 Global portfolio company. It is surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a company profile; no public developer API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Pluang
providers.description: Pluang is an Indonesian multi-asset investment and trading platform that lets retail users invest across a single app in US stocks and ETFs (fractional from $1), Indonesian stocks, cryptocurrencies with staking, mutual funds (Reksa Dana), physical gold and silver, options, and leveraged crypto futures. Features include Auto Invest dollar-cost averaging, the Pocket portfolio bundling tool, TradingView-powered charting, USD yield products, and the Aura AI recommendation assistant. Pluang operates under OJK and Bappebti regulatory oversight across its subsidiaries and reports 12M+ users. It exposes no public developer API; this profile captures its public web, legal, and security surface. Surfaced as an accel portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Possible Finance
providers.description: Possible Finance is a consumer fintech company offering small-dollar installment loans and credit-building products through a mobile app. Its core products are the Possible Loan (up to $500 with flexible repayment schedules), the Possible Advance (up to $300 drawn against a future paycheck), and Bill & Rent Reporting that builds credit history by reporting on-time payments to the credit bureaus. The company charges no late fees or penalty charges and uses AI-driven underwriting based on real banking activity rather than FICO scores, serving borrowers who are underserved by traditional credit. Possible Finance operates as a Delaware Public Benefit Corporation and is backed by Union Square Ventures. It is a mobile-app, consumer-facing product with no public developer API surface; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Qsic
providers.description: Qsic (styled QSIC) is an Australian-founded, AI-driven in-store audio and retail media platform, headquartered in Melbourne with a North American office in Dallas, Texas. The platform blends curated music, targeted audio advertising and store-level intelligence, deploying either over a retailer's existing speaker infrastructure or over premium smart speakers, and adapting playback to ambient conditions, dayparts and shopper behaviour. Qsic sells three connected products — In-Store Audio, Ads and Intelligence — and positions the combination as a way to turn physical stores into measurable retail media networks with store-level performance reporting and demand-side platform integration. Publicly reported deployments include 7-Eleven ("Gulp Radio"), Dollar General, Coles Liquor and Mecca. Qsic runs a live JSON API host at api.getqsic.com and a Vanta-hosted trust center, but publishes no public developer portal, API reference or machine-readable specification as of this profile.

providers.name: Qworum
providers.description: Qworum builds distributed web applications using micro‑frontends and micro‑services architecture. The platform enables developers to compose modular front‑end components that run independently yet integrate seamlessly, offering scalable, maintainable solutions for complex web ecosystems. Qworum provides tooling, runtime support, and APIs to orchestrate these components, targeting modern web development teams seeking flexibility and performance.

providers.name: Radish Health
providers.description: Radish Health is a healthcare company that provides employers with a modern employee health benefit, pairing each member with a dedicated care team and physicians who handle medical issues directly or coordinate specialist referrals. The service emphasizes direct-access primary care over phone, video, and in-person visits, with rapid response times and appointment coordination aimed at reducing employer healthcare costs while improving the patient experience. Radish Health is delivered through patient-facing web and mobile apps (iOS and Android) and an employer benefits program; it is a Techstars portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass, Radish Health publishes no public API, developer portal, or technical documentation — this profile captures its identity, legal/support surfaces, and domain security posture only.

providers.name: Recursyv
providers.description: Recursyv provides enterprise integration and AI solutions, connecting managed service providers (MSPs) with various SaaS platforms such as Autotask, ServiceNow, Jira, HubSpot, ConnectWise, HaloPSA, Freshservice, and CRM systems. Their platform offers ready‑made integrations, bespoke use cases, and managed integration services, supported by a support portal and pricing plans. Recursyv aims to streamline service‑desk to service‑desk workflows and deliver AI‑enhanced automation for B2B customers.

providers.name: Rediem
providers.description: Rediem is a community loyalty platform that enables brands to build personalized, omnichannel loyalty programs. It offers tools for zero‑party data collection, AI receipt scanning, quizzes, polls, surveys, and gamified experiences to deepen customer relationships. The no‑code builder lets teams launch and adapt programs without developer bottlenecks, while impact dashboards showcase social and environmental contributions. Rediem aims to transform loyalty from point‑based systems into community‑driven engagement, supporting brands in retaining customers and driving sustainable growth.

providers.name: Regular Finance
providers.description: Regular Finance (Regular) is a French fintech offering a consumer digital-asset yield account. Customers deposit euros by bank transfer and earn roughly 5.50% annual interest paid daily, backed by regulated stablecoins such as EURC and USDC placed into on-chain liquidity pools and yield protocols. Withdrawals are free at any time and no crypto knowledge is required. Regular is a Techstars-backed company headquartered in France; the product is entirely consumer-facing (web and mobile app at app.regular.eu) and publishes no public developer API, SDK, MCP server, or technical documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Rezilient Health
providers.description: Rezilient Health is an employer-sponsored primary and specialty care provider that combines physical CloudClinics with telehealth to deliver unlimited, zero-cost care to employees on behalf of employers, health plans, health systems, and brokers. Its hybrid CloudClinic model pairs on-site medical staff with remote physicians and connected diagnostic equipment so members can access in-person and virtual visits, with the goal of lowering total healthcare spend and improving clinical outcomes. Rezilient offers patient-facing web and mobile apps for scheduling and care, but publishes no public developer portal, API, SDK, or documentation surface. This profile was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; the honest result is that Rezilient operates a consumer/enterprise healthcare service rather than a developer platform.

providers.name: Season Health
providers.description: Season Health is a food-as-medicine platform that helps people living with chronic conditions eat well and live well. It connects patients with registered dietitians, personalized nutrition and meal plans, and medically-tailored groceries and meals, and works with health plans and care providers to deliver nutrition care as a covered benefit. The consumer and provider experiences run through app.seasonhealth.com; the company is a HIPAA-covered digital health service. Season Health is backed by a16z. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs — api.seasonhealth.com is a private application backend — so this profile captures the company's real public web properties rather than an API program.

providers.name: SiMa
providers.description: SiMa.ai is a Silicon Valley machine-learning semiconductor company building a co-optimized hardware and software platform for physical AI at the edge. Its MLSoC (Machine Learning System-on-Chip) family — including the Modalix line delivering roughly 50 TOPS under 10 watts in multiple form factors — targets drones, robotics, automotive, industrial, retail, government, and healthcare. The developer experience centers on the Palette software suite and an agentic development environment that compiles and deploys computer-vision and multimodal models onto SiMa silicon, backed by a Developer Center, a model browser, a Hugging Face model hub (simaai), and a community forum. SiMa.ai ships downloadable SDK/CLI tooling and evaluation hardware (Modalix DevKit) rather than a hosted public HTTP API.

providers.name: Sira Medical
providers.description: Sira Medical develops augmented reality software that transforms 3D radiological imaging into patient-specific holographic models projected onto real-world backgrounds. Delivered through head-mounted AR devices (such as Microsoft HoloLens) and mobile platforms, the technology helps surgeons perform preoperative planning with greater confidence, clinicians educate patients with understandable visualizations, medical schools train students on patient-specific anatomy, and medical-device makers design and validate implants. The company is backed by 500 Global, Eileses Capital, UCSF Innovation Ventures, and Microsoft for Startups. Sira Medical operates as a clinical AR software vendor and does not currently expose a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its public identity, legal, and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Slice
providers.description: Slice provides a global equity compliance and tax platform that helps companies manage cap tables, equity grants, stock options, and related regulatory reporting across multiple jurisdictions. Their SaaS solution automates equity plan administration, share registry, warrant management, and compliance workflows, offering tools for board approvals, 83(b) elections, and global reporting to keep companies tax‑compliant and reduce manual effort.

providers.name: Solovis
providers.description: Solovis is a multi-asset investment analytics and portfolio management software platform for institutional investors, including endowments, foundations, pension plans, outsourced CIOs (OCIOs), and family offices. It aggregates data across public and private asset classes into a single dashboard for portfolio modeling, performance analysis, risk analytics, and reporting. Core products include Portfolio Analytics, Risk Analytics, Predict (performance and risk prediction for asset allocation), Risk Pro (factor-based risk analytics, formerly Venn Pro), and Analyst Services for outsourced data capture and portfolio data aggregation. Solovis became part of Nasdaq's investment intelligence business following its 2020 acquisition. The platform is delivered as a private, authenticated SaaS accessed through a client login; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer API, documentation portal, OpenAPI specification, or `/.well-known/` discovery surface. The host api.solovis.com exists but is fully authentication-gated (HTTP 401) with no public specification.

providers.name: SyncOnSet Technologies
providers.description: SyncOnSet Technologies is an Emmy Award-winning digital continuity, inventory, and money-tracking platform for film and television production, now part of Entertainment Partners. It replaces paper continuity binders with a collaborative online/offline web and mobile app that manages automatic script breakdowns and revisions, continuity photos, costume and wardrobe pieces, hair and makeup looks, props, set decoration, and locations, alongside per-character and per-scene budgeting and asset reports from prep through wrap. SyncOnSet is a login-gated SaaS application (production teams access it by account) and exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or self-serve developer program, so this profile captures its identity, published web properties, and a domain-security probe rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Syvizo
providers.description: Syvizo provides a low-code/no-code API platform that enables developers to design, build, test, and govern APIs and integrations without lock‑in. Their Open Studio offers visual API creation, while Open Runtime runs open‑source projects. The NextGen API Gateway delivers advanced traffic management, security, and governance features. Syvizo aims to simplify API lifecycle management for enterprises and developers alike, emphasizing flexibility, open standards, and integration capabilities across cloud environments.

providers.name: Tagged
providers.description: Tagged is a social discovery and dating platform founded in 2004 and based in San Francisco, where members browse profiles of people nearby or worldwide, chat, play social games, exchange tags and virtual gifts, and make new connections. Originally a standalone social network backed by early investors including Uncork Capital (formerly SoftTech VC), Tagged was acquired by MeetMe in 2017 for roughly 60 million dollars and today operates as a consumer brand within The Meet Group (part of the ParshipMeet Group) alongside apps such as MeetMe, Skout, and LOVOO. The current tagged.com is a consumer-facing web and mobile social-dating experience with no public developer program or API; a legacy REST-style API (tagged.com/api.php) that once powered third-party integrations has been retired. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record rather than an API producer.

providers.name: Tellus
providers.description: Tellus is a consumer fintech company whose mobile app pairs high-yield savings tools with real-estate-backed lending and property management. Members earn competitive rates on cash held in Tellus accounts, funded by the company's portfolio of residential real-estate loans, with deposits held at FDIC-insured partner banks. The app also offers a mobile wallet, a business wallet, and property-management tooling for landlords and property owners. Tellus is a private, venture-backed startup (an a16z portfolio company); it operates as a direct-to-consumer mobile product and does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation.

providers.name: Tiff's Treats
providers.description: Tiff's Treats is an Austin, Texas cookie company founded in 1999 by University of Texas students Tiffany Taylor and Leon Chen, built around warm, baked-to-order cookies delivered same-day. The company operates roughly 90 bakery-storefronts across Texas and the southern and western United States, combining walk-in retail with an owned delivery fleet, an online ordering platform at cookiedelivery.com, and iOS and Android ordering apps. Alongside consumer delivery it runs a substantial corporate gifting, catering, e-gift-card and special-events business, plus an "Elites" subscription membership and a rewards program. Tiff's Treats has raised more than $50 million in outside investment, including a $25 million round led by Morgan Stanley Expansion Capital, and counts Andy Roddick, Brooklyn Decker, Kendra Scott and Dirk Nowitzki among its investors. It is a direct-to-consumer food and delivery operator, not a software vendor: it publishes no developer portal, no public API, and no machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Trade Republic
providers.description: Trade Republic is a Berlin-based digital bank and Europe's largest savings platform, offering commission-optimized trading of stocks, ETFs, derivatives, and crypto, ETF and stock savings plans, interest on uninvested cash, and a Visa card. Trade Republic Bank GmbH holds a full German banking license and serves customers across European markets. The company publishes no public developer API, API documentation, or first-party SDKs — its mobile and web apps run on a private WebSocket-based backend (api.traderepublic.com) that a community ecosystem of unofficial clients has grown around.

providers.name: TransDigm Group
providers.description: TransDigm Group is a leading global designer, producer, and supplier of highly engineered aerospace components, systems, and subsystems for use on nearly all commercial and military aircraft. The company operates 49 independent operating units producing proprietary, sole-source components including actuation systems, ignition systems, fuel systems, airframe and flight control components, cockpit security systems, seatbelts, airbags, pumps, valves, switches, and cockpit displays. TransDigm serves commercial airlines, defense OEMs, aerospace distributors, and the US Department of Defense.

providers.name: TrustBooks
providers.description: TrustBooks provides a cloud‑based trust accounting solution tailored for small law firms, ensuring compliance with State Bar trust accounting requirements. The platform automates 3‑way reconciliations, generates detailed reports, and offers a free 14‑day trial to streamline trust account management. It helps firms maintain accurate records, meet regulatory standards, and improve operational efficiency.

providers.name: UCBOS
providers.description: UCBOS, operating under the brand Karolium, provides a zero‑code enterprise AI platform that enables businesses to integrate, orchestrate, and compose applications without writing code. The platform offers iPaaS, oPaaS, aPaaS, and AIPaaS capabilities, including supplier collaboration, procurement control tower, contract manufacturing, and predictive analytics such as lead‑time prediction and demand forecasting. It targets enterprises seeking rapid digital transformation, operational intelligence, and reduced technical debt.

providers.name: Vedanta Biosciences
providers.description: Vedanta Biosciences is a late clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered at 19 Blackstone Street in Cambridge, Massachusetts, founded by PureTech Health together with a group of scientific co-founders who pioneered the modern understanding of cross-talk between the human microbiome and the immune system. The company develops a potential new category of oral Live Biotherapeutic Products built from rationally defined consortia of human commensal bacteria grown from pure clonal cell banks rather than donor-derived stool, and it maintains technical expertise in the manufacture of live organisms. Its lead program, VE303, is an eight-strain defined bacterial consortium in the global Phase 3 RESTORATiVE303 registrational study for the prevention of recurrent Clostridioides difficile infection, following Phase 2 results showing a greater than 80% reduction in the odds of CDI recurrence versus placebo; VE202 is in development for inflammatory bowel disease and VE707 for prevention of multidrug-resistant organism infections. Vedanta has raised a $68 million Series D and a $106.5 million financing, and its programs are supported by non-dilutive awards from BARDA and CARB-X. Vedanta is a therapeutics developer, not a software vendor: it runs a WordPress marketing and corporate site, publishes no developer portal, no SDKs, no GitHub organization and no machine-readable API contract, and an August 2026 probe of vedantabio.com found no OpenAPI, no /llms.txt, no MCP endpoint, no A2A agent card and an empty /.well-known/ discovery surface.

providers.name: VetSource
providers.description: VetSource is a veterinary technology and pharmacy company founded in 2008 that delivers a suite of pharmacy, technology, and business services for the pet health industry. Its offerings span home-delivery prescription management (an online pharmacy and prescription workflow that lets veterinary practices prescribe and fulfill medications with compliance and revenue tools), the Vet2Pet client-engagement platform (a custom-branded app connecting practices with pet owners for communication, reminders, loyalty, and telehealth), and data/analytics services that provide industry benchmarking and practice performance insights. VetSource serves veterinary practices and pet owners across North America. No public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation is published; this profile captures the company identity and probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: Wialon
providers.description: Wialon provides a comprehensive fleet management and digitalization platform, offering GPS tracking, asset monitoring, and telematics integration for vehicles, equipment, and personnel. Their services include a robust API and SDKs for developers to build custom solutions, a marketplace of integrations, and tools for analytics, routing, and compliance. The company serves logistics, transportation, agriculture, and public sector customers worldwide.

providers.name: Wonderskin
providers.description: Wonderskin is a direct-to-consumer beauty and cosmetics brand best known for its WONDER BLADING all-day peel-off lip stain, along with longwear eyeliners, serum foundations, blush, brow products, skincare, and beauty tools sold through its Shopify-powered online store. The company runs a SKINSIDER loyalty membership, publishes THE SKINSIDER beauty and lifestyle blog, and partners with athletes and celebrities on product marketing. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Insight Partners. As a consumer e-commerce retailer, Wonderskin publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable API surface; this profile captures the brand identity, customer-facing web properties, and a domain-security probe rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Zed
providers.description: Zed is a BSP-supervised fintech building a premium consumer credit card for Southeast Asians, headquartered in Manila with an engineering team in San Francisco. Its flagship product is the Zed Card, a Titanium Mastercard with no foreign transaction fees, no annual fees, flexible installments, and an accompanying mobile app that offers real-time statements, spend notifications, and unlimited self-destructing virtual cards for online purchases. The company raised a $16.5M Series A led by Accel with participation from Valar Ventures and fintech operators from Nubank, Square, and Mercury. Zed is a consumer-facing financial product and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation.

providers.name: Zen Cart
providers.description: Zen Cart is an open‑source e‑commerce platform that enables merchants to build and manage online stores. It offers a flexible, modular architecture with a wide range of extensions, themes, and payment integrations, supporting both small businesses and larger enterprises. The community‑driven project provides extensive documentation, developer guides, and support forums, allowing developers to customize and extend functionality through plugins and custom code.

providers.name: Zenlist
providers.description: Zenlist is a collaborative home-search platform for real estate agents and their clients, with MLS-level search on MLS inventory, in-app chat, listing notes, showing requests and itineraries across Mac, Windows, iOS and Android apps, and enterprise offerings for brokerages, teams and MLSs (for example the SFAR MLS mobile app). It contributes open-source RESO tooling on GitHub, including a Rust implementation of RESO RCP-19 RETS validation expressions with compliance tests, and runs a public Rules Playground (rules.zenlist.dev) for listing validation rules. Zenlist publishes no public API, developer documentation or machine-readable contract.

providers.name: Aboon
providers.description: Aboon is a digital 401(k) retirement-plan platform and third-party administrator (TPA) that helps financial advisors and employers design, launch, and manage workplace retirement plans. It pairs AI-powered workflows with dedicated human plan consultants to generate customized 401(k) proposals in minutes, streamline recordkeeper onboarding, handle digital plan contracting and census intake, and run ongoing compliance testing and Form 3(16) administration. Aboon markets partnerships with major recordkeepers (American Funds, Empower, John Hancock, and others) and serves a network of advisors nationwide. It is a fintech company backed by Bain Capital Ventures. No public developer/API surface has been identified.

providers.name: acjlabs-com
providers.description: ACJ Labs (Agentic Commerce Junction Labs) is an Australian‑based portfolio lab building focused, inspectable software tools for the agentic‑commerce ecosystem. Their products include catalog attribute normalization, receipt extraction, and other MCP‑style APIs that provide transparent confidence scores and plain‑English rationales. All tools are open‑source, MIT‑licensed, and offered on a free tier with no credit‑card required. The company operates under IMD Solutions Pty Ltd (ABN 72 124 377 635).

providers.name: AImport
providers.description: AImport provides Argentine import intelligence, offering data on imports, tariffs, and product origins. The platform aggregates customs data, presenting dashboards, radar views, and AI‑driven insights for businesses and developers. Users can explore import statistics, connect their systems via ImportConnect, and query the data through AI assistants like ImportBrain. The service is in beta, delivering free access to import data and upcoming paid plans.

providers.name: Amgen
providers.description: Amgen is committed to unlocking the potential of biology for patients suffering from serious illnesses by discovering, developing, manufacturing and delivering innovative human therapeutics. As a pioneer in biotechnology since 1980, Amgen uses living cells to make biologic medicines addressing cardiovascular metabolic conditions, oncology, inflammation, rare diseases, and bone health, operating in approximately 100 countries worldwide.

providers.name: Angi
providers.description: Angi (formerly Angie's List, founded 1995) is a digital home services marketplace connecting homeowners with home service professionals for repair, maintenance, and improvement projects. Angie's List merged with IAC's HomeAdvisor in 2017 under parent ANGI Homeservices Inc.; in March 2021 the consumer brand and parent company were both renamed Angi, with HomeAdvisor continuing as the pro-facing "Angi Leads" lead-generation business. IAC fully spun off its stake in April 2025, making Angi Inc. (NASDAQ: ANGI) an independent public company. Angi does not operate a self-serve public developer portal or publish an API reference. It does offer a gated, partner-only lead-delivery mechanism: Angi Ads/Angi Leads pushes new homeowner leads as JSON to a webhook URL a pro's CRM provides (authenticated with an X-API-KEY header), and an OAuth-style "Sign in with Angi" account-linking flow used by a short list of approved CRM/field-service partners (ServiceTitan, Jobber) to receive lead and booking data. Both require a direct arrangement with an Angi Ads Client Success Manager rather than self-serve API keys.

providers.name: AquaMania
providers.description: AquaMania manufactures PVC furniture for pools and changing rooms, offering a configurator, pricing, and tender package tools for B2B customers. Based in Saint‑Petersburg since 2017, the company provides 9 years of experience, 162 SKUs, and 9 MCP tools for contractors, designers, and government orders.

providers.name: Atypical AI
providers.description: Atypical AI is an artificial-intelligence and learning-science lab building generative-AI learning products for educators, learners, and content creators. Its flagship product, ExamJam, is an AI tutor that pairs adaptive, personalized tutoring with trusted exam content from major publishers (Pearson, McGraw Hill, Collins) to help students prepare for and revise toward their exams. Founded in 2023 and based in San Francisco, the woman-owned company builds personalized tutoring, exam preparation, content creation, collaboration, and student-success measurement tools grounded in learning science. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of bloomberg-beta; it publishes a consumer product surface (web + mobile) and no public developer API at this time.

providers.name: Aura Finance
providers.description: Aura Finance is an employer-sponsored financial wellness platform that blends behavioral psychology with money management to help employees reach financial stability and peace of mind. The San Francisco fintech — a Techstars Economic Mobility 2023 company and an SEC-registered investment adviser (CRD 318940) — delivers goal-based automated investing, one-on-one financial coaching over chat, budgeting and saving tools, financial-literacy workshops, mindfulness exercises to reduce money stress, and a money-personality quiz, offered through a B2B2C model to organizations and their workforces. The company publishes no public developer program, API, or SDKs; its member application lives at web.aurafi.io.

providers.name: Autobooks
providers.description: Autobooks provides a connected banking platform for small businesses, offering invoicing, payment links, checkout pages, tap‑to‑pay, bill payment, accounting, lending and cash‑balance tools. It integrates receivables, payables and financial reporting into digital banking, enabling businesses and their banks to see real‑time financial activity.

providers.name: Beam
providers.description: Beam is a construction financial management platform for residential and commercial contractors, headquartered in San Francisco. Its cloud software unifies estimating and proposals, progress invoicing with online payment collection, job costing and real-time profitability, expense management via the Beam Card, bill-pay automation, lien-waiver and compliance tracking, project management (daily logs, scheduling, change orders), and a cash-management account that earns cash back. Beam integrates with QuickBooks Online, CompanyCam, RenoFi and XactRemodel, and relies on vetted partners including Stripe, Footprint and CapitalOS for payments and KYC/KYB. Beam does not currently publish a public developer API, documentation surface, or SDKs; this profile captures its identity and security posture.

providers.name: Being Health
providers.description: Being Health is a modern psychiatry practice that provides psychiatry, Spravato® treatment, psychotherapy, functional medicine and wellness services—all in one place. It offers integrated mental health care with in‑network insurance plans, virtual and in‑person appointments, and a focus on coordinated treatment for conditions such as anxiety, depression, PTSD, and more. Founded in 2023 and based in New York, Being Health aims to improve mental wellbeing through comprehensive, evidence‑based care.

providers.name: Boundaryintelligentcontrol
providers.description: Boundary provides runtime context governance for enterprise AI, enabling organizations to control what business context AI systems can access before sensitive data reaches the model. Their platform offers field-level classification, fail-closed design, and integrates with various enterprise tools to ensure data privacy and compliance across AI deployments.

providers.name: C the Signs
providers.description: C the Signs is a London-based healthcare technology company, founded in 2016 by Dr Bea Bakshi and Dr Miles Payling, that uses artificial intelligence to help clinicians detect and refer patients at risk of cancer at the earliest, most treatable stage. Registered as an MHRA Class I medical device, its clinical decision support platform analyzes more than 1,000 validated, evidence-based data points across signs, symptoms and risk factors to recommend the right investigations or urgent referrals in under 60 seconds. The platform is used widely across the UK's NHS and health systems, has helped identify over 70,000 patients with cancer across 100+ cancer types at reported 99% sensitivity, and is backed by an $8M Series A investment from Khosla Ventures. It has no public developer API; this profile tracks the company as an API Evangelist network lead.

providers.name: Cado Gifts
providers.description: Cado Gifts, Inc. (CADO Gifting) is a luxury and corporate gifting company operating a Shopify-hosted direct-to-consumer storefront at cadogifting.com, serving the UAE and international markets with curated executive, host, and occasion gift collections plus a corporate/bulk gifting program. The business runs on Shopify (customer accounts, checkout, and blog/journal content) rather than a first-party public API; it was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. No developer program, OpenAPI, or public API documentation is published; the only machine surface discovered is Shopify's Customer Account OIDC/OAuth well-known documents served under the store's own host.

providers.name: CalculPro
providers.description: CalculPro provides professional online calculation tools for the building industry, offering over 120 calculators covering heating, plumbing, ventilation, electricity, structure, and more. The platform follows French DTU, NF, and Eurocode standards, delivering detailed formulas, references, and calculation notes to help architects, engineers, and tradespeople justify designs and generate client proposals.

providers.name: Chefhero
providers.description: Chefhero, now operating as Notch, provides a cloud‑based platform that automates accounts receivable, invoice management and payment processing for food‑service businesses and other SMBs. The Toronto‑based company rebranded in 2021 to focus on digitizing the wholesale food‑service supply chain, offering tools for customers, distributors and finance teams to streamline billing, collections and reconciliation.

providers.name: Chipotle Mexican Grill
providers.description: Chipotle Mexican Grill is a Fortune 500 fast-casual restaurant chain serving burritos, bowls, tacos, salads, and quesadillas made with responsibly sourced, classically-cooked, real ingredients. Founded in 1993 in Denver, Colorado and headquartered in Newport Beach, California, Chipotle operates more than 3,500 restaurants across the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, France, Germany, Kuwait, and the United Arab Emirates. The company is widely recognized as a digital ordering and loyalty leader in the restaurant industry through its Chipotle Rewards program, native iOS and Android apps, and digital ordering platforms (web ordering, group ordering, and catering). Chipotle does not currently publish a public consumer-facing developer API catalog; partner integrations such as third-party delivery (DoorDash, Uber Eats, Grubhub) are managed through bilateral agreements, and supplier and franchise integrations occur through internal portals.

providers.name: Cobalt
providers.description: Cobalt is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: vc-portfolio; backed by techstars) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.

providers.name: Coinslot
providers.description: Coinslot provides micro‑APIs that AI agents can pay for autonomously via x402 (USDC). No signup is required – insert a coin and get a result. The platform offers 12 micro‑APIs, each callable by AI or humans with credits, built and operated by an AI. It aims to be the vending machine for machines, exposing simple, pay‑per‑call endpoints for tasks like currency conversion, weather, and more.

providers.name: Constellaintelligence
providers.description: Constella provides identity risk intelligence and dark web monitoring through high‑velocity APIs. It aggregates verified breach data, compromised credentials, and other identity signals from surface, deep, and dark web sources. The platform offers real‑time threat data via a secure API endpoint, enabling organizations to detect account takeover, session hijacking, ransomware precursors, and other identity‑based attacks. Constella serves enterprises, fintech, law‑enforcement, and security teams with curated, de‑duplicated data, extensive coverage of over 1 trillion records, and flexible integration options for risk modeling and investigative workflows.

providers.name: Copify
providers.description: Copify is a digital marketing agency that provides services such as paid media, SEO, web design, social media marketing, content creation, and e‑commerce marketing to businesses across various industries. It offers consulting and campaign management to help clients increase conversions, grow revenue, and manage ad spend.

providers.name: Crytek
providers.description: Crytek is a German video game developer and publisher, known for creating the CryEngine and titles such as Far Cry, Crysis, and Hunt: Showdown. The company focuses on cutting‑edge graphics technology and immersive gaming experiences, operating globally with offices in Frankfurt, Berlin, and international studios. Crytek provides developer tools, game updates, and community support through its official website and various digital platforms.

providers.name: Culturerobotics
providers.description: Culture Biosciences (formerly Culturerobotics) provides cloud‑connected bioreactor platforms and software for cell culture and bioprocess development. Their suite includes the Console software, Stratyx and Nexxys bioreactors, enabling remote experiment design, real‑time monitoring, data analytics, and AI‑driven insights. The company serves synthetic biology, protein therapeutics, and viral vector developers, offering resources such as white papers, technical bulletins, case studies, and webinars to accelerate bioprocess innovation.

providers.name: Curative
providers.description: Curative is a health insurance and healthcare services company founded in 2020 that reengineered the employer-based health plan around simplicity, engagement, and cost transparency. Its fully insured and level-funded plans give members a competitive monthly premium with zero copays, deductibles, or out-of-pocket costs, starting each member with a baseline visit that tailors a preventative care plan. Curative serves more than 1,200 employer clients and over 165,000 members, reached profitability, and achieved unicorn status ($1.275B valuation) following a $150M Series B round backed by DCVC. Curative operates as a HIPAA-regulated health plan; it has no public developer/API program, so this API Evangelist profile captures company identity, its member/provider web surface, and probed domain-security posture rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Curve
providers.description: Curve is a London-based fintech, founded in 2015 by Shachar Bialick, that consolidates multiple debit and credit cards into a single smart card and mobile wallet. Its "over-the-top" banking platform lets customers spend from any linked Mastercard or Visa card, switch the funding source of a past purchase up to 120 days later with "Go Back in Time", avoid foreign-exchange fees, earn cashback, and pay in instalments with Curve Flex. Premium tiers (Curve Pay X / Pro / Pro+) add insurance, lounge access, and richer rewards. Curve is backed by Seedcamp and Speedinvest among others. Curve does not publish a public developer API — it acts as an open-banking consumer to aggregate customer account balances rather than exposing a provider API.

providers.name: DataNexus MCP
providers.description: DataNexus MCP provides public data intelligence for AI agents, offering 55 tools across seven data categories including nonprofit, security, compliance, patents, domain, govcon, and regulatory information. Users can connect via Claude.ai in seconds, obtain API keys through a simple signup, and access comprehensive documentation and use‑case examples. The platform emphasizes open access to structured data for AI-driven insights and supports integration through multiple SDKs and third‑party portals.

providers.name: DataSynca
providers.description: DataSynca provides an integration, automation, and AI gateway platform that connects disparate systems, automates workflows, and incorporates AI-driven decision making. The platform offers a visual canvas, pre-built connectors for 400+ apps, data mapping, and enterprise deployment options, targeting regulated industries such as banking, insurance, healthcare, and the public sector.

providers.name: Daupler
providers.description: Daupler provides a cloud-based Response Management System (RMS) for utilities, public works, and service organizations that automates and coordinates emergency and service-request response. Its product suite spans Daupler Answering (after-hours call center), Dispatch Assist and AI-driven call management, Callout crew notification, Notify mass notification via SMS/email/phone, Engage customer portal, Event Detection for multi-incident coordination, and Analytics for incident and team-performance insight. Daupler serves water, sewer, electric, multi-utility, trash-collection, and public-works operators. The RMS is built on RESTful services and integrates with CMMS, work-order, AMI, IoT sensor, billing, CIS, CRM, OMS, GIS, and citizen-request systems, though Daupler exposes no public self-serve developer API or documentation. Backed by Techstars.

providers.name: Discz
providers.description: Discz is a consumer mobile application that blends music discovery with social chat, styled as a modern, MySpace-inspired music community. Users discover songs, build music profiles, and chat with others around shared taste in music. The iOS app is developed by Discz, a Y Combinator-backed startup and a portfolio company of DCM Ventures. Discz publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; its surface is the consumer iOS app distributed through the Apple App Store.

providers.name: Djust
providers.description: DJUST is a French all-in-one, modular B2B commerce platform that helps distributors, wholesalers, manufacturers and retailers launch and automate their B2B eCommerce and eProcurement operations. The platform covers automated order management (24/7 online ordering), AI-assisted quoting with automatic pricing and discounts, integrated online payments with deadline tracking, a conversational AI sales assistant, real-time sales analytics, and prebuilt ERP/CRM integrations. Customers include Eiffage, Auchan Retail and Lesaffre; DJUST reports EUR 1.5B GMV and 2M orders processed in 2025. Backed by Speedinvest.

providers.name: eGifter
providers.description: eGifter is a digital gift card platform that allows people to easily send and receive gift cards for a wide variety of retailers and brands. Users can choose from hundreds of options including popular stores, restaurants, and entertainment venues. Whether it's for a birthday, holiday, or just to show appreciation, eGifter makes it simple to find the perfect gift for any occasion.

providers.name: ELEV8
providers.description: EAS Innovations Inc operates ELEV8, an end-to-end, cloud-based dealer management system (DMS) built for independent auto dealers and automotive finance companies. The platform unifies real-time accounting, inventory management, CRM and desking, loan servicing, payments and collections into a single fully-integrated system. It offers per-seat pricing, user-based access rights, user-level audit logs, whitelisted IP addresses, multi-rooftop access and department-level restrictions, and is delivered as a SaaS web application at app.elev8dms.com. EAS Innovations is a 500 Global portfolio company. No public developer API is currently published.

providers.name: Eloquii
providers.description: ELOQUII is a plus-size women's fashion retailer offering trend-driven, fashion-forward apparel and accessories in sizes 14 through 32, including dresses, workwear, outerwear, denim, and occasion wear with frequent seasonal collection refreshes. Known for its fit-obsessed design and inclusive sizing, the brand operates a direct-to-consumer ecommerce storefront at eloquii.com alongside select retail locations. ELOQUII was founded as a plus-size line, acquired by Walmart in 2018, and is now part of FullBeauty Brands. It was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; it publishes a consumer ecommerce experience but no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Enable
providers.description: Enable Medicine is a healthcare and life-sciences data company that licenses an integrated, AI-ready index of clinical, spatial, cellular, and molecular data. Its research platform helps biopharma companies, academic institutions, and healthcare providers run spatial-biology analysis — spatial proteomics, cell phenotyping, tumor-microenvironment characterization, immune profiling, and biomarker identification — across 20+ disease areas over harmonized datasets spanning 10M+ patients and 125M+ cells. The platform is delivered through a login-gated web application at app.enablemedicine.com; no public developer API is currently documented. Backed by initialized-capital, insight-partners, lightspeed-venture-partners, menlo-ventures, norwest-venture-partners, and sierra-ventures.

providers.name: Enfusion
providers.description: Enfusion is a cloud-native, front-to-back investment management platform for hedge funds and asset managers, unifying portfolio management (PMS), order and execution management (OEMS), pre- and post-trade compliance, a unified IBOR/ABOR accounting book of record, and analytics on a single SaaS database. It serves over 1,000 clients across 30 countries, offers direct connectivity to 300+ liquidity sources via FIX, and maintains a 4M+ instrument security master. Enfusion was acquired by Clearwater Analytics (CWAN) in 2025; the enfusion.com domain now redirects to cwan.com, where Enfusion is offered as a product line. There is no public developer portal or open API specification: the platform API and knowledge base are gated behind the client web application and Zendesk help center. This profile was surfaced as an ICONIQ Capital portfolio lead and enriched from public marketing, support, and legal surfaces.

providers.name: enrich
providers.description: Enrich is a private, invite-only membership network for senior technology leaders — VPs, Directors, and CXOs from companies including Google, Slack, Anthropic, and OpenAI. It runs peer-led conversations with executive coaching, curated small-group and monthly in-person dinners, expert-led operator discussions, topic-based peer groups (organizational design, career transitions), and a private Slack community for real-time peer advice. Backed by Bloomberg Beta and Cowboy Ventures, and added to the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio lead. Enrich publishes no public developer API, SDK, or API documentation surface — it is a community/membership product, not an API provider.

providers.name: Enurgen
providers.description: Enurgen is a solar energy software company whose DUET platform uses 3D physics-based modeling to optimize photovoltaic assets across their entire lifecycle. The platform spans three products - Design, Construction, and Operations - helping large-scale solar developers, independent power producers, EPC engineers, and asset managers improve energy yield estimates, validate construction against expected performance, and monitor plants in production to close the gap between forecasted (P50) and actual field output. Enurgen is a Techstars-backed company; customers include Scatec, Potentia, Lightsource, Eni, and Kiewit. The company operates a customer web application at app.enurgen.com but does not currently publish a public developer API, documentation, or SDKs. This API Evangelist profile is an enrichment pass that captures the company's public web properties and domain security posture.

providers.name: Ergatta
providers.description: Ergatta is a connected-fitness company that makes game-based home rowing machines, pairing WaterRower-derived water-resistance hardware handcrafted in Rhode Island with a gamified software platform of interactive challenges (Endeavor, Meteor, Wavelength), live and on-demand races, scenic rows, coached classes, and custom workouts. Ergatta sells the Luxe and Lite rowers plus upgrade kits for existing WaterRower and Concept2 machines, delivered through a Shopify-hosted direct-to-consumer storefront with a membership subscription. Ergatta does not publish a public developer API; this API Evangelist profile captures its public web surface and identity for network discovery.

providers.name: EspoCRM
providers.description: EspoCRM is an open-source Customer Relationship Management (CRM) platform that enables businesses to manage their sales, marketing, and customer support processes. It offers a flexible, customizable solution with features such as lead management, opportunity tracking, activity streams, and integration capabilities. EspoCRM provides a modern web interface, role-based access control, and extensible architecture through extensions and API access, allowing developers to build custom workflows and integrate with external services. The platform is designed for small to medium-sized enterprises seeking a cost-effective, self-hosted CRM solution.

providers.name: Farmers Insurance Exchange
providers.description: Farmers Insurance Exchange is a Fortune 500 inter-insurance exchange and the largest of the three reciprocal exchanges that make up the Farmers Insurance Group of Companies, underwriting auto, home, specialty property, life and commercial lines across the United States and managed by Farmers Group, Inc. This repository captures any APIs, developer tools, and machine-readable API artifacts associated with Farmers Insurance Exchange. Farmers operates a developer portal at developer.farmers.com titled "Farmers Insurance APIs", but the entire portal is an Okta sign-in wall: no OpenAPI, API reference, quickstart or pricing page is reachable without partner credentials, and the same wall stands in front of the ePartner portal. No public API contract has been observed.

providers.name: Flossy
providers.description: Flossy is a Santa Monica, California healthcare technology company that builds AI agents ("AI coworkers") for dental practices, veterinary clinics and med spas. Its named agents cover front-office and revenue-cycle work: Fiona handles inbound and outbound patient communication and scheduling across phone, SMS and web chat; Betsy scores call-center quality and marketing performance; Michael captures insurance, verifies benefits and surfaces billing insights; and Reid forecasts revenue and optimizes schedule capacity and staffing. FlossyHQ is the operator console the practice works in, and Agent Builder lets practices assemble custom agents. Founded in 2020 by Miles Beckett and Steve Seigel, Flossy began as a pay-as-you-go dental care marketplace and has since repositioned around agentic automation for practice operations. Flossy publishes no public developer program, API reference or machine-readable specification; the one publicly reachable first-party integration surface is the embeddable Fiona web-chat widget.

providers.name: Forwardlane
providers.description: ForwardLane Technologies builds Signal Studio, a decision intelligence platform that transforms enterprise data into auditable actions rather than dashboards. Users ask questions in natural language and receive Next Best Actions with complete audit trails in seconds, powered by a semantic data layer, multi-agent AI orchestration, a no-code signal builder, and in-database processing so data never leaves the customer environment. Validated across eight years of Fortune 500 production, Signal Studio serves financial services, private credit and private equity, real estate, energy and oil and gas, and government, with BYOK support for any LLM, cloud, or inference provider. Led by CEO Nathan Stevenson. ForwardLane exposes no public developer API surface; this profile captures the company's public identity and security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: GMX (mail)
providers.description: GMX (mail) is a German email and cloud service provider offering free webmail, cloud storage, news, and premium upgrades. It serves millions of users with web and mobile interfaces, providing features such as personal email addresses, cloud backup, and integrated news and entertainment content. The service emphasizes security, data protection, and a range of optional paid features for enhanced mailbox capacity and functionality.

providers.name: Good Driver
providers.description: Good Driver Club (formerly Good Driver Mutuality) is an insurtech company backed by Ribbit Capital and Hedosophia. It runs a membership-based, cost-sharing alternative to traditional collision and comprehensive auto coverage: members pay weekly pledges into a shared community pool that covers vehicle damage from accidents, weather, theft, and other qualifying events across 5,000+ partner repair shops nationwide, and accident-free members keep their unused pledge balances as savings. It is explicitly not insurance. The product is delivered through a consumer mobile app (Good Driver Club on Google Play); the company publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: GoodShip
providers.description: GoodShip is a freight orchestration and procurement platform for shippers, brokers, and asset-based carriers. It unifies TMS tender, contract-award, and location data, enriches it with real-time market rates, and layers AI-assisted bid analysis (via its Laney AI transportation analyst), lane- and carrier-level performance analytics, carrier scorecards, and in-app collaboration on top. Teams run mini-bids and full-network RFPs, benchmark spend against the market, and take corrective action without dedicated developer resources. Plug-and-play with major transportation management systems; backed by Bessemer Venture Partners and serving US and Canadian operations.

providers.name: Grid Squid
providers.description: Grid Squid provides a unified CRM API that connects developers to five major CRM platforms, simplifying authentication, bulk import/export, and data synchronization. The service offers a single endpoint to manage contacts, leads, and other CRM entities, reducing integration complexity and accelerating time‑to‑market for SaaS applications.

providers.name: HelprNow
providers.description: HelprNow (operating as Giftr, by Helpr Asia) is Malaysia's leading online gift marketplace, helping people improve relationships with loved ones through a seamless gifting experience. It delivers flowers, cakes, balloons, chocolates, personalised gifts, hampers and gift cards with same-day and nationwide delivery options. The storefront runs on Shopify (helpr-asia.myshopify.com), so its public technical surface is a consumer commerce site rather than a developer API program; the only machine-discoverable interfaces are Shopify's customer-account OAuth2/OpenID Connect endpoints served under giftr.my/.well-known/. Backed by 500 Global; profiled in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead.

providers.name: Hemlane
providers.description: Hemlane is a technology platform for managing long-term rental properties, combining AI tools with human support to assist with tenant placement, rent collection, lease management, maintenance coordination, and eviction support. The platform operates across all 50 US states and has processed over $1.8B in payments.

providers.name: Hidrate
providers.description: HidrateSpark is the world's smartest water bottle brand, tracking daily water intake with a Bluetooth-connected sensor puck that glows to remind you to drink and syncs to the HidrateSpark hydration app, Fitbit, and Apple Watch. The company (originally Hidrate, Inc., a Techstars-backed startup) sells its smart bottles and accessories through a Shopify-hosted direct-to-consumer storefront at hidratespark.com. It does not publish a first-party developer or product API; the only machine-facing surface is the Shopify platform layer — OIDC/OAuth customer accounts and the Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) agent-commerce endpoints that let buyer-approved AI shopping agents browse and check out.

providers.name: Hrmony
providers.description: Hrmony is a Berlin-based employee-benefits platform that lets German employers offer modern, tax-advantaged perks to their staff — meal allowances (Essenszuschuss), the 50 euro monthly non-cash benefit (Sachbezug) and benefit card, mobility and public-transit budgets, health and recreation benefits, internet-cost subsidies and digital gifts — all managed through an admin portal and employee app with built-in payroll and tax compliance. Its Hrmony Embedded product exposes this benefits infrastructure as a white-label RESTful API so software platforms and SaaS providers can integrate multiple benefit modules without building the tax-compliance, operations or regulatory layer in-house. Hrmony is backed by Techstars. This API Evangelist profile was enriched from the company's public web surface; no public developer documentation or OpenAPI is currently published (Embedded onboarding is partner-gated).

providers.name: Instride Health
providers.description: InStride Health is a virtual mental health provider delivering specialized, insurance-based treatment for children, teens, and young adults ages 7 to 24 who struggle with anxiety, OCD, panic, phobias, school avoidance, and related disorders.
