Its structured four-to-eight month program pairs each patient with a coordinated care team of a therapist, a psychiatric prescriber, and an exposure coach, combining evidence-based cognitive behavioral therapy and exposure-and-response prevention delivered over telehealth. The company is backed by General Catalyst and tracked in the API Evangelist network; it operates as a clinical care provider and publishes no public API, developer program, or SDK.

providers.name: Internet Brands
providers.description: Internet Brands is a KKR-owned digital media and software company, founded in 1998 and headquartered in El Segundo, California, that operates a portfolio of vertical franchises across health, dental, legal, and auto/home/travel markets. Its brands include WebMD and Medscape (health), WebMD Ignite and PulsePoint (health engagement), Henry Schein One and Dentrix (dental SaaS), FindLaw and Avvo (legal), and CarsDirect and Fodor's (auto, home, and travel). It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and Redpoint Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. The holding company does not publish a single unified public developer API; developer surfaces live with its individual operating brands.

providers.name: ironSource
providers.description: ironSource is a Tel Aviv-based mobile game growth platform, acquired by Unity Technologies in a $4.4B all-stock deal that closed in November 2022 and is now operated as part of Unity's Grow Solutions group. The company builds an end-to-end suite for mobile game developers spanning ad monetization, user acquisition, and ad operations. Its flagship product LevelPlay is a unified in-app bidding and ad mediation platform that brokers Rewarded Video, Interstitial, and Banner ad demand across the ironSource Ads network, AdMob, AppLovin, Meta Audience Network, Pangle, Mintegral, Unity Ads, Vungle, and dozens of other ad sources. ironSource Ads is its self-serve ad network and user-acquisition platform offering CPI, CPE, ROAS-optimized, and SKAdNetwork-aware campaign management. Adjacent products include Aura (an on-device content marketplace for carriers and OEMs that originated from the 2021 Bigabid/Soomla portfolio and earlier hardware OEM deals), Tapjoy Offerwall (acquired 2022) for rewarded engagement, and Ad Quality for ad-content monitoring. Developer access is via a REST surface hosted at platform.ironsrc.com — including the Monetization Reporting API (v5/v4), ironSource Ads Reporting API, Application API (v6), Campaign API suite (Campaigns, Audiences, Country Groups, Bidding, Assets, Creatives), SKAN Reporting API, and Cost API — authenticated with Bearer tokens issued from the platform dashboard. Real client integration is delivered via native SDKs (iOS, Android, Unity, Flutter, React Native, Adobe AIR, Xamarin) plus the LevelPlay mediation adapter ecosystem published on github.com/ironsource-mobile. As of 2026 the developers.is.com knowledge center 301-redirects to docs.unity.com, consolidating ironSource documentation inside Unity Grow alongside Unity Ads. No public OpenAPI, Postman collection, or JSON Schema bundle is published by ironSource for the REST surface; documentation is human-readable HTML on docs.unity.com/en-us/grow.

providers.name: iTrustCapital
providers.description: iTrustCapital (legal entity ITC2.0, Inc.) is a US fintech software platform for alternative assets, offering 24/7 self-directed access to dozens of cryptocurrencies and physical precious metals through three account types: tax-advantaged self-directed Crypto IRAs for retirement savings, Premium Custody Accounts (PCA) for everyday non-retirement investing, and Treasury Accounts for businesses, trusts, non-profits and other entities. The platform charges a 1% cryptocurrency transaction fee with no monthly, annual, startup, exit, storage or transfer fees, and runs a closed-loop system backed by third-party US banks, custodians (iTrust Custodial Services, Fortis Bank) and institutional storage providers. iTrustCapital is not an exchange, custodian, trust company, broker-dealer or investment adviser; all transactions on the platform are self-directed. As of this profiling pass the company publishes NO public developer API — its own help center states that it "does not offer any API integration to any third-party applications, including self-trading bots and coin trackers." Access is via the web app and the iOS/Android mobile apps only.

providers.name: Its Good
providers.description: It's Good is a social dining recommendation app that reimagines how people discover restaurants and bars by surfacing recommendations from trusted friends rather than crowdsourced reviews from strangers. Founded in 2023 and co-founded by Mike Rosenthal (CEO) and musician John Legend, the iOS app lets people save the places they love, organize their lists, and share personalized recommendations within a curated community of people they know and admire. The company is backed by a seed investment from Lightspeed Venture Partners. It's Good is a consumer mobile product and does not currently publish a public API or developer platform.

providers.name: Jack in the Box
providers.description: Jack in the Box Inc. (NASDAQ: JACK), founded in 1951 and headquartered in San Diego, California, is a quick-service restaurant company operating and franchising approximately 2,200 Jack in the Box hamburger restaurants across 21 U.S. states. In December 2021 the company acquired Del Taco for $575M; in August 2025 it announced a strategic review of Del Taco and on October 2025 agreed to divest Del Taco (~600 locations) to Yadav Enterprises for $115M, with the transaction closing December 22, 2025. Digital channels include the Jack in the Box mobile app, Jack Pack loyalty program, online ordering, and integrations with third-party delivery platforms (DoorDash, Grubhub, Uber Eats). The company does not publish a public developer API; all digital ordering, loyalty, and franchise systems are operated via internal platforms and partner integrations.

providers.name: Josys
providers.description: Josys is a SaaS and IT asset management platform providing automated provisioning, license optimization, and device management. Josys publishes a developer API for programmatic access to the platform.

providers.name: Leaner Technologies
providers.description: Leaner Technologies (株式会社Leaner Technologies) is a Tokyo-based B2B SaaS company founded on February 22, 2019 by CEO Yusuke Ohira, operating under the mission "調達のスタンダードを刷新し続ける" (continuously renew the standard of procurement). It builds the "Leaner" (リーナー) cloud suite for corporate procurement and purchasing departments: Leaner購買 (purchasing), a purchase-to-pay system covering quotation, approval workflow, ordering, receiving and payment; Leaner sourcing, a quotation and sourcing workspace; Leaner Connect, an SRM supplier-relationship platform; plus procurement BPO and consulting services. The platform aggregates supplier and EC catalogs (including Amazon Business and MonotaRO) into cross-catalog search, and applies AI to classify purchasing data for indirect-spend visibility and cost optimization. The company holds ISMS ISO/IEC 27001:2013 / JIS Q 27001:2014 certification (registration JP21/080659, February 2021). Leaner publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or client SDKs as of this enrichment pass — its integration surface is delivered through partner catalog connections rather than a self-serve API program.

providers.name: Life is Tech
providers.description: Life is Tech, Inc. (ライフイズテック株式会社) is a Tokyo-based education technology company founded on 6 July 2010 by Yusuke Mizuno, delivering digital, programming and AI education to Japanese teenagers, schools, municipalities and employers. Its products are "Life is Tech !" IT camps and year-round schools for junior and senior high school students, "Life is Tech ! Lesson" — a cloud-based information and programming curriculum used by roughly 4,000 public and private schools across some 600 municipalities — "Life is Tech ! Leaders" for university students, "Life is Tech ! Career" digital job-hunting support, and DX Readiness corporate digital-skills training. The company is a certified B Corporation (October 2022, the first Japanese EdTech to certify) and holds the PrivacyMark. Life is Tech sells finished learning products to schools and consumers; it publishes no public developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable contract.

providers.name: LiveJournal
providers.description: LiveJournal is a long‑standing blogging and social networking platform founded in 1999. It allows users to create journals, share posts, comment, and interact through communities. The service offers APIs for accessing public journal content, user profiles, and community feeds, supporting developers building integrations and analytics tools. LiveJournal continues to host a vibrant community of writers and readers worldwide.

providers.name: Mocklets
providers.description: Mocklets provides an HTTP-based mock API simulator that helps developers simulate APIs for faster parallel development and more comprehensive testing. It offers a smart way to mock your APIs, enabling teams to create realistic API responses, test edge cases, and accelerate integration workflows without relying on live services.

providers.name: MOO
providers.description: MOO is a London-founded online print and design company that produces premium custom business cards, postcards, flyers, stickers, notebooks, packaging, and branded promotional merchandise for individuals and businesses. Backed by Index Ventures, MOO combines a browser-based design experience with commercial printing, and sells tiered business plans (Business, Advanced, Enterprise) with team management and design services. MOO does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation; its developer-style subdomains resolve to the main storefront rather than an API surface. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.name: Nebex
providers.description: Nebex operates Nebra Exchange, an exchange platform for the global space economy that connects commercial space suppliers, sovereign buyers such as governments and space agencies, and financial institutions. The platform aims to standardize space-commerce infrastructure so demand can find supply faster, workflows can be coordinated across multilateral participants, and capital can participate through transparent structures, facilitating complex transactions from demand to delivery including sourcing, coordination, and settlement. Founded by Tejpaul Bhatia (CEO) and Anand Subramanian (COO), both formerly of Axiom Space, Nebex is backed by GV. The company currently offers early, invite-based access to the Nebra Exchange platform and does not yet publish a public API, developer portal, or SDK program.

providers.name: olareg
providers.description: olareg is an open-source (Apache-2.0) minimal OCI-conformant container registry that runs as a container, a standalone binary, or embedded in Go unit tests, storing content in the OCI Layout.

providers.name: Pacto
providers.description: Pacto is a Mexican fintech company modernizing payment acquisition for banks and hospitality businesses, moving them "de lo legacy a lo digital" (from legacy to digital). Pacto builds point-of-sale (POS) software and payment terminals: a miniPOS terminal and "Ordena y Paga" (order-and-pay) terminals plus value-added modules for banks, and a full restaurant POS suite (Pacto POS, Pacto GetNet, Order & Pay QR ordering, bill splitting, inventory, and reporting) for restaurants, cafes, bars, and fast-food counters. Backed by 500 Global and Banco Santander's GetNet, Pacto helps traditional financial institutions and merchants accept digital card payments and manage operations. This profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company; Pacto publishes a marketing site, blog, and pricing but no public developer API or documentation at this time.

providers.name: Pantomath
providers.description: Pantomath is an AI‑powered Data Operations Center that monitors and autonomously resolves data issues across the entire data stack. It provides a unified observability platform for data pipelines, enabling proactive detection, automated remediation, and comprehensive analytics for enterprises seeking to ensure data reliability and quality.

providers.name: Pivotal Health
providers.description: Pivotal Health (formerly Radix Health) is a healthcare technology company and self-described "IDR Authority" that helps medical providers secure fair out-of-network reimbursement through the federal Independent Dispute Resolution (IDR) process created by the No Surprises Act. Its platform combines automated eligibility screening, dispute submission software integrated with major revenue cycle management (RCM) systems, payer data, and white-glove managed services across emergency medicine, anesthesiology, radiology, surgery, pathology, air ambulance, and hospitals and health systems. Pivotal Health is backed by Bessemer Venture Partners.

providers.name: PROOF
providers.description: PROOF is a digital art and NFT platform built on the belief that "art is proof of our collective humanity." It is the company behind Moonbirds (its flagship profile-picture collection), the 1,000-member PROOF Collective, and collections including Oddities, Mythics, and the Grails art-collector experience, alongside the Lunar Society community-governance program, a research arm, live events, and a podcast. PROOF is backed by a16z and Kindred Ventures. Its public surface is a consumer/collector documentation site (docs.proof.xyz) and marketing site; PROOF does not currently publish a programmatic developer API, OpenAPI spec, SDKs, or webhooks.

providers.name: QueryPal
providers.description: QueryPal provides an agentic AI-powered customer service platform that transforms any application into a self‑driving product. Unlike traditional chatbots, QueryPal's AI researches, reasons, and resolves complex Tier 3 support issues within the customer's secure cloud environment, cutting resolution times in half and dramatically reducing support costs while boosting satisfaction. Backed by Sequoia Capital, the solution scales operations without increasing headcount, offering a seamless, privacy‑first experience for enterprises.

providers.name: QurAlis
providers.description: QurAlis Corporation is a clinical-stage biotechnology company founded on December 12, 2016 in Cambridge, Massachusetts by Drs. Kasper Roet, Kevin Eggan and Clifford Woolf together with Q-State Biosciences, and staffed by neurodegenerative biologists out of Harvard Medical School and Harvard University. The company develops precision medicines for amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), frontotemporal dementia (FTD) and other neurodegenerative and neurological diseases, built on the discovery — published in Nature Neuroscience by co-founder Kevin Eggan's lab — that loss of normal TDP-43 function drives a decrease in STATHMIN-2 (STMN2) expression and impairs neuronal repair. Its lead candidates are QRL-201, a first-in-class molecule intended to restore STMN2 expression in ALS (ANQUR trial), and QRL-101, a potentially best-in-class selective Kv7.2/7.3 ion channel opener for hyperexcitability-induced disease progression in ALS as well as epilepsy and pain; a third program targets UNC13A cryptic-exon mis-splicing. Therapies are built on the proprietary FlexASO® anti-sense oligonucleotide splice-modulator platform. QurAlis publishes a corporate site covering its story, pipeline, platform, people, patient resources, presentations and press releases, but runs no developer program: no API documentation, no SDKs, no developer portal, no GitHub organisation and no machine-readable API contract of any kind.

providers.name: Radial Analytics
providers.description: Radial Analytics, operating as Radial Care, provides AI‑driven decision support software for value‑based care. The platform integrates clinical, claims, and quality data to deliver real‑time, individualized insights for provider organizations such as ACOs, hospitals, and health systems, as well as for payers including Medicare Advantage plans. It aims to reduce total medical expenditure while improving quality of care and operational efficiency.

providers.name: Ribose Inc.
providers.description: Ribose Inc. builds the digital infrastructure for the standards community, providing open‑source platforms that modernize how standards bodies author, publish, and govern their specifications. The company offers tools for collaborative editing, version control, and compliance tracking, serving a global network of standards organizations and contributors.

providers.name: Scuba
providers.description: Scuba (Scuba Analytics, formerly Interana) is a real-time behavioral and customer analytics platform for self-service exploration of large-scale event data, backed by Battery Ventures and DCVC. The company is rebranding to Behavure AI and extending its behavioral query engine to detect drift, explain decisions, and govern AI agents across models, systems, and users. Scuba publishes product user guides, admin guides, a glossary, dated release notes, and a Tableau connector at docs.scuba.io (now docs.behavure.ai), but does not currently expose a public developer REST API reference, SDKs, or machine-readable API specification.

providers.name: Shiori
providers.description: Shiori is an open-source, self‑hosted bookmark manager written in Go. It offers a simple web interface and command‑line tool for adding, editing, deleting, and searching bookmarks, with support for SQLite, PostgreSQL, MariaDB, and MySQL. Shiori can archive page content for offline reading, import from Pocket, and provides optional browser extensions. The project is MIT‑licensed and aims to give users a fast, organized place for all their links.

providers.name: Smartex
providers.description: Smartex is an AI and computer-vision company founded in 2018 and headquartered in Porto, Portugal that builds hardware-enabled software for the textile manufacturing industry. Its systems inspect fabric in real time on the knitting machine to detect defects at the source, cutting textile waste, CO2 emissions, water, energy and rework. The product suite spans CORE (a machine-vision inspection add-on for circular knitting machines), FACT (an all-in-one digital factory-management platform for production visibility and quality control) and LOOP (supply-chain communication and traceability). Smartex is backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, DCVC, Tony Fadell's Build Collective, H&M Group, SOSV/HAX, Spider Capital, Momenta Ventures and Fashion for Good. It does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; customer access is through the FACT platform login. This profile was surfaced from the VC-portfolio pipeline and enriched from Smartex's public web surface.

providers.name: SmartShoot
providers.description: SmartShoot is a San Francisco-based (founded 2012) photography and video production platform that connects enterprises and marketing teams with a managed network of more than 200,000 professional photographers and videographers to produce custom, on-brand photo and video content at scale. The web-based platform coordinates shoot booking, project collaboration, editing, and cloud-based delivery across many locations, serving e-commerce, real estate, and multi-location brands such as Google, YouTube, Uber, Expedia, and Yelp. SmartShoot is a B2B managed-service marketplace with no publicly documented developer API, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDK, MCP server, or developer portal as of this enrichment pass; it was surfaced as a portfolio company of Uncork Capital.

providers.name: Somethings
providers.description: Somethings is a teen mental health support platform that connects adolescents with Certified Peer Specialist Mentors through a mobile app for iOS and Android. Rather than traditional therapy or AI chatbots, teens can call or chat anytime with trained mentors who have personal lived experience overcoming challenges like anxiety, depression, self-harm, eating disorders, and ADHD, backed by clinical supervision. The service is HIPAA-compliant and sold to health plans, insurers, employers, and directly to parents. Somethings is a venture-backed company in the API Evangelist network; it operates a consumer/clinical mobile product and does not currently publish a public developer API surface.

providers.name: StatusPRO
providers.description: StatusPRO is a sports technology and gaming company founded by former professional athletes, building extended reality (XR) products that pair competitive training tools for elite athletes with immersive gaming experiences for consumers. Its flagship product, NFL PRO ERA, is an officially NFL- and NFLPA-licensed virtual reality football game for Meta Quest headsets, and its StatusPRO Visualizer powers immersive broadcast perspectives used by ESPN on NFL Live. The company operates a live-services consumer game rather than a developer platform: it publishes no public API, developer portal, or API documentation. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record; it carries no API surface at this time.

providers.name: Svbtle
providers.description: Svbtle is a minimalist publishing and blogging platform designed to work the way your brain does, pairing a distraction-free Markdown editor with a simple dashboard for organizing drafts, developing ideas, and publishing to a clean reading experience. Created by Dustin Curtis and operated by Neutral Corporation, Svbtle emphasizes longevity through its "Forever Promise" that published writing remains permanently accessible online. Svbtle is a subscription-based writer's network rather than a developer platform: as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI definition, OAuth authorization server, or .well-known metadata, and each blog is exposed only as a human-readable site with an RSS feed.

providers.name: TandemAI
providers.description: TandemAI is an integrated drug discovery contract research organization (CRO) that combines proprietary AI and physics-based computational methods with in-house high-performance computing and extensive wet-lab operations to accelerate pharmaceutical research. Its cloud-enabled, data-centric, browser-based platform, TandemViz, spans hit finding, hit-to-lead and lead optimization, digital assays and workflows, medicinal chemistry and synthesis, biological assays, and a peptide platform. TandemAI is offered as an FTE-based service model that bundles wet-lab services with complimentary access to its AI and computational tools, or as a stand-alone SaaS software license. The company merged with Perpetual Medicines and is backed by Qiming Venture Partners.

providers.name: The Atavist
providers.description: The Atavist is a pioneering digital longform-storytelling brand founded in 2009 by Evan Ratliff, Jefferson Rabb, and Nicholas Thompson. It comprises The Atavist Magazine, which publishes one immersive work of narrative nonfiction each month and has earned National Magazine Award and Emmy recognition, and the Atavist multimedia publishing platform for building rich, media-driven stories. Automattic (the company behind WordPress.com) acquired both the magazine and the platform in 2018; the platform's storytelling features were folded into WordPress.com and the magazine now runs on Newspack by Automattic. The Atavist exposes no public developer API or documented developer program — it is a reader-facing publication at magazine.atavist.com.

providers.name: TRDATA
providers.description: TRDATA (TRDATA Technology Limited) is a real-time financial information and communication platform for professional traders, aggregating over-the-counter (OTC) quotes, prices, news, and analytics from market makers across fragmented fixed-income and emerging-market instruments. It covers Ukrainian, CEEMEA, and global bonds, currencies, commodities, and derivatives from local and international data providers, and bundles analytics tools such as a Bond Calculator, Bond Calendar, Swap Curves, real-time asset charts, and a TRDATA Excel add-in. More than 800 institutions -- including Societe Generale, UniCredit, Raiffeisen, BNP Paribas, Barclays, Deutsche Bank, and Commerzbank -- use the platform to read and exchange market information. TRDATA is backed by 500 Global. As of this profile the company publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or documentation surface; access is via registration and the hosted platform.

providers.name: Utilidata
providers.description: Utilidata is an Ann Arbor, Michigan software company building Karman, a distributed AI platform that runs on a custom NVIDIA system-on-module embedded directly into electrical infrastructure — smart meters and grid-edge devices on the utility side, PDUs and power trays inside AI data centers. Karman processes high-resolution AC metrology locally (single-cycle waveform statistics at 1+ MS/s sample rates) to produce "data products" such as Power Quality Analytics, enabling millisecond-level power control, GPU/PSU failure prediction, phase balancing and power-aware scheduling. Utilidata publishes the Karman Power Aware Module as Apache-2.0 open source: a Rust reference implementation that serializes Karman data products as Protocol Buffers (package utilidata.karman.bibimbap.v1), transports them over ZeroMQ, and exposes them to Prometheus and TimescaleDB through a Helm-packaged Kubernetes stack. The company has raised a $100M Series C and counts NVIDIA, Microsoft Climate Innovation Fund, American Electric Power and Renown Capital Partners among its backers.

providers.name: Verisian
providers.description: Verisian is an AI infrastructure platform for clinical trials, giving pharmaceutical sponsors and CROs the information infrastructure required to deploy AI across their experts and processes. The platform provides full study traceability and automates statistical programming workflows: automating the validation of SDTM and ADaM analysis datasets (turning time-consuming QC double-programming into value-generating QA oversight), and generating complete define-XML files and draft reviewer's guides that are guaranteed consistent with the underlying analysis, so teams are submission-ready in hours. Verisian is cloud native, compatible with any statistical computing environment (SCE), storage, or compute, and integrates through simple file transfer with no complex API integration required. It serves statistical programmers, statisticians, data managers, medical writers, clinicians, and regulatory teams across in-house and CRO-outsourced operating models; Bayer is a named customer. There is no public developer API surface — the product is an enterprise application (app.verisian.com) accessed after sales onboarding.

providers.name: Via Transportation
providers.description: Via Transportation provides on-demand public mobility solutions, offering microtransit, fixed‑route, paratransit, and student transit services. Their platform enables cities, transit authorities, universities, and corporations to launch flexible shared‑ride programs, improve rider experience, and optimize transit operations through advanced scheduling and AI‑driven analytics.

providers.name: Watch Club
providers.description: Watch Club is a mobile streaming and social platform for young adults, built around original coming-of-age teen drama series that viewers watch and then discuss with other fans through polls, episode reactions, and community threads. Its first original series, RETURN OFFER, launches February 2026, with a slate of additional YA series in development. The app is available on iOS and is operated by Kino Technologies Inc. Watch Club is a GV (Google Ventures) portfolio company in the consumer sector; it publishes no public developer API surface as of this profile.

providers.name: WE11DONE
providers.description: WE11DONE (pronounced "well done") is a Seoul-based fashion label founded in 2015 by Dami Kwon and Jessica Jung, the duo behind the Seoul concept boutique Rare Market. The brand fuses late-1990s and early-2000s streetwear and athleisure aesthetics into a globally distributed designer ready-to-wear line, sold through its own e-commerce storefront at we11-done.com and stockists worldwide. Surfaced as a consumer-sector portfolio company of hongshan and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead. An enrichment pass on 2026-07-21 confirmed the company operates a direct-to-consumer retail website but publishes no developer API surface: no developer portal, API reference, well-known metadata, or llms.txt were found.

providers.name: WeGoWhere
providers.description: WeGoWhere is a consumer social-activity coordination mobile app (originally launched as EatMatch) that helps friends discover what the people around them are doing and join those plans in real life. Available on iOS and Android with more than 700,000 active users, the app centers each hangout on a dedicated group chat for attendees plus high-resolution photo and video sharing, spanning activities such as dining, movies, photography, sports, karaoke, and general socializing. Based in Bangkok, Thailand, the company raised US$1.2M in seed funding in 2023 and is backed by 500 Global. WeGoWhere is a consumer mobile product and does not currently publish a public API, developer platform, or SDK.

providers.name: Zentist
providers.description: Zentist is a cloud-based revenue cycle management (RCM) platform built specifically for dental support organizations (DSOs) and multi-location dental practices. Its flagship product, Remit AI, uses artificial intelligence to automate electronic remittance advice (ERA) and explanation of benefits (EOB) parsing, payment posting, denial and adjustment categorization, and claims status tracking, while Cavi AR drives intelligent accounts-receivable follow-up. Executive dashboards deliver practice-level and organization-wide analytics. Trusted by more than 400 DSOs, Zentist reports doubling RCM productivity and cutting the cash-to-claim cycle in half within the first 100 days. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; Zentist operates as a login-gated SaaS application with no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: zicron-ai
providers.description: Zicron AI offers an AI‑powered productivity suite called Memex that captures, organizes, and makes searchable all of a user's communications, meetings, notes, and relationships. Built with privacy‑first principles, the platform unifies email, calendar, CRM, and personal knowledge into a single contextual assistant that learns from user behavior to surface relevant information and automate routine tasks.

providers.name: Adoc (Viva Innovation)
providers.description: Adoc is the corporate web presence of Viva Innovation Inc. (주식회사 비바이노베이션), a Seoul, South Korea health-technology company founded in January 2018 and based in Gangnam-gu, which operates the health-checkup and medical-records platform 착한의사 (Chakan Uisa / Kindoc). Consumers use the Kindoc mobile and web apps to pull scattered personal medical records into one place, run an AI symptom check against personal and Health Insurance Review and Assessment Service data, compare hospital examination packages and their costs, and book discounted health screenings; employers buy the same screenings as corporate checkup programs, and partner hospitals join through a hospital-affiliation program. For providers the company sells a medical cloud — Kindoc Care CMS and Kindoc Care PMS for checkup centres — alongside a medical AI line it splits into Preventive AI (test-item recommendation, plain-language result explanation, biomarker and biological-age analysis), Clinical AI (comprehensive findings generation, abnormal-finding triage, follow-up test recommendation) and Decision Support AI (disease-risk analysis from repeated checkup results, endoscopy anaesthesia-risk prediction, real-time endoscopic polyp detection), plus a generative "주치의 AI" assistant published as Dr.Patch at chat.kindoc.ai and a research arm, Kindoc Labs. Everything the company ships is a consumer app, a partner landing page or hospital-side software: as of this profile it publishes no developer portal, no API reference, no SDK and no machine-readable API contract on any host it operates.

providers.name: Agentic Enterprises
providers.description: Agentic Enterprises S.A. operates the agent-bev platform, a business‑to‑business hub for the beverage alcohol sector. It provides a unified catalogue where buyers and sellers can discover, compare, and order products across all makers and markets. The service runs on the Model Context Protocol (MCP) and integrates with AI models like Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini, offering a neutral, ad‑free marketplace for agents.

providers.name: Agriful
providers.description: Agriful (Agriful Software Inc.) is a cloud ERP for the fresh produce industry, founded in 2022 by Patrick Crowley (CEO) and Deep Randhawa (CTO) and backed by Fractal Software and Reservoir Ventures. Its web platform runs sales and purchase order entry, live inventory control, lot-level traceability for FSMA and PTI compliance, produce-specific AR/AP accounting and grower settlements, and customizable reporting for produce brokers, marketers, packer-shippers, wholesalers and distributors. As of this profile Agriful publishes no developer program, API reference, OpenAPI or GraphQL schema, SDK, CLI, Postman collection or webhook catalog. The single live machine surface on its domain is the RedwoodJS GraphQL endpoint at api.agrifulsoftware.com/graphql that backs its own single-page application; it answers anonymous requests but has introspection disabled in production and is documented nowhere.

providers.name: Albo
providers.description: Albo (albo.com, formerly albo.mx) is a Mexican digital financial services company founded in 2016 and operating since 2022 as an Institución de Fondos de Pago Electrónico (IFPE) authorized by the Comisión Nacional Bancaria y de Valores (CNBV) and regulated by Banco de México. Albo ships a mobile-first personal account with a Mastercard debit card — SPEI transfers, bill payments, cash deposit and withdrawal at partner locations, and real-time notifications — alongside "albo empresa", a business account for payroll, employee cards, and bulk dispersion of up to 3,000 transactions at a time. Adjacent credit (abea, by Aureo Lab) and crypto (albit, by Indigo DeFi) products are offered by independent partners. Albo publishes no public developer program: no developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDK, webhook catalog, or sandbox was found on any albo.com, albo.mx or albo.live host.

providers.name: Alli Connect
providers.description: Alli Connect provides peer support and wellness software for public safety agencies, including law enforcement, fire, EMS, and military. Their platform enables internal peer connections, therapist matching with AI, digital resource centers, wellness check‑ins across six domains, and 24/7 clinical support for critical incidents. The solution aims to improve mental health outcomes and resilience for first‑responders and related personnel.

providers.name: AMP Robotics
providers.description: AMP Robotics (operating as AMP Sortation) is an artificial-intelligence company for the waste and recycling industry that designs, builds, and operates advanced, cost-competitive facilities to process single-stream recycling and municipal solid waste. Its Smart Sortation technology suite combines computer vision (real-time material characterization), high-speed air-jet sortation (Jet and MicroJet), and robotic-arm sortation (Delta) to raise material-recovery rates, cut contamination, and extend landfill life. The flagship AMP ONE platform delivers fully automated, facility-scale sortation processing from 10K to 1M+ tons annually for waste haulers, material-recovery facilities, and municipalities. AMP Robotics is a Google Ventures (GV) portfolio company. No public developer API, API documentation, or developer portal is published; this profile is maintained for network discovery and identity.

providers.name: Arrive AI
providers.description: Arrive AI (Nasdaq: ARAI) is an autonomous last-mile delivery company headquartered in Fishers, Indiana, founded by Dan O'Toole and originally operating as DroneDek. Its patented Autonomous Last Mile (ALM) platform is anchored by the Arrive Point, an AI-powered smart mailbox that accepts and dispatches parcels to and from drones, ground robots and human couriers, with temperature-controlled compartments, real-time tracking, smart logistics alerts and chain-of-custody controls aimed at healthcare, pharmacy and e-commerce logistics. The company markets hardware plus a network service; as of this profile it publishes no public developer program, API reference or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Artificial Intelligence Underwriting Company
providers.description: Artificial Intelligence Underwriting Company (AIUC) is a San Francisco-based AI agent standards and insurance company that builds confidence infrastructure for enterprises adopting AI agents. It pairs AIUC-1 — described as the world's first AI agent standard, spanning data & privacy, security, safety, reliability, accountability, and societal risk — with insurance products that protect organizations against AI agent failures. Developed with input from over 100 Fortune 500 CISOs and mapped to frameworks including ISO 42001, NIST AI RMF, and MITRE ATLAS, AIUC certifies AI agents against defined controls through accredited auditors. The company is backed by Emergence Capital and does not currently publish a public API or developer surface.

providers.name: Assertion AI
providers.description: Assertion AI provides a shared memory platform for AI coding agents such as Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex, enabling every session to build on prior team decisions, experiments, and insights. The service offers a free starter tier and an optional agent with no compaction and half the price, aiming to boost productivity and reduce duplicated effort across development teams.

providers.name: Auxia
providers.description: Auxia is an agentic marketing platform that enables enterprises to orchestrate personalized, AI‑driven customer journeys across web, mobile, and lifecycle channels. It integrates first‑party data, automates growth experiments, and continuously optimizes experiences using proprietary machine learning, helping marketers increase conversion, retention, and revenue.

providers.name: Avelios
providers.description: Avelios Medical provides a modular, data‑driven clinic platform that integrates digital treatment documentation, AI‑powered analytics, and automated administrative processes. Their operating system enables intelligent patient care across hospitals and clinics, offering SaaS solutions for digital infrastructure, treatment planning, and big‑data research. Founded to transform healthcare delivery, Avelios combines innovative software with a focus on data security and regulatory compliance, serving the European market and expanding globally.

providers.name: Awardco
providers.description: Awardco is an all-in-one employee recognition, rewards, and engagement platform built around a global rewards marketplace that includes a native Amazon Business integration, gift cards, service awards, and swag. Awardco exposes a documented public REST API at https://api.awardco.com/api for administrators and integration partners - callers authenticate with a permission-scoped API key passed as a request header, all responses are JSON with a success flag, and all timestamps are ISO 8601. The API is not open self-serve - it is gated behind an Awardco account and the API Key Management permission, and partners additionally send an X-Partner-Id header. Documented capabilities cover user provisioning (create, import, reset password), recognizing employees and awarding points, and retrieving or scheduling reports. Awardco also ships prebuilt HRIS, SSO/SAML, Slack, and Microsoft Teams integrations plus Awardco Connect for custom flows. Exact request and response schemas for individual methods are not published on the open web, so the API surfaces below are modeled from Awardco's public documentation and help center rather than a released OpenAPI definition.

providers.name: Based
providers.description: Based is a consumer crypto super app built on Hyperliquid that unifies trading, prediction markets, and real-world payments in a single self-custody account. Users trade spot and perpetual futures with sub-second execution and deep liquidity, speculate on prediction markets, and spend crypto from Solana, Arbitrum, and Polygon at 70+ million Visa merchants across 160+ countries via Based debit cards, including the premium Gold+ card. BasedCloud lets partners spin up white-label Hyperliquid trading frontends (web, mobile, desktop, Telegram), and a three-tiered affiliate program amplifies Hyperliquid referral fees. Based is backed by Pantera Capital, Coinbase Ventures, Hashed, Ethena, and Spartan Group. It publishes consumer product docs on GitBook and an agent-oriented llms.txt index, but exposes no public developer API of its own — programmatic trading runs on the underlying Hyperliquid API.

providers.name: Bayzat
providers.description: Bayzat provides a cloud‑based HR, payroll, benefits and spend‑management platform for companies in the UAE, KSA and GCC. Their solution automates core HR processes, payroll processing, employee benefits administration, corporate card spend, and integrates AI‑driven analytics to streamline workforce management and finance operations. Serving over 4,000 enterprises, Bayzat emphasizes compliance with regional regulations and offers a unified employee experience across hiring, onboarding, performance, and off‑boarding.

providers.name: BeeKeeperAI
providers.description: BeeKeeperAI provides a confidential execution platform, EscrowAI®, that protects sensitive data and proprietary AI models by leveraging confidential computing. It helps organizations mitigate cybersecurity risks associated with agentic AI while ensuring ROI and compliance. The platform offers secure AI and data processing for enterprises seeking to harness AI safely.

providers.name: Belfry
providers.description: Belfry Software provides security guard management software, offering scheduling, timekeeping, operations, payroll, and billing solutions for security companies. Their platform includes AI-driven teammate features, recruiting tools, and on-demand pay for officers, aiming to streamline security operations and improve workforce efficiency.

providers.name: BetaFinds
providers.description: BetaFinds is a platform that discovers, curates, and showcases early-stage startups. Users can browse startup listings, upvote projects, and engage in community discussions. The site provides searchable startup data, categories such as AI, and integrates a sign‑in portal for contributors. It aims to connect founders with early adopters and investors, fostering visibility for emerging companies.

providers.name: Breather
providers.description: Breather provides on-demand access to a global network of coworking spaces, meeting rooms, and private offices. Users can book desks, conference rooms, or entire offices by the hour, day, or month across more than 260 cities in 20 countries. The platform offers flexible pricing, a seamless reservation experience, and integrates with Deskpass for unified account management, catering to individuals, small businesses, and large enterprises seeking productive work environments.

providers.name: Cabela's
providers.description: Cabela's is a specialty retailer of hunting, fishing, camping, and outdoor recreation merchandise, operating retail stores and an e-commerce platform. Cabela's is a subsidiary of Bass Pro Shops following the 2017 acquisition, and continues to operate under its own brand with retail locations and a consumer-facing web storefront.

providers.name: Calderdale Data Works
providers.description: Calderdale Data Works is a local council open-data portal for United Kingdom running CKAN. It exposes the CKAN catalog API, a standardized machine-readable interface over approximately an open datasets, supporting programmatic dataset search, metadata retrieval, and resource access. Because it runs CKAN, it shares a consistent API surface with every other CKAN portal, making it uniformly harvestable and integrable.

providers.name: California Health and Human Services
providers.description: California Health and Human Services is a state government open-data portal for United States running CKAN. It exposes the CKAN catalog API, a standardized machine-readable interface over approximately 481 datasets, supporting programmatic dataset search, metadata retrieval, and resource access. Because it runs CKAN, it shares a consistent API surface with every other CKAN portal, making it uniformly harvestable and integrable.

providers.name: California Natural Resources Agency
providers.description: California Natural Resources Agency is a state government open-data portal for United States running CKAN. It exposes the CKAN catalog API, a standardized machine-readable interface over approximately 21,080 datasets, supporting programmatic dataset search, metadata retrieval, and resource access. Because it runs CKAN, it shares a consistent API surface with every other CKAN portal, making it uniformly harvestable and integrable.

providers.name: California Open Data
providers.description: California Open Data is a state government open-data portal for United States running CKAN. It exposes the CKAN catalog API, a standardized machine-readable interface over approximately 4,456 datasets, supporting programmatic dataset search, metadata retrieval, and resource access. Because it runs CKAN, it shares a consistent API surface with every other CKAN portal, making it uniformly harvestable and integrable.

providers.name: caller-kit-com
providers.description: CallerKit provides a Caller ID API and global phone lookup service, offering access to a database of over 3 billion phone numbers with verified contact names and aliases. The platform supports real‑time search by number, name, or email, bulk verification, and enriched data delivery for developers, CRMs, verification systems, and other applications. Features include fast, scalable lookups, rate‑limited API access, detailed analytics, and secure encrypted data handling.

providers.name: Carbon Robotics
providers.description: Carbon Robotics is a Seattle-based physical-AI and agricultural robotics company building autonomous systems that help farmers cut costs and reduce chemical use. Its flagship LaserWeeder G2 uses computer vision and high-power lasers to eliminate weeds without herbicides, and its Carbon Autonomy product adds remote-supervised autonomy to compatible John Deere tractors. The underlying Carbon AI Large Plant Model is trained on 150 million labeled plants across 15 countries and 100+ crops. Carbon Robotics operates a customer grower cloud portal and Starlink-connected fleet control, but publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDKs, or developer portal as of this profiling.

providers.name: Cellsavers
providers.description: Cellsavers provides home care and repair services, offering TV mounting, appliance repair, handyman services, iPhone repair, smart home installation, garage door repair, and plumbing. The company serves millions of households, emphasizing vetted technicians and a comprehensive service platform.

providers.name: ChatSee
providers.description: ChatSee provides an AI runtime feedback platform for enterprise AI systems, offering observability, governance, and reliability tools for autonomous agents. Their solution captures failure events, provides operational learning, and helps product, engineering, and security teams monitor and improve AI agent behavior in production environments.

providers.name: Chief Information Officers Council
providers.description: The Chief Information Officers Council (CIOC) is the principal interagency forum for improving agency practices related to the design, acquisition, development, modernization, use, sharing, and performance of federal information resources. Established by Executive Order 13011 in 1996 and codified in the E-Government Act of 2002 (44 U.S.C. 3603), the Council is comprised of the Chief Information Officers and Deputy CIOs of executive branch agencies, the Federal CIO at OMB (who serves as Chair), the Federal Chief Information Security Officer, and the Administrator for Electronic Government. The CIOC develops recommendations for OMB IT policy, identifies opportunities to improve federal IT performance, coordinates multi-agency IT initiatives such as cybersecurity and cloud adoption, supports federal IT workforce development, and disseminates effective IT management practices across the federal government. The Council publishes guidance, playbooks, committee output and its charter through councils.gov, the consolidated federal executive councils hub GSA launched in March 2026; its long-standing home at cio.gov now redirects there. The Council operates no developer program and publishes no API.

providers.name: CircleBack
providers.description: CircleBack is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: secondary-market) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.

providers.name: Clear Ballot
providers.description: Clear Ballot Group, Inc. is an election technology company that builds transparent, verifiable voting systems for election administrators across the United States. Its flagship ClearVote platform spans vote-by-mail processing, in-person voting, ballot design, and independent post-election audit and results-verification software, alongside offerings for ranked-choice voting and elections-as-a-service. Clear Ballot operates as a closed, certified election-systems vendor rather than a public API platform, so this profile is identity- and security-focused: it captures the company's public web presence, domain-security posture, and its published vulnerability-disclosure program. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Click Therapeutics
providers.description: Click Therapeutics, Inc. is a New York-headquartered digital medicine company founded in 2012 by David Benshoof Klein that develops, validates, and commercializes software as prescription medical treatments — the category it named Digital Therapeutics. Its AI-enabled platform targets diseases with an underlying neurological or behavioral component through cognitive and neurobehavioral mechanisms, delivered as smartphone software used independently or alongside biomedical therapy (Software-Enhanced Drugs). Authorized and commercial programs include CT-152 (Rejoyn, major depressive disorder, developed with Otsuka), CT-132 (episodic migraine) and AspyreRx (type 2 diabetes), with a pipeline spanning schizophrenia (CT-155 with Boehringer Ingelheim, CT-156), opioid use disorder, multiple sclerosis, atopic dermatitis, obesity, oncology, insomnia and acute coronary syndrome. Click publishes no public developer program, API, or SDK — its software is distributed as regulated prescription therapeutics, not as a platform.

providers.name: Coco Robotics
providers.description: Coco Robotics is a Santa Monica, California urban robotics company operating a fleet of zero-emission, remotely-supervised sidewalk delivery robots ("Cocobots") for last-mile food, grocery and retail delivery. Merchants do not integrate with Coco directly: Coco is consumed as a delivery service provider through Uber Eats, DoorDash, Wolt and Olo Dispatch, and the company publishes no developer portal, API documentation, SDKs or webhooks of its own. Its public software surface is limited to a marketing site, a customer order-tracking web app, and a GitHub organization of forked ROS and infrastructure tooling.

providers.name: Cognichip
providers.description: Cognichip is an AI-first semiconductor company revolutionizing the way chips are designed. Its core technology, Artificial Chip Intelligence (ACI), is built on what the company describes as the world's first physics-informed foundation AI model tailored for chip design, positioning ACI as a new scaling factor for semiconductors. ACI aims to understand, learn, and solve chip design problems with designer-level cognitive abilities, reducing design effort by roughly 75% and cutting completion time in half to address the industry bottleneck where chip development can take three to five years. Founded by semiconductor and AI veterans including CEO Faraj Aalaei and CTO Ehsan Kamalinejad, the company is backed by Lux Capital, Mayfield, and Seligman Ventures, has Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan on its board, and was named to Fast Company's World's Most Innovative Companies of 2026. Added to the API Evangelist network and enriched by the pipeline; the company publishes a marketing and corporate presence today with no public developer or API surface.

providers.name: Cornerstone Robotics
providers.description: Cornerstone Robotics (CSR) is a Hong Kong-headquartered surgical robotics manufacturer founded in 2019 at Hong Kong Science Park, building the Sentire Endoscopic Surgical System (C1000) — a multi-specialty, minimally invasive robot-assisted surgery platform developed entirely in-house and indicated for general surgery, gynecology, thoracic and urology. The Sentire system has received regulatory clearance in China (NMPA), the European Union and Singapore, and has completed multicenter clinical trials in China and the United Kingdom. The company operates three global R&D hubs, six business centers and a 30,000 square meter manufacturing facility, and sells a regulated physical medical device rather than software: it publishes no developer portal, no public API, no SDKs and no machine-readable specifications.

providers.name: Cytovale
providers.description: Cytovale is a San Francisco-based medical diagnostics company that develops early-detection technology for sepsis. Its flagship product, IntelliSep, is the first and only FDA-cleared in vitro diagnostic test for sepsis: it uses microfluidics, high-speed video, and computer-vision algorithms to measure the biophysical rigidity of tens of thousands of white blood cells, detecting the immune activation that signals sepsis risk and returning a risk stratification in roughly eight minutes. The test runs on the Cytovale System medical device in emergency-department settings. Cytovale is venture-backed by Norwest Venture Partners, Sands Capital, and the Global Health Investment Corporation. The company operates as a clinical/diagnostics device maker and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or API documentation surface.

providers.name: data.overheid.nl
providers.description: data.overheid.nl is a national government open-data portal for Netherlands running CKAN. It exposes the CKAN catalog API, a standardized machine-readable interface over approximately 20,386 datasets, supporting programmatic dataset search, metadata retrieval, and resource access. Because it runs CKAN, it shares a consistent API surface with every other CKAN portal, making it uniformly harvestable and integrable.

providers.name: Datenregister Berlin
providers.description: Datenregister Berlin is a municipal government open-data portal for Germany running CKAN. It exposes the CKAN catalog API, a standardized machine-readable interface over approximately 2,609 datasets, supporting programmatic dataset search, metadata retrieval, and resource access. Because it runs CKAN, it shares a consistent API surface with every other CKAN portal, making it uniformly harvestable and integrable.

providers.name: Deer Supply & Research
providers.description: Deer Supply & Research is a Canadian supplier of GLP‑1 weight‑loss medications such as Retatrutide, Tirzepatide, and Semaglutide, offered as pre‑filled, ready‑to‑use pens, along with recovery peptides and ancillary capsules. They ship discreetly across Canada, emphasizing consistent quality, regulatory compliance, and customer support in both English and French. The company also provides lab results, detailed product information, and a research blog for health‑focused consumers.

providers.name: Diagonal Therapeutics
providers.description: Diagonal Therapeutics is a Watertown, Massachusetts clinical-stage biotechnology company founded in 2022 by CEO Alex Lugovskoy in partnership with Atlas Venture, developing "clustering" agonist antibodies that switch broken signaling pathways back on rather than inhibiting them. Its DIAGONAL product engine pairs computational epitope filtering with experimental screening — generating roughly 200,000 candidate antibody sequences per target, clustering them by predicted shape, binning by receptor complementarity and assembling multispecific antibodies from those bins — to make agonist antibody discovery tractable. The lead program, DIAG723, is a first-in-class ALK1:BMPRII clustering agonist antibody that restores ALK1 signaling; it holds US FDA and EMA orphan drug designation for hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia (HHT) and entered the Phase 1/2 DIAMOND trial (NCT07623525), with a first patient dosed in July 2026, alongside preclinical work in pulmonary arterial hypertension. The pipeline extends into hematology, hepatology, nephrology and cardiovascular disease. The company has raised roughly USD 255 million across a USD 128 million Series A (April 2024, co-led by BVF Partners and Atlas Venture) and an oversubscribed USD 125 million Series B (January 2026, co-led by Sanofi Ventures and Janus Henderson Investors). Diagonal is a therapeutics developer rather than a software vendor: it operates a Next.js marketing site backed by a Sanity CMS, and publishes no developer portal, no API documentation and no machine-readable API contract of any kind.

providers.name: dreamgames
providers.description: Dream Games is a mobile gaming developer with offices in Istanbul and London that builds high-quality, long-lifecycle casual puzzle games, best known for Royal Match and Royal Kingdom. The company combines technology and creativity to produce polished match-3 titles played by tens of millions of players worldwide, and it was surfaced as a portfolio company of balderton-capital. Dream Games operates as a consumer game publisher rather than an API provider: it publishes no public developer portal, OpenAPI, SDKs, or programmatic API surface. This profile therefore captures the company's real public web, legal, and security surface (website, terms, privacy, careers, help center, and a published security.txt) rather than developer artifacts.

providers.name: Drip Capital
providers.description: Drip Capital is a digital trade finance and working capital company founded in 2016, headquartered in Palo Alto, California, with operations in Mumbai, India and Mexico City, Mexico. It provides collateral-free post-shipment finance to small and medium-sized exporters and importers through data-driven underwriting, offering invoice factoring, export finance, an importer credit program, supply chain and vendor financing, receivables financing, and revolving lines of credit. The company has financed over $9 billion in trade transactions for 11,000+ businesses worldwide. Drip Capital does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile captures its identity and public web properties. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel, Initialized Capital, Wing Venture Capital, and Y Combinator.

providers.name: Dropzone AI
providers.description: Dropzone AI delivers an Agentic SOC platform built around an autonomous AI SOC Analyst that handles tier-1 alert triage and threat hunting 24/7. The platform ships pre-trained, is coachable in natural language, and connects via secure APIs to 90+ existing security tools (SIEM, EDR/XDR, identity, cloud, threat intel). Dropzone does not publish a customer-facing REST API; integration is delivered through its outbound connectors and partner program.

providers.name: Dyson
providers.description: Dyson is a British technology company that designs and manufactures household appliances such as vacuum cleaners, air purifiers, hair care tools, and lighting. Known for its innovative engineering and sleek design, Dyson sells products worldwide through its website and retail partners, and provides developer resources for its connected devices and services.

providers.name: EasyOnward
providers.description: Travel risk intelligence – passport, visa, transit, and baggage analysis for every itinerary. EasyOnward provides comprehensive travel risk assessments, helping travelers and businesses understand visa requirements, transit restrictions, and baggage allowances across global destinations. The platform offers real-time updates and detailed insights to ensure safe and compliant journeys.

providers.name: Frec
providers.description: Frec is a San Francisco fintech offering tax-aware, automated direct indexing for retail investors. Its products — Classic Direct Indexing, Long Short Direct Indexing, Diversify, Trade, Treasury cash management, and a Portfolio Line of Credit — replicate market indices with individual stocks while running automated tax-loss harvesting to minimize capital gains taxes at fees starting around 0.09%. Frec is an SEC-registered investment adviser and SIPC member managing over $1.25B in assets, founded by Mo Al Adham and backed by Greylock. The company ships a consumer investing app and website but does not currently expose a public developer API, so this profile is identity- and security-posture-only.

providers.name: Frollo Australia Pty LTD
providers.description: Frollo Australia Pty LTD is Australia’s leading Open Banking provider, delivering businesses and mortgage brokers efficiency tools, exceptional customer experiences, and empowering consumers to achieve their financial goals through integrated financial insights and budgeting tools.

providers.name: getagentdocs-com
providers.description: AgentDocs provides an AI‑powered office suite designed for personal AI agents. It offers Docs, Sheets, Slides, Database, Drive, and Pages that agents can read, write, and edit in real time. The platform emphasizes cheap, fast, agent‑first collaboration, with markdown‑native live co‑editing, version history, and integration with Claude. Publicly available at getagentdocs.com, it includes guides, a blog, and pricing information, targeting developers and enterprises building AI‑agent workflows.

providers.name: Goldsky
providers.description: Goldsky is a blockchain data platform that provides managed indexing, streaming, and RPC infrastructure for EVM and non-EVM chains. Core products are Subgraphs (hosted GraphQL indexers compatible with The Graph), Mirror (change-data-capture streaming of onchain data into customer databases and data warehouses), Turbo (vectorized real-time data pipelines with SQL transforms), Compose (orchestration of onchain-x-offchain workflows), and Edge RPC (high-performance EVM RPC with debug and trace). Developers interact via a CLI, a web dashboard, and REST + GraphQL APIs. Sinks supported include PostgreSQL, ClickHouse, Kafka, MySQL, Webhooks, S3, AWS SQS, Elasticsearch, S2, and Parquet.

providers.name: Goomp Inc, Kalendar AI
providers.description: Kalendar AI (Goomp Inc / Kalendar Inc, a Delaware corporation operating from New York) is an autonomous AI sales-agent platform that automates B2B outbound prospecting end to end. It sources ideal-customer prospects from a database of hundreds of millions of professionals and companies, generates and sends personalized outreach through dedicated AI-managed mailbox infrastructure, qualifies replies, and books meetings directly onto the user's calendar. As of the 2026-08-13 enrichment pass the company has rebranded to Cockpit AI and migrated to oncockpit.ai — kalendar.ai now 301-redirects site-wide, and the new site's robots.txt carries an explicit "Block legacy Kalendar.ai paths" section. The product is now framed as named AI workers you "hire" (Vinay for outbound, Amara), which research prospects, draft proposal documents, send from the customer's own email and LinkedIn accounts, and book meetings, with a human approval step before anything ships. Investors named on the site are 500 Global, Boost VC, Asymmetry Ventures and Village Global. The company runs a live API host (api.oncockpit.ai, which self-identifies as the "Cockpit AI API") and still serves a legacy ChatGPT plugin manifest at /.well-known/ai-plugin.json declaring OAuth with read/write scopes, but it publishes no developer portal, no API reference, no OpenAPI, no SDK, no webhook catalog, no MCP server and no pricing page.

providers.name: Gridware
providers.description: Gridware builds grid intelligence technology for electric utilities. Its Active Grid Response (AGR) platform pairs pole-mounted GridScope sensors with analytics to bring real-time visibility into the physical, electrical, and environmental condition of every span of the distribution grid, closing the "Hazard Awareness Delay" between when a fault or hazard occurs and when a utility detects it. Gridware supports fault prevention, faster power restoration, wildfire and hazard response, and grid asset management. Headquartered in San Francisco with an Applied Research Complex in Richmond, California, the company is backed by True Ventures. Gridware does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation; this profile captures its public identity, trust/compliance posture, and domain security.

providers.name: Gyant
providers.description: Gyant was a San Francisco-based digital health company that built an AI-powered conversational virtual assistant for health systems, guiding patients through symptom checking, care navigation, and triage across web and messaging channels. In 2022 Gyant was acquired by Fabric (fabrichealth.com), and gyant.com now redirects to Fabric's healthcare care-access platform, which combines conversational AI with physician-built clinical protocols for virtual care, patient engagement, and clinical automation. Gyant does not publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs; this profile captures the company's identity, published legal/compliance surface, and domain security posture.

providers.name: Health Scholars
providers.description: Health Scholars — which rebranded to UpSkillAI in 2025 and now trades at upskillai.com — builds AI-powered extended reality (XR/VR) simulation training for mission-critical, hands-on work in healthcare, emergency medical services, stroke assessment and defense. The platform pairs voice-driven VR simulations with simulation management and readiness reporting, letting hospital systems, first responders and government programs run standardized protocol training on headsets without instructors or extra equipment. Customers reach it through a hosted web console at app.upskillai.com. The company publishes no public developer program: there is no developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI or other machine-readable contract, SDK, webhook catalog or public pricing. The production backend behind its own application (api.upskillai.com, with the legacy AWS API Gateway host api.healthscholars.com) is private and rejects unauthenticated requests.

providers.name: Hidden Level
providers.description: Hidden Level is a U.S.-based defense and aerospace technology company that turns radio-frequency (RF) activity into trusted airspace intelligence. Its passive RF sensing platform detects and tracks unmanned aerial systems (drones) and other activity across air, ground, sea, and space domains without requiring emitters or heavy on-site infrastructure. Hidden Level packages this as hardware sensor platforms, software platforms, and data platforms serving defense and military, critical infrastructure protection, homeland security, and public safety customers. The company hosts its platform on AWS with least-privilege access, MFA, and TLS 1.3 API communications, aligns corporate controls to NIST SP 800-171, and emphasizes U.S. design and manufacturing. Backed by Costanoa Ventures. This API Evangelist profile tracks Hidden Level's public web and security surface; the company does not currently publish a public developer portal, API reference, or SDKs.

providers.name: Inherent
providers.description: Inherent Labs provides a recursively self‑improving AI platform that discovers new knowledge. The site describes itself as a system that continuously improves to uncover information, positioning itself in the AI research and knowledge discovery space.

providers.name: Joy
providers.description: Joy (withjoy.com) is a consumer wedding and event planning platform that gives couples a free personalized wedding website, an all-in-one universal registry, guest list management, digital and printed save-the-dates and invitations, smart RSVP tools, hotel room blocks, and a companion mobile app. The company has since expanded into baby planning with Joy Baby. Joy is a business-to-consumer product and does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or OpenAPI specification; this profile therefore carries identity and link-property metadata and live security probes rather than machine-readable API artifacts.

providers.name: Juniper Behavioral Health
providers.description: Juniper Behavioral Health (now operating as Camber, camber.health) is a healthcare revenue-cycle-management (RCM) software company for specialty and behavioral health providers. Founded in 2021 and backed by a16z, Y Combinator, and Craft Ventures, the company automates medical billing, claims processing, denial management, and payment analytics so behavioral and specialty clinicians (ABA, PT, ENT, allergy) can collect more from insurance and spend less time on administrative overhead. Their platform is built on AI systems trained on more than $2.5B in claims data. This profile was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and enriched from the public Camber website; the company exposes a customer web application (app.camber.health) and a published responsible-disclosure policy but no public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation at this time.

providers.name: Juxta
providers.description: Juxta is a San Francisco positioning-technology company building a hardware-free Universal Positioning System (UPS) that delivers real-time indoor and outdoor tracking for people, assets, and robots with sub-meter accuracy indoors and roughly 3-meter accuracy outdoors. Rather than relying on satellites, beacons, or cameras, Juxta uses the inertial (IMU) sensors already present in mobile devices, robots, and machinery combined with machine-learning "synthetic fingerprinting" to map and track subjects in GPS-denied environments such as warehouses, hospitals, underground facilities, and battlefields. Its drag-and-drop deployment ingests a floorplan, satellite image, or CAD file and goes live in hours, priced by mapped area and assets tracked. Juxta serves defense, logistics and robotics, and healthcare, and is backed by Y Combinator and other early-stage investors. Access today is through a partner portal and booked demo; no public developer API is documented.

providers.name: KUKA
providers.description: KUKA AG is a German industrial automation company headquartered in Augsburg, Bavaria, founded in 1898 and majority-owned by China's Midea Group since 2016. KUKA designs and manufactures industrial robots, autonomous mobile robots (AMRs), production cells, controllers, and the software stack that drives them. Its product portfolio spans six-axis articulated robots (KR series), sensitive collaborative robots (LBR iiwa, LBR iisy), mobile platforms (KMR iiwa, KMP), and palletizing/welding/CNC cells, controlled by the KR C4 and KR C5 / KR C5 micro controller generations. The robot software stack centers on KUKA System Software (KSS/VSS) for KR C4-class hardware, the newer iiQKA.OS / iiQKA.OS2 operating system for KR C5, and the KUKA Robot Language (KRL) for motion programming, with extension surfaces including KUKA.RobotSensorInterface (RSI), KUKA.EthernetKRL, KUKA.PLC mxAutomation for external PLC control, KUKA.OPC UA, and KUKA.AppTech / iiQKA App Builder for option packages. Engineering and simulation are delivered through iiQWorks (iiQWorks.Sim, iiQWorks.App Builder, iiQWorks.Copilot) and KUKA.Sim, while operational software includes KUKA Xpert (documentation/cloud), KUKA iiQoT (condition monitoring), and KUKA Connect / my.KUKA customer portals. KUKA does not publish a first-party public REST/OpenAPI developer API or an official GitHub organization for its robot control stack; integration is performed through proprietary protocols (RSI, EthernetKRL, mxAutomation, OPC UA, PROFINET, EtherCAT) and SDKs distributed via the iiQKA Creator portal and KUKA Xpert. A meaningful body of open-source KUKA integration code lives in the community-maintained kroshu GitHub organization (ROS 2 drivers, external-control SDK, URDF robot descriptions) and the roboticsapi / openkuka projects. KUKA serves automotive, electronics, battery, metal, consumer goods, healthcare, aerospace, and e-commerce logistics customers, and through its Swisslog subsidiary extends into warehouse and intralogistics automation.

providers.name: Lawn Love
providers.description: Lawn Love is an on-demand lawn care and outdoor home services marketplace that matches homeowners with vetted, independent lawn care professionals across more than 120 US cities. Customers get instant online quotes and book mowing, fertilization, aeration, seeding, pre-emergent and general weed control, bush trimming, leaf removal, gutter cleaning, yard clean-up and snow removal, on either pay-as-you-go or recurring schedules, and manage jobs through the my.lawnlove.com customer app and iOS/Android apps; providers take and service work through pros.lawnlove.com and the Lawn Love for Providers apps. Lawn Love operates as part of LawnStarter. It publishes no public developer API, no developer portal and no API documentation - the api.lawnlove.com host is an undocumented, noindexed backend serving its own web and mobile clients.

providers.name: LF Research
providers.description: LF Research is the Linux Foundation's research arm that publishes reports and studies on open source trends, OSPO practices, technology adoption, and industry analysis. It provides data-driven insights to help organizations understand and participate in open source ecosystems.

providers.name: Lifesum
providers.description: Lifesum is a Stockholm-based digital health company whose consumer mobile application helps people improve their well-being through food logging, calorie and macronutrient tracking, personalized meal plans, recipes, and habit building. Backed by Balderton Capital, the company operates a subscription business-to-consumer product across iOS and Android in a dozen languages. As of this profile Lifesum publishes no public developer program, API documentation, or partner API portal, so this entry is an identity-only company record in the API Evangelist network rather than an API profile.

providers.name: Marcus by Goldman Sachs
providers.description: Marcus by Goldman Sachs is the U.S. consumer banking brand of The Goldman Sachs Group, launched in 2016 to offer no-fee high-yield Online Savings Accounts and Certificates of Deposit (CDs) directly to retail customers online. Deposits are held at Goldman Sachs Bank USA, a New York State-chartered bank and member of the Federal Reserve System, insured by the FDIC. After Goldman's broad retreat from consumer lending, Marcus no longer originates personal loans and now centers on digital deposit products. Marcus operates NO public first-party consumer developer API and runs no self-serve developer portal for its retail banking products; the Goldman Sachs Developer platform (developer.gs.com) serves institutional Transaction Banking and Marquee offerings, not Marcus consumer banking. Consumer-permissioned account data (balances, transactions, account/holder info) is reachable only through third-party open-finance aggregators such as Plaid, Flinks, and MX, not a documented Marcus API. As a bank chartered in the U.S., Goldman Sachs Bank USA is subject to the emerging CFPB Section 1033 personal financial data rights framework, but no first-party FDX-conformant Marcus developer interface is publicly documented as of this record.

providers.name: Meela
providers.description: Meela is an AI voice companion and voice-based ride service built for older adults, backed by Bain Capital Ventures. Members connect through scheduled phone calls with no app, device, or subscription required — Meela calls on a chosen schedule, remembers names, preferences, and past conversations, and shares select privacy-conscious insights with caregivers. A "Meela for Business" offering brings the same companionship to senior living facilities with care-team dashboards, mood/engagement alerts, and EHR documentation, and the company advertises HIPAA and SOC 2 compliance. Meela publishes only a consumer marketing site and a member sign-in portal; it exposes no public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface at this time.

providers.name: Mobilize
providers.description: Mobilize (mobilize.io) is a community and learning software platform purpose-built for associations and professional networks, now operating under the Forj brand (forj.ai). The platform unifies member community and continuing education in one place through its products Forj Connect (peer-to-peer and group member communication), Forj Learn (a learning management system for continuing education, certification, and social learning), and Journey by Forj (a combined community-and-learning experience). Mobilize was surfaced as a portfolio company of Trinity Ventures. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a member/admin web application (app.mobilize.io) and a Zendesk help center but no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal, so this profile carries verified company identity and link properties rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Modern Animal
providers.description: Modern Animal is a membership-based veterinary healthcare company operating physical primary and urgent care clinics across major U.S. metropolitan regions, combining in-clinic visits with 24/7 virtual veterinary consultations, pharmacy and prescription management, dental care, surgery, and preventive care. It runs a subscription membership model (All Access, Essential, and Pay As You Go tiers) with transparent, upfront pricing and a companion mobile app for booking and virtual care. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of dcm-ventures and susa-ventures. Modern Animal is a consumer veterinary brand and publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Modular Robotics
providers.description: Modular Robotics is a Boulder, Colorado hardware and educational-robotics company best known for Cubelets, magnetic modular robot construction blocks organized into SENSE, THINK, and ACT categories, and the MOSS building system. It also produces the Dexter Industries STEM product line, including the GoPiGo Raspberry Pi robot, BrickPi (LEGO Mindstorms plus Raspberry Pi), GrovePi, and the micro:bit GiggleBot.
