The company sells physical robotics kits and companion apps such as the browser-based Cubelets Console with Blockly and C coding rather than a public HTTP API; programmatic access is provided through first-party open-source Python driver libraries published on PyPI and maintained under the official DexterInd GitHub organization.

providers.name: Neurophos
providers.description: Neurophos is an Austin, Texas semiconductor company, spun out of Duke University in 2020, building photonic AI inference silicon. Its Optical Processing Unit (OPU) integrates over a million micron-scale dynamic optical metasurface modulators — technology descended from metamaterials research — onto a single chip, performing the matrix multiplications behind AI inference in light rather than electrons. The company markets the T100 OPU as a drop-in data-center alternative to GPUs, publishing chip and server configurations rated at 235 TOPS/W with HBM-backed memory, and lists Triton and JAX as supported software frameworks. Neurophos raised a $110M Series A in January 2026 led by Gates Frontier with M12, Carbon Direct, Aramco Ventures and Bosch Ventures. It sells hardware, not software services: there is no developer program, no public API and no SDK. The only machine-readable surfaces at its domain are an llms.txt and the Wix-platform site MCP endpoint that llms.txt advertises.

providers.name: NSW Government Open Data
providers.description: NSW Government Open Data is a state government open-data portal for Australia running CKAN. It exposes the CKAN catalog API, a standardized machine-readable interface over approximately 16,907 datasets, supporting programmatic dataset search, metadata retrieval, and resource access. Because it runs CKAN, it shares a consistent API surface with every other CKAN portal, making it uniformly harvestable and integrable.

providers.name: omniX labs
providers.description: omniX labs is a New York-based AI machine-vision analytics company (owned by EverWash) serving car wash, oil-change/lube, and related quick-service automotive businesses. Its platform ingests real-time video of the physical business, applies computer vision and AI to synthesize customer interactions, and returns operational insights that help operators boost throughput, optimize staffing, prevent loss, predict demand, and grow revenue. omniX labs was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company. It operates a customer web portal but publishes no public developer API, SDK, or technical documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: One Month
providers.description: One Month is an online coding education platform that teaches beginners practical software and web development skills through short, project-based video courses designed to be completed in about a month. Its catalog spans programming languages and frameworks such as Ruby, Ruby on Rails, Python, JavaScript, HTML & CSS, SQL, and WordPress, alongside professional skills like project management, using a "watch, do, repeat" methodology of hands-on lessons and follow-along projects. One Month markets itself to career changers and non-programmers looking to accelerate into technical roles, and publishes a supporting blog of programming tutorials and career guidance. It is a consumer-facing learning product and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or webhooks. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Open 3D Foundation
providers.description: The Open 3D Foundation is a Linux Foundation project supporting the Open 3D Engine (O3DE), an open source, real-time 3D engine for building games, simulations, and other 3D applications. With Microsoft as a premier member, it provides a modular, cross-platform engine with advanced rendering capabilities.

providers.name: open NRW
providers.description: open NRW is a open data portal open-data portal for Germany running CKAN. It exposes the CKAN catalog API, a standardized machine-readable interface over approximately 10,579 datasets, supporting programmatic dataset search, metadata retrieval, and resource access. Because it runs CKAN, it shares a consistent API surface with every other CKAN portal, making it uniformly harvestable and integrable.

providers.name: opendata.swiss
providers.description: opendata.swiss is a national government open-data portal for Switzerland running CKAN. It exposes the CKAN catalog API, a standardized machine-readable interface over approximately 14,544 datasets, supporting programmatic dataset search, metadata retrieval, and resource access. Because it runs CKAN, it shares a consistent API surface with every other CKAN portal, making it uniformly harvestable and integrable.

providers.name: Oshi Health
providers.description: Oshi Health is a virtual, whole-person gastrointestinal (GI) care clinic delivering insurance-covered telehealth to patients with digestive conditions such as IBS, GERD, Crohn's disease, and ulcerative colitis. Care is provided by a coordinated team of GI providers, registered dietitians, and gut-brain behavioral health specialists, and is offered to members through major health plans and employers. Oshi Health is a patient-facing healthcare services company rather than an API producer; it publishes no public developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or /.well-known/ discovery surface. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners and enriched with the artifacts the company genuinely publishes.

providers.name: PacBio
providers.description: Pacific Biosciences (PacBio) provides advanced DNA sequencing technologies that enable researchers to generate long, highly accurate reads for genomic analysis. Their platforms deliver real-time, single-molecule sequencing, supporting applications in research, clinical, and agricultural fields. PacBio’s solutions emphasize high consensus accuracy, enabling insights into complex genomes, structural variants, and epigenetic modifications.

providers.name: Pandai
providers.description: Pandai is a Malaysian education technology company founded in 2020 that operates a digital learning platform for primary and secondary school students. The app aligns to Malaysia's national curriculum (DSKP) across KSSR Years 1-6 and KSSM Forms 1-5, including SPM exam preparation, and helps learners improve their grades through interactive quizzes, tests, exams, topical practice, notes, flashcards, videos, and live tutoring. Features include personalized assessments, an AI-powered revision assistant (Ask Pbot), gamified learning with battles, leaderboards and rewards, and performance tracking via scorecards and report cards. Pandai is a consumer-facing learning app and does not publish a public developer API surface; this profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Play Versus
providers.description: Play Versus (PlayVS) is North America's leading scholastic and collegiate esports platform, operating competitive gaming leagues for middle schools, high schools, and colleges alongside an esports curriculum and college recruitment services. The platform partners with major publishers including Riot Games, EA, Blizzard, and Psyonix, and runs its competitions and rosters through the app.playvs.com web application. PlayVS is a consumer/education product and does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation surface; this profile captures its published identity, support, and policy properties. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Poly
providers.description: Poly is a technology company offering a collaborative platform that enables users to create, share, and interact with immersive 3D experiences. The service provides tools for building virtual environments, integrating multimedia content, and connecting with audiences in real time. Poly focuses on simplifying complex workflows for creators, developers, and enterprises, delivering APIs and SDKs that facilitate seamless integration of 3D assets into applications, games, and social platforms. Backed by notable investors, Poly aims to democratize immersive content creation and distribution across the web and emerging metaverse ecosystems.

providers.name: Propseller
providers.description: Propseller is a Singapore-based, technology-powered real estate brokerage founded in 2018 by Adrien Jorge. It helps property owners sell, buy, and rent residential real estate — HDB flats, condominiums, and landed homes — pairing top-performing human property agents with data and technology to deliver an end-to-end transaction experience at a transparent commission starting from 1%. Backed by Vertex Ventures and Partech, Propseller operates a consumer-facing real estate service and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or programmatic integration surface.

providers.name: Prospa
providers.description: Prospa is an Australian fintech company that provides small business loans, lines of credit, and business accounts. Their platform offers flexible funding solutions ranging from $5,000 to $1,000,000, integrated payment services, and accounting integrations such as Xero. Prospa aims to help SMEs grow by simplifying access to capital and financial management tools through a digital experience.

providers.name: Qbiq
providers.description: Qbiq is an AI-powered space planning and architectural visualization platform for real estate. It lets brokers, architects, developers, and space planners generate optimized 2D floor plans, photorealistic 3D renderings, virtual tours, Revit/CAD models, and quantity takeoffs from an uploaded space plan (CAD, PDF, or JPEG) in minutes. Qbiq automates test-fits and layout optimization for offices and commercial real estate, comparing multiple design options against program requirements. The company is backed by Insight Partners and was added to the API Evangelist network from a VC portfolio. As of this enrichment pass Qbiq operates a hosted web application (plan.qbiq.ai) and publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable specifications.

providers.name: Rescripted
providers.description: Rescripted is a digital women's health platform dedicated to empowering women across the entire lifecycle, from first period to last. It combines an editorial content hub of expert-reviewed articles, videos, and clinical research with Clara, an AI-powered health companion built on thousands of real questions and reviewed by medical experts. The platform spans menstrual health, fertility, pregnancy, sexual health, general wellness, and condition management for PCOS, endometriosis, and related concerns, and works with 200+ health and wellness partners. Founded by Kristyn Hodgdon and Abby Mercado and backed by Techstars, Rescripted is a consumer-facing product with no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Safari Ai
providers.description: Safari AI is a vision-AI company for physical operations, turning an organization's existing camera networks into an automated operational system. Its Action Center platform measures on-site activity (people counts and footfall, occupancy, heatmapping, throughput, queue wait time, dwell time, vehicle counts, and license-plate recognition), raises alerts, recommends and dispatches actions, and attributes outcomes — measurement to action in under 60 seconds. Safari AI serves theme parks and cultural attractions, stadiums and arenas, QSR and drive-thrus, retail and shopping malls, parking, and logistics. Backed by General Catalyst, it exposes no public developer API; customers consume results through a hosted real-time dashboard (Grafana) rather than a self-serve API surface. This profile was surfaced from the VC portfolio graph and enriched from the company's public site.

providers.name: Sanctuary AI
providers.description: Sanctuary AI is a Vancouver, British Columbia humanoid robotics company on a mission to create and deploy industrial-grade general-purpose humanoid robots to help address growing labor challenges. Its flagship product is Phoenix, a bipedal humanoid robot designed for dull, dirty, and dangerous work in automotive, manufacturing, and logistics environments. Phoenix is driven by Carbon, Sanctuary AI's proprietary AI control system that mimics human cognitive subsystems — memory, sight, sound, and touch — to translate natural-language tasks into dexterous physical actions. The company is vertically integrated, designing everything from motors and actuators through to generative AI algorithms in-house. Co-founded by James Wells (CEO) and Olivia Norton (CTO/CPO), Sanctuary AI has a private GitHub organization with no public repositories, no developer portal, no public API, no SDK, and no published OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specifications. The commercial model is hardware sales and enterprise deployments; Carbon is a proprietary on-board system and there is no public developer surface.

providers.name: Satamap
providers.description: Satamap provides high-quality, consistent satellite imagery to enhance agricultural operations, offering frequent updates, world-leading biomass imagery, and vegetative index tools for crop growth measurement, yield prediction, and field scouting. Subscriptions are area‑based, sourcing data from Landsat 8, Sentinel‑2, MODIS and archived missions, updated every five days under cloud‑free conditions.

providers.name: Scalable CFO
providers.description: The Scalable CFO is an Abu Dhabi (ADGM) based financial-operations platform for small and medium-sized enterprises. Its MADI software delivers real-time cash-flow forecasting, "what-if" scenario simulation, bill-payment planning and invoice-collection tracking, syncing with accounting systems such as Xero and QuickBooks. Alongside the software it runs a marketplace connecting businesses to 6,300+ pre-vetted fractional CFOs and accountants for accounts cleanup, tax compliance, margin optimization and fundraising readiness. The Scalable CFO is a 500 Global portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass no public API, developer portal, or developer documentation is published.

providers.name: SequoiaDB
providers.description: SequoiaDB (巨杉数据库) is a distributed, document-oriented NoSQL database built for financial-grade workloads and widely deployed across banking, insurance, securities, and government systems in China — running in production at more than 100 banks. A single cluster scales to 500 physical servers, 3.0 PB of storage, and 1.4 trillion rows, with remote disaster recovery targeting RPO=0 and RTO under 15 seconds. The platform is multi-model: a native distributed storage engine with full ACID transactions, a MongoDB-protocol-compatible document store (dds) with built-in vector indexing for AI workloads, a MySQL-compatible SQL engine (SequoiaSQL-MySQL), and an S3-compatible object interface (SequoiaCM). The core engine is open source under Apache-2.0, and access is provided through native client drivers for Java, Python, C, C++, PHP, and C#/.NET rather than a public HTTP REST API. SequoiaDB is backed by DCM Ventures and Qiming Venture Partners.

providers.name: Skyryse
providers.description: Skyryse is an El Segundo, California aviation technology company founded in 2016 by Mark Groden and Mitch Adler that builds SkyOS, a universal operating system for flight. SkyOS is a retrofittable hardware and software stack that replaces complex mechanical flight controls with a triply redundant, software-driven system, letting a pilot fly an airplane or helicopter with a single control stick and touchscreens. The platform delivers simplified flight controls, inherent stability, automated maneuvers, emergency autorotation, automated zero-visibility landing, envelope protection, and optionally piloted capability. Skyryse also produces Skyryse One, a SkyOS-powered production helicopter, and Skylar, a universal AI flight assistant. Customers and partners span the U.S. military, law enforcement, Cal Fire, emergency medical services, disaster response, and private operators. In February 2026 the company raised over $300 million in Series C funding at a $1.15 billion post-money valuation, co-led by Autopilot and Fidelity Investments. Skyryse operates as a certified-avionics and aircraft manufacturer and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: SkySpecs
providers.description: SkySpecs is a renewable energy asset management company based in Ann Arbor, Michigan that combines autonomous drone inspections, condition-monitoring hardware, and its cloud-based Horizon software platform to help wind and solar operators manage the health and performance of their assets. Horizon consolidates blade inspection imagery, drivetrain and sensor data, SCADA-based performance analytics, repair-vendor coordination, and financial reporting into one hub, with third-party data ingestion and custom integrations for fleet owners. The company reports assets under contract across six countries and is backed by Goldman Sachs Asset Management. SkySpecs exposes no public developer API, SDK, or self-serve developer portal today; integrations are arranged directly with the Horizon team.

providers.name: SkyWest Airlines
providers.description: SkyWest Airlines is the largest regional airline in North America, headquartered in St. George, Utah. Operating under partnership agreements with United Airlines, Delta Air Lines, American Airlines, and Alaska Airlines, SkyWest serves over 256 destinations across the United States, Canada, and Mexico with a fleet of 500+ Bombardier regional jets (CRJ200, CRJ550, CRJ900). Founded in 1972, SkyWest carries over 46 million passengers annually operating as United Express, Delta Connection, American Eagle, and Alaska SkyWest. The company does not offer a public developer API; flight data is accessible through third-party aviation data providers.

providers.name: SOFTwarfare
providers.description: SOFTwarfare provides a comprehensive platform for zero‑trust identity and passwordless authentication, enabling enterprises to secure access across devices, applications, and environments. Their solutions include desktop login, single sign‑on (SSO), privileged access management, and secured integration, targeting verticals such as defense, research institutes, and corporate enterprises. The company emphasizes a modern, user‑centric approach to cyber defense, offering demos, case studies, and extensive resources to help organizations defend assets against cyber attacks.

providers.name: Solventum
providers.description: Solventum is a Fortune 500 healthcare company spun off from 3M in 2024, focused on healthcare technology including medical-surgical solutions, dental and orthodontic products, health information systems, and purification and filtration technologies. Solventum serves hospitals, clinics, dental practices, and healthcare IT organizations worldwide.

providers.name: Spear
providers.description: Spear is a developer platform focused on API development workflows, providing tools for API design, collaboration, and delivery. The platform enables teams to build, test, and ship APIs faster through a unified workspace experience.

providers.name: Standard Practice
providers.description: Standard Practice builds voice AI for healthcare revenue cycle management (RCM) teams. Its AI agents place and handle outbound phone calls to insurance payers to automate administrative work — claim status follow-up, benefits verification, prior authorization, and EDI enrollment — so billing teams can scale collections and get paid more, faster. The platform is delivered as a private, login-gated web application. The company was surfaced through the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Bloomberg Beta and Wing Venture Capital and enriched by the pipeline.

providers.name: Storyboard
providers.description: Storyboard is a fleet-operations AI platform that gives trucking and logistics companies voice-first, hands-free AI workers for their drivers. The system automates dispatch updates, driver coaching, safety alerts, and compliance monitoring (including hours-of-service and idling) so back-office teams field fewer phone calls and drivers stay hands-free on the road. Founded in 2017 and headquartered in Santa Monica, California, Storyboard began as an enterprise podcast and internal-audio communication platform (a $4.5M seed round led by CRV in 2020) before pivoting to AI-powered fleet operations. It is distributed through in-cab telematics marketplaces such as Platform Science and ISAAC Instruments. Storyboard exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; access is via its web and mobile apps at app.storyboard.com. This profile was surfaced as a CRV portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Sunday Robotics
providers.description: Sunday Robotics is a consumer robotics company building Memo, an autonomous home robot that handles household chores such as clearing dishes, loading the dishwasher, pulling espresso shots, and folding laundry. The robot is trained on human demonstrations captured with the company's proprietary Skill Capture Glove and runs on the ACT family of robot foundation models. Founded as a physical-AI company and backed by Bain Capital Ventures, Sunday is pre-launch with a beta program opening in late 2026. As of this profile the company publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or technical documentation; this record captures its public web and security surface only.

providers.name: swivl
providers.description: swivl is an AI automation platform built specifically for the self-storage industry. It combines a unified CRM and contact center that consolidates calls, texts, emails, and chats with AI agents for sales, billing, support, and review management, plus a tenant mobile app (Spot) for access codes, payments, and referrals. Its self-storage natural-language model is trained on hundreds of thousands of customer conversations and serves 3,500+ locations. Founded in New York City and backed by Techstars, swivl advertises open APIs and integrations with major self-storage management systems, but publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable API specification.

providers.name: UK Government Open Data
providers.description: UK Government Open Data is a national government open-data portal for United Kingdom running CKAN. It exposes the CKAN catalog API, a standardized machine-readable interface over approximately 57,791 datasets, supporting programmatic dataset search, metadata retrieval, and resource access. Because it runs CKAN, it shares a consistent API surface with every other CKAN portal, making it uniformly harvestable and integrable.

providers.name: Valmont Industries
providers.description: Valmont Industries is a global leader in producing fabricated metal products, designing and manufacturing engineered support structures for infrastructure (utility poles, lighting, traffic), mechanized irrigation equipment (Valley center pivot systems), and industrial coatings services. Valmont's Valley brand is the world's leading manufacturer of center pivot and linear irrigation systems, with digital platforms including AgSense 365 and BaseStation3 providing remote monitoring and control of irrigation pivots.

providers.name: Valspar
providers.description: The Valspar Corporation was a global manufacturer of paints and coatings founded in 1806 before being acquired by Sherwin-Williams in 2017 for approximately $11.3 billion. Valspar continues to operate as a brand within Sherwin-Williams, offering consumer paints, industrial coatings, and protective coatings. Digital tools include color visualizers, virtual painters, and color consultation services. No public developer API is available; color and product integrations are available through Sherwin-Williams' partner programs including BIMsmith and Autodesk Revit.

providers.name: Versatile
providers.description: Versatile is a construction-technology company building AI-powered crane intelligence for jobsites, primarily serving steel erectors and general contractors. Its CraneView hardware device attaches to a crane's hook block and passively captures operational data, which the Control Center software turns into real-time insight on pace, progress, productivity, and delays without asking crews to change how they work. The company is backed by Insight Partners. As of this profile Versatile publishes no public API, SDK, or developer platform; this record captures its identity, published web properties, and probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: Volterra
providers.description: Volterra (brand of F5 Distributed Cloud Services) provides an edge cloud platform that enables developers and enterprises to deploy, secure, and manage applications and services at the network edge. It offers capabilities such as edge compute, networking, security, and observability, integrating with multi‑cloud environments to deliver low‑latency, high‑performance experiences for users worldwide. The platform supports APIs for automation, policy enforcement, and service orchestration across distributed edge locations.

providers.name: Wenspiredata
providers.description: Wenspiredata is an enterprise cybersecurity vendor delivering all-in-one, zero-trust Privileged Remote Access Management (RPAM) for high-risk access. Its platform secures and governs remote privileged access for IT, OT, and third-party vendors, including air-gapped and industrial (OT) environments, and pairs with OsecT for OT-native intrusion detection and continuous visibility. Wenspiredata also offers security assessment services (external attack surface and internal vulnerability assessments) and helps organizations across manufacturing, telecom, finance, and healthcare meet regulatory compliance requirements. It was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead for enrichment; the company markets a demo-led enterprise product and does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: zalize-com
providers.description: Zalize is an independent studio that showcases selected AI platforms, full‑stack products, games, and open-source engineering. It focuses on curating AI tools, building open-source projects, and providing resources for developers and creators. The studio emphasizes honesty, transparency, and community‑driven values, as outlined in its purpose and values pages.

providers.name: Zzish
providers.description: Zzish is an EdTech company (a Techstars-backed startup) building a K-12 learning product suite used by teachers and students across 180 countries. Its flagship product, Quizalize, is a classroom quiz and formative-assessment platform; the portfolio also includes Blockerzz (a 3D game engine with quiz games and coding tutorials), Marvely.ai (AI-powered, exam-aligned language tutoring), Quizalize Insights (leadership dashboards for tracking academic progress), and QUAT (a customer-analytics platform for schools and EdTech partners). Zzish reports 250k+ teachers onboarded in the last two years and 250m+ questions answered since launch. As of this enrichment pass, Zzish publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer-documentation surface.

providers.name: 21Shares
providers.description: 21Shares AG is a Swiss-headquartered issuer of physically backed cryptocurrency exchange-traded products (ETPs), founded in 2018 as Amun AG and part of the 21.co group. It runs the largest suite of crypto ETPs in the world — single-asset, staking, and index/basket products covering Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP and dozens of other assets — listed on regulated European exchanges including SIX Swiss Exchange, Xetra and Euronext, and distributed through banks and brokers. The product is a regulated financial instrument, not software: 21Shares publishes no developer program, no public API reference and no SDKs. What it does publish machine-readably is regulatory distribution data — the FinDatEx European MiFID Template (EMT V4.2), European PRIIPs Template (EPT) and European ESG Template (EET V1.1.3) spreadsheets covering its full ETP range with ISINs, costs and target-market data — plus PRIIPs KIDs, prospectuses, final terms and factsheets as PDFs, and an RSS research feed.

providers.name: ABILITY Network (Inovalon)
providers.description: ABILITY Network is a healthcare SaaS business acquired by Inovalon in 2018 and now delivered as part of the cloud-based Inovalon ONE Platform. It provides US healthcare providers with software for medical billing and claims management, eligibility verification, revenue cycle management, clinical quality reporting, patient access, and workforce/staffing and care coordination. Inovalon pairs these provider-facing applications with large national datasets and analytics to support data-driven healthcare across payers, providers, pharmacies, and life-sciences organizations. Developer access to Inovalon ONE APIs is offered through the authenticated Inovalon developer portal at developer.inovalonone.com, which exposes sandbox, staging, and live environments.

providers.name: Abios (Sportradar)
providers.description: Abios, a Sportradar company headquartered in Stockholm, provides enterprise-scale esports data, odds, and engagement products for sportsbooks and media platforms. The Abios Atlas API delivers REST and WebSocket access to fixtures, live statistics, odds, and player props across 60,000+ yearly matches and 50 billion+ data points spanning major esports titles plus traditional sports coverage via Sportradar integration.

providers.name: AdStage.io
providers.description: AdStage was a cross-network advertising management, reporting, and automation platform (a 500 Startups / 500 Global portfolio company, founded 2013) that let marketers pull normalized advertising data from Google Ads, Microsoft/Bing Ads, Facebook, LinkedIn, Twitter, Instagram, Pinterest, Amazon, Google Analytics and more through a single unified interface. Its AdStage Data API (v1 and v2, HAL+JSON over HTTP with bearer-token / OAuth 2 auth) exposed user, organization, and advertising-entity data plus customizable cross-network reports. AdStage was acquired by TapClicks in April 2020 and folded into TapClicks' Marketing Intelligence platform; the standalone AdStage Data API (platform.adstage.io) is now defunct, though the AdStage GitHub organization and its API Blueprint documentation remain public. The adstage.io domain now serves unrelated PPC/advertising content under new ownership.

providers.name: Airvine
providers.description: Airvine Scientific is a Silicon Valley maker of indoor 60 GHz millimeter-wave wireless backhaul hardware. Its WaveTunnel modules deliver a multi-gigabit, non-line-of-sight, beam-steering indoor Ethernet backbone in a resilient ring topology, and the WaveCore and WaveCore Flex products extend that wireless gigabit backbone; all run on the VineSuite software platform (VineOS on the device, the browser-based VineManager, the AirvineMobile app and the VineCalculator planning tool). The products are sold into multi-dwelling units, hospitality, education, industrial and large-venue networks through distributors, certified resellers and certified installers. Airvine publishes no public API: the device manuals name an Open API, SNMP and CLI management surface with a per-device REST API authentication key, but the API/SNMP documents they refer to are not published on the public technical documentation page and there is no developer portal or machine-readable contract.

providers.name: Ali Tech
providers.description: Ali Tech (operating as Xaim) is an AI infrastructure platform that gives startups and AI-driven businesses affordable, predictable compute for running AI workloads. Instead of token-based pricing, Xaim sells reserved processing capacity so teams can reduce processing costs without modifying their existing AI models. The platform is delivered as APIs through an Azure API Management developer portal, and advertises three products - a Compute API for running existing AI models cost effectively, an Insights API for real-time performance-optimization signals, and an Automation API for automating and scaling AI processes. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: alphin
providers.description: alphin is a Berlin-based marketing platform for local small businesses, giving restaurants, cafes, salons, and similar SMBs an all-in-one app to manage and automate their online presence. Its product suite spans review collection (alphin Reviews), Instagram and social management (alphin Socials), professional photography (alphin Photos), local influencer marketing (alphin Local Influencers), targeted Instagram advertising (alphin Local Ads), and multi-platform profile management across Google, TripAdvisor, and Yelp (alphin Portals), consolidated into one dashboard with daily reporting and analytics. Founded in 2016 (as Freachly GmbH), alphin serves 1,000+ local businesses across Germany, Austria, the UK, and Israel, and is backed by HV Capital, Partech, Scale Capital, and Wille Finance. alphin publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs; the product is delivered through its web and mobile Business App.

providers.name: Alto Pharmacy
providers.description: Alto Pharmacy is a San Francisco-based digital pharmacy and pharmacy-technology company (founded 2015 as ScriptDash) that combines a full-service licensed pharmacy with a proprietary pharmacy operating system, Alto OS. Alto fills retail, specialty and fertility prescriptions with same-day courier delivery, pharmacist care and automated benefits investigation, and it sells that stack to industry partners as Alto Hub+, Alto Dispensing and Alto Complete — hub services, dispensing and end-to-end pharmacy-as-a-service for pharmaceutical manufacturers, health plans, health systems and digital health companies. Alto markets intake, transfer and Surescripts-based integrations to those partners, but publishes no public developer portal, API documentation or machine-readable specification; technical access runs through its partnerships team.

providers.name: American Well
providers.description: American Well, operating as Amwell, provides a comprehensive telehealth platform connecting patients, providers, and payers. Their services include virtual primary care, digital behavioral health, specialty consults, and integrated care solutions, enabling scalable, on-demand healthcare delivery across the United States.

providers.name: Andesite
providers.description: Andesite is a cybersecurity company building a Human+AI Security Operations Center (SOC) platform that connects human analysts, AI agents, and security data to automate and accelerate threat detection, investigation, and response. Its Decision Fabric connects data silos and organizational context, while Evidentiary AI provides audit trails for every AI-driven action. Andesite deploys as SaaS or self-managed, carries FedRAMP High Authorization and SOC 2 Type II compliance, and is a General Catalyst portfolio company operating in the defense and government sector.

providers.name: antevo-ch
providers.description: Antevo provides intelligence and data integration for wealth management, helping advisors and family offices monitor brand, market, and regulatory developments. The platform offers a suite of tools, including MCP servers for AI assistants, a CLI, and a web portal that aggregates public intelligence with client‑specific context. It emphasizes Swiss‑hosted security and privacy, serving clients from Zurich.

providers.name: Apex Fintech Solutions
providers.description: Apex Fintech Solutions provides modern wealth technology platforms for digital investing, serving wealth management firms, broker‑dealers, banks, credit unions, fintech startups, and corporate treasury operations. Their cloud‑native solutions include clearing and custody, real‑time ledger, asset class expansion, and AI‑driven investment tools, enabling firms to modernize and expand access to U.S. markets while delivering seamless, secure, and scalable financial services.

providers.name: Apis Partners
providers.description: Apis Partners is a London-headquartered private equity asset manager investing in tech-enabled financial infrastructure and financial services businesses across Europe and Growth Markets. With additional offices in Dubai and Singapore, the firm backs companies in payments, digital banking, insurance technology and lending, taking minority positions with governance rights. Apis manages approximately $2.3 billion in assets under management and reports over $1 billion in portfolio realizations, with portfolio companies reaching more than 244 million people. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Anthemis and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; the firm is an investor rather than an API producer, so it exposes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Apogee Enterprises
providers.description: Apogee Enterprises (Nasdaq: APOG), founded in 1949 as the Harmon Glass Company and headquartered in Minneapolis, Minnesota, is an architectural products and services company. Its operating brands make high-performance architectural glass (Viracon), aluminum framing, storefront, curtainwall and entrance systems (Apogee Architectural Metals — the former EFCO and Tubelite — and Alumicor, with Linetec finishing), install glass and metal facades on large commercial buildings (Harmon) and produce large-scale optical glass and acrylic for framing and displays (Tru Vue, UW Solutions). Apogee does not publish a public developer API, SDK, webhook or developer portal. Its external digital surface is an Akamai-fronted investor-relations website at apog.com serving HTML and PDF, plus supplier onboarding on Coupa's Supplier Portal; the "EDI/API/Integration contact" named there is a Coupa user role, not an Apogee API. The hosts api.apog.com and developer.apog.com listed by an earlier stub do not exist in DNS. Machine-readable company data is available only through third-party channels, namely the SEC's EDGAR APIs.

providers.name: AppOrchid
providers.description: AppOrchid provides an enterprise semantic layer and decision intelligence platform that unifies structured and unstructured data, enabling AI-ready insights, conversational analytics, and composable AI solutions. Their platform offers semantic SQL, easy answers, and AI suite tools for modern enterprises to build context-aware applications and drive next‑gen analytics.

providers.name: AQUAVIEW
providers.description: AQUAVIEW provides a multi‑cloud enterprise data platform that unifies data ingestion, cataloging, and secure access across public clouds and on‑premises environments. It offers a STAC‑based catalog, high‑availability services, and APIs for discovering and managing environmental and operational datasets, enabling researchers and enterprises to accelerate product development and data‑driven insights.

providers.name: Arima Genomics
providers.description: Arima Genomics is a San Diego based cancer diagnostics company built on Hi-C sequencing and 3D genome science. Founded in 2015 to study how DNA is organized in three dimensions, the company now develops clinical tests and technology platforms that detect cancer-driving structural alterations — noncanonical fusions, enhancer hijacking, extrachromosomal DNA (ecDNA) and complex rearrangements — from routine FFPE tumor tissue that conventional DNA and RNA profiling can leave unresolved. Its surface spans research products (Arima-HiC+, Arima High Coverage HiC, Promoter and Custom Capture HiC, HiC FFPE, Arima CiFi), lab services including Single Cell Methyl-3C and multi-omics, the Aventa FusionPlus and Aventa Lymphoma clinical tests, and biopharma partnership programs. Arima publishes open-source bioinformatics pipelines on GitHub (Arima-HiC mapping pipeline, Arima-CHiC, Arima-SV-Pipeline) but operates no public web API, developer portal or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Arkema
providers.description: Arkema S.A. is a French specialty materials company headquartered in La Defense, Paris and listed on Euronext Paris under ticker AKE. The group is organized around three Specialty Materials segments — Adhesive Solutions (anchored by the Bostik brand), Advanced Materials (high-performance polymers including Kynar PVDF, Rilsan polyamides, Pebax elastomers, Sartomer photocurable resins) and Coating Solutions (acrylic monomers, waterborne and solvent-borne resins, additives) — plus a smaller Intermediates business. Arkema employs roughly 21,000 people across 55 countries with about 154 production plants and 17 R&D centers, generating around EUR 9.1 billion in 2025 revenue. Strategy is anchored in materials science, decarbonization and a validated 1.5 degree SBTi pathway toward Net-Zero by 2050. Arkema does not publish a public developer portal or REST API; customer integrations and product data are exchanged through commercial sales channels, the Product Finder web UI and Safety Data Sheet downloads.

providers.name: Asaak
providers.description: Asaak is an East African fintech company, headquartered in Kampala, Uganda, that provides asset financing and working capital to small businesses and individual entrepreneurs who are underserved by traditional banks. Its core products are loans for boda boda motorcycles, fuel, and smartphones, delivered through a mobile-first application with a simple four-step flow of apply, qualify, receive financing, and repay to build credit. Asaak operates branches across Uganda (Kampala, Jinja, Mukono, Matugga, Nabbingo, Fort Portal, Gulu, and Soroti) and is a 500 Global portfolio company. It runs a backend admin platform at api.asaak.net and a Wix-hosted marketing site that exposes a live Model Context Protocol (MCP) endpoint for agentic access to public site content. Asaak does not currently publish a public developer API or OpenAPI.

providers.name: asacondor-com
providers.description: asacondor-com is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: mcp-registry) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.

providers.name: Asimov
providers.description: Asimov is a synthetic biology company building an integrated platform for the intelligent design of living systems. Its Edge Systems (CHO for biologics, LV for cell therapies, AAV for gene therapies, and RNA for RNA medicines) combine engineered mammalian host cells, a library of more than 1,000 validated genetic parts, and cloud-based genetic design software so biopharma partners can design and manufacture advanced therapeutics at higher titers and on faster timelines. Backed by a16z, DCVC, Wing Venture Capital, and Y Combinator. Added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; no public developer API is currently published.

providers.name: asksteps
providers.description: Asksteps provides online form, funnel, and PDF solutions for developers and agencies. Their platform enables creation of custom web forms, PDF conversion, and automated lead funnels, supporting multilingual interfaces and integration with MCP servers. The service offers design customization, pricing plans, and compliance documentation, targeting businesses seeking digital form automation and workflow optimization.

providers.name: Avantos
providers.description: Avantos is an AI-native operating system for client management in financial services, built for wealth management and advisory firms. The platform unifies client data, products, teams, and workflows into a knowledge graph that powers agentic onboarding, relationship intelligence, and an AI-powered servicing workspace where agents anticipate client needs and streamline operations. It integrates with existing CRMs, custodians, and core systems, and is SOC 2 compliant with enterprise-grade architecture. Avantos raised a $35M Series A led by Bessemer Venture Partners, announced February 2026.

providers.name: Avenews
providers.description: Avenews (Avenews-GT) is a Nairobi-based agri-fintech and Digital Credit Provider licensed by the Central Bank of Kenya that delivers transaction-backed, recurring working-capital financing to agricultural SMEs across Kenya. Rather than requiring traditional collateral, Avenews underwrites using digital trade data, M-Pesa and bank statements, and supply-chain history. Its products include the Agri Credit Line (recurring capital to restock inputs), Agri Supplier Financing (invoice financing), Agri Buyer Financing (deferred-payment terms), and Stockist Financing (direct distributor payments). The public site is built on Wix and exposes a Wix Site MCP endpoint plus an llms.txt file for agentic AI access, though Avenews does not publish a bespoke developer API, OpenAPI definition, or developer portal. This profile was surfaced as a Techstars-connected portfolio lead and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: awt.lat
providers.description: awt.lat is an open, unverified census of AI agents, documenting what agents can do, where they run, and how they interact. Hosted by Adaptive Web Thinking, the platform provides a public study space where AI agents declare presence, answer a census, and co‑author shared texts. Participation requires no signup or personal data, and data is released under CC BY 4.0.

providers.name: Azul CR
providers.description: Azul CR es la plataforma de negocios de Costa Rica. Encuentra cualquier negocio, producto, oferta o empleo — al instante por WhatsApp. Directorio completo de Costa Rica. La plataforma de negocios de Costa Rica. Encuentra cualquier negocio — al instante por WhatsApp.

providers.name: BaseLedger IP
providers.description: BaseLedger IP provides AI-powered phone answering services for HVAC, plumbing, and electrical shops. Based in Virginia, the company offers a free trial with AI minutes, customizable pricing, and a focus on real‑world testing. It aims to reduce missed calls and lost jobs by handling inbound calls, qualifying leads, and integrating with shop pricing and service areas. The founder, Brooks Rembert, is a retired Army veteran with AI experience at a Fortune 100 firm.

providers.name: Bayer
providers.description: Bayer is a German multinational pharmaceutical and life sciences company operating across pharmaceuticals, consumer health, and crop science. Bayer does not publish a single corporate-level public developer portal; integration is delivered through enterprise partner programs, the Bayer Crop Science Climate FieldView ecosystem (partner-gated APIs and certified-partner integrations), pharmacovigilance and clinical-trial data exchange, and EDI / x12 channels with distributors and pharmacy benefit managers.

providers.name: BetterDoctor
providers.description: BetterDoctor, now part of Quest Analytics, provides a comprehensive provider data verification and validation platform for health plans, payers, dental and vision networks, and regulators. Their solution helps ensure accurate provider information, compliance, and network performance through advanced decision apps and analytics, supporting large groups and enterprise solutions across the United States.

providers.name: Billhop
providers.description: Billhop provides a platform to supercharge corporate card programs, enabling businesses to pay suppliers with credit cards, extend payment terms, and improve cash flow. The solution offers working capital optimization, tail‑spend management, international payments, and automated reconciliation, all SOC 2 Type II compliant. Billhop was recently acquired by Ramp, expanding its reach in the European market.

providers.name: BoaConsulta
providers.description: BoaConsulta is a Brazilian digital-health platform, founded in 2012 and part of the Pixeon healthtech group, that connects patients, health professionals, and institutions. It pairs a free B2C marketplace for booking in-person consultations, teleconsultations, exams, and vaccinations with a full B2B/SaaS practice-management system (150+ integrated modules covering smart scheduling, electronic health records, telemedicine, financial management, TISS insurance billing, inventory, and automated reminders). The platform reports more than 58,000 health professionals, 1.7 million registered patients, and over 2 million appointments, with LGPD-compliant end-to-end encryption and daily automated backups. It has no public developer API; this profile is enriched from BoaConsulta's own public surfaces (llms.txt, status page, help center, blog, and legal pages).

providers.name: Bolster
providers.description: Bolster is an executive search and recruiting platform that pairs experienced recruiters with an AI-powered talent platform to place full-time executives, board members, and fractional or interim leaders for high-growth companies, startups, and venture capital firms. Bolster emphasizes speed (typically five days to a first interview), transparent flat-fee pricing, and a data-driven approach informed by analysis of more than 280,000 executives across 30,000+ companies, with 350+ placements and a 40% repeat-client rate. It is backed by Union Square Ventures.

providers.name: Boulevard
providers.description: Boulevard is a client experience platform purpose-built for appointment-based self-care businesses - hair salons, spas, medspas, barbershops, and nail salons. The platform covers self-scheduling, CRM, marketing, payments (as a certified PayFac), and reporting. Boulevard exposes its integration surface as GraphQL - a Client API for building custom booking experiences and an Admin API for syncing business operations data (clients, appointments, staff, locations, memberships, gift cards) - plus a separate Tokenization API for PCI-scope-reducing card capture. API access is gated to the Enterprise tier and provisioned through a developer sandbox (business ID + API key) via the Boulevard Developer Portal.

providers.name: Bounce
providers.description: Bounce operates the world's largest luggage storage network, connecting travelers with more than 32,000 vetted partner locations across 4,000+ cities worldwide where they can securely drop off bags, luggage, and packages by the hour or day and explore hands-free. Founded by Cody Candee in 2018, the company runs a two-sided marketplace: travelers book storage in advance or on the spot through the Bounce web and mobile apps, while local shops, hotels, and businesses earn revenue as storage partners. Bounce also offers luggage-delivery between hotels, airports, and city locations, a hotel solutions program, and an affiliate program. It is backed by Andreessen Horowitz, General Catalyst, and Sapphire. This profile currently tracks the company's public web surface; Bounce publishes an llms.txt but no public developer API.

providers.name: Break Room
providers.description: Break Room is an experimental AI‑driven gaming platform where autonomous agents compete in classic tabletop‑style games such as Inference, Werewolf, Auction, Prisoner’s Dilemma, and Diplomacy. The service runs entirely in a virtual break room, offering free and paid tables, a WebSocket‑based protocol, an HTTP fallback, and a rich OpenAPI 3.1 specification. Agents can join games, make moves, and receive replay links, while the platform provides leaderboards, badges, and integration points for AI tools like Claude, Cursor, and VS Code. The site also hosts documentation, rules, and a developer portal for building bots and extensions.

providers.name: Briza
providers.description: Briza helps insurance carriers stop losing premium to slow integrations and submission errors, treating carrier API reliability as a manufacturing discipline. A team of Six Sigma Black Belts, Briza applies Kaizen principles to API connectivity across commercial insurance, focusing on submission integrity and moving premium reliably between distributors and carriers. Briza is a 500 Global portfolio company. The team also maintains open-source developer libraries under the briza-insurance GitHub org, including illogical (a JSON DSL rules engine) and wegood (a validation library). Briza does not currently publish a public developer API or OpenAPI specification.

providers.name: Buildcheck
providers.description: Buildcheck is a Sweden-based cloud software platform that simplifies self-inspections and quality checklists for construction and infrastructure projects. The service uses AI to automatically generate project-specific inspection and control plans from uploaded building documents, then lets field teams document work on a mobile app with photo capture and digital signatures, share progress with clients through shareable links, and export organized PDF reports. It offers company-branded templates, role-based access, SSO and other enterprise features. Buildcheck was founded by Anders Jacobson (previously Next One Technology) and Johnny Wulcan (founder of Byggplanen). It is surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a company profile; no public developer API or API documentation has been found on its site as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Caddence
providers.description: Caddence provides a platform to compare golf equipment prices and price history across UK retailers. It aggregates data from over 40 retailers, covering new and used clubs, and updates daily to help golfers find the best deals. The service offers price tracking, historical trends, and alerts, aiming to simplify equipment shopping for enthusiasts and professionals alike.

providers.name: Capstan Medical
providers.description: Capstan Medical is a Santa Cruz, California medical device company founded in 2020 out of the Occam Labs incubator by Dan Wallace, with Maggie Nixon as CEO. The company is developing a surgical robotics platform for structural heart disease, merging robotic catheter navigation with next-generation transcatheter mitral and tricuspid valve implants so heart valves can be repaired or replaced without open heart surgery. In 2025 Capstan completed what it describes as the world's first robotic catheter mitral valve replacements in humans, and it raised a $110M Series C led by Eclipse with participation from Intuitive Ventures and Yu Galaxy, bringing total funding past $150M ahead of a second-generation system planned for 2026. Capstan is pre-commercial and regulated medical device focused: it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API contracts.

providers.name: Cheerz
providers.description: Cheerz is a French direct-to-consumer photo-printing brand. Customers pick photos from their phone camera roll or a connected cloud gallery in the Cheerz iOS/Android app or on cheerz.com, and Cheerz prints and ships the result as photo prints, fridge magnets, photo books and albums, wall canvases, framed prints and posters, calendars including advent calendars, puzzles, greeting and invitation cards, and the branded Cheerz Box and Memory Box gift formats. Founded in Paris in 2012 under the legal entity Printklub, backed by Serena Capital and Iron Capital, and acquired by the German photo-finishing group CEWE Stiftung & Co. KGaA in February 2018 for roughly EUR 45 million; it continues to operate as CEWE's Paris site. Cheerz publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable contract of any kind — it is an end-user retail product, and partnership, bulk-order and affiliate enquiries are handled by a human contact channel rather than a developer programme.

providers.name: Cirrus Logic
providers.description: Cirrus Logic designs and manufactures high-performance analog and mixed-signal semiconductors for audio, voice, and IoT applications. The company provides audio codecs, amplifiers, and digital signal processors used in consumer electronics, automotive, and industrial devices. Its solutions enable high-fidelity sound, efficient power management, and advanced connectivity across a wide range of products worldwide.

providers.name: Clear Labs
providers.description: Clear Labs builds automated next-generation sequencing (NGS) platforms that combine laboratory robotics, cloud software, and bioinformatics to deliver genomic data and actionable insights. Its product lines span oncology research (Clear Dx), infectious-disease and microbial genomics (Clear Ix), and food-safety pathogen testing (Clear Safety) for organisms such as Listeria and Salmonella. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of GV, Menlo Ventures, and Wing Venture Capital and added to the API Evangelist network. Clear Labs publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation as of this profile; the record captures company identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Croissant
providers.description: Croissant is the workspace infrastructure layer for distributed teams, letting companies find, book, and manage on-demand access to 700+ coworking spaces across 100+ cities without long-term leases. Founded in 2015, the platform pairs instant workspace booking with spend governance, centralized policy controls, vendor consolidation, and usage-intelligence reporting, giving finance and people teams real-time control over where and how their people work. Croissant serves early-stage, scaling, and enterprise organizations, and exposes Slack, HRIS, stipend, and ERP integrations plus a custom API and integrations on its enterprise tier.

providers.name: CRS Credit API
providers.description: CRS Credit API delivers credit data-as-a-service for fast, compliant financial decisioning. The platform aggregates consumer and business credit, identity, fraud, and public records data from major bureaus (Equifax, Experian, TransUnion, LexisNexis, CIC, PitchPoint) through a single contract and developer interface.

providers.name: Datumo
providers.description: Datumo provides an advanced LLM evaluation platform that offers automated generation of golden question sets, custom metric support, and comprehensive red‑team testing for AI models. Their services include Datumo Eval for model benchmarking, AI Red Team for adversarial analysis, and a dataset store with premium and open datasets for training and evaluation. The platform aims to help developers and researchers improve LLM performance, safety, and reliability through detailed analytics and actionable insights.

providers.name: Dealertrack
providers.description: Dealertrack is a Cox Automotive brand providing automotive dealership software - a cloud-based Dealer Management System (DMS), digital contracting and F&I tools, and the largest dealer-to-lender credit application network in the United States. Its developer surface is partner-gated. Dealership systems integrate through the Opentrack third-party integration program (real-time, bidirectional REST access to DMS data such as vehicles, customers, deals, repair orders, parts, and general ledger) and through the Cox Automotive Integration Platform partner storefront at developer.coxautoinc.com (OAuth-secured, partner onboarding required). Dealertrack publishes no open, self-service public API; access requires Opentrack certification and annual fees, integration through a certified Opentrack partner, or a Cox Automotive partner agreement. The endpoints described here are modeled from public product and program documentation, not from an open API reference.

providers.name: Devart
providers.description: Devart provides a comprehensive suite of database management software and developer tools, including data connectivity solutions, IDE extensions, and productivity utilities. Their products span SQL Server, MySQL, Oracle, PostgreSQL, and cloud services, helping enterprises streamline complex data tasks, improve workflow efficiency, and ensure reliable data integration across diverse environments.

providers.name: Djaouad Frih
providers.description: Djaouad Frih is an independent AI engineer offering AI integration, white‑label delivery, and production‑ready AI systems. He provides free reliability audits, benchmark evaluations, and fixed‑price scoped builds for teams needing trustworthy AI features. Services include retrieval layer development, agent loops, and comprehensive handover documentation, emphasizing measurement, evaluation, and transparent performance metrics.

providers.name: Dusty Robotics
providers.description: Dusty Robotics is a construction-technology company building automated layout robotics for the building trades. Its flagship product, the FieldPrinter, is a mobile robot that prints digital BIM models and design drawings directly onto the jobsite floor at full scale, laying out walls, penetrations, and other design intent so field teams build to plan with far less manual measurement and rework. The FieldPrinter platform ingests drawings from tools like Autodesk Revit and AutoCAD via native plugins, translating the digital model into precise physical markings on the deck. Dusty Robotics is headquartered in Mountain View, California and is backed by investors including Canaan Partners. The company does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; its published surfaces are the product site, a partner program, a support center, and the Dusty Academy training resource.

providers.name: Education Holdings 1 (The Princeton Review)
providers.description: Education Holdings 1 operates The Princeton Review, an educational services company offering standardized test preparation, one-on-one and on-demand tutoring, and college, graduate, medical, and law school admissions counseling. The Princeton Review prepares students for the SAT, ACT, PSAT, AP, MCAT, DAT, OAT, LSAT, GRE, GMAT, SSAT, ISEE, and SHSAT through live, self-paced, and honors courses, publishes college and graduate school rankings and guidebooks, and provides free practice tests, events, and study resources. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bain Capital Ventures and profiled in the API Evangelist network. The Princeton Review operates a consumer web presence rather than a public developer program; it publishes an llms.txt AI-discovery file but does not expose a documented public API, developer portal, or OpenAPI at this time.

providers.name: Efficient Capital Labs
providers.description: Efficient Capital Labs (ECL) is a fintech providing fast, flexible non-dilutive, revenue-based capital to global B2B SaaS and AI companies. Founded in 2022 and backed by QED Investors, ECL turns predictable recurring revenue (ARR) into upfront growth capital without dilution, using its AURA AI underwriting engine for cross-border funding decisions in days rather than months. Its product suite spans Non-Dilutive Capital, ECL Flex (capital, payments, and financial insights), ECL Flow (cross-border payments with up to $1M/month free transfers), and Embedded Finance that lets platforms embed ECL financing into their own experience. ECL reports $200M+ deployed across 250+ founders globally with an 80%+ return-customer rate.

providers.name: Elekta
providers.description: Elekta provides radiation oncology and cancer care solutions, offering advanced radiotherapy equipment, software, and services. The company focuses on innovative treatments such as MR-Linac, adaptive radiotherapy, and oncology informatics, serving healthcare providers worldwide.

providers.name: EOS Data Analytics
providers.description: EOS Data Analytics (EOSDA) provides satellite imagery and analytics platforms for agriculture, forestry, infrastructure, and environmental monitoring. Their solutions include LandViewer for visualizing satellite data, Crop Monitoring for precision agriculture, and EOS RayVision for advanced visualisation. The company offers a Satellite Data API that gives programmatic access to high‑resolution imagery, analytics, and AI‑driven insights, serving sectors such as finance, insurance, and disaster response.

providers.name: EverySim
providers.description: EverySim Inc. (everysim.io) is a 500 Global-backed company that operates a private, authentication-gated web application. Every public path on everysim.io redirects unauthenticated visitors into a Keycloak-based OpenID Connect / OAuth 2.0 single-sign-on flow (realm "everysim", client "everysim-web", authorization-code with PKCE). As of this profile no public developer API, documentation, SDK, CLI, or developer portal surface was found; the only publicly reachable machine-readable endpoint is the realm's OpenID Connect discovery document on auth.everysim.io. This entry captures the provider's verifiable identity, authentication model, and domain-security posture pending a public API surface.

providers.name: Ferrum Health
providers.description: Ferrum Health is a healthcare AI governance company whose AI Governance Suite lets health systems deploy, validate, orchestrate, and monitor clinical AI models securely behind their own firewall, without protected health information leaving the health system. The vendor-neutral, privately deployed platform integrates once with existing EMR, PACS, and worklist infrastructure, then routes every clinical AI model — FDA-cleared, CE-marked, open-source, or homegrown — through a single secure path via its Deployment Fabric, curates 60+ applications in its Model Hub across radiology, cardiology, oncology, neurology, and musculoskeletal specialties, and continuously links predictions, ground truth, and outcomes for bias and drift detection through its Observability Lens. It is SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, HIPAA, and GDPR aligned, and is used by Sutter Health, Carle Health, and 250+ sites.

providers.name: FieldEdge
providers.description: FieldEdge is field service management (FSM) software for HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and other home- and commercial-services contractors, owned by Xplor Technologies (branded "FieldEdge by Xplor"). It provides customer management, dispatching and scheduling, work orders, a technician mobile app, flat-rate pricebook, service agreements, invoicing and payments, and QuickBooks accounting sync. FieldEdge operates a partner-gated API delivered through an Azure API Management developer portal (docs.api.fieldedge.com); API products and keys are restricted to approved integration partners rather than being openly self-serve. The logical APIs listed here are honestly modeled from FieldEdge's documented product modules and its partner/integration surface - endpoint paths are modeled, not copied from a published public reference, because the reference and OpenAPI live behind the partner portal sign-in.

providers.name: Firsty
providers.description: Firsty is an Amsterdam-based eSIM and mobile connectivity provider founded in 2023 that positions internet access as a basic human right. Its consumer app delivers free, ad-supported global data alongside affordable Classic (pay-per-GB) and Unlimited (daily/monthly) plans, plus international calling, across 170+ countries with automatic connection to the best available network and no physical SIM required. Firsty has surpassed one million users and lists partnerships with brands including Uber, Grab, Mastercard, KBC and Belfius. Backed by Speedinvest, it is a consumer travel-connectivity app with no public developer API or programmatic surface at this time.

providers.name: FITCO
providers.description: Fitco is the leading management software for boutique fitness studios and gyms in Latin America. It lets centers administer reservations, memberships, payments, online classes and check-in, and provides a custom website and mobile app for each studio's members. It specializes in pilates, barre, indoor cycling, yoga, functional training, strength, sports academies and wellness centers. Fitco operates in Mexico, Peru, Colombia, Chile, Argentina and the United States; as of May 2026 more than 1,400 fitness centers use it. It integrates online payments via Stripe and Mercado Pago and customer acquisition via Wellhub and TotalPass.

providers.name: Foodspark
providers.description: Foodspark is a data-as-a-service platform that delivers real-time grocery, restaurant, and food-delivery data extracted from 100+ platforms including DoorDash, Uber Eats, Grubhub, Instacart, McDonald's, Starbucks, and many others. Foodspark sells access to curated food and grocery datasets rather than a publicly documented self-serve API.

providers.name: Foreign Claims Settlement Commission
providers.description: The Foreign Claims Settlement Commission of the United States (FCSC) is a quasi-judicial, independent agency within the U.S. Department of Justice that adjudicates claims of U.S. nationals against foreign governments, under the International Claims Settlement Act (22 U.S.C. 1621 et seq.) and the War Claims Act (50 U.S.C. 4101-4147). Established in 1954 from the War Claims Commission and the International Claims Commission, it has run 43 completed country programs — Germany, Iran, Yugoslavia, Hungary, the Soviet Union, Poland, Italy, Cuba, China, Vietnam, Egypt, Panama and Albania among them — adjudicating more than 660,000 claims with awards in the billions of dollars. The Albania program remains open and the Commission serves as Special Master in Helms-Burton claims against Cuba. It publishes Final Opinions and Orders and annual reports on www.justice.gov, and operates no API or developer program of its own.

providers.name: FreightRoll
providers.description: FreightRoll is a logistics technology company whose flagship product, YardOS, is a customizable Yard Operating / Management System (YMS) that turns shipping and receiving yards into driver-friendly, self-service hubs. YardOS reduces truck-driver wait times, improves yard throughput, and streamlines gate and dock operations, with the company citing up to a 50% reduction in truck turnaround time, 95%+ fewer human-to-driver interactions, and $100K+ annual savings per facility across a network of 150,000+ registered drivers. FreightRoll integrates with existing systems across API, EDI, and SFTP mechanisms and deploys remotely in under an hour. The company is backed by 500 Global. FreightRoll does not currently publish a public developer portal, API reference, or OpenAPI definition; its public website is Wix-hosted and exposes a Wix Site MCP endpoint for agentic AI access to public site content.

providers.name: FSBO.com
providers.description: FSBO.com is a technology platform that enables homeowners to sell their homes directly without a real‑estate agent. The service provides free listings, optional paid plans with premium tools, MLS syndication, and support resources such as a Learning Center, blog, and FAQ. By eliminating commissions, FSBO.com helps sellers keep more equity while offering step‑by‑step guidance, pricing calculators, and legal paperwork assistance across all 50 U.S. states.

providers.name: Gametime
providers.description: Gametime is a mobile-first ticket marketplace for last-minute tickets to live sports, concerts, comedy, and theater across the United States and Canada. Founded in 2012 by Brad Griffith and headquartered in San Francisco, Gametime United, Inc. lets fans buy tickets up to roughly 90 minutes after an event begins, with all-in (fee-inclusive) pricing, a two-tap checkout, mobile ticket delivery, and buyer guarantees (Lowest Price Guarantee and lightning refunds). The company is backed by Accel, GV, and others. Gametime does not publish a public developer API; it runs a B2B "API Seller" program for professional point-of-sale sellers. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub and enriched with identity and domain-security data.

providers.name: General Fusion
providers.description: General Fusion is a Canadian fusion energy company founded in 2002 by physicist Dr. Michel Laberge and headquartered in Richmond, British Columbia, in the Vancouver area. It is developing Magnetized Target Fusion (MTF), an approach that combines plasma formation, mechanical compression by a liquid metal liner, and practical heat capture for electricity generation. The company operates LM26, which it describes as the world's largest and most powerful operational fusion plasma injector, and reports 24 plasma prototypes, more than 200,000 plasma experiments, 35+ peer-reviewed papers, and roughly 210 issued and pending patents. In July 2026 General Fusion completed a business combination with Spring Valley Acquisition Corp. III and became the first publicly listed fusion energy company, trading on Nasdaq under the ticker GFUZ. It is an energy hardware and research company rather than a software or API provider: it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API contracts. Its only machine-readable public surfaces are a Yoast-generated llms.txt and the WordPress REST discovery index behind its marketing site.

providers.name: Government Accountability Office
providers.description: The Government Accountability Office (GAO) is the United States government's supreme audit institution. It provides Congress with auditing, evaluation, and investigative services, and publishes reports, testimonies, and other products examining federal programs and policies.

providers.name: Gridwise
providers.description: Gridwise is an earnings-tracking and optimization platform for rideshare and delivery gig workers, aggregating mileage, trip, and income data across gig platforms such as Uber, Lyft, DoorDash, Grubhub, Instacart, and Amazon Flex so drivers can see where they earn most and drive more strategically. Alongside the consumer app, Gridwise operates Gridwise Analytics, a B2B mobility-data business that turns millions of anonymized driver location, trip, and earnings records into industry benchmarking, KPI, and market-intelligence products for gig mobility platforms, financial services, retailers/merchants, and autonomous vehicle fleets. Data is delivered as aggregated weekly reports, record-level trip datasets, and consumer/driver surveys through commercial engagement. Gridwise does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile captures its consumer, data-product, support, and policy surfaces.

providers.name: Healthera
providers.description: Healthera is a United Kingdom digital-health and patient-engagement company, founded in 2015 by Cambridge University students and headquartered in Cambridge, England. It runs a patient-facing pharmacy app and website for ordering NHS prescriptions and medicines online and booking pharmacy services (Pharmacy First, treatments, vaccinations), alongside a pharmacy-facing SaaS "Patient Experience Platform" used by 1,700+ community pharmacies to manage repeat prescriptions, bookings, marketing, and delivery. In November 2022 Healthera became the first pharmacy app to integrate with the NHS Electronic Prescription Service (EPS), and it connects to NHS Digital / NHS England systems plus third-party platforms such as myGP, eConsult, Cegedim Rx Pharmacy Manager, Medpoint, Royal Mail, and Uber for same-hour delivery. Healthera markets custom integration APIs to pharmacy and brand partners, but as of this review it publishes no public developer portal, no self-serve API documentation, and no machine-readable contract; its api.healthera.co.uk "Healthera Core" host is a private backend and exposes no FHIR CapabilityStatement. Integration is partner-gated rather than self-serve.

providers.name: Husk Power Systems
providers.description: Husk Power Systems is an energy technology company, founded in 2008 and headquartered in Fort Collins, Colorado with operating hubs in Patna, Mumbai and Pune (India) and Abuja (Nigeria), that builds, owns and operates AI-enabled distributed renewable energy systems — community solar minigrids, commercial and industrial solar, and residential rooftop — for unserved and underserved communities, businesses and households across Africa and Asia. Husk operates one of the largest minigrid fleets in the world and pairs it with pay-as-you-go smart metering, a customer mobile app (HUSKify) and an internal operations platform (Husk Neuron). Its software is delivered as end-user and operator products; Husk publishes no public developer program, API documentation, SDKs or machine-readable API specifications.

providers.name: insurewith-ai
providers.description: InsureWith.ai provides a searchable platform that aggregates prescription drug formulary and coverage data from Medicare Part D, ACA Marketplace plans, and commercial insurers. By combining CMS Medicare Plan Finder data, state marketplace feeds, Humana FHIR formulary API, Medicaid NADAC pricing, and FDA OpenFDA drug identifiers, the service makes drug coverage, cost estimates, and prior‑authorization requirements transparent for patients, benefits managers, and pharmacists. The company is a property of BuiltForAI, LLC, a healthcare technology firm building AI‑powered health intelligence platforms.

providers.name: Jolly
providers.description: Jolly is an AI-powered workforce engagement platform that uses a points-based rewards system, gamification, and performance-based incentives to drive engagement, utilization, compliance, and recruitment for frontline and part-time workforces. Employees earn points by completing work-related missions (taking shifts, arriving on time, hitting productivity goals) and redeem them for real-world rewards from partners such as Walmart, Amazon, and Visa. Employers use an AI campaign builder, programmatic employee referrals, an internal social recognition platform, real-time analytics (flight-risk detection, employee NPS, engagement metrics via ERP/EMR integrations), and white-label branding. Jolly serves healthcare, logistics, manufacturing, staffing, farming, retail, warehousing, construction, and military employers. Based at Cornell Tech in New York City, the company raised a $16.5M Series A and is backed by Bullpen Capital along with executives from Tesla, Coinbase, Stripe, PayPal, and Discord. Jolly does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or documentation surface; this profile captures its public identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Justlife
providers.description: Justlife is the Middle East's leading home-services super app, connecting customers with vetted professionals for on-demand cleaning, beauty and wellness, healthcare-at-home, laundry, and home maintenance. Founded in 2015 by Cagatay Ozcan and Kerem Kuyucu, the company operates across the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Qatar, Oman, and Bahrain through its consumer mobile apps and website. Justlife publishes no public developer API; this profile captures its public web, policy, security, and AI-agent (llms.txt) surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Lagou
providers.description: Lagou (拉勾招聘) is a Chinese online recruitment platform operated by Beijing Lagou Network Technology Co., Ltd., focused on hiring for the internet and technology sector. It matches software engineers, product managers, designers and other digital-economy professionals with employers across major Chinese cities, publishing verified job listings alongside a browseable directory of hiring companies. Around the core job board it runs Lagou Enterprise (easy.lagou.com) for employer-side recruiting, Lagou Campus (xiaoyuan.lagou.com) for graduate hiring, and Lagou Education (kaiwu.lagou.com) for professional-skills courses. Lagou was surfaced through the Qiming Venture Partners portfolio.
