The platform covers invoicing, collections, cash application, deductions, credit, dispute management, financial close, reconciliation, consolidation, and cash forecasting. HighRadius serves 1,500+ enterprise customers and ships pre-built integrations with 50+ ERPs and systems including SAP, Oracle, Microsoft Dynamics, and NetSuite. Integration is delivered through those pre-built ERP connectors and partner engagements rather than a public self-serve developer API; the company publishes a Trust Center documenting SOC 2, ISO 27001, PCI DSS, and GDPR posture.

providers.name: HomeVision
providers.description: HomeVision is an AI-powered collateral underwriting and appraisal quality-control platform for mortgage lenders and appraisal management companies (AMCs). Its MIRA platform pairs machine intelligence with human review to transform unstructured appraisal content — narrative commentary, sketches, photos and addenda — into structured, review-ready data using OCR, large language models, natural language processing and computer vision, and integrates with popular LOS and AMS platforms plus external data such as public records and MLS. Founded in 2019 and based in San Francisco, HomeVision is backed by Initialized Capital and Newark Venture Partners, and offers private API integration to customer order-management systems (no public developer portal).

providers.name: IEX
providers.description: IEX Group, Inc. operates the IEX Exchange, a U.S. equities market focused on providing fair and transparent trading. The company offers market data, trading venues, and technology solutions for investors and institutions. IEX emphasizes speed bumps to reduce predatory high‑frequency trading, and provides APIs for market data, order routing, and analytics. It is publicly known for its mission to level the playing field for all market participants.

providers.name: iManage
providers.description: iManage is the leading AI‑powered knowledge work platform for legal and professional services. It manages, organizes, and activates corporate knowledge, enabling smarter decisions while securely connecting people and AI. The solution offers document management, collaboration tools, and AI‑driven insights to streamline workflows across firms.

providers.name: Internet Assigned Numbers Authority
providers.description: The Internet Assigned Numbers Authority (IANA) performs the global coordination of the DNS Root, IP addressing, and other Internet protocol resources. IANA maintains the protocol registries, top-level domain delegations, time zone database, and language subtag registry that the Internet relies on. Bulk registry data is published as machine-readable files distributed via rsync and FTP rather than through a public REST API.

providers.name: Jones
providers.description: Jones is a full-service SaaS platform purpose-built for insurance compliance in construction and commercial real estate, unifying Certificate of Insurance (COI) collection, deep insurance auditing, workflow automation, and a licensed brokerage in one platform. It pairs hundreds of insurance specialists with AI agents to review COIs and policies at enterprise scale, and is used by general contractors, construction managers, owner-operators, REITs, property management teams, and insurance brokers to manage compliance across large portfolios of subcontractors, vendors, and tenants. Jones offers two engagement models: Jones Software (self-managed) and Jones Operator (an AI-driven concierge that runs day-to-day insurance tasks). Reported scale: 40,000+ projects, 3 billion+ square feet, and 50 million+ insurance documents processed for 300+ industry leaders. Headquartered in New York, NY, Jones was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and Foundry Group.

providers.name: Lupin & Holmes
providers.description: Lupin & Holmes is an offensive-security and social-engineering research firm that blends adversarial creativity with rigorous logic to strengthen defensive security practices. Its flagship product, Depi, is a proactive cybersecurity dashboard for software supply-chain protection, giving security teams real-time visibility into dependency vulnerabilities, patch tracking, and risk response. The company also publishes hands-on security research covering supply-chain attacks, dependency confusion, and CI/CD exploitation. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Seedcamp and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Margo
providers.description: Margo is a Linux Foundation open standard initiative for interoperability at the edge of industrial automation ecosystems. Founded by ABB, Capgemini, Microsoft, Rockwell Automation, Schneider Electric, and Siemens, it defines mechanisms for interoperability between edge applications, devices, and orchestration software.

providers.name: Merlin Labs
providers.description: Merlin (Merlin Labs, Inc., NASDAQ: MRLN) is a Boston-headquartered aerospace and defense company founded in 2018 that builds takeoff-to-touchdown flight autonomy for legacy and next-generation aircraft. Its product is the Merlin Pilot, an aircraft-agnostic, AI-powered autonomy stack that pairs machine-learning mission planning with deterministic, hardcoded fallback flight systems, and that has flown hundreds of autonomous flights from test facilities in Kerikeri (New Zealand), Quonset Point (Rhode Island) and Bedford/Hanscom (Massachusetts). Merlin is a prime contractor to USSOCOM for C-130J autonomy, works with the U.S. Air Force on KC-135 tanker autonomy, and collaborates with Northrop Grumman, Honeywell, GE Aerospace and Israel Aerospace Industries. The company holds a New Zealand Part 146 aircraft design organization designation and reached Stage of Involvement 3 (SOI 3) with the Civil Aviation Authority of New Zealand in August 2026. Merlin became publicly traded in March 2026 through a business combination with Inflection Point Acquisition Corp IV. Merlin sells embedded flight-autonomy software to aircraft OEMs, primes and government programs; it publishes no public developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable contract.

providers.name: Metromile
providers.description: Metromile is a pay-per-mile auto insurance platform powered by telematics and data science. Customers attach the Pulse OBD device to their vehicle to track mileage; premiums consist of a base monthly rate plus a per-mile charge, rewarding low-mileage drivers with significant savings. Beyond consumer insurance, Metromile Enterprise offers a cloud-based REST API platform for property and casualty insurers covering touchless claims automation, accident reconstruction (Replay), fraud detection (Detect), digital FNOL reporting (Report), and back-office workflow automation (Streamline). Metromile was acquired by Lemonade in July 2022.

providers.name: Miso Robotics
providers.description: Miso Robotics is a Pasadena, California kitchen-automation company that builds AI-powered robotics and restaurant operations software for commercial food service. Its flagship product, Flippy, is an autonomous fry station that uses computer vision and NVIDIA-accelerated motion planning to identify food items, detect doneness and run up to 100 baskets per hour on existing commercial fryers from Frymaster, Henny Penny and Pitco. Miso also ships Zippy (built on the acquired Zignyl platform), a real-time digital shift manager for forecasting, scheduling, task management, incentives and payroll that connects to restaurant point-of-sale systems. Customers include White Castle, Jack in the Box, CaliBurger and Auntie Anne's. Miso publishes no public developer API, no OpenAPI/AsyncAPI contract and no SDKs; its integrations are delivered as private partner connections (Toast, PAR and other POS vendors) arranged through sales, and its public GitHub organization carries ROS/robotics and cloud-infrastructure forks used internally rather than a client-facing API surface.

providers.name: Mortgage Industry Standards Maintenance Organization (MISMO)
providers.description: Mortgage Industry Standards Maintenance Organization (MISMO) is a nonprofit association that develops and maintains data standards for the mortgage finance industry. It provides a comprehensive reference model, logical data models, XML schemas, and implementation guides that enable consistent data exchange among lenders, servicers, investors, and technology providers. MISMO’s resources support regulatory compliance, improve operational efficiency, and foster innovation across the mortgage ecosystem.

providers.name: National Bank of Canada
providers.description: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada, TSX: NA) is a Schedule I chartered bank headquartered in Montreal, Quebec, founded in 1859. It is the sixth-largest of Canada's Big Six banks and the leading bank in Quebec, serving personal, commercial, wealth-management, and financial-markets clients. On open finance, National Bank is a notable first-mover: it was the first major Canadian bank to launch a secure, consent-based data-sharing API for retail customers, but it does NOT operate a public self-serve first-party developer portal. Programmatic access to customer financial data is delivered through aggregators rather than a downloadable public API — principally Flinks, the Montreal aggregator in which National Bank holds an ~80% stake, via its Open Banking Environment (OBE), and also through Plaid. National Bank and Flinks are founding participants of the FDX Canada working group, aligning their data-sharing on the FDX technical standard, and the bank is positioning ahead of Canada's forthcoming, legislated-but-not-yet-operational Consumer-Driven Banking framework (Budget 2024 / FCAC oversight). Today access is voluntary and aggregator-mediated; there is no operational open-banking mandate and no public first-party API surface.

providers.name: Noh
providers.description: Noh is a Brazilian consumer fintech (neobank) founded in November 2021 by Ana Zucato and Octavio Turra, headquartered in Sao Paulo, SP. Noh pioneered Brazil's first joint account and shared card for couples, letting two partners manage money together with equal permissions, real-time expense visibility, automatic categorization, and a shared spending limit based on combined income. Products include a joint checking account, a shared Visa card (prepaid and credit), and payments via Pix, boleto, and card, plus joint investing. It is a consumer mobile app (iOS and Android) with no public developer API, developer portal, or documentation surface at this time. Backed by Kindred Ventures and other investors; added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead company profile.

providers.name: Nuvocargo
providers.description: Nuvocargo is an AI-powered freight-management platform for North American truckload logistics, focused on the US-Mexico-Canada cross-border corridor. Its "Nuvo AI" system coordinates a network of specialized agents (quoting, negotiation, booking, dispatch, tracking, exception handling, audit, and payment) to automate the freight load lifecycle, and it pairs that software with licensed freight brokerage, managed transportation, and customs-brokerage services. The company was surfaced through the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Homebrew and QED Investors. As of this enrichment pass Nuvocargo publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal; onboarding is contact-gated ("zero-integration" pilots), so this profile captures the company identity, legal/resource surface, and domain-security posture rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: O11
providers.description: O11 is a Y Combinator (Winter 2026) startup building custom AI software for financial services firms. Rather than forcing teams onto a new external platform, O11 embeds AI-driven automation directly into the tools finance teams already use every day — Excel, PowerPoint, Word, and other enterprise applications — so users can generate presentations, spreadsheets, and documents and automate workflows without switching contexts. The company positions itself against the observation that a majority of firms still rely on legacy software where generic bolt-on AI features fail to deliver real value. As of this profile O11 publishes a marketing site (o11.ai) but no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or developer documentation could be found; this remains an early-stage identity profile in the API Evangelist network awaiting a public API surface.

providers.name: PlusMargin
providers.description: PlusMargin (Plus Margin) is a Bangkok, Thailand based digital marketing and business consulting practice operating under the tagline "Connect | Engage | Convert." The firm focuses on inbound marketing strategy, personalized and AI-assisted marketing, buyer-persona development, and customer-journey mapping for its clients, and publishes Thai-language editorial content across marketing, business, advertising, technology, learning, insurance, and lifestyle topics. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global — where secondary sources describe an earlier Singapore-founded "predictive persuasion" e-commerce personalization product — but the domain today serves a four-page consulting and content site with no trace of that platform. Enrichment on 2026-08-12 confirmed no product API, no developer portal, no SDKs on any package registry, no /.well-known/ discovery surface, no llms.txt and no agent card. The one callable, machine-readable surface is the stock WordPress REST API the marketing site exposes at /wp-json — 237 routes across 11 namespaces, anonymously readable for content — which is WordPress core's API rather than a product PlusMargin designed, documents, or supports.

providers.name: Polsia
providers.description: Polsia is an autonomous AI business-management platform marketed as "AI that runs your company while you sleep." It deploys a set of specialized AI agents — business planning, competitor research, social media, ads, email outreach, customer support, code generation, finance, and deployment — coordinated by an orchestrator to run a company's daily operations on recurring schedules for a monthly subscription plus a share of revenue generated on the platform. Founded by Ben Sera and backed by True Ventures and Sound Ventures (raised $30M at a $250M valuation in 2026), Polsia is a hosted consumer/SMB SaaS product and does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or MCP server.

providers.name: proteanTecs
providers.description: proteanTecs is an Israeli deep data analytics company for advanced electronics. It embeds on-chip monitoring Agents (UCT, margin, path margin, I/O and power monitors) into semiconductor designs and pairs them with cloud and edge machine-learning applications that report health, performance, reliability and quality of chips and systems from design through production test into field operation. Solutions cover power and performance optimization, RAS, functional safety and diagnostics, chip production, system production and advanced packaging, and are consumed by semiconductor, data center, AI/HPC, automotive, telecom and mobile customers. The company markets APIs and data connectors for integrating its analytics with ATE testers and third-party analytics tools, but publishes no public developer program, API reference or machine-readable contract.

providers.name: Ranger AI
providers.description: Ranger AI, operating as Ranger RFX Inc., provides an AI‑powered intelligence layer for industrial engineering. It helps organizations automate RFP responses, evaluate tenders, and review contracts by extracting answers from technical documents and citing sources. The platform targets procurement automation, engineering document analysis, and enterprise AI applications, delivering accurate, citation‑backed insights to streamline decision‑making in industrial contexts.

providers.name: rekord
providers.description: Rekord is a Dublin-based fintech platform that helps banks and fintechs automate credit underwriting and customer onboarding. Its AI-native decisioning platform unifies data from many sources into a single view, orchestrates decision workflows, runs a natural-language policy engine, and provides AI-assisted case management so credit and risk teams can make defensible, transparent decisions at scale. Rekord surfaces the signal buried in large volumes of applicant and transaction data to speed underwriting and onboarding while enforcing identity verification and compliance. It is a portfolio company of point-nine. Rekord does not currently publish a public developer API, documentation portal, or machine discovery surface; this profile captures its public identity and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Robotiq
providers.description: Robotiq designs and manufactures collaborative robotics hardware and software — adaptive grippers, vacuum grippers, force-torque sensors, wrist cameras, and pre-engineered workcells for palletizing, machine tending, screwdriving, and assembly. Founded in 2008 and headquartered in Lévis, Quebec, Canada, the company helps manufacturers automate repetitive tasks by embedding task intelligence ("Intelligence Made Physical") directly into end-of-arm tooling for platforms such as Universal Robots, FANUC CRX, and Omron/Techman. Robotiq publishes open-source ROS drivers and a C++ gripper SDK through its GitHub organization, but it does not operate a public web/REST API — this profile captures its developer-facing identity, open-source SDKs, and domain security posture rather than a hosted API surface.

providers.name: Robylon AI
providers.description: Enterprise AI customer-support platform spanning voice, WhatsApp, chat, email, social media and ticketing. The platform runs AI agents against a customer knowledge base with configurable personas, model selection, human-agent handover and assignment logic, and its APIs let external systems interact with Robylon and trigger workflows including voice and outbound automation. Documentation is public and extensive and the docs host serves both an llms.txt index and an unauthenticated MCP server; what is not published is a machine-readable contract for the product API itself.

providers.name: roli
providers.description: ROLI (Luminary ROLI Ltd.) is a British music-technology company known for expressive electronic instruments — the Seaboard, LUMI Keys keyboards, and the modular BLOCKS system — together with companion software such as ROLI Dashboard, ROLI Connect, Equator, and ROLI Learn. Its instruments pioneer MPE (MIDI Polyphonic Expression) for per-note pitch, timbre, and dynamics control. For developers, ROLI publishes first-party SDKs under the github.com/weareroli organization — the C++ BLOCKS-SDK and roli_blocks_basics for building applications that talk to BLOCKS hardware, and the archived mpejs library for MPE MIDI in the browser. ROLI is backed by Balderton Capital and Index Ventures. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead and enriched with real developer, SDK, and domain-security artifacts.

providers.name: Salt Security
providers.description: Salt Security provides an AI-powered API security platform that discovers all APIs, stops API attacks in real-time, and provides remediation insights. The platform delivers full lifecycle API security through API discovery, posture governance, and advanced threat protection using patented AI and ML technology. Salt Security announced an Agentic AI Security platform and MCP Discovery capabilities in 2026.

providers.name: Scarlet
providers.description: Scarlet is Europe's only Notified Body specialised in software and AI-based medical devices. Operating at scarlet.cc, Scarlet certifies Software as a Medical Device (SaMD) and AI as a Medical Device (AIaMD) under the EU Medical Device Regulation (MDR), streamlining conformity assessment, CE marking, and certificate transfers for manufacturers who ship iteratively and release frequently. Backed by Creandum, Scarlet was built to bring modern, fast-moving regulatory certification to AI and software medical-technology companies. Scarlet is a regulatory and certification services provider; it currently publishes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Simplifi by Quicken
providers.description: Simplifi by Quicken is a personal finance management application that aggregates financial accounts from over 14,000 institutions, enabling users to track spending, manage budgets, monitor investments, set savings goals, and access projected cash flow analytics. The platform uses OAuth-based API connections to banks and purpose-built APIs to billers to pull data into a unified financial dashboard available on web and mobile.

providers.name: SnapCare
providers.description: SnapCare is an Atlanta-based healthcare workforce company, founded in 2017 as SnapNurse and relaunched under the SnapCare name in 2023, that pairs a national clinician marketplace with Booker, its SaaS workforce platform for hospitals, post-acute facilities, agency suppliers and clinicians. Booker combines predictive scheduling against census and historical demand trends, real-time per-diem shift fulfillment, internal float-pool management, same-day pay, and escalation of unfilled shifts to approved contingent suppliers. SnapCare acquired predictive staffing analytics vendor Medecipher in 2024 and merged with the nurse community connectRN in April 2026, raising a Series A led by Suvretta Capital. SnapCare sells the platform to healthcare organizations rather than to developers; no public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable API contract was found on its public surface.

providers.name: Solve Data
providers.description: Solve Data provides a marketing automation platform that simplifies content creation, message personalization, and campaign management. It removes complexity by offering reusable content blocks, intelligent frequency management, and real‑time analytics, helping brands deliver targeted messages without manual effort. The solution includes audience segmentation, decision engine, and audit trails, and is trusted by enterprises for scalable, data‑driven communications.

providers.name: Sparkles
providers.description: Sparkles (sparkles.dev) is a San Francisco developer-tools startup in Y Combinator's Winter 2026 batch building AI coding agents for a whole team, not just engineers. A technical owner connects the company's GitHub repositories and configures environment variables, after which any teammate on a company email address can describe a change and have an agent implement it inside an isolated sandbox and open a GitHub pull request for developer review. Positioned as "Lovable for existing projects," it lets marketers, designers, and operations staff ship safe code changes without needing to know Git or the command line. As of this profile Sparkles exposes only a marketing and product website plus legal pages; it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, CLI, or OpenAPI, so this record captures verified company identity rather than an API surface.

providers.name: Springshare
providers.description: Springshare provides a suite of library services and tools, including LibGuides, LibCal, LibAnswers, LibWizard, and many others, to help libraries manage resources, engage patrons, and streamline operations. Their platform supports public, academic, K‑12, and special libraries, offering customizable solutions for content discovery, event scheduling, reference services, and analytics. Springshare’s products are designed to improve library workflows, enhance user experiences, and foster community engagement across a wide range of library environments.

providers.name: Straiker
providers.description: Straiker is an AI-native security company for agentic AI, founded by security veterans from Palo Alto Networks. It protects every layer of AI agent deployments from prompts to infrastructure with a closed-loop system that pairs autonomous adversarial testing with sub-second runtime defense. Its products are Ascend AI (autonomous AI threat detection that integrates into CI/CD to test agents for prompt injection, tool manipulation, goal hijacking and data leakage), Defend AI (agentic runtime security that blocks identity abuse, memory poisoning, data exfiltration and malicious MCP connections in real time using proprietary LLM judges), and Discover AI (agent/MCP discovery and posture management). Straiker is backed by Bain Capital Ventures and Lightspeed Venture Partners. Its developer documentation and API/SDK integration surface are gated behind an enterprise access code; there is no public API reference.

providers.name: Tamr
providers.description: An enterprise data management company that uses machine learning to automate the mastering, enrichment, and classification of messy data across disparate sources. Helps large organizations unify customer, supplier, and product data to power analytics and AI initiatives.

providers.name: Tass Vision
providers.description: Tass Vision is a venture-backed technology startup that operates a product website at tassvision.ai. It markets two named products, SITRAC and VITRAC, each with its own product page and pricing page, alongside About, How It Works, Blog, Calendar, and Contact sections. The public site is a Vue single-page web application with Zendesk-based customer support. The company is backed by 500 Global and Big Sky Capital among a cluster of Central Asian venture funds and accelerators (IT Park Uzbekistan, Astana Hub, National UzVC, and others). As of this profiling the company exposes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API specifications; this profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched with a live domain-security probe.

providers.name: TreeHouse Foods
providers.description: TreeHouse Foods is one of the largest manufacturers of private label packaged foods and beverages in North America, producing snack and convenience foods for retail grocery and foodservice customers. The company is publicly traded on the NYSE (THS) and is headquartered in Oak Brook, Illinois. TreeHouse Foods produces over 1,600 SKUs across snacking, beverage, and meal preparation categories.

providers.name: TTRacing
providers.description: TTRacing is a Malaysian gaming chair and gaming furniture brand selling ergonomic gaming chairs, office chairs, and accessories through an online Shopify storefront at ttracing.my. The store is agent-commerce ready: it publishes an llms.txt and agents.md with explicit agent instructions, a UCP (Universal Commerce Protocol) discovery document at /.well-known/ucp, and a hosted Model Context Protocol (MCP) endpoint that lets AI shopping agents search the catalog, build carts, and run buyer-approved checkout. Human customer accounts are handled via Shopify's OpenID Connect / OAuth 2.0 authorization server. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched from live probes of its public agent-facing surface.

providers.name: Twelve
providers.description: Twelve is a carbon transformation company that converts CO2, water, and renewable electricity into fuels and chemicals that serve as drop-in replacements for petroleum-based products. Its proprietary eManufacturing technology powers AirPlant One in Moses Lake, Washington, which produces E-Jet sustainable aviation fuel and E-Naphtha, while its eMade program partners with consumer brands on CO2-made materials. Investors include TPG, DCVC, Microsoft, Carbon Direct, Breakout Ventures, and the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative. Twelve publishes no public developer API, but its Wix-hosted site exposes an llms.txt and a live site MCP endpoint for agentic access.

providers.name: Twill
providers.description: Twill is a referral-based recruiting platform with the tagline "talent recommended talent." It makes hiring easier and faster by having a network of more than 50,000 vetted, experienced professionals across engineering, product, sales, and growth recommend their peers and friends for open roles, producing warm introductions to passive candidates instead of recruiter cold outreach. Twill advertises an average 22-day time to hire, a 90-day retention guarantee on placements, flat-fee pricing, and intelligent matching built in partnership with MIT's Generative AI Lab. The company is backed by Bloomberg Beta and does not currently publish a public developer API or API documentation; api.withtwill.com serves its private platform backend.

providers.name: Unacademy
providers.description: Unacademy is a Bangalore-based online learning platform — one of India's largest — offering live classes, courses, study material, and test preparation for competitive exams including UPSC Civil Services, IIT JEE, NEET-UG, SSC, CA Foundation, and CSIR UGC NET, delivered through its web platform and dedicated learner, educator, and parent mobile apps. Backed by SoftBank Vision Fund, Unacademy runs a consumer platform on an internal API (api.unacademy.com) but publishes no public developer program, API documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Underdog Fantasy
providers.description: Underdog (Underdog Sports, formerly Underdog Fantasy) is a Brooklyn, New York based sports gaming company founded in 2020 by Jeremy Levine that operates daily fantasy sports, pick'em, and — since 2025 — federally regulated sports prediction markets on its own proprietary technology stack. Its consumer products include Classic Pick'em, Pick'em Champions, Best Ball and other Draft Games, Streaks, Team Picks, and the Underdog Predict prediction-markets exchange, delivered through iOS, Android, and web apps rather than a public developer API. Underdog reached roughly $500M in annual revenue within five years, was valued at $1.2B after a Spark Capital-led Series C in March 2025, acquired CFTC-registered derivatives infrastructure in March 2026, and in July 2026 was the subject of a proposed acquisition by IG Group. The company publishes no developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API contract; its public technical surface is limited to an RFC 9116 security.txt with a PGP key, a Honeybadger-hosted status page covering its API and Stats services, and the Underdog-Inc GitHub organization.

providers.name: Unlearn
providers.description: Unlearn is a San Francisco AI company that builds digital twin generators for clinical trials — machine learning models trained on patient-level historical data that forecast an individual participant's clinical outcomes under control or standard of care. Sponsors use these AI-generated digital twins to plan trials, monitor clinical data, and run smaller, more powerful studies; the approach is qualified by the EMA and aligned with current FDA guidance. Unlearn is backed by 8VC and DCVC and publishes no public developer API.

providers.name: Wander
providers.description: Wander is a vertically integrated luxury hospitality company offering smart vacation homes with hotel-grade amenities, dedicated remote-work spaces, and 24/7 concierge service across North America. Founded by John Andrew Entwistle and headquartered in Austin, Texas, Wander powers owners and operators through WanderOS, its proprietary agentic AI operating system that automates dynamic pricing, operations, and guest support. The company raised a $50M Series B in 2025 co-led by QED Investors and Fifth Wall, with Redpoint Ventures, Uncork Capital, Starwood, and Breyer Capital participating, bringing total funding past $100M. Wander ships no public developer API, but publishes a deliberately agent-ready web surface: an llms.txt, an AI sitemap of 8,500+ markdown property pages with live 90-day pricing and availability refreshed daily, and Content-Signal AI-use permissions in robots.txt.

providers.name: Wodan AI
providers.description: Wodan AI provides zero‑trust AI solutions that run machine‑learning models on encrypted data without ever decrypting it. By leveraging advanced cryptographic techniques, the platform enables enterprises to extract insights from sensitive information while preserving privacy and complying with regulations such as GDPR and the EU AI Act. Their services target identity verification, financial services, industrial IP protection, and broader AI‑driven analytics, offering a secure, collaborative environment for data‑intensive workloads.

providers.name: Xpertsea
providers.description: Xpertsea is an aquaculture technology company (backed by QED Investors) that has rebranded its product as Kampi (bekampi.com) — an AI-powered shrimp-farming management app used by producers in Ecuador to monitor ponds, track growth and feed, and make production decisions in real time from mobile and web apps. xpertsea.com now 301-redirects to bekampi.com. The company publishes no public developer program or API surface: no docs/api/developer subdomains, no OpenAPI, and no API client SDKs (its @xpertsea npm scope holds two 2022-era UI-component forks). bekampi.com does publish an llms.txt, captured in this repository.

providers.name: Zageno
providers.description: ZAGENO is a multi-supplier e-commerce marketplace and procurement platform for pharma and life-science R&D labs. It lets scientists search, compare, and order more than 50 million SKUs from over 6,000 global suppliers through a single consolidated catalog and checkout, with real-time availability, spend visibility, and automated approval workflows. ZAGENO connects into enterprise procure-to-pay and ERP systems (Coupa, SAP Ariba, Jaggaer, Procurify, NetSuite, QuickBooks and more) through a single PunchOut/cXML catalog integration rather than a public developer API. Founded in 2015 and headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, it is backed by General Catalyst, Grazia Equity, and Capnamic Ventures.

providers.name: Zmanda
providers.description: Zmanda is an enterprise backup and recovery software provider and the commercial steward of the open-source Amanda (Advanced Maryland Automatic Network Disk Archiver) project. Its products protect Linux, Windows and macOS systems, databases, and application data with agent-based and agentless backups that write to local disk, tape, and public-cloud object storage. The company maintains an active GitHub organization (github.com/zmanda) around the Amanda backup engine and related tooling, operates a customer-facing management portal at the Zmanda Network (network.zmanda.com), and publishes API documentation for programmatic backup and recovery management at api.zmanda.com. Zmanda was an early portfolio company of Canaan Partners.

providers.name: zovo-one
providers.description: Zovo publishes 108 Chrome extensions and free online tools, serving over 150,000 users. Built and maintained by a single developer, Michael Lip, the extensions cover productivity, privacy, and developer utilities. Free features run locally in the browser, while optional Pro upgrades unlock additional capabilities for a monthly or lifetime fee. The site also offers browser-based tools such as calculators, converters, and editors, all accessible without installation. Zovo’s open‑source code is hosted on GitHub under the MIT licence.

providers.name: کافه باشور
providers.description: کافه باشور یک کافه و کافی‌شاپ در بلوار پیروزی مشهد است که با ارائه منوهای متنوع از صبحانه تا دسرهای روزانه، فضای داخلی بدون دود و حیاط باز، خدمات رزرو میز و تحویل آنلاین را فراهم می‌کند. هدف این کافه ارائه تجربه‌ای صمیمی و آرام برای مهمانان است و به‌صورت شفاف درباره منو، قیمت و ساعات کاری اطلاعات را در وب‌سایت خود منتشر می‌کند.

providers.name: 3D New Era AI
providers.description: 3D New Era AI offers an open-source architecture and interiors editor powered by a multi‑modal conversational AI. Users can design homes by speaking to the AI, which draws, furnishes, lights, and renders realistic images in real time. The platform runs on Windows, macOS, and Linux, and includes an MCP server for extensibility. It aims to democratize high‑quality interior design through accessible AI tools.

providers.name: 409A Providers
providers.description: 409A Providers is an information site that compares 409A valuation providers for US startups. It publishes list prices, turnaround times, audit support details, and who signs the reports, based on each provider’s own published pages as of the date shown.

providers.name: 7-Eleven
providers.description: A global convenience store chain offering everyday essentials, snacks, and beverages. Known for its 24/7 operations and Slurpee brand drinks.

providers.name: A2A Retailmedia
providers.description: A2A Retailmedia is an agentic commerce hub that connects grocery retailers with makers through a Model Context Protocol (MCP) door. It enables retailers to claim media cards for each grocery banner and allows makers’ agents to discover and purchase media placements. The platform supports over 8,600 grocery banners across 20 markets, handling hundreds of thousands of makers. It offers self‑service setup, card claiming, and enrollment flows, and provides documentation and API access via a developer portal. Powered by gtinfetch.ai, A2A Retailmedia aims to streamline media buying on the shelf.

providers.name: A2Me
providers.description: A2Me (Ancestors to Me) is a family connection platform — Connect Today. Remember Forever. Share memories, plan events and trips, build your family tree, and preserve your legacy, without the distractions of traditional social media.

providers.name: Abiomed
providers.description: Abiomed is a Danvers, Massachusetts medical device manufacturer and, since December 22 2022, a standalone business inside Johnson & Johnson MedTech, which acquired it for approximately $16.6 billion. The company designs, manufactures and supports the Impella family of percutaneous micro-axial heart pumps — Impella CP, 5.5, RP Flex and the SmartAssist sensor line — used for temporary mechanical circulatory support during high-risk percutaneous coronary intervention and in cardiogenic shock, alongside the Automated Impella Controller console, the Breethe OXY-1 ECMO system and the Impella Connect remote case-review service. Its product is regulated hardware sold to hospitals and cath labs, supported by a 24/7 clinical support centre, not software sold to developers. Abiomed's digital surface is limited to two end-user products: Impella Connect, a customer-only clinician portal that receives one-way RTMPS video of the console screen over port 443, and the Impella App for clinical reference. Abiomed publishes no developer portal, no API reference, no OpenAPI or other machine-readable specification, no SDK on npm, PyPI or any other registry, and maintains no public source-code organisation; the corporate site abiomed.com now redirects to the brand site at heartrecovery.com.

providers.name: Accolade
providers.description: Accolade is a personalized healthcare and benefits navigation platform for employers and health plans. It pairs members with a care team of advocates, registered nurses, physicians, and mental-health specialists to help them understand their benefits, find in-network care, book appointments, and manage chronic and complex conditions. Accolade combines this human advocacy with virtual primary care, expert medical opinion, and mental-health services delivered through its member web and mobile apps. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network. Accolade is a member-facing benefits platform and does not publish a public API, developer portal, or developer documentation.

providers.name: actnano
providers.description: actnano, Inc. is a Massachusetts-based advanced materials company that develops and manufactures PFAS-free protective nanocoatings for electronics. Its flagship Advanced nanoGUARD technology is a gel-state, 100% fluorine-free conformal coating applied to printed circuit board assemblies, connectors, antennas, LEDs and high-heat-generating components, delivering up to IPx8 moisture and condensation protection without trapping heat or degrading signal integrity. Founded in 2012 and headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, with a Munich center of excellence and operations in Mexico and Japan, actnano serves mobility and automotive electronics, consumer electronics, AI and data-center infrastructure, solar, industrial electronics, medical devices and optical anti-fog applications. The company states REACH and RoHS compliance and ISO 9001:2015 certification, and is backed by BMW i Ventures, Porsche Ventures and Emerald Technology Ventures. actnano is a materials manufacturer: it publishes no public developer program, API, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Adept
providers.description: Adept was an AI research lab building action-taking foundation models (the ACT family) that can use software tools and complete tasks across business applications. In mid-2024, several Adept co-founders and senior researchers joined Amazon's AGI organization in a non-acquisition arrangement, and Amazon licensed Adept's technology. Adept the entity continues to exist, but it has no current public commercial API; its primary remaining footprint is open-source models published on Hugging Face (Fuyu-8B, Persimmon-8B) and historical research outputs (ACT-1, ACT-2).

providers.name: Agent Papers
providers.description: Agent Papers is a registry and platform that aggregates API information for companies providing identity, communication, financial, and legal services to AI agents. It offers a searchable catalog, categorized listings, and tools for developers to integrate agent‑centric infrastructure such as phone numbers, email, addresses, wallets, and compliance resources. The site is regularly updated and includes documentation, changelogs, and an MCP interface for programmatic access.

providers.name: Agentero
providers.description: Agentero is a digital insurance network and insurtech platform, founded in 2017 and based in Oakland, California, that gives independent property & casualty insurance agents market access to 100+ national and regional carriers alongside modern agency technology. Its unified command center lets agents get appointed, quote and bind policies, manage carrier appointments, and reconcile commissions from a single portal, with no startup fees or minimum-volume requirements. Agentero also offers an AI Appetite Checker that matches risks to the right carriers and Producerflow, a compliance and producer-management solution for carriers, MGAs, and agencies. Agentero is a portfolio company backed by Union Square Ventures.

providers.name: AMC Global Media
providers.description: AMC Global Media Inc. (NASDAQ: AMCX), known as AMC Networks until its 2026 rebrand, is a global entertainment company that owns and operates AMC, BBC America, IFC, SundanceTV and We TV, the AMC+, Acorn TV, Shudder, Sundance Now, HIDIVE and ALLBLK streaming services, AMC Studios, IFC Films and AMC Networks International. It distributes 33 FAST channels across 22 platforms and sells advertising through its Audience+ audience data platform and AMCN Outcomes measurement product. The company publishes no public developer program and no machine-readable API contract: affiliate distribution runs through a login-gated partner portal, advertising is booked through sales, and broadcast delivery is contracted through its Broadcasting & Technology group. The legacy domain www.amcnetworks.com now redirects to www.amcglobalmedia.com.

providers.name: Antheia
providers.description: Antheia, Inc. is a Menlo Park, California synthetic-biology company that manufactures biosynthetic key starting materials (KSMs) and active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) for essential medicines. Founded on Christina Smolke's Stanford research, Antheia engineers yeast strains that reconstruct long, complex plant biosynthetic pathways and ferment sugar into molecules previously obtainable only through agricultural cultivation, compressing production timelines from years to weeks. Commercial products include fermentation-derived thebaine, oripavine and scopolamine, with a development pipeline of 70+ KSMs and APIs spanning neurology, gastrointestinal and oncology programs. NOTE FOR THE CATALOG: Antheia's "APIs" are Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients, not web APIs — the company publishes no developer API, SDK, or machine-readable interface contract.

providers.name: Apellatechnology
providers.description: Apellatechnology, operating under the brand Apella, provides ambient AI solutions for operating rooms, optimizing surgical capacity, reducing delays, and improving turnover efficiency. Their platform integrates with EHR systems to deliver real-time analytics, predictive case duration, and resource optimization for hospitals and surgical teams.

providers.name: Aprende
providers.description: Aprende (Aprende Institute) is an online vocational education platform delivering Spanish-language courses and diplomados to Hispanic entrepreneurs and professionals across the United States and Latin America. The platform offers on-demand, mobile-friendly training across six main areas — gastronomy, entrepreneurship, wellness, beauty, skilled trades, and hospitality/events — taught by expert instructors, and is backed by 500 Global. It operates as a consumer education company with no public developer API surface; this profile tracks its identity and web properties in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: AstroTune
providers.description: AstroTune provides a web-based Vedic astrology platform that calculates natal charts using traditional Jyotish methods. Users input birth date, time, and location to receive detailed charts, including ayanamsa, house systems, and planetary positions. The service emphasizes transparency about data handling and offers tools for learning about zodiac signs, nakshatras, and planetary influences.

providers.name: Authoryze
providers.description: Authoryze provides MCP-native payment infrastructure that lets AI agents make purchases using single-use virtual cards. It offers spending limits, merchant approvals, audit trails, and team budgeting, supporting integrations with OpenAI, Claude, and other AI services. Plans start at $39.99/month for up to 100 transactions, with per-transaction pricing for higher volumes. The platform emphasizes security by never exposing real credit card details to agents.

providers.name: AutoAlign AI
providers.description: AutoAlign AI provides worker‑first industrial AI solutions that empower frontline workers with real‑time visual assistance, guided work instructions, hazard detection, and automatic documentation. Their platform integrates AI into smart glasses, tablets, and phones to capture tribal knowledge, improve safety, and increase productivity across industries such as automotive, aerospace, energy, and construction. By delivering step‑by‑step guidance and on‑demand answers, AutoAlign AI helps companies reduce errors, streamline processes, and enhance overall operational efficiency.

providers.name: Avant
providers.description: Avant is a Chicago-based financial technology company that provides consumer credit products to middle-income U.S. consumers, primarily unsecured personal loans of roughly $2,000-$35,000 (9.95%-35.99% APR, 24-60 month terms) for debt consolidation, emergencies, home improvement, and other needs, alongside the Avant Credit Card issued through WebBank. Founded in 2012 and backed by investors including QED Investors and 500 Global, Avant operates a mobile-first lending and card-servicing platform with a customer help center, personal-finance blog, and SCRA support for military members. Avant is a consumer-facing product company and does not publish a public developer API or portal; this profile captures its public web, security, and support surfaces.

providers.name: Aviyair
providers.description: Aviyair provides global coverage of flight and airport information including real-time and historical flight tracking, flight schedules with airline arrival and departure times, IATA and ICAO codes, airline routes, and flight delays information.

providers.name: Baba
providers.description: Baba Care, Inc. is a healthcare company that provides patient advocacy and care-navigation services for Medicare beneficiaries in the United States. Operating under the tagline "Healthcare simplified," Baba pairs each member with a dedicated advocate who handles their healthcare headaches — coordinating care, benefits, and administrative tasks — with the service covered by Medicare. The member experience is delivered through a login-gated web application at baba.care; the company publishes no public developer or API surface at this time. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of General Catalyst and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: Bacca.ai
providers.description: Bacca.ai is an AI-driven Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) platform that deploys an autonomous agent functioning as a Tier-1 on-call engineer. It ingests operational context from Slack, Jira, documentation, logs, traces, and metrics to build a proprietary Knowledge Graph of an organization's systems, then contextualizes and deduplicates alerts, identifies root causes with high accuracy, automates incident war rooms and post-mortem generation, and surfaces reports on system failures and hotspots. Bacca reports cutting Mean Time To Resolution (MTTR) by roughly 40-60%. Founded in 2023 and headquartered in San Francisco, the company deploys on Google Cloud (cloud or on-prem) with single-tenant data isolation and SOC 2 Type I & II attestation. Backed by Homebrew.

providers.name: Backbone
providers.description: Backbone sells handheld gaming controllers and devices, such as the Backbone Pro and Backbone One, along with the Backbone App that lets gamers play mobile, console, and PC games on their phones or stream from cloud services. The products target gamers who want portable, low‑latency control for services like Xbox Cloud Gaming, PlayStation Remote Play, Steam Link, Apple Arcade, and NVIDIA GeForce NOW.

providers.name: BAE Systems
providers.description: BAE Systems is a British multinational defense, security, and aerospace company and one of the largest defense contractors globally. BAE Systems does not publish public developer APIs; technology integration is delivered through classified and ITAR-controlled customer programs, the Discover supplier portal, defense-program-specific data exchanges (e.g. F-35 ALIS / ODIN, Eurofighter), and FMS / government-to-government channels.

providers.name: Bambora
providers.description: Bambora, now part of Worldline, provides payment solutions for businesses, including card acquiring, online checkout, invoicing, and open banking services. The company offers a unified platform for merchants to accept payments across channels, manage transactions, and access financial data APIs. With a focus on security and compliance, Bambora serves retailers, e‑commerce, and enterprises in Europe and beyond.

providers.name: Beam
providers.description: Beam Mobility provides safe, sustainable, technology-backed shared micromobility solutions, connecting cities globally with e-scooters and bikes. Their platform offers fleet management, rider safety features, insurance, and a developer-friendly API for partners to integrate services, access vehicle data, and manage operations.

providers.name: Begonia.pro
providers.description: Simplifying Local SEO for Small Businesses: Our Mission Begonia.pro was born to help local shop owners, artisans and freelancers improve online visibility, attract more customers, and increase revenue. The platform offers easy-to-use tools optimized for smartphones, providing fast rankings without hours of work. Founded by Antoine Frankart with 15 years of web and communication experience, Begonia.pro aims to make web marketing accessible and effective.

providers.name: BHP
providers.description: BHP is one of the world's largest mining companies, headquartered in Melbourne, Australia. BHP does not publish a public developer portal; integration is delivered through enterprise procurement systems for tier-1 and tier-2 suppliers, charter and shipping data exchanges for commodity logistics, and standard commodity-trading and assay data exchange formats with customers and exchanges (LME, SHFE).

providers.name: BillTrim
providers.description: BillTrim is a consumer bill-management and negotiation service that helps households lower, monitor, and pay their recurring bills. Its team negotiates with providers on the customer's behalf (up to twice a year), watches for price increases before autopay processes, and can pay bills automatically from a connected bank account. BillTrim advertises support for 20,000+ service providers across internet, cable, phone, insurance, and other recurring household expenses. Backed by 500 Global, it operates as a consumer-facing web and mobile application; no public developer API or developer portal is currently published.

providers.name: Bugcrowd
providers.description: Bugcrowd API for interacting and tracking the reported issues programmatically

providers.name: Cactos
providers.description: Cactos is a Finnish clean-energy company that designs, manufactures, and operates smart battery energy storage systems (BESS) for commercial, industrial, and grid-scale use. Its hardware line (Cactos Mylo commercial storage and Cactos Cardo backup power, built in part from second-life Tesla EV batteries) is paired with Cactos Spine, a cloud software platform that optimizes each unit for load shifting, peak shaving, demand-charge reduction, solar self-consumption, backup power during outages, and participation in electricity and grid-balancing markets. Cactos serves logistics, manufacturing, EV charging, agriculture, real estate, and commercial-property operators. It is a portfolio company of Union Square Ventures. As of this profile, Cactos publishes no public developer API, SDK, or API documentation; the Cactos Spine app at app.cactos.com is a customer-facing management console rather than a documented developer API.

providers.name: Cala Systems
providers.description: Cala Systems designs and manufactures intelligent heat pump water heaters that customize heating for each home daily, delivering reliable hot water while significantly reducing energy costs. Proudly designed and assembled in the USA, the company focuses on innovative, energy‑efficient solutions for residential water heating, backed by extensive technical specifications, savings calculators, and a network of professional installers.

providers.name: Cencurity
providers.description: Cencurity provides a security gateway for LLM agents that detects and blocks prompt leakage, secrets, PII, and risky output in real time. It offers centralized dashboards, end‑to‑end log analysis, policy‑first detection, automatic redaction, and audit‑ready reporting. The service integrates with any LLM and IDE and is built for developers who need governed AI coding without disrupting workflows.

providers.name: Centivo
providers.description: Centivo is a primary-care-centered health plan administrator for self-funded employers, founded in 2017 and headquartered in New York City. Sold through benefits brokers and consultants, it serves mid-market employers (roughly 50 or more employees) and covers about 77,000 members across 160 businesses. Members get $0 primary care to encourage early intervention, and employers typically save 15-30% versus traditional fully-insured plans through a primary-care-first model, the cost advantages of self-funding, and directly negotiated health-system partnerships. Centivo operates member, employer, provider, and referral portals plus iOS/Android member apps; it does not publish a public developer API. Backed by Bain Capital Ventures and JPMorgan Chase's Morgan Health.

providers.name: Cintra Supply
providers.description: Cintra Supply is a US wholesale distributor of industrial and operational supplies, offering multi‑category B2B products such as MRO, janitorial, packaging, safety, electrical, datacom, IT hardware, batteries, backup power, and HVAC. They provide quotes in minutes with nationwide delivery and no minimum order requirements, serving customers across the United States.

providers.name: Clearscore
providers.description: ClearScore is a London-founded fintech (2015) that gives consumers free access to their credit score and report and matches them to financial products — credit cards, loans, car finance, insurance and more — through a personalised financial marketplace. It also runs ClearScore Protect (dark-web identity monitoring), DriveScore (driving-behaviour scoring) and Open Banking features, and operates across the UK, South Africa, Australia, Canada and New Zealand. Its B2B arm, ClearScore Connect, exposes credit-data and eligibility services to partner lenders through a partner-gated developer portal (docs.clearscore.com). Backed by QED Investors. This profile was surfaced as a QED portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; ClearScore's developer API is documented behind a password-gated ReadMe.io portal, so no public OpenAPI or machine-readable spec could be captured.

providers.name: Cleo
providers.description: Cleo provides a holistic, cost‑saving caregiving support platform for working parents, caregivers, employers, health plans, and consultants. It offers proactive family care solutions that claim up to 3× ROI, improving workforce productivity, employee retention, and mental health while reducing healthcare costs across the globe.

providers.name: Clickable
providers.description: Clickable is a marketing analytics and digital advertising platform founded in 2006 that serves as an ads and analytics partner for businesses and agencies. The company builds award-winning pay-per-click (PPC) advertising tools for search and social campaigns and delivers customized reporting that cuts through data overload so marketers can focus on the metrics that matter. Clickable also offers VIN retention reporting purpose-built for automotive dealerships to improve customer retention. Backed by Union Square Ventures, the company focuses on relationship-driven managed advertising and analytics services rather than a public developer API.

providers.name: Clipboard Health
providers.description: Clipboard Health provides an on-demand staffing platform that connects healthcare facilities with qualified professionals such as nurses, therapists, and support staff. The service enables facilities to post shifts quickly, offering hourly rates without fees for posting or canceling, and ensures rapid coverage with most shifts filled within an hour. Clipboard Health verifies background checks, licenses, and certifications of its workforce, and offers tools for facilities to manage staffing, view credentials, and export audit records. The platform emphasizes flexibility, allowing last‑minute coverage and supporting a wide range of roles across regions.

providers.name: Collision (now Web Summit Vancouver)
providers.description: Collision was the major annual North American technology conference organized by Web Summit, held in Toronto from 2019 through 2024 and widely dubbed the "Olympics of Tech." Beginning in 2025, the event was relocated to the Vancouver Convention Centre and rebranded as Web Summit Vancouver, aligning with the global Web Summit family (Lisbon, Rio, Doha, Qatar). Web Summit Vancouver is contracted through at least 2027 and was held May 27-30, 2025; Web Summit Vancouver 2026 is scheduled for May 11-14, 2026. The Collision brand is retired but this profile is preserved for historical reference. Collision/Web Summit does not publish a public developer REST API; the conference operates speaker, partner, attendee, and press portals.

providers.name: Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States
providers.description: The Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States (CFIUS) is an inter-agency committee chaired by the U.S. Department of the Treasury that reviews certain foreign investment transactions for national security implications. CFIUS reviews are governed by the Defense Production Act and Section 721, and were significantly strengthened by the Foreign Investment Risk Review Modernization Act of 2018 (FIRRMA). On September 15, 2022, President Biden issued Executive Order 14083 directing CFIUS to focus on emerging national security risks. CFIUS work is largely confidential, and the public-facing surface is limited to regulations, annual reports to Congress, FAQs, declarations and notices guidance, and case studies.

providers.name: Conexus Credit Union
providers.description: Conexus Credit Union is Saskatchewan's largest credit union, a member-owned cooperative financial institution headquartered in Regina with over $10 billion in consolidated assets under management, more than 140,000 members, roughly 30 branches, and over 800 employees across the province. As a provincially regulated Saskatchewan credit union it operates under a cooperative charter, with member deposits guaranteed by the Credit Union Deposit Guarantee Corporation (CUDGC). In November 2024 Conexus announced its intent to explore a merger with Cornerstone and Synergy credit unions. Conexus does not publish a first-party public developer API or a developer portal; developer.conexus.ca does not resolve, and /developer and /api on the corporate site return 404. Consumer financial-data access is provided through third-party aggregators (notably Plaid in Canada) via screen-scraping and connection-based data sharing rather than a first-party API. Digital and online banking are delivered through core-banking and fintech partners (banking.online.conexus.ca), and investing runs through the credit-union system's Aviso Wealth / Qtrade and Thrive Wealth partners. Canada's federal Consumer-Driven Banking (open banking) framework, overseen by the Financial Consumer Agency of Canada (FCAC), is legislated but not yet operational, so Conexus's open-finance access remains voluntary and aggregator-mediated today.

providers.name: Crabi
providers.description: Crabi is a Mexican digital auto-insurance company (insurtech) offering fully online vehicle policies purchasable in about fifteen minutes from a mobile device. Coverage spans material damage, theft, third-party civil liability, medical expenses, and roadside and legal assistance across 27 Mexican states, sold and serviced through its mobile apps, online quoter (cotizador), and customer login portal. The company is regulated in Mexico by the CNSF and CONDUSEF and is a portfolio company of 500 Global. Crabi publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs; this profile captures its identity and public web surface.

providers.name: CUUP
providers.description: CUUP, Inc. is a New York City-based direct-to-consumer intimates brand founded in 2018 by Abby Morgan and Kearnon O'Molony, offering precision-fit bras, underwear, loungewear, apparel, and swim across an extended range of cup and band sizes sold through its shopcuup.com online store. Backed by Insight Partners and Forerunner Ventures, CUUP was acquired by FULLBEAUTY Brands in July 2023 and now runs on the FULLBEAUTY commerce platform. As a consumer retail company it exposes no public developer API; this API Evangelist profile captures its public web presence, domain security posture, and commercial policy pages.

providers.name: Dalma
providers.description: Dalma is a French insurtech offering pet health insurance for dogs and cats, reimbursing veterinary bills (up to 100%, no deductible, EUR 2,500 annual ceiling) with fast payouts (50% within 30 seconds) and unlimited teleconsultations with veterinarians via its mobile app. Founded in Paris and backed by Northzone, Dalma insures 60,000+ pets across France and has expanded to Germany. It is a direct-to-consumer insurance brand with a member app (app.dalma.co) and a quote/subscription funnel; it publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI definition, SDK, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Datawisp
providers.description: Datawisp is a no‑code analytics platform that enables users to analyze data and discover insights without technical expertise. It offers a node‑based interface for building data‑processing pipelines, AI‑powered assistance via Wispy for natural‑language chart creation, real‑time collaboration, and sharing capabilities. The platform runs in the browser and supports a variety of data blocks for filtering, sorting, visualizing, and more, targeting both technical and non‑technical users.

providers.name: DESERT FARMS
providers.description: Desert Farms Inc. is a direct-to-consumer camel milk brand founded in 2013 by Walid Abdul-Wahab and headquartered in Santa Monica, California. The company sources 100% pure camel milk from a network of small family-owned camel dairies across the United States and sells raw and pasteurized camel milk, frozen and powdered camel milk, plus camel-milk-based soaps and skincare, direct to consumers through its Shopify storefront at desertfarms.com and through select retail grocers. Backed by 500 Global, Desert Farms is a consumer packaged goods and e-commerce company rather than an API provider; it exposes no first-party developer API. Its public web surface runs on Shopify, whose Customer Account API OpenID Connect discovery documents are served on the storefront domain for customer login. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub and enriched with the domain-security, well-known, and site link-property signals that are genuinely present.

providers.name: District Cover
providers.description: District Cover is a commercial insurance managing general agent and surplus-lines broker focused on urban businesses. It underwrites flexible commercial coverage for city-based retailers, restaurants, bakeries, laundromats, dry cleaners, salons, law and medical offices, and multi-location mid-market operators, using block-level risk scoring drawn from crime and fire analytics rather than broad ZIP-code assessments. The platform supports real-time submissions, multi-location quoting, and property-only endorsements, and is distributed to brokers through a licensed producer network operating across multiple U.S. states. District Cover publishes no public API or developer program; broker access is delivered through a hosted Insly portal.

providers.name: Drain Prices
providers.description: Drain Prices provides up‑to‑date UK emergency drain unblocking cost data, offering price ranges for call‑outs, jetting, CCTV surveys and excavations. The site aggregates local contractor quotes, explains responsibility for blocked drains, and supplies a free data set for homeowners and professionals.

providers.name: Drone Licence Checker UK
providers.description: Drone Licence Checker UK provides a free online tool to help UK drone operators determine whether they need to register their drone, obtain an Operator ID or Flyer ID, and understand the applicable CAA rules. The site offers guides, data tables, and links to official UK Civil Aviation Authority resources, covering categories A1, A2, A3, weight thresholds, camera requirements, and near‑people flight restrictions as of 2026.

providers.name: Earnest
providers.description: Earnest is a technology-driven consumer finance lender headquartered in San Francisco, offering student loan refinancing, private student loans, Parent PLUS loan refinancing, and personal loans through Earnest Operations LLC and its bank partner FinWise Bank. Founded in 2013 and backed by investors including Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Battery Ventures, and Slow Ventures, Earnest uses data-driven underwriting and merit-based pricing to serve borrowers, reporting more than $24 billion in student loans refinanced and over 420,000 clients. Earnest is a consumer-facing lending brand and does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or API reference; this profile captures its public web, security, and legal surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Eisen
providers.description: Eisen is an AI-enabled compliance operations platform for financial institutions and digital asset companies, managing escheatment (unclaimed property), disbursement, customer outreach, and 1099 tax reporting across all account types. Its product suite includes an Escheatment Manager that tracks state compliance deadlines and dormancy rules, a Disbursement Manager that automates personalized customer payments, an Outreach Manager that re-engages dormant account holders, and a 1099 Reporting Manager for tax reporting. Eisen handles dormant accounts, stale checks, account wind-downs, and forced closures, and is backed by Cowboy Ventures, Homebrew, and Index Ventures. As of this profile Eisen exposes no public developer API, portal, or documentation; this record captures its identity and public web surface.

providers.name: Ejen2u
providers.description: Ejen2u is a Malaysian reseller and agent-management technology company that operates one of the country's largest cloud-based reseller ecosystems for MSME brand owners, stockists, agents, dropshippers, and affiliates. Its platform spans EjenGO, a digital reseller and stockist management system; WEMAP, an entrepreneurial education program; and EjenVenture, custom reseller-network solutions for corporate brands, alongside fintech and logistics integrations (Pos Laju, Boost, Curlec, Delyva, J&T). Founded in 2019 and headquartered in Seri Kembangan, Ejen2u is backed by 500 Global, Gobi Partners, and Artem Ventures, and has facilitated hundreds of millions of ringgit in reseller commerce across a network of hundreds of thousands of agents. It exposes no public developer API today; this profile is an API Evangelist network entry enriched from public sources.

providers.name: Electric Car Scheme
providers.description: The Electric Car Scheme is a UK B Corp providing electric vehicle salary sacrifice as an employee benefit. Employees lease any electric car of their choice with the monthly cost deducted from gross salary before Income Tax and National Insurance, saving 20-50% versus a personal lease, while employers save on Class 1A National Insurance. Packages are all-inclusive (lease, insurance, maintenance, servicing and breakdown) with Complete Protection covering employees who leave partway through a lease term. The company integrates with employer payroll systems via API or SFTP and offers Single Sign-On for employees, plus an included Charge Scheme for charging access.

providers.name: ESPHome
providers.description: ESPHome is an open-source platform that simplifies building custom smart home devices using ESP8266/ESP32 microcontrollers. It provides a visual device builder, YAML configuration files, and seamless integration with Home Assistant, allowing users to create sensors, switches, lights, and more without extensive coding. The platform offers extensive component libraries, OTA updates, and local control, emphasizing privacy and flexibility for hobbyists and developers alike.

providers.name: Euler Motors
providers.description: Euler Motors is an Indian electric commercial vehicle manufacturer headquartered in New Delhi, building battery-electric cargo and light commercial vehicles for last-mile logistics — the HiLoad and Turbo electric three-wheelers and the Storm EV four-wheeler light commercial vehicle range. Alongside the vehicles the company operates Euler Shepherd, a connected-vehicle telematics platform delivered as two end-user products: Shepherd Lite (a mobile app for real-time vehicle location, battery state of charge, range, charging status and alerts) and Shepherd Enterprise (a browser-based fleet console with trip, utilization and operations reporting). Euler Motors publishes no public developer program: there is no developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDK, webhook catalog or partner integration documentation on any host it controls. The Shepherd web console is a single-page application whose backend answers anonymous requests with 403, so the telematics data surface is reachable only to vehicle owners inside the product. The company does publish an llms.txt at its web root, directing AI crawlers to its product, service-network and blog pages.

providers.name: Fabric Technologies
providers.description: Fabric Technologies operates Fabric by Gerber Life, a direct-to-consumer financial services platform built for parents and families. The company offers term life insurance with an instant online quote and application flow, UGMA custodial investment accounts and 529 college-savings plans for children, and digital estate-planning tools including free wills. Fabric is backed by Gerber Life, part of Western & Southern Financial Group, and was originally venture-funded by Bessemer Venture Partners. The platform emphasizes fast, accessible, mobile-first family financial planning spanning protection, wealth-building, and legacy planning. Fabric is a consumer-facing service and does not currently publish a public developer API or portal.

providers.name: Fashinza
providers.description: Fashinza is a tech-enabled apparel manufacturing and supply-chain platform that connects fashion brands and retailers with a vetted global network of garment manufacturers. It streamlines end-to-end production: sourcing designs and fabrics, AI-powered supplier matching, tech-pack and sample creation, real-time production tracking, quality control, and merchandising and forecasting support so brands can move from design to delivery in shortened 30-45 day cycles. Backed by Accel and Prosus Ventures, the company operates a buyer login and a supplier onboarding surface but publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs at this time.

providers.name: Fibraweb, S.p.a.
providers.description: Fibraweb S.p.A. is an Italian telecommunications infrastructure operator, founded in 2012 and headquartered in Perugia (Umbria), that designs, builds and operates its own fiber-optic access network for businesses, wholesale operators and public administrations. The company delivers FTTH/FTTB ultra-broadband internet access, dedicated internet access circuits, and local and long-distance voice/telephony services across the Umbria, Marche, Toscana and Lazio regions, with a proprietary network of roughly 1,500 km of fiber reaching 150 industrial zones and the ability to connect over 30,000 companies. Fibraweb is a Battery Ventures portfolio company (investors also include Equiter and GTD Grupo Teleductos) and holds ISO 9001, ISO/IEC 27001 and ISO/IEC 27017 certifications. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; the company does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation.

providers.name: Finch Legal
providers.description: Finch Legal (Finch) is an AI-powered pre-litigation platform built for personal injury law firms, combining US-based expert legal operators with AI agents to run cases on autopilot from intake through demand. Its services span 24/7 bilingual intake and client sign-up, insurance claim and police-report retrieval, treatment tracking with client check-ins, and expert-reviewed demand-letter generation, with beta capabilities for medical chronologies and litigation support. Finch writes updates directly into a firm's existing case-management system rather than adding a new tool, integrating with Filevine, Smokeball, Litify, Neos, SmartAdvocate, MyCase, Clio, Casepeer, and Cloudlex. The company is SOC 2 certified, headquartered in New York City, and backed by venture investors. Finch exposes no public developer API, documentation, or SDK at this time; this profile captures its identity and security posture.

providers.name: Finni Health
providers.description: Finni Health is a telehealth company that connects families of children on the autism spectrum with Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA) therapists and mental health providers. Operating across more than 30 states, Finni offers both in-home and in-clinic ABA therapy with flexible scheduling, handles insurance coordination and billing for its provider network, and gives parents a portal for progress tracking and family-led goal setting. The company positions itself as an operating platform for ABA practices as well as a care provider for families, but publishes no public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable API specifications at this time.

providers.name: Freckle Education
providers.description: Freckle is an adaptive learning platform from Renaissance that delivers differentiated, standards-aligned math and English Language Arts (ELA) practice for K-12 students. Teachers assign work and monitor progress while students practice at their own level, with the platform adapting question difficulty to each learner across 70,000+ math questions and 1,000+ ELA passages. Administrators manage rosters and dashboards at the school and district level. Freckle is a school- and classroom-facing application acquired by Renaissance Learning; it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or a developer portal, so this profile captures its identity, published web properties, and probed domain-security posture rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Fy
providers.description: Fy! (iamfy.co) is an online marketplace for wall art and home decor, curating canvas prints, framed prints, gallery wall sets, and handmade UK-manufactured frames from a community of independent artists. The storefront runs on Shopify and offers an AI-powered "Advisor" tool for personalized wall-design recommendations, an art-for-business program, and an artists hub for creators. Fy was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. It publishes no first-party developer API; the only machine-readable surface reachable on the domain is the Shopify Customer Account OIDC/OAuth discovery served by the platform.

providers.name: Genesis Energy
providers.description: Genesis Energy, L.P. (NYSE: GEL) is a diversified midstream energy master limited partnership headquartered in Houston, Texas. It operates offshore crude oil and natural gas pipelines and platforms in the Gulf of Mexico, onshore pipelines and terminals, marine transportation for refined products and crude, and a sulfur services and soda ash (alkali) chemicals business serving refineries, producers, and industrial and commercial customers. It is a pipeline and chemicals operator, not a software vendor: it publishes no developer program, no API and no machine-readable API contract. Its only public machine-readable surface is the FERC-mandated informational posting website it runs for its interstate natural gas pipeline, which serves NAESB WGQ-shaped location and capacity data as anonymous file downloads.

providers.name: Glassdoor
providers.description: Glassdoor is an online platform for company reviews, salary reports, and job listings, now part of Recruit Holdings (alongside Indeed) and tightly integrated with the broader Workday talent ecosystem. Historically Glassdoor offered a public Partner Job Search / Employer Reviews API (api.glassdoor.com/api/api.htm), but the program was closed to new applications in 2021 and active integrations require an existing partner relationship. Current API access is enterprise sales-led for ATS, programmatic recruitment, and employer-brand partners. No self-serve developer portal is active today.

providers.name: Global ID
